questions.explanation: No renewal provision names Class C in a bar or non-renewability list, so Class C licenses are renewable on the general terms. The non-renewability provisions in the renewal rules are directed at the entry-level license, not at Class C.

questions.question: Why can waste sludge from an extended aeration plant often be sent to dewatering or drying without a separate sludge digestion step?

answers.text: Extended aeration sludge contains no volatile solids at all
The sludge is disinfected by the long exposure to air in the basin
The long aeration period has already oxidized much of the sludge's degradable material, so it arrives well stabilized
Extended aeration plants are exempt from stabilizing sludge before disposal, because sludge from this mode never requires any further stabilization

questions.explanation: The extended aeration period keeps solids under aeration long enough that much of their degradable content is consumed in the basin, leaving a well-stabilized waste sludge. It still contains volatile solids and is not disinfected, so stabilization in the basin — not an exemption — is what makes the direct route possible.

questions.question: The chief operator is away from the plant for the day. Which role provides the on-site supervision and operation of the facility during that absence?

answers.text: The operator in charge for the facility
The newest operator in training
The permittee's office manager
The next shift's relief operator, by phone

questions.explanation: The operator in charge is the licensed operator charged with on-site supervision and operation of the facility in the chief operator's absence. That duty cannot be handed to an untested trainee or handled remotely by a relief operator.

questions.question: The effluent weir plates on a primary clarifier are made adjustable, with slotted bolt holes. What maintenance purpose does that serve?

answers.text: The operator can raise or lower the weirs to change the tank's surface loading from week to week as flows change
A weir gone out of level as a tank settles can be raised or lowered back to a level line
The plates can be lifted clear so a worker can enter the launder
The height of the weir plate sets the sludge blanket draw-off rate

questions.explanation: Adjustable plates exist so a weir thrown out of level by settlement can be trued up again, restoring an even flow over its whole length. Sliding them does not change the tank's surface loading, and weir height has nothing to do with sludge draw-off.

questions.question: In hot weather a pond develops a bright, paint-like blue-green scum that collects in mats on the surface. What does this appearance indicate?

answers.text: The pond has finished treatment and the scum is a harmless layer of pure oxygen bubbles trapped in foam
Iron bacteria have taken over the pond and are precipitating mineral films across the surface, tinting the whole cell as they spread through the warm water
A chemical spill has coated the pond, and the color will clear as soon as the spill is diluted by rainfall
Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) have come to dominate the pond's algae population under warm, nutrient-rich conditions

questions.explanation: The paint-like blue-green mat is the classic look of a cyanobacteria bloom, which thrives in warm, nutrient-rich pond water. It is a living algal population, not a spill coating or a mineral precipitate.

questions.question: A plant switches its final disinfection step to ultraviolet light. What limitation of ultraviolet light must the operating plan account for downstream of the channel?

answers.text: It leaves a long-lasting residual that must be removed before the water can be discharged
It works only when the water is completely free of chlorine
It leaves no residual, so it gives no protection beyond the exposure point
It requires the effluent to be heated before discharge

questions.explanation: Ultraviolet light inactivates organisms as the water passes the lamps but leaves nothing behind to keep disinfecting, unlike a chemical residual. Any storage or conveyance after the channel gets no continuing protection from the ultraviolet step.

questions.question: Wet dewatered biosolids are being composted, but the piles are dense, soggy, and turning odorous in the core despite regular turning. Mixing in wood chips improves them. What did the wood chips provide?

answers.text: Extra nitrogen in the chips to feed the composting organisms throughout the pile
A chemical disinfectant that sterilizes the pile
Porosity for airflow and absorption of excess moisture
A seal over the pile surface that traps heat

questions.explanation: Bulking agents such as wood chips open the pile's structure so air can move through it and soak up free moisture, keeping the process aerobic. Dense, wet piles go anaerobic in the core and generate the odors described.

questions.question: A plant flows 0.62 MGD and needs a dose of 3.4 mg/L of active chemical. The product on hand is 65% pure. How many pounds of product must be fed per day?

answers.text: 17.58 lb/day
27.05 lb/day
41.66 lb/day
11.43 lb/day

questions.explanation: The active need is 0.62 x 3.4 x 8.34 = 17.58 lb/day, and dividing by 0.65 for the product strength gives 27.05 lb/day of product. Feeding only 17.58 lb of product would deliver just 65% of the intended dose.

questions.question: A plant conditioning sludge ahead of pressure filtration has long used a two-chemical program. Which pair is the classic conditioning combination for that duty?

answers.text: Polymer and chlorine dioxide
Sodium hypochlorite and alum
Ferric chloride and lime
Methanol and caustic soda

questions.explanation: Ferric chloride with lime is the long-standing inorganic conditioning pair for vacuum and pressure filtration, building a rigid sludge structure that releases water under pressure. The other pairs are disinfection or alkalinity chemicals, not filter conditioning programs.

questions.question: Two plants discharge similar effluent quality, one to a large river and one to a small, slow-moving stream. Why is the smaller stream at greater risk from the discharge?

answers.text: The small stream is at greater risk because its banks are closer together, so the discharge plume touches both banks and cannot disperse across the channel
The small stream provides far less dilution, so the effluent makes up a larger share of the flow and its effects are concentrated
Effluent always damages small streams because they contain no organisms
The large river is at greater risk because its flow spreads contaminants farther

questions.explanation: Impact depends on dilution: in a small stream the effluent is a large fraction of the total flow, so its oxygen demand and other effects fall on a small volume of water. The same effluent in a large river is diluted many times over.

questions.question: A facultative pond system receives an average of 472 lb of BOD per day. The pond's water surface covers 8.6 acres. The operator spreads the daily BOD load over the surface area to find the organic loading rate. What is it?

answers.text: 5.49 lb/acre/day
40.59 lb/acre/day
54.88 lb/acre/day
109.77 lb/acre/day

questions.explanation: Organic loading = BOD load / area = 472 / 8.6 = 54.88 lb/acre/day. The 109.77 result halves the pond area before dividing, doubling the loading.

questions.question: Between weekly laboratory solids results, an operator watches the effluent turbidity trend on the bench meter each shift. What does a sudden turbidity climb most usefully warn of?

answers.text: Solids are beginning to carry over the clarifier weirs before the next laboratory result would show it
The chlorine feed pump has lost prime
The chlorine feed pump at the disinfection system has lost its prime and is delivering no chemical to the contact basin
The grit channel velocity has fallen

questions.explanation: Turbidity responds to the same fine particles that make up effluent solids, so a fast climb is an early, same-shift warning of carryover that the slower gravimetric test would only confirm days later. It carries no information about feed pumps or grit channels.

questions.question: After heavy rain, the plant's influent flow surges while laboratory results show the arriving wastewater is noticeably weaker than usual. What best explains the combination?

answers.text: Rain-driven infiltration and inflow added mostly clean water, raising the hydraulic load while diluting the wastewater's strength
Residents used far more water indoors during the storm, concentrating the waste
The laboratory samples were taken from the treated effluent by mistake
The collection system leaked wastewater out faster than the plant could receive it, so only the strongest wastewater from the nearest homes arrived

questions.explanation: Infiltration and inflow add groundwater and stormwater to the sewers, so flow rises sharply while the waste itself is diluted and weaker. Indoor use does not surge with rainfall in a way that would concentrate the waste.

questions.question: A daily settle test on the same mixed liquor shows the settled volume climbing steadily over a week while the MLSS result stays about the same. How should the operator use that trend?

answers.text: Ignore it, because only the MLSS number matters when judging how the solids are behaving
Settling is worsening; act on wasting and process checks before the clarifier suffers
Dilute the settle test sample so the reading returns to normal
Report the clarifier as failed and shut the basin down the same day

questions.explanation: At an unchanged solids concentration, a rising settled volume means each unit of solids is taking up more space — the early signature of poorer settling that will load the clarifier blanket. The trend's value is the lead time it gives for wasting and process corrections.

questions.question: Over several months a horizontal pump's vibration has steadily grown, though the impeller is clean and the bearings are sound. The mounting feet are found slightly loose on the base. What is the most likely explanation?

answers.text: The concrete base has absorbed wastewater over the years and swollen unevenly underneath the pump feet, tilting the unit
Falling discharge pressure has moved the pump out to the end of its curve
The motor windings have weakened and are pulling the rotor off center
Loose anchor bolts let the pump shift on its base, and the vibration grows as the looseness grows

questions.explanation: A pump that is no longer clamped firmly to its base can move under its own forces, and each bit of added looseness lets the movement grow, which matches a steady months-long rise in vibration with healthy internals. Swollen bases, weak windings, and curve position do not explain loose mounting feet.

questions.question: Wastewater is steadily leaking from the base of a trickling filter's rotary distributor, around the center column where the arms are fed. What is the most likely source?

answers.text: The distributor arms themselves have developed pinhole leaks along their full length, spraying water down at the base
The filter media has settled several inches under its own weight and is forcing stored water out at the base of the bed
The seal or packing where the rotating column meets the stationary feed pipe has worn and no longer holds the flow
The underdrains beneath the media are plugged solid, so filtered water is backing up and out around the center column

questions.explanation: The distributor's center column is the one rotating-to-stationary joint in the feed path, and its seal is the wear point that leaks there. Media settlement and underdrain plugging change ponding and drainage, not a leak at the column base.

questions.question: Tailwater at a Parshall flume has risen until the flume is submerged, but the operator keeps computing flow from the upstream head alone. What is wrong with those figures?

answers.text: Submergence makes the flume under-read by a wide margin, so figures taken that way are safely conservative for reporting
Submerged flow warps the flume throat and permanently changes its shape
Submerged flow breaks the single-head relationship — a second head measurement is needed to correct the flow
The stilling well necessarily fouls whenever the flume is submerged

questions.explanation: A Parshall flume's simple head-versus-flow relationship holds only for free flow; once tailwater submerges the throat, the downstream head must also be measured and a submergence correction applied. Reading the upstream head alone overstates the flow, and submergence does not warp the flume.

texas-wastewater-operator-class-b.quiz_title: Texas Wastewater Operator Class B Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How often must a wastewater system operations company renew its registration?

answers.text: Every three years
Only when it takes on a new facility or system
Every year, on the anniversary of its initial registration
Every five years, when its chief operator renews

questions.explanation: Operations companies register initially and renew every three years, on the registration cycle rather than on any individual operator's license cycle. Taking on a new facility does not by itself reset or replace that renewal cadence.

questions.question: A crew is setting up for a permitted wet-well entry that will use a tripod over the opening. When must the retrieval system be ready?

answers.text: Rigged and in place before the first entrant enters, so a rescue can begin immediately without another entry
Kept assembled in the service truck until it is actually needed, because retrieval equipment standing at the opening interferes with the entry work
Rigged after the first entrant is inside, because only then is the correct anchor point known
Rigged only if an entrant reports a problem, because setting it up in advance slows the entry work

questions.explanation: Non-entry rescue only works if the retrieval system is already rigged when trouble occurs; assembling it after an entrant collapses loses the minutes that decide the outcome. The tripod's position over the opening is known before anyone enters.

questions.question: Where do foam-forming filamentous organisms concentrate in an activated sludge system?

answers.text: In the clarifier sludge blanket, where settled solids rest below the liquid surface for hours
In the effluent, after passing freely over the clarifier weirs
In the grit chamber, attached to settled mineral particles
In the surface foam, where they are stabilized by their water-repelling cell surfaces

questions.explanation: Foam-forming organisms have water-repelling surfaces that attach to air bubbles and accumulate in the surface foam, which is why wasting foam removes them disproportionately. They do not preferentially concentrate in the clarifier blanket or the grit chamber.

questions.question: Which set lists the aids an examinee is authorized to use during the Class B examination?

answers.text: Pencil or pen, proctor-provided scratch paper, and a programmable graphing calculator
Pencil or pen, proctor-provided scratch paper, and a non-programmable calculator
Pencil or pen, personal notes, and a non-programmable calculator
Pencil or pen, reference books, and a non-programmable calculator

questions.explanation: The authorized aids are a pencil or pen, scratch paper provided and monitored by the proctor, and a non-programmable calculator. Personal notes and reference books are not authorized aids.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a selector zone at the head of an activated sludge basin?

answers.text: To settle grit before it can wear the aeration equipment
To disinfect the influent before it reaches the mixed liquor
To store peak wet-weather flow in the basin until the downstream units can accept it without washing solids out
To expose return sludge to a high food concentration that favors floc formers over filaments

questions.explanation: A selector gives floc-forming organisms first access to a high concentration of food, so they outcompete filamentous organisms that thrive when food is dilute throughout the basin. A selector does not settle grit, disinfect, or store peak flow.

questions.question: How should a senior operator best develop a shift operator in charge who has never led the response to a process upset?

answers.text: Keep the operator away from upset situations until a promotion requires leading one, to avoid mistakes during real events
Let the operator lead the next upset response entirely alone, with no senior operator present to advise or intervene if the response goes wrong
Assign the operator only routine rounds and readings for the foreseeable future, postponing any upset experience indefinitely
Delegate the lead role on an upset response while supervising and coaching through it

questions.explanation: Delegating the lead role under supervision builds the operator's judgment on a real event while the senior operator remains available to intervene. Withholding all upset experience leaves the operator unprepared for the first solo event.

questions.question: A new operator assumes the headworks grinder removes the solids it shreds, the way the bar screen removes its screenings. What is the correct understanding of the grinder's action?

answers.text: It removes the shredded solids through its discharge chute, which must be emptied and hauled away with the plant screenings
It dissolves organic solids on contact, so only grit and plastics remain in the flow after it
It removes exactly the same material as a screen, and the two units are interchangeable in duty
It cuts solids into small pieces that stay in the wastewater and pass on downstream; it removes no material from the flow

questions.explanation: A grinder's cutters only subdivide solids; everything it shreds stays in the flow and travels downstream, which is why it protects pumps without producing a removed-solids stream. It neither hauls material out like a screen nor dissolves what passes through it.

questions.question: As sustained cold weather arrives, a pond system's effluent quality slips even though loads are unchanged and oxygen stays adequate. A parallel cell stands empty after summer maintenance. What is the sound seasonal response?

answers.text: Rest the working cell and run the whole flow through the empty cell so it warms up first
Accept the slippage, because temperature has no effect on pond treatment rates at any load, so no change in operation is needed until the warm season returns on its own
Double the recirculation rate so the same water passes the algae twice as often each day
Put the standby cell into service alongside the working cell so total detention lengthens while bacterial rates are slowed by the cold

questions.explanation: Pond bacteria work more slowly in cold water, so the system compensates with more time: adding the standby cell lengthens detention at the same load. Recirculating faster does not add detention volume, and simply accepting the slippage ignores an available cell.

questions.question: A delivered load of sodium hypochlorite assays noticeably weaker than the strength the feed pump settings assumed, and the effluent residual has sagged since the delivery. What adjustment keeps the applied dose on target?

answers.text: Hold the feed settings unchanged, because strength differences average out over a full tank and the residual will return to normal on its own once this load has been in service for a week or two
Dilute the new load further so it matches the pump's original calibration curve
Reset the feed rate using the measured strength of the delivered chemical so the same mass of chlorine is applied
Sample the residual less often until the next delivery, so the sag does not trigger false alarms

questions.explanation: Dose is a mass of chlorine per volume of wastewater, so when the product carries less chlorine per gallon, more product must be fed to deliver the same mass. Feeding by the label strength after an assay shows otherwise guarantees an underdose.

questions.question: Solids in a gravity thickener keep rising to the surface trailing fine bubbles even though the blanket is being kept shallow, and the feed is well-nitrified return sludge. What is carrying the solids up?

answers.text: Grease worked into the sludge at the head of the plant, lightening every particle it coats
Air entrained by the thickener's rotating rake as it stirs the blanket on each pass
Oxygen released by algae growing on the thickener's sunlit surface during the day
Denitrification in the blanket, whose nitrogen gas attaches to the solids and floats them

questions.explanation: Nitrified sludge held in an oxygen-free blanket denitrifies, and the nitrogen gas bubbles that form buoy the solids to the surface regardless of blanket depth. The remedy targets detention and nitrate in the blanket, not grease removal at the headworks.

questions.question: During an upset the operator reconstructs the chlorine balance in steps: the feed was raised to a dosage of 9.47 mg/L, the outlet residual held at 2.13 mg/L, and the difference between the chlorine applied and the chlorine remaining is the demand the upset imposed. What was the demand, in mg/L?
questions.explanation: Demand = 9.47 - 2.13 = 7.34 mg/L. The upset consumed most of a much larger dose, which is why the feed had to be raised so far to hold the 2.13 mg/L residual.

questions.question: A digester's volatile acids have risen sharply over three days after a period of heavy sludge pumping into it, gas quality is deteriorating, and pH has begun to edge down. What is the correct first response?

answers.text: Increase the feed rate with the strongest sludge available, so the acid formers are diluted by fresh material entering the tank
Raise the digester temperature quickly by several degrees, because hotter conditions force the methane formers to consume acids faster
Cut back or pause the feed and protect the digester's alkalinity, giving the methane formers time to consume the accumulated acids
Drain and reseed the digester at once, because a rising volatile acid level always means the existing biology is already lost

questions.explanation: An overload means acids are being made faster than the slower methane formers can use them; reducing the load and preserving buffer lets them catch up while the population is still viable. Adding feed or swinging temperature adds stress to the very organisms that must recover.

questions.question: A food-processing discharge with very high salt content reaches the plant and biological performance drops, with no toxic chemical identified. What is the likely mechanism?

answers.text: The high dissolved salt stresses the treatment organisms osmotically, inhibiting their activity
The salt raises the wastewater temperature beyond the range the treatment organisms can tolerate for very long
Salt discharges always improve settling and cannot inhibit treatment, so the cause must be something else entirely
The salt consumed the wastewater's dissolved oxygen directly, leaving too little for the treatment organisms

questions.explanation: A large dissolved-salt load changes the osmotic environment the treatment organisms live in and can inhibit their activity even when no conventional toxicant is present. The effect is on the organisms themselves, not a direct consumption of oxygen by the salt.

questions.question: Reviewing basin loading in steps: the applied load has been worked out at 2,014 pounds of biochemical oxygen demand per day. The solids inventory is the sum of two basins holding 2,150 pounds and 1,650 pounds of mixed liquor solids. The loading carried by each pound of solids is the ratio of the two totals. What is the food-to-microorganism ratio?
questions.explanation: Inventory is 2,150 + 1,650 = 3,800 pounds, so the ratio is 2,014 / 3,800 = 0.53. The 1.89 option inverts the ratio, dividing the solids by the food instead of the food by the solids.

questions.question: An operator needs to judge whether the morning load surge is overwhelming the aeration basin and must choose sampling to support an aeration change within the same shift. Which approach fits that decision?

answers.text: Collect a single composite and wait for the five-day demand result before changing anything
Rely on last week's permit samples, which describe the same influent stream
Grab samples with fast plant-run tests taken through the surge
Send samples to an outside laboratory and hold the process unchanged for a week

questions.explanation: Same-shift process decisions need data on the same timescale: grab samples with rapid measurements taken through the event show what the basin is experiencing while it can still be corrected. Composite and five-day analyses describe the event only after it has passed.

questions.question: At the start of a storm, the headworks sees a sudden surge of grit and debris heavier than the flow increase alone would explain. What accounts for it?

answers.text: Material deposited in the collection lines during dry weather is flushed out by the first storm flows
Rainwater generates grit as it falls through the air and runs across the ground on its way into the system
The preliminary treatment equipment manufactures debris whenever the flow through it rises suddenly at the headworks
Operators upstream are dumping grit they have stored at lift stations into the lines during the storm to clear their sumps

questions.explanation: Solids and grit settle in collection lines during low dry-weather flows and are scoured out when storm flows arrive, so the first flush delivers an accumulated load to preliminary treatment. The material was already in the system, waiting to be mobilized.

questions.question: A colorimetric nutrient test on a strongly colored effluent sample reads implausibly high, and a sample blank prepared without the color-forming reagent shows substantial absorbance of its own. What is the correct analytical response?

answers.text: Report the high reading, because color always means more nutrient
Account for the sample's own color with the blank so only the reagent-produced color is measured
Dilute the sample until its natural color disappears completely
Switch the sample over to a suspended solids test, where its natural color can simply be ignored entirely

questions.explanation: A sample blank reveals how much absorbance comes from the sample's own color rather than the analytical reaction, and correcting for it isolates the color the reagent actually produced. Diluting until the color vanishes also dilutes the analyte and still leaves the interference unmeasured.

questions.question: A lift station pump overheats and delivers almost nothing. Its discharge gate valve handle turns freely and the stem rises to the full-open position, yet a gauge just past the valve shows almost no pressure while the pump strains. What has most likely happened inside the valve?

answers.text: The valve packing has failed, letting the discharge escape around the stem and starve the line
The gate has separated from its stem, so the stem travels as if opening while the gate stays seated across the flow path
The valve was installed backward, so its gate lifts against the flow and seals tighter as it opens
The stem threads are stripped at the top, so the valve is actually open and the pump itself has failed

questions.explanation: A stem that rises and turns normally while the gate it left behind stays across the port explains full-open indications with almost no flow and a straining pump. A packing leak would show as external leakage and would not block the line.

questions.question: A two-stage trickling filter plant assigns nearly all of its carbonaceous removal to the first filter and expects ammonia conversion mainly in the second. What is the first stage's role called and why does the arrangement work?

answers.text: It is a contact filter; holding the flow first equalizes temperature so the second stage's film never experiences a change
It is a polishing filter; straining solids first raises the ammonia concentration the second stage needs to begin nitrifying
It is a humus filter; settling sloughed film first prevents the second stage from receiving any oxygen demand at all
It is a roughing filter; removing the carbon load first leaves the second stage's film free of fast-growing competitors so nitrifiers can establish

questions.explanation: A roughing first stage strips most of the carbonaceous load, and only with that competition removed can the slow-growing nitrifiers hold film space and oxygen in the second stage. The first stage does not raise ammonia or remove all oxygen demand; it changes who can grow downstream.

questions.question: A mechanical bar screen that raked reliably now blinds during wet-weather flows, and the upstream channel level surges before the rake finally starts by hand. The rake motor and chain test fine, but the stilling well for the differential-level sensor is packed with grit and rags. What is the corrective action?

answers.text: Shorten the timer interval so the rake runs constantly and ignore the level signal until the wet season ends whenever the upstream level begins to climb during a storm event of any size
Open the bypass gate a fixed amount during every storm so part of the flow never reaches the screen
Raise the rake start setpoint so the mechanism runs less often and wears more slowly through the storm
Clean the stilling well and verify the sensor reads the true level difference so rake starts again track actual screen blinding

questions.explanation: The rake responds to the level difference across the screen; with the sensing well fouled, the control never sees the blinding that is actually occurring, so restoring clean, accurate sensing restores automatic starts. Constant timer running masks the fault while wearing the mechanism and bypassing sends unscreened flow forward.

texas-wastewater-operator-class-a.quiz_title: Texas Wastewater Operator Class A Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: When does a Class A candidate who tests by computer learn the examination result?

answers.text: When the license itself is issued, about a week later
Immediately, at the testing center
Only after requesting the score in writing
By mail, after the results are reviewed centrally

questions.explanation: Computer-based testing provides the score immediately at the center. The candidate does not wait for mailed results or for the license to be issued to learn the outcome.

questions.question: A station tour finds a wet-well hatch propped open with no barrier while a lone operator works nearby on another task. What must the chief require?

answers.text: Guarding, a cover, or an attendant at the opening whenever it is open and not actively in use
A sign on the hatch warning visitors to watch their step while work is underway at the station
A rope laid on the floor around the opening to mark where the safe walking zone ends
Nothing further, because the operator on site is experienced and knows the hatch is open

questions.explanation: An open well is both a fall opening and a source of hazardous atmosphere, and familiarity is the classic setup for a fall. Physical guarding or a cover, not signage or memory, is what protects the next person through the room.

questions.question: What does a state point analysis tell the chief operator of a large activated sludge plant?

answers.text: The exact filament species responsible for a bulking episode, read from the shape of the flux curve
Whether the clarifier's operating point sits within its thickening capacity or has passed beyond it
The oxygen transfer efficiency of the aeration grid serving the basin ahead of the clarifier
The alkalinity that will remain in the effluent once nitrification there is fully complete

questions.explanation: State point analysis plots the clarifier's operating point against its limiting solids flux curve, showing whether the unit is underloaded, critically loaded, or overloaded in thickening. It is a clarifier solids-flux tool; it identifies neither filaments nor aeration efficiency.

questions.question: What coverage must a Category A facility have?

answers.text: Round-the-clock on-site staffing every day, with no telephone or pager provision in the rule
Operated at least five days a week by the chief or a required-level operator, available by telephone or pager seven days a week
Operation seven days a week by the chief personally, with no separate availability requirement on any other day of the week at all
Operation three days a week by any licensed operator, with telephone availability on operating days only

questions.explanation: The facility must be operated at least five days per week by the licensed chief operator or an operator at the required level or higher, who must be available by telephone or pager seven days per week. The chief need not personally work every operating day.

questions.question: An effluent BOD result returns implausibly low from a sample drawn downstream of chlorination, and the bench sheet shows the sample was neither neutralized nor seeded. What went wrong?

answers.text: The sample was simply too warm on arrival, and warmth always lowers a BOD result to nearly zero regardless of the waste's strength
The chlorine in the sample raised its oxygen level, which the test then reads as negative demand
Nothing went wrong with the test, because chlorine has no effect inside a sealed BOD bottle
Chlorine kept disinfecting inside the bottle, suppressing the test organisms, so the sample must be dechlorinated and seeded

questions.explanation: Residual chlorine carried into the bottle continues to act on the test organisms, so the measured demand reflects disinfection rather than the wastewater's content; neutralizing the chlorine at collection and seeding the sample restores a valid test. Warmth does not erase demand, and chlorine exerts no such oxygen effect.

questions.question: An investigation confirms an operator falsified entries in an operating log. What is the upper-management response?

answers.text: Quietly correct the log entries and say nothing about it, so the operator is not discouraged from reporting in future
Transfer the operator to the laboratory, where entries matter less
Address it through the documented disciplinary process, applied consistently and with the facts recorded
Dismiss every operator on that shift, whether involved or not

questions.explanation: Falsified records are a serious integrity matter handled through the documented disciplinary process, with the facts recorded and the process applied consistently. Quiet correction hides the problem, and punishing uninvolved staff is not a defensible process.

questions.question: A large plant in a dense neighborhood draws repeated odor complaints traced to its open headworks and primary tanks, even though the processes run well. What facility modification addresses the complaints at their source?

answers.text: Plant a row of tall trees along the fence line so the odors leaving the plant are hidden from the neighbors who complain
Pump sludge out of the primary tanks far more often so nothing rests in them long enough to turn septic and release odor at the surface
Enclose the headworks and primary surfaces and collect the captured air for treatment before it is released to the neighborhood
Add fragrance masking at the fence line so the air leaving the plant smells acceptable even though the odor sources stay open

questions.explanation: Covering the sources and treating the collected air removes the odor load itself; trees hide nothing from the nose, withdrawal changes do not stop surface emissions from open tanks, and masking perfumes a problem instead of capturing it.

questions.question: A soil-bottom pond cell loses water through a permeable native bottom, and the rehabilitation plan for its outage calls for rebuilding the bottom as a soil liner. What work does that rehabilitation consist of?

answers.text: Amend the bottom soil with fine clay material and compact it in controlled layers, building a low-permeability soil liner across the cell floor
Pave the cell floor with concrete panels, because a rigid slab is the only bottom treatment that can reduce water loss from a pond of this size
Spread the sludge already in the cell evenly over the floor, because a layer of pond sludge seals a permeable bottom by itself
Line the cell with the geotextile fabric used for road work, because any manufactured sheet placed on the floor stops the water loss

questions.explanation: A soil liner works by mixing clay-rich material into the bottom and compacting it so the pores that carried water are closed; it is a recognized repair where a soil liner fits the plan. Sludge layers wash and crack, road fabric is not a barrier, and concrete is not the only way to cut a bottom's permeability.

questions.question: At night a large plant's flow falls to a small fraction of its daytime peak, and the effluent chlorine residual repeatedly overshoots, overloading dechlorination, while daytime control is good. What facility-level change best corrects this?

answers.text: Add a smaller trim feed pump or staged feed capacity so chlorine feed can turn down at low flows
Raise the daytime dose so the night overshoot looks smaller by comparison
Take the residual analyzer offline at night so the overshoot stops being recorded
Hold night flow in the influent wet well and release it in one large morning surge through the contact basin

questions.explanation: A feed system that cannot turn down below the night requirement will overshoot whenever flow collapses; adding trim capacity matched to low flow fixes control at both ends of the range. Recording less or surging flow hides or worsens the problem.

questions.question: A large plant's dewatering results stay poor even as the polymer dose is raised, and the chief suspects the polymer itself is wrong for the sludge. Which evaluation should guide the change?

answers.text: Run the current polymer at double dose for a full week and judge the cake, and keep doubling the dose each week until the cake finally firms up
Test candidate polymers of different charge and molecular weight with bench drainage tests, and select by how the sludge actually releases water
Switch to whichever polymer the neighboring plant uses, at the same dose
Judge polymers by the clarity of the mixing-tank solution alone

questions.explanation: Bench drainage testing of polymers with different charge and weight characteristics shows which product fits this sludge's surface chemistry, which dose alone cannot fix. Doubling a mismatched polymer wastes chemical, another plant's sludge differs from this one, and solution clarity says nothing about drainage performance.

questions.question: A state point plot for one of a large plant's clarifiers puts the operating point above the limiting flux curve during the afternoon peak, and the blanket is rising toward the weirs. What is the chief's best move?

answers.text: Increase the return sludge rate sharply, since a higher underflow always relieves an overloaded state point
Raise the mixed liquor concentration further, so the floc becomes heavier and settles through the overload
Wait for the overnight low flow to arrive, since an overloaded state point corrects itself without action
Bring the standby clarifier into service and trim the solids loading on the overloaded unit

questions.explanation: An operating point above the limiting flux means the clarifier cannot pass the applied solids downward, so solids accumulate and the blanket climbs; adding area and cutting the unit's solids loading restores a workable point. Raising return rate or mixed liquor concentration adds to the flux the unit already cannot pass.

questions.question: A vendor offers a large plant a continuing program of cultured organisms, promising to dose its way out of recurring nitrification losses that follow cold snaps and load swings. How should the chief evaluate the offer?

answers.text: Reject outside sludge under all circumstances, including emergency reseeding after a genuine kill
Buy a double quantity of the culture, so half can be stored in the equalization basin as a reserve for the next cold snap
Accept it at once, because dosed cultures permanently replace a plant's own nitrifying population
Judge it against the governing facts: dosed organisms persist only if the plant's conditions suit them

questions.explanation: Any introduced organism survives only where temperature, solids age, and food suit it, which are the same conditions governing the plant's own nitrifiers; the recurring losses trace to those conditions, not to a shortage of purchased culture. Emergency reseeding after a genuine kill is a different, legitimate case.

questions.question: A chief must decide whether a system's wet-weather surges come mainly from rainfall entering through defects or from direct storm connections. What analysis separates the two?

answers.text: Measuring chlorine demand on wet and dry days, since stormwater raises demand more than groundwater does, and repeating the comparison each season so the pattern can be tracked across wet and dry years of record
Comparing flow response timing and size against rainfall records: rapid, storm-tracking rises point to direct inflow, while slower, season-long elevation points to groundwater infiltration
Counting the manholes in each sub-basin, because more structures always means more rainfall entry
Reviewing pump run times alone, which show the total extra flow but not its entry pathway

questions.explanation: Rainfall-dependent entry tracks storms closely and recedes quickly, while groundwater infiltration follows the water table and lingers. Matching the flow record against rainfall timing is how the chief apportions the problem before choosing rehabilitation or disconnection work.

questions.question: During an upset a large plant treats 13.5 MGD at a chlorine dose of 3.3 mg/L using a hypochlorite product that is 72 percent of full strength. The effluent turbidity is 3.1 units, the contact basin holds 0.9 million gallons, and two of three basins are in service. How many pounds of product per day must be fed?

answers.text: 267.51 pounds per day
371.55 pounds per day
5,160.38 pounds per day
516.04 pounds per day

questions.explanation: Product feed = 13.5 x 3.3 x 8.34 / 0.72 = 516.04 pounds per day. Turbidity, basin volume, and basins in service do not enter it; 371.55 ignores the purity correction and 267.51 multiplies by the purity instead of dividing.

questions.question: A large plant's effluent BOD results run unexpectedly high for a well-nitrified effluent, while its carbonaceous results from an outside laboratory come back much lower. What distortion should the chief operator suspect in the plant's own test?

answers.text: The effluent's remaining solids are consuming oxygen on the filter paper, and filtering the sample a second time would have removed the problem entirely
Nitrogenous oxygen demand is being exerted in the bottle by nitrifying organisms, inflating the result unless a nitrification inhibitor is used
The dilution water is too pure for any oxygen demand to register
The incubator is holding the bottles slightly below the set temperature

questions.explanation: A nitrified effluent carries nitrifying organisms that exert nitrogenous demand in the BOD bottle, so an uninhibited test reports carbonaceous plus nitrogenous demand and reads high. Solids are removed from the measured portion by the test setup, pure dilution water is the intent, and a small temperature offset would lower, not raise, the result.

questions.question: A large new industrial customer proposes discharging to the utility's system. What should the chief operator do before the utility accepts the discharge?

answers.text: Accept the discharge as soon as the customer agrees to pay its sewer charges in full, without evaluating the volume or character of the waste against the plant's capacity or its permit
Refuse the discharge outright, together with every other new industrial discharge, on the ground that a treatment plant should serve homes and small businesses only
Accept the discharge to begin on the customer's proposed start date, and evaluate its effects on the plant afterward, once the discharge has been running for a trial period
Evaluate the proposed volume and character of the discharge against the plant's capacity and permit limits, and set the acceptance conditions the discharge will have to meet

questions.explanation: Acceptance of a major discharge is a utility-level decision made before the flow arrives: capacity, permit limits, and stated conditions first. Evaluating after the discharge begins puts the plant and its permit at risk.

questions.question: An anaerobic digester at a large plant shows a steadily rising volatile-acid-to-alkalinity ratio over two weeks while pH still reads normal and gas production has begun to slip. What should the chief operator do?

answers.text: Wait for the pH to confirm the trend, because the ratio cannot move before the pH does
Increase the raw sludge feed rate to give the acid-forming organisms more material to work on
Draw down the digester level quickly, because a high ratio means the vessel is simply too full
Cut or pause feeding and hold the digester on its buffered reserves, because a rising ratio is the early warning that acid production is outrunning methane formation

questions.explanation: Volatile acids accumulate before the buffer is exhausted and pH falls, so a rising acid-to-alkalinity ratio is the earliest reliable souring warning; easing feed lets methane formers catch up. Feeding harder or waiting for the pH drop lets the digester go fully sour.

questions.question: A lift station's delivered flow and discharge pressure have both fallen gradually over two years. The force main, discharge elevation, and valve positions are unchanged, suction supply is ample, and the motor draws normal current. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: Wear-ring clearances have opened, letting discharge water recirculate internally to suction instead of leaving the pump
The force main has silently grown longer, raising friction head until the pump can no longer reach its former duty point
The wastewater has become less dense, so the same impeller speed can no longer develop the pressure it once produced
The check valve has begun opening too fully, allowing discharge flow to escape back into the wet well during operation

questions.explanation: Gradual loss of both head and delivered flow on an unchanged system is the signature of internal wear: enlarged wear-ring clearances short-circuit flow from discharge back to suction inside the casing. A piping change would be needed to move the system curve, and none occurred here.

questions.question: Maintenance valving left a two-stage trickling filter plant running with its finishing filter first and its high-rate roughing filter second. Since the swap, the lead filter ponds under the raw load and the trailing filter's effluent has worsened. What should the chief operator order?

answers.text: Leave the order exactly as maintenance left it, since two filters in series treat the same in either sequence
Raise recirculation on the lead filter indefinitely until it learns to tolerate the raw load as a roughing unit and give it a full season to prove the conversion works
Convert the trailing filter into a clarifier so the lead filter's ponding solids are captured after they form
Restore the designed order with the roughing filter first to absorb the strong load and the finishing filter second to polish what remains

questions.explanation: Series stages are specialized: the roughing stage is built to absorb strong load and shed heavy film, and the finishing stage to polish weak flow, so reversing them overloads the polisher and starves the rougher of its role. Recirculation cannot turn a finishing bed into a roughing bed.

questions.question: A primary clarifier receives 1,840,000 gallons per day over a surface area of 2,150 square feet. The clarifier is 11 ft deep, its sludge blanket measures 0.8 ft, and its effluent suspended solids that day are 118 mg/L. What is the surface loading in gallons per day per square foot?

answers.text: 742.55 gpd/sq ft
855.81 gpd/sq ft
968.42 gpd/sq ft
1,070.00 gpd/sq ft

questions.explanation: Surface loading is flow divided by surface area: 1,840,000 divided by 2,150 gives 855.81 gallons per day per square foot. Tank depth, blanket depth, and effluent quality do not enter a surface loading rate.

intro-statistics.quiz_title: Introductory Statistics Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Daily high temperature measured in degrees Fahrenheit is an example of which level of measurement?

answers.text: Interval
Nominal
Ordinal
Ratio

questions.explanation: Fahrenheit has equal intervals but no true zero meaning 'no temperature,' so it is interval. Ratio data require a genuine zero point.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of the coefficient of variation over the standard deviation when comparing two data sets?

answers.text: It is always smaller than the standard deviation
It never changes when data are rescaled
It works even when the mean is exactly zero
It is unitless (SD divided by the mean), so it fairly compares variability for variables measured in different units or at very different scales

questions.explanation: Because CV expresses spread as a proportion of the mean, dollars can be compared with kilograms, or thousands with millions, on equal footing.

questions.question: Given P(A or B)=0.80, P(A)=0.50, and P(A and B)=0.10, what is P(B)?
questions.explanation: Rearrange the addition rule: P(B)=0.80-0.50+0.10=0.40.

questions.question: What does a 95% confidence level correctly mean?

answers.text: There is a 95% probability that the true parameter lies in the one interval already computed
95% of the sample data lie inside the computed interval
About 95% of intervals built by this method from repeated samples would capture the true parameter
The parameter falls in the interval in 95% of individual observations

questions.explanation: Confidence refers to the long-run success rate of the method over repeated samples. Once computed, an interval either contains the fixed parameter or it does not.

questions.question: What makes a point influential in a regression analysis?

answers.text: It has the largest response value in the data set
It lies exactly on the fitted line
Removing it would noticeably change the fitted line, such as its slope or intercept
Its residual is exactly zero

questions.explanation: An influential point exerts a strong effect on the regression result; removing it changes the conclusions in a meaningful way.

questions.question: A farmer wants to know whether a new fertilizer causes tomato plants to grow taller. Which design can best support a causal conclusion?

answers.text: Give the new fertilizer to the sunniest row and compare it with a shadier row
Randomly assign the new fertilizer to some plants and the standard fertilizer to others, then compare growth
Ask gardeners who already bought the new fertilizer whether their plants look taller
Measure plants in one garden this year and in a different garden last year

questions.explanation: Random assignment balances other influences (sun, soil, watering) across groups, so a growth difference can be attributed to the fertilizer. The other designs leave obvious confounders.

questions.question: Why can a well-designed randomized experiment support a cause-and-effect conclusion more strongly than an observational study?

answers.text: Experiments always use larger samples
Random assignment tends to balance other influences across groups, isolating the treatment effect
Observational studies never collect numeric data
Experiments do not need a comparison group

questions.explanation: Random assignment makes groups similar on other factors on average, so differences are more credibly due to the treatment. Observational studies cannot balance unmeasured factors this way.

questions.question: In a box plot, the length of the box (from its left edge to its right edge) represents which measure?

answers.text: The interquartile range (IQR)
The full range
The standard deviation
The mean

questions.explanation: The box runs from the first quartile Q1 to the third quartile Q3, so its length is Q3 - Q1, the IQR. It covers the middle 50% of the data.

questions.question: Weights are bell-shaped with mean 50 kg and standard deviation 5 kg. By the empirical rule, about what percent of weights are above 65 kg?

answers.text: About 2.5%
About 16%
About 0.15%
About 5%

questions.explanation: 65 kg is 3 standard deviations above the mean. About 99.7% lie within 3 standard deviations, leaving about 0.3% in both tails, or about 0.15% above 65 kg.

questions.question: A wait for an elevator is equally likely to be any time between 0 and 20 minutes. What is the probability the wait is less than 5 minutes?
questions.explanation: For a uniform distribution, probability is length over total length: 5 / 20 = 0.25.

questions.question: A population has mu = 30 and sigma = 6. For n = 36, the standard error is 1. What is P(29 < x-bar < 31)? Use the values for z = -1 and z = 1.
questions.explanation: The bounds give z = -1 and z = 1, so the probability is 0.8413 - 0.1587 = 0.6826.

questions.question: In a 2-row table, the first row total is 90. The expected counts computed for that row are 33 and 57. Which check confirms consistency?

answers.text: They multiply to the grand total.
Each equals the corresponding observed count.
Their average equals the chi-square statistic.
They sum to 90, matching the row total, as expected counts in a row must.

questions.explanation: Expected counts preserve the row and column totals, so a row's expected counts sum to its row total (33+57=90).

questions.question: A survey of landline owners is used to estimate opinions of all adults, but many younger adults have only cell phones and are missed. This is mainly an example of:

answers.text: Response bias from wording
A placebo effect
Random sampling error
Undercoverage, because part of the population is missing from the frame

questions.explanation: The landline frame leaves out cell-only adults, so part of the population had no chance of selection. That is undercoverage.

questions.question: A pictograph shows this year's corn production icon twice as tall AND twice as wide as last year's icon, to represent a doubling of production. How does the picture visually overstate the change?

answers.text: Area grows by a factor of 4 (2 x 2), so readers perceive roughly a quadrupling for what is only a doubling
The icon understates the change by a factor of 2
Doubling height alone would have quadrupled the area
Pictographs cannot mislead because they use pictures instead of numbers

questions.explanation: Scaling a picture in both dimensions multiplies its area by 2 x 2 = 4. The eye judges area, so a 2-fold increase in the data looks like about a 4-fold increase.

questions.question: Total time T = X + Y where X has mean 15 min (SD 2) and Y has mean 10 min (SD 2), independent. A manager budgets the mean plus claims SD(T)=4 min. Correct SD(T)?

answers.text: 4 min exactly
About 5.66 min
About 2.83 min
0 min

questions.explanation: Variance adds: 4+4=8, SD=sqrt(8), about 2.83. SDs themselves never simply add for independent variables.

questions.question: A one-sample t test of mean daily screen time, H0: mu = 4 hours versus Ha: mu != 4, returns t = -1.20 and P = 0.24. Which conclusion in context is correct at the 5% level?

answers.text: The data do not provide convincing evidence that mean daily screen time differs from 4 hours.
Mean screen time is proven to be exactly 4 hours per day.
There is convincing evidence mean screen time is below 4 hours, because t is negative.
There is a 24% chance the null hypothesis is true.

questions.explanation: With P = 0.24 > 0.05 we fail to reject H0. The negative sign alone does not create significance, and failing to reject is not proof of the null value.

questions.question: Software reports a 95% confidence interval of (-0.09, -0.02) for the difference in proportions preferring Brand X (younger buyers minus older buyers). What does this say?

answers.text: Plausible values put younger buyers' preference rate 2 to 9 percentage points below older buyers'.
Younger buyers prefer Brand X more, because both endpoints are small.
Between 2% and 9% of younger buyers prefer Brand X.
The interval is invalid because proportions cannot be negative.

questions.explanation: The interval is for a difference of proportions, which can be negative. Entirely negative values mean the first group's proportion is plausibly lower by 0.02 to 0.09.

questions.question: In a clinical trial, 400 patients are randomly assigned to receive either a new drug or the standard drug, and their change in systolic blood pressure after 8 weeks is recorded. Identify the experimental units and the response variable.

answers.text: Units: the two drugs; Response: the patients' ages
Units: the 8 weeks; Response: which drug was given
Units: the 400 patients; Response: change in systolic blood pressure
Units: the clinic staff; Response: number of patients enrolled

questions.explanation: Experimental units are who or what the treatments are applied to, here the patients. The response is the outcome measured on each unit, the change in blood pressure.

questions.question: For a strongly skewed distribution, which pair of summaries is generally most appropriate?

answers.text: Mean and standard deviation
Mean and range
Median and IQR
Mode and variance

questions.explanation: The median and IQR are resistant to extremes, so they describe center and spread better when data are skewed. The mean and standard deviation are pulled by the tail.

questions.question: Each of 5 independent trials has success probability 0.20. What is P(at least one success)?
questions.explanation: Use the complement: 1 minus the probability of zero successes. Zero successes has probability (0.80)^5=0.32768, so the answer is about 0.67.

anatomy-physiology.quiz_title: Anatomy & Physiology Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Water is called the body's universal solvent mainly because:

answers.text: It dissolves every substance equally, including all fats completely
It is the most abundant gas in blood
It prevents all solutes from moving
Many polar and ionic substances dissolve in it, allowing transport and chemical reactions

questions.explanation: Water's polarity lets it dissolve ions and polar molecules, though nonpolar fats dissolve poorly.

questions.question: The long central shaft of a long bone is called the:

answers.text: Diaphysis
Epiphysis
Metaphysis
Periosteum

questions.explanation: The diaphysis is the long, cylindrical shaft of a long bone between its two ends.

questions.question: The quadriceps femoris group as a whole is the prime mover for:

answers.text: Extending the knee
Flexing the knee
Plantarflexing the foot
Inverting the foot

questions.explanation: All quadriceps heads converge on the patellar tendon to extend the knee, so extending the knee is correct.

questions.question: A student shifts gaze from a distant board to a nearby book. Which change occurs?

answers.text: The lens becomes more convex to increase refractive power
The lens becomes flatter to decrease refractive power
The cornea becomes markedly more curved
The eyeball shortens along its anterior-posterior axis

questions.explanation: Near objects need more refraction, achieved by a rounder, more convex lens during accommodation.

questions.question: Ventricular ejection begins at the moment when:

answers.text: Atrial pressure exceeds ventricular pressure
The SA node fires
The T wave ends and diastole is complete
Ventricular pressure exceeds arterial pressure

questions.explanation: Semilunar valves open when ventricular pressure surpasses arterial pressure, starting ejection, so the correct answer is ventricular pressure exceeding arterial pressure.

questions.question: Using the rule of nines for an adult, one entire upper limb (arm) accounts for what percentage of total body surface area?
questions.explanation: Each entire arm is assigned 9% in the adult rule of nines.

questions.question: In an adult, the tapered inferior end of the spinal cord itself most typically terminates at which vertebral level?

answers.text: Between the L1 and L2 vertebrae
Between the T9 and T10 vertebrae
Between the L4 and L5 vertebrae
At the level of the sacral hiatus

questions.explanation: The cord ends as the conus medullaris near L1-L2 in adults, so the tapered inferior end of the spinal cord terminates between the L1 and L2 vertebrae.

questions.question: Which adrenal cortex zone is outermost and consists of small, tightly packed clusters of cells?

answers.text: Zona fasciculata
Zona reticularis
Zona glomerulosa
Adrenal medulla

questions.explanation: The zona glomerulosa is the thin outermost layer of the adrenal cortex, arranged in clusters.

questions.question: The biconcave disc shape of a mature red blood cell is advantageous mainly because it does what?

answers.text: Allows the cell to divide rapidly while circulating in the blood
Stores large amounts of DNA and protein in a central nucleus
Produces most of its ATP by aerobic respiration in mitochondria
Increases surface area relative to volume and shortens diffusion distance for gases

questions.explanation: The biconcave shape maximizes surface area for gas exchange and lets the cell flex through capillaries.

questions.question: Which layer of a blood vessel wall is in direct contact with the blood and consists of endothelium over a thin basement membrane?

answers.text: Tunica intima
Tunica media
Tunica externa
Tunica adventitia serosa

questions.explanation: The inner lining that touches the lumen is the tunica intima, so the keyed answer is the tunica intima.

questions.question: Protection produced after receiving a vaccine that stimulates memory cell formation is:

answers.text: Artificially acquired active immunity
Naturally acquired passive immunity
Artificially acquired passive immunity
Innate immunity from barriers

questions.explanation: A vaccine artificially stimulates the person's own immune system to make memory cells, so the correct answer is artificially acquired active immunity.

questions.question: Most amino acids absorbed from the small intestine ultimately enter which vessel system for transport to the liver?

answers.text: The thoracic duct directly
The lacteal lymphatic at the center of the villus, draining into the thoracic duct
The hepatic artery
The hepatic portal blood capillaries of the villus

questions.explanation: Amino acids enter villus blood capillaries and travel via the hepatic portal vein to the liver, so portal blood capillaries is correct.

questions.question: A patient cannot empty the bladder fully, has a rising blood urea level, and ultrasound shows a normal heart and lungs. Which system is the primary source of the problem?

answers.text: The urinary system
The respiratory system
The nervous system only
The digestive system

questions.explanation: Failure to empty the bladder with rising urea (a waste normally excreted in urine) points to the urinary system as the primary source.

questions.question: After an ankle injury, a clinician turns the sole of the foot outward, away from the other foot, to test the joint. What movement is this?

answers.text: Inversion
Dorsiflexion
Extension
Eversion

questions.explanation: Eversion turns the sole of the foot laterally, away from the midline.

questions.question: When a person moves from a bright room into darkness and also becomes alert to a threat, sympathetic action on the airways helps breathing how?

answers.text: By causing bronchoconstriction
By stopping respiratory muscle activity
By causing bronchodilation, widening the airways
By closing the glottis

questions.explanation: Beta-2 relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle increases airflow during fight-or-flight, so sympathetic action causes bronchodilation, widening the airways.

questions.question: In an upright resting person, both ventilation and perfusion are greatest at the bases of the lungs, but perfusion increases more toward the base mainly because of:

answers.text: Surfactant being absent at the apices under typical conditions
Bronchioles being closed at the bases in a healthy resting adult
Higher oxygen pressure at the apices under normal resting conditions
Gravity acting on pulmonary blood flow

questions.explanation: Gravity increases pulmonary blood flow toward the lung bases more than it increases ventilation, so that is the correct answer.

questions.question: Red blood cells are placed in an intravenous solution that has the same effective solute concentration as their cytoplasm. What is predicted for the cells?

answers.text: Swelling and bursting (hemolysis)
Shrinking and wrinkling (crenation)
No net change in cell volume
Rapid division to replace lost cells

questions.explanation: In an isotonic solution water moves in and out at equal rates, so red blood cells show no net change in volume.

questions.question: The pancreas contains both ducted clusters that secrete digestive enzymes into the intestine and ductless clusters that secrete insulin into the blood. How is the pancreas best described?

answers.text: A purely endocrine gland
A mixed gland with both exocrine and endocrine portions
A purely exocrine gland
A holocrine gland only

questions.explanation: The pancreas is a mixed gland: its acinar portion is exocrine and its islets are endocrine.

questions.question: Scenario: Repeated vomiting that loses gastric hydrochloric acid most likely produces which acid-base disorder, before compensation?

answers.text: Metabolic alkalosis
Metabolic acidosis
Respiratory acidosis
Respiratory alkalosis

questions.explanation: Loss of hydrochloric acid removes hydrogen ions and leaves bicarbonate behind, producing a primary metabolic alkalosis.

questions.question: A newborn has a continuous murmur and bounding pulses, and imaging shows a vessel still connecting the aorta and pulmonary trunk. The most likely diagnosis is:

answers.text: Patent ductus venosus
Persistent foramen ovale alone with no shunt
Patent umbilical vein
Patent ductus arteriosus

questions.explanation: Failure of the ductus arteriosus to close leaves an aorta-to-pulmonary connection producing a continuous murmur, so the correct answer is patent ductus arteriosus.

introductory-physics.quiz_title: Introductory Physics I-II Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Convert 6 kg to g.
questions.explanation: Multiply by the conversion factor: 6 x 1000 = 6000 g.

questions.question: Doubling an object's speed multiplies its kinetic energy by

answers.text: four
two, in direct proportion
eight, because energy is cubic
one half, because time halves

questions.explanation: KE depends on v squared, so doubling v gives 2^2 = 4 times the KE.

questions.question: A 9 kg object moves at 8 m/s. What is its momentum?

answers.text: 72 kg m/s
144 kg m/s
36 kg m/s
82 kg m/s

questions.explanation: p = m v = 9 x 8 = 72 kg m/s.

questions.question: The tension in a massless, frictionless-pulley rope is

answers.text: the same throughout the rope
larger on the side with the heavier mass always
zero wherever the rope changes direction
equal to the sum of both end forces

questions.explanation: For an ideal rope and pulley, tension is uniform along the rope.

questions.question: Two objects with the same momentum but different masses have

answers.text: exactly the same kinetic energy always
different kinetic energies, the lighter one having more
the same speed in every situation
kinetic energies with the heavier one larger

questions.explanation: KE = p^2/(2m): at fixed p, the smaller mass has the larger KE.

questions.question: A rotating body has moment of inertia 6 kg m^2 and angular velocity 4 rad/s. What is its angular momentum?

answers.text: 24 kg m^2/s
48 kg m^2/s
12 kg m^2/s
34 kg m^2/s

questions.explanation: L = I omega = 6 x 4 = 24 kg m^2/s.

questions.question: If the distance between two gravitating masses doubles, the force becomes

answers.text: one half as large, proportionally
twice as large as before
one quarter as large
unchanged, since mass is unchanged

questions.explanation: An inverse-square law gives 1/2^2 = 1/4 the force.

questions.question: An oscillator completes one cycle every 0.5 s. What is its frequency?

answers.text: 2 Hz
4 Hz
1 Hz
12 Hz

questions.question: A laboratory freezer is held at -40 degrees Celsius. What is this temperature in kelvin?
Coulomb's law has the same inverse-square form as gravity, but electric forces can be

answers.text: attractive only, exactly like gravity
felt only between neutral objects
either attractive or repulsive, unlike gravity's attraction only
stronger at larger distances

questions.explanation: Like charges repel and opposite charges attract; gravity only attracts.

questions.question: Two tones of 220 Hz and 198 Hz are played together. What beat frequency is heard?

answers.text: 44 Hz
11 Hz
22 Hz
32 Hz

questions.explanation: The beat frequency is the difference between the two frequencies: 220 - 198 = 22 Hz.

questions.question: An appliance rated at 90 W runs for 5 hours. How many watt-hours of energy does it use?

answers.text: 900 Wh
450 Wh
225 Wh
460 Wh

questions.explanation: Energy = P t = 90 x 5 = 450 Wh.

questions.question: A 4 kg object falls from rest through a height of 5 m with no air resistance. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, what is its speed at the bottom?

answers.text: 10 m/s
20 m/s
5 m/s
0 m/s

questions.explanation: m g h = (1/2) m v^2, so v = sqrt(2 g h) = sqrt(100) = 10 m/s; the mass cancels.

questions.question: A 50 kg passenger's elevator accelerates upward at 4 m/s^2 from rest for 2 s (g = 10 m/s^2). How far does it rise in that time?

answers.text: 8 m
4 m

questions.explanation: Distance = (1/2) a t^2 = 0.5 x 4 x 2^2 = 8 m; the passenger's mass affects the forces, not this distance.

questions.question: A diver is 15 m below the surface of a lake (water density 1000 kg/m^3, g = 10 m/s^2). What is the gauge pressure there, in kilopascals?

answers.text: 300 kPa
150 kPa
75 kPa
160 kPa

questions.explanation: Gauge pressure = rho g h = 1000 x 10 x 15 = 150000 Pa = 150 kPa.

questions.question: A diver is 40 m below the surface of a lake (water density 1000 kg/m^3, g = 10 m/s^2). What is the gauge pressure there, in kilopascals?

answers.text: 800 kPa
200 kPa
410 kPa
400 kPa

questions.explanation: Gauge pressure = rho g h = 1000 x 10 x 40 = 400000 Pa = 400 kPa.

questions.question: A heater warms 2.5 kg of material (specific heat 400 J/(kg K)) by 16 K in exactly 60 s. What average power was delivered to the material?
A force of 15 N acts along the hypotenuse of a 9-12-15 right triangle, with the horizontal leg 9. What is the horizontal component of the force?

answers.text: 9 N

questions.explanation: The horizontal component scales with the leg ratio: (9/15) x 15 = 9 N.

questions.question: A 50 kg passenger stands on a scale in an elevator accelerating upward at 2 m/s^2 (g = 10 m/s^2). What does the scale read (the normal force)?
questions.explanation: The floor must supply m g plus m a: 50 x (10 + 2) = 600 N.

questions.question: A gas starts at 120 kPa, 5 L, 200 K and changes to volume 10 L and temperature 400 K. Using P2 = P1 V1 T2 / (T1 V2), what is the new pressure?

answers.text: 240 kPa
120 kPa
60 kPa
130 kPa

financial-accounting.quiz_title: Financial Accounting Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which financial statement reports revenues and expenses for a period of time?

answers.text: The balance sheet
The retained earnings statement
The statement of cash flows
The income statement

questions.explanation: The income statement summarizes revenues and expenses over a period to yield net income or loss. The balance sheet is dated at a point in time, and the other two statements track equity changes and cash movements rather than performance.

questions.question: What does the basic accounting equation state?

answers.text: Liabilities equal assets plus stockholders' equity
Stockholders' equity equals revenues minus liabilities
Assets equal liabilities plus stockholders' equity
Assets equal revenues minus expenses

questions.explanation: Assets are the resources a business owns, and they are financed either by creditors or by owners, so assets must equal the two claims against them. The revenue-minus-expense formulas describe income computation, not the claim structure, and placing equity on the asset side reverses the relationship.

questions.question: A credit to the Service Revenue account has what effect?

answers.text: It decreases revenue and equity
It increases Cash directly
It increases revenue and therefore stockholders' equity
It increases liabilities

questions.explanation: Credits increase revenue accounts, and revenue increases equity. A credit never decreases revenue, the cash effect depends on the paired debit rather than the credit itself, and revenue is an equity element, not a liability.

questions.question: How is a net loss shown in the worksheet's statement columns?

answers.text: It is entered in the balance sheet credit column only
It is entered in the income statement credit column and the balance sheet debit column
It is omitted until the loss is confirmed by an auditor
It is entered as a negative revenue in the adjusted trial balance

questions.explanation: A net loss means income statement debits exceed credits, so the loss figure goes in the income statement credit column to balance that pair, and in the balance sheet debit column because a loss decreases equity. It is a normal worksheet result that is neither omitted nor recorded as negative revenue.

questions.question: What is the normal balance of an asset account?

answers.text: Debit
Credit
Zero at all times
Whichever side was used last

questions.explanation: Assets normally carry debit balances because debits increase them. A credit normal balance belongs to liabilities, equity, and revenues, and balances persist rather than resetting or switching with the last entry.

questions.question: Financial statements prepared for periods shorter than a full year, such as monthly or quarterly statements, are called what?

answers.text: Interim financial statements
Liquidating statements
Pro forma tax returns
Audited annual reports

questions.explanation: Interim statements cover periods of less than one year, such as a month or a quarter. Liquidation concerns ending a business, tax returns are filings rather than statements, and annual reports by definition cover a full year.

questions.question: Employees earn $5,000 for a five-day workweek, paid on Fridays. If the period ends on Wednesday, what salaries have accrued?
questions.explanation: Three of five days have been worked, so three-fifths of $5,000, which is $3,000, is accrued expense and payable. One day would be $1,000, two days $2,000, and the full week has not yet been earned by period end.

questions.question: A company has a $100,000 long-term note; $15,000 of principal is due within the next year and $85,000 after that. How is the note presented?

answers.text: The entire $100,000 is shown as long-term
The entire $100,000 is shown as current
Only the $85,000 is reported; the $15,000 is expensed
$15,000 is shown as a current liability and $85,000 as a long-term liability

questions.explanation: The portion of long-term debt maturing within the coming year is reclassified as current, while the remainder stays long-term, so the note is split $15,000 current and $85,000 long-term. Showing it all in either category misstates working capital, and principal due is a liability, not an expense.

questions.question: At year-end, goods purchased by a retailer are in transit and were shipped FOB shipping point. The retailer should:

answers.text: Exclude the goods until they physically arrive
Include the goods in its ending inventory because it owns them in transit
Ask the seller to include them instead
Record them as goods held on consignment

questions.explanation: FOB shipping point transferred title when the carrier received the goods, so the buyer owns them during transit and includes them in ending inventory even though they are not yet on the premises. Excluding owned goods would understate inventory, and they are purchased goods, not consignments.

questions.question: Gross profit is $44,000 and total operating expenses are $18,000, with no other revenues or expenses. What is income from operations?
questions.explanation: Income from operations equals gross profit minus operating expenses: $44,000 minus $18,000 equals $26,000. Adding the figures gives $62,000, and restating gross profit or operating expenses alone skips the step that produces operating income.

questions.question: On January 1 a company paid $36,000 for a three-year insurance policy. At that date, the prepayment is classified as:

answers.text: Entirely current, because insurance is an operating cost
Entirely noncurrent, because the policy runs three years
$12,000 as a current asset and $24,000 as a noncurrent asset, matching the portions that expire within and beyond the next year
An expense, so no asset is reported at all

questions.explanation: A multi-year prepayment is divided by the benefit period: one year of coverage, $12,000, will be consumed within the coming year and is current, while the remaining $24,000 benefits later years and is noncurrent. It is an asset at payment, not an immediate expense.

questions.question: Interest of $900 accrued on a note payable was recorded by debiting Interest Expense and crediting Interest Receivable. What is the effect of this single error?

answers.text: Liabilities are overstated by $900
Interest expense is overstated by $900
Cash is understated by $900
Interest expense is correct, but assets and liabilities are each understated by $900 because the credit landed in a receivable instead of the payable

questions.explanation: The debit side is right, so the expense stands. But crediting a receivable shrinks assets by $900 while the true obligation is never recorded, shrinking liabilities by $900 as well — the balance sheet contracts on both sides while income looks fine.

questions.question: Inventory layers are: beginning 100 units at $10, a purchase of 100 units at $12, and a purchase of 100 units at $14. If 220 units are sold, what is ending inventory under FIFO?
questions.explanation: Under FIFO the ending 80 units are the most recently purchased: 80 units at $14 equals $1,120. Pricing the remaining units at the oldest $10 cost gives the $800 LIFO-style figure, using the middle $12 layer gives $960, and valuing all 80 units as if a further full layer existed at $14 for 100 units gives $1,400.

questions.question: In a periodic system, recorded purchases for the year are understated by $4,000 because an invoice for goods counted in ending inventory was never recorded, and ending inventory itself is correctly counted. What is the effect?

answers.text: Cost of goods sold is overstated by $4,000
Cost of goods sold is understated by $4,000 and net income is overstated by $4,000
Net income is understated by $4,000
Ending inventory must also be understated by $4,000
