Only outdoors at noon to establish the building's baseline

questions.explanation: Light matters where eyes and tasks meet, so measurements belong at work-plane height across a representative grid. Recording whether daylight contributed keeps the reading interpretable when savings and adequacy are judged later.

questions.question: A compressor averages 90 kW loaded for 70% of its run time and 28 kW unloaded for the remaining 30%. What is its average power draw?

answers.text: 59 kW, from simply averaging 90 kW and 28 kW.
90 kW, because unloaded hours can be ignored in an average.
71.4 kW, from 0.70 times 90 kW plus 0.30 times 28 kW.
118 kW, because loaded and unloaded draws are added together.

questions.explanation: Average power is the time-weighted sum: 0.70 times 90 equals 63 kW, and 0.30 times 28 equals 8.4 kW, totaling 71.4 kW. The auditor uses logged loaded and unloaded fractions rather than a simple midpoint, which would understate the draw.

questions.question: Before a site visit to a large office, which trend-log request is most useful for the auditor?

answers.text: A single screenshot of current conditions at noon
One day of data at one-hour intervals for the visit day only
Two to four weeks of data at 5- to 15-minute intervals for key points such as zone temperatures, valve and damper positions, fan status, and setpoints, covering occupied and unoccupied periods
A printed list of controller serial numbers

questions.explanation: Useful audit trends span representative weeks, capture nights and weekends, and are frequent enough to reveal cycling, overrides, and simultaneous heating and cooling. A single snapshot cannot show any of those.

questions.question: A client with a limited budget asks whether to audit one large headquarters or five small clinics at Level 1. The auditor's guidance should weigh:

answers.text: Where total energy spend and likely opportunity are greatest relative to the decisions each audit will inform
Auditing the buildings closest to the auditor's office first
The age of the buildings' paint and finishes
Which buildings have the newest meters

questions.explanation: Prioritization follows energy spend, opportunity, and decision value — the purpose of portfolio screening.

questions.question: A model predicts a distribution warehouse uses 18% more electricity than its bills show, fairly evenly across months. What is the auditor's best first response?

answers.text: Accept the model and report the higher figure
Check modelled schedules, plug loads and operating hours against what was observed on site
Reduce every model output by exactly 18% and move on
Replace the bills with the model in the savings calculation

questions.explanation: A persistent, even bias usually points to an input such as hours or internal loads that observation can correct.

questions.question: A client will fund only one of two independent measures this year. Both have positive NPV. What additional figure best supports your sequencing recommendation?

answers.text: The vendor's preferred installation order
The alphabetical order used in the audit table
The cost of delay: savings forgone for each year the unfunded measure waits
The age of the older equipment, regardless of savings

questions.explanation: For independent measures the choice is timing, not exclusion. Quantifying forgone savings per year of delay shows the client what waiting costs.

questions.question: You find a steam heating system with failed steam traps in a hospital wing that is overheating. Failed traps passing live steam cause what audit finding?

answers.text: Reduced fuel use
Improved condensate return
Wasted steam energy, distribution losses, and loss of temperature control
Lower boiler load

questions.explanation: Traps passing live steam waste boiler fuel, overload condensate systems, and make zone temperatures hard to control.

questions.question: A dormitory considers lowering its water heater setpoint from 140 F (with mixing valves) to 120 F storage with the mixing valves removed to save energy. How do you advise?

answers.text: Approve it as a pure energy saving with no other effects
Advise against storing at 120 F without a legionella control plan, and quantify that the standby saving is small compared with the health risk management involved
Recommend storing at 100 F instead for even more savings
State that setpoint has no effect on standby loss

questions.explanation: Standby loss does fall with lower storage temperature, but storing tepid water without a pathogen control strategy trades a modest saving for a serious health risk. The auditor quantifies the small saving and recommends keeping controlled hot storage with tempered delivery.

questions.question: During a hotel audit you find PTAC sleeves poorly sealed to the wall, with outdoor air whistling in around 120 units. What do you document and recommend?

answers.text: Replace all PTAC units with new models
Ignore sleeve leakage because units heat and cool the room anyway
Seal and insulate around each sleeve during a room-by-room pass and include the infiltration saving in the envelope section
Add a vestibule to the main entrance as the only fix

questions.explanation: Sleeve gaps are distributed infiltration paths that bypass the envelope in every room. A systematic sealing pass is low-cost per unit and the combined saving across 120 units is material to the envelope total.

questions.question: You find a constant-volume reheat system serving a lab building where codes require constant airflow. Your recommendation should respect what constraint?

answers.text: Ventilation and exhaust requirements may prohibit airflow reduction, so savings must come from reset and reheat limits
Airflow can be cut freely
Reheat should be increased
Economizers are prohibited

questions.explanation: In lab and exhaust-driven spaces required airflow limits VAV conversion, so auditors focus on temperature reset and reheat control.

questions.question: An auditor benchmarking a newly acquired office has only eight months of bills, spanning winter through summer but missing the autumn shoulder season. What is the defensible treatment of a benchmark built from this record?

answers.text: Present it as provisional, disclose the incomplete year, and avoid simple annualization without accounting for the missing season's loads.
Multiply the eight-month total by 1.5 and report the result as a verified annual EUI.
Fill the missing months with the peer median EUI for the building type.
Report the eight-month total as if it were a full year to keep the schedule.

questions.explanation: A partial year misses seasonal loads and cannot be stretched by a flat factor without distortion. The auditor labels the result provisional and completes a full twelve months before relying on the comparison.

questions.question: A warehouse bundle costs $133,000 after incentives and saves $28,000 per year in energy plus $5,000 per year in avoided lamp and ballast maintenance. What payback using total annual benefit do you report?

answers.text: About 4.8 years, using energy savings only
About 4.0 years, using $33,000 in total annual benefit
About 2.7 years, dividing cost by the maintenance saving alone
About 5.3 years, adding maintenance cost to the numerator

questions.explanation: Total annual benefit = $28,000 + $5,000 = $33,000. Payback = $133,000 / $33,000 = 4.03 years, about 4.0 years. Avoided maintenance is a benefit that belongs in the denominator with energy savings, using the net-of-incentive cost.

questions.question: An envelope upgrade cuts a building's design cooling load from 150 tons to 120 tons just as its chiller is due for replacement. How should the auditor capture the full benefit?

answers.text: Size the replacement chiller to the reduced load and credit both the energy saving and the avoided capital cost of the larger machine
Order the original 150-ton chiller so capacity is available if loads rebound
Ignore the load reduction because chiller size does not affect project cost
Credit only the envelope energy saving and omit any equipment effect from the report

questions.explanation: Sequencing envelope work before equipment replacement lets the smaller plant be bought, a real capital saving auditors call an interactive effect. Oversized replacements also suffer worse part-load performance.

questions.question: A standard-efficiency motor uses 62 kW input for a given load; a premium unit would use 58 kW for the same load over 7,000 hours at $0.09 per kWh. What annual saving supports the replacement case?

answers.text: $1,260 per year
$3,600 per year
$2,520 per year
$252 per year

questions.explanation: Power saved is 62 - 58 = 4 kW, giving 4 x 7,000 = 28,000 kWh per year. At $0.09 per kWh the annual saving is 28,000 x $0.09 = $2,520.

questions.question: During a solar PV screening at a warehouse, the auditor finds a large flat roof that is 18 years old and due for replacement in two years. What is the correct audit recommendation?

answers.text: Note that reroofing should precede or accompany the PV installation, and include the timing and cost implication in the report rather than assuming the roof is ready
Ignore roof age because panels protect the roof indefinitely
Recommend installing PV immediately with no mention of the roof
Reject solar permanently for this building

questions.explanation: Installing a 25-year array on a roof with two years of life left creates removal and reinstallation cost; the auditor must flag sequencing and its economics honestly.

questions.question: Last year a plant's peak was 1,000 kW under a tariff with an 85% ratchet. This year a measure holds every month's peak at or below 700 kW. Once the old peak leaves the ratchet window, what billed-demand floor will the ratchet impose from the new peak?

answers.text: 850 kW
595 kW
700 kW

questions.explanation: New ratchet floor = 0.85 x 700 kW = 595 kW, below the 700 kW actual peaks, so actual peaks will govern billing. Sustained peak control eventually lowers the ratchet floor itself.

questions.question: A parking garage retrofit uses bi-level fixtures that run at 30 percent power when unoccupied, which loggers show is 65 percent of the 8,760 hours. Full power is 1,800 watts for the zone. What annual energy use should the auditor estimate for the zone after retrofit?

answers.text: About 15,800 kilowatt-hours per year, from 1.8 kW x 8,760 at full power throughout
About 4,700 kilowatt-hours per year, from 1.8 kW x 0.30 x 8,760 as if always unoccupied
About 8,600 kilowatt-hours per year, from 1.8 kW x (0.35 x 8,760 + 0.30 x 0.65 x 8,760)
About 2,600 kilowatt-hours per year, from 1.8 kW x 0.35 x 0.65 x 8,760

questions.explanation: Occupied hours: 0.35 x 8,760 = 3,066 h at 1.8 kW = 5,519 kWh; unoccupied: 0.65 x 8,760 = 5,694 h at 0.54 kW = 3,075 kWh; total about 8,594 kWh, or about 8,600 kWh per year. The auditor weights each power level by its share of hours rather than averaging the percentages.

questions.question: A warehouse office has measured infiltration of 250 cfm and a winter design temperature difference of 30 F. What sensible infiltration load do you calculate?

answers.text: 8,100 Btu/h
2,700 Btu/h
810 Btu/h

questions.explanation: Sensible load = 1.08 x cfm x delta-T = 1.08 x 250 x 30 = 8,100 Btu/h. This load is separate from, and additional to, conduction through the envelope surfaces.

certified-fraud-examiner.quiz_title: ACFE Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a trial balance in detecting accounting fraud?

answers.text: To prove that no fraud has occurred
To replace the need for source documents
To value inventory for tax purposes
To check that total debits equal total credits and surface out-of-balance manipulations

questions.explanation: A trial balance verifies the mechanical equality of debits and credits; imbalances can reveal posting manipulations, though balanced entries can still be fraudulent.

questions.question: Tokenization reduces card fraud risk in stored payments because:

answers.text: It stores the full card number in more places
It replaces the card number with a substitute value that is useless to thieves if the merchant's stored data is breached
It eliminates the need for authorizations
It guarantees every transaction is legitimate

questions.explanation: Tokens have no value outside their intended context, so a breach of stored tokens does not yield usable card numbers. Authorization and fraud checks still apply to each transaction.

questions.question: An examiner needs to annotate relationships between documents while analyzing them. Where should those annotations go?

answers.text: On sticky notes attached to the originals
In pencil on the backs of originals
In the evidence log's description field
On working copies or in a separate analysis file, never on the original evidence

questions.explanation: Analysis belongs on copies and in workpapers so the originals remain exactly as collected and available for independent examination.

questions.question: What are compensatory damages in a civil fraud case intended to do?

answers.text: Punish the defendant in proportion to their wealth regardless of loss
Pay the plaintiff a fixed statutory bonus for filing suit
Reimburse the court for the cost of the trial
Make the injured party whole for actual losses caused by the fraud, such as funds taken, costs incurred, and proven consequential losses

questions.explanation: Compensation ties recovery to proven, caused loss. Punishment is the separate function of punitive damages, which have their own requirements.

questions.question: Communicating the program to employees should emphasize:

answers.text: Technical descriptions of audit sampling methods
Threats of prosecution as the sole message
What the standards are, that monitoring and proactive audits occur, how to report, and that reports are protected and acted upon
Communication only when a fraud case becomes public

questions.explanation: Communication drives both deterrence and reporting: employees must know the rules, believe detection is real, and trust the reporting route. Fear-only messaging suppresses tips.

questions.question: Reviewing the payroll master file change log for after-hours changes by the payroll processor is a detection step for:

answers.text: Unauthorized rate, deduction, or employee-record changes that enable payroll schemes
Vendor invoice duplication
Customer payment lapping
Inventory shrinkage

questions.explanation: Payroll schemes often require standing-data changes; logs showing who changed what and when expose unauthorized modifications.

questions.question: A casino patron buys chips with a large amount of illicit cash, gambles minimally, and redeems the chips for a check. The stage of laundering this best illustrates is:

answers.text: Integration only, because a check was issued
Structuring of bank deposits
Layering through international trade
Placement, because illicit cash is being introduced into a financial channel in a form that looks like legitimate winnings

questions.explanation: Placement is getting criminal proceeds into the legitimate system. Converting cash to chips and then to a check disguises the cash's origin as gambling proceeds.

questions.question: A subject is suspected of stealing to cover a family medical crisis. Which statement best reflects theme development?

answers.text: 'We will prosecute unless you confess in five minutes.'
'Sometimes good people under enormous pressure at home make a decision they would never normally make; help me understand what was happening then.'
'Your coworkers all say you are a thief.'
'Only a criminal would do what you did.'

questions.explanation: The statement offers a sympathetic rationalization tied to the subject's circumstances, lowering the barrier to admission; the alternatives shame or threaten.

questions.question: A witness asks to have their union representative or attorney present. How should the examiner handle the request?

answers.text: Cancel the entire investigation
Follow applicable law, policy, and counsel guidance, and document how the request was addressed
Interview the representative instead about all topics
Refuse and lock the interview room door

questions.explanation: Representation rights vary by setting and jurisdiction; handling the request lawfully and on the record protects the interview's product.

questions.question: A suspended employee asks whether suspension means the company has decided they stole funds. How should the suspension be framed and handled to reduce legal risk?

answers.text: As a neutral, documented interim measure to protect people, assets, and evidence while facts are gathered, without prejudging the outcome
As punishment that will be announced to customers
As a finding that will be reversed only if they confess
As an unpaid penalty with no written record

questions.explanation: Framing suspension as a neutral protective step, consistently applied and documented, avoids converting an interim measure into a prejudgment that supports defamation or wrongful-discipline claims.

questions.question: An examiner is invited to lead an advanced course on a fraud topic they last studied many years ago and have not practiced since, with no time to prepare updates. Accepting as-is would most directly violate which duty?

answers.text: Professional competence, because presenting as current an expertise the examiner has allowed to lapse, without preparation or disclosure, misleads those relying on it
The duty to accept all teaching invitations
There is no duty implicated by teaching
Confidentiality, because course material is sensitive

questions.explanation: Competence is a continuing duty, not a one-time achievement. Examiners must maintain their knowledge or be candid about its limits before others rely on it.

questions.question: A board asks how its organization's fraud program compares with recognized practice and whether its structure has blind spots. Which step best answers that question?

answers.text: Asking program staff to rate their own maturity without criteria
Benchmarking the program against a recognized framework and peer practice, supplemented by independent evaluation of components
Counting how many peer organizations reported fraud last year
Reviewing only the program's budget against peers' budgets

questions.explanation: Framework-based benchmarking plus independent evaluation reveals structural gaps that internal familiarity hides. Budget or incident comparisons alone do not assess program quality.

questions.question: An employee demands a fee from job applicants, claiming it is required to forward their applications to hiring managers. Applicants who refuse are not forwarded. This demand is best described as:

answers.text: A kickback paid willingly by applicants
An illegal gratuity
Bid rigging in hiring
Economic extortion, because access is withheld unless the demanded payment is made

questions.explanation: Using gatekeeping power to extract payment under threat of exclusion is extortion; the applicants pay to avoid harm, not to gain improper influence.

questions.question: A losing bidder protests that the winner was allowed to revise a material price error after bid opening while others were held to their bids. Unequal post-opening corrections raise concern about:

answers.text: Bid responsiveness rules only for the loser
Clarifications of minor informalities
Favoritism in bid evaluation that undermines equal treatment of competitors
A sealed bidding method that requires discussion

questions.explanation: Material changes after opening, granted selectively, can convert a losing favored bid into the winner.

questions.question: A defendant offers to plead guilty and cooperate against a scheme organizer in exchange for sentencing consideration. Who decides whether to accept that bargain?

answers.text: The prosecutor, subject to court approval of the plea, with the examiner able to supply factual input but not to promise or approve terms
The fraud examiner who investigated the scheme
The victim company's chief executive alone
The defendant's employer through human resources

questions.explanation: Plea authority rests with the prosecution and the court. Examiner promises about plea terms would be unauthorized and could damage the case.

questions.question: A proposed team member is the subject's former business partner and still holds a financial interest with them. What should happen during team assembly?

answers.text: The conflict should be disclosed and the person removed or recused from affected work
The interest is irrelevant if the person is experienced
The person should lead interviews of the subject for insight
The interest should be hidden to avoid delaying the plan

questions.explanation: Conflicts of interest threaten objectivity and credibility, so they must be surfaced during planning and managed by recusal or replacement.

questions.question: Assessment results are ready for the executive team. Which presentation is most likely to produce sound decisions?

answers.text: A single overall fraud score with no supporting detail
A list of every scenario ever brainstormed, with no ratings or priorities
The prioritized residual risks, how they compare with tolerance, the key control gaps behind them, the proposed responses and owners, and the areas not covered
A narrative naming the employees the team considers most suspicious

questions.explanation: Decision-ready communication is prioritized, tolerance-based, and action-oriented, and it discloses coverage limits. Scores without context and suspicion lists without evidence both mislead.

questions.question: A finance employee notices a wire instruction email thread where the supplier tone, signature, and domain all changed subtly after the first genuine message. This is a sign the attacker may have:

answers.text: Been added as an approved vendor
Updated their branding legitimately
Inserted themselves into an ongoing thread to redirect the payment at the final step
Requested a routine address change

questions.explanation: Thread hijacking places the fraudulent instruction inside a trusted conversation, with small changes as the tell.

questions.question: A witness testifies in court that a coworker told them last year that the manager approved the false invoices, offered to prove the manager approved them. Why is hearsay the central issue?

answers.text: The coworker was not under oath at trial only
The statement is a document, not testimony
The manager was not present in the hallway
It is an out-of-court statement offered to prove the truth of what it asserts, which is the definition of hearsay

questions.explanation: Hearsay is an out-of-court statement offered for its truth; unless an exemption or exception applies, it is generally excluded.

questions.question: A purchasing manager accepts secret payments from a vendor in exchange for steering contracts to that vendor at inflated prices. Which category best fits the manager's conduct toward their own employer?

answers.text: A lawful sales commission
Commercial bribery — a secret payment to influence business conduct in breach of a duty of loyalty
A facilitating payment
Mere poor negotiation

questions.explanation: Secret payments to an agent to influence business decisions for the payer's benefit, without the principal's consent, constitute commercial bribery.

certified-treasury-professional.quiz_title: AFP Certified Treasury Professional (CTP) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the purpose of a cash concentration system?

answers.text: To hide balances from treasury
To move funds from depository and subsidiary accounts into a central concentration account where the net position can be invested, used to pay down debt, or fund disbursements
To increase the number of bank fees paid
To keep each unit's cash permanently separate

questions.explanation: Concentration gathers scattered balances into one pool under central control. Pooling is what allows netting, efficient investing, and precise funding of disbursements.

questions.question: Why should a hedge's maturity be matched to the underlying exposure's value date?

answers.text: Matching maturities makes the hedge qualify as a natural hedge
It guarantees the forward rate will be better than spot
It removes the need for settlement liquidity
A mismatch leaves the firm unhedged for the gap or forces an early close-out at market rates

questions.explanation: If the hedge settles before or after the cash flow, the firm faces a period of renewed exposure or must roll or close the hedge, adding cost and risk.

questions.question: What information does an implied forward rate derived from the yield curve give a borrower?

answers.text: A guaranteed rate the borrower can demand from its bank next year
The market-implied rate for a future period, useful as the break-even against which a decision to fix now or wait can be judged
The rate the central bank has already decided to set next year
Proof that fixing today will always be the cheaper choice

questions.explanation: Forward rates are the curve's break-even expectations. If a borrower fixes at a rate below the implied forward, the market is pricing in higher future rates; the forward frames the decision but guarantees nothing about what will actually happen.

questions.question: Before remitting unclaimed property to a state, what step is a holder generally expected to take?

answers.text: Publish the owner's banking details on the company website
Make reasonable due diligence efforts, such as mailing a notice to the owner's last known address, to reunite the owner with the property
Transfer the property to the employee who discovered it
Wait for the owner to contact the company on their own

questions.explanation: Due diligence gives owners a final chance to claim their property before escheatment. The outreach and its results are documented as part of the holder's compliance file.

questions.question: Forecast granularity should match the decision being made. The most sensible pairing is:

answers.text: Daily granularity for a five-year strategic forecast
Annual totals for next week's borrowing decision
Daily granularity for the next few weeks of funding decisions, weekly or monthly for longer planning horizons
Hourly forecasts for the annual budget

questions.explanation: Precision and effort should follow decision needs; distant daily detail is false precision, while near-term totals hide funding peaks.

questions.question: If a firm's collection float is $400,000 and its disbursement float is $250,000, what is its net float and what does it mean?

answers.text: Net float is $650,000 in the firm's favor
Net float is zero
Net float is $150,000 against the firm, because more cash is in transit inbound than outbound
Net float is $150,000 in the firm's favor from disbursements alone with collections ignored

questions.explanation: Net float = disbursement float minus collection float = $250,000 - $400,000 = -$150,000. The negative $150,000 means $150,000 more is tied up in collections than is offset by disbursements.

questions.question: A steady climb in days inventory outstanding (DIO), outpacing sales growth, should prompt treasury to flag:

answers.text: Excess cash available for investment
Faster supplier payments
Cash increasingly absorbed by inventory, with added obsolescence and markdown risk
Improving receivable quality

questions.explanation: Inventory growth beyond sales needs consumes liquidity and raises the risk that stock will not convert at full value.

questions.question: Why do most commercial paper issuers maintain a backup bank line of credit even though it costs a commitment fee?

answers.text: To earn interest on the line
To assure investors and rating agencies that maturing paper can be repaid if the market freezes and new paper cannot be rolled
To satisfy the bond indenture
To replace the need for any cash balances forever

questions.explanation: Rollover risk is commercial paper's central danger. A committed backup line converts a market-access risk into a known fee, which is why agencies expect it.

questions.question: An e-commerce unit processes refunds. Treasury advises refunding to the original payment method primarily because it does which of the following?

answers.text: Allows the unit to delay refunds indefinitely
Reduces fraud and disputes, since refunds to a different destination are a common route for diverting money
Eliminates the transaction fee charged on the original sale
Increases the unit's days sales outstanding

questions.explanation: Original-method refunds keep money returning to the verified payer, which curtails refund fraud and simplifies reconciliation and chargeback defense.

questions.question: In continuity planning, what is the main reason treasury processes are ranked by criticality instead of being treated as equally important?

answers.text: Ranking determines which employees receive promotions
Banks charge lower fees for processes ranked as critical
Lower-ranked processes are permanently discontinued after a disaster
Restoration resources are limited during an event, so the processes whose failure causes the greatest harm must be recovered first

questions.explanation: Prioritization focuses scarce recovery resources where consequences are most severe, such as payments that prevent default or keep employees paid. The business impact analysis supplies the evidence for the ranking.

questions.question: A 'defense in depth' approach to treasury system security means:

answers.text: Layering preventive, detective, and corrective controls so no single failure exposes funds or data
Buying the most expensive security product available
Relying on one very strong password as the only control
Placing all security responsibility on the bank

questions.explanation: Multiple independent layers, such as access control, encryption, monitoring, and recovery, reduce the chance that one gap leads to loss.

questions.question: A treasurer uses an interest rate swap alongside a new fixed-rate bond issue. The most common treasury reason is to:

answers.text: Avoid repaying principal
Increase flotation costs deliberately
Convert the effective interest exposure to floating (or the reverse) to fit the firm's asset and risk profile without changing the bond itself
Eliminate the indenture

questions.explanation: Swaps reshape interest exposure synthetically while the underlying bond terms stay intact. They manage rate risk; they do not remove the debt.

questions.question: A firm pays for many small bank services with fees instead of balances. In a rising-rate environment, why might it reconsider using balances?

answers.text: Banks stop accepting fees
Balances earn nothing when rates rise
Rising rates increase the value of earnings credit generated by balances, so compensating the bank with balances can become cheaper than paying hard-dollar fees
Fees become illegal when rates rise

questions.explanation: The fees-versus-balances choice is an interest rate comparison. When earnings credit rates climb, idle-looking balances do more work, shifting the cheaper compensation method.

questions.question: If the pool header account ends the day overdrawn because total participant withdrawals exceeded deposits, the overdraft cost should be:

answers.text: Borne under the pooling agreement's allocation rules by the participants whose net borrowing created it
Ignored because the pool is internal
Charged equally to every employee
Converted into a dividend

questions.explanation: Pooling agreements allocate interest and overdraft costs to net borrowers and credit net lenders, keeping subsidiary results fair and auditable.

questions.question: A borrower prepays $10,000,000 of a term loan with lenders holding 50/30/20 shares. Under pro rata application, the 30% lender receives:
questions.explanation: Prepayments, like fundings, are shared by exposure: 30% x $10,000,000 = $3,000,000. No lender is singled out unless the agreement permits selective purchases.

questions.question: A treasury policy requires investments to be limited to approved instruments. A portfolio report shows a holding outside that list. The first compliance step is to:

answers.text: Ignore it if the holding is performing well
Reclassify the holding in the report so it appears compliant
Escalate the breach, assess exposure, and dispose of or formally exception the holding under policy procedures
Wait until maturity without notifying anyone

questions.explanation: Policy breaches require escalation and a documented response; performance does not excuse non-compliance, and relabeling conceals the breach.

questions.question: A treasurer uses a value-dating practice question: a receipt is expected 'this week.' Why is that insufficient for positioning?

answers.text: Banks report only monthly
Positioning needs the specific value date the funds become collected, because a Monday versus Friday receipt changes borrowing and investing on each intervening day
Receipts only occur on Fridays
Weekly totals are prohibited

questions.explanation: Liquidity decisions are dated, not weekly. Vague timing hides the daily gaps and surpluses that positioning exists to manage.

questions.question: An account's ledger and collected balances differ persistently by roughly two days of deposit volume. This gap most likely represents:

answers.text: Deposit float - checks deposited but not yet collected and available
A bank error repeated daily
Unrecorded service charges
An unauthorized withdrawal

questions.explanation: Collected balances lag ledger balances by the clearing time of deposited items; understanding that float prevents over-investing unavailable funds.

questions.question: A logistics firm knows it must pay $900,000 of equipment deposits in stages. It invests $300,000 to mature in one year, $300,000 in two years and $300,000 in three years. What technique is this and what cash does each maturity release?

answers.text: Laddering; each maturity releases $300,000 of principal in its year
Barbelling; each maturity releases $450,000 because only two dates are used
Bulleting; all $900,000 is released at the three-year date
Duration matching; each maturity releases $900,000 every year

questions.explanation: Equal amounts placed at successive maturities form a ladder. Here $900,000 / 3 rungs = $300,000 per rung, so $300,000 of principal returns in year one, year two and year three respectively.

questions.question: Scenario: Treasury negotiates lower bank fees after showing a bank its consolidated wallet of business. Which technology output made this negotiation possible?

answers.text: A list of complaints collected from subsidiaries
The bank's published annual report alone
Consolidated reporting of balances, volumes, and services used across accounts and entities
A forecast of next year's sales growth

questions.explanation: Wallet analysis depends on complete, consolidated data about the relationship, which treasury systems assemble from statements and fee data.

arizona-independent-adjuster.quiz_title: Arizona Independent Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which situation best shows insurable interest by a business partner?

answers.text: A former partner who sold out five years ago insures the store for himself
One partner insures the partnership's Phoenix store because its destruction would cut her income and capital
A customer insures the store hoping for a payout if it closes
A competitor insures the store to fund expansion if it burns

questions.explanation: A current partner has a direct financial stake in the store's continued existence. A former partner who sold out no longer stands to lose, which is the key distinction.

questions.question: A loss payee endorsement on equipment in Mesa primarily protects whom, and how?

answers.text: The equipment vendor, by guaranteeing its sales price on every return
The insured's customers, by paying them for late deliveries
The lender or lessor, by directing loss payment for that equipment to it as its interest appears
The producer, by guaranteeing commission after a loss

questions.explanation: Loss payee status is about the property claim check, not liability status. It ensures a party with a financial interest in damaged equipment is paid to the extent of that interest.

questions.question: Which statement about HO-3 exclusions is correct?

answers.text: Open-perils means no exclusion can ever apply
Open-perils covers intentional damage by the insured
Open-perils eliminates the need to read the policy
Open-perils dwelling coverage is still subject to exclusions such as earth movement, flood and neglect

questions.explanation: Open perils means the cause need not be named, not that exclusions disappear. Intentional damage by the insured and the listed catastrophic exclusions remain outside coverage.

questions.question: What are supplementary payments under Part A?

answers.text: A second liability limit hidden in Part D
Payments the insured must make to the insurer after trial
The claimant's attorney fees in every case
Amounts the insurer pays in addition to the limit, such as bail bond and post-judgment interest items the form lists

questions.explanation: The form lists specific extra amounts payable on top of the limit of liability, which is why an adjuster does not deduct those listed items from the limit itself.

questions.question: Why are objective findings weighted heavily alongside subjective pain complaints?

answers.text: Subjective complaints must be ignored entirely in every claim
Objective findings alone determine the settlement with no other input
Pain can never be compensated without a fracture
Objective findings corroborate the nature and extent of injury and help calibrate treatment and damages to evidence

questions.explanation: Corroborating findings strengthen or temper the evaluation of reported symptoms and treatment, grounding value in evidence. Ignoring all subjective reports, using findings as the sole input, or requiring a fracture for pain recovery each distort that balance.

questions.question: Adjuster Grace explains a Yuma claim where two separate hailstorms in one policy period each caused covered damage. She correctly notes the deductible generally:

answers.text: Applies only once per policy period no matter how many losses occur
Applies separately to each occurrence of loss
Is waived for the second storm because the first was paid
Doubles automatically for the second occurrence

questions.explanation: Property deductibles typically apply per occurrence, so each storm bears its own deductible. A once-per-period deductible describes an aggregate deductible design, not the standard per-occurrence form.

questions.question: Which scenario most clearly supports a punitive damages claim rather than compensatory damages alone?

answers.text: A clerk makes an arithmetic error on a single invoice that is later corrected
A careful driver momentarily misjudges a stopping distance and rear-ends another car
A company knowingly keeps selling a product it has documented will catch fire, conceals the reports, and a buyer is burned
A homeowner forgets to salt an icy step one morning and a visitor slips

questions.explanation: Knowingly selling a documented fire hazard while concealing reports shows malice or conscious disregard well beyond ordinary carelessness. A momentary misjudgment, a single oversight or a corrected arithmetic error are ordinary negligence or mistake, supporting compensation at most.

questions.question: How does loss settlement ordinarily differ between a DP-1 and a qualifying DP-2 or DP-3?

answers.text: DP-1 always pays replacement cost and the other forms pay actual cash value
All three forms always pay replacement cost with no condition
All three forms always pay market value
DP-1 settles on an actual cash value basis, while DP-2 and DP-3 can provide replacement cost settlement when the insurance-to-value condition is met

questions.explanation: The basic form is an actual cash value form, while the broad and special forms allow replacement cost settlement if the dwelling is insured to the required percentage of replacement value. Market value is not the settlement basis under any of these forms.

questions.question: A trailer owned by the named insured is used with a covered auto. How is it treated?

answers.text: Trailers are never covered for any purpose
Trailers are covered only as dwellings
Trailer damage is always paid under medical payments
Owned trailers can be covered autos for liability under the definitions, while physical damage needs the trailer to be described or otherwise covered

questions.explanation: Liability follows the described trailer combination, but damage to the trailer itself requires its own physical damage grant, a distinction adjusters must explain clearly.

questions.question: A driver uses the insured sedan to deliver goods for pay at the time of the crash, a use the form excludes unless an exception applies. What should the adjuster do?

answers.text: Pay without asking about the use at the time of loss
Investigate the delivery facts, apply the livery or delivery exclusion and any endorsement or exception, and reserve rights in writing
Deny every claim the driver ever files
Rewrite the policy after the accident to add the use

questions.explanation: Use at the time of loss controls the exclusion analysis, so the adjuster documents what was being carried, for whom, and whether any buy-back or exception was purchased.

questions.question: A crop hail policy and a multi-peril policy sit side by side in grower Rosa's file in Casa Grande. How does the crop hail policy differ?

answers.text: Crop hail covers every peril the multi-peril policy covers, plus price risk
Crop hail is issued only by the federal government
Crop hail is a narrower, named-peril product focused on hail damage, and it can respond without waiting for end-of-season yield results
Crop hail pays only for damage to farm buildings

questions.explanation: Crop hail is a private, single-peril-focused product that pays on the hail damage itself, which is why growers layer it over broader yield protection.

questions.question: A catastrophe adjuster's insurer-sent storm assignment in Arizona ends. What happens to the adjuster's authority under the exemption?

answers.text: The adjuster may begin representing insureds, since the adjuster is now known locally
The exemption converts automatically into a four-year Arizona license
The exemption ends with the assignment; further adjusting in Arizona requires an Arizona license unless another exemption applies
The adjuster may keep adjusting any Arizona claims for one more year

questions.explanation: Exemption authority is assignment-bound: when the particular loss or catastrophe series work ends, so does the excuse from licensure.

questions.question: Adjuster Omar is reviewing a Tucson claim where the insured never sent the required proof of loss described in the policy. Omar's coverage review should focus on the policy's:

answers.text: Conditions, which set duties and requirements that must be satisfied
Declarations, which list the insured's name and address
Endorsement schedule, which adds a new vehicle
Marketing materials, which describe the insurer generally

questions.explanation: Proof-of-loss duties are conditions precedent to recovery under many policies. Declarations identify the insured but do not impose the post-loss duties at issue.

questions.question: All of the following are true about additional insureds EXCEPT:

answers.text: An additional insured may unilaterally raise the policy limits for its own benefit
The named insured's premium is based in part on exposures that generate additional insured obligations
Certificates often evidence additional insured status, but the endorsement itself controls the coverage
An additional insured can generally make a claim and receive a defense for covered suits within the endorsement's scope

questions.explanation: Limits are set by the policy the named insured bought; an additional insured cannot raise them on its own. The endorsement, not the certificate, is the controlling document when the two differ.

questions.question: An adjuster asks homeowner Noah in Peoria to separate damaged from undamaged property and make the damaged items available for inspection. Under what duty does this fall?

answers.text: The duty to show and preserve damaged property and cooperate with the investigation as the conditions require
No duty, because inspection is optional for the insured
The duty belongs only to the mortgage company
The liability defense duty

questions.explanation: Cooperation and inspection duties let the insurer verify the loss it is asked to pay. Refusing all inspection while demanding payment contradicts the conditions the insured agreed to.

questions.question: A business income policy has a limit of $120,000 with a monthly limit factor of 1/4 as stated in the stem. What is the most payable for business income loss in any one month?
questions.explanation: The monthly limitation caps each month at the stated fraction of the limit. One-fourth of $120,000 is $30,000 per month, even if the actual monthly loss is larger.

questions.question: All of the following are part of the Arizona fingerprint process EXCEPT:

answers.text: Using the state public safety portal process
Using Fieldprint for fingerprinting
Paying the separate fingerprint-processing charges
Paying the $120 license fee to Fieldprint as the fingerprint fee

questions.explanation: Fingerprints run through the public safety portal and Fieldprint with their own charges; the $120 amount is the license fee, not a fingerprint fee paid to Fieldprint.

questions.question: EXCEPT — Which of the following parties would NOT ordinarily request a certificate of insurance?

answers.text: A landlord leasing warehouse space in Phoenix
A customer buying a single retail item with no contract, lease, or loan involved
A general contractor hiring a subcontractor in Scottsdale
A lender financing commercial equipment in Tucson

questions.explanation: Certificates exist to prove compliance with a contractual insurance requirement. An ordinary retail purchase creates no such requirement, unlike leases, subcontracts, and financed purchases.

questions.question: All of the following Section I items involve limitations rather than total exclusions in common adjusting EXCEPT:

answers.text: Intentional arson by the named insured, which is an excluded intentional loss
Pair or set loss, where the form may pay the reasonable difference in value
Loss settlement reduction when insurance to value is not maintained
Deductible application to a covered loss

questions.explanation: Pair-or-set, insurance-to-value and deductible provisions adjust how much is paid for a covered loss. Arson by the insured removes coverage for the loss itself, which is a true exclusion.

questions.question: All of the following would be business personal property for a Tucson medical office under BOP Section I EXCEPT:

answers.text: The building's load-bearing exterior wall, which is part of the building itself
Exam tables used to treat patients
Computers used for scheduling and billing
Medical supplies held for use in the practice

questions.explanation: Contents the practice owns and uses in its business are business personal property, while a load-bearing exterior wall is part of the insured building and belongs under building coverage, not contents coverage.

arkansas-independent-adjuster.quiz_title: Arkansas Independent Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: If a policy form and an endorsement conflict, the usual rule is that:

answers.text: The endorsement controls, because it was added to modify the base form for that insured
Neither applies and the policy is void automatically
The older document always controls regardless of intent
The advertising brochure controls over both

questions.explanation: A later, specific endorsement is meant to change the standard form and generally prevails over it. Automatic voidness is not the consequence of a form-endorsement conflict.

questions.question: A fraternal benefit society provides insurance benefits primarily to:

answers.text: Any member of the general public who walks in
Employees of the state insurance department
Only stockholders who buy shares
Its members, who belong to the society's lodge or membership system

questions.explanation: Fraternal insurers operate for their members under a lodge system. Membership, not share ownership, is the gateway to their insurance benefits.

questions.question: What is the reasonable person standard?

answers.text: The objective measure of care that an ordinarily prudent person would exercise under similar circumstances
The highest level of care achievable with unlimited resources
A standard that applies only to licensed professionals
Whatever the defendant personally believed was careful enough

questions.explanation: Negligence measures conduct objectively against the ordinarily prudent person in similar circumstances. A defendant's subjective belief that the conduct was fine does not control, and the standard is reasonableness rather than perfection.

questions.question: What taxes and fees, if any, enter a cash total loss settlement?

answers.text: Sales tax is never considered under any source
Registration for the next five years is standard
Every fee the dealer charges on any future purchase
Only those the policy, endorsement, or applicable law requires — the adjuster identifies the governing source rather than assuming every fee is owed

questions.explanation: Tax and fee treatment is source-driven; the adjuster cites the policy or law that applies in that file instead of promising dealer charges wholesale.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a bodily injury reserve review after surgery is recommended?

answers.text: To update the reserve to reflect the materially increased treatment cost, recovery time, and damages exposure shown by the new medical information
To lock the reserve at its original figure for consistency
To reduce the reserve because surgery makes settlement less likely
To close the file until surgery is complete and bills arrive

questions.explanation: Material medical developments require reserve updates reflecting the changed exposure, with the file kept active through treatment. Freezing, cutting, or shelving the reserve and file in response to surgery misstates and mishandles the claim.

questions.question: Why do adjusters refer suspected application misrepresentation to underwriting or coverage counsel rather than deciding rescission alone at the claim desk?

answers.text: Adjusters are never allowed to read applications
Materiality and reliance are fact-specific determinations that affect whether the contract can be voided
Coverage counsel must approve every routine claim payment
Rescission is automatic for any inaccurate word in an application

questions.explanation: Rescission depends on proving the statement false, material, and relied upon, which requires careful review. Minor inaccuracies do not automatically void a policy, contrary to the automatic-rescission distractor.

questions.question: Why does the principle of utmost good faith matter most at application and claim time?

answers.text: It allows the insurer to rewrite the policy after a loss
Each party relies heavily on the honesty and disclosure of the other
It guarantees payment even when a loss is excluded
It removes the need for any written policy wording

questions.explanation: Utmost good faith requires full honesty because the insurer relies on the applicant's disclosures and the insured relies on the insurer's promise. It never authorizes rewriting terms after a loss to suit either side.

questions.question: Compared with the standard mortgage clause, an open or simple loss payable clause gives the payee:

answers.text: Only the rights the insured has, so the insured's breach that voids coverage can also defeat the payee's recovery
Immunity from every policy condition regardless of the insured's conduct
Ownership of the policy and the right to rewrite its terms
Greater protection than the standard mortgage clause in every case

questions.explanation: The open loss payable clause is derivative: the payee stands in the insured's shoes. The standard mortgage clause, by contrast, creates an independent contract that can survive the borrower's voiding act.

questions.question: What role does 'direct' play in the phrase 'direct physical loss'?

answers.text: The loss must be paid directly to the insured with no mortgagee interest of any kind
The damage must be visible from the street without entering the property
The covered peril must directly produce physical damage to covered property, as opposed to a purely economic loss with no physical damage
The insured must file the claim directly with the insurer's home office

questions.explanation: Direct physical loss requires actual physical injury to property caused by the peril, not a standalone economic disappointment. Filing location, payee rules and street visibility are unrelated to the causation concept.

questions.question: Which statement about dwelling Coverage A settlement best helps an insured understand the declarations?

answers.text: The declarations amount is a limit, not a promise that every loss will be paid at that full amount
The declarations amount can be exceeded whenever repairs cost more
The declarations amount guarantees market value at sale
The declarations amount is paid automatically for any damage, however small

questions.explanation: A stated limit caps what the form will pay for a covered loss; it is not an agreed payout for any incident. Treating the limit as an automatic payment confuses a maximum with a measure of actual damage.

questions.question: State inspectors require periodic jurisdictional inspections of the boilers at a Jonesboro hospital. Why do those inspections matter to the insurance program?

answers.text: Passing inspection permanently eliminates the need for insurance
Many equipment breakdown programs rely on and coordinate with required jurisdictional boiler inspections, and keeping inspections current helps keep the coverage and the equipment in compliance
Inspection certificates replace the policy as proof of coverage
Inspectors set the hospital's insurance premiums by law

questions.explanation: Boiler insurance grew up alongside jurisdictional inspection regimes; the adjuster should verify inspection status as part of handling and documenting the risk and any loss.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a qualification for an Arkansas adjuster license today?

answers.text: Passing the required written examination
Legal age of majority
Proof of 12 months of experience or a 12-month apprenticeship under a licensed adjuster
Residency or reciprocal-state licensure

questions.explanation: NIPR states expressly that Arkansas no longer requires proof of 12 months of experience or apprenticeship; older sources repeating it are stale.

questions.question: All of the following are examples of a physical hazard EXCEPT:

answers.text: A driver who regularly texts while driving on I-40 near Little Rock
A frayed electrical cord in a Fayetteville warehouse
Icy steps outside a Jonesboro storefront
Worn tires on a delivery van

questions.explanation: Texting while driving reflects careless behavior, a moral or morale concern, not a physical condition of property. Worn tires, icy steps, and frayed cords are tangible physical conditions that increase loss risk.

questions.question: EXCEPT — Which of the following is NOT accomplished by an endorsement?

answers.text: Raising a property limit after a values increase
Adding a newly purchased vehicle to a commercial auto policy
Retroactively erasing a loss that has already occurred from the claim record
Adding an additional insured for liability coverage

questions.explanation: Endorsements change contract terms going forward or as agreed from an effective date, but they do not rewrite history to make a known, already-occurred loss disappear.

questions.question: All of the following are characteristics of an agreed value provision EXCEPT:

answers.text: It is commonly used for unique or hard-to-value property
When it applies, a coinsurance penalty is typically suspended for covered losses
The insurer and insured agree in advance on the value used for loss settlement
It requires the insured to prove the property's value again after every loss before payment

questions.explanation: Agreed value is set before the loss, so the parties do not re-prove that agreed value after the loss in order to use it. The advance agreement is precisely what distinguishes this method, and it commonly suspends a coinsurance penalty while it is in effect.

questions.question: Scenario: Adjuster Elena handles a heat-related covered loss at a El Dorado produce packer's cold-storage building. The packer rents refrigerated trucks to save incoming produce. How should Elena classify the truck rental?

answers.text: As an uncovered cost because mitigation is never compensable
As potential extra expense incurred to continue operations and mitigate the loss after direct physical damage
As a crime loss because the produce was at risk of theft
As a business income amount with no documentation needed

questions.explanation: Renting substitute cold storage is classic mitigation spending above normal operations. Elena should verify it was necessary, loss-caused, and reasonable, then handle it under the extra expense provisions.

questions.question: All of the following are Arkansas total-loss rules EXCEPT:

answers.text: Taxes and transfer fees are included in replacement and cash settlements
The offer and rejection of a replacement must be documented
Deviation deductions must be itemized and dollar-specified
The insurer may require the claimant to travel any distance necessary to inspect a replacement automobile

questions.explanation: Unreasonable travel demands are expressly prohibited; the other three are the rule's own requirements.

questions.question: A Jonesboro homeowner's insurer pays for water damage caused by a failed washing-machine hose made by a national manufacturer. The strongest subrogation practice is for the adjuster to:

answers.text: Settle and close without noting the product involved
Advise the homeowner to discard the hose to avoid clutter
Retain the failed hose, photograph the scene, and record the product identifiers before disposal
Mail the hose back to the homeowner without documentation

questions.explanation: Recovery against a manufacturer turns on the failed product and documented identifiers. Undocumented disposal, the tempting shortcut, destroys the proof the recovery would need.

questions.question: A named perils policy lists windstorm. A Little Rock homeowner proves a severe thunderstorm windstorm tore shingles from the roof. The insurer wants to deny based on a wear-and-tear exclusion for the old shingles. Which burden statement is correct?

answers.text: The homeowner has met the initial burden by proving a named peril, and the insurer must support the exclusion it is asserting
The mortgage company decides which party bears the burden
The homeowner must also disprove every exclusion in the policy before any payment can be considered
The insurer may deny without identifying any policy language

questions.explanation: Once the insured proves the named windstorm peril, the party relying on wear and tear must establish that exclusion. The insured is not required to negate every exclusion in the form in advance.

questions.question: Which business would most likely fall outside standard BOP eligibility and need a commercial package policy instead?

answers.text: A large auto dealership with extensive open lot inventory and high total values
A small owner-operated hair salon in a strip center
A neighborhood gift shop with modest inventory
A two-person accounting office

questions.explanation: BOP eligibility is aimed at smaller, lower-hazard operations with value and size limits; large dealerships and similar high-value or high-hazard risks are written on commercial package or specialized forms.

california-independent-adjuster.quiz_title: California Independent Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: When does a binder typically provide temporary evidence of insurance?

answers.text: From binding until the policy is issued or the binder expires or is replaced
Never; binders have no legal effect in any state
For exactly ten years regardless of its terms
Only after the first claim is paid

questions.explanation: A binder is temporary proof of coverage pending policy issuance, governed by its own stated period and conditions. It does have legal effect, contrary to the final distractor.

questions.question: What is the practical difference between a misrepresentation and a breach of warranty for coverage?

answers.text: There is no difference; the terms are fully interchangeable
A warranty never affects coverage under any circumstances
Misrepresentation can only occur after a loss happens
A misrepresentation generally must be material to affect coverage, while a warranty is a strict condition of the contract

questions.explanation: Materiality is the gate for misrepresentation remedies, whereas warranties bind as contract conditions. Timing also differs: misrepresentation typically occurs in the application before inception, not only after a loss.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a managing general agent (MGA) for an insurer?

answers.text: To adjust only the insurer's largest catastrophe claims
To lend premium funds to insureds
To act as the state's insurance regulator
To underwrite, bind, and service business for the insurer within delegated authority, often including appointing producers

questions.explanation: MGAs exercise delegated underwriting and production authority for carriers. Regulation belongs to the state department, not to a private MGA, so that choice confuses private delegation with public authority.

questions.question: Pain and suffering, emotional distress and loss of consortium are classified as:

answers.text: General damages, a form of noneconomic compensatory damages
Punitive damages in every case
Property damages
Special damages because they appear on a bill

questions.explanation: These harms compensate for real but non-billable injury, so they are general compensatory damages. They become punitive only if an award is meant to punish, which is a different category with a different test.

questions.question: Which set lists the four elements a claimant must prove to establish negligence?

answers.text: Contract, offer, acceptance, and consideration
Duty, breach of duty, causation, and damages
Intent, motive, malice, and punishment
Notice, appraisal, subrogation, and salvage

questions.explanation: Negligence requires a duty owed, a breach of the standard of care, causation linking the breach to harm, and actual damages. Intent and malice belong to intentional-tort analysis, not to the basic negligence elements.

questions.question: A Stockton claimant submits receipts for a hotel stay after a covered fire, but the dates include two nights before the fire occurred. Adjuster Lee should:

answers.text: Pay the full receipts without questions to maintain goodwill
Add extra nights to the payment to offset the confusion
Ask the claimant to explain the discrepancy, verify the records, and pay only the amounts properly supported as covered
Deny the entire claim automatically and report the claimant for prosecution

questions.explanation: A date mismatch may be error or padding; verification and a chance to explain come first, with payment limited to what is supported. Automatic prosecution referrals and unquestioning payment both skip the investigation.

questions.question: During a Sacramento cabin claim, adjuster Ruth needs the policy period and the dwelling limit. She should look first at:

answers.text: The conditions section for the appraisal clause
The declarations page for that policy
The definitions of 'occurrence'
A prior year's cancelled policy for the same insured

questions.explanation: Period and limits are declarations items specific to that contract. A cancelled prior policy cannot supply the current contract's numbers.

questions.question: Why do policies prohibit the insured from signing a release with a negligent third party before the insurer pays?

answers.text: Releases are illegal documents in all contexts
A release automatically cancels the insured's own policy
The insurer wants the insured to remain angry at the third party
The release could destroy the insurer's subrogation rights against that party

questions.explanation: Impairing subrogation by releasing the wrongdoer can prejudice the insurer and breach policy conditions. Releases themselves are lawful; the problem is giving one away before the insurer's rights are protected.

questions.question: An insured with Special-form coverage suffers direct physical loss from a cause the form does not name and does not exclude or limit. The usual result is:

answers.text: The loss is paid only at actual cash value even if the policy is on a replacement cost basis
The loss is denied because every covered cause must be named
The loss is covered only if a Basic-form peril also occurred
The loss is covered because Special form is written on an open-perils basis

questions.explanation: Under Special form, a cause does not need to be named to be covered; it needs to avoid the exclusions and limitations. Requiring the cause to be named would turn Special form back into a named-perils form.

questions.question: What does the cancellation language printed on most certificates tell the certificate holder?

answers.text: The certificate holder can block cancellation by objecting in writing
The insurer promises the holder 60 days of personal notice before any cancellation
Notice of cancellation will be provided in accordance with the policy provisions, and the policy itself controls
Coverage for the holder continues for 30 days after the policy cancels

questions.explanation: Modern certificate wording removed any independent notice promise. Cancellation rights and notice duties live in the policy and applicable law, not in the informational certificate.

questions.question: The phrase 'all risk' in connection with open perils coverage is potentially misleading because:

answers.text: Open perils coverage applies only to liability losses
Open perils policies cover fewer perils than Basic named perils policies
The policy still contains exclusions, limitations and conditions, so not literally every risk is covered
The phrase means the insured bears all the risk with no insurance

questions.explanation: All-risk is informal shorthand for open perils, not a promise to pay every loss. Reading the exclusions and conditions remains essential, which is why adjusters should use the term special or open perils in file notes.

questions.question: What role does 'direct' play in the phrase 'direct physical loss'?

answers.text: The loss must be paid directly to the insured with no mortgagee interest of any kind
The damage must be visible from the street without entering the property
The covered peril must directly produce physical damage to covered property, as opposed to a purely economic loss with no physical damage
The insured must file the claim directly with the insurer's home office

questions.explanation: Direct physical loss requires actual physical injury to property caused by the peril, not a standalone economic disappointment. Filing location, payee rules and street visibility are unrelated to the causation concept.

questions.question: Adjuster Marco is handling a San Diego fire claim. The insured demands payment from two insurers for the full amount of the same loss from each. Marco correctly explains that indemnity:

answers.text: Prevents recovering more than the actual loss for the same damage
Applies only to liability claims and never to property
Requires each insurer to pay the full loss independently
Lets the insured choose the higher of the two payments plus the lower one

questions.explanation: Other-insurance and indemnity principles coordinate payments so total recovery does not exceed the loss. Paying the full loss twice, the demand here, is exactly what indemnity forbids.

questions.question: All of the following are examples of a physical hazard EXCEPT:

answers.text: A driver who regularly texts while driving on I-10 near Los Angeles
A frayed electrical cord in a San Diego warehouse
Icy steps outside a Sacramento storefront
Worn tires on a delivery van

questions.explanation: Texting while driving reflects careless behavior, a moral or morale concern, not a physical condition of property. Worn tires, icy steps, and frayed cords are tangible physical conditions that increase loss risk.

questions.question: A one-year policy with a $1,200 annual premium is cancelled on a pro rata basis exactly 3 months after inception, with no other charges stated. The unearned premium refund is:
questions.explanation: Three months is one quarter of the year, so the earned premium is one quarter of $1,200, or $300. The unearned refund is $1,200 minus $300, which equals $900.

questions.question: Scenario: San Diego retailer Ana buys an adjoining storefront and asks her producer to 'just note it in the file.' Adjuster Tom later handles a fire there. What is the coverage concern?

answers.text: Coverage applies but the deductible is doubled for noted locations
Without an endorsement adding the premises, the new storefront may not be a covered location at all
File notes automatically extend property coverage to any building the insured buys
The fire is covered because Ana paid rent on the new space

questions.explanation: Property coverage follows scheduled locations and the new-acquired-property provisions, not informal file notes. Tom must check whether any endorsement or automatic provision reaches the unscheduled storefront.

questions.question: Marcus insures a Sacramento warehouse under a valued policy provision for a stated $250,000. A covered total loss destroys the warehouse. Subject to the policy terms, the settlement basis is:

answers.text: The warehouse's depreciated book value on the owner's tax return alone
The cost of the smallest warehouse that could store the same goods
Whatever a buyer might offer for the vacant land after the fire
The $250,000 value stated in the policy

questions.explanation: A valued or agreed-value approach uses the amount fixed in the policy for a covered total loss. Tax book value and post-loss land offers do not replace the value the insurer and insured placed in the contract.

questions.question: A Stockton warehouse is valued at $1,000,000 as stated in the stem. The policy requires 80% coinsurance and the owner carries a $600,000 limit as stated in the stem. A covered partial loss of $100,000 occurs as stated in the stem, ignoring any deductible. The coinsurance-adjusted payment is:
questions.explanation: Required insurance is 80% of $1,000,000, or $800,000. The recovery ratio is $600,000 divided by $800,000, or 75%, so 75% of the $100,000 loss is $75,000. Paying the full loss ignores the underinsurance penalty.

questions.question: All of the following are essential elements of a legally enforceable contract EXCEPT:

answers.text: Legal purpose and competent parties
An offer and an acceptance of that offer
A requirement that the agreement be written on an insurer's preprinted form
Consideration exchanged by the parties

questions.explanation: Contracts require offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties, and legal purpose; a preprinted insurer form is not an element. Many binding agreements arise without any particular form, so the form requirement is the outlier.

questions.question: All of the following are differences between a loss payee and an additional insured EXCEPT:

answers.text: A loss payee's interest is in receiving property loss proceeds
An additional insured is usually added by endorsement at the request of the named insured under a contract
A loss payee is entitled to set the policy premium and choose the insurer
An additional insured receives liability protection under the policy

questions.explanation: Neither a loss payee nor an additional insured sets premiums or selects the insurer; that is the named insured's and insurer's role. The real distinction is proceeds interest versus liability protection.

sat.quiz_title: SAT (Digital SAT) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A sample starts with 13 cells and doubles every 15 minutes. How many cells are there after 1 hour?
questions.explanation: Use the definitions directly. Convert units first: 1 hour is 4 fifteen-minute periods. The amount is multiplied by 2 a total of 4 times: 13 x 2^4 = 208. Choosing 52 usually signals a period-count slip that counts the periods in the wrong unit, halving the number of growth periods somewhere in the middle steps.

questions.question: A savings balance starts at 192 dollars and doubles every year in a model. Which expression gives the modeled balance after t years?
questions.explanation: Use the definitions directly. Each period multiplies the amount by 2, so after t periods the starting amount 192 has been multiplied by 2 a total of t times: 192(2)^t. Choosing 2(192)^t usually signals an exponent placement error that raises the starting amount to the power instead of the growth factor somewhere in the middle steps.

questions.question: An equation from a review sheet: (x + 2)/4 = (x + 3)/5. Solve for x.
questions.explanation: Cross-multiply to clear both fractions: 5(x + 2) = 4(x + 3), which expands to 5x + 10 = 4x + 12. Collect terms: 1x = 2, so x = 2. The tempting value 6 comes from a sign slip when the constant terms are collected after cross-multiplying, which is why that option cannot be correct.

questions.question: The equation 40/(x - 1) = 8 has one solution. What is that solution?
questions.explanation: Use the definitions directly. Multiply both sides by the denominator and divide by 8: x - (1) = 40/8 = 5. So x = 1 + 5 = 6. Students who make an early-stop error that reports the denominator's value instead of solving for x land on 5; the careful path above gives the keyed value.

questions.question: In a morning commute count, 27 of the entries are bus riders and 60 are walkers. What percent of all the entries are bus riders?
questions.explanation: Identify the whole and the part first. The whole is 27 + 60 = 87, so the percent is 27/87 × 100 = 31%. Watch for the part/whole swap trap, which produces 45% and is a common slip here.

questions.question: For two bakery counters tracked by loaf count, Bakery East follows C = 6n + 16 and Bakery West follows C = 3n + 25. The graphs intersect at (3, 34). What is the meaning of 3 in this situation?

answers.text: The total combined value of both options after 3 loaves
The number of loaves at which the two options give the same value, 34
The value, 34, that each option reaches after 6 loaves
The number of loaves at which the first option reaches 34 for the first time only

questions.explanation: An intersection point belongs to both graphs at once. At the input 3, both models give the same output 34, so 3 is the number of loaves where the two options match. The second coordinate 34 is the shared value itself, which is what the tempting option describes instead of the input. Watch out for The value, 34, that each option reaches after 6 loaves: it follows from describing the shared output value instead of the input at which the two models agree, and it does not satisfy both original equations when tested.

questions.question:
The maker fills object cells for the studio's brass kaleidoscopes. _____, the maker also fills two-mirror and three-mirror cells differently, since each mirror system wants its own size of fragment.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

answers.text: Instead
Specifically
In addition
In fact

questions.explanation: The sentence after the blank adds a further point of the same kind: the passage notes that object cells are filled for brass kaleidoscopes and then adds that cells for different mirror systems are filled differently. 'In addition' expresses exactly this addition relationship. By contrast, 'Instead' would mark an opposition or reversal between the two ideas, and no such relationship holds between these ideas.

questions.question:
At a kite-making workshop, kite makers were test-flying new bridles in the field behind the shop. The team had reason to stir, and the record shows why: she moved the soup around with a ladle to keep it from sticking. The group returned to the example whenever progress was assessed.

As used in the passage, 'stir' most nearly means

answers.text: move a liquid around with a spoon
pour a liquid out
freeze a liquid solid
leave a liquid untouched

questions.explanation: What the passage describes — she moved the soup around with a ladle to keep it from sticking — matches move a liquid around with a spoon, which is what 'stir' means here. 'leave a liquid untouched' fails because the passage gives no indication of that quality, while it directly demonstrates move a liquid around with a spoon.

questions.question: Someone labels jars of dried herbs for winter. The diagonals of a rhombus measure 8 units and 5 units (workbook set of 2287 figures). What is its area, in square units?
questions.explanation: The area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals: 8 x 5 / 2 = 20 square units. The strongest distractor, 40, comes from the multiplying the diagonals without halving error.

questions.question: The total cost at a sailboat rental dock is a $29 harbor fee plus $13 for each hour sailed. Which expression gives the total cost, in dollars, for n hours?
questions.explanation: The per-hour charge multiplies the count: 13n. The one-time fee is added once: C(n) = 13n + 29. The choices that multiply the fee by n, or subtract it, misplace the fixed amount. A student who lands on C(n) = 29n + 13 has typically fallen for a swapped slope/intercept placement that multiplies the one-time fee by the count; the check step rules it out.

questions.question: The point (9, 66) lies on both the graph of y = x^2 + 8x - 87 and the graph of y = 6x + 12. Which statement correctly describes what that means?

answers.text: The two functions have no values in common near x = 9.
At x = 9, the quadratic function reaches its maximum value, 66.
At x = 9, the two functions have the same value, 66.
At x = 66, the two functions have the same value, 9.

questions.explanation: Work through it step by step. A point lying on both graphs has coordinates satisfying both equations at once. At x = 9, the line gives 6(9) + 12 = 66, and the quadratic gives the same output 66, so the functions agree there. Choosing At x = 9, the quadratic function reaches its maximum value, 66. usually signals an interpretation error that treats an intersection as an extreme value of one function alone somewhere in the middle steps.

questions.question: Crates of apples wait beside the market stall. At a scale of 1 centimeter to 30 centimeters, a model water tower measuring 4 centimeters is displayed with 163 other pieces nearby. How tall, in meters, is the structure it represents?
