answers.text: 4 flawed units would treat the stated percentage itself as a count, ignoring that the run contains two hundred fifty units, not one hundred in the bolts operation.
25 flawed units would apply the flaw rate to the wrong base, overstating the expectation by a factor that the run size does not support.
10 flawed units is the expectation, because an expected count multiplies the flaw probability by the run size: 0.04 x 250 units at the Cobalt Street plant.
100 flawed units would multiply the percentage by the run size without converting 4% into its decimal form of 0.04 first.

questions.explanation: Curing 250 bolts while flaws strike 4 percent predicts 0.04 multiplied by 250, giving ten flawed bolts as Juniper Stanton's long-run expectation for next week.

questions.question: A paired t-test on 15 technicians shows mean error rate fell by 2.1 points, with the interval for mean change running from a fall of 3.8 to a fall of 0.4. How does that interval inform the verdict?

answers.text: The interval suggests errors rose, because negative thinking dominates the lower bound value listed.
The interval proves every technician improved equally, because ranges describe individuals directly.
The interval must be ignored, because paired tests communicate exclusively through t-statistics alone.
The interval excludes zero change, supporting a genuine average reduction in errors after training.

questions.explanation: An interval for the mean difference that stays clear of zero aligns with rejecting no change. It also bounds the plausible size of the average fall.

questions.question: A manager assumes buyers want the cheapest model, but interviews show durability matters more. What lesson follows?

answers.text: Checking assumptions against real customer input prevents optimising the wrong characteristic.
Interviews should be discounted whenever they contradict a manager's market intuition.
The lesson is that price never influences purchasing decisions in any product category.
Durability should now be maximised regardless of cost, segment, or stated trade-offs.

questions.explanation: Assumed priorities often miss. Gathering actual voice of the customer redirects effort toward characteristics buyers truly value.

nate-certification.quiz_title: NATE Certification Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A jug of descaler in the service van has lost its label after a cap leak soaked the paper. What handling rule applies to that now-unidentified chemical container?

answers.text: Smell the contents to guess the product
Pour it into a labeled bottle of similar cleaner
Do not use it; identify the contents through proper channels or dispose of it per procedure
Use it on the next job to test its strength

questions.explanation: Unlabeled chemicals cannot be handled safely because no one knows their hazards, antidotes, or compatibility; sniffing, guessing, or transferring into another product bottle risks violent reactions and poisonings. Unidentified containers follow identification or disposal procedures.

questions.question: A hermetic compressor data plate lists locked-rotor amps of 54 and rated-load amps of 9 for the same voltage. How many times larger is the stalled draw than the rated running draw?

answers.text: The stalled draw is 6 times the rated draw.
The stalled draw is 486 times the rated draw.
The stalled draw is 45 times the rated draw.
The stalled draw is 63 times the rated draw.

questions.explanation: Dividing locked-rotor amps by rated-load amps shows the severity of a stalled start: several times normal current flows with no rotation, which is why overloads must clear a locked compressor quickly before winding damage accumulates.  Calculation: 54 / 9 = 6.

questions.question: An instructor points at the middle of a running condenser coil and asks what the refrigerant is doing there. Which answer is right?

answers.text: It is fully subcooled liquid gaining sensible heat
It is a saturated mixture, condensing from vapor to liquid and giving up latent heat at a nearly constant temperature
It is fully superheated vapor absorbing heat from the air
It is frozen solid until it reaches the metering device

questions.explanation: Through most of the condenser the refrigerant is a saturated vapor-liquid mixture changing phase at its condensing temperature; desuperheating happens at the inlet and subcooling only near the outlet.

questions.question: Secondary air in a conventional gas burner is best described as which of the following?

answers.text: A backup supply delivered by a second inducer motor on large furnaces
Air injected into the vent connector to cool flue gases before the roof
Air drawn around the flame at the burner ports that completes combustion of the gas not fully burned by primary air alone
The pressurized air a direct-vent unit pulls through its outdoor intake pipe

questions.explanation: Combustion at an atmospheric burner uses staged air: primary air premixed in the venturi, then secondary air surrounding the flame in the combustion chamber to finish oxidizing fuel. Intake piping on sealed units supplies both to the burner compartment, but the primary-secondary distinction describes mixing at the flame itself.

questions.question: For a recovery job on a large charge, the technician removes Schrader cores with a valve-core tool instead of pushing them open with hose depressors. What is gained?

answers.text: The compressor can be run backward to push the charge out
The refrigerant is automatically reclaimed to virgin purity standards
The system can be recovered without a recovery machine of any kind
A much larger, unrestricted flow path, so vapor and liquid move faster and recovery time drops substantially

questions.explanation: A depressed core is a tiny orifice; a removed core opens the full port bore. On large charges that difference multiplies across every minute of the job, which is why core removal with a shutoff-equipped tool is standard practice for serious recovery work.

questions.question: A crew lead uses a pocket digital hygrometer for quick comfort screenings but schedules a careful sling psychrometer comparison for it every season. What is the sound reasoning behind pairing the two instruments that way?

answers.text: The digital unit is always more accurate, so the sling comparison is only a formality for paperwork
The digital unit is fast and convenient for screening, while the sling provides an independent reference that can expose sensor drift before it misleads diagnoses
Slinging a psychrometer recalibrates any digital sensor held nearby during the process
Two instruments agreeing once guarantees both stay accurate for the rest of their service lives

questions.explanation: Electronic humidity sensors drift with age and contamination, so convenience instruments need periodic reality checks against a method with different failure modes. The sling comparison can reveal an offset worth correcting or documenting. Proximity does not recalibrate anything, and a single past agreement is not a lifetime guarantee — which is exactly why the comparison repeats.

questions.question: While inspecting a rooftop unit, a trainee asks why a dead short line-to-neutral trips a breaker almost instantly while a normal compressor start, though heavy, usually does not. What explanation is most accurate?

answers.text: A short reduces current because voltage collapses to zero at the breaker panel.
Breakers trip on voltage alone and ignore how much current is flowing.
A short provides a near-zero-resistance path, so current surges far beyond the rating until protection opens.
Compressor starting current is higher than short-circuit current in all cases.

questions.explanation: Current rises as circuit resistance falls, and a bolted short leaves only conductor and source resistance to limit flow. That extreme surge operates protective devices quickly, unlike a brief, limited motor inrush.

questions.question: A float switch in a condensate pan is wired to break the cooling call when condensate rises after a drain blockage in a ceiling air handler. Why is breaking the control call, rather than the line-voltage feed, a common wiring choice for this device?

answers.text: Float switches cannot physically be built to open any electrical circuit.
Breaking the call keeps the compressor running so the pan drains faster.
Line-voltage interruption would stop condensate production too slowly to matter.
Low-voltage control wiring is simpler and safer to route to a small switch, and interrupting the call stops the equipment that produces condensate.

questions.explanation: Small safety switches are typically rated for control-circuit duty, and stopping the cooling call removes the source of condensate before overflow damages ceilings. Some designs interrupt only the outdoor unit call, with the same protective intent.

questions.question: In heating at 20 degrees outside, a Kirbyville-area tech — working a mutual-aid call in cold country — notes the outdoor coil frosting evenly top to bottom, then clearing fully each defrost. What verdict fits?

answers.text: The coil is failing because any visible frost is abnormal
Normal behavior: even frost that clears completely is the system working as designed in cold weather
The defrost board must be set to its shortest interval immediately
The charge is low because frost reaches the bottom rows

questions.explanation: Even, full-coil frost in cold weather simply shows the whole evaporator surface doing its job, and complete clearing shows defrost doing its job. Patchy frost, frost that survives defrost, or a banded pattern is where trouble hides. Teaching homeowners this distinction prevents panic calls and keeps techs from fixing healthy systems.

questions.question: Equalizing pressures, warm suction at the valve, and low capacity in both modes have already cleared the compressor as healthy on a Winter Park call. The valve is condemned. What shop discipline governs the replacement job?

answers.text: Recover the charge, keep the new valve body cool and its ports capped until the moment of brazing, fit a new bi-flow drier, evacuate deeply, and weigh the charge back in
Swap the valve hot with the charge in place to save time
Reuse the old drier since it 'looks fine'
Charge by feel afterward because the scale is at the shop

questions.explanation: A reversing valve job touches every discipline at once: refrigerant handling, contamination control, heat management at the brazes, moisture removal, and exact recharge. Skipping any one — especially reusing a drier that has seen a failed valve's debris — writes the sequel to the same failure. The complete sequence is the repair; the part swap is only its middle.

questions.question: A trainee measures the evaporator saturation temperature is 36°F and the suction-line temperature is 47°F, then announces the coil has 83 degrees of superheat. What error produced that announcement?

answers.text: The gauge manifold was connected to the wrong service ports entirely
The suction line was measured in Celsius and reported as Fahrenheit
The coil was measured before the blower had started that morning
The two temperatures were added instead of subtracted; the true superheat is 11°F

questions.explanation: Superheat = 47°F − 36°F = 11°F. Adding 47 and 36 gives the announced 83, a classic first-month mistake. Superheat is a temperature difference between vapor and its own saturation point, never a sum of the two readings.

questions.question: In cooling mode on a humid Rapid City afternoon, which component outdoors is acting as the evaporator's partner by rejecting the house's heat to outside air — stated in cycle terms?

answers.text: The outdoor coil absorbs heat in both modes and never rejects any
The accumulator condenses the refrigerant outdoors in cooling
The outdoor coil is the condenser in cooling, giving up heat so indoor evaporation can absorb more
The indoor coil condenses in cooling while the outdoor coil meters

questions.explanation: Cooling is the familiar air-conditioning arrangement: the indoor coil evaporates and absorbs heat, the compressor lifts the vapor, and the outdoor coil condenses and rejects that heat outside. Heating simply reverses which coil does which job. Keeping the condenser/evaporator labels tied to mode prevents a host of diagnostic mix-ups.

questions.question: Occupants report static shocks, dry throats, and shrinking wood joints in January. Indoor temperature is normal. Which single measurement would most likely confirm the suspected cause?

answers.text: Relative humidity, which will probably read quite low, in the teens or twenties percent
Outdoor dew point alone, which fully determines indoor conditions in winter
Static pressure in the supply plenum, which causes static electricity in rooms
Discharge air temperature, which will probably read far above design value

questions.explanation: Winter dryness symptoms track low relative humidity caused by heating cold outdoor air. A hygrometer reading confirms it before adding humidification. Furnace discharge temperature and duct static do not create room static shocks, and outdoor dew point alone ignores indoor moisture sources and the heating effect on relative humidity.

questions.question: A pressure reading across a wet evaporator coil is nearly double the manufacturer's wet-coil allowance at the measured airflow. The coil face looks clean from the return side. What hidden condition reconciles a clean face with a choking pressure drop?

answers.text: Wet coils are supposed to double their dry pressure allowance daily
Dirt and biofilm are packed deep inside the fin pack where return-side inspection cannot see them, throttling the passages between fins
The manometer hoses are reversed on their pressure ports
The filter upstream is filtering too well for the coil to work

questions.explanation: Coil fouling is a depth problem: lint and growth migrate into the fin pack and bridge the narrow air passages from within. The visible face can pass a flashlight test while the core of the coil is effectively insulated and plugged, which the pressure-drop reading reports honestly.

questions.question: Fossil kit nuance in Aberdeen: the kit's temperature sensor is strapped to the suction line instead of sensing outdoor air after a hurried repair, and changeover now happens at odd times linked to compressor runs. Why does the strapped location lie?

answers.text: The sensor now reads refrigerant-line temperature, which swings with system operation far beyond air temperature, so fuel decisions follow machine state instead of weather
Suction lines are the manufacturer-preferred place for air sensors
The sensor reads correctly but the kit interprets suction data as wind speed
Odd changeover timing after a repair is always a coincidence

questions.explanation: Sensor meaning comes from placement. A line-mounted sensor reports the refrigeration cycle's moods: cold in cooling-adjacent operation, warmer after runs, none of it a proxy for outdoor air. Restoring the sensor to its specified ambient location and re-verifying changeover across a temperature swing repairs the information, not just the timing.

questions.question: A technician at a farmhouse finds the flexible connector at the furnace pinched nearly flat where a storage shelf was built against it, though no leak is detected today. What is the correct service disposition?

answers.text: Replace the damaged connector and restore clear access, because a mechanically damaged connector is a future leak risk even while it happens to seal today
Leave it, since connectors that are not leaking need no attention
Straighten the pinch with pliers and reuse the same connector
Wrap the pinch in tape as a permanent protective repair

questions.explanation: Connectors fail from exactly this kind of crushing and fatigue, often without warning odor beforehand. A pinched connector has consumed its safety margin even if a detector reads zero this morning. Renewal with a listed connector, proper routing, and re-established clearance is the only disposition that treats the finding as the hazard it is.

questions.question: A tech commissioning a dual-fuel system in Franktown must pick a changeover temperature with no load calculation available and a homeowner who hates cold drafts. Which approach is defensible?

answers.text: Start conservatively near the manufacturer's suggested changeover, document it, and adjust after observing a cold snap — a recorded starting point refined by evidence
Set it to the highest possible value so the furnace always leads
Set it to the lowest possible value so the heat pump never rests
Refuse to set anything and leave the system in manual mode

questions.explanation: Without a calculated balance point, the manufacturer's default exists precisely as a safe starting estimate. Commissioning is an iterative craft: record the setting, watch real performance in real cold, and tune. What is not defensible is an extreme setting chosen blind, or leaving a new system with no automatic changeover at all.

questions.question: During heavy exercise in a training video, about half a pound of sweat evaporates from a person's skin. Evaporating one pound of water takes roughly 970 Btu. About how much heat does that evaporation remove?

answers.text: About 1,940 Btu, from doubling the per-pound value for a half pound
About 970 Btu, the full per-pound value regardless of the amount evaporated
About 97 Btu, from shifting the decimal on the per-pound value
About 485 Btu, from half a pound times roughly 970 Btu per pound

questions.explanation: Latent removal scales with mass evaporated: 0.5 x 970 = 485 Btu carried away as vapor, which is why sweating cools the body when air can accept the moisture. Using the full pound value ignores the stated half pound, doubling inverts the scaling, and a decimal slip understates a major cooling mechanism. Numeric: 0.5*970 = 485.

questions.question: The previous tenant reported intermittent cooling; the new service agreement starts with baseline measurements on a hot afternoon. For a 4-ton heat-cooling split at a lakeside home with a fixed orifice, the charging chart target is 12°F of superheat at today's indoor wet-bulb and outdoor dry-bulb conditions, and the measured superheat is 21°F. By how much does the measured value miss the target, and in which direction?

answers.text: It misses by 9°F above target, meaning the coil is being starved, consistent with low charge or a restriction, so diagnose before adding refrigerant
It misses by 33°F, found by adding target and measured superheat
It misses by 14°F above target, using the difference between suction and liquid temperatures
The two values are treated as equal once the system has run steadily for fifteen minutes

questions.explanation: Deviation = measured superheat minus chart target = 21°F − 12°F = 9°F. The sign shows direction: positive means superheat is too high (starved coil) and negative means too low (overfed coil) for a fixed-orifice system under these conditions.

questions.question: In a cold-climate cabin, the furnace sequence reaches flame, the blower starts, and within a minute the flames shrink and gutter each time a nearby exhaust fan in the small utility space switches on. Shutting the exhaust fan off restores steady flames. What interaction is occurring?

answers.text: The exhaust fan is stealing voltage so the gas valve half-closes
The exhaust fan is depressurizing the space and competing with the furnace venting, disturbing combustion air and draft
Flames shrink because the thermostat lowers its setpoint when fans run
The fan blows supply air backward through the registers into the burners

questions.explanation: In tight small spaces, powerful exhaust can pull the room negative enough to fight an appliance that depends on that room for combustion air or natural vent flow. Flame disturbance that tracks the exhaust fan exactly is an air-balance problem, and sealed combustion or adequate makeup air is the durable correction.

iassc-lean-six-sigma-black-belt.quiz_title: IASSC Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Why does the hidden factory resist ordinary improvement prioritization in many plants?

answers.text: Operators hide rework deliberately to protect overtime earnings, and only surveillance reveals the true scale of the activity
Its work is normalized inside standard routings and labor standards, so no report ever isolates it as waste available for elimination
Hidden-factory output is sold as seconds at a discount, making its economics look attractive in contribution reports, if the budget holder approves
Accounting standards forbid separating rework labor, so managers must estimate the hidden factory from scrap value alone

questions.explanation: Rework embedded in standard times and routings becomes invisible by design; deliberate concealment, seconds sales, and accounting prohibitions misdescribe a structural visibility problem.

questions.question: A centered process has limits exactly four overall standard deviations on each side of the mean. What is its Pp?

answers.text: Pp is 2.67, because the full width of eight sigma divided by three gives the performance index for this process
Pp is 4.00, because the index reports the sigma distance from the mean to each limit without further adjustment
Pp is 0.75, because performance indices invert the ratio of tolerance width to the natural process spread used
Pp is 1.33, because the tolerance width of eight sigma divided by six sigma gives the performance index value

questions.explanation: Pp = (USL-LSL)/(6 x overall sigma) = 8 sigma / 6 sigma = 1.33. Centering makes Ppk equal to Pp in this symmetric case.

questions.question: Which phrasing correctly states what a Kruskal-Wallis rejection supports, absent any shape assumptions?

answers.text: The group with the largest sample has the largest median, because rank sums grow automatically with the size of each group
Every pair of groups differs significantly, because omnibus rejection is defined as all pairwise differences holding at once
All group means are different from one another in a specified direction that the statistic prints alongside its p-value here
At least one group's distribution is stochastically different, with values from it tending to sit higher or lower than others

questions.explanation: The defensible omnibus claim is distributional: at least one population tends to produce larger (or smaller) values than another. Pairwise and median-specific claims each demand further work or further assumptions.

questions.question: A grower tests five two-level inputs on tomato yield in a single replicate of a full factorial. How large is the run list?

answers.text: Thirty-two runs, from 2 multiplied by itself five times, covering each of the five factors' level pairings
Ten runs are enough, since five factors with two levels apiece contribute two runs per factor to the total
Sixty-four runs are required, which is the count belonging to six two-level factors rather than five here
Twenty runs result, because five factors at two levels produce four runs for every factor in the design

questions.explanation: With k=5, runs = 2^5 = 32, the full set of level combinations for five two-level factors.

questions.question: Which operators need control-plan training first when a plan launches across three shifts with limited trainer capacity?

answers.text: The day shift only, because night and weekend shifts can copy day-shift practice from the posted charts
Supervisors exclusively, since floor operators absorb plan requirements by imitating their supervisor, leaving direct operator instruction for a later training round
The newest hires, because experienced operators can be assumed competent on any new plan by default
Those covering the checks and reactions for critical characteristics on every shift, so no shift ever runs a critical control with untrained cover here

questions.explanation: Coverage logic governs sequencing: every shift needs certified capability on the highest-risk controls from the first day the plan is live.

questions.question: A Black Belt presents savings using straight wages while finance insists on loaded rates including benefits and payroll taxes. Whose convention governs the charter?

answers.text: Finance's loaded-rate convention, agreed and recorded at charter time, because benefit figures must be comparable across every project the portfolio reports
The Black Belt's wage figure, because improvement teams best understand what an hour in their process is actually worth
Whichever rate produces the larger benefit, since the charter's purpose is to win approval for worthwhile projects, because unwinding it later is somebody else's problem
A midpoint between the two rates, splitting the difference so neither party's convention dominates the calculation

questions.explanation: Comparability across the portfolio requires one agreed rate convention, set with finance before work starts; local knowledge, approval-seeking, and midpoint splits sacrifice that consistency.

questions.question: A Black Belt needs a quick check of a new fixture and runs a short study: 2 operators, 5 parts, 2 trials. The results look poor. What is the right weight to give this outcome?

answers.text: Treat it as a screening signal: a poor result warrants a fuller study, but the small design's estimates carry wide uncertainty
Treat it as definitive, because gage estimates stabilize completely once total measurements reach twenty in a study
Ignore it, because studies below ten parts are incapable of detecting even a completely unusable measurement system
Treat the poor result as proof the fixture is worse than the old one, since small studies bias estimates upward

questions.explanation: Small designs give imprecise variance estimates, so a poor screening result is a warning that justifies a proper study rather than a final verdict — but it is a real signal, not noise to be ignored.

questions.question: A team tests a claim that a process mean exceeds a regulatory floor. The analyst writes the alternative as 'mean equals the floor' by mistake, computes a tiny p-value, and claims victory. What went wrong conceptually?

answers.text: The boundary claim sat in the wrong seat: p-values flow from the default's distribution, so the scrambled setup voids the meaning
Nothing went wrong, because p-values are symmetric and can be computed from whichever statement the analyst finds convenient
The only slip is labeling, which a footnote can repair while preserving the victory claim and its supporting arithmetic
The floor should have been replaced by the sample mean in both statements, which would have made the victory claim rigorous

questions.explanation: Every p-value is anchored to the default position's sampling distribution; swapping the statements changes the anchor, so the tiny value no longer testifies about the claim being advanced.

questions.question: A predictor's variance inflation factor is 10, computed from an auxiliary R-squared of 0.90 when that predictor is regressed on the others. Verify and interpret.

answers.text: VIF = 1/(1 - 0.90) = 10 confirms it: the predictor is heavily explained by its companions, inflating its coefficient's variance
VIF = 1 - 0.90 = 0.10, so the predictor is nearly independent and its standard error is comfortably small, and the line crews would work to it
VIF = 1/(1 - 0.90) squared = 100, meaning the coefficient is ten times less precise than reported
VIF = 0.90/0.10 = 9, close to the threshold but computed by dividing the wrong pair of quantities here

questions.explanation: 1/(1 - 0.90) = 10 exactly; a VIF at that level says the coefficient's variance is inflated tenfold by overlap with other predictors.

questions.question: A study of solder defects uses each printed board twice: once as its own experimental unit and again after rework as a second unit. Why does a reviewer object?

answers.text: The objection is misplaced, because defect counts from the same board are actually more comparable than across boards
The reworked board is not an independent unit, so treating it as one understates error and overstates the evidence
Boards may be reused freely provided the run order is shuffled, which restores independence between the two passes
Rework is objectionable only because it doubles the study cost without adding any new factor combinations

questions.explanation: Experimental units must be independent; a reworked board carries its history with it, so its second result is correlated with the first.

questions.question: Phase I data for a new chart included a weekend when a substitute resin was used. Limits computed from all the data are wide, and phase II rarely signals. What went wrong?

answers.text: Phase I data must contain no special causes whatsoever, so the chart has to be discarded and the process requalified from scratch after that resin weekend.
Wide limits are correct here because phase II limits are required to widen every time phase I grows longer
The substitute resin weekend should have been charted as its own subgroup, which alone would have fixed the limits
The contaminated phase I sample inflated the variation estimate, so the trial limits are too generous and real departures hide inside them

questions.explanation: Phase I exists to estimate the stable process; leaving a known disturbed period in the estimate bakes its extra variation into every future limit.

questions.question: A Black Belt reviewing a supplier's CuSum finds the target was set to the average of the last month, which included a known bad week. What is the core defect?

answers.text: The defect is that targets must be specification midpoints, and using an observed monthly average is prohibited in CuSum work even when that week is excluded.
The target absorbed the bad week's bias, so the chart now treats a shifted level as normal and accumulates evidence against the wrong centre
A one-month baseline is too short by rule; CuSum targets require a minimum of twelve months of history before use
Including the bad week only affects the first plotted point, after which the statistic corrects itself automatically

questions.explanation: A CuSum measures departure from its target; a contaminated target shifts the zero point and the chart will defend the wrong level as if it were the aim.

questions.question: A fishbone session for invoice errors produces 60 candidate causes. The sponsor asks which three matter. The Black Belt's next step should be:

answers.text: Ask each participant to defend their own suggestions, then keep the three argued most persuasively in the room
Keep all sixty in scope until Improve, because narrowing causes early risks discarding the true root cause unknowingly, since missing it costs far more
Pareto the candidates against occurrence data — error logs, stratification by type and source — to shortlist causes for verification
Select the three causes cheapest to fix, since early wins matter more than causal importance at this stage of DMAIC

questions.explanation: Brainstormed volume must be reduced with evidence: error records stratified by type, shift, or source show where occurrences concentrate, pointing verification at plausible major causes.

questions.question: To estimate defect rates across three plants with very different volumes, a team samples proportionally within each plant. Which method and benefit?

answers.text: Cluster sampling, chosen because sampling whole plants is cheaper than sampling within every plant in the study
Stratified sampling, ensuring each plant is represented in proportion and plant-level comparisons remain possible
Simple random sampling across the pooled output, which automatically guarantees the proportional plant mix desired
Systematic sampling from the combined shipping stream, which represents plants in proportion to their shipment timing

questions.explanation: Dividing the population into plant strata and sampling within each is stratified sampling; it guarantees representation and supports per-stratum estimates.

questions.question: Two candidate fits for the same data differ only in that one was estimated on 18 points and the other on 60 points spanning the same x range. Why will the larger study's slope interval usually be tighter?

answers.text: More observations shrink the slope's standard error, since residual noise averages down while the x spread stays comparable
Larger samples raise the critical t value sharply, and that increase is what narrows intervals in practice
Sixty points guarantee a higher R-squared, and higher explained variation is what mechanically tightens slope intervals
The interval narrows because the slope estimate itself must grow with sample size, dwarfing its standard error

questions.explanation: Slope standard error falls roughly with the square root of n; more points over the same range pin the line's tilt down harder.

questions.question: A fractional screen estimates a contrast labelled A at 14 units, where A is aliased with BC. Later work shows the BC interaction is actually 10 units. What follows?

answers.text: A's effect must be 24, because aliased effects always add constructively in fractional designs
The later finding invalidates the screen retroactively, so all its other contrasts must also be discarded
A remains 14 regardless, because aliasing affects only the interpretation of inactive effects
Much of the 14 may belong to BC, so A's own contribution could be as small as roughly 4 units

questions.explanation: The contrast estimated A + BC = 14; if BC = 10, the portion attributable to A is about 14 - 10 = 4.

questions.question: A Black Belt sees a histogram of bolt torque with a sharp cutoff at the lower specification and a normal-looking body above it. What likely happened?

answers.text: The process naturally produces truncated data, because torque distributions terminate at specification limits physically
Parts below the limit were screened out before the histogram, so the data describe inspected output, not the process itself
The gauge cannot read below the limit, which proves the measurement system needs a wider range instrument installed
The cutoff proves the process is incapable, because capable processes never show abrupt edges in their histograms

questions.explanation: A hard edge at the spec is the signature of prior sorting: the process distribution was amputated by inspection, and capability read from it would be flattered.

questions.question: A call center's handle-time data fail every normality test, with p-values below 0.01 in samples of 30, 80, and 200 calls drawn weeks apart. A manager suggests collecting a much larger sample so the data themselves will become normal. Why is that reasoning wrong?

answers.text: Larger samples do become normal, but only after the count passes one thousand calls in a single uninterrupted sample
The reasoning is right for handle times because service data always converge to a bell shape as volume grows
Larger samples reveal the true skewed shape more clearly; the central limit effect applies to sample means, not to the raw call times
The tests fail only because of the small samples, and at 200 calls a p-value below 0.01 carries no information at all, across all shifts

questions.explanation: Collecting more calls sharpens the picture of a skewed population rather than changing it; the central limit theorem describes averages of samples, so raw handle times keep their skew no matter how many are gathered.

questions.question: A Black Belt sizes a two-sample t study to detect a 0.4-standard-deviation mean difference with power 0.80 at alpha 0.05. A planning table suggests about 100 observations per group. The client offers 40 per group 'to start.' What consequence should be spelled out?

answers.text: Power stays at 0.80 because the planning table's figures embed a safety factor of more than two that real studies never actually consume
At 40 per group, power for the targeted difference sinks toward roughly 0.40, so a null outcome leaves the question genuinely open
The smaller study becomes a pilot whose significant results are trustworthy but whose null results are even more decisive than the full study's
Reducing group size raises power in two-sample designs, because fewer observations tighten the sampling distribution of the difference

questions.explanation: Power curves are unforgiving at small standardized effects: 0.4 sigma needs roughly 100 per group for 80% power, and 40 per group buys little better than a coin flip weighted toward missing.

questions.question: A molding plant wants its andon escalation to be economically rational. Pulls currently stop the whole line for any fault, including faults one operator can clear in seconds. What refinement preserves the system?

answers.text: Abolish line stops entirely and log every fault for weekly review, since stop costs always exceed defect costs in high-volume molding operations
Tier the response: operator-clearable faults get a brief signal and local fix, while faults beyond a defined time or scope escalate to a full stop
Charge the cost of each stop to the pulling operator's department budget, creating a financial incentive to reserve pulls for severe faults only
Require supervisor pre-approval before any pull, ensuring only economically justified stops interrupt the line during scheduled production time

questions.explanation: Tiered escalation keeps fast local response cheap and reserves expensive full stops for faults that need them. Pre-approval or abolition would destroy the signal's immediacy.

cscp.quiz_title: CSCP (Certified Supply Chain Professional) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Absolute forecast errors over four months were 15, 10, 10 and 15 units. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?

answers.text: 10 units
17.5 units
12.5 units
15 units

questions.question: A plant manager asks Zain Malik, who runs supply chain planning, about capacity management basics. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: Capacity planning compares required load to demonstrated capability at each planning level (resource planning for the S&OP horizon, rough-cut for the master schedule, detailed CRP for MRP) — overloads are resolved by changing capacity, changing the plan, or both, not by releasing orders earlier
Demonstrated capacity means the rated maximum in the equipment manual
CRP is used at the S&OP level of planning
Releasing orders earlier increases a work center's capacity

questions.explanation: Load versus demonstrated capability, level by level — and paper releases create no capacity.

questions.question: Sage Kowalski is a supply chain manager at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about make-or-buy analysis. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Only direct production costs belong in a make-or-buy comparison
Outsourcing always reduces total cost
Strategic importance is irrelevant to make-or-buy

Make-or-buy compares the full internal cost and strategic value of making (control, capability, capacity use) against buying (supplier economics, focus, flexibility), including hidden costs and risks on both sides — core, differentiating capabilities are the hardest to justify outsourcing

questions.explanation: Compare full costs and strategic consequences; what differentiates you is rarely what you hand away.

questions.question: A plant manager asks Zain Malik, who runs supply chain planning, about warehousing functions and types. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: Warehouses do more than store: they consolidate and break bulk, cross-dock, postpone and customize, and buffer supply against demand; distribution centers emphasize flow-through speed while storage warehouses emphasize holding — the network role decides the design
Warehousing adds no value beyond storage
Cross-docking means storing goods for long periods
A distribution center's main function is long-term storage

questions.explanation: Storage is one job of a warehouse; flow, mixing, and finishing are the others.

questions.question: Annual demand is 6,250 units, ordering cost is $40 per order, and annual holding cost is $2 per unit. What is the economic order quantity?

answers.text: 354 units
500 units
550 units
460 units

questions.question: Nadia Petrov works in supply chain management for a regional distributor in Memphis and is reviewing the bullwhip effect. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: Larger order batches reduce the bullwhip effect

Small changes in end-customer demand amplify as orders move upstream (retailer to distributor to manufacturer to supplier) because of batching, lead times, forecast updating, and shortage gaming — causing excess inventory and capacity swings at the upstream end; sharing true demand data and smoothing ordering dampen it
Bullwhip is caused by customers changing their minds too often
The bullwhip effect means end demand is always the most volatile

questions.explanation: Amplification upstream is an information and policy problem — visibility and smoother ordering are the countermeasures.

questions.question: Wanda Kaczmarek is a supply chain manager at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about the role of inventory — and its costs. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: Holding cost is only the warehouse rent
Higher inventory always improves profitability
Inventory is a free asset once purchased

Inventory exists to decouple supply from demand, buffer variability, and protect service — but it carries holding costs (capital, storage, insurance, obsolescence, shrinkage, typically a substantial annual percentage of item value) and hides problems, so inventory policy is an explicit service-versus-cost decision

questions.explanation: Buffers are bought with carrying cost; the policy question is how much service that money should buy.

questions.question: A plant manager asks Wren Castellano, who runs supply chain planning, about sustainability in supply chain design. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Sustainable practices never reduce cost
Sustainability concerns only the firm's own facilities
Product end-of-life is outside supply chain responsibility

Sustainable supply chain practice integrates environmental and social criteria into sourcing, design, logistics, and end-of-life management (emissions, waste, circularity, labor standards) — increasingly a customer, regulatory, and risk requirement, and often aligned with cost through waste and energy reduction

questions.explanation: From sourcing to end-of-life, with cost synergies where waste falls — sustainability is a design criterion, not a brochure.

questions.question: Wanda Kaczmarek is a supply chain manager at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about early-warning and risk monitoring. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Material risks are monitored with leading indicators and event intelligence (supplier financial health, port congestion, weather, geopolitical signals) tied to playbooks that trigger action early — monitoring without pre-agreed triggers produces informed spectators, not resilience
Supplier financial distress is not a supply risk signal
Playbooks should be written after an event occurs
Annual risk reviews are sufficient monitoring for critical suppliers

questions.explanation: Signals, thresholds, playbooks — monitoring earns its cost only when it moves decisions earlier.

questions.question: Greta Johansson is a supply chain manager at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about reverse logistics — the returns flow. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: All returned products should be scrapped
Returns have no effect on customer loyalty or margin
Reverse logistics is the same process as outbound distribution run backward without changes

Reverse logistics manages returns, repairs, refurbishment, resale, recycling, and disposal of products moving backward from customers — designed deliberately (clear policies, disposition rules, recovery value), it protects margin and compliance instead of being an unplanned cost sink

questions.explanation: The backward flow carries value and risk; disposition discipline decides which one dominates.

questions.question: Greta Johansson is a supply chain manager at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about channel relationships and conflict. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: Adding a direct channel never affects distributor relationships

Distribution channels (distributors, wholesalers, retailers, direct) each add value and margin; channel conflict arises when routes compete (for example direct sales undercutting distributors) and is managed by clear role definition, pricing discipline, and differentiated offers
Channel members add cost but no value in all cases
Price undercutting partners is a sustainable growth strategy

questions.explanation: Every channel must earn its margin by adding value — and the routes must not be set against each other.

questions.question: During an operations review in Duluth, Owen Gallagher raises the topic of supplier performance management. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Performance data should come from each party's separate records
Scorecards are mainly a tool for punishing suppliers annually

Supplier performance is managed through agreed metrics (quality, on-time delivery, cost, responsiveness), regular scorecards and business reviews, corrective action for gaps, and development or exit for persistent failure — measured jointly, from shared data
A supplier meeting minimum price needs no performance review

questions.explanation: Measure jointly, review regularly, fix or exit deliberately — performance is managed, not hoped for.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Bangor, Bruno Ferreira — the supply chain lead — is handling a question on service recovery and complaint handling. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Complaints should be routed away from operations to protect focus
Customers who complain are usually lost regardless of response
Compensation alone, without root-cause correction, is complete recovery

Service failures are inevitable; recovery quality (speed, ownership, fair remedy, and root-cause correction) determines whether the customer relationship survives — and complaint data are a free quality signal the supply chain should mine systematically

questions.explanation: Recover fast and fairly, then fix the cause — a complaint handled well can bind tighter than no failure at all.

questions.question: During an operations review in Tucson, Zoe Lindqvist raises the topic of supply chain performance measurement — SCOR-type thinking. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Supply chain performance is assessed across reliability (perfect order), responsiveness (cycle time), agility (flexibility and adaptability), cost, and asset efficiency (turns, cash-to-cash cycle) — and improving one attribute at the expense of the others without seeing the trade-off is how dashboards mislead
Cash-to-cash cycle is a customer service metric
Responsiveness and reliability are the same attribute
The SCOR perspective measures only supply chain cost

questions.explanation: Reliable, responsive, agile, cheap, asset-light — pick your position knowing you cannot max all five.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Savannah, Drew Bennett — the supply chain lead — is handling a question on business continuity planning. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Recovery time objectives are set by the IT department alone
Continuity plans need no testing if well documented
Continuity planning applies only to natural disasters

Continuity planning identifies critical processes, their recovery time objectives, alternate sites/suppliers/systems, and communication plans, and tests them through exercises — an untested plan is a hypothesis, and recovery objectives must be set by business impact, not convenience

questions.explanation: Impact sets the recovery clock; exercises prove the plan can beat it.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Fresno, Logan Pierce — the supply chain lead — is handling a question on information flow and visibility. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Information sharing increases the bullwhip effect

End-to-end visibility — shared, timely data on orders, inventory, and shipments across partners (through EDI, portals, or shared systems) — is what lets a global network react to disruption and demand change as one system instead of a chain of surprises
Visibility means each partner keeps better internal records
Visibility is only a customer-service feature

questions.explanation: A network can only coordinate what it can see; shared data is the nervous system.

questions.question: Nadia Petrov works in supply chain management for a regional distributor in Memphis and is reviewing capacity management basics. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Capacity planning compares required load to demonstrated capability at each planning level (resource planning for the S&OP horizon, rough-cut for the master schedule, detailed CRP for MRP) — overloads are resolved by changing capacity, changing the plan, or both, not by releasing orders earlier
Releasing orders earlier increases a work center's capacity
CRP is used at the S&OP level of planning
Demonstrated capacity means the rated maximum in the equipment manual

questions.explanation: Load versus demonstrated capability, level by level — and paper releases create no capacity.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Tucson, Tatum Herrera — the supply chain lead — is handling a question on supplier relationship management (SRM). Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: SRM applies segmentation and structured engagement to the supply base — governance, joint improvement, innovation access, and risk monitoring concentrated on strategic suppliers — mirroring CRM on the buy side
All suppliers receive identical governance under SRM
SRM means negotiating harder with every supplier annually
SRM is the purchasing department's filing system

questions.explanation: CRM's discipline pointed upstream: segment, govern, improve together where it matters.

questions.question: Chiamaka Eze, a supply chain professional supporting operations, must apply the correct practice for total cost of ownership in sourcing. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Quality failure costs are excluded from TCO
TCO analysis applies only to capital equipment
TCO equals the invoice price plus freight

Total cost of ownership counts acquisition price plus ordering, transport, duty, carrying, quality failure, administration, and disposal costs over the item's life — a higher-priced local supplier can be the lower-TCO choice once freight, inventory, and defect costs are counted

questions.explanation: The invoice is the visible tip; TCO prices the whole iceberg.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Boise, Logan Pierce — the supply chain lead — is handling a question on factors in global facility location. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Global location analysis weighs labor and productivity, logistics infrastructure, trade rules and tariffs, tax and incentives, political and currency risk, proximity to suppliers and markets, and the ability to staff skills — low wage rates alone routinely lose to total-cost analysis
Currency risk does not affect location decisions
The lowest-wage country is the correct location choice
Tariffs are irrelevant if labor is cheap

questions.explanation: Wages are one line of a landed-cost and risk ledger, not the decision.

cpim.quiz_title: CPIM (Certified in Planning and Inventory Management) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A plant manager asks Mateo Rossi, who runs production planning, about supply chain risk in strategy. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: Single sourcing everything is the strategic optimum

Strategic planning treats supply risk explicitly — mapping critical dependencies, weighing resilience investments (buffers, dual sources, postponement) against their cost, and maintaining continuity plans for the flows the business cannot afford to lose
Continuity planning is an operations detail outside strategy
Resilience investments are pure cost with no strategic role

questions.explanation: Strategy prices the bad day in advance and buys exactly the resilience the critical flows need.

questions.question: During an operations review in Savannah, Jamie Carter raises the topic of choosing a forecasting technique. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Regression is a judgmental technique

Technique follows pattern and horizon: naive and moving averages for level demand, trend methods (regression, trend-adjusted smoothing) when a trend is real, seasonal indices multiplied onto deseasonalized forecasts for seasonal products, and causal models when a driver (price, promotions, housing starts) genuinely moves demand
Seasonal demand is forecast best by ignoring the seasonal component
One technique should be used for all products to keep planning consistent

questions.explanation: Diagnose the pattern first — level, trend, seasonal, causal — then pick the tool built for it.

questions.question: In cycle counting, 380 of 400 counted records prove accurate within tolerance. What is the inventory record accuracy?
questions.explanation: Accuracy = 380 / 400 x 100 = 95 percent.

questions.question: During an operations review in Tampa, Owen Gallagher raises the topic of push versus pull distribution. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: Push and pull describe manufacturing scheduling only
Pull allocation is best when a scarce product must be rationed

Push distribution allocates central stock to locations by forecast or fair-share rules (effective for promotions and scarce supply); pull distribution lets locations draw by their own replenishment logic (responsive to local demand) — most networks mix them by product and situation
Fair-share allocation ignores current local stock

questions.explanation: Allocate centrally when supply is scarce or promoted; let locations pull when local signals rule.

questions.question: During an operations review in Savannah, Owen Gallagher raises the topic of choosing a forecasting technique. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Seasonal demand is forecast best by ignoring the seasonal component

Technique follows pattern and horizon: naive and moving averages for level demand, trend methods (regression, trend-adjusted smoothing) when a trend is real, seasonal indices multiplied onto deseasonalized forecasts for seasonal products, and causal models when a driver (price, promotions, housing starts) genuinely moves demand
Regression is a judgmental technique
One technique should be used for all products to keep planning consistent

questions.explanation: Diagnose the pattern first — level, trend, seasonal, causal — then pick the tool built for it.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Austin, Ximena Torres — the planning manager — is handling a question on the push-pull boundary. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: The boundary cannot move once chosen

The push-pull boundary (decoupling point) is where a product stops being built to forecast (push) and starts being completed against actual orders (pull): make-to-stock places it at finished goods, assemble-to-order at components, make-to-order at raw materials, and engineer-to-order at design
Engineer-to-order completes products entirely to forecast
Make-to-stock places the decoupling point at raw materials

questions.explanation: Where forecast hands over to orders — the single most consequential positioning choice in a supply chain.

questions.question: Priya Nair is a production planner at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about product life cycle and demand planning. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Decline-phase replenishment carries no special risk
Maturity demand is the hardest to forecast

Demand behavior follows the life cycle: introduction (low, erratic, judgment-led forecasts), growth (trend methods, capacity risk), maturity (stable, seasonal, statistical forecasting at its best), and decline (falling trend, obsolescence risk on every replenishment decision)
Statistical forecasting works best at product introduction

questions.explanation: The life cycle tells you how much to trust the data and how much inventory risk each order carries.

questions.question: Amara Diallo is a production planner at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about managing supplier disruption with buffers. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: External supply risk is buffered deliberately: safety stock for variable lead times, qualified second sources for critical items, contractual flexibility (surge capacity, expedite terms), and supplier financial monitoring — sized by the cost of the stockout, not by habit
Penalty clauses deliver parts during a supplier's outage
Buffers for purchased items are unnecessary if contracts have penalty clauses
A second source needs no qualification until the disruption occurs

questions.explanation: Contracts allocate blame; buffers and qualified alternates deliver parts.

questions.question: A plant manager asks Tara O'Brien, who runs production planning, about takt time and line pacing. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Takt is computed from the total calendar time including breaks and downtime not worked

Takt time equals available production time divided by the customer demand in that period — the drumbeat every station must meet; a station slower than takt starves the line's output no matter how fast the others run
Takt time rises when customer demand rises
Takt time is set by the fastest machine's cycle time

questions.explanation: Demand sets the beat: available time over required units. Balance the line to it.

questions.question: Kai Watanabe is a production planner at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about the elements of manufacturing lead time. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: Lead time consists only of setup plus run
Queue time decreases as more work is released to the floor
Run time is the largest element of lead time in most plants

Manufacturing lead time is queue (waiting before setup), setup, run, wait (after completion, before move), and move time — and in most shops queue dominates, which is why lead time falls when WIP and lot sizes fall, not when run speeds rise

questions.explanation: The order spends its life waiting; shrink the pile and you shrink the lead time.

questions.question: During an operations review in Austin, Jesse Alvarez raises the topic of statistical process control — common versus special causes. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: SPC distinguishes common-cause variation (the process's natural noise, addressed by process improvement) from special-cause variation (assignable events, addressed by finding and removing the event); reacting to common-cause noise as if it were special (tampering) makes variation worse
Control limits are the customer's specification limits
Every out-of-trend point requires operator adjustment
A process in control is necessarily capable of meeting specifications

questions.explanation: In control is not the same as capable — and adjusting a stable process is how good parts go bad.

questions.question: Greta Johansson is a production planner at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about lot-sizing techniques compared. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: EOQ-based lots ignore carrying cost
Lot-for-lot minimizes the number of orders placed
Period order quantity orders a fixed number of units each time

Lot-for-lot orders exactly the net requirement (minimal inventory, most orders); fixed order quantity uses a set amount such as an EOQ; period order quantity covers a fixed number of periods' requirements; part-period balancing and least-unit-cost refine the trade between ordering and carrying cost

questions.explanation: Every lot rule trades setups against stock; the item's cost and demand pattern pick the winner.

questions.question: Elif Yilmaz works in planning and inventory management for a regional manufacturer in Burlington and is reviewing strategic buffers in S&OP. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A buffer is the same as forecast error

S&OP sets deliberate strategic buffers — inventory, capacity, or time — sized to the uncertainty of each family, and reviews them as conditions change; buffers are policy decisions with named owners, not accidents of overproduction
Buffers should be eliminated to make the plan lean
Buffer policy is set once and never reviewed

questions.explanation: A buffer you chose and sized is strategy; a buffer that accumulated is waste.

questions.question: Umar Farouk works in planning and inventory management for a regional manufacturer in Salem and is reviewing rough-cut capacity planning (RCCP). Which statement is correct?

answers.text: RCCP validates the MPS against critical resources using bills of capacity or resource profiles (standard hours per unit by work center), flagging overloads while there is still time to change the schedule, the capacity, or the promise — before MRP generates thousands of dependent orders
Overloads found by RCCP are resolved by MRP automatically
RCCP runs after MRP has released all planned orders
RCCP validates every work order in detail

questions.explanation: Check the critical few resources against the master schedule early, in aggregate hours.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Madison, Ximena Torres — the planning manager — is handling a question on lot-sizing techniques compared. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Lot-for-lot minimizes the number of orders placed

Lot-for-lot orders exactly the net requirement (minimal inventory, most orders); fixed order quantity uses a set amount such as an EOQ; period order quantity covers a fixed number of periods' requirements; part-period balancing and least-unit-cost refine the trade between ordering and carrying cost
Period order quantity orders a fixed number of units each time
EOQ-based lots ignore carrying cost

questions.explanation: Every lot rule trades setups against stock; the item's cost and demand pattern pick the winner.

questions.question: Quinn Adams, a materials planner supporting production, must apply the correct practice for managing backorders and backlog. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Backlog (all unfilled orders) and backorders (the overdue portion) are managed by explicit priority rules, honest promise dates, and root-cause work on the stockouts creating them — silently re-promising dates destroys the credibility every other plan depends on
Backorders have no effect on demand planning data
Re-promising without changing supply restores service
Backlog and backorder are identical terms

questions.explanation: Promise honestly, prioritize explicitly, fix the cause — backlog is a service debt with interest.

questions.question: Lena Fischer is a production planner at a mid-sized manufacturer and is asked about capacity requirements planning (CRP). Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: CRP and RCCP are the same technique at different names
CRP uses only forecast data
CRP validates the aggregate production plan

CRP explodes planned and open orders through routings to compute detailed load by work center and period; unlike RCCP it uses actual order quantities and due dates, and its output (load profiles) drives overtime, alternate routing, or schedule changes

questions.explanation: RCCP checks the master schedule with profiles; CRP loads the real orders, center by center.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Des Moines, Ximena Torres — the planning manager — is handling a question on the purpose and cadence of S&OP. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: S&OP plans individual SKUs week by week
S&OP's output is a statistical forecast

S&OP runs monthly at the product-family level, stepping through demand review, supply review, and an executive reconciliation that produces one plan in units and money — its product is decisions (what to make, buy, staff, and promise), not a forecast
S&OP meets only when a crisis occurs

questions.explanation: Families, monthly, one plan, executive-owned decisions — the rest is detail.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Des Moines, Ximena Torres — the planning manager — is handling a question on nearshoring, offshoring, and reshoring in planning. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: Unit price is the correct sole criterion for sourcing location
Lead-time variability does not affect inventory cost
Reshoring is always the lowest total cost option

Location sourcing decisions weigh unit cost against lead time and its variability, pipeline inventory, responsiveness, and disruption risk — a cheaper unit price with a twelve-week variable lead time can cost more in safety stock and stockouts than it saves

questions.explanation: Planners price lead time and variability, not just the unit — distance is an inventory decision.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Tampa, Rosa Delgado — the planning manager — is handling a question on SMED and 5S in planning terms. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: SMED converts internal setup work (done while stopped) to external work (done while running) and streamlines the rest, cutting changeover time and therefore economic lot sizes; 5S workplace organization removes search and motion waste — both enlarge planning's feasible set: smaller lots, faster response
5S is a housekeeping campaign unrelated to planning
Shorter setups make larger lots more economical
SMED aims to eliminate the need for any setup work whatsoever

questions.explanation: Cut the changeover and the lot size follows — setup reduction is a planning-degree-of-freedom.

florida-community-association-manager.quiz_title: Florida Community Association Manager (CAM) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A plant manager asks Finley Ross, who manages several Florida associations, about when a CAM license is required. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: A Florida CAM license is required when a person is paid to manage a community association that has more than 10 units or an annual budget over $100,000 — the license attaches to compensated management services such as handling association funds, preparing budgets, and giving meeting notices
Anyone who manages any Florida rental property needs a CAM license
A license is required only for associations with more than 100 units
Volunteer board members managing their own association without pay need a CAM license

questions.explanation: More than 10 units or over $100,000 in budget, for pay — that is the licensing trigger.

questions.question: A monthly assessment of $350 is increased by 15 percent. What is the new monthly assessment?
questions.explanation: New assessment = $350 x 115 percent = $402.

questions.question: During an operations review in Tucson, Omar Haddad raises the topic of return of records and funds at termination. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: When a management contract ends or is terminated, the manager must promptly return all association funds, official records, and property in their possession and may not withhold them over a fee dispute — the association's records belong to the association, not to the manager
A manager may hold records until all disputed invoices are paid
Copies may be kept and originals destroyed at contract end
Return of property is due within one year of termination

questions.explanation: At the door, everything goes back — promptly, completely, and without ransom.

questions.question: During an operations review in Bangor, Robin Hughes raises the topic of fines and the hearing committee. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The fining committee may consist of the board's own members
The board may fine an owner and lien the unit in a condominium once the fine exceeds $1,000
No hearing is required if the violation is documented photographically

Before a fine or suspension may be imposed, the owner must receive notice and an opportunity for a hearing before a committee of owners who are not board members or their household members; the committee must approve the fine, and in a condominium a fine may not become a lien, while in an HOA a fine of $1,000 or more may become a lien

questions.explanation: Notice, hearing, independent committee — and the condo/HOA lien difference is a bright line.

questions.question: Marley Cohen, a community association manager, must apply the correct practice for competitive bidding thresholds. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: Bidding is required only for contracts over $100,000
Bids are never required because the board has contracting authority
Attorney and accountant engagements are subject to the same bid rule as landscaping

For contracts for goods or services exceeding the statutory percentage of the association's total annual budget (including reserves) — 5 percent for both condominiums and HOAs — the association must obtain competitive bids, subject to exceptions such as emergencies, sole-source items, and licensed professional services

questions.explanation: Five percent of the budget including reserves triggers the bid rule — with named exceptions, not vibes.

questions.question: Chiamaka Eze, a community association manager, must apply the correct practice for fair housing in association management. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: An association may enforce a no-pets rule against an assistance animal
Reasonable accommodation requests may be denied for paperwork defects in all cases
Familial status is not a protected class in Florida community associations

Federal fair housing law prohibits discrimination in housing based on race, color, religion, sex, handicap (disability), familial status, and national origin — managers must apply rules uniformly, grant reasonable accommodations for disabilities (such as assigned parking or assistance animals despite a no-pet rule), and avoid steering or selective enforcement

questions.explanation: Seven protected classes, uniform enforcement, and real accommodations — fair housing is daily CAM law.

questions.question: Wanda Kaczmarek is a newly licensed CAM at a Florida management firm and is asked about statutory reserves — condominiums. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: Reserves are optional line items the board may include or omit freely
Reserve funding may be waived by the board alone without an owner vote
Reserve accounts may be spent on operating shortfalls without owner approval

Condominium budgets must include reserves for capital expenditures and deferred maintenance — roof replacement, building painting, pavement resurfacing, and any other item with a cost or deferred cost over the statutory threshold — computed by the statutory formula, unless the owners vote to waive or reduce them as the statute allows (with post-Surfside structural reserves non-waivable for covered buildings)

questions.explanation: Formula-funded reserves for the big-ticket items; waivers belong to the owners, and structural reserves for taller buildings can no longer be waived away.

questions.question: Emerson Clark, a community association manager, must apply the correct practice for unit owner insurance responsibilities. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: Loss assessment coverage reimburses owners for the association's regular budget shortfalls

In a condominium the unit owner typically carries an HO-6 style policy for the portions of the unit the association does not insure (flooring, fixtures within the unit as allocated, personal property, and loss assessment coverage) — the manager must be able to explain the boundary because post-loss fights start exactly there
The association insures owners' personal property inside units
Unit owners need no insurance because the association insures everything

questions.explanation: Association policy, owner policy, and a statutory boundary between them — know where the line runs.

questions.question: Yuki Tanaka, a community association manager, must apply the correct practice for association powers — assessments and liens. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Associations have no lien rights; all collections are unsecured
Assessment authority exists only if each owner individually consents each year
An association may lien an owner's unit based only on an oral promise to pay

Associations derive their power to assess owners, and to lien and foreclose for unpaid assessments, from the statutes and their recorded documents; the association's lien for unpaid assessments is a continuing lien that relates back to the recording of the declaration

questions.explanation: Assessment power is statutory and documentary — and the lien reaches back to the declaration.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Des Moines, Logan Pierce — the senior CAM — is handling a question on estoppel certificates. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: The association may disclaim the amounts stated in its own certificate
An association has 30 days to issue an estoppel certificate
Estoppels are optional courtesies the manager may decline to issue

When a unit or parcel is sold, the association must furnish an estoppel certificate within 10 business days after receiving a written or electronic request, stating the amounts owed; the certificate binds the association as to the amounts stated, and the fee the association may charge is capped by statute

questions.explanation: Ten business days, statutorily capped fee, and the association lives with the numbers it certifies.

questions.question: A plant manager asks Zain Malik, who manages several Florida associations, about maintenance responsibilities — common elements. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: Unit owners maintain the roof and structural components in a condominium
Maintenance duties are identical regardless of the declaration
Deferring all maintenance is a lawful budget strategy without consequence

In a condominium, the association maintains the common elements and association property, while unit owners maintain their units and limited common elements as the declaration allocates; the manager's job is to inventory the obligations, fund them through the budget and reserves, and document inspections and repairs

questions.explanation: The declaration allocates it, the budget funds it, the manager calendar drives it.

questions.question: Morgan Ellis is a newly licensed CAM at a Florida management firm and is asked about statutory reserves — condominiums. Which advice is correct?

answers.text: Reserve funding may be waived by the board alone without an owner vote

Condominium budgets must include reserves for capital expenditures and deferred maintenance — roof replacement, building painting, pavement resurfacing, and any other item with a cost or deferred cost over the statutory threshold — computed by the statutory formula, unless the owners vote to waive or reduce them as the statute allows (with post-Surfside structural reserves non-waivable for covered buildings)
Reserve accounts may be spent on operating shortfalls without owner approval
Reserves are optional line items the board may include or omit freely

questions.explanation: Formula-funded reserves for the big-ticket items; waivers belong to the owners, and structural reserves for taller buildings can no longer be waived away.

questions.question: Nia Thompson works as a licensed CAM for associations in Florida in Provo and is reviewing official records access — condominiums. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: Personnel records and privileged attorney communications are as open as financial records

A condominium association must make its official records available to an owner (or their authorized representative) for inspection and copying within 5 business days after receiving a written request, during reasonable business hours, at the association's records location
Owners may inspect records only at the annual meeting
Records access may be delayed up to 30 days at the manager's discretion

questions.explanation: Five business days, written request, reasonable hours — with privileged and protected categories withheld by law.

questions.question: Cameron Ortiz is a newly licensed CAM at a Florida management firm and is asked about fidelity bonding for those who handle funds. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Fidelity bonding is optional for managers who are individually licensed
The bond amount is fixed at $10,000 by statute
Fidelity bonds cover property damage from storms

An association must obtain and maintain fidelity bonding (insurance) covering every person who controls or disburses association funds — including the manager — in an amount not less than the maximum funds in that person's custody at any time

questions.explanation: Whoever touches the money is bonded, up to the most they could touch — fidelity is the embezzlement backstop.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Savannah, Drew Bennett — the senior CAM — is handling a question on grounds for discipline of a CAM. What is the correct rule?

answers.text: Minor bookkeeping sloppiness can never be a disciplinary matter

A CAM's license may be disciplined for fraud, deceit, gross negligence, incompetence, or misconduct in practice — including misusing association funds, failing to account for money and property, and violating the governing statutes and rules
Discipline is handled by the association's board rather than the Department
A licensee may be disciplined only after a criminal conviction

questions.explanation: Fraud, deceit, negligence, incompetence, misconduct — and mishandling the association's money sits at the center.

questions.question: Nina Petrova, a community association manager, must apply the correct practice for annual financial reporting tiers. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Every association must obtain a full audit regardless of revenue
The reporting level is chosen freely by the manager each year
Financial reports are prepared for the board only and never shared with owners

Each year the association must prepare a financial report whose required level of rigor scales with total annual revenue — from a report of cash receipts and expenditures at the lowest revenues, through compiled and reviewed statements, to a full audit at the highest tier — and must deliver it (or notice of its availability) to owners within the statutory period

questions.explanation: Revenue sets the rigor: report, compilation, review, audit — and owners get it on the statutory clock.

questions.question: At a distribution operation in Richmond, Hassan Iqbal — the senior CAM — is handling a question on open board meetings (sunshine). Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Meetings with the association's attorney about litigation may never be closed

Board meetings at which association business is conducted must be open to the members, who have the right to speak on agenda items; narrow exceptions allow closed sessions for consultation with the association's attorney about proposed or pending litigation and for personnel matters
Boards may close any meeting by majority vote
