Move on quickly when several learners appear confused to protect the schedule, and revisit the point only if it appears on the assessment consistent with how the program documents and reviews its own performance for the reasons recorded in the program's planning and review documentation in the ordinary course of professional SH&E training practice at a well-run program as part of the training standards the instructional trainer is accountable for upholding

questions.explanation: Clarifying confusion and de-escalating conflict respectfully restores conditions for learning.

bcsp-stsc-safety-trained-supervisor-cons.quiz_title: BCSP Safety Trained Supervisor Construction (STSC) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Nina Petrova must identify the correct statement about documenting inspection findings and follow-up. The crew concerned is new to this area of the site. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: When an inspection finds a hazard, the supervisor mentions it verbally in passing and keeps no written record, trusting memory to track the fix even across shift changes, subcontractor handoffs, and several days of competing production priorities.

When an inspection finds a hazard, the supervisor records what was found, where it is, who owns the fix, and when it is due, then verifies the correction was actually completed rather than trusting that an assignment alone closed the item.

When an inspection finds a hazard, the supervisor documents only the hazards that were easy to fix that day, and leaves serious or expensive findings off the record so the inspection report looks clean for the project file for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

When an inspection finds a hazard, the supervisor marks the item closed as soon as any worker says it will be handled later, without returning to the location to verify the correction was completed and remains effective during work as part of the practice expected of a construction supervisor

questions.explanation: Written findings with an owner, a due date, and verified closure are what turn inspections into corrections.

questions.question: During a coordination meeting in Richmond, Jordan Lee raises the topic of deck openings and edge protection. The discussion follows a busy week on the job site. What is the correct approach?

answers.text: The supervisor ensures floor and roof openings are covered with secured, clearly marked covers or protected by guardrails, and verifies edges where work occurs have guardrails, safety nets, or personal fall protection in place before the crew starts work at height.

Guardrails can be removed for an entire shift while materials are being delivered to the floor, as long as the crew working that floor is experienced and aware the rails are temporarily down for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation in the ordinary course of front-line supervision on a well-run construction site

An opening may be left uncovered during active material loading if a worker stands nearby to warn others verbally, because covers slow the hoisting cycle and warnings are considered equivalent protection as part of the safety standards the work-group leader is accountable for upholding

Plywood laid loosely over an opening without fastening or marking is sufficient protection, since its weight alone will keep it in place and workers will recognize it as a cover by its appearance for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

questions.explanation: Secured covers and continuous edge protection prevent workers and materials from falling through openings or off unprotected edges.

questions.question: Nina Petrova, a crew leader on a concrete structure crew, is asked about housekeeping for access and egress. The supervisor is covering the site while a colleague is away. What is the correct approach?

answers.text: The supervisor keeps walkways, stairs, and work areas free of scrap, cords, and stored materials, requires prompt cleanup of debris and spills, provides containers for waste, and treats blocked exits or cluttered access routes as hazards to correct the same shift they are found.

Scrap and offcuts may accumulate in a corner of the work area until the end of the week, when a dedicated cleanup crew clears everything at once to avoid interrupting daily production tasks under the safety program the organization has committed itself to follow in accordance with the site's documented safety program and the supervisor's duties

Materials may be staged temporarily in stairwells and exit routes during deliveries, because workers know the site layout and can step around stored items even in low light or an emergency evacuation in the ordinary course of front-line supervision on a well-run construction site

Extension cords crossing walkways need no covers or elevation for short jobs, since the crew working that area is aware of them and visitors are expected to watch their step throughout the site in accordance with the site's documented safety program and the supervisor's duties as reviewed during crew briefings and department safety meetings

questions.explanation: Continuous housekeeping prevents the trips, falls, and blocked escape routes that cluttered construction areas reliably produce.

questions.question: Stefan Braun must identify the correct statement about respirator use beyond handing out masks. The crew concerned is new to this area of the site. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Before assigning respirators, the supervisor allows workers to share respirators during a shift without cleaning between users, reasoning that the filter does the protecting and the facepiece itself needs no hygiene attention at all in the interest of worker safety and health on every shift the crew works

Before assigning respirators, the supervisor buys one size in bulk and hands it to every worker, assuming a tight strap pull guarantees a proper seal regardless of face shape, size, or facial hair interfering with the edges for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

Before assigning respirators, the supervisor skips fit testing for experienced workers because years on the job are treated as proof that any respirator they choose will protect them adequately during dusty operations on site as part of the safety standards the work-group leader is accountable for upholding

Before assigning respirators, the supervisor ensures each user is medically able to wear one, is fit tested for the specific model and size, is trained in its use and limits, and shaves or adjusts facial hair so the seal is not broken.

questions.explanation: A respirator protects only when the wearer can use it safely and the facepiece seals properly every time.

questions.question: Taylor Brooks must identify the correct statement about flammable liquid storage on construction sites. A crew member has asked for guidance on the standard. What is the correct approach?

answers.text: The supervisor allows unlimited quantities of flammable liquids to accumulate at each work area to reduce trips to storage, reasoning that scattered placement is safer than a single designated controlled storage location on the construction site consistent with how the crew documents and reviews its own performance

The supervisor stores spare solvent and fuel containers inside the stairwell and exit corridor because the space is shaded and convenient, even though a fire there would block the crews primary escape route from the floor for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

The supervisor stores gasoline for equipment in open buckets near the work face for convenient refueling throughout the day, assuming an open container is no different from an approved closed container as long as smoking is discouraged nearby as reviewed during crew briefings and department safety meetings

The supervisor stores flammable liquids in approved closed containers kept in a designated area away from ignition sources and exits, limits the quantity at the work face to what the task needs, and ensures bonding and grounding practice is followed during dispensing where required.

questions.explanation: Approved containers, controlled quantities, and separation from ignition and exits keep a small leak from becoming a major fire.

questions.question: Quinn Adams, a foreman on a commercial building project, double-checks the practice standard for leading toolbox talks that change field behavior. The case involves a crew in the first weeks of a new project phase. What is the correct approach?

answers.text: An effective toolbox talk is brief, focused on a hazard the crew will actually face that day, delivered in language the crew understands, invites worker input and questions, and ends with clear expectations the supervisor reinforces during the shift.

An effective toolbox talk is delivered only to document compliance after an incident has occurred, rather than as a routine start-of-shift practice tied to the hazards, weather, and tasks the crew is about to perform in accordance with the site's documented safety program and the supervisor's duties

An effective toolbox talk reads a generic printed topic word for word regardless of the days actual work, takes no questions to save time, and collects signatures as the only evidence that any communication took place that morning because the standard exists to prevent injuries and illnesses before they occur

An effective toolbox talk covers as many unrelated topics as possible in one long session at the start of the project, so the supervisor does not need to hold further talks when new hazards appear in later phases in the ordinary course of front-line supervision on a well-run construction site

questions.explanation: Toolbox talks work when they are timely, relevant, interactive, and reinforced in the field during the shift.

questions.question: Paulina Wojcik, a foreman on a renovation project in an occupied building, is asked about excavation cave-in warning signs. A crew member has asked for guidance on the standard. Which action is most appropriate?

answers.text: Minor cracks behind the trench edge are treated as normal settling and work continues while the crew keeps an eye on them, stopping only if a large amount of soil actually falls into the excavation consistent with how the crew documents and reviews its own performance

Seeping water is pumped out by a worker standing in the trench while digging continues around him, because brief exposure during cleanup is considered part of normal excavation work consistent with how the crew documents and reviews its own performance for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

When the supervisor sees tension cracks behind the trench edge, slumping soil, bulging at the base, or water seeping into the excavation, work stops and workers leave the trench until the competent person evaluates the protective system and conditions again.

Bulging at the trench base is pushed back into place with a shovel by the nearest worker so the crew can finish the current run of pipe before the competent person is called over in the ordinary course of front-line supervision on a well-run construction site

questions.explanation: Cracks, slumping, bulging, and water are recognized precursors to cave-ins, so work must stop before soil movement becomes a collapse.

questions.question: Cameron Ortiz, a crew leader on a concrete structure crew in Memphis, is consulted on struck-by hazard control in work areas. The supervisor is covering the site while a colleague is away. Which action is most appropriate?

answers.text: The supervisor controls struck-by exposure by securing tools and materials at height, keeping workers clear of loads and moving equipment, requiring hard hats where overhead work occurs, and coordinating simultaneous operations so one trade work does not endanger another below or beside it.

Simultaneous work on multiple levels of the same elevation needs no coordination between foremen, as each crew is responsible only for watching its own materials and movements during its own tasks as part of the safety standards the work-group leader is accountable for upholding under the safety program the organization has committed itself to follow

Workers below overhead operations may continue their tasks if they wear hard hats, because the helmet alone is considered sufficient protection against tools or materials that might fall from the level above in the interest of worker safety and health on every shift the crew works whenever the work is performed within the supervisor's area of responsibility

Tools used at height can rest unsecured on beams and ledges between uses, provided the worker is careful, since tethering every tool slows the work and dropped tools are regarded as rare events as part of the safety standards the work-group leader is accountable for upholding under the safety program the organization has committed itself to follow

questions.explanation: Securing materials, clearing drop zones, and coordinating trades address struck-by events, which helmets alone cannot prevent.

questions.question: Paulina Wojcik, a foreman on a renovation project in an occupied building, double-checks the practice standard for wind chill and wet clothing management. A crew member has asked for guidance on the standard. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: The supervisor accounts for wind chill by using the air temperature alone to plan the day, ignoring wind speed entirely even though strong wind on an elevated deck can cool exposed skin far faster than still air in the ordinary course of front-line supervision on a well-run construction site

The supervisor accounts for dangerous cold by moving all breaks outdoors to the most exposed corner of the site so workers harden to conditions, rather than providing the sheltered warm area cold stress prevention requires as part of the practice expected of a construction supervisor

The supervisor accounts for wind and moisture by shortening exposure during high wind chill, providing a place to change out of wet clothing, rotating crews out of exposed elevated work, and rescheduling non-essential outdoor tasks when conditions become dangerous.

The supervisor accounts for wet clothing by telling crews to keep working in rain-soaked layers until the shift ends, assuming body heat will dry the clothing safely even as moisture accelerates heat loss in cold wind under the safety program the organization has committed itself to follow

questions.explanation: Wind and wetness multiply heat loss, so exposure time, dry clothing, and shelter must be managed together.

questions.question: Wanda Kaczmarek, a foreman on a commercial building project in Burlington, is consulted on solvent use and skin protection. The work covers structural, mechanical, and finishing trades on the same site. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: When painters use solvents daily, the supervisor issues any available cloth gloves because they absorb liquid and keep hands comfortable, assuming the solvent will evaporate before it can affect the skin underneath during a normal shift in the interest of worker safety and health on every shift the crew works

When painters and cleaners use solvents daily, the supervisor selects gloves rated for the specific product in use, provides a place to remove contaminated clothing, and replaces breakthrough-damaged gloves promptly rather than letting crews wash gloves in solvent to reuse them.

When cleaners use solvents daily, the supervisor encourages rinsing bare hands with the solvent itself to remove paint quickly, treating that practice as efficient hygiene rather than repeated skin exposure to a harmful chemical because the standard exists to prevent injuries and illnesses before they occur

When crews use solvents daily, the supervisor keeps one shared pair of chemical gloves at the gang box for everyone, reasoning that occasional barehanded use between turns is too brief to matter for skin protection because the standard exists to prevent injuries and illnesses before they occur

questions.explanation: Solvent-resistant gloves matched to the product prevent skin absorption and dermatitis from repeated daily contact.

questions.question: Nina Petrova, a foreman on a commercial building project in Burlington, is consulted on extinguisher for flammable liquid fires. The case involves a crew in the first weeks of a new project phase. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: For a gasoline spill fire, the supervisor directs a worker to throw buckets of water onto the burning pool, reasoning that water always extinguishes any fire even though it can spread burning fuel across a wider area as reviewed during crew briefings and department safety meetings

For a solvent fire, the supervisor has workers fan the area with plywood sheets to blow the flames out, assuming moving air will extinguish a liquid fire rather than feeding it oxygen and pushing it toward other materials in the interest of worker safety and health on every shift the crew works

For a spill fire involving gasoline, solvents, or other flammable liquids, the supervisor uses an extinguisher suited to liquid fuel fires, avoids spraying so forcefully that burning liquid splashes and spreads, and stops the fuel source only when it can be done safely.

For a flammable liquid fire near a fuel container, the supervisor orders a laborer to carry the burning container outdoors by hand, prioritizing removal of the container over alarm, evacuation, and safe extinguishing from a protected position because the standard exists to prevent injuries and illnesses before they occur

questions.explanation: Liquid fires need the correct agent applied gently, because water and forceful discharge spread burning fuel.

questions.question: Yusuf Rahman, a crew leader on a concrete structure crew in Burlington, is consulted on fair and consistent enforcement of safety rules. The crew concerned is new to this area of the site. Which action is most appropriate?

answers.text: Ethical supervision enforces rules harshly right after an incident for a short period, then lets enforcement fade as production pressure returns, which workers accept as the normal cycle of attention on a busy construction project for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

Ethical supervision enforces safety rules consistently for every worker, trade, and shift, applying the same expectations to high producers, friends, subcontractors, and new hires, because selective enforcement teaches the crew that rules are negotiable for favored people.

Ethical supervision enforces safety rules strictly for new hires but relaxes them for veteran high producers whose experience is trusted, because consistent enforcement with proven workers would feel disrespectful and harm morale on the crew over time as part of the safety standards the work-group leader is accountable for upholding

Ethical supervision overlooks a friends repeated violations to preserve the working relationship, addressing the behavior only if someone outside the crew complains or an incident forces the issue into the open during a formal review consistent with how the crew documents and reviews its own performance

questions.explanation: Consistent enforcement for everyone is what makes safety expectations credible across the whole crew.

questions.question: While preparing for the STSC examination, Vera Sokolov — a general foreman reviewing site safety with the project team — reviews excavation permit and daily soil checks. The team is reviewing the case at its regular morning briefing. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Before workers enter a trench or excavation, the supervisor allows entry while spoil piles sit at the very edge and ladders are placed far apart, reasoning that experienced workers can climb the walls quickly if conditions change for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

Before workers enter a trench or excavation, the supervisor lets the equipment operator decide whether sloping is needed based on how the digging felt, without a competent person inspection or any documented soil classification that morning as part of the practice expected of a construction supervisor

Before workers enter a trench or excavation, the supervisor relies on last weeks inspection because the soil looked stable then, and assumes the same protective system will remain adequate regardless of rain or nearby equipment vibration as part of the practice expected of a construction supervisor

Before workers enter a trench or excavation, the supervisor ensures a competent person has inspected the excavation that day, classified the soil, confirmed protective systems are in place, and checked for water accumulation or changing conditions after any rain event.

questions.explanation: Daily competent person inspection, soil classification, and protective systems must be confirmed before anyone enters an excavation.

questions.question: A project manager asks Marco Silva, a general foreman reviewing site safety with the project team, to confirm the correct standard for trench access and safe worker entry. The team is reviewing the case at its regular morning briefing. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Workers may climb down the trench wall or step on the shoring braces to save time when the ladder is at the far end, as long as they are wearing boots with good tread and someone watches them because the standard exists to prevent injuries and illnesses before they occur

A single ladder at one end of a long trench is considered enough for the whole crew, even when workers are spread out, because moving additional access points would slow production and clutter the work area whenever the work is performed within the supervisor's area of responsibility

The supervisor ensures workers enter and exit the trench using a ladder, ramp, or other safe access placed where workers can reach it quickly, and keeps travel paths inside the trench clear so no one has to climb on protective systems or spoil.

Access equipment is placed outside the protected area of the trench so it does not interfere with digging, and workers cross the unprotected zone quickly at the start and end of each task in the ordinary course of front-line supervision on a well-run construction site

questions.explanation: Safe, readily reachable access prevents falls during entry and allows workers to escape quickly if trench conditions deteriorate.

questions.question: A project manager asks Marco Silva, a general foreman reviewing site safety with the project team, to confirm the correct standard for acclimatization for new and returning workers. The team is reviewing the case at its regular morning briefing. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A supervisor protects new hires and workers returning from time away by gradually increasing their workload and heat exposure over their first days back, pairing them with an experienced buddy, and watching closely for confusion, stumbling, or stopped sweating.

A supervisor protects new workers in heat by keeping them isolated from the main crew so they are not distracted, even though isolation removes the buddy who would notice early confusion or collapse and summon help promptly as part of the practice expected of a construction supervisor

A supervisor protects returning workers by treating a week away as irrelevant and restoring their full workload and full heat exposure on the first morning back, without any buddy observation during the initial days of return in the interest of worker safety and health on every shift the crew works

A supervisor protects new hires in hot weather by assigning them the heaviest tasks on their first day to prove they can handle the job, reasoning that immediate full exposure builds heat tolerance faster than a gradual schedule for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

questions.explanation: Gradual exposure lets the body adjust to heat, and close observation catches workers who are not adjusting safely.

questions.question: While preparing for the STSC examination, Jesse Alvarez — a site supervisor coordinating several trade contractors — reviews utility strike and structural emergency response. The case is being prepared for discussion in a toolbox talk. What is the correct approach?

answers.text: If a utility is struck, the supervisor delays calling emergency services while the project team discusses cost and schedule consequences first, prioritizing notification of management over the immediate safety call responders need to control the hazard in the interest of worker safety and health on every shift the crew works

If sudden cracking and shifting appear in a structure, the supervisor sends workers back in to shore it up immediately without evaluation, assuming quick action by the regular crew is safer than evacuating and waiting for qualified assessment as part of the practice expected of a construction supervisor in the normal course of day-to-day workplace safety practice

If a crew strikes a gas line, the supervisor has workers pinch and tape the line and continue working nearby while a repair is scheduled for later, treating an active gas leak as a routine maintenance issue on the site for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation in the ordinary course of front-line supervision on a well-run construction site

If a crew strikes a gas line, damages a critical utility, or notices sudden cracking, shifting, or partial collapse in a structure, the supervisor stops work, evacuates the affected area upwind and uphill where relevant, eliminates ignition sources safely, and calls emergency services and the utility owner immediately.

questions.explanation: Evacuation and immediate notification keep a utility strike or structural failure from escalating into an explosion or collapse.

questions.question: A project manager asks Robin Hughes, a general foreman reviewing site safety with the project team, to confirm the correct standard for holding paramount the safety of workers and public. The team is reviewing the case at its regular morning briefing. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The guiding commitment of the safety supervisor is to protect experienced workers first and give less attention to visitors and the public near the site, because the crew faces the hazards for the longest hours each day whenever the work is performed within the supervisor's area of responsibility

The guiding commitment of the safety supervisor is to hold the safety, health, and welfare of workers and the public above schedule, cost, and personal advancement, making that priority visible in daily decisions about how work is planned and performed.

The guiding commitment of the safety supervisor is to balance safety equally against schedule in every decision, accepting additional risk whenever a deadline is important enough, because leadership is ultimately judged on delivery above all other outcomes.

The guiding commitment of the safety supervisor is to protect the companys reputation first, on the theory that a strong reputation funds good programs, even if that means downplaying a hazard that could embarrass the project publicly for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

questions.explanation: Safety of people comes before schedule, cost, reputation, and personal interest in a supervisors decisions.

questions.question: While preparing for the STSC examination, Casey Nguyen — a general foreman reviewing site safety with the project team — reviews excavation permit and daily soil checks. The project's safety committee is examining this practice standard. Which of the following is the correct practice?

answers.text: Before workers enter a trench or excavation, the supervisor allows entry while spoil piles sit at the very edge and ladders are placed far apart, reasoning that experienced workers can climb the walls quickly if conditions change whenever the work is performed within the supervisor's area of responsibility

Before workers enter a trench or excavation, the supervisor lets the equipment operator decide whether sloping is needed based on how the digging felt, without a competent person inspection or any documented soil classification that morning as part of the safety standards the work-group leader is accountable for upholding

Before workers enter a trench or excavation, the supervisor relies on last weeks inspection because the soil looked stable then, and assumes the same protective system will remain adequate regardless of rain or nearby equipment vibration whenever the work is performed within the supervisor's area of responsibility

Before workers enter a trench or excavation, the supervisor ensures a competent person has inspected the excavation that day, classified the soil, confirmed protective systems are in place, and checked for water accumulation or changing conditions after any rain event.

questions.explanation: Daily competent person inspection, soil classification, and protective systems must be confirmed before anyone enters an excavation.

questions.question: Kai Watanabe, a foreman on a renovation project in an occupied building, is asked about crane lift planning and load path control. The project manager has asked what the crew's practice is. Which action is most appropriate?

answers.text: Workers may walk briefly beneath a suspended load to guide it by hand when the landing point is close, because a slow-moving load under an experienced operator presents little practical danger because the standard exists to prevent injuries and illnesses before they occur

If wind picks up during a series of lifts, the operator alone decides whether to continue based on how the load feels, without input from the supervisor or a review of the lift plan for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation in the ordinary course of front-line supervision on a well-run construction site

Lift planning can be skipped for repetitive picks of similar materials, since the crew already knows the routine and a fresh briefing each time would add delay without changing how the lift proceeds in the interest of worker safety and health on every shift the crew works

Before a lift, the supervisor confirms the load path and landing area are planned, workers are briefed and kept out from under suspended loads, the operator and signal person agree on communication, and the lift is stopped whenever conditions or visibility deteriorate.

questions.explanation: Planned load paths, clear exclusion under loads, and stop authority keep crane lifts controlled when conditions change.

questions.question: A project manager asks Dakota Reyes, a construction supervisor preparing for the STSC examination, to confirm the correct standard for automated external defibrillator readiness. The discussion follows a busy week on the job site. Which action is most appropriate?

answers.text: Where a defibrillator is provided, the supervisor never checks its readiness indicator or pad expiration because the device was new at project start, assuming it will function perfectly months later without any inspection at all for the reasons recorded in the crew's planning and review documentation

Where a defibrillator is provided, the supervisor stores it in a locked office that is empty during early and weekend shifts, reasoning that theft prevention matters more than immediate access when a worker collapses on site whenever the work is performed within the supervisor's area of responsibility

Where a defibrillator is provided on site, the supervisor keeps it in a known accessible location, ensures trained users are present on each shift, checks its readiness indicator and pads on schedule, and has it brought to any collapsed worker while emergency services are called.

When a worker collapses and is unresponsive, the supervisor waits for the ambulance rather than starting resuscitation and sending for the site defibrillator, believing only hospital staff should attempt any intervention before transport arrives consistent with how the crew documents and reviews its own performance

questions.explanation: A maintained, accessible defibrillator with trained users can restore a heartbeat when minutes decide the outcome.

ohio-public-adjuster-exam-prep.quiz_title: Ohio Public Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the scope of the Ohio public adjuster definition?

answers.text: Public adjusting in Ohio covers only life and health claims.
A public adjuster is an insurer's salaried employee who settles the company's own claims.
Only a licensed insurance producer may negotiate a property claim settlement.

An Ohio public insurance adjuster is a person, firm, association, partnership, or corporation who, for compensation, acts on behalf of or aids in any manner an insurer or insured or another in negotiating for, or effecting, the settlement of a claim for loss or damage under a policy insuring real or personal property.

questions.explanation: In one line: Compensation plus negotiating or effecting settlement of a property claim is the core of the definition.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes strict and absolute liability?

answers.text: Strict (absolute) liability imposes responsibility for harm from abnormally dangerous activities or defective products without requiring proof of negligence.
Strict liability is a defense that eliminates liability.
Strict liability requires proving the defendant was careless.
Strict liability applies to ordinary household activities.

questions.explanation: Some activities are so dangerous that liability follows the harm itself — blasting and keeping wild animals are the classic examples in the tort objectives. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing settlement options. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Insurers may settle only in cash.
The insured chooses the settlement option in all cases.
Taking the property requires a court order in every case.

Standard property policies give the insurer settlement options on a covered loss — pay the value or the cost of repair or replacement, repair or replace the property itself, or take the property at the agreed or appraised value — exercised as the policy states and within the claims rules' timelines.

questions.explanation: Options belong to the insurer by the contract's terms; the adjuster's job is to police value and timing within them. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: On the subject of the betterment cap on auto parts, which statement is right?

answers.text: Betterment may exceed the cost of the new parts installed.
Betterment is a flat percentage the insurer chooses.

Ohio limits an auto betterment deduction to the measurable market-value decrease from poorer condition or prior damage, or the documented condition, age, wear, rust, and missing-parts factors, and in no case more than the replacement cost of the parts.
There is no limit on betterment deductions in Ohio.

questions.explanation: Betterment measures the value actually gained and can never exceed what the new parts cost. Candidates miss this when they rely on how other licenses or other states handle the same issue.

questions.question: Regarding physical hazard, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A physical hazard is a physical condition of the property, its occupancy, or its use that increases the chance of loss.
A physical hazard is carelessness after buying insurance.
A physical hazard is the insured's dishonest intent.
A physical hazard is the uncertainty of loss itself.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: Frayed wiring, a wood-shake roof in a brush zone, and storing flammables are physical hazards — tangible conditions an adjuster documents on inspection.

questions.question: Regarding what the application discloses — five years of work, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Only the applicant's current job is listed.
Employment history is required only of entity applicants.
The lookback period is two years of employment.

The Ohio application must set forth the business or employment in which the applicant has been engaged for the five years next preceding the application, with the name and address of the business and the names and addresses of the applicant's employers.

questions.explanation: In one line: Five years of work history, with employers identified, is part of the trustworthiness record.

questions.question: A home that cracks and settles over an abandoned underground mine presents a mine subsidence claim. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: compensatory damages make the injured party whole; punitive damages punish
mine subsidence coverage addresses collapse of underground mines in Ohio's coal regions
the federal terrorism backstop is a listed Ohio basics topic, distinct from state residual programs
FAIR Plan coverage follows failure to obtain coverage voluntarily, not price shopping

questions.explanation: The example points to mine subsidence coverage addresses collapse of underground mines in Ohio's coal regions. The peril is the ground giving way over old underground workings, not mining operations themselves.

questions.question: A covered item has a replacement cost of $20,000. Depreciation of 20% applies for its age and condition. What is the item's actual cash value?
questions.explanation: Actual cash value is replacement cost minus depreciation: $20,000 x (1 - 0.20) = $16,000. The depreciation withheld is $4,000.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing the Ohio special provisions endorsement on the dwelling form. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Ohio dwelling policies are issued on the unmodified national form.
The special provisions endorsement is a flood endorsement.
Only commercial policies carry state special provisions endorsements.

The Ohio dwelling policy is issued with the Ohio special provisions endorsement, which adapts the standard dwelling form's terms for Ohio and is among the selected endorsements the Ohio outline lists for the dwelling policy.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: Read the Ohio dwelling form with its Ohio endorsement attached; the endorsement is part of the tested form.

questions.question: A homeowners policy shows a Coverage A dwelling limit of $300,000. Using the form's standard percentage, what is the limit for Coverage C (personal property)?
questions.explanation: Coverage C (personal property) is set at 50% of Coverage A in the standard form: 50% x $300,000 = $150,000.

questions.question: Regarding increased cost of construction in the BOP, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: The coverage applies to undamaged buildings with no loss.
Ordinance costs are unlimited in the base BOP.
Increased cost of construction pays fines for code violations before a loss.

The BOP provides a limited increased cost of construction additional coverage, paying the added cost to comply with ordinances or laws when repairing or rebuilding after a covered loss, up to the form's stated percentage or amount.

questions.explanation: The key point: A modest built-in ordinance cushion exists in the BOP; larger ordinance exposure needs a fuller endorsement.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the value of business personal property away from the premises?

answers.text: Off-premises property of others is covered without limit.
Property at a second owned location is covered automatically.

Business personal property away from the described premises is covered only in limited circumstances — such as at a fair, trade show, or exhibition, in transit with a common carrier, or at a premises the insured does not own — and for limited amounts.
Business personal property is covered worldwide to its full limit.

questions.explanation: The key point: Commercial property is location-centric; property that travels needs inland marine or a specific extension, a gap adjusters find after trade-show losses.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Insurable interest exists when a person benefits financially from the property's continued existence and would be harmed by its loss; for property it must exist at the time of loss.

answers.text: dishonesty or character defects in the insured
temporary proof of coverage before the policy issues
a financial stake in the property's preservation
compensatory damages make the injured party whole; punitive damages punish

questions.explanation: That description defines a financial stake in the property's preservation. Property insurance is not a wager: the claimant must stand to lose financially from the property's damage, and that stake is measured when the loss occurs.

questions.question: Mr. Alvarez is adjusting a claim at a single-family home after a kitchen fire. The file raises the issue of the adjuster's core duties. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The adjuster's duty is to maximize the estimate by any arguable method.
Documentation duties belong to the insurer alone.
The adjuster guarantees the settlement amount to the client.

A public adjuster's working duties are to inspect and document the loss, build a fair and honest inventory and estimate, present and negotiate the claim for the insured under the written contract, keep the required transaction records, and conduct the engagement within Ohio's prohibited-activity rules.

questions.explanation: Honest numbers, complete files, and rule-bound conduct are the job description. Candidates miss this when they rely on how other licenses or other states handle the same issue.

questions.question: A failed supply line is saved, tagged, and stored so the insurer's expert can test it for the subrogation case. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: do not dispose of evidence or impair recovery rights
loss of use and time-element amounts turn on the period of restoration and documented expenses
the insured must produce books and records and cooperate with the insurer's reasonable investigation
no settlement posture may exceed what the client engagement authorizes

questions.explanation: The example points to do not dispose of evidence or impair recovery rights. Throwing away the failed pipe or signing a release with the negligent installer can gut both the claim and the carrier's recovery — adjusters protect the evidence chain.

questions.question: A mostly empty warehouse, vacant for a full quarter, suffers a theft the vacancy condition excludes outright. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: a declarations, conditions, and one or more coverage forms build the policy
plate glass and outdoor signs need specific treatment
loss restrictions when a building is largely vacant over 60 days
breakdown programs include consequential coverages

questions.explanation: The example points to loss restrictions when a building is largely vacant over 60 days. Vacancy changes the risk, so the form changes the deal: named peril categories vanish and surviving losses take the 15% reduction after the 60-day line.

questions.question: A fire closes a business for 2 months. The business's net income would have been $15,000 per month, and its continuing normal operating expenses are $8,000 per month. What is the business income loss for the closure?
questions.explanation: Business income loss combines lost net income and continuing expenses: ($15,000 + $8,000) x 2 months = $46,000.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Ohio's valued policy law is a fire-and-lightning, total-loss rule; it does not convert partial losses, or losses from other perils, into valued settlements.

answers.text: risk as the uncertainty of financial loss
the valued policy rule is a fire and lightning, total-loss rule only
offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties, and legal purpose
who makes the claim against whom

questions.explanation: That description defines the valued policy rule is a fire and lightning, total-loss rule only. Peril and totality both matter: fire or lightning, and a total loss, before the rule engages.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? The burden of proving that a covered loss occurred and the amount of that loss rests on the claimant, which is why the adjuster's inventory, photographs, estimates, and records — not the insurer's file — must carry the value case.

answers.text: the claimant must prove the existence and amount of the loss
salvage value offsets the loss, and the adjuster may hold no interest in the salvage of a loss adjusted
depreciation reflects age, condition, and wear, and its computation must be documentable
a sworn statement of the loss the insured submits to the insurer

questions.explanation: That description defines the claimant must prove the existence and amount of the loss. He who claims, proves: coverage, occurrence, and amount are the claimant's evidentiary load.

questions.question: A fire at a repair garage destroys three customer cars; the shop's CGL raises the care, custody, or control exclusion. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: necessary extra costs to continue operations after a covered loss
net income plus continuing normal operating expenses during restoration
dwellings, barns, livestock, and farm machinery in one program
no liability coverage for property in the insured's custody

questions.explanation: The example points to no liability coverage for property in the insured's custody. A repair shop that burns its customers' goods learns the CCC exclusion the hard way; the customer's property belonged on a property form.

rdcs.quiz_title: RDCS — Registered Diagnostic Cardiac Sonographer Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Tomas is a cardiac sonographer at a hospital echocardiography laboratory reviewing a sampled case file. Which of the following best describes ejection fraction calculation 3?

answers.text: A left ventricular volume study in a follow-up study after myocardial infarction measures an end-diastolic volume of 150 milliliters and an end-systolic volume of 75 milliliters, giving an ejection fraction expressed as a rate of 50 percent, computed as 75 divided by 150 and multiplied by 100.

A left ventricular volume study in a follow-up study after myocardial infarction measures an end-diastolic volume of 75 milliliters and an end-systolic volume of 75 milliliters, giving an ejection fraction expressed as a rate of 200 percent, computed as 150 divided by 75 and multiplied by 100.

A left ventricular volume study in a follow-up study after myocardial infarction measures an end-diastolic volume of 150 milliliters and an end-systolic volume of 75 milliliters, giving an ejection fraction expressed as a rate of 75 percent, computed as the count of 75 alone without regard to the total.

A left ventricular volume study in a follow-up study after myocardial infarction measures an end-diastolic volume of 150 milliliters and an end-systolic volume of 75 milliliters, giving an ejection fraction expressed as a rate of 45 percent, computed as 75 divided by 150 and multiplied by 100.

questions.explanation: A ventricle that empties poorly leaves a large end-systolic volume, which is why the difference term shrinks as systolic function worsens. This is the standard echocardiography laboratory practice whenever ejection fraction calculation 3 is at issue.

questions.question: Elif is a newly credentialed cardiac sonographer being mentored at a cardiology practice imaging suite. Regarding respirophasic doppler variation in tamponade, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Tamponade abolishes all respiratory variation in Doppler inflow, so mitral and tricuspid velocities remain fixed throughout breathing.
In tamponade, mitral inflow normally rises sharply with inspiration while tricuspid inflow falls by a similar amount.

Tamponade produces exaggerated respirophasic variation in Doppler inflow, typically a fall in mitral inflow velocity of more than twenty five percent with inspiration and a reciprocal rise in tricuspid inflow during the same phase.
Doppler variation in tamponade is best assessed during a breath hold, because breathing removes the diagnostic pattern entirely.

questions.explanation: Recording Doppler with a respirometer trace helps link velocity changes directly to inspiratory and expiratory timing. That is the sound approach to respirophasic doppler variation in tamponade.

questions.question: Sana is a cardiac sonographer at a university cardiac imaging department reviewing a sampled case file. Which of the following best describes ebstein anomaly tricuspid displacement?

answers.text: Ebstein anomaly is defined by apical displacement of the septal tricuspid leaflet, which atrializes part of the right ventricle and is usually accompanied by tricuspid regurgitation and right atrial enlargement.
Ebstein anomaly displaces the mitral valve apically and atrializes part of the left ventricle.
The septal tricuspid leaflet is displaced toward the base in Ebstein anomaly, not the apex.
Tricuspid regurgitation is absent in Ebstein anomaly because the leaflets coapt normally.

questions.explanation: The functional right ventricle is small while the anatomic right atrium becomes markedly enlarged. The other choices distort the principle behind ebstein anomaly tricuspid displacement.

questions.question: Priya is a cardiac sonographer at a cardiology practice imaging suite reviewing a sampled case file. Which of the following best describes aortic root dimension measurement?

answers.text: Aortic root diameter is commonly measured at end diastole at the sinuses of Valsalva using leading-edge technique.
Aortic root diameter is measured at peak systole at the leaflet tips only.
Aortic root diameter is measured in the apical view at the annulus during filling.
Aortic root diameter excludes the sinuses and is taken only in the ascending aorta.

questions.explanation: The sinuses of Valsalva are the widest part of the root and the standard site for root diameter comparison. That is the sound approach to aortic root dimension measurement.

questions.question: Marta has asked Vera, an experienced cardiac sonographer, a question about a case under review. Regarding parasternal long axis plane, which choice states the practice a cardiac sonographer should follow?

answers.text: The parasternal long-axis view shows the left ventricle, mitral valve, aortic valve, and aortic root in one plane.
The parasternal long-axis view shows all four chambers with the apex pointing down.
The parasternal long-axis view is obtained from the suprasternal notch window.
The parasternal long-axis view excludes the aortic root from the field.

questions.explanation: Rotating ninety degrees clockwise from this position produces the parasternal short-axis series of views. This is the standard echocardiography laboratory practice whenever parasternal long axis plane is at issue.

questions.question: At an accredited echocardiography laboratory, a cardiac sonographer considers the best way to proceed with a complex study. The situation turns on pulmonic stenosis gradient assessment. Which proposition states the sound approach?

answers.text: Pulmonic stenosis severity is graded mainly from the mitral inflow E wave velocity.
Pulmonic stenosis severity is graded mainly from the peak gradient across the pulmonic valve on continuous wave Doppler.
A peak pulmonic gradient below 20 mmHg indicates severe valvular pulmonic stenosis.
Pulmonic stenosis gradients are measured only during diastole when the valve is closed.

questions.explanation: The systolic gradient across the pulmonic valve reflects how much the narrowed orifice obstructs right ventricular outflow. This is the standard echocardiography laboratory practice whenever pulmonic stenosis gradient assessment is at issue.

questions.question: A training session for cardiac sonographers at a hospital echocardiography laboratory takes up a practice scenario. Which statement about restrictive versus constriction respiratory variation correctly resolves the issue presented?

answers.text: Restriction shows marked respiratory variation in mitral inflow and constriction shows none.
Both conditions are separated mainly by ejection fraction, which is low in constriction.
Hepatic vein expiratory diastolic reversal is a classic sign of myocardial restriction.
Constriction shows exaggerated respiratory variation in mitral inflow, while restriction shows little respiratory change.

questions.explanation: In restriction the stiff myocardium itself limits filling, and inflow varies little across the respiratory cycle. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about restrictive versus constriction respiratory variation.

questions.question: During a case review at a hospital echocardiography laboratory, a question about echocardiography laboratory practice comes up. Regarding pacing and defibrillator lead appearance, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Device leads are echo lucent and invisible, so a bright linear structure in the right heart excludes a lead.
Pacemaker and defibrillator leads appear as bright linear echo densities crossing the right heart, and defibrillator leads are distinguished by a thicker coil segment along their course.
Defibrillator leads are thinner than pacing leads along their entire length with no coil segment.
A lead seen crossing the tricuspid valve must be an artifact because leads terminate in the vena cava.

questions.explanation: Bright linear echoes traversing the right atrium and tricuspid valve toward the right ventricle suggest leads. This is the standard echocardiography laboratory practice whenever pacing and defibrillator lead appearance is at issue.

questions.question: In a laboratory meeting at a hospital echocardiography laboratory, cardiac sonographers raise a question about standard practice. Which statement about chaperone offer and documentation correctly resolves the issue presented?

answers.text: A chaperone should never be offered because the offer itself implies the examination is inappropriate.
Offering a chaperone for examinations involving chest exposure respects patient comfort and facility policy, and the presence or decline of a chaperone should be noted in the record.
Chaperones are required only when the sonographer and patient are of the same gender.
If a patient declines a chaperone, the examination must be cancelled and rescheduled for another day.

questions.explanation: A chaperone provides comfort and a witness during examinations that require exposure, and the offer supports patient trust. This is the standard echocardiography laboratory practice whenever chaperone offer and documentation is at issue.

questions.question: During a case review at a community hospital ultrasound department, a question about echocardiography laboratory practice comes up. Regarding relevant cardiac and surgical history, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Surgical history is irrelevant once a patient has fully recovered from the earlier procedure.

Prior valve surgery, implanted devices, known congenital lesions, and previous interventions should be elicited because they change expected anatomy, imaging approach, and interpretation of prosthetic or repaired structures.
A prosthetic valve should be assessed with exactly the same expectations as a native valve.
History of endocarditis should not be mentioned when the current study evaluates a valve lesion.

questions.explanation: Accurate history also prevents mistaking expected postoperative appearance for new pathology in the current report. The other choices distort the principle behind relevant cardiac and surgical history.

questions.question: Dalia and another cardiac sonographer disagree about the right approach and check the standard practice. Regarding flow dependence of gradients, which choice states the practice a cardiac sonographer should follow?

answers.text: Transvalvular gradients fall as flow increases across a fixed orifice.
Transvalvular gradients are completely independent of flow rate.
Transvalvular gradients rise with increased flow even when anatomic valve area is unchanged.
Transvalvular gradients are determined solely by blood pressure levels.

questions.explanation: Valve area methods are preferred in abnormal flow states because areas are less flow dependent than gradients. That is the sound approach to flow dependence of gradients.

questions.question: In a laboratory meeting at a community hospital ultrasound department, cardiac sonographers raise a question about standard practice. Which statement about focal zone placement correctly resolves the issue presented?

answers.text: The focal zone should always be placed at the skin surface so the near field shows the sharpest detail.
The focal zone should be placed at or just deep to the structure of interest, because the beam is narrowest at the focus and lateral resolution is best at that depth.
Lateral resolution is best far away from the focal zone, where the beam has spread the widest.
Moving the focus changes axial resolution only, and lateral detail stays identical at every depth.

questions.explanation: As views change during a study, repositioning the focus to the new structure of interest is a routine optimization step. The other choices distort the principle behind focal zone placement.

questions.question: Mina has asked Devon, an experienced cardiac sonographer, a question about a case under review. Regarding patient prosthesis mismatch concept, which choice states the practice a cardiac sonographer should follow?

answers.text: Patient-prosthesis mismatch means a normally functioning prosthesis is too small for the patient's body size and flow needs.
Patient-prosthesis mismatch means the prosthesis has torn loose from its sewing ring.
Mismatch is diagnosed when a prosthetic valve shows a paravalvular leak on color Doppler.
A small indexed effective orifice with high gradients and normal occluder motion argues against mismatch.

questions.explanation: The valve itself works as designed, but its orifice is small relative to body size, leaving persistently high gradients. That is the sound approach to patient prosthesis mismatch concept.

questions.question: Hugo is reviewing the worksheet for a patient with congenital heart disease now followed in an adult clinic at an accredited echocardiography laboratory. Which of the following best describes aortic root measurement convention?

answers.text: Aortic size can be compared reliably even when each study uses a different plane, phase, and edge convention.
A one millimeter difference between studies always proves true aneurysm growth regardless of technique.
Aortic dimensions are measured in a consistent plane and cardiac phase and compared over time, because small differences in technique can mimic real growth of the root or ascending aorta.
Aortic measurements do not need a recorded location because diameter is uniform along the ascending aorta.

questions.explanation: Measurements are interpreted with body size, growth rate, symptoms, and associated valve disease rather than in isolation. That is the sound approach to aortic root measurement convention.

questions.question: Oscar is a newly credentialed cardiac sonographer being mentored at a university cardiac imaging department. Regarding septal occluder device follow up, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: After septal occluder placement, follow-up imaging confirms device position across the septum, checks for residual shunt around the device, and watches for pericardial effusion as a sign of erosion or perforation.
A mean gradient of 40 mmHg or higher across the aortic valve supports severe aortic stenosis.
A correctly placed occluder sits entirely in the left atrium without straddling the septum.
Severe mitral stenosis is supported when the mitral valve area is 1.5 square centimeters or less.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. The device should straddle the septum with discs on each side and no impingement on nearby structures.

questions.question: Sana is reviewing the worksheet for a patient with a suspected pericardial effusion referred urgently at a cardiology practice imaging suite. Which of the following best describes wall filter effect on doppler?

answers.text: A wall filter that is set too high adds low-velocity noise to the spectral display.
A wall filter affects only color Doppler and never spectral tracings.
A wall filter that is set too high can remove true low-velocity flow signals from the spectral display.
A wall filter removes high-velocity signals while preserving low velocities.

questions.explanation: Low-velocity signals matter for diastolic filling patterns and venous flow, so filters are kept modest for those signals. The other choices distort the principle behind wall filter effect on doppler.

questions.question: A laboratory manager at a community hospital ultrasound department reviews a practice question with cardiac sonographer Tessa. Regarding fractional shortening calculation 5, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: An M-mode study in a follow-up recording after treatment for heart failure measures a left ventricular end-diastolic dimension of 13 millimeters and an end-systolic dimension of 39 millimeters, giving a fractional shortening expressed as a rate of 400 percent, computed as 52 divided by 13 and multiplied by 100.

An M-mode study in a follow-up recording after treatment for heart failure measures a left ventricular end-diastolic dimension of 52 millimeters and an end-systolic dimension of 39 millimeters, giving a fractional shortening expressed as a rate of 25 percent, computed as 13 divided by 52 and multiplied by 100.

An M-mode study in a follow-up recording after treatment for heart failure measures a left ventricular end-diastolic dimension of 52 millimeters and an end-systolic dimension of 39 millimeters, giving a fractional shortening expressed as a rate of 65 percent, computed as 13 plus 52 and multiplied by 100.

An M-mode study in a follow-up recording after treatment for heart failure measures a left ventricular end-diastolic dimension of 52 millimeters and an end-systolic dimension of 39 millimeters, giving a fractional shortening expressed as a rate of 30 percent, computed as 13 divided by 52 and multiplied by 100.

questions.explanation: A ventricle that contracts weakly shortens little, which is why the difference term shrinks as systolic function worsens. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about fractional shortening calculation 5.

questions.question: Sana is reviewing the worksheet for an older patient with atrial fibrillation referred for a cardiac ultrasound study at a community hospital ultrasound department. Regarding papillary muscle rupture complication, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Papillary muscle rupture after infarction causes acute severe mitral regurgitation with a flail leaflet and a hyperdynamic ventricle.
A pseudoaneurysm has a narrow neck relative to its sac, while a true aneurysm has a wide neck and a wall containing myocardium.
Papillary muscle rupture after infarction causes slowly progressive mild mitral stenosis.
Echocardiography should attempt to show both coronary ostia arising from the appropriate aortic sinuses in the short-axis view.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Sudden loss of leaflet support floods a small unprepared atrium, so severe regurgitation appears with vigorous ventricular motion.

questions.question: Rosa, a cardiac sonographer, is performing a study for a patient with a known cardiomyopathy returning for a function check at a community hospital ultrasound department. Regarding lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Lipomatous hypertrophy thickens the fossa ovalis most and thins the surrounding septum.
Lipomatous hypertrophy thickens the interatrial septum with fat that spares the fossa ovalis, producing a characteristic dumbbell or hourglass shape rather than a discrete encapsulated tumor.
Mass characterization weighs attachment width, mobility, location, and tissue appearance together, because a narrow stalk with free mobility and a broad sessile base point toward different diagnoses.

A sinus venosus defect lies outside the true atrial septum near a vena cava junction and is strongly associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous return, most often of the right upper pulmonary vein.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Fat above and below a spared fossa ovalis creates the recognizable dumbbell septal configuration.

questions.question: Hugo, a cardiac sonographer, is performing a study for a patient referred for a stress echocardiogram for exertional chest discomfort at a hospital echocardiography laboratory. Regarding tissue doppler e prime site, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Tissue Doppler e prime is measured at the septal and lateral mitral annulus in the apical four-chamber view.
Diastolic function grading uses multiple parameters together, including e prime, E/e prime, left atrial volume, and tricuspid velocity.
Tissue Doppler e prime is measured at the mitral leaflet tips in the parasternal view.
Planimetry traces the anatomic valve orifice in short axis at the leaflet tips to measure valve area directly.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. The small sample is placed at the annulus-myocardium junction so myocardial velocities dominate the recorded signal.

tennessee-public-adjuster-exam-prep.quiz_title: Tennessee Public Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding the law-practice fence, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Adjusters may file suit for insureds as part of adjusting.
A public adjuster license doubles as a limited law license for claims.
The fence applies only to adjusters who charge hourly fees.
Nothing in the Tennessee public adjuster rules authorizes a public adjuster, or a person operating at an adjuster's direction, to engage in conduct that is the practice of law.

questions.explanation: Adjusting is not lawyering: when a claim needs legal process, it goes to an admitted attorney. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: A fire closes a business for 1 months. The business's net income would have been $8,000 per month, and its continuing normal operating expenses are $5,000 per month. What is the business income loss for the closure?
questions.explanation: Business income loss combines lost net income and continuing expenses: ($8,000 + $5,000) x 1 months = $13,000.

questions.question: On the subject of the building and personal property form, which statement is right?

answers.text: Business personal property cannot be covered with the building.
Commercial property uses the homeowners forms.
The core commercial property coverage form insures buildings and business personal property, with causes-of-loss forms — basic, broad, or special — supplying the peril terms.
The causes-of-loss form is optional decoration with no effect.

questions.explanation: Form plus causes-of-loss selection is the commercial product's architecture: what is covered, then what can hurt it. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Tennessee criminal history fee?

answers.text: The fee is four hundred eighty dollars.
The forty-eight dollars is paid to the exam vendor as part of the exam fee.

The criminal history record check for a Tennessee public adjuster candidate costs forty-eight dollars, made payable to the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, apart from the collector's administrative fee.
The background check is free for first-time applicants.

questions.explanation: In one line: Forty-eight dollars to the bureau, plus the collector's fee — two separate small payments, neither of them the exam fee.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Tennessee exam's size and clock?

answers.text: The exam is an open-book take-home test.
The exam has one hundred questions and two hours.
The Tennessee public adjuster examination is administered by the department's contracted testing vendor and consists of fifty scored questions with a sixty-minute time limit.
The department proctors the exam only at its Nashville office on paper.

questions.explanation: In one line: Fifty questions, one hour, vendor-administered — a short, fast exam where Tennessee law is fifteen of the fifty questions.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing what the Tennessee bond lets the commissioner recover. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The bond covers only the adjuster's office rent defaults.

The Tennessee bond specifically authorizes recovery by the commissioner on behalf of any person in the state who sustained damages as the result of the adjuster's erroneous acts, failure to act, conviction of fraud, or conviction of unfair practices as a public adjuster.
Recovery is limited to the department's own enforcement costs.
The bond pays the adjuster's own business debts.

questions.explanation: The bond exists for harmed members of the public, collected through the commissioner — erroneous acts, inaction, fraud, and unfair practices are its named triggers. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: Mr. Novak is adjusting a claim at an office condo after vandalism. The file raises the issue of the post-offer fee cap. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Post-offer contracts are uncapped.
The post-offer cap is twenty-five percent of the total settlement.

If a Tennessee public adjuster contract is formed after the carrier has made an offer, the fee may not exceed twenty-five percent of the difference between the insurer's last offer and the final settlement.
The post-offer cap is fifteen percent of the increase.

questions.explanation: After an offer exists, the percentage rides only on the improvement the adjuster adds — twenty-five percent of the increase, never of the whole. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: A detached workshop behind the house is destroyed by fire and settled under Coverage B's percentage limit. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: structures on the premises separated from the dwelling
motor vehicles, animals, and property of roomers are standard exclusions from Coverage C
principal, obligee, and surety
open perils on both dwelling and personal property

questions.explanation: The example points to structures on the premises separated from the dwelling. Detached garages, sheds, and fences live in Coverage B at a built-in 10% of the dwelling limit unless the insured buys more.

questions.question: A candidate is studying peril, defined. Which of the following is a correct statement?

answers.text: A peril is a condition that increases the chance of loss.
A peril is the specific cause of a loss — fire, lightning, windstorm, hail, and theft are perils — and whether a peril is covered decides whether a claim is paid.
A peril is the insurer's profit margin.
A peril is the amount of a deductible.

questions.explanation: Perils cause losses; hazards make them likelier. Claims work starts by naming the peril correctly.

questions.question: Mr. O'Brien asks how concealment and fraud provisions works in a property claim. Which explanation is correct?

answers.text: Property forms provide that the policy may be void — or the claim denied — if the insured intentionally conceals or misrepresents a material fact, or commits fraud, in the application or the claim.
Fraud provisions apply only before the policy issues.
Small exaggerations on a claim are expressly permitted.
The insurer must prove the weather caused the misstatement.

questions.explanation: Material and intentional are the twin elements: honest mistakes are corrected, deliberate deception forfeits. Candidates miss this when they rely on how other licenses or other states handle the same issue.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing named perils versus open perils. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Named perils shifts the burden to the insurer.
The two approaches differ only in premium.

Under a named-perils form, only the perils listed are covered and the insured must show the loss came from one of them; under an open-perils form, all direct physical loss is covered unless excluded, and the insurer must point to an exclusion to deny.
Open perils covers only the perils it lists.

questions.explanation: The burden flips with the form: list-and-prove for named perils, cover-and-exclude for open perils. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing where Tennessee applications are filed today. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The forty-eight hour wait applies before taking the exam, not after.
Candidates file directly with the exam vendor for licensure.
Applications are filed only on paper at the county courthouse.
Tennessee public adjuster applications are filed electronically through the national insurance producer registry, after the candidate waits forty-eight hours from passing so the exam result posts.

questions.explanation: Sequence matters: pass, wait forty-eight hours for the score to post, then file electronically.

questions.question: Mr. Haddad is adjusting a claim at a retail store after a windstorm. The file raises the issue of what a Tennessee renewal filing contains. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Exam proof must be filed again at every renewal.
Bond proof replaces the education proof at renewal.
A renewal filing is the fee alone.

A Tennessee renewal application contains a completed renewal form signed as the rule requires, proof of the required continuing education (or of the home-state equivalent), and the one hundred dollar renewal fee.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: Form, education proof, fee — the same three-part discipline as the initial filing, minus the examination.

questions.question: A home has a replacement cost of $500,000. Its homeowners policy requires insurance of at least 80% of replacement cost for full replacement cost settlement. The owner carried $280,000. A covered partial loss of $40,000 occurs. Because the home was underinsured, how much will the insurer pay for the loss (before any deductible)?
questions.explanation: The 80% requirement is $400,000. The owner carried $280,000, a ratio of 0.70. The partial loss is scaled by that ratio: $40,000 x 0.70 = $28,000.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? A physical hazard is a physical condition of the property, its occupancy, or its use that increases the chance of loss.

answers.text: a line-item estimate of the work needed to restore the property
the insured retains a small, predictable share of each loss
offer, acceptance, consideration, competent parties, and legal purpose
a physical condition of the property or its use

questions.explanation: That description defines a physical condition of the property or its use. Frayed wiring, a wood-shake roof in a brush zone, and storing flammables are physical hazards — tangible conditions an adjuster documents on inspection.

questions.question: A commercial building is valued at $600,000. Its policy has a 80% coinsurance clause. The owner carried $360,000 of insurance. A covered loss of $100,000 occurs, and the deductible is $1,000. How much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Coinsurance required 80% of $600,000, which is $480,000. The payment ratio is $360,000 / $480,000 = 0.75. Applied to the $100,000 loss gives $75,000, minus the $1,000 deductible = $74,000.

questions.question: When both sides agree a roof is covered but fight over its price, appraisal is the built-in answer. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: a valuation-only process for disputes about the amount of loss
coverage only for listed perils versus coverage for all perils not excluded
physical damage itself versus the financial consequences that flow from it
a condition that increases the probability or severity of a loss

questions.explanation: The example points to a valuation-only process for disputes about the amount of loss. Value, not coverage — appraisal prices the loss while coverage disputes stay with the policy and, if needed, the courts.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Complaints about Tennessee public adjusters are handled by the department's consumer insurance services section, and on notice of a complaint the adjuster must send a written response to that section within thirty days.

answers.text: public adjusting reaches only first party claims on the insured's own property
funds held for an insured go into a non-interest-bearing escrow or trust account
prior out-of-state licensure and new-resident timing can exempt an applicant from the exam
a written response to the consumer services section within thirty days of notice

questions.explanation: That description defines a written response to the consumer services section within thirty days of notice. Thirty days, in writing, to the consumer services section — ignoring a complaint is itself a compliance failure.

questions.question: After a moderate quake cracks a home's foundation, the owner learns her earthquake policy's 15% deductible applies before any payment. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: earth movement is endorsed or separately insured, usually with a percentage deductible
principal, obligee, and surety
commercial counterpart of the mortgagee clause
umbrella policies add liability limits above underlying policies

questions.explanation: The example points to earth movement is endorsed or separately insured, usually with a percentage deductible. Percentage deductibles are the earthquake signature: 10% of a $600,000 limit means the insured absorbs the first $60,000 of quake damage.

questions.question: A woman insures a rental house she owns; a passerby who merely likes the house could not collect for its fire damage. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: the loss of value from age, wear, and obsolescence applied in cash-value settlements
the most the policy pays, with lower inside caps for special categories
a financial stake in the property's preservation
