questions.question: A heavy electric pickup variant needs replacement tires, and two candidates share the same size. The tables help decide by comparing which property?

answers.text: The advertised tread-life slogan
The depth of sidewall lettering
The country named on the label
Load-carrying capacity at the intended inflation pressure for each candidate

questions.explanation: Same-size tires can carry different loads, especially standard versus HL or LT constructions. Comparing table load capacity at service pressure is how the correct candidate is chosen.

questions.question: A customer asks the mobile technician to 'just make them extra tight' for peace of mind on a long trip. How is that request handled?

answers.text: Torque stays at the vehicle maker's specification, and the technician explains that over-torquing can yield studs, warp components and make roadside removal extremely difficult
The nuts are torqued well past specification because tighter is safer
One extra impact-gun burst is added after the torque wrench pass
The front wheels are over-torqued and the rears left at specification

questions.explanation: Specification torque is an engineered value, not a minimum. Exceeding it damages the very hardware the customer is relying on, which the technician explains while holding the correct value.

questions.question: A mounted assembly will not hold pressure and leaks at the rim flange. Before any re-inflation attempt, the technician should do what?

answers.text: Keep topping it up until the leak seals itself
Add a can of emergency sealant as standard practice
Deflate it, demount as needed, and find the leak cause such as seat corrosion, bead damage, or a faulty valve
Return it, because slow leaks usually stop

questions.explanation: A leaking assembly is diagnosed deflated, because the cause is at the bead, wheel, or valve. Returning a leaking assembly guarantees a low-pressure comeback or failure.

questions.question: After a driveway pressure correction, the warning lamp stays on for the first part of the customer's drive, then goes out. How is this explained?

answers.text: The lamp staying on proves a sensor was damaged during service
Many systems need the vehicle driven for a period after pressures are corrected before the warning clears, which is normal behaviour to explain so the customer does not mistake it for a fault
The system always needs a scan tool to clear a low-pressure lamp
The customer must disconnect the battery to reset the lamp

questions.explanation: Warning lamps commonly clear only after a drive cycle at corrected pressures. Explaining the expected behaviour in advance prevents an unnecessary return visit and builds trust in the service.

questions.question: During peak season a van arrives wearing light truck tires marked with a 'C' type designation in the size. What does that designation signal to the technician?

answers.text: A commercial-duty light truck construction built for higher load and inflation demands of van and working-vehicle service, covered by the federal tire-servicing awareness taught in the program
A tire approved only for cold climates
A tire that must be inflated with carbon dioxide
A cosmetic grade for the store's pricing tiers

questions.explanation: C-type light truck tires are heavier-duty constructions for load-carrying vans and trucks, and the training treats their service with added care. Recognising the designation changes how pressures and loads are checked.

questions.question: During removal for a winter swap, the valve stem on one assembly is cracked and the TPMS sensor body is corroded. Recording and acting on this at the RIST stage matters because:

answers.text: The parts can be assessed after delivery more conveniently
Cracked stems seal better once cold weather arrives
Sensors are unrelated to tire service inspections
Valve and sensor condition are part of the assembly inspection, and renewing failed service parts now prevents a leak or lamp the customer will blame on the changeover

questions.explanation: RIST inspection covers the whole assembly, not just the tire carcass. Catching valve and sensor defects at removal turns a future comeback into a planned repair.

questions.question: Before balancing a wheel that has just come off a muddy rural driveway, the technician cleans the wheel thoroughly. Why is this a balance-accuracy step, not cosmetics?

answers.text: Mud, stones in the tread and old weight residue are real mass that the balancer will try to correct; removing them first means the correction applies to the wheel itself
Because the balancer's camera cannot see a dirty wheel
Because mud insulates the wheel from the balancer shaft
Because a clean wheel is lighter and needs no weights

questions.explanation: Anything stuck to the assembly is imbalance the machine will measure and chase. Cleaning first — including old weights and trapped stones — makes the reading describe the assembly as it will actually run.

new-york-city-high-pressure-boiler-opera.quiz_title: New York City High Pressure Boiler Operating Engineer Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which of the following is the soundest guidance on new york city examination administrator role?

answers.text: The New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer examinations are developed and administered by the fire department.
The Department of Buildings contracted CPS HR Consulting to develop and administer the examinations for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license.
The citywide administrative services department develops and administers the examinations for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license.
Pearson VUE developed the examinations for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license and also issues the license.

questions.explanation: Explanation: For the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license, the Department of Buildings contracted CPS HR Consulting to develop and administer the license examinations. The citywide administrative services department is not the administrator of this examination, despite its similar sounding city role.

questions.question: Which of the following is the soundest guidance on new york city blowoff piping waste removal role?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows that blowoff piping carries water, sludge, and sediment removed from the bottom of the boiler safely away to a suitable disposal point, and is built to withstand hot and intermittent flow under pressure.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes blowoff piping is an open overflow vent that never carries pressure or heated water.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes blowoff piping may discharge scalding water freely wherever it is convenient in the boiler room.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes blowoff piping returns sludge and sediment to the feedwater supply so nothing is wasted.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer respects the blowoff line as a waste path with real energy in it, because what leaves the boiler bottom is hot, dirty, and under pressure until it is safely cooled and contained, and sound piping, sound valves, and a proper destination are what keep a routine removal of waste from becoming a scalding hazard in the plant.

questions.question: Which of the following is most consistent with sound practice in new york city boiler horsepower as a defined unit in words?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer defines one boiler horsepower as a measure of electrical power drawn by the feed pump motor, with no connection to water evaporated by the boiler.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer defines one boiler horsepower as the evaporation of thirty four and one half pounds of water per hour from and at the temperature of boiling water at atmospheric pressure.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer defines one boiler horsepower as the evaporation of one hundred pounds of water per hour from cold feedwater at any temperature the operator chooses to assume.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer defines one boiler horsepower as the pressure in the steam drum expressed in pounds, because horsepower and pressure are the same quantity in boiler work.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer treats boiler horsepower as a defined evaporation unit rather than a pressure or an electrical rating, based on a stated weight of water evaporated per hour from and at boiling temperature, because that common basis lets boilers of different designs be compared by the steam they can actually produce.

questions.question: Which of the following is most consistent with sound practice in new york city combustion air supply role?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows fuel burns and releases its heat with no oxygen present in the furnace.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows combustion air is supplied only to cool the boiler room in warm weather.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows combustion air is admitted to dilute the flame until burning nearly stops.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows combustion air supplies the oxygen that lets fuel burn and release its heat inside the furnace.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer guards the air supply as carefully as the fuel supply, because oxygen is a true partner in burning, and a boiler that is short of air cannot burn its fuel fully no matter how much fuel the burner tries to deliver into the furnace.

questions.question: Which of the following is most consistent with sound practice in new york city tube failure repair awareness?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer investigates the cause behind a tube failure during repair, looking for overheating, corrosion, scale, or flame impingement, so the repair addresses the reason and not only the ruined tube
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer repairs a tube failure by fitting a thicker tube in the same spot while leaving heavy scale and blocked circulation untouched
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer treats every tube failure as random bad luck requiring no investigation, since replacing the tube alone always cures the trouble completely
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer assumes overheating that burst one tube leaves every neighboring tube and sheet completely undamaged and fit for service

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer hunts the cause of a tube failure because tubes rarely fail without a reason the plant can correct, and overheating, waterside scale, corrosion, or direct flame attack will destroy the replacement just as surely, so repair that includes diagnosis protects neighboring tubes and prevents a repeating cycle of failures.

questions.question: Regarding new york city corrosion as inspection defect, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer recognises corrosion as proof the water treatment is working better than expected this season.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer recognises corrosion as a defect only when it appears on the outside paint of the boiler casing.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer recognises corrosion as an inspection defect that wastes metal, thins pressure parts, and can progress from pitting to leakage or failure if left unchecked.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer recognises corrosion as a harmless colour change that strengthens pressure parts over time.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer takes corrosion seriously because it removes metal from parts whose strength depends on their thickness. Pitting and general wasting found early can be measured and judged, while corrosion left alone deepens until the part leaks or can no longer hold pressure safely.

questions.question: Regarding new york city scale formation in the boiler, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows scale appears only in cold water lines and can never form in a hot boiler.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows scale forms from soot blowing in from the furnace through the steam outlet.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows scale is a soft foam that floats on the water and never touches any surface.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows scale forms when hardness matter in heated boiler water settles out and bakes onto hot internal surfaces as a hard deposit.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer connects scale directly to untreated hardness and heat, because minerals that stay dissolved in cool water come out of solution at hot surfaces, and preventing that deposit through softening and treatment protects the boiler every day it fires.

questions.question: Which of the following is most consistent with sound practice in new york city repair versus alteration meaning?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer understands ordinary cleaning and painting of a boiler casing as an alteration of the pressure vessel itself

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer understands a repair as work that restores a vessel to its original sound condition, while an alteration changes the original design, arrangement, or pressure carrying intent of the vessel
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer understands an alteration as nothing more than a very large repair, with no change in design or intent involved at all
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer understands repair and alteration as two names for exactly the same work, differing only in how long the job happens to take

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer keeps repair and alteration distinct because restoring original condition follows proven paths, while changing the original design raises fresh questions about strength, materials, and approval, and confusing the two can let design changing work slip through disguised as routine restoration.

questions.question: Regarding new york city operating adjustments as tested material, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer expects operating adjustments to be judged solely by how quiet the boiler room sounds.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer expects operating adjustments to matter only on the day the boiler was first commissioned.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer expects operating adjustments to be private habits that no inspector may observe or question.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer expects operating adjustments, such as correct firing, draft, and water level control in service, to be treated as tested material an inspector may observe or ask about.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer keeps operating adjustments in proper order because inspection covers the plant in service, not only its metal when cold. Firing, draft, and water level control show whether the boiler is actually being run within safe practice, which is why adjustments and their results form legitimate tested material.

questions.question: During a plant review of new york city feedwater regulator purpose, which of the following should the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer affirm?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes a feedwater regulator lowers boiler level by blowing down the water column at set intervals.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes a feedwater regulator holds steam pressure steady by venting steam from the boiler outlet.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes a feedwater regulator controls fuel pressure to the burner and has no connection with water level.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows that a feedwater regulator controls the flow of feedwater automatically to hold the boiler water level near its desired point as steam demand rises and falls.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer values the regulator for the steadiness it brings, feeding in proportion to demand instead of in surges by hand, because a level that hunts widely invites priming at the high side and uncovered surfaces at the low side, while a well kept regulator keeps level, circulation, and steam quality calm together.

questions.question: Regarding new york city gradual steam pressure raising, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer raises steam pressure without watching level or joints, because leaks and level swings only matter after the boiler is placed on the line
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer raises steam pressure with all vents and drains left open so the climb goes faster and condensate never collects anywhere
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer raises steam pressure in a single quick surge so the safety valves are proven under full load at the very start

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer raises steam pressure gradually after warmup, watching expansion, joint tightness, water level, and gauge response as pressure climbs toward the normal working range

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer raises pressure gradually so expansion stays orderly and small leaks, sticking gauges, or level swings announce themselves while firing can still be eased, whereas a sudden climb hides those warnings inside a rush of change and can carry a minor defect straight into full working pressure.

questions.question: Regarding new york city experience route other jurisdiction license, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: A reciprocity style route for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license accepts a driver license from another jurisdiction held for five years.

A reciprocity style route for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license accepts an expired license from a jurisdiction that ignores the national boiler and pressure vessel code.
A reciprocity style route for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license requires no employment at all during the last seven years.

A reciprocity style route for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license accepts a high pressure license or certification from another jurisdiction that follows the national boiler and pressure vessel code, held for five years with employment during five of the last seven years.

questions.explanation: Explanation: This route toward the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license depends on a high pressure license or certification from another jurisdiction that follows the national boiler and pressure vessel code. It must have been held for five years, with employment during five of the last seven years.

questions.question: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer is reviewing new york city maximum allowable working pressure meaning with a senior engineer. Which statement should guide the engineer's work?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes maximum allowable working pressure is the pressure at which a boiler is expected to burst in testing.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows that maximum allowable working pressure is the highest pressure at which a boiler or vessel is permitted to operate, a ceiling that normal operation must not exceed.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes maximum allowable working pressure is the average pressure a boiler carries during an ordinary working day.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes maximum allowable working pressure may be exceeded briefly whenever demand is heavy and the gauge is watched.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer reads the maximum allowable working pressure as the boundary drawn by design, material, and approval for that vessel, not as a target to approach, and firing, safety valve setting, and operating habit are all arranged to stay within it, because beyond that line the margin that protects metal, joints, and people is being spent.

questions.question: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer is reviewing new york city lubrication rounds duty with a senior engineer. Which statement should guide the engineer's work?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer ignores a hot and noisy bearing on rounds whenever its motor is still turning, since a running machine has proven it needs no attention
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer fills every bearing housing completely to the brim on rounds so no bearing can ever run short of oil between watches
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer oils rotating equipment only after it begins to seize or smoke, because lubricant added earlier is wasted on healthy bearings

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer checks oil levels, bearing condition, and lubrication of pumps, fans, and motors on rounds, and reports heating, noise, or leakage at once instead of waiting for a bearing to fail

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer includes lubrication in every round because feed pumps and draft fans are the auxiliaries the boiler depends on minute by minute, and a bearing caught while merely warm and noisy can be saved with oil or a planned repair, while the same bearing ignored becomes a seized pump and a boiler starved of feed or air.

questions.question: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer is reviewing new york city score release consent and question ownership with a senior engineer. Which statement should guide the engineer's work?

answers.text: The testing centre owns the examination questions for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license and may sell copies to candidates.
A candidate may refuse score release and still have results sent automatically for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license.

At scheduling, a candidate must consent to release the score to the Department, and the examination questions for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license are the copyrighted property of the Department.
The examination questions for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license belong to each candidate who takes the test.

questions.explanation: Explanation: Scheduling the examination for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license requires the candidate consent to release the score to the Department. The questions themselves remain the copyrighted property of the Department, so candidates may not treat them as their own material to copy or distribute.

questions.question: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer is reviewing new york city checking condensate return quality with a senior engineer. Which statement should guide the engineer's work?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows returned condensate should never be looked at or tested before it enters the feed system.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows any condensate, however dirty or oily, is always suitable as feedwater without question.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows returned condensate is watched and tested for contamination and hardness so only suitable water is reused as feedwater for the boiler.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows condensate quality is judged by tasting a sample drawn from the return line.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer protects the boiler at the return line, because condensate is only an asset while it stays clean, and steady watching catches a leaking heater or a fouled process early, before contaminated returns undo the good work of treatment.

questions.question: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer is reviewing new york city experience route approved apprenticeship with a senior engineer. Which statement should guide the engineer's work?

answers.text: An apprenticeship route for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license is completed by watching plant operations for one summer.
An apprenticeship route for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license accepts an unregistered informal apprenticeship of six months with no further experience.
An apprenticeship route for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license requires ten years of apprenticeship and no other experience.

An apprenticeship route for the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license requires a registered approved apprenticeship of at least two years plus three years of experience within the last seven years.

questions.explanation: Explanation: The apprenticeship route toward the New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer license combines a registered approved apprenticeship of at least two years with three additional years of experience gained within the last seven years. An informal or unregistered apprenticeship does not satisfy the first part of this route.

questions.question: Maya Singh, a New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer working in a residential high-rise plant in New York City, is preparing on new york city healthy flame appearance. Which of the following reflects sound practice?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows a healthy flame is steady, well shaped, firmly seated at the burner, and free of heavy smoke and wild flickering.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows a healthy flame drives hard against the furnace wall and stays pressed there.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows a healthy flame regularly blows out and relights itself many times each minute.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows a healthy flame is lopsided, smoky, and constantly lifting away from the burner.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer learns the look of a sound flame for each fuel so trouble is spotted early, because a flame that lifts, pulses, smokes, or strikes the furnace surfaces is reporting bad mixing, bad air, or a burner fault before instruments confirm it.

questions.question: David Kim, a New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer working in a high-rise office tower boiler plant in New York City, is preparing on new york city makeup water tank as auxiliary plant equipment. Which of the following reflects sound practice?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer keeps the makeup water tank as auxiliary plant equipment with a proven usable level, a working supply control, and a clear overflow path so losses in the plant can be replaced without delay.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer keeps the makeup water tank as auxiliary plant equipment only for washing floors, because makeup water never enters the boiler feed system at all.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer keeps the makeup water tank as auxiliary plant equipment sealed against any overflow, because an overflow path has no useful purpose on a storage tank.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer keeps the makeup water tank as auxiliary plant equipment deliberately empty so the feed pumps always draw directly from the street supply alone.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer watches the makeup tank as the reserve that replaces water lost through leaks, blowdown, and process use, because a tank found empty, overfilled, or with a failed supply control during heavy demand turns a manageable loss into a low water emergency at the boiler itself.

questions.question: Nina Petrov, a New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer working in a New York City municipal heating plant, is preparing on new york city piping joints and connections character. Which of the following reflects sound practice?

answers.text: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes the material of a piping gasket has no relation to the temperature of the fluid it must seal.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes a leaking piping joint will always seal itself with scale and can be left without concern.

A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer knows that piping joints and connections, whether flanged, welded, or threaded, must suit the pressure and temperature of the service and be made up properly so they remain tight in use.
A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer believes any piping joint form is suitable for any pressure if it is tightened hard enough at assembly.

questions.explanation: Explanation: A New York City high pressure boiler operating engineer treats every joint as a pressure boundary made by human hands, dependent on matched parts, sound surfaces, suitable gasket material, and even make up, because high pressure steam finds the smallest flaw in that boundary, cuts it larger with each escape, and punishes hurried or mismatched joint work without mercy.

north-carolina-independent-adjuster.quiz_title: North Carolina Independent Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: The declarations page of a policy typically contains which information?

answers.text: The full text of every exclusion in standardized wording only
The insurer's annual financial statements
The adjuster's internal claim notes
The named insured, policy period, limits, deductibles, and premium for that specific insured

questions.explanation: Declarations personalize the policy with who, what, when, limits, and price. Claim notes and financial statements are not part of the issued policy's declarations.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a managing general agent (MGA) for an insurer?

answers.text: To adjust only the insurer's largest catastrophe claims
To underwrite, bind, and service business for the insurer within delegated authority, often including appointing producers
To lend premium funds to insureds
To act as the state's insurance regulator

questions.explanation: MGAs exercise delegated underwriting and production authority for carriers. Regulation belongs to the state department, not to a private MGA, so that choice confuses private delegation with public authority.

questions.question: Which set lists the four elements a claimant must prove to establish negligence?

answers.text: Intent, motive, malice, and punishment
Duty, breach of duty, causation, and damages
Contract, offer, acceptance, and consideration
Notice, appraisal, subrogation, and salvage

questions.explanation: Negligence requires a duty owed, a breach of the standard of care, causation linking the breach to harm, and actual damages. Intent and malice belong to intentional-tort analysis, not to the basic negligence elements.

questions.question: What does salvage value do in a total loss where the insured retains the vehicle?

answers.text: Salvage is added to the payment as a bonus
The retained salvage value is deducted from the settlement because the insured keeps an asset with remaining value
Salvage has no effect when the owner keeps the car
The insurer must pay the loan balance instead

questions.explanation: Owner-retained salvage prevents double recovery: the insured receives value in cash plus the wreck itself, so the wreck's value offsets the cash payment.

questions.question: What makes medical charges reasonable and necessary for evaluation purposes?

answers.text: Treatment is necessary only if the claimant's attorney selected the provider
Only the cheapest available treatment counts as necessary
Any charge a provider bills is automatically reasonable
The treatment was appropriate for the diagnosed injury, related to the accident, and charged at rates consistent with the area and service

questions.explanation: Reasonableness and necessity turn on appropriateness to the injury, accident-relatedness, and customary charges for the service and area. Billed amounts alone, cheapest-only rules, and attorney selection do not establish any of those elements.

questions.question: Why do adjusters refer suspected application misrepresentation to underwriting or coverage counsel rather than deciding rescission alone at the claim desk?

answers.text: Materiality and reliance are fact-specific determinations that affect whether the contract can be voided
Adjusters are never allowed to read applications
Rescission is automatic for any inaccurate word in an application
Coverage counsel must approve every routine claim payment

questions.explanation: Rescission depends on proving the statement false, material, and relied upon, which requires careful review. Minor inaccuracies do not automatically void a policy, contrary to the automatic-rescission distractor.

questions.question: Why does the principle of utmost good faith matter most at application and claim time?

answers.text: Each party relies heavily on the honesty and disclosure of the other
It allows the insurer to rewrite the policy after a loss
It removes the need for any written policy wording
It guarantees payment even when a loss is excluded

questions.explanation: Utmost good faith requires full honesty because the insurer relies on the applicant's disclosures and the insured relies on the insurer's promise. It never authorizes rewriting terms after a loss to suit either side.

questions.question: Why do contracts commonly require one party to be added as an additional insured on another party's liability policy?

answers.text: To transfer the named insured's license to the additional insured
To guarantee the contract price will never change
To align insurance protection with the contract's allocation of risk, so the party that required the status is defended for claims arising from the other party's operations
To allow the additional insured to stop paying its own taxes

questions.explanation: Additional insured requirements back up indemnity and risk-allocation promises in construction, lease and service contracts. They transfer specified liability protection, not licenses, tax duties or price guarantees.

questions.question: Efficient proximate cause doctrine holds that when a loss follows a chain of events:

answers.text: The adjuster may select the cause that produces the lowest payment
Every cause in the chain must be covered or nothing is covered
Coverage is determined by the peril that set the chain in motion, if that peril is the efficient or dominant cause
Coverage is always determined by the last event to touch the property, no matter what started the chain

questions.explanation: The doctrine looks to the cause that started the train of events in motion, not mechanically to the last link. It also forbids picking a cause based on which outcome is cheapest for the insurer.

questions.question: A dwelling policy shows Coverage A of $300,000 and the insured asks what the automatic other-structures amount is. The adjuster should state:

answers.text: $90,000, which is 30 percent of the dwelling limit
$300,000, equal to the dwelling limit
$150,000, which is half the dwelling limit
$30,000, which is 10 percent of the dwelling limit

questions.explanation: Ten percent of $300,000 is $30,000 for other structures. The one-half and 30-percent figures are derivations used for other coverages and would overstate this particular automatic limit.

questions.question: A small charter operator in Fayetteville suffers hull damage to its aircraft in a hard landing. Which specialty line's adjustment skills apply?

answers.text: Boiler coverage, because aircraft have engines
Surety bonding, because the operator holds a license
Crop insurance, because the landing occurred near a field
Aviation insurance, where hull damage and liability are adjusted with attention to airworthiness, certified repair, and regulatory documentation

questions.explanation: Aircraft losses belong to aviation insurance, a specialty line where repair standards, certification, and regulatory records shape the adjustment.

questions.question: A North Carolina application was submitted seven months ago and the candidate never tested. What is the application's status?

answers.text: It stays valid for a full two years
It remains valid until the candidate tests once
It converts automatically into a license application renewal
It is no longer valid, because initial applications are valid for six months

questions.explanation: Six months is the validity window. At seven months without testing, the application has expired.

questions.question: All of the following describe morale hazards EXCEPT:

answers.text: Carelessness about locking doors after buying theft coverage
A carefully maintained sprinkler system in a Durham office building
Indifference to a small leak because a policy covers water damage
An insured who leaves keys in an unlocked car because insurance will pay

questions.explanation: A maintained sprinkler system is a protective safeguard, not an attitude of indifference. Morale hazard arises from carelessness or indifference that develops because insurance exists to absorb the loss.

questions.question: Scenario: Charlotte retailer Ana buys an adjoining storefront and asks her producer to 'just note it in the file.' Adjuster Tom later handles a fire there. What is the coverage concern?

answers.text: Without an endorsement adding the premises, the new storefront may not be a covered location at all
File notes automatically extend property coverage to any building the insured buys
The fire is covered because Ana paid rent on the new space
Coverage applies but the deductible is doubled for noted locations

questions.explanation: Property coverage follows scheduled locations and the new-acquired-property provisions, not informal file notes. Tom must check whether any endorsement or automatic provision reaches the unscheduled storefront.

questions.question: A commercial roof in Charlotte would cost $20,000 to replace. It is 10 years into a 20-year useful life, with straight-line depreciation and no other adjustment stated. What is its actual cash value?
questions.explanation: Ten years divided by a 20-year life is 50% depreciation. Fifty percent of $20,000 is $10,000 of depreciation, leaving an actual cash value of $20,000 minus $10,000, or $10,000.

questions.question: A business income policy has a limit of $120,000 with a monthly limit factor of 1/4 as stated in the stem. What is the most payable for business income loss in any one month?
questions.explanation: The monthly limitation caps each month at the stated fraction of the limit. One-fourth of $120,000 is $30,000 per month, even if the actual monthly loss is larger.

questions.question: Two people are injured in one North Carolina accident under a minimum-limits policy, each with seventy thousand dollars of bodily injury damages. The policy pays:

answers.text: One hundred thousand to the first claimant only
Seventy thousand to each from the liability coverage
Thirty thousand to each under the current limits
Fifty thousand to each, reaching the one hundred thousand per-accident bodily injury cap

questions.explanation: Per-person and per-accident caps both bind. Each claimant is capped at fifty thousand, and together they exhaust the one hundred thousand accident limit.

questions.question: A Jacksonville homeowner's insurer pays for water damage caused by a failed washing-machine hose made by a national manufacturer. The strongest subrogation practice is for the adjuster to:

answers.text: Settle and close without noting the product involved
Retain the failed hose, photograph the scene, and record the product identifiers before disposal
Mail the hose back to the homeowner without documentation
Advise the homeowner to discard the hose to avoid clutter

questions.explanation: Recovery against a manufacturer turns on the failed product and documented identifiers. Undocumented disposal, the tempting shortcut, destroys the proof the recovery would need.

questions.question: A Jacksonville cabin insured on an open perils basis is damaged by an excluded earth-movement event. The owner argues the policy must pay because earth movement is not in a list of covered perils he was shown. The adjuster should explain that:

answers.text: Open perils policies have no exclusions, so the loss must be paid
Earth movement becomes covered whenever the amount exceeds the deductible
Open perils coverage is defeated by an applicable exclusion even though the grant itself is broad
The owner is correct because only named perils policies use exclusions

questions.explanation: The broad grant and the exclusions work together under open perils: an excluded cause is not covered. Exclusions are not unique to named-perils forms, and the deductible never creates a covered cause.

questions.question: Which business would most likely fall outside standard BOP eligibility and need a commercial package policy instead?

answers.text: A two-person accounting office
A large auto dealership with extensive open lot inventory and high total values
A neighborhood gift shop with modest inventory
A small owner-operated hair salon in a strip center

questions.explanation: BOP eligibility is aimed at smaller, lower-hazard operations with value and size limits; large dealerships and similar high-value or high-hazard risks are written on commercial package or specialized forms.

north-carolina-building-contractor.quiz_title: North Carolina Building Contractor Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Building pad compaction on a student housing project in Boone is verified how?

answers.text: By driving over it and judging the feel
By the color of the soil after rolling
By field density testing of the compacted lifts against the specified density, lift by lift
By counting the roller's passes alone

questions.explanation: Passes and feel do not prove density. Testing each lift is what shows the specification was actually met.

questions.question: A roof cricket or saddle on a school building project in Charlotte is built where, and why?

answers.text: At the ridge for decoration
Under every skylight curb
Inside the gutter
Behind a chimney or other wide obstruction on the slope, to split and divert water around it instead of letting it pond against the uphill flashing

questions.explanation: Any wide uphill obstruction is a dam. The cricket is the small roof that moves the water around it.

questions.question: A plan's scale is used by the estimator on a retail center project in Asheville to do what?

answers.text: Decorate the title block
Convert measurements taken from the drawing into real dimensions of the work, checking them against figured dimensions wherever the drawings give them
Replace all written dimensions
Measure only when no dimensions exist and trust the scale over the figures

questions.explanation: Figured dimensions govern over scaled ones. Scaling is a check and a fallback, not the authority.

questions.question: High-strength bolting on a dealership building project in Goldsboro achieves its clamping force how, in principle?

answers.text: By using the largest wrench available once
By painting the bolts after snugging them by feel
By welding every bolt after installation
By tightening the bolt assembly to a verified tension using an approved method, so the connected plies are clamped together as the design assumes

questions.explanation: Pretensioned joints work by clamping force, and that force must be achieved by a verified method, not by feel.

questions.question: Hot weather concreting on a school building project in Charlotte calls for extra care mainly because of what?

answers.text: Concrete never sets in hot weather
Hot weather always doubles the strength
Forms cannot be used above mild temperatures
Rapid moisture loss and faster setting, which can cause plastic shrinkage cracking and a weaker surface if curing is not protected

questions.explanation: Heat accelerates both setting and drying. Protecting moisture and timing the finishing are the countermeasures.

questions.question: Post-tensioning tendons on a distribution center project in Salisbury may be stressed only when what condition is met?

answers.text: The crew has a free afternoon
The forms look dry
The tendons have been in place a full month
The concrete has reached the strength the design specifies for stressing, verified as the documents require

questions.explanation: Stressing too early can crush or crack immature concrete. The specified strength is the gate.

questions.question: Roof trusses on a clinic building project in Lumberton arrive on site and one is damaged in unloading. The framer should do what?

answers.text: Nail a board alongside the break and set it
Use it in the middle of the roof where it is hidden
Cut out the damaged web and continue
Keep it out of the structure and get a repair designed or approved by the truss designer or engineer rather than sistering boards by guess

questions.explanation: A truss is an engineered system whose members work together. Field-designed repairs guess at forces the designer calculated.

questions.question: A payment bond on a municipal building project in Wilmington on public work protects whom, and why does that matter more there?

answers.text: Only the owner's lender
Subcontractors and suppliers, who cannot lien public property — the bond is their substitute remedy for getting paid
The general contractor's own profit
No one; it is a formality

questions.explanation: Public property cannot be liened, so the bond stands in the lien's place for the people who furnished the work.

questions.question: Sports lighting on a dealership building project in Goldsboro must be aimed and shielded to achieve what two goals at once?

answers.text: The brightest possible light in all directions
Light aimed at the spectators for visibility
Only the field's centre needs light
Even, glare-controlled light on the playing surface for the athletes, and minimal spill and glare onto neighbours and the sky

questions.explanation: Good sports lighting is precision optics on poles: bright where the game is, dark where it is not.

questions.question: A pump is used to place concrete on a mixed-use building project in Cary. The mix must be adjusted how, compared with chute placement?

answers.text: Any mix pumps if enough water is added
It must be a pumpable mix — cohesive and properly graded — approved for pumping, not simply the chute mix with water added at the pump
Pumping needs no mix change and no approval
The pump operator may redesign the mix freely

questions.explanation: Pumping is a different placement method with its own mix requirements. Water is not the adjustment.

questions.question: Soil and existing-conditions information in the documents on a warehouse project in Durham is handled by the prudent bidder how?

answers.text: He studies what is furnished, visits the site, and prices the conditions he can foresee, while noting the contract's rules for conditions that differ from those indicated
He assumes perfect conditions in every bid
Site visits are a waste of bid time
Differing conditions are always the contractor's cost by law

questions.explanation: Ground risk is allocated by the documents and priced by the informed. The site visit is part of the estimate.

questions.question: Soil and existing-conditions information in the documents on a laboratory building project in Durham is handled by the prudent bidder how?

answers.text: He assumes perfect conditions in every bid
Site visits are a waste of bid time
Differing conditions are always the contractor's cost by law
He studies what is furnished, visits the site, and prices the conditions he can foresee, while noting the contract's rules for conditions that differ from those indicated

questions.explanation: Ground risk is allocated by the documents and priced by the informed. The site visit is part of the estimate.

questions.question: Grouting of reinforced masonry on a courthouse annex project in Asheville must be consolidated and the cells must be kept how before grouting?

answers.text: Partially filled with rubble to save grout
Wet with standing water
Clean and free of mortar fins and debris that would block the grout, so the grout fully fills the cells around the reinforcement
Blocked at random to create chambers

questions.explanation: Grouted reinforcement only works if grout actually surrounds the steel. Cleanouts and inspection exist for that reason.

questions.question: Refrigerant and condensate lines on a student housing project in Boone from rooftop and air-handler equipment must be routed and supported so that what is avoided?

answers.text: The lines looking untidy
Any need for a drain at all
Noise from the equipment
Condensate overflow into ceilings and walls, and refrigerant line damage — water from a clogged or badly sloped drain is one of the commonest building leaks

questions.explanation: Condensate is a plumbing problem attached to a mechanical system. Its drains deserve the same respect as any waste line.

questions.question: Marks on a bank building project in Burlington have faded or been destroyed by site traffic before the dig is finished. The excavator should do what?

answers.text: Have the facilities re-marked through the one-call process rather than digging from memory of where the marks were
Dig from the superintendent's recollection
Assume the lines follow the old marks exactly
Repaint the marks himself where he thinks they were

questions.explanation: Only the operators' locators can restore authoritative marks. Memory is not a marking system.

questions.question: Truss bracing on a parking deck project in Charlotte — temporary during erection and permanent in the finished roof — is required because of what?

answers.text: Bracing is only to keep trusses from blowing off the truck
Trusses are stable as soon as they touch the walls
Bracing replaces the roof sheathing
Individual trusses are slender and unstable out of plane; bracing ties them into a system that can carry its design loads and survive erection

questions.explanation: A truss alone is a mechanism waiting to fold sideways. Bracing is what makes the roof a structure.

questions.question: Steel lintels, shelf angles, and embed plates for masonry on a warehouse project in Durham must be coordinated early primarily because of what?

answers.text: They are cast or built into other trades' work on a schedule — a missed embed cannot be added after the concrete or masonry has closed over its location
They are the most expensive items on the job
They can always be surface-mounted later with equal performance
Coordination is a paperwork formality

questions.explanation: Embeds are one-way doors in the schedule. Coordination is how they exist when the pour or the wall arrives.

questions.question: A takeoff finds a net quantity of 300 units and the estimate adds a waste allowance of 15 percent. Using order quantity = net quantity + net quantity x waste percent / 100, how many units should be ordered?

answers.text: 390 units
345 units
370 units
300 units

questions.explanation: Allowance = 300 x 15 / 100 = 45. Order quantity = 300 + 45 = 345 units.

questions.question: A worker on a laboratory building project in Durham is found operating equipment he is not trained or authorized to run. The supervisor's correct action is to do what?

answers.text: Stop the work, remove him from the equipment, and address it as a training and enforcement failure — not let it continue because the work is behind
Look the other way if he seems capable
Punish only if an accident happens
Let him finish the shift first

questions.explanation: Unauthorized operation is a system failure caught in time. Stopping it is the supervisor's core function.

questions.question: A contractor bidding work on a community college building project in Gastonia must include in his price the costs of supervision, temporary facilities, insurance, and taxes — not only direct labor and materials — because of what?

answers.text: Owners reimburse them separately by law
Those job and overhead costs are real costs of delivering the work; a bid that omits them wins the job and loses the money
They are optional courtesies
They are covered by the performance bond

questions.explanation: Underpricing indirect costs is how profitable-looking bid days become losing jobs. The full cost is the only honest base.

louisiana-independent-adjuster.quiz_title: Louisiana Independent Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which feature of a valued policy is an exception to strict indemnity measurement?

answers.text: It pays nothing unless the insured proves negligence
It pays the face amount agreed in advance for a total loss, regardless of actual cash value at that time
It always pays twice the actual loss amount
It eliminates the need for insurable interest

questions.explanation: A valued policy fixes the amount in advance for total loss, departing from after-the-fact value measurement. It does not remove insurable interest, which remains required.

questions.question: Who must generally agree to a policy change that reduces coverage mid-term?

answers.text: The insurer and the named insured, documented by endorsement, rather than a producer acting alone
Only the adjuster assigned to the last claim
No one, because reductions take effect automatically when premium is late
Only the certificate holder for the policy

questions.explanation: A contract cannot be rewritten by one outsider. Material mid-term reductions need the contracting parties' agreement and an endorsement so the claim file later shows exactly what was in force.

questions.question: What is the difference between vacancy and unoccupancy for homeowners adjusting?

answers.text: They mean exactly the same thing in all forms
Unoccupancy is always worse and always voids coverage
Vacancy generally means the building lacks both occupants and customary furnishings, while unoccupancy means occupants are absent but the home remains furnished and intended for return
Vacancy applies only to commercial buildings

questions.explanation: Adjusters must separate a truly vacant building from a furnished home whose occupants are traveling. Applying vacancy limitations to a merely unoccupied home overstates the restriction.

questions.question: What is the insurer's duty to defend under Part A?

answers.text: To prosecute the insured's own claim against another driver
To defend only if the insured is ultimately found liable
To defend a suit seeking covered damages, with the duty generally ending when the applicable limit is exhausted by judgment or settlement
To defend every lawsuit against the insured for any reason

questions.explanation: The defense duty attaches to suits seeking damages within coverage and is broader than the duty to indemnify, but it is tied to the liability limit and the relief sought.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a bodily injury reserve review after surgery is recommended?

answers.text: To lock the reserve at its original figure for consistency
To update the reserve to reflect the materially increased treatment cost, recovery time, and damages exposure shown by the new medical information
To reduce the reserve because surgery makes settlement less likely
To close the file until surgery is complete and bills arrive

questions.explanation: Material medical developments require reserve updates reflecting the changed exposure, with the file kept active through treatment. Freezing, cutting, or shelving the reserve and file in response to surgery misstates and mishandles the claim.

questions.question: What happens when an insured carries a limit equal to the full coinsurance requirement and suffers a covered partial loss?

answers.text: The insurer pays double the loss as a compliance reward
The deductible is refunded in full at claim time
Coinsurance converts the policy into a liability policy
The loss is paid up to the limit without a coinsurance penalty, subject to the deductible and other terms

questions.explanation: Meeting the coinsurance requirement removes the proportional penalty; ordinary terms like the deductible still apply. No bonus or refund is triggered by compliance.

questions.question: Which scenario most clearly supports a punitive damages claim rather than compensatory damages alone?

answers.text: A clerk makes an arithmetic error on a single invoice that is later corrected
A careful driver momentarily misjudges a stopping distance and rear-ends another car
A company knowingly keeps selling a product it has documented will catch fire, conceals the reports, and a buyer is burned
A homeowner forgets to salt an icy step one morning and a visitor slips

questions.explanation: Knowingly selling a documented fire hazard while concealing reports shows malice or conscious disregard well beyond ordinary carelessness. A momentary misjudgment, a single oversight or a corrected arithmetic error are ordinary negligence or mistake, supporting compensation at most.

questions.question: What insurance-to-value condition is commonly required for replacement cost loss settlement under DP-2 and DP-3?

answers.text: The dwelling must be insured to at least 50 percent of its market value
The dwelling must be insured to at least 80 percent of its full replacement cost at the time of loss
No minimum amount of insurance is ever required
The contents must be insured to 100 percent of market value

questions.explanation: Replacement cost settlement under the broad and special dwelling forms is tied to carrying at least 80 percent of replacement cost. Using market value as the yardstick is wrong because the condition measures insurance against replacement cost, not sale price.

questions.question: A college student is a family member but lives at school most of the year with the insured car. Why must the adjuster dig into residency and garaging?

answers.text: Because residency affects family member status and garaging affects rating, and the facts determine which provisions apply
Because Part B never covers students
Because students are never insureds
Because the car becomes a commercial auto at school

questions.explanation: Away-at-school facts are fact-specific: the adjuster examines household residency, vehicle garaging, and any student endorsement rather than applying a blanket student exclusion.

questions.question: An adjuster suspects a policy was obtained by concealing a household driver. What is the ethical, lawful handling?

answers.text: Investigate fully, document the application facts, and make the coverage decision on verified evidence with a clear written explanation
Deny immediately on suspicion alone to save time
Ignore the issue and pay a known fraudulent amount
Tell the claimant a false reason for denial

questions.explanation: Suspicion is not proof; a complete investigation and an honest written decision satisfy both the policy conditions and fair claims standards.

questions.question: Mortgage guaranty and financial guaranty are specialty products an adjuster may see described in a commercial file. What do they fundamentally guarantee?

answers.text: The physical condition of buildings securing the loans
Crop yields used to repay farm loans
Payment of defined financial obligations, such as mortgage loan defaults or bond debt service, when the obligor fails to pay as agreed
The honesty of the lender's own employees

questions.explanation: Guaranty lines are financial in nature: they stand behind specified payment obligations rather than insuring physical property or employee honesty.

questions.question: A worker is injured in a Baton Rouge accident in August 2024. How long does the injury claim have before it prescribes?

answers.text: Two years from the day the injury was sustained
One year from the day treatment ended
Two years from the day the insurer denied the claim
One year from the day the injury was sustained

questions.explanation: Injury claims arising on or after July 1, 2024 prescribe in two years, measured from the day the injury or damage was sustained.

questions.question: Adjuster Omar is reviewing a Baton Rouge claim where the insured never sent the required proof of loss described in the policy. Omar's coverage review should focus on the policy's:

answers.text: Conditions, which set duties and requirements that must be satisfied
Marketing materials, which describe the insurer generally
Endorsement schedule, which adds a new vehicle
Declarations, which list the insured's name and address

questions.explanation: Proof-of-loss duties are conditions precedent to recovery under many policies. Declarations identify the insured but do not impose the post-loss duties at issue.

questions.question: All of the following are true about additional insureds EXCEPT:

answers.text: An additional insured may unilaterally raise the policy limits for its own benefit
The named insured's premium is based in part on exposures that generate additional insured obligations
Certificates often evidence additional insured status, but the endorsement itself controls the coverage
An additional insured can generally make a claim and receive a defense for covered suits within the endorsement's scope

questions.explanation: Limits are set by the policy the named insured bought; an additional insured cannot raise them on its own. The endorsement, not the certificate, is the controlling document when the two differ.

questions.question: All of the following are true of HO-5 EXCEPT:

answers.text: It provides broader contents coverage than HO-3
It is intended for owner-occupied dwellings that qualify for the program
It limits the dwelling to basic-form perils only
It remains subject to policy exclusions and conditions

questions.explanation: The comprehensive form expands rather than narrows coverage, so limiting its dwelling to basic perils contradicts its purpose. Its breadth still does not remove exclusions and conditions.

questions.question: A New Orleans hotel suffers covered damage and loses room revenue, but also saves the housekeeping wages and laundry costs it would have incurred for those rooms. How does that affect the claim?

answers.text: Saved, noncontinuing expenses reduce the business income loss because indemnity covers net income plus expenses that actually continue
Saved expenses are added to the loss as a penalty
The claim is denied because some expenses were saved
Savings are ignored and gross room revenue is paid in full

questions.explanation: If an expense stops during the shutdown, the business did not lose it. Crediting noncontinuing expenses keeps the payment at true economic loss rather than a windfall.

questions.question: A catastrophe adjuster working a hurricane in Louisiana has registration privileges revoked on the spot. Which complaint about the process is answered by the rules?

answers.text: Revocation of those privileges can occur without notice and hearing
Revocation can only happen at renewal time
Revocation requires the adjuster's written consent
Revocation always requires 60 days of notice

questions.explanation: Catastrophe privileges are uniquely revocable without notice and hearing, unlike ordinary license actions.

questions.question: EXCEPT — Which of the following parties would NOT ordinarily request a certificate of insurance?

answers.text: A landlord leasing warehouse space in New Orleans
A customer buying a single retail item with no contract, lease, or loan involved
A general contractor hiring a subcontractor in Lafayette
A lender financing commercial equipment in Baton Rouge

questions.explanation: Certificates exist to prove compliance with a contractual insurance requirement. An ordinary retail purchase creates no such requirement, unlike leases, subcontracts, and financed purchases.

questions.question: An adjuster asks homeowner Noah in Mandeville to separate damaged from undamaged property and make the damaged items available for inspection. Under what duty does this fall?

answers.text: The duty belongs only to the mortgage company
The duty to show and preserve damaged property and cooperate with the investigation as the conditions require
No duty, because inspection is optional for the insured
The liability defense duty

questions.explanation: Cooperation and inspection duties let the insurer verify the loss it is asked to pay. Refusing all inspection while demanding payment contradicts the conditions the insured agreed to.

questions.question: All of the following would be business personal property for a Baton Rouge medical office under BOP Section I EXCEPT:

answers.text: The building's load-bearing exterior wall, which is part of the building itself
Exam tables used to treat patients
Computers used for scheduling and billing
Medical supplies held for use in the practice

questions.explanation: Contents the practice owns and uses in its business are business personal property, while a load-bearing exterior wall is part of the insured building and belongs under building coverage, not contents coverage.

hawaii-business-law.quiz_title: Hawaii Business and Law Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What basic rights do shareholders hold in a Hawaii contracting business in Kailua as a corporation?

answers.text: They direct daily field operations on every project
They withdraw corporate funds freely for personal use
They elect directors, vote on major corporate changes, and share in distributions when declared
They sign contracts that bind the corporation whenever they wish

questions.explanation: Shareholders own and vote, while day to day direction sits with directors and officers.

questions.question: Which body licenses contractors statewide for a Hawaii contracting firm in Honolulu?

answers.text: The largest supplier the firm buys materials from
The Contractors License Board, acting within the professional and vocational licensing division of the state commerce and consumer affairs department
The county building department in the county where the work sits
The trade association the firm chooses to join

questions.explanation: Contractor licensing in Hawaii is a statewide function of the board within the licensing division.

questions.question: What are the employer duties around protective equipment at a Hawaii contracting business in Kailua?

answers.text: Workers must always supply and maintain their own required gear
Equipment condition is the worker concern alone
Providing equipment excuses the firm from checking its use
To provide the required equipment without shifting its cost burden improperly, maintain it, and ensure workers use it correctly

questions.explanation: Providing, maintaining, and enforcing equipment use belong together.

questions.question: What is the accounting equation that underlies the books of a Hawaii contracting business in Honolulu?

answers.text: What the firm owns equals what it owes plus the ownership interest, so every recorded event keeps the books in balance
Expenses end when a job ends
Profit equals the balance in the bank account
Revenue always equals cash received

questions.explanation: The equation keeps assets, obligations, and ownership interest in balance.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a written safety programme at a Hawaii design-build contracting firm in Kailua Kona?

answers.text: To create paperwork that substitutes for safe practice
To shift all safety duties onto the newest workers
To be written once and never revisited
To set out responsibilities, procedures, training, and review so hazard control is systematic rather than improvised

questions.explanation: A written programme turns safety into an organised system.

questions.question: How does arbitration differ from mediation for a dispute involving a Hawaii building contracting company in Kailua Kona?

answers.text: Arbitration produces only a nonbinding suggestion
An arbitrator hears the case and issues a binding decision, while a mediator helps the parties reach their own settlement
A mediator imposes a binding award on both parties
Both processes always end with a jury verdict

questions.explanation: Arbitration decides the dispute and mediation facilitates a voluntary settlement.

questions.question: How can a written agreement change at-will status at a Hawaii general contracting company in Kailua?

answers.text: Only a verbal promise can change at-will status
Written promises never bind an employer
A promise of continued employment or a stated process for ending it can bind the firm beyond ordinary at-will terms
Handbook wording can never create obligations

questions.explanation: Words the firm puts in writing can limit its own freedom to dismiss.

questions.question: What should a Hawaii general contracting company in Waianae do when materials arrive on site?

answers.text: Install materials immediately before any inspection occurs
Accept every delivery unchecked and store it wherever space exists
Inspect them against the accepted submittal and order, note damage or shortages at delivery, and store them protected as the manufacturer directs
Reject materials that match the order to keep suppliers alert

questions.explanation: Delivery inspection and proper storage protect material quality and payment accuracy.

questions.question: How does an express contract differ from an implied contract for a Hawaii design-build contracting firm in Aiea?

answers.text: An express contract is always oral and an implied contract is always written
An implied contract has no legal effect under any circumstances
An express contract states its terms in words, while an implied contract is shown by the conduct of the parties
An express contract needs no agreement on price or scope

questions.explanation: Express terms are stated directly and implied terms are inferred from behavior.

questions.question: How should a Hawaii contracting firm in Kailua-Kona separate direct costs from indirect costs in an estimate?

answers.text: Direct costs trace to specific work on the project, while indirect costs support the work without belonging to a single item
Direct costs include only office rent and company advertising
Indirect costs are the profit added at the end of the bid
Direct costs are always paid by the customer and indirect costs by subcontractors

questions.explanation: Direct costs attach to project work and indirect costs support performance more generally.

questions.question: Why should a Hawaii contracting business in Waianae investigate incidents and near misses?

answers.text: Near misses prove the system is working perfectly
Investigation is needed only when an insurer demands it
To find the causes and correct them, so the same weakness does not produce the next, larger loss
To find a person to blame and close the file

questions.explanation: A near miss is a free lesson; investigation is how the lesson is collected.

questions.question: How should a Hawaii contracting business in Kailua-Kona separate direct costs from indirect costs in an estimate?

answers.text: Direct costs include only office rent and company advertising
Indirect costs are the profit added at the end of the bid
Direct costs trace to specific work on the project, while indirect costs support the work without belonging to a single item
Direct costs are always paid by the customer and indirect costs by subcontractors

questions.explanation: Direct costs attach to project work and indirect costs support performance more generally.

questions.question: A job of a Hawaii building contracting company in Waipahu has a total estimated cost of $245,000 and costs incurred to date of $175,000. What is the cost to complete?
questions.explanation: Cost to complete = total estimated cost - costs incurred = 245,000 - 175,000 = $70,000.

questions.question: Why can a lien generally not attach to public property in work by a Hawaii building contracting company in Waipahu?

answers.text: Government owners are exempt from paying for work
Because public property is held for public use and may not be seized or sold to satisfy a private claim
Liens are unnecessary because public work is always prepaid
Public projects never leave anyone unpaid

questions.explanation: Public property is shielded from seizure for private claims.

questions.question: Why must withheld payroll amounts at a Hawaii building contracting company in Mililani never fund operations?

answers.text: Trust treatment applies only to large payrolls
Because they are trust amounts taken from worker pay for the government, and using them exposes the firm and those directing it to serious consequences
Successful trading excuses the borrowing
Temporary use is acceptable if repaid quietly

questions.explanation: Trust money is never working capital.

questions.question: A consumer complaint about the work of a Hawaii construction firm in Lihue reaches the board. How should the firm respond?

answers.text: Cooperate with the inquiry, respond as required, and produce its records, treating the complaint as part of licensed accountability
Destroy job records so the inquiry ends quickly
Ignore the inquiry because complaints are private disputes only
Refuse all contact until the customer withdraws the complaint

questions.explanation: Answering to the regulator is part of the bargain of holding a license.

questions.question: How does a force majeure clause help a Hawaii general contracting company in Lihue when extraordinary events beyond its control halt the work?

answers.text: It allocates relief, usually added time, for delays caused by events neither party controls, as the clause defines
It transfers all project risks to the customer permanently
It excuses the contractor from finishing the project at all
It guarantees added payment for every weather day

questions.explanation: Force majeure language defines relief for truly uncontrollable events.

questions.question: The balance sheet of a Hawaii building contracting company in Hilo shows total assets of $160,000 and equity of $120,000. Using assets = liabilities + equity, what are the firm's total liabilities?
questions.explanation: Liabilities = assets - equity = 160,000 - 120,000 = $40,000.

questions.question: When might a Hawaii building contracting company in Hanapepe need cover for errors in professional services it supplies, such as design work it undertakes?

answers.text: When the firm takes on design or professional duties, because general liability cover is aimed at injury and damage, not pure professional error
Never, because design mistakes cause no losses
Professional duties are covered by vehicle cover
Only if a customer insists in writing

questions.explanation: Taking on professional duty creates a distinct exposure needing its own treatment.

questions.question: On a job for a Hawaii design-build contracting firm in Honolulu, costs incurred to date are $680,000 and total estimated cost is $800,000. What is the percent complete, computed as costs incurred divided by total estimated cost?
questions.explanation: Percent complete = 680,000 / 800,000 = 85%.

new-hampshire-independent-adjuster.quiz_title: New Hampshire Independent Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the role of a special investigations unit (SIU) within an insurer?

answers.text: To set premium rates for all new policies
To sell policies in territories without producers
To investigate suspected fraud using trained staff, coordinate evidence, and support referrals to authorities when warranted
To replace adjusters on every large claim regardless of suspicion

questions.explanation: SIU is the insurer's specialized fraud-investigation function. Rate-setting and sales belong to other departments, and SIU involvement is driven by suspicion indicators, not claim size alone.

questions.question: An additional insured under a liability policy is best described as:

answers.text: Anyone who receives a property loss check as a lender
A person or organization added by endorsement that receives liability coverage under the named insured's policy, usually for liability arising from the named insured's operations or work
A beneficiary who automatically owns the policy
The insurer's appointed adjuster for a claim

questions.explanation: Additional insured status is a liability concept: the endorsement extends defense and indemnity, typically tied to the named insured's work or operations. Receiving a property check as a lender describes a loss payee, a different role.

questions.question: What is the insured's duty regarding damaged personal property documentation?

answers.text: Destroy receipts to speed the claim
Provide only a total dollar figure with no itemization ever required
Refuse to list property that was completely destroyed
Prepare an inventory showing quantity, description, actual cash value and amount of loss, with bills and receipts when available

questions.explanation: An itemized inventory is how contents losses are verified and valued. A bare total with no items gives the adjuster nothing to test against the policy's limits and valuation rules.

questions.question: A trailer owned by the named insured is used with a covered auto. How is it treated?

answers.text: Trailers are covered only as dwellings
Trailers are never covered for any purpose
Owned trailers can be covered autos for liability under the definitions, while physical damage needs the trailer to be described or otherwise covered
Trailer damage is always paid under medical payments

questions.explanation: Liability follows the described trailer combination, but damage to the trailer itself requires its own physical damage grant, a distinction adjusters must explain clearly.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a bodily injury reserve review after surgery is recommended?

answers.text: To lock the reserve at its original figure for consistency
To update the reserve to reflect the materially increased treatment cost, recovery time, and damages exposure shown by the new medical information
To reduce the reserve because surgery makes settlement less likely
To close the file until surgery is complete and bills arrive
