answers.text: When the insured and insurer disagree on the value of the property or the amount of loss, the policy's appraisal clause lets either party demand, in writing, that each side select a competent, impartial appraiser; the appraisers choose an umpire, and an award agreed by any two of the three sets the amount of loss — appraisal decides value, not coverage.
An appraisal award may be set at any figure the umpire prefers.
Appraisal decides whether the loss is covered.
The insurer's appraiser must be its own employee.

questions.explanation: In one line: Appraisal is a valuation machine, not a coverage court — and in Kansas a public adjuster's own conduct rules forbid wearing the appraiser's hat on their own claim.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of matching and uniformity?

answers.text: Matching is never a legitimate valuation issue.

Valuation disputes often turn on matching: whether repairing only the damaged portion of a roof plane, facade, or floor leaves a reasonably uniform appearance, or whether the scope must extend so new work matches the surviving property in kind, quality, and appearance.
The scope always extends to the whole exterior automatically.
Contractors alone decide matching questions.

questions.explanation: Matching fights are scope fights: documented evidence of color, profile, and the availability of original materials is what resolves them. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: On the subject of equipment breakdown, which statement is right?

answers.text: The coverage excludes the failed object itself.
Spoilage extensions require no breakdown trigger.
Wear and tear is covered as breakdown.

Equipment breakdown coverage insures sudden and accidental mechanical breakdown, electrical arcing, and pressure-equipment failure of boilers and machinery, paying for repair or replacement of the equipment, resulting damage to other property, and related business income and spoilage where the form provides.

questions.explanation: Breakdown is the peril the standard form excludes and this coverage restores — with the failed machine, not just its consequences, at the center. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: On the subject of contract contents — the claim described, which statement is right?

answers.text: A Kansas public adjuster contract must contain the insured's full name and street address, the name of the insurer and the policy number, and a description of the loss and its location.
The insurer's identity is confidential and omitted.
The loss description may simply say 'property damage'.
The policy number may be added after settlement.

questions.explanation: The rule, applied: The contract ties the engagement to one insured, one insurer, one policy, and one described loss at a stated location — specificity is the requirement.

questions.question: A covered item has a replacement cost of $30,000. Depreciation of 10% applies for its age and condition. What is the item's actual cash value?
questions.explanation: Actual cash value is replacement cost minus depreciation: $30,000 x (1 - 0.10) = $27,000. The depreciation withheld is $3,000.

questions.question: Ms. Chen is adjusting a claim at a single-family home after a kitchen fire. The file raises the issue of employee theft coverage. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The coverage requires the employee to be convicted first.
Employee theft covers any employee error that costs money.

The commercial crime form's employee theft coverage pays for loss of money, securities, and other property resulting directly from theft committed by an employee — a dishonest taking by someone in the insured's service — with discovery and prior-fraud provisions shaping which losses qualify.
Losses caused by the insured's partners are covered as employee theft.

questions.explanation: The embezzling bookkeeper is the archetypal crime claim: proof centers on the employee's dishonest act and the direct loss it caused. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing the deductible's function. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Percentage deductibles are computed on the loss in every form.
The deductible is paid by the insurer to the insured.

A deductible is the stated amount or percentage of each covered loss the insured retains before the insurer pays — reducing small-claim costs, aligning the insured's care incentives, and lowering premium in exchange for retained risk.
The deductible applies once per policy term.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: Retained risk is the price of the premium saved: every valuation ends by subtracting the retention the insured agreed to keep.

questions.question: Mr. Novak is adjusting a claim at a retail store after a windstorm. The file raises the issue of contract contents — identity and license. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A Kansas public adjuster contract must contain the legible full name of the public adjuster signing it, the adjuster's permanent home state business address and phone number, and the adjuster's license number.
The contract need not identify which individual adjuster signed it.
A trade name alone satisfies the identity requirement.
The license number is optional if the insured already knows it.

questions.explanation: The insured must be able to identify, locate, and verify the exact licensed individual they hired — from the face of the contract. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing no false or malicious statements. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Statements to prospective clients are unregulated.
Exaggerating an insurer's conduct is fair salesmanship.

A Kansas public adjuster may not knowingly make any oral or written material misrepresentations, or statements that are false or maliciously critical and intended to injure any person engaged in the business of insurance, to an insured client or a potential insured client.
Only written falsehoods are covered.

questions.explanation: In one line: Kansas polices the pitch as well as the practice: winning a client with knowing falsehoods about insurers is itself an ethics violation.

questions.question: Mrs. Okafor is adjusting a claim at a condominium unit after a theft. The file raises the issue of attorney exemption. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The exemption lets attorneys employ unlicensed adjusters freely.
A license as a public adjuster is not required of an attorney-at-law admitted to practice in Kansas when acting in that professional capacity as an attorney.
A disbarred attorney keeps the exemption.
Any attorney from any state may adjust Kansas claims without a license.

questions.explanation: The exemption follows the law license and the legal work — it is the practice of law that is carved out, not the person in all they do. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: Mr. O'Brien asks how proof of loss works in a property claim. Which explanation is correct?

answers.text: The proof of loss may be submitted at any time before suit is filed, regardless of policy terms.
Verbal notice to an agent is a proof of loss.

A proof of loss is the insured's signed, sworn statement, submitted within the time the policy requires after the insurer's request, stating the time and origin of the loss, the insured's interest and all other interests in the property, the cash value of each item and the amount claimed, all other insurance, and the changes in title or occupancy since the policy issued.
A proof of loss is the adjuster's own estimate form.

questions.explanation: In one line: The proof is the insured's formal, sworn number — the claim the insurer must answer — which is why its contents and deadline are dictated by the policy.

questions.question: A family's normal monthly living expenses are $3,000. While their fire-damaged home is repaired, their temporary living costs are $4,100 per month for 6 months. How much additional living expense does Coverage D pay?
questions.explanation: Coverage D pays the increase over normal expenses: ($4,100 - $3,000) x 6 months = $6,600. It does not pay the family's normal expenses, which they would have had anyway.

questions.question: Mrs. Okafor is adjusting a claim at a duplex after a burst supply line. The file raises the issue of subrogation. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Subrogation lets an insurer that has paid a loss pursue the negligent third party to recover what it paid, standing in the insured's place.
Subrogation is the transfer of the policy to a new owner.
Subrogation is the insured's right to cancel mid-term.
Subrogation lets the insured collect twice for one loss.

questions.explanation: In one line: After paying, the insurer inherits the insured's claim against whoever caused the loss — and the public adjuster must protect that right, for example by preserving evidence and the salvage.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Kansas public adjusting concerns first-party claims: claims the insured makes under the insured's own insurance contract for loss or damage to the insured's own real or personal property.

answers.text: within twelve months, on proof and a reinstatement fee
public access in the home state
the insured's own claim under their own policy
helpers who only gather facts or give technical support

questions.explanation: That description defines the insured's own claim under their own policy. First-party is about whose policy and whose property: the adjuster stands on the insured's side of the insured's own contract.

questions.question: A business that sells its fire-damaged building along with the pending claim assigns the proceeds right — a transfer the form permits after loss. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: the insured's rights may pass, duties may not be dumped
the statutory baseline behind property forms
who counts as an insured under the form
the policy's fact sheet: who, what, where, how much

questions.explanation: The example points to the insured's rights may pass, duties may not be dumped. Consent guards the risk the insurer agreed to take; the post-loss claim is a chose in action the insured may sell or pledge.

questions.question: A commercial building is valued at $1,000,000. Its policy has a 80% coinsurance clause. The owner carried $400,000 of insurance. A covered loss of $50,000 occurs, and the deductible is $500. How much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Coinsurance required 80% of $1,000,000, which is $800,000. The payment ratio is $400,000 / $800,000 = 0.50. Applied to the $50,000 loss gives $25,000, minus the $500 deductible = $24,500.

questions.question: After a moderate quake cracks a home's foundation, the owner learns her earthquake policy's 15% deductible applies before any payment. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: earth movement is endorsed or separately insured, usually with a percentage deductible
defense costs and other supplementary payments are outside the limit
the policy is void as to an insured who intentionally conceals or misrepresents
Coverage C pays others' medical expenses without fault

questions.explanation: The example points to earth movement is endorsed or separately insured, usually with a percentage deductible. Percentage deductibles are the earthquake signature: 10% of a $600,000 limit means the insured absorbs the first $60,000 of quake damage.

questions.question: A report that fixes the night of the warehouse fire and maps damage to building, stock, and business income coverages gives the file its working structure. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: age, condition, and remaining service life
when repaired work must blend with the undamaged
occurrence date, coverages, and the facts of the loss
photographs, measurements, and preserved evidence

questions.explanation: The example points to occurrence date, coverages, and the facts of the loss. The outline names two of these expressly — occurrence date and coverages — because a report missing either cannot anchor deadlines or route damage to the right limits.

questions.question: A homeowner cannot know whether a kitchen fire will happen this year; that uncertainty is what she insures against. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: a financial stake in the property's preservation
risk as the uncertainty of financial loss
liability without proof of negligence for abnormally dangerous activities
the damage itself versus its consequences

questions.explanation: The example points to risk as the uncertainty of financial loss. Risk is the uncertainty itself — the chance that a loss may occur — not the cause of loss (the peril) or the condition that raises its likelihood (the hazard).

florida-public-adjuster-exam-prep.quiz_title: Florida Public Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding the definition of peril, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A peril is the cause of a loss, such as fire, windstorm, or theft.
A peril is the value exposed to loss.
A peril is the uncertainty that a loss will occur.
A peril is a condition that increases the chance of a loss.

questions.explanation: Perils are the causes named (or covered) in the policy — fire and theft are perils; the uncertainty is risk and the aggravating condition is a hazard. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: Regarding recoverable depreciation, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Repairs need never be completed to recover depreciation.
Depreciation withheld is never recoverable under any policy.

Under replacement cost policies, the insurer may pay actual cash value first and release the withheld depreciation when the insured completes the repairs within the policy's terms and documents the cost.
The insured must sue to recover any withheld depreciation.

questions.explanation: In one line: The two-step settlement — ACV now, depreciation on completion — is why adjusters drive the repair documentation to the finish line.

questions.question: Regarding the HO-6 form, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: The HO-6 provides no personal property coverage.
The HO-6 is a landlord's dwelling policy.
The HO-6 insures the entire condominium building for the association.
The HO-6 is written for condominium unit owners, covering the unit's interior items the owner is responsible for, personal property, and liability.

questions.explanation: The key point: Condo ownership splits the building (association's master policy) from the unit interior and contents (the owner's HO-6) — adjusters coordinate the two on every condo loss.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of what an apprentice may not do?

answers.text: An apprentice may sign contracts whenever the supervisor is away.

A public adjuster apprentice has the same authority as the employing licensed public adjuster or firm except that the apprentice may not execute contracts for the services of a public adjuster or public adjusting firm.
Executing contracts is the apprentice's main duty.
An apprentice may execute contracts for claims under $10,000.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: Contract execution is the bright line of the apprenticeship: the licensed public adjuster signs; the apprentice assists with everything else.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing no paid referrals. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Referral fees are allowed if disclosed to the client.
Only cash referral fees are barred; gifts are fine.

A Florida public adjuster may not accept referrals under any agreement to compensate the referrer, and may not compensate any person — except another public adjuster — directly or indirectly, for the principal purpose of referring business.
Paying roofers per signed client is standard and lawful.

questions.explanation: Referral money corrupts the advice chain, so Florida bans it in both directions, with a single exception for adjuster-to-adjuster compensation. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: Regarding first notice of loss and reserves, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A reserve is money already paid to the insured.
The insured sets the reserve for the insurer.
At first notice of loss the claim file is opened and the insurer sets a reserve — its working estimate of the claim's ultimate cost — which is revised as investigation develops the facts.
Reserves are set once and never changed.

questions.explanation: Reserves explain carrier behavior: a file reserved far below the documented scope is a file the public adjuster's evidence must move. Candidates miss this when they rely on how other licenses or other states handle the same issue.

questions.question: Mr. O'Brien is adjusting a claim at an office condo after vandalism. The file raises the issue of fidelity bonds. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Fidelity bonds are performance bonds for public works.
Fidelity bonds guarantee that a contractor will finish a project.
Fidelity bonds insure a building against fire.
Fidelity bonds protect an employer against loss caused by the dishonest acts of bonded employees.

questions.explanation: The key point: Where surety guarantees performance to a third party, fidelity protects the employer itself from its own employees' dishonesty.

questions.question: Mrs. Lindqvist is adjusting a claim at a rental cottage after a hailstorm. The file raises the issue of the vacancy condition. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Under the vacancy condition, when a dwelling is vacant for more than 60 consecutive days before a loss, certain perils — including vandalism, glass breakage, and water damage from plumbing — are not covered, and other losses are reduced.
The vacancy period in the standard form is 10 days.
Vacancy never affects coverage if premiums are paid.
A vacant home keeps full coverage for vandalism indefinitely.

questions.explanation: Adjusters calendar vacancy carefully: beyond the form's 60-day line, whole peril categories fall away and remaining losses take a percentage reduction. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: Mrs. Tanaka is adjusting a claim at a condominium unit after a theft. The file raises the issue of the thirty-day inspection. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The inspection window is six months.
When a Florida property claim investigation requires a physical inspection, the insurer must generally conduct the inspection within thirty days after receiving the proof-of-loss statement.
Inspections may be scheduled at the carrier's leisure.
Only the insured's adjuster ever inspects in Florida.

questions.explanation: Thirty days to put eyes on the damage keeps the carrier's valuation anchored to the actual loss rather than to photographs and delay. Candidates miss this when they rely on how other licenses or other states handle the same issue.

questions.question: Mr. Alvarez is adjusting a claim at a single-family home after a kitchen fire. The file raises the issue of the Florida bond. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The Florida bond is $20,000, like most states.
A $5,000 cash deposit may replace the bond at the applicant's option.
The bond is filed with the applicant's county clerk.
A Florida public adjuster applicant must file an original $50,000 surety bond on the form the Department provides, mailed to the Bureau of Licensing in Tallahassee.

questions.explanation: Fifty thousand dollars is Florida's financial-responsibility figure — double many states' — and the original bond goes to the Department on its own form. This is a point adjusters are expected to apply on real claims, not just recite.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing no charging without a contract. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: A 'consultation fee' may be charged after unsuccessful solicitation.
The insurer may be billed for the adjuster's pre-contract work.
Photos taken during solicitation may be sold to the client later.

A Florida public adjuster, apprentice, or firm that solicits a claim but does not enter into a contract with the insured may not charge the insured, or receive payment from any other source, for any service related to that claim.

questions.explanation: No contract, no compensation — from anyone. The rule kills the fallback of billing for the sales effort itself.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing who counts as a Florida public adjuster. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: A public adjuster is only a person who owns a public adjusting firm.
A public adjuster is any adjuster employed by an insurance company to settle its claims.

In Florida, a public adjuster is a person who, for money, commission, or anything else of value, prepares or files a claim for an insured, helps an insured negotiate or settle a claim, advertises for such work, or solicits, investigates, or adjusts such claims for a public adjuster.
A public adjuster is an unlicensed helper who works for free.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: Florida's definition turns on two things: compensation and working the claim for the insured's side — filing, negotiating, advertising, soliciting, investigating, or adjusting all count, however the person labels the service.

questions.question: A denial citing 'wear and tear' must be supported by the carrier's proof, not merely asserted in a letter. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: ambiguous policy language is construed against the insurer
investigate, evaluate, and negotiate
damage to property versus loss that follows from it
the insured proves the loss; the insurer proves the exclusion

questions.explanation: The example points to the insured proves the loss; the insurer proves the exclusion. Burden allocation is strategy: the adjuster builds the covered-loss proof, then makes the carrier carry its exclusion with evidence.

questions.question: A fire closes a business for 2 months. The business's net income would have been $10,000 per month, and its continuing normal operating expenses are $3,000 per month. What is the business income loss for the closure?
questions.explanation: Business income loss combines lost net income and continuing expenses: ($10,000 + $3,000) x 2 months = $26,000.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Offering substantially less than the amount ultimately recovered in litigation, in a way that compels the insured to sue to recover what is due, is an unfair claims practice in Florida.

answers.text: the regulator may grant insurers limited extra time after emergencies
compelling litigation by offering substantially less is unfair
grounds for refusal, suspension, or revocation
a physical inspection is due within thirty days after proof of loss

questions.explanation: That description defines compelling litigation by offering substantially less is unfair. The practice is judged by the pattern: offers so low they force suit, exposed when the eventual recovery dwarfs what was offered.

questions.question: Mr. Alvarez is adjusting a claim at a small warehouse after a sprinkler leak. The file raises the issue of signatures of all named insureds. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A Florida public adjuster contract requires the signatures of all named insureds; if a signature is unavailable, the adjuster must submit an affidavit signed by the available named insureds attesting they have authority to enter the contract and settle all claim issues for the named insureds.
Only the adjuster signs a Florida contract.
One spouse's signature always binds every named insured automatically.
Missing signatures may simply be noted as 'unavailable' with no affidavit.

questions.explanation: Because the contract commits every named insured's claim, Florida wants every signature — or a sworn affidavit standing in for the missing ones. Candidates miss this when they rely on how other licenses or other states handle the same issue.

questions.question: Mr. Alvarez is adjusting a claim at a rental cottage after a hailstorm. The file raises the issue of first-party versus third-party claims. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A first-party claim is filed by the insurer against the insured.
A first-party claim is made by the insured against the insured's own insurer; a third-party claim is made by someone else against the insured (and the insured's liability coverage).
A third-party claim is a claim for damage to a neighbor's property the insured does not cover.
First-party and third-party claims are the same claim seen by two adjusters.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: Public adjusters work first-party property claims: their client claims under the client's own policy. A visitor suing the homeowner is a third-party claimant.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Vicarious liability holds one party responsible for the wrongful acts of another, most commonly an employer for an employee acting within the scope of employment.

answers.text: a condition increasing the chance or severity of loss
line-item estimating prices each repair operation separately
bonds many licensees must post to obtain and keep a license
one party held liable for another's acts

questions.explanation: That description defines one party held liable for another's acts. Employers answer for employees' on-the-job negligence — a doctrine that matters when a contractor's or firm's employee causes a client's loss.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Coverage D responds when a covered loss makes the residence premises unfit to live in, paying additional living expense or fair rental value, and covers certain civil-authority prohibited-use losses.

answers.text: replacement cost available when insured to 80% of value
personal property in a dwelling policy is limited and peril-dependent
business income and extra expense are the BOP's loss-of-use answer
additional living expense, fair rental value, and prohibited use

questions.explanation: That description defines additional living expense, fair rental value, and prohibited use. Loss of use keeps the household running during repairs: the increase over normal living costs, or rent lost, for the shortest reasonable repair period.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? A Florida public adjuster may not charge more than 10 percent of insurance claim payments for claims based on events under a Governor's state-of-emergency declaration, for claims made during the year after the declaration.

answers.text: the insurer must meet with the public adjuster on scope
every applicant must pass the Florida public adjuster exam
10 percent for claims made in the year after an emergency declaration
no salvage interest without affidavit consent; no power to choose repairers

questions.explanation: That description defines 10 percent for claims made in the year after an emergency declaration. The one-year, 10-percent rule is Florida's core consumer protection in catastrophe adjusting; after that year the ordinary cap takes over.

georgia-public-adjuster-exam-prep.quiz_title: Georgia Public Adjuster Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes subrogation?

answers.text: Subrogation is the insured's right to cancel mid-term.
Subrogation is the transfer of the policy to a new owner.
Subrogation lets the insured collect twice for one loss.
Subrogation lets an insurer that has paid a loss pursue the negligent third party to recover what it paid, standing in the insured's place.

questions.explanation: The key point: After paying, the insurer inherits the insured's claim against whoever caused the loss — and the public adjuster must protect that right, for example by preserving evidence and the salvage.

questions.question: On the subject of Coverage A — Dwelling, which statement is right?

answers.text: Coverage A covers detached garages and fences.
Coverage A covers the insured's furniture and clothing.
Coverage A covers the insured's liability to others.
Coverage A pays for direct physical loss to the dwelling on the residence premises, including structures attached to it.

questions.explanation: In one line: Coverage A is the house itself — the main structure and what is attached to it; detached structures move to Coverage B and contents to Coverage C.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the DP-2 broad form?

answers.text: The DP-2 always includes liability coverage.
The DP-2 covers fewer perils than the DP-1.
The DP-2 (broad form) adds the broad named perils — including weight of ice and snow, collapse, and accidental discharge of water — and can provide replacement cost settlement.
The DP-2 is an open-perils form.

questions.explanation: Stepping from DP-1 to DP-2 buys the broad peril list and the option of replacement cost — the two upgrades adjusters check on every landlord loss. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: A public adjuster is reviewing reporting to the principal. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Principals learn outcomes only from the settlement check.

An adjuster investigates and reports to his or her principal — the insurer for a staff or independent adjuster, the insured for a public adjuster — keeping the principal informed of coverage questions, valuation, and settlement posture.
Reporting duties end after the first inspection.
Adjusters report only to the opposing side.

questions.explanation: Why it matters: Loyalty runs through reporting: the principal who hired the adjuster is entitled to the facts as they develop, not as a final surprise.

questions.question: When a claim turns on vacancy versus unoccupancy, which statement governs?

answers.text: Vacancy rules apply only to auto policies.
Vacancy and unoccupancy are identical in Georgia law.
A building is vacant when it lacks both occupants and the contents usual for its use, and merely unoccupied when people are absent but the furnishings and property of the occupancy remain.
A furnished home during a long vacation is vacant.

questions.explanation: The distinction decides real claims: policies restrict coverage after a period of vacancy, while a temporarily empty but furnished home is only unoccupied.

questions.question: The carrier pays the total loss on a burned delivery van and takes title to the wreck for its scrap value. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: the insurer may take salvage after paying a total loss
compensatory damages make the injured party whole; punitive damages punish
temporary proof of coverage before the policy issues
the insurer steps into the insured's shoes against the party at fault

questions.explanation: The example points to the insurer may take salvage after paying a total loss. Salvage is the tail of indemnity: full payment plus keeping the wreck would overpay the loss, so the wreck follows the money.

questions.question: A covered item has a replacement cost of $12,000. Depreciation of 60% applies for its age and condition. What is the item's actual cash value?
questions.explanation: Actual cash value is replacement cost minus depreciation: $12,000 x (1 - 0.60) = $4,800. The depreciation withheld is $7,200.

questions.question: A stolen five-year-old sofa settles at its depreciated value under a base-form contents claim. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: flood, surface water, and backup exclusions with an ensuing-loss analysis
the landlord's insurable interest in tenant-made improvements varies
earth movement is endorsed or separately insured, usually with a percentage deductible
contents settle at ACV unless replacement cost is endorsed or applies

questions.explanation: The example points to contents settle at ACV unless replacement cost is endorsed or applies. The ACV default on contents is why the inventory's depreciation column matters — and why the replacement-cost endorsement is worth its premium.

questions.question: Mr. Haddad is adjusting a claim at a retail store after a windstorm. The file raises the issue of credit card and forgery. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The base form pays unlimited credit card fraud losses.
Homeowners forms include a limited amount (commonly $500) for legal obligations from theft or unauthorized use of credit cards, forgery, and counterfeit money.
Forgery losses are excluded from every homeowners form.
This coverage reimburses the card issuer, not the insured's obligation.

questions.explanation: It is a small built-in coverage most insureds never know they have — one more line item a thorough adjuster checks on a burglary claim. That is the position the file documentation should reflect.

questions.question: Regarding representations and misrepresentation, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Representations are guarantees of literal truth like warranties.
Every innocent mistake voids a policy automatically.

Statements an applicant makes are representations — statements believed true to the applicant's knowledge — and an insurer may defeat coverage for a misrepresentation only when it is material: it would have changed the insurer's decision to issue the policy or its price.
Materiality is irrelevant to misrepresentation defenses.

questions.explanation: Examined closely: Materiality is the whole doctrine: trivial errors do not void policies; risk-changing ones can.

questions.question: Mrs. Okafor is adjusting a claim at a farmhouse after a lightning strike. The file raises the issue of adverse selection. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Adverse selection is an insurer's practice of canceling poor risks.
Adverse selection is the tendency of persons with a higher-than-average chance of loss to seek insurance more eagerly than average risks.
Adverse selection is the spreading of risk across many insureds.
Adverse selection is fraud committed after a loss occurs.

questions.explanation: Why it matters: If only the worst risks bought insurance, premiums would spiral; underwriting and the law of large numbers are the counterweights to adverse selection.

questions.question: Mr. Ferreira is adjusting a claim at a retail store after a windstorm. The file raises the issue of concealment and warranty. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Warranties are judged only by materiality, never accuracy.

Concealment is the intentional withholding of a material fact the applicant knows and should communicate, while a warranty is a statement or condition guaranteed true — breach of a warranty can void coverage even without intent to deceive.
Concealment and warranty are the same doctrine.
Concealment requires no knowledge by the applicant.

questions.explanation: Adjusters keep the trio straight — representation, concealment, warranty — because each carries a different burden and a different consequence. A public adjuster who gets this wrong exposes the client to a short payment or a compliance problem.

questions.question: A settlement values the specials from invoices, the generals for the injury's human cost, and no punitive element absent egregious conduct. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: the insured may not abandon damaged property to the insurer
compensatory damages make the injured party whole; punitive damages punish
the insurer may take salvage after paying a total loss
who makes the claim against whom

questions.explanation: The example points to compensatory damages make the injured party whole; punitive damages punish. Adjusters valuing liability claims sort damages into these boxes: itemizable specials, intangible generals, and punitives that punish rather than compensate.

questions.question: Wind tears shingles from an HO-3 home (open perils) and rain ruins the furniture inside (a named peril analysis for contents). This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: BOP property settles at replacement cost when the limit reflects value
special form coverage on the dwelling, named perils on personal property
loss of money, securities, and other property by employee dishonesty
up to $1,000 for assessments charged by a homeowners or condo association

questions.explanation: The example points to special form coverage on the dwelling, named perils on personal property. HO-3 is the workhorse owners form: the building gets open-perils protection, and contents get the broad named-peril list — the split adjusters check first on any contents claim.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? The CGL excludes property damage to personal property in the insured's care, custody, or control — the reason bailees and repairers buy specialized property coverage instead.

answers.text: earth movement is endorsed or separately insured, usually with a percentage deductible
reporting forms adjust limits to fluctuating values
builders risk style coverage within dwelling forms
no liability coverage for property in the insured's custody

questions.explanation: That description defines no liability coverage for property in the insured's custody. A repair shop that burns its customers' goods learns the CCC exclusion the hard way; the customer's property belonged on a property form.

questions.question: The adjuster's scope includes smoke remediation in unaffected rooms and code-required electrical work the carrier's estimate left out. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: the loss must fall inside the policy period to be covered
do not dispose of evidence or impair recovery rights
a line-item estimate of the work needed to restore the property
item, quantity, cost, and actual cash value for each item

questions.explanation: The example points to a line-item estimate of the work needed to restore the property. Most settlement fights are scope fights: rooms, trades, and operations the insurer's estimate omitted are where public adjusters earn their fee.

questions.question: The carrier's request letter starts the sixty-day proof-of-loss clock the adjuster calendars the same day. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: notice is prompt; proof of loss follows the policy's clock
Georgia's guaranty association pays covered claims of insolvent insurers
supplementary payments are paid in addition to the limit
all parts of the policy are read together

questions.explanation: The example points to notice is prompt; proof of loss follows the policy's clock. Two clocks, two documents: notice opens the claim quickly, and proof of loss formalizes it on the form's own deadline.

questions.question: A commercial building is valued at $800,000. Its policy has a 80% coinsurance clause. The owner carried $384,000 of insurance. A covered loss of $150,000 occurs, and the deductible is $500. How much will the insurer pay?
questions.explanation: Coinsurance required 80% of $800,000, which is $640,000. The payment ratio is $384,000 / $640,000 = 0.60. Applied to the $150,000 loss gives $90,000, minus the $500 deductible = $89,500.

questions.question: After a small roof leak, an owner ignores it for a year; the resulting rot is analyzed under the neglect exclusion and duties to protect. This situation best illustrates which of the following?

answers.text: personal property in a dwelling policy is limited and peril-dependent
medical expenses for others regardless of fault
business income and extra expense are the BOP's loss-of-use answer
no coverage for losses the insured intends or fails to mitigate

questions.explanation: The example points to no coverage for losses the insured intends or fails to mitigate. Intent and neglect bookend the claim: the insured may not manufacture a loss or let a covered loss grow through inaction.

questions.question: Which concept is described here? Georgia resident licensing applications, including the public adjuster application, are submitted online through Sircon, and renewals are filed through Sircon or NIPR.

answers.text: age, Georgia presence, and good character
contracts may not force adjuster-only checks or block civil remedies
the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire regulates Georgia adjusters
resident applications are filed online through Sircon

questions.explanation: That description defines resident applications are filed online through Sircon. Sircon is the single doorway for Georgia licensing paperwork — applications, renewals, and provider CE reporting all run through it.

abpts-ocs.quiz_title: ABPTS Orthopaedic Clinical Specialist (OCS) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Examine this short item. Which statement gives the primary action of the adductor magnus?

answers.text: Adducts the hip, with its hamstring part assisting hip extension
Extends the knee, with its oblique fibres guiding patellar tracking
Flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm
Flexes and ulnar-deviates (adducts) the wrist

questions.explanation: The adductor magnus acts to do the following: adducts the hip, with its hamstring part assisting hip extension. The other choices describe actions of other muscles.

questions.question: Consider the material below. Which finding constitutes a positive Yergason test?

answers.text: Pain in the bicipital groove, or palpable subluxation of the tendon
The thumb interphalangeal joint flexes (flexor pollicis longus compensating) to hold the paper
Reproduction of the patient's posterior pelvic pain during the thrust
Increased anterior translation with a soft or absent end point compared with the other side

questions.explanation: For the Yergason test (which assesses long head of biceps (and superior labral) pathology, using resisted supination and external rotation), the positive finding is: pain in the bicipital groove, or palpable subluxation of the tendon.

questions.question: Study the following item. The Ottawa ankle rules guide which decision?

answers.text: Whether surgery is needed
Whether to apply a cast
Whether the ligament is Grade II or III
Whether radiography is needed after acute ankle injury, based on bony tenderness and ability to bear weight

questions.explanation: Ottawa rules are a validated decision aid to reduce unnecessary ankle and foot radiographs.

questions.question: Here is an OCS practice item. Spondylolysis rehabilitation in a young athlete centres on what?

answers.text: A period of rest from extension-loading sport, trunk and hip strengthening in neutral ranges, and graded return including extension reintroduction criteria
Immediate return to bowling in cricket / gymnastics extension loads
Surgery for all cases
Complete rest for a year in all cases

questions.explanation: Bone stress needs rest from the provoking load plus capacity building.

questions.question: Review the item that follows. What does the Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM) measure?

answers.text: Shoulder pain and function combining a pain rating with daily-activity items
Pain intensity on a 0-10 scale, interpreted against the patient's own baseline and meaningful-change thresholds
Foot and ankle function in daily life and sport subscales
Disability from neck pain, scored 0-50 (or as a percentage) with higher scores meaning more disability

questions.explanation: The Foot and Ankle Ability Measure (FAAM) measures: foot and ankle function in daily life and sport subscales. It is re-administered at review points to judge change against meaningful thresholds.

questions.question: The item below tests specialist knowledge. Which statement gives the primary action of the tensor fasciae latae?

answers.text: Extends the great toe and dorsiflexes the ankle
Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot
Flexes and abducts the hip and tensions the iliotibial band
Extends the knee and flexes the hip

questions.explanation: The tensor fasciae latae acts to do the following: flexes and abducts the hip and tensions the iliotibial band. The other choices describe actions of other muscles.

questions.question: First read the material, then answer. Following lumbar microdiscectomy, standard early advice includes what?

answers.text: No walking until the three-month review
Early walking and gradual activity resumption, avoiding prolonged sitting and heavy lifting or loaded flexion-rotation early, per the surgeon's instructions
Immediate heavy deadlifting to strengthen the back
Strict bed rest for four weeks

questions.explanation: Early mobilisation after microdiscectomy supports recovery; loading restrictions in the first weeks protect against re-herniation while tissues heal.

questions.question: The short text below is followed by a question. Which finding constitutes a positive Hawkins-Kennedy test?

answers.text: Raising the unaffected leg reproduces pain in the affected leg
Reproduction of the patient's leg pain (not just back or hamstring pull) in the sensitive range, altered by ankle movement
Reproduction of shoulder pain during the manoeuvre
The elbow drops backward or the wrist flexes to compensate during the press

questions.explanation: For the Hawkins-Kennedy test (which assesses rotator cuff-related subacromial pain, using forced internal rotation at 90 degrees of flexion), the positive finding is: reproduction of shoulder pain during the manoeuvre.

questions.question: Work through this item carefully. Which finding constitutes a positive Valgus stress test (knee)?

answers.text: Pain, crepitus or reproduction of symptoms with axial compression and rotation of the thumb metacarpal
Tingling radiating into the median digits on tapping
Reproduction of shoulder pain near end-range elevation
Excessive medial joint opening or pain, with laxity graded against the other side

questions.explanation: For the Valgus stress test (knee) (which assesses medial collateral ligament and medial capsular integrity), the positive finding is: excessive medial joint opening or pain, with laxity graded against the other side.

questions.question: Read this item carefully. A patient with fibromyalgia is referred for knee pain. Planning should do what?

answers.text: Treat the knee as if the fibromyalgia does not exist
Refuse treatment
Apply maximal local loading immediately
Treat the knee within a whole-person plan — sleep, activity pacing and graded exercise — recognising central pain mechanisms amplify local symptoms

questions.explanation: Comorbid nociplastic pain changes dosage and expectations for local treatment.

questions.question: This item is part of OCS practice. Minimal detectable change (MDC) differs from MCID in that MDC is what?

answers.text: The maximum possible score
The average score of healthy people
The change patients find important
The smallest change that exceeds the instrument's measurement error — a statistical property, not a judgement of importance

questions.explanation: A change must first exceed MDC to be real, and exceed MCID to matter — both checks are applied at review.

questions.question: Examine the following item. Mentoring a junior colleague through a complex case is part of specialist practice because why?

answers.text: Mentoring is a management-only duty
Specialists should guard knowledge
It is unpaid extra with no professional standing
The DSP's professional roles include education and contributing to the body of knowledge and the profession's development

questions.explanation: Teaching is written into the specialist role definition, not an optional extra.

questions.question: This question practises a tested skill. Using standard goniometric reference values, what is the typical range for hip flexion with the knee flexed?

answers.text: 135 degrees
100 degrees
120 degrees
155 degrees

questions.explanation: Standard goniometric references put typical hip flexion with the knee flexed at about 120 degrees; the other values belong to other motions or exceed the normal arc.

questions.question: Study the material that follows. Which presentation warrants same-day emergency referral rather than routine therapy assessment?

answers.text: A patient with mild tennis elbow
A patient with back pain who cannot pass urine, with numbness in the saddle region
A patient with chronic knee stiffness
A patient with localised back ache after gardening

questions.explanation: Cauda equina features are the emergency; the rest are routine presentations.

questions.question: Here is another practice item. Planning for a young hypermobile patient with recurrent shoulder subluxations should emphasise what?

answers.text: Immobilisation as the long-term strategy
Progressive rotator cuff and scapular strengthening, proprioceptive training and activity modification, with surgical opinion if instability persists despite rehabilitation
Aggressive end-range stretching
Overhead throwing volume increases

questions.explanation: Dynamic stability substitutes for lax passive restraints — the core of hypermobility care.

questions.question: Consider each choice carefully here. For greater trochanteric pain syndrome, patient education must include which sleep and sitting modifications?

answers.text: Avoid lying on the painful side (or use a pillow between the knees side-lying on the other side) and avoid sitting with legs crossed or in low chairs that adduct the hip
Stand with weight always on the painful leg in adduction
Sit cross-legged for long periods
Sleep directly on the painful trochanter to desensitise it

questions.explanation: Compression avoidance extends into daily postures, not just exercise selection.

questions.question: Read carefully, then choose the best answer. The highest level of evidence for a therapy question is generally considered to be what?

answers.text: A systematic review/meta-analysis of well-conducted randomised controlled trials (with individual high-quality RCTs just below)
A single expert's opinion
A case report
A cross-sectional survey

questions.explanation: The evidence hierarchy tops out at synthesised RCT evidence for intervention questions.

questions.question: The following item is original practice material. A child or adolescent athlete with extension-related low back pain and pain on single-leg hyperextension testing raises suspicion of what?

answers.text: Pars interarticularis stress reaction or spondylolysis
Lumbar disc herniation with radiculopathy in most cases
Sacroiliac joint infection
Hip labral tear

questions.explanation: Extension-loading pain in a young athlete is the classic presentation of a pars stress injury.

questions.question: Take a moment with this item. A physical therapist evaluates a 57-year-old man with diabetes who presents following months of finger stiffness in the mornings. Examination shows painful clicking and locking of the ring finger in flexion, with a tender nodule at the A1 pulley. Which diagnosis is MOST likely?

answers.text: Ankle osteoarthritis
Trigger finger
Lumbar radiculopathy (L5)
Mallet finger

questions.explanation: The combination — months of finger stiffness in the mornings, with painful clicking and locking of the ring finger in flexion, with a tender nodule at the A1 pulley — is the classic presentation of trigger finger. The other choices do not fit this finding pattern.

questions.question: Here is an item to work through. Superficial heat is most appropriate for which presentation?

answers.text: Over a suspected DVT
A fresh ankle sprain in the first hours
Subacute or chronic muscle spasm and stiffness before exercise, avoiding acute injury, insensate skin and areas of poor circulation
Over an insensate foot

questions.explanation: Heat eases stiffness to enable movement; its contraindications (acute trauma, sensory loss, thrombosis) are the examination point.

corrections-officer-ny-dcas.quiz_title: Corrections Officer Entrance — NY DCAS Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Passage: Order: Post Key Control. A key-control order states that the post key ring for a housing area holds 16 keys and that keys are never to leave the facility, be duplicated, or be left unattended. Officer Whitfield signs the ring out at the start of the tour, counts the keys in front of the relieving officer at tour change, and reports a missing key to the control room immediately — before any other task. A key found damaged is tagged, removed from service, and recorded in the key log the same tour. According to the passage, According to the order, when does Officer Whitfield count the keys on the ring?

answers.text: at the start of the tour only, alone
report it to the control room immediately, before any other task
in front of the relieving officer at tour change
it is tagged, removed from service, and recorded in the key log the same tour

questions.explanation: Keys are counted in front of the relieving officer at tour change. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: A housing unit has 4 tiers, and each tier holds 7 cells. How many cells does the unit hold in total?
questions.explanation: Multiply tiers by cells per tier: 4 x 7 = 28.

questions.question: Visualization: on a desk, from left to right, stand a cap, a log book, a radio, a flashlight. In a mirror facing the desk, which object appears second from the left in the mirror image?

answers.text: a radio
a cap
a log book
a flashlight

questions.explanation: Reversing the row for the mirror image puts the third object from the real left into the second position from the image's left. No outside information is needed; the stem supplies what matters.

questions.question: Passage: Standard: Log-Book Entries. A log-book standard states that entries in the Housing Area 3A log book must be made in ink, in chronological order, and initialed by the officer making them. Officer Hobson must never leave blank lines between entries, must draw a single line through any error and initial the correction, and must record every count, search, incident, and supervisory visit on the tour it occurred. An entry about another tour may be added only as a late entry labeled with the date and time it is actually written. Based on the passage, According to the standard, how must an error in a log-book entry be corrected?

answers.text: every count, search, incident, and supervisory visit on the tour it occurred
by tearing out the page and starting again
by drawing a single line through the error and initialing the correction
only as a late entry labeled with the date and time it is actually written

questions.explanation: The standard prescribes a single line through the error, initialed — never erasure or removal. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Memorization: a post telephone list gives the number sequence 6-8-8-1-1. What is the first digit in the sequence?
questions.explanation: Counting into the sequence 6-8-8-1-1, the first digit is 6.

questions.question: For a formal incident report, which sentence is punctuated correctly? The sentence in this set quotes a supervisor speaking about verifying counts.

answers.text: Supervisor Farrar said "All counts, must be verified before the tour ends."
Supervisor Farrar said, "All counts must be verified before the tour ends."
Supervisor Farrar said, "All counts must be verified before the tour ends".
Supervisor Farrar said "All counts must be verified before the tour ends".

questions.explanation: A direct quotation after 'said' takes a comma before the quote, and the period sits inside the closing quotation mark. Candidates should prefer the version that would be accepted unchanged in an official report.

questions.question: The following tasks appear on a tour schedule: inspect the tier and cells at 16:40; review the movement list at 14:40; sign the log book at 15:00; count and verify the area at 16:35. Putting the tasks in the order they must be performed, earliest first, gives which sequence?

answers.text: review the movement list, sign the log book, count and verify the area, inspect the tier and cells
review the movement list, sign the log book, inspect the tier and cells, count and verify the area
review the movement list, count and verify the area, sign the log book, inspect the tier and cells
review the movement list, inspect the tier and cells, count and verify the area, sign the log book

questions.explanation: Reading the printed times in order gives the sequence: review the movement list at 14:40; sign the log book at 15:00; count and verify the area at 16:35; inspect the tier and cells at 16:40.

questions.question: Using the facility map: the control room is directly north of the chapel, the recreation yard gate is directly east of the chapel, the visiting room entrance is directly south of the chapel, and the school area is directly west of the chapel. An officer at the chapel turns to face north. Which location is now on the officer's behind?

answers.text: the control room
the visiting room entrance
the school area
the recreation yard gate

questions.explanation: Facing north, the officer's behind points south, and the visiting room entrance is the location directly south of the chapel.

questions.question: For stated housing-area rules, the written rule for the area states: 'Complaints about medical care are recorded and forwarded to the clinic; officers do not judge their validity.' A person complains about a clinic decision the officer personally agrees was correct. Applying the rule, what must the officer do?

answers.text: hold the departure and reconcile the discrepancy with a supervisor before leaving
decline the gift and report the offer as procedure requires
refuse to hand over the key; the worker is escorted or the task is arranged through a supervisor
record the complaint and forward it to the clinic without judging it

questions.explanation: The rule separates recording from judging; the officer's own view of the merits is not a filter. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: For the DCAS Correction Officer exam, what does DCAS mean by the ability called Written Comprehension for a Correction Officer?

answers.text: they are sealed in a Yondr pouch until after the exam event, and using one can nullify the score and bar the candidate from civil service tests for up to five years
promotion to Captain (Correction), and from that title to Warden (Correction) at several assignment levels
two years of active service in a reserve component or the National Guard with an honorable discharge, not counting Individual Ready Reserve time
understanding written sentences and paragraphs, such as interpreting facility policies and regulations

questions.explanation: Written Comprehension is the reading ability — understanding written material and carrying out procedures based on it. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: At the start of the tour, Housing Area 2D held 25 sets of recreation equipment. During the period, 9 sets were signed out. How many sets remained in the storage room?
questions.explanation: Subtract what was signed out: 25 - 9 = 16. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Passage: Facility Notice: Counts and Verification. A facility notice on counts states that during the day tour, the officer assigned to Housing Area 5B must count and verify every person in custody in the area twice: once at 7:00 a.m. and once before the tour ends. At the 7:00 a.m. count, Officer Alvarez counted 22 people in the housing unit and 7 people who had returned early from a program area, for a verified total of 29. If the two counts disagree, the officer must recount immediately, notify the area supervisor, and record both counts and the recount in the log book before leaving the post. According to the passage, What is the main purpose of the notice?

answers.text: 29 people
to state how counts are taken, verified, and recorded when they disagree
recount immediately, notify the area supervisor, and record both counts and the recount in the log book
to announce a change in visiting hours

questions.explanation: Every sentence of the notice concerns counting, verifying, and recording counts. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: Under the area's assignment rule, a person may be assigned to the school program seats only if the person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation. In Housing Area 6C, one person has completed the program orientation but has no equivalency goal on file. Applying the rule, which conclusion must be true?

answers.text: That person may be assigned if a supervisor waives the rule verbally
That person may be assigned to the school program seats
The rule applies only to officers, never to assignments
That person may not be assigned to the school program seats

questions.explanation: For the school program seats, the rule requires every stated condition — that the person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation. This person misses one, so the assignment is barred.

questions.question: During one week, Officer Kowalski drove 3 escorted trips totaling 42 miles. What was the average number of miles driven for each trip?

answers.text: 14 miles
13 miles
42 miles
16 miles

questions.explanation: Average means total divided by trips: 42 / 3 = 14 miles per trip.

questions.question: During the evening tour, an officer notices that a normally busy dayroom is empty while a large group has gathered out of camera view in a corridor. What should the officer do, according to the standard reference material on the subject? Candidates meet the item in a practice review.

answers.text: treat the unusual gathering as a possible developing problem: observe, notify a supervisor, and do not enter the blind spot alone
the conflict between the verbal and written orders must be clarified with a supervisor so the officer follows the controlling instruction
assume the group is holding a meeting and ignore it
a sudden behavior change in one group can signal a planned disturbance or a medical emergency and warrants immediate attention

questions.explanation: Deliberate use of a blind spot plus an emptied common area is a warning pattern; the response is observation and backup, not a solo entry.

questions.question: A log-book entry must be spelled correctly. Which word below is spelled correctly? Choose the correct spelling of the word meaning: the gear issued for duty, such as radios and keys.

answers.text: equipment
equipmnet
equipmentt
equipement

questions.explanation: 'equipment' is the correct spelling of the word meaning the gear issued for duty, such as radios and keys; the other choices misplace or drop letters. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Which duties does the published Correction Officer job description assign around searches and safety? The question belongs to a general-knowledge drill.

answers.text: request medical assistance for inmates when necessary, and observe inmates to make recommendations concerning medical and psychiatric referrals
inspecting assigned areas for conditions threatening safety and security, and conducting searches to detect contraband
medical and psychological assessment, a qualifying physical test, drug screening before appointment with random testing during Academy training, and a background investigation
remembering information such as words, numbers, pictures and procedures, alone or in combination

questions.explanation: Inspection for hazards and searches for contraband are core published duties of the title. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: A tour commander in Housing Area 4B is shown this pattern: Four complaints in one week all describe cold food arriving in the same housing area; other areas served by the same kitchen reported no problem, and the area is the last stop on the cart route. Which conclusion follows best from the pattern?

answers.text: Something on the route to that area — timing or cart handling — is likely cooling the food
The observations show the facility should close the area involved
Every area in the facility has exactly the same problem at the same rate
The complaints must all be false because they agree

questions.explanation: Inductive reasoning combines separate observations into the general conclusion they jointly support: something on the route to that area — timing or cart handling — is likely cooling the food. The other choices either overstate the facts or ignore the pattern. This answer holds up under the facts as presented.

questions.question: Memorization: study this scene. In the visiting room, 7 people wore orange shirts, 3 wore blue shirts, and 8 wore yellow shirts. Seated nearest the door was Mr. Donnelly; seated in the middle was Mr. Castillo; seated nearest the window was Mr. Grimaldi. Who was seated nearest the window?

answers.text: Mr. Castillo
Mr. Farrar
Mr. Donnelly
Mr. Grimaldi

questions.explanation: The scene places the named person nearest the window in its final seating detail. No outside information is needed; the stem supplies what matters.

questions.question: The assignment rule for the area states that a person may be assigned to the school program seats only if the person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation. In the visiting area, one person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation. Applying the rule, which conclusion must be true?

answers.text: The rule applies only to officers, never to assignments
The rule does not apply inside a housing area
That person may be assigned if a supervisor waives the rule verbally
That person may be assigned to the school program seats

questions.explanation: For the school program seats, the rule requires that the person has a high-school equivalency goal on file and has completed the program orientation — and this person does, so the rule permits the assignment. It is the response a careful reviewer would expect on this fact pattern.

naa-camt.quiz_title: NAA CAMT — Certified Apartment Maintenance Technician Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam — Fixed Set

questions.question: Which of these assertions about refrigerator cooling diagnosis fails to hold up?

answers.text: Poor refrigerator cooling can come from dirty condenser coils, blocked vents, or a failing door seal.
Food temperatures and air flow between compartments are checked before major parts are replaced.
Dirty condenser coils improve heat transfer and should never be cleaned.
The refrigerator is unplugged before fan blades or electrical covers are handled.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Most cooling complaints trace to airflow, coils, seals, or fans that can be checked in order, while blocked vents, dirty coils, and careless defrosting hide the real fault and can damage the appliance.

questions.question: On the subject of pool equipment mechanics, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Pool pumps lose prime when suction side air leaks or low water level let air enter the system.
High filter pressure always means the gauge is wrong and cleaning can be skipped.
Running a pool pump dry keeps the seals flexible and extends motor life.
A strainer basket can be removed and left out so water flows faster to the filter.

questions.explanation: Pool equipment depends on a full prime, clean baskets, and sound filtration, while dry running, missing baskets, and ignored pressure or air leaks damage motors and leave water cloudy and unsafe.

questions.question: One statement about energy and water conservation in repairs is not true. Which one is it?

answers.text: A running toilet or dripping faucet is treated as resource waste, not merely a minor annoyance, and prioritized accordingly.
When replacing components, the technician follows the property's efficiency standards rather than installing the least efficient option by default.
Repairs that conserve resources — fixing leaks promptly, sealing drafts, restoring insulation disturbed during work — are part of environmentally responsible maintenance.
Efficiency standards apply to new construction, never to replacement parts.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Responsible maintenance conserves by default: leaks fixed promptly, disturbed insulation restored, and replacements that respect the property's efficiency standards.

questions.question: Which claim about exterior lighting check should be discarded as false?

answers.text: Walkways, stairwells, and parking areas should all be included when checking exterior lighting.
Exterior lighting checks should be done after dark so burned out or dim fixtures are actually visible.
Burned out bulbs in stairwells can wait until a resident complains before being addressed.
The technician should report broken fixture covers and exposed wiring found during a lighting check as safety concerns.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Checking lighting after dark in all travel areas reveals dark spots and damaged fixtures that affect safety and security, allowing timely repair before residents are put at risk.

questions.question: For asking clarifying questions upward, which statement holds true?

answers.text: Restating an assignment wastes a supervisor time and adds no real value.
An unclear instruction should be guessed at so the day is not slowed down.
Asking for clarification signals incompetence and should be avoided at all costs.
Asking a supervisor to clarify an unclear instruction prevents work done the wrong way.

questions.explanation: Asking clarifying questions upward, and restating assignments to confirm priorities, prevents rework and unsafe assumptions, and supervisors view thoughtful questions as engagement rather than weakness.

questions.question: Among these statements on wall anchor and mounting, one is incorrect. Identify it.

answers.text: The correct anchor for a load depends on wall material, with hollow wall anchors, stud anchoring, and masonry anchors each suited to different conditions.
Heavy or safety related items such as grab bars and large fixtures should be anchored into framing or proper blocking whenever possible.
Before drilling, the technician should check for plumbing and wiring that may run behind the chosen mounting location.
Grab bars anchored only into drywall provide full support for a falling person.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Mounting safety rests on matching the anchor to both the wall and the load, preferring framing for anything a person may grab or that carries real weight. Checking for hidden pipes and wires before drilling prevents a simple mounting task from creating a plumbing or electrical emergency.

questions.question: Erin Sullivan is reviewing briefing material on airflow diagnosis. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Crushed, disconnected, or leaking ducts in attics or crawl spaces waste conditioned air and should be repaired and resealed.
Rooms that are far from the air handler or have closed doors and no return path often run warmer or cooler than the rest of the unit.
Weak airflow at registers prompts checks of the filter, blower operation, closed or blocked registers, and duct connections.
Blocking a return grille with furniture improves circulation by redirecting the air.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Airflow is half of comfort delivery, so the path from filter to blower to duct to register is checked as a chain. Finding crushed or disconnected ducts and blocked returns explains many uneven room complaints without touching the refrigeration circuit.

questions.question: A team discussion turns to winter pipe protection. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: A frozen pipe should be thawed gently with warm air, never with an open flame, and checked for splits once flow returns.
Insulation makes it impossible for any pipe to freeze regardless of temperature or exposure.
A pipe that froze but did not burst while frozen is guaranteed undamaged after thawing.
Turning heat completely off in a vacant unit during a freeze protects the plumbing system.

questions.explanation: Freeze protection focuses on the most exposed piping, gentle thawing, and a careful leak check after thaw, because splits often reveal themselves only when water flows again. Resident guidance and vacant unit heat are part of the same prevention system.

questions.question: A junior colleague makes several claims about glove selection for tasks. Which claim should a mentor correct?

answers.text: Thicker gloves always provide better protection for every kind of task.
Chemical resistant gloves are chosen based on the product being handled and its label guidance.
Cut resistant gloves suit sheet metal and glass handling where sharp edges are present.
Gloves are removed or changed when torn so hands are not exposed mid task.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Glove material and fit must match cuts, chemicals, or contamination risks and be changed when damaged, while loose gloves near rotating parts and one pair for every job spread harm instead of preventing it.

questions.question: Which claim about work order tracking for preventive tasks should be discarded as false?

answers.text: Preventive tasks should be entered as work orders so completion can be tracked like any other maintenance work.
Work order notes for preventive tasks should be left blank to keep the system tidy.
Notes on each preventive work order should include findings and parts used for future reference.
Tracking shows which homes or systems are overdue so the team can recover the schedule before gaps grow.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Entering preventive tasks as tracked work orders with findings and parts used makes overdue work visible, supports planning, and creates the history that proves the program is being followed.

questions.question: A study partner asks a fellow applicant about communicating delays promptly. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Revised times should be kept vague so the technician cannot be held to them.
Delay notices are the office job alone, even when the technician learns first.
Offering a revised time when communicating a delay gives the resident a clear expectation.
Giving a reason for a delay sounds like an excuse and should always be avoided.

questions.explanation: Communicating delays promptly means notifying the resident as soon as the delay is known, briefly explaining why, and offering a revised time, which respects the resident day and preserves trust.

questions.question: A team discussion turns to confidentiality of resident information. Which explanation is accurate?

answers.text: Confidentiality ends when a resident moves out, so old details can be shared freely.
A resident phone number from a work order may be used for personal contact later.
Discussing a resident payment or lease details with other residents is acceptable small talk.
Resident information seen on paperwork should be kept secure and out of public view.

questions.explanation: Confidentiality means using resident contact and schedule information only for the service task, keeping paperwork secure, and never sharing lease, payment, or personal details with others.

questions.question: Peter Lindqvist is walking the grounds on a daily property inspection. On the question of leaving entry notice behind, which statement holds true?

answers.text: Notices are only for repairs that failed, not for completed work.
Leaving the door unlocked after a visit helps the resident get in more easily.
The notice includes how to contact the office if the problem continues or returns.
A notice should list problems the technician noticed in the resident housekeeping.

questions.explanation: A clear notice and a relocked door tell an absent resident what was done and how to get help, while silence and unsecured doors create worry, callbacks, and avoidable security risk.

questions.question: What should a beginning maintenance technician understand about interior coating application? Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Interior paint should be applied in even coats, keeping a wet edge to avoid lap marks and uneven sheen.
Rolling in random directions with a dry roller produces the smoothest finish.
One very thick coat always looks better and lasts longer than thinner even coats.
A second coat can be applied immediately over a still tacky first coat in all conditions.

questions.explanation: Application technique shows in the finished wall, so wet edges, orderly cutting in, and respect for drying time produce an even sheen. Rushing recoats or laying paint too thick traps solvents and creates the lap marks and peeling that prompt repaint calls.

questions.question: A stakeholder repeats something they read online about inspection report writing. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: Inspection reports record observed conditions precisely — location, condition, and severity — rather than conclusions the inspector did not verify.
Inspection reports are complete when the walk ends, even if entries are finished later from memory.
Recommended actions in a report are separated clearly from observed facts.
Life safety and water intrusion findings are flagged in the report with the urgency their risk deserves.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Inspection reports separate observation from recommendation, state severity honestly, and flag urgent risks plainly — the format that lets management act without a second visit.

questions.question: While preparing notes after a preventive maintenance day, Julia Santos double-checks notes on seasonal pool closing. Which statement should be corrected?

answers.text: Closing procedures should include inspecting and securing the cover so it stays safe and in place through the off season.
Seasonal pool closing should include cleaning the pool, lowering or managing water as directed, and protecting equipment from freezing.
Pipes, pumps, and filters should be prepared for cold weather following the established closing checklist.
The pool gate can be left unlatched during winter because the pool is closed.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Proper seasonal closing protects the shell, plumbing, and equipment from freeze and debris damage, secures the cover and barrier, and makes the next opening faster, safer, and less costly.

questions.question: Michael Novak is reviewing briefing material on manufacturer training resources. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Checking manufacturer resources before servicing unfamiliar equipment reduces guesswork and errors.
