Too many tucks were used, making the splice grip the line too firmly
The core and cover were not milked back and buried to the lengths the splice depends on for grip

questions.explanation: Double-braid eye splices hold by friction over a proper bury length, with the cover milked back over the core to lock it. Shortening the bury or failing to milk the cover leaves a splice that looks complete but slips under load, which is why test-loading new pendants before passenger service is standard practice.

questions.question: After a service, a returned life raft is reinstalled on the passenger vessel with its painter secured to a nearby rail by a crew member's knot. The master orders it redone to the vessel's strong point arrangement. Why does the painter attachment matter so much?

answers.text: Painters are purely decorative streamers on raft containers
Any knot anywhere works because painters never take real loads
The painter is the link that inflates the raft and holds it alongside; a weak or wrong attachment can lose the raft or fail to inflate it
The painter must be left completely unattached to float free

questions.explanation: Everything a raft does, inflating, staying alongside for boarding, and being towed clear, begins with its painter and the strength of what it is tied to. A casual attachment to a light rail can tear away with the raft or leave it drifting uninflated, so masters verify painter leads and weak-link arrangements personally rather than assuming the servicing yard finished the job.

questions.question: Before a night departure the master confirms the steering has been tested, the compasses compared, clocks synchronized, and the departure checks reported by each department rather than assuming silence means readiness. What system is the master actually operating?

answers.text: A departure checklist culture in which readiness is positively reported item by item, because unreported failures stay invisible until the vessel is committed
A tradition performed only for visiting company executives
A substitute for the vessel's certificated manning
A way to delay departure until daylight in all cases

questions.explanation: Checklists convert assumptions into verifications at the last moment they are cheap: alongside, with room to fix or cancel. Positive reporting matters; 'no complaints' is not the same as 'tested and working.' Masters who insist on the ritual are buying the right to discover a steering defect at the dock instead of in the channel.

questions.question: Creeping up behind a slow fish packer in a wide estuary reach, you honestly cannot place your approach: it might fall inside the sector her sternlight paints, or it might sit a degree outside it on her quarter. The answer decides who manoeuvres. Which assumption must you sail under?

answers.text: That you are crossing, because boundary water belongs to the crossing rule by convention.
That you are the overtaking vessel — when the sector boundary cannot be settled, the approaching vessel adopts the overtaking burden and keeps clear until completely past and clear.
That the packer yields, because slowness forfeits protection along sector boundaries.
That both vessels halve speed and share the burden until the sector can be surveyed.

questions.explanation: The overtaking doubt rule spends uncertainty on the vessel best placed to bear it: the one approaching from astern, with the speed advantage and the view. She assumes the heavier classification, keeps clear on that basis, and never needs the boundary surveyed at all.

questions.question: The vessel receives a digital selective calling distress alert on the radio and the master must decide how much of the response can rest on the alert's automatically included position. What governs confidence in that built-in position?

answers.text: The position is only as good as the navigation input connected to the radio and the time since it was last updated, so it is cross-checked and the sending vessel is contacted while the response is organized
A distress alert's position is guaranteed accurate because it is digital
Alert positions are computed by the shore station receiving the call
If no position is included, the alert can be disregarded entirely

questions.explanation: Digital alerts carry whatever position the distressed vessel's radio was fed, which may be fresh satellite data or hours-old manual entry. Treating the field as a strong lead that still needs confirmation is the balance the system was designed around.

questions.question: Two identical inspected vessels carry the same passenger count, but one has its passengers seated in an enclosed main cabin while the other allows the same number to ride on an exposed flying bridge several feet higher. In a sudden squall, why is the flying-bridge vessel at greater risk?

answers.text: Passengers seated higher raise the combined center of gravity and present slightly more windage, so the same gust produces heel against a smaller righting margin than in the vessel carrying its people low.
Flying bridges are inherently unlawful on all passenger vessels.
Squalls only endanger passengers who are standing, not seated.
The risk is identical, because passenger weight never affects stability once seated.

questions.explanation: Stability bookkeeping counts passengers where they actually sit. A crowd carried high lifts the center of gravity measurably — dozens of people are tons of movable weight — which is why stability letters specify how many passengers each deck may carry.

servsafe-manager.quiz_title: ServSafe Food Manager Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the manager's responsibility for thermometers used in a steakhouse?

answers.text: Keep one thermometer locked in the office
Rely on touch and color to judge doneness
Provide enough accurate thermometers, ensure they are calibrated and sanitized, and verify staff use them correctly
Replace thermometers only when they break

questions.explanation: Monitoring is only as good as its instruments; calibration is a management duty.

questions.question: What must the labels on chemical containers at a steakhouse show?

answers.text: A color code known to one employee is enough
The common name of the chemical's contents on every container, including spray bottles filled from a bulk supply, so nothing is ever mistaken for food or another chemical
Empty soda bottles may be reused for chemicals without labels
Labels are needed only on the original bulk container

questions.explanation: Working containers are where chemical accidents happen; identity travels with the liquid.

questions.question: Which cooking requirement applies to poultry at a stadium concession stand?

answers.text: Poultry may be served medium rare on request
Poultry follows the same minimum as whole-muscle beef
Poultry is safe when the juices look clear, whatever the temperature
Poultry must be cooked to the highest temperature on the cooking ladder, one hundred sixty-five degrees Fahrenheit, with no rest time needed

questions.explanation: Poultry carries the ladder's top requirement; appearance never replaces the thermometer.

questions.question: What is a cross-connection, and why is it dangerous at a coffee shop with a sandwich bar?

answers.text: A connection between two sinks
Any pipe that crosses a wall
A physical link between the safe water supply and a source of contamination, such as a hose left submerged in a mop bucket, which can let dirty water be drawn back into the supply
A backup water line for emergencies

questions.explanation: A submerged hose turns a bucket into part of the plumbing; the link is the hazard.

questions.question: How must a warewashing machine at a hospital cafeteria be checked?

answers.text: If it runs and sounds normal, it is sanitizing
Machine checks are the repair company's yearly job only
Verify it reaches the conditions on its data plate, confirm sanitizing with the appropriate test or indicator, and check that washed items come out clean
Items that look wet are sanitized

questions.explanation: A machine's plate states its operating promise; staff verify the promise is kept.

questions.question: Why must food handlers in an assisted-living dining service use a hair restraint?

answers.text: Restraints protect hair from kitchen heat
Hair is a physical contaminant and a carrier of microorganisms; restraints keep it out of food and off food-contact surfaces
Hair in food is only a problem if a guest sees it
Restraints are a uniform fashion rule

questions.explanation: Hair restraint is contamination control, not appearance policy.

questions.question: Why are food shields and covered displays not a substitute for temperature control at a commissary kitchen?

answers.text: Covered food holds its temperature indefinitely
Shields are required only for cold food
Temperature checks stop once a shield is installed
Shields block contamination from guests but do nothing to hold temperature; displayed food still needs its hot or cold holding control and checks

questions.explanation: Each control addresses one route of harm; none covers for another.

questions.question: What does monitoring mean in a food safety management system in a commissary kitchen?

answers.text: Routinely checking and documenting conditions such as temperatures, sanitizer strength, and employee practices against set standards
Counting the money at closing
Checking the weather forecast
Watching the dining room during rush

questions.explanation: Monitoring is the routine measurement that tells managers whether controls are holding.

questions.question: How must utensils in active use be stored between servings at a coffee shop with a sandwich bar?

answers.text: In a container of room-temperature water that is never changed
In the food with the handle out, under running water in a dipper well, or on a clean sanitized surface, and cleaned on the scheduled interval
In the server's apron pocket
On the counter next to the register

questions.explanation: In-use utensils are food-contact surfaces and stay controlled between uses.

questions.question: What must the labels on chemical containers at an assisted-living dining service show?

answers.text: Empty soda bottles may be reused for chemicals without labels
The common name of the chemical's contents on every container, including spray bottles filled from a bulk supply, so nothing is ever mistaken for food or another chemical
Labels are needed only on the original bulk container
A color code known to one employee is enough

questions.explanation: Working containers are where chemical accidents happen; identity travels with the liquid.

questions.question: What should staff at an assisted-living dining service check first when a delivery arrives?

answers.text: Accept everything and sort out problems during preparation
Sign the invoice before looking at the food
Inspect the delivery vehicle and the food's condition, temperatures, packaging, and dates before accepting it, and reject items that fail
Put frozen food away first and inspect paperwork later

questions.explanation: Inspection happens at the door, while rejection is still possible.

questions.question: Why is thawing food on the counter at a coffee shop with a sandwich bar prohibited?

answers.text: It is prohibited because it takes too long
Counter thawing is only a quality problem
Frozen food cannot grow pathogens on its surface
The surface of the food sits in the temperature danger zone for hours while the center is still frozen, allowing pathogens to multiply

questions.explanation: Surface time in the danger zone, not the frozen center, is the hazard.

questions.question: What preparation practice protects ready-to-eat produce at a bakery-cafe from the raw meat prepped in the same kitchen?

answers.text: Rinse the board with water between tasks
Produce needs no protection because it is washed later
Schedule and separate the work: prep produce first or in a separate area, with cleaned and sanitized surfaces and washed hands between tasks
Prep meat first so it is out of the way

questions.explanation: Order, place, and sanitation together keep raw contamination off food eaten raw.

questions.question: A sewage backup occurs in the food-preparation area at a quick-service restaurant. What is the only correct response?

answers.text: Mop the area and continue serving
Move preparation to the dining room
Serve only cold food until it is fixed
Stop food operations in the affected area, discard exposed food, and do not resume until the backup is corrected and the area is cleaned and sanitized and the authority's direction is followed

questions.explanation: Sewage in a food area is an imminent health hazard; service from that area stops.

questions.question: A bulk bin of flour at a school cafeteria is unlabeled and sits beside an identical bin of a powdered chemical cleaner. What is the core failure?

answers.text: The bins should be different colors only
The flour should be used up quickly
Food and chemicals must be identified and separated; unlabeled, adjacent containers invite a mix-up that poisons food
Nothing is wrong if staff are careful

questions.explanation: Identification plus separation is the control; memory is not.

questions.question: A food handler in a deli operation vomited earlier today but now feels fine. May the handler work?

answers.text: Yes, on dish duty only
Yes, if gloves are worn
Yes, if no more vomiting occurs during the shift
No. Vomiting requires exclusion for the period the food code specifies, because feeling better does not mean shedding has stopped

questions.explanation: Exclusion periods are based on pathogen shedding, not on how the employee feels.

questions.question: Why must dumpster lids and doors at a childcare center kitchen stay closed and drain plugs stay in place?

answers.text: It is only a courtesy to neighbors
Plugs are removed to let liquid drain onto the pad
Lids matter only in summer
Openings invite pests and let liquid leak and odors spread; closed, plugged containers deny pests both food and entry

questions.explanation: Every opening in a refuse container is a pest doorway.

questions.question: A thermometer display at a coffee shop with a sandwich bar reads 203 degrees Fahrenheit. Using Celsius = (Fahrenheit - 32) x 5 / 9, what is that temperature in degrees Celsius?

answers.text: 95 degrees Celsius
100 degrees Celsius
90 degrees Celsius
105 degrees Celsius

questions.explanation: Celsius = (203 - 32) x 5 / 9 = 95 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: A specification sheet at a hotel banquet kitchen gives a holding temperature of 85 degrees Celsius. Using Fahrenheit = Celsius x 9 / 5 + 32, what is that temperature in degrees Fahrenheit?

answers.text: 176 degrees Fahrenheit
185 degrees Fahrenheit
203 degrees Fahrenheit
194 degrees Fahrenheit

questions.explanation: Fahrenheit = 85 x 9 / 5 + 32 = 185 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.question: Cooked food at a nursing-home kitchen is cooling and must drop from 135 degrees Fahrenheit to 70 degrees Fahrenheit within 2 hours, which is 120 minutes. It has been cooling for 45 minutes. How many minutes remain in the first cooling stage?

answers.text: 75 minutes
65 minutes
90 minutes
105 minutes

questions.explanation: Minutes remaining = 120 - 45 = 75 minutes.

ccma.quiz_title: Certified Clinical Medical Assistant (CCMA) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A medication order reads 2500 mg. How many grams is this dose when expressed in grams?

answers.text: 2.5 grams
0.25 grams
25 grams
250 grams

questions.explanation: There are 1,000 milligrams in one gram, so 2,500 milligrams divided by 1,000 equals 2.5 grams.

questions.question: Which discharge instruction is appropriate after a routine venipuncture?

answers.text: Remove the bandage as soon as the patient reaches the car and resume weight training with the arm
Keep the bandage on for the period advised, avoid heavy lifting with that arm for a while, and report expanding swelling, pain, or continued bleeding
Soak the arm in hot water that evening to prevent bruising
Expect the arm to bleed lightly for the rest of the day as normal

questions.explanation: Simple aftercare instructions protect the puncture site and tell the patient which developments should be reported.

questions.question: Between patients, how should the electrocardiograph's patient cable and lead wires be cared for?

answers.text: Clean and disinfect the cable and lead wires according to the manufacturer's instructions and office infection-control policy, and inspect them for damage
Soak the entire cable in disinfectant overnight after every use
Wipe the cable only when it looks visibly dirty
Coil the cable tightly around the machine and never inspect it

questions.explanation: Cables contact skin and are handled between patients; manufacturer-directed cleaning, disinfection, and inspection maintain both infection control and function.

questions.question: A patient returns for suture removal. Before starting, what should the medical assistant verify?

answers.text: The provider's order for removal, the wound's appearance, and that the correct removal supplies and good lighting are ready
That the patient wants every other suture left in place permanently
That no order is needed if the sutures look loose
That the wound should be soaked in water first

questions.explanation: Removal requires an order, a wound check, and ready supplies with good lighting so healing can be assessed as sutures come out.

questions.question: A patient is unsure whether the patient portal account was activated. Which support step helps most?

answers.text: Give the patient a staff member's login to use temporarily
Tell the patient the portal is optional so activation does not matter
Ask the patient to create several accounts until one works
Check the activation status, resend the invitation if needed, and walk the patient through signing in and setting a password

questions.explanation: Checking status, resending the invitation, and guided sign-in resolve activation problems without sharing credentials.

questions.question: A note describes the knees as positioned below the hips. Which positional term means below or toward the feet?

answers.text: Superior
Proximal
Inferior
Dorsal

questions.explanation: Inferior means below or toward the feet.

questions.question: At what angle is the needle typically inserted for a routine antecubital venipuncture, and how is the bevel oriented?

answers.text: About 80 to 90 degrees to the skin, with the bevel facing down
Flat against the skin at nearly 0 degrees, bevel sideways
About 60 degrees, pushing straight down through the vein
About 15 to 30 degrees to the skin, with the bevel facing up

questions.explanation: A shallow angle with the bevel up lets the needle slide into the vein lumen with the least tissue and vein damage.

questions.question: The provider removes a tissue sample during a procedure. What is the medical assistant's role with the specimen?

answers.text: Label the container at the patient's side with verified identifiers, place it in the correct preservative as directed, and document the handoff
Label the container later from memory at the front desk
Hold the specimen in an unlabeled cup until the end of the day
Discard any sample that looks too small to test

questions.explanation: Side labeling with verified identifiers, the correct preservative and a documented handoff prevent specimen mix-ups and lost results.

questions.question: A patient is collecting a stool specimen at home for occult blood testing using cards. Which instruction is correct?

answers.text: Apply a thin smear from different areas of the stool to the card windows as directed, avoid contaminating the sample with toilet water or urine, and return the card within the stated time
Collect one large sample in a jar of water
Take samples only from a single spot on one stool
Store the completed card in a hot car until the next appointment

questions.explanation: Correct card technique, uncontaminated sampling from different areas, and timely return keep the test valid.

questions.question: Halfway through a multi-tube draw, the assistant realizes the serum tube was filled before the light blue-top tube. What is the best response?

answers.text: Complete the draw, flag the coagulation specimen for the laboratory with a note about the collection order, and follow laboratory direction on whether it must be recollected
Say nothing and send both tubes, because the laboratory cannot tell
Pour the citrate tube's blood into a fresh tube so it looks newly drawn
Discard the patient's other correctly drawn tubes as well

questions.explanation: A sequence error that may affect a specimen is disclosed to the laboratory with the specimen, which decides acceptability, rather than being hidden or disguised.

questions.question: A patient asks to be worked in for an earache today, and the schedule is full. What should the medical assistant do first?

answers.text: Promise a specific time before checking with anyone
Tell the patient the practice never sees anyone the same day
Check with the provider or follow the practice's work-in policy, and offer the earliest appropriate option based on that guidance
Add the patient to the schedule without informing the provider

questions.explanation: Work-in requests follow practice policy and provider input; promising a time before checking can create commitments the schedule cannot keep.

questions.question: After hearing the provider's explanation, a competent adult declines a recommended test and asks to leave. What is the correct handling?

answers.text: Respect the decision, notify the provider promptly, and document the refusal and the information given under clinic policy
Insist the test is required and schedule it anyway
Tell the patient insurance will be cancelled if the test is refused
Ask a family member to overrule the patient

questions.explanation: A competent adult may refuse care after being informed; the refusal is honored, the provider is told, and the exchange is documented.

questions.question: A patient with a muscle disorder has impaired energy production in muscle cells. Which organelle produces most of the cell's usable energy?

answers.text: Golgi apparatus
Endoplasmic reticulum
Mitochondria
Nucleolus

questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the cell's ATP through cellular respiration, supplying energy for muscle contraction and other work.

questions.question: Before spirometry, a patient mentions recent eye surgery and significant chest discomfort when straining. What should the medical assistant do?

answers.text: Coach the patient to blow more gently and proceed without reporting
Reschedule the patient without telling the provider why
Pause and report this to the provider before testing, since forceful blowing raises pressures that can matter after certain surgeries or with chest symptoms
Proceed, because spirometry is noninvasive and always safe

questions.explanation: Recent surgery and chest symptoms can make forceful exhalation unsafe; provider review precedes testing.

questions.question: A waived glucose-type meter displays an error code during quality control that the manual links to a damaged strip vial left open. What should the medical assistant do?

answers.text: Ignore the code if patient readings look reasonable
Close the vial tightly and reuse the same strips after an hour
Continue using the vial and note the error code only
Discard the compromised strips, open a new vial, repeat control testing, and document the problem and resolution

questions.explanation: Compromised strips can bias results; replacing them and repeating controls confirms the system is sound again.

questions.question: A patient has limited reading ability and is embarrassed about it. How should the medical assistant adapt education about a new medication routine?

answers.text: Provide the standard dense instruction sheet and suggest a family member read it aloud at home
Speak more loudly and slowly, assuming hearing is also a problem
Skip education and note that the patient is noncompliant with instructions
Use plain spoken language, a simple picture-based schedule, and teach-back, offering materials without drawing attention to reading level

questions.explanation: Plain language, visual schedules, and teach-back deliver the content respectfully without shaming the patient or abandoning education.

questions.question: A coworker's draft letter to a patient is filled with abbreviations and technical terms the patient is unlikely to understand. What is the best improvement?

answers.text: Add a dictionary page so the patient can look up each term
Send it unchanged because technical language looks more professional
Rewrite the letter in plain language, spelling out terms and keeping the provider's meaning unchanged
Shorten the letter by removing the instructions entirely

questions.explanation: Patient correspondence works only if the reader can act on it, so plain language replaces jargon while the clinical meaning stays intact.

questions.question: A semicritical instrument's high-level disinfection log shows the soak time was much shorter than the product requires, but the instrument was already returned to the procedure area. What should the medical assistant do?

answers.text: Add the missing minutes to the log so the record matches the requirement
Remove the instrument from service, notify the supervisor, and reprocess it for the full required time before any use
Soak the instrument in water for the remaining time to complete the total
Use the instrument promptly so the short soak matters less

questions.explanation: Shortened high-level disinfection cannot be corrected on paper or with water; the item must be withdrawn and fully reprocessed.

questions.question: A patient presents with sudden severe tearing pain between the shoulder blades and a weak pulse in one arm. The provider is with another patient. What should the medical assistant do?

answers.text: Room the patient routinely and complete a full review of systems first
Reassure the patient that muscle strain is common and offer a massage referral
Ask the patient to return tomorrow when the schedule is lighter
Recognize a possible life-threatening emergency, alert the provider immediately, and activate emergency services per protocol

questions.explanation: Sudden tearing pain between the shoulder blades with a pulse difference can signal a major blood-vessel emergency and must be escalated immediately.

questions.question: A patient who recently moved within the same city asks that future screening reminders go to a new phone number. Why does updating this detail matter for care coordination?

answers.text: Contact details are administrative trivia unrelated to clinical care
The old number should be kept as primary because it worked before
Reminders will find the patient regardless of the number on file
Accurate contact information is what makes reminder, result-notification, and referral outreach reach the patient; updating it at the request prevents future missed loops

questions.explanation: Every coordination loop depends on reaching the patient; keeping contact data current is foundational coordination work, not trivia.

ascp-mlt.quiz_title: ASCP Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which historical practice tested donor plasma against recipient cells and is no longer routinely performed?

answers.text: The antibody screen
The direct antiglobulin test
The major crossmatch
The minor crossmatch

questions.explanation: The minor crossmatch fell from routine use as donor antibody screening and component preparation improved.

questions.question: Which quality control practice applies when a new lot of glucose meter strips is put into service?

answers.text: Use patient specimens to test the new lot without controls
Skip controls if the lot number differs by only one digit
Test the new lot with control solutions and verify performance before patient use, documenting the check
Assume the new lot matches the old lot code without verification

questions.explanation: Lot changes require control verification and correct code or calibration entry before patient testing, with documentation under the point-of-care quality program.

questions.question: Hypoglycemia documented in the laboratory is best confirmed under which specimen practice?

answers.text: A urine glucose collected several hours later
A random capillary result from a poorly perfused finger without confirmation
A hemoglobin A1c drawn the following week
A properly collected laboratory plasma glucose drawn during symptoms, handled to prevent glycolysis

questions.explanation: Reliable confirmation requires an accurate plasma measurement at the time of symptoms with glycolysis controlled, because delays and capillary limitations can misclassify borderline values.

questions.question: What is the basic design of a mixing study for a prolonged clotting time?

answers.text: Patient plasma is diluted tenfold in saline and the test is repeated
Patient whole blood is mixed with reagent red cells and observed for agglutination
Patient plasma is heated and the test is repeated on the supernatant
Patient plasma is mixed with normal pooled plasma, typically in equal parts, and the clotting test is repeated

questions.explanation: Normal pooled plasma supplies roughly half-normal levels of every factor, which is enough to normalize the test if a factor deficiency is the cause of the prolongation.

questions.question: A stool culture is set up. Why is a selective medium for enteric pathogens included alongside enriched media?

answers.text: To make all organisms grow faster
To suppress competing normal bowel flora so enteric pathogens can be recovered and recognized
To replace the need for incubation
To sterilize the normal flora in the patient specimen container

questions.explanation: Selective agents inhibit much of the dense normal flora that would otherwise overgrow slower or less numerous pathogens on nonselective plates.

questions.question: During emergency release before testing is complete, which red cell choice is standard for a patient of unknown group?

answers.text: Group A plasma
Group O Rh-negative red cells, with Rh-positive substitution governed by inventory policy for defined populations
Group AB red cells
The first unit on the shelf

questions.explanation: Group O red cells lack A and B antigens; Rh-negative is preferred when Rh type is unknown, with policy-based exceptions when inventory is limited.

questions.question: A sediment shows cholesterol crystals as flat plates with notched corners in urine with heavy proteinuria and oval fat bodies. What pattern do they complete?

answers.text: An acute bacterial pattern
A contamination pattern
A normal fasting pattern
A lipid-rich nephrotic laboratory pattern

questions.explanation: Cholesterol plates accompany lipiduria and heavy proteinuria. Together with oval fat bodies they complete a lipid-rich sediment pattern.

questions.question: A salicylate level is markedly increased and a repeat on the same specimen agrees, with quality control acceptable. What is the correct action?

answers.text: Report the average of salicylate and acetaminophen results
Hold the result until symptoms are documented by the bench
Release the verified result promptly and follow critical or urgent notification procedure as applicable
Dilute the specimen until the value falls in range and report that value

questions.explanation: Markedly increased toxicology results that verify on repeat are released promptly with required notification. The bench does not delay results pending clinical documentation.

questions.question: In a factor assay, why are several dilutions of patient plasma tested and checked for parallelism with the standard curve?

answers.text: Multiple dilutions are used only to consume extra reagent
Nonparallel results suggest an inhibitor or interfering substance distorting the assay rather than a true single-factor level
Parallelism confirms the platelet count in the plasma
Dilutions are averaged to hide out-of-range results

questions.explanation: If the patient's dilution curve does not run parallel to the reference curve, the measured activity changes with dilution, a hallmark of interference that must be flagged rather than reported as a clean factor level.

questions.question: A differential report notes marked anisocytosis, and the automated red cell distribution width is increased. What does anisocytosis describe?

answers.text: Variation in red cell shape
Variation in hemoglobin color between cells
Clumping of red cells into stacks
Variation in red cell size

questions.explanation: Anisocytosis is the morphologic term for increased size variation among red cells, which the distribution width quantifies.

questions.question: A susceptibility control organism gives a zone well below its expected range while patient plates look typical. What is the disposition?

answers.text: Withhold affected patient results, investigate media, disk storage, and inoculum, and repeat controls acceptably before reporting
Report patient results because they look typical
Report only the resistant patient results
Enlarge patient zones by the same amount the control was low

questions.explanation: Control failure invalidates confidence in the run regardless of how patient plates appear. The system must be corrected and re-verified.

questions.question: A dilution is made by adding 0.5 mL of specimen to 4.5 mL of diluent, and the diluted specimen measures 12 units. What is the original concentration?

answers.text: 24 units
120 units
60 units
6 units

questions.explanation: The total volume is 5.0 mL, so the dilution factor is 5.0 divided by 0.5, which is 10; 12 multiplied by 10 equals 120.

questions.question: During identification, every panel cell is reactive and the autocontrol is negative, but the pattern strengthens markedly with enzyme-treated cells. Which broad category is most consistent with this behavior?

answers.text: A simple cold agglutinin
Rouleaux from elevated plasma proteins
An antibody to a high-prevalence antigen or multiple alloantibodies requiring referral-level workup
A clerical error in panel lot selection

questions.explanation: Pan-reactivity without self-reactivity, especially with enzyme enhancement, raises the possibility of an antibody against an antigen present on nearly all cells and warrants escalation beyond routine bench interpretation.

questions.question: A laboratory receives a request to add a blood urea nitrogen to a serum specimen that has been stored refrigerated for several days within the validated stability limit and shows no hemolysis. What is the correct approach?

answers.text: Verify stability and specimen acceptability in the procedure, then perform the add-on if criteria are met
Add water to restore the original volume before testing
Always refuse add-on testing regardless of stability data
Rerun the specimen only after freezing and thawing it twice

questions.explanation: Add-on testing is governed by validated stability, storage, volume, and integrity criteria. When those criteria are met the test can be performed and documented.

questions.question: A cerebrospinal fluid specimen arrives three hours after collection and the count is low, with many degenerated neutrophils noted. What should accompany the report?

answers.text: No comment, because timing does not affect fluid counts
A corrected count doubled to compensate for delay
A comment documenting delayed processing and cell degeneration that may lower the count
A statement that infection is excluded by the low count

questions.explanation: Delayed cerebrospinal fluid processing causes cell loss, so the limitation is documented transparently rather than hidden by an invented correction.

questions.question: A serum specimen for allergen-specific immunoglobulin E testing arrives refrigerated two days after collection and properly labeled. What handling principle applies?

answers.text: The specimen must always be rejected solely because it was not tested the same day
The specimen should be frozen and thawed repeatedly before testing
Serum immunoglobulin E is relatively stable refrigerated for short periods, so testing may proceed if the specimen meets acceptance criteria in procedure
Whole blood should be added back to the serum before testing

questions.explanation: Properly collected serum kept refrigerated within validated stability limits remains acceptable for many serologic assays. Acceptance follows the procedure criteria rather than same-day testing alone.

questions.question: After a positive culture result was released, the laboratory discovers the specimen had been mislabeled and the result belongs to a different specimen. What is the correct quality response?

answers.text: Issue a corrected report promptly, directly notify the receiver of the original result, document the event, and escalate through the laboratory's quality process
Quietly edit the result in the system
Leave the original result because a correction is confusing
Wait for someone to question the result

questions.explanation: A wrong-patient result is a serious quality event. Transparent correction, direct notification, and documented quality follow-up are all required.

questions.question: Panel reactions show negativity with cells lacking the K antigen and strong reactions with K-positive cells, while the patient's own cells are K-negative. Which specificity is most consistent?

answers.text: Anti-D
Anti-K
Autoantibody
Anti-c

questions.explanation: An alloantibody pattern that tracks with K antigen presence, in a K-negative patient, identifies anti-K.

questions.question: A chemistry result is inconsistent with the clinical picture and the specimen was drawn above an intravenous line infusing a solution containing that analyte. What is the most likely explanation and correct action?

answers.text: The first result should be averaged with the repeat result
The analyzer calibration failed for that single specimen
The analyte is produced by the infusion tubing
Intravenous fluid contamination diluted or spiked the specimen, so a properly collected repeat specimen is required

questions.explanation: Drawing above an infusing line can contaminate or dilute blood with infusate, a classic preanalytical error. The result is not reported as valid and a correct recollection is obtained.

questions.question: When reading a disk diffusion plate, several zones have a thin haze of growth inside an otherwise clear zone edge that the method defines. Following the method's reading rules, the technician should:

answers.text: Measure to the plate edge whenever any haze appears
Read the zone using the endpoint the standardized method specifies for that drug and organism, and escalate if the growth pattern is unclear
Ignore all growth inside every zone
Report the drug as resistant whenever haze is seen

questions.explanation: Standardized reading rules define which growth is counted for each drug-organism combination. Unclear patterns are escalated rather than guessed.

ace-cpt.quiz_title: ACE Certified Personal Trainer (ACE CPT) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Where is the gluteus medius located?

answers.text: the front of the upper arm
the chest
along the spine in the back
the side of the hip

questions.explanation: The gluteus medius is located in the side of the hip. Surface anatomy guides assessment, cueing, and exercise selection.

questions.question: Which statement best defines antagonist?

answers.text: the speed of each phase of a repetition, often written as eccentric-pause-concentric-pause seconds
exercise alternating higher-intensity work periods with recovery periods
the principle that adaptations match the exact demands imposed, so training should mirror the desired outcome
the muscle that opposes the primary mover for a given movement

questions.explanation: Antagonist is correctly described by the keyed statement. The other statements define different concepts in this domain, so matching the term to its own description is the skill being tested.

questions.question: Which session structure best fits a client with 30 minutes per session?

answers.text: Paired multi-joint exercises with minimal rest transitions to maximize work density
Maximal testing at every session until the schedule changes
A five-day body-part split regardless of the constraint
Random exercise selection each visit with no recorded progression

questions.explanation: Session structure follows the client's schedule, level, and constraints. The keyed structure fits the stated situation; the alternatives ignore it.

questions.question: Which statement best defines session RPE?

answers.text: a pre-made strategy for handling predictable obstacles to an action plan
a brief session-start review of sleep, soreness, illness, and motivation used to adjust the day's plan
a whole-session difficulty rating multiplied by duration to estimate training load
exercise adjustments during pregnancy, such as avoiding prolonged supine positions after the first trimester and monitoring intensity by talk test

questions.explanation: Session RPE is correctly described by the keyed statement. The other statements define different concepts in this domain, so matching the term to its own description is the skill being tested.

questions.question: Which statement best defines emergency action plan?

answers.text: a written, rehearsed procedure for responding to medical and facility emergencies, including roles and equipment locations
a situation where a trainer's personal interests could improperly influence professional judgment
written permission from a client to use their image in marketing materials
a limit that keeps the trainer-client relationship businesslike and protects both parties

questions.explanation: Emergency action plan is correctly described by the keyed statement. The other statements define different concepts in this domain, so matching the term to its own description is the skill being tested.

questions.question: Which assessment emphasis best fits a client preparing for a firefighters' physical test?

answers.text: Job-task simulations and the specific strength, endurance, and aerobic measures the test uses
A maximal one-repetition-maximum battery for every muscle group
Only a body-weight measurement
No assessment; begin the hardest program immediately

questions.explanation: Assessment follows the client's goal and status: the keyed measures produce the information the program will actually use, at an appropriate challenge level — here, that is: job-task simulations and the specific strength, endurance, and aerobic measures the test uses.

questions.question: Which assessment emphasis best fits a desk worker with neck and shoulder tension complaints?

answers.text: A maximal one-repetition-maximum battery for every muscle group
Only a body-weight measurement
No assessment; begin the hardest program immediately
Posture screening, shoulder mobility, and trunk/neck endurance observation, with referral if pain is significant

questions.explanation: Assessment follows the client's goal and status: the keyed measures produce the information the program will actually use, at an appropriate challenge level — here, that is: posture screening, shoulder mobility, and trunk/neck endurance observation, with referral if pain is significant.

questions.question: A client covers 10 km in 25 minutes at a steady pace. What is the average pace per kilometer?

answers.text: 2.5 minutes per kilometer
1.4 minutes per kilometer
24 minutes per kilometer
3.7 minutes per kilometer

questions.explanation: Pace = time / distance = 25 / 10 = 2.5 min/km.

questions.question: At session check-in, a client reports signs of a developing cold with fever. What is the best adjustment?

answers.text: Refer every decision to a physician regardless of scope
Keep the plan unchanged and tell the client to try harder
End the session plan for the day and advise rest and medical guidance if symptoms worsen
Cancel the program until circumstances are perfect

questions.explanation: Autoregulation matches the day's training to the client's actual state while protecting the program's direction. The keyed adjustment responds to the specific report; cancelling everything or ignoring the report both fail the client — here, that is: end the session plan for the day and advise rest and medical guidance if symptoms worsen.

questions.question: In professional practice, what does the term "competition taper" refer to?

answers.text: using resistance bands in place of cables or weights when traveling or training at home
a chosen repeatable test, such as a 2,000-meter row, used to judge fitness change
seated and supported exercises for clients with limited balance or mobility
reducing volume while keeping some intensity before an event so the client peaks

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the accepted meaning of competition taper. The other statements define different concepts in this domain.

questions.question: In training-business practice, the term "additional insured" means:

answers.text: encouraging satisfied clients to recommend services without paying undisclosed kickbacks or making false claims
a federal tax ID used by a business for tax filings and banking
a party added to an insurance policy so the policy also protects them, commonly required by gyms for trainers
a summary enabling another trainer to serve a client safely during the primary trainer's absence

questions.explanation: The keyed statement correctly defines additional insured. The other statements define different business or safety concepts.

questions.question: In professional practice, what does the term "equipment recall awareness" refer to?

answers.text: monitoring manufacturer recalls and removing affected equipment from service
asking permission before any physical cueing contact and respecting a client's refusal
stating prices, expirations, and refund terms clearly before purchase
arranging interpretation or translated materials so clients fully understand consent and instructions

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the accepted meaning of equipment recall awareness. The other statements define different concepts in this domain.

questions.question: A client weighs 95 kg and stands 185 cm tall. What is the client's body mass index, rounded to one decimal place?
questions.explanation: BMI = weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared: 95 / (1.85)^2 = 27.8.

questions.question: Using the Karvonen method, what target heart rate corresponds to 78% of heart-rate reserve for a 43-year-old with a resting heart rate of 67 bpm?

answers.text: 162 bpm
169 bpm
145 bpm
153 bpm

questions.explanation: Maximum = 177; reserve = 110; target = 67 + 78% x 110 = 153 bpm.

questions.question: A 27-year-old client (resting heart rate 64 bpm) will train in the 70–80% heart-rate-reserve zone. Using the Karvonen method, what is the target heart-rate range?
questions.explanation: Maximum = 193 bpm; reserve = 129; low end = 64 + 70% x 129 = 154; high end = 64 + 80% x 129 = 167 bpm.

questions.question: A client has mastered the standard overhead press and needs a greater challenge. Which progression is appropriate?

answers.text: Skip progressions and test a maximum attempt every session
Repeat the identical standard version for six more months
a barbell push press
Remove the exercise and replace it with stretching

questions.explanation: Once the standard overhead press is mastered, a barbell push press raises the demand while keeping the pattern. Identical work no longer drives adaptation.

questions.question: A client asks the trainer to adjust their implanted medical device settings before exercise. What should the trainer do?

answers.text: Adjust it if the client explains how
Search online for instructions and proceed
Ask another member who has the same device
Decline — device settings are managed by the client's medical team — and follow the clinician's exercise guidance

questions.explanation: The keyed action protects safety, follows policy and ethics, and keeps the trainer inside professional boundaries. The alternatives defer, hide, or profit from the problem — here, that is: decline — device settings are managed by the client's medical team — and follow the clinician's exercise guidance.

questions.question: A client's resting blood pressure, measured correctly on two occasions, averages 122/77 mmHg. Using standard adult categories, which classification fits — and what is the trainer's role?

answers.text: Stage 2 hypertension range (at or above 140/90) — the trainer records, informs, and refers per screening protocol rather than diagnosing
Normal (below 120/80) — the trainer records, informs, and refers per screening protocol rather than diagnosing
Elevated (systolic 120–129 with diastolic below 80) — the trainer records, informs, and refers per screening protocol rather than diagnosing
Stage 1 hypertension range (130–139 or 80–89) — the trainer records, informs, and refers per screening protocol rather than diagnosing

questions.explanation: Trainers classify screening values against standard categories to decide referral, but the classification is a screening step, not a diagnosis. Values are categorized by the higher of the systolic or diastolic band — here, that is: elevated (systolic 120–129 with diastolic below 80) — the trainer records, informs, and refers per screening protocol rather than diagnosing That is the response the facts in this item call for: a client's resting blood pressure, measured correctly on two occasions, averages 122/77 mmHg. Using standard adult categories, which classification fits — and what is the trainer's role.

questions.question: A 24-year-old client has a resting heart rate of 62 bpm. Using the Karvonen (heart-rate reserve) method with an age-predicted maximum of 220 minus age, what is the target heart rate at 70% of heart-rate reserve?

answers.text: 171 bpm
147 bpm
156 bpm
164 bpm

questions.explanation: Maximum = 220 - 24 = 196 bpm; reserve = 196 - 62 = 134; target = 62 + 70% x 134 = 156 bpm.

questions.question: An activity rated at 8 METs is performed by a 90 kg client for 40 minutes. Using kcal/min = METs x 3.5 x body mass (kg) / 200, approximately how many kilocalories are expended?

answers.text: 539 kcal
504 kcal
476 kcal
564 kcal

questions.explanation: Rate = 8 x 3.5 x 90 / 200 kcal per minute; over 40 minutes that totals about 504 kcal.

rnc-ob.quiz_title: Inpatient Obstetric Nursing (RNC-OB) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which blood pressure pattern meets the diagnostic threshold for hypertension in pregnancy?

answers.text: Mild dependent ankle edema at the end of the day
Weight gain of 1 pound over the past week
Headache that resolves promptly after acetaminophen
A blood pressure of 162/112 mmHg that persists on repeat measurement

questions.explanation: Hypertension in pregnancy is systolic 140 or higher or diastolic 90 or higher on two readings; a persistent reading in the 160s/110s exceeds the severe threshold. A single mildly elevated value requires confirmation rather than diagnosis.

questions.question: Placenta previa, accreta spectrum, and abruption share which most serious maternal risk?

answers.text: Massive obstetric hemorrhage
Fetal exsanguination
Fetal growth restriction
Disseminated intravascular coagulation

questions.explanation: All three placental disorders can produce sudden, large-volume maternal hemorrhage; anticipation — typed and crossmatched blood, large-bore access, and a hemorrhage cart — is the common nursing thread.

questions.question: After membranes rupture, contractions often intensify because of which mechanism?

answers.text: Uteroplacental blood flow decreases during contractions
Maternal catecholamine release inhibiting contractions
Oxytocin release triggered by cervical stretch
Fundal dominance of contraction propagation

questions.explanation: With the forewaters gone, the presenting part applies directly to the cervix, increasing stretch-mediated oxytocin release and contraction strength — one reason amniotomy can augment labor.

questions.question: A vigorous newborn is born through meconium-stained fluid. Which action is correct?

answers.text: Dry and stimulate the newborn and proceed with routine care, reserving suction for obstruction
Support the patient in a knee-chest or steep Trendelenburg position during transport
Provide supportive care with oxygen, ventilation support, and preparation for massive transfusion
Give broad-spectrum antibiotics and an antipyretic and notify the newborn team

questions.explanation: Vigorous infants born through meconium need no airway intervention beyond routine care. Suctioning — including intubation for suction — is reserved for the nonvigorous infant or an obstructed airway, per current neonatal resuscitation guidance.

questions.question: Which position and environment define safe sleep teaching for discharge?

answers.text: Place the newborn skin-to-skin with the mother and monitor temperature
Begin positive-pressure ventilation for apnea or a heart rate under 100
Perform the critical congenital heart disease pulse oximetry screen after 24 hours
Supine on a firm, flat, bare surface in the parents' room, with no soft bedding, positioners, or bed-sharing

questions.explanation: That is the safe-sleep standard — back to sleep, bare crib, room-sharing without bed-sharing — taught before discharge and modeled in the nursery; skin-to-skin time is for awake, supervised periods.

questions.question: Which management should the nurse anticipate on admission for a pregnant patient in diabetic ketoacidosis?

answers.text: Encourage the patient to skip breakfast before the glucose tolerance test
Restrict all carbohydrate intake for the remainder of the pregnancy
Start an insulin infusion per protocol and obtain arterial blood gases and electrolytes
Document the finding and recheck glucose at the next prenatal visit

questions.explanation: DKA management is insulin infusion, aggressive isotonic fluids, potassium-guided electrolyte replacement, and acid-base monitoring, with continuous fetal monitoring once the mother is stabilized. Correcting the mother is the fetal resuscitation.

questions.question: Which initial evaluation step is most important when a patient at 30 weeks presents with suspected preterm labor?

answers.text: Discharge the patient home without evaluation because she is not yet at term
Give tocolysis to gain time for corticosteroids, magnesium neuroprotection, and transport
Perform a sterile speculum examination and assess cervical change over time
Give antibiotics to prolong pregnancy when membranes are intact and there is no infection

questions.explanation: Evaluation confirms or refutes cervical change, checks for ruptured membranes and infection, and avoids repeated digital examinations when membrane status is uncertain. Documented change over time is the diagnostic anchor.

questions.question: A tracing shows baseline fluctuations with an amplitude range of 6 to 25 beats per minute. Which NICHD term applies?

answers.text: Minimal variability
Tachysystole
Marked variability
Moderate variability

questions.explanation: Moderate variability (6–25 bpm) is the single most reliable indicator that the fetus is not acidemic at that moment, because it reflects an intact, oxygenated fetal nervous system.

questions.question: Which perineal incision, once routine, is now performed only for specific indications such as expediting birth for fetal compromise?

answers.text: Cesarean birth
Forceps-assisted birth
Trial of labor after cesarean
Episiotomy

questions.explanation: Routine episiotomy does not protect the perineum and increases severe tear risk with median cuts; restrictive use — for fetal indications or operative birth — is the standard. Median incisions heal with less pain but extend into the sphincter more often than mediolateral.

questions.question: Which cultural-care action best supports a patient whose beliefs shape her expression of labor pain?

answers.text: Reassure the patient that the headache will resolve and encourage oral fluids and caffeine per orders
Assess the patient's coping and ask what she needs rather than relying only on a pain score
Encourage the patient to self-administer the gas beginning just before each contraction peaks
Monitor blood pressure closely and treat hypotension with position change, fluids, and a vasopressor per orders

questions.explanation: Pain expression is culturally patterned — stoicism in one culture, vocalization in another — and neither maps directly onto pain intensity or need. Asking the patient what she wants, with interpreter support as needed, replaces assumptions with her own goals.

questions.question: A patient's culture observes a postpartum confinement period with specific dietary practices. Which nursing approach is correct?

answers.text: Schedule the comprehensive postpartum visit by 12 weeks, with contact within the first 3 weeks
Use a qualified medical interpreter for all teaching and consent discussions
Place the newborn skin-to-skin on the mother's chest immediately after birth
Screen for food insecurity, transportation, and housing needs and connect the family with resources

questions.explanation: Cultural practices around rest, food, and seclusion are accommodated within safety limits — the nurse asks what the practices involve, negotiates the few true conflicts (such as warning-sign follow-up), and documents the plan.

questions.question: A hand is felt alongside the fetal head in the pelvis during a vaginal examination. Which diagnosis best fits these findings?

answers.text: Compound presentation
Umbilical cord prolapse
Intraamniotic infection (chorioamnionitis)
Brow presentation

questions.explanation: A compound presentation — usually a hand beside the head — often resolves as the extremity retracts with descent. Persistent compound presentation with arrest or cord involvement changes the plan.

questions.question: At 26 weeks, Jasmine, a 31-year-old G1P0, presents with fever, flank pain, nausea, and costovertebral angle tenderness. Which diagnosis best fits these findings?

answers.text: HIV infection
Chlamydia infection
Pyelonephritis
Influenza

questions.explanation: Fever with flank pain and CVA tenderness in pregnancy is pyelonephritis until proven otherwise. It usually requires hospital admission for IV antibiotics and monitoring because it can trigger sepsis, respiratory complications, and preterm labor.

questions.question: A modified biophysical profile (nonstress test plus amniotic fluid index) shows a reactive NST but an amniotic fluid index of 3 cm. Which interpretation is correct?

answers.text: Polyhydramnios
Nonreactive nonstress test
Negative (normal) contraction stress test
Oligohydramnios

questions.explanation: An AFI of 5 cm or less (or a single deepest pocket under 2 cm) is oligohydramnios. Because fluid reflects longer-term placental function, an abnormal fluid result makes the modified BPP abnormal even with a reactive NST, and delivery planning follows at term.

questions.question: A patient with an occiput posterior fetus has severe back pain in labor. Which position is most likely to help rotation and relieve pain?

answers.text: Notify the provider of the finding promptly
Assess the fundus, lochia, vital signs, and bladder at regular intervals
Hands-and-knees or another forward-leaning position
Apply fundal pressure to speed the birth

questions.explanation: Hands-and-knees unloads the sacrum, relieving back pain, and lets gravity encourage the occiput to rotate toward anterior; sacral counterpressure during contractions helps as well.

questions.question: Oxytocin is infusing for augmentation and the patient reaches the active phase with strong spontaneous contractions. Which evidence-based option exists?

answers.text: Begin continuous fetal monitoring and contraction monitoring
Document the indication for induction in the record
Discontinue the oxytocin infusion now that active labor is self-sustaining, with monitoring continuing
Stop the oxytocin infusion and begin intrauterine resuscitation

questions.explanation: Once active labor is established, stopping oxytocin in selected patients reduces tachysystole and related cesareans without clearly worsening outcomes — an elective discontinuation, distinct from stopping for a concerning tracing.

questions.question: A patient is 7 cm dilated with contractions every 2–3 minutes and is focused inward, no longer chatting between contractions. Which stage and phase is she in?

answers.text: Fourth stage
First stage, active phase
First stage, latent phase
Third stage

questions.explanation: Active phase begins around 6 cm in contemporary practice and is marked by more rapid dilation and the behavioral shift toward concentration and reliance on support.

questions.question: Maria, a 28-year-old G2P1, at 30 weeks reports using methamphetamine. She is hypertensive, tachycardic, and reports decreased fetal movement. Which complication is the team most alert for, given the vasoconstrictive effects of stimulants?

answers.text: Alcohol use disorder
Opioid use disorder
Perinatal depression
Placental abruption

questions.explanation: Stimulant vasoconstriction and acute hypertension can shear the placenta, causing abruption; hypertension with decreased fetal movement after methamphetamine use is evaluated with that emergency at the top of the list.

questions.question: A newborn's cord artery gas shows pH 7.22, a high-normal pCO2, and a base deficit of 6 mmol/L after a short second stage with deep variable decelerations. Which interpretation is most likely?

answers.text: A reassuring response to fetal stimulation
Umbilical venous values reflecting placental function
Respiratory acidemia
Mixed respiratory and metabolic acidemia

questions.explanation: Brief cord compression near birth produces a mild, predominantly respiratory picture that clears rapidly. The base deficit is only mildly elevated, arguing against significant metabolic accumulation.

questions.question: Severe perineal pain and pressure with an inability to void 4 hours after a vaginal birth, and a tense, discolored bulge at the introitus, most likely indicate what?

answers.text: Lochia serosa
Uterine atony
Perineal hematoma
Lochia rubra

questions.explanation: A vulvovaginal hematoma collects blood in the closed perineal space: pain out of proportion, urinary retention, and a tense purple mass. Small stable ones are observed; expanding ones need surgical evacuation — and the blood loss is hidden, so vital signs and hemoglobin are tracked.

nln-nex.quiz_title: NLN NEX (Nursing Entrance Exam) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A synonym for 'capable' is:

answers.text: reliable
distinguish
able
shortage

questions.explanation: 'Able' is a synonym for 'capable', which means: having the ability to do something well. Synonyms share essentially the same meaning.

questions.question: What is the range of 12, 78, 6, 9, 17?
questions.explanation: The range is the largest value minus the smallest: 78 - 6 = 72. This is a standard fact at the high-school and early-college level covered by the entrance examination.

questions.question: What is true about oxidation?

answers.text: A physical change alters a substance's form but not its identity, while a chemical change produces a new substance
Organic compounds are compounds that contain carbon, usually bonded to hydrogen
Oxidation is a chemical reaction in which a substance loses electrons, often by combining with oxygen
Metals are generally shiny, malleable, and good conductors of heat and electricity, while nonmetals are generally poor conductors

questions.explanation: Rusting is the slow oxidation of iron in the presence of water and oxygen. This is a standard fact at the high-school and early-college level covered by the entrance examination.

questions.question: What is 112 ÷ 8?
questions.explanation: Divide: 112 ÷ 8 = 14, because 8 × 14 = 112. Division and multiplication are inverse operations, so the check confirms the quotient.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Engineering students study famous failures as carefully as famous successes. A bridge that collapsed in high winds in 1940 taught designers how structures twist in moving air, a lesson no textbook had conveyed. Investigators traced the disaster to a design that had never been tested in a wind tunnel. Modern practice now requires such testing for long bridges. The failure, costly as it was, permanently changed what engineers are expected to check.

What is the main idea of the passage about learning from failure in engineering?

answers.text: Studying engineering failures has led to lasting improvements in design practice
The desert tortoise is adapted to survive long dry periods, largely by living underground
Ferry commuters value predictability and comfort more than speed
The community orchestra thrives on neighborhood connection as much as musical quality

questions.explanation: The passage as a whole presents this main idea: Studying engineering failures has led to lasting improvements in design practice. The other choices state ideas from other passages or narrower points.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

When the recycling company raised its fees, the town council faced a choice: raise taxes, charge households directly, or end curbside recycling. At the public hearing, residents surprised the council by favoring the household fee, provided low-income families were exempted. Several speakers noted that they had sorted recyclables for years and considered the habit part of being a good neighbor. The council adopted the fee with the exemption, and participation barely changed.

Which detail is stated in the passage about the town's recycling decision?

answers.text: Children read to daily hear millions more words by kindergarten than children who are not
Money spent at a local farm is likely to be spent again within the region
The vault was sited so permafrost would keep seeds frozen even if cooling systems failed
The council adopted the household fee with an exemption for low-income families

questions.explanation: The passage states this directly: The council adopted the household fee with an exemption for low-income families. The other choices are statements drawn from other passages.

questions.question: Solve for x: x + 22 = 58
questions.explanation: Subtract 22 from both sides to isolate x: x = 58 - 22 = 36. Checking, 36 + 22 = 58. This is a standard fact at the high-school and early-college level covered by the entrance examination.

questions.question: For the trachea, pick the accurate statement.

answers.text: The gallbladder is a small sac beneath the liver that stores bile and releases it into the small intestine
The diaphragm is the dome-shaped muscle beneath the lungs that is the main muscle of breathing
The trachea is the windpipe, a tube reinforced with cartilage rings that carries air from the larynx to the bronchi
The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the human body and is located in the thigh

questions.explanation: Cartilage rings keep the trachea open so air can always pass. This is a standard fact at the high-school and early-college level covered by the entrance examination.

questions.question: Select the meaning of the word 'controversial'.

answers.text: to make or become less in size, importance, or intensity
giving rise to public disagreement or debate
to eat, drink, or use up something
a thing made for a particular purpose, especially a piece of equipment

questions.explanation: The word 'controversial' means: giving rise to public disagreement or debate. In context: The new policy proved controversial among residents.

questions.question:
Read the passage.

Plains Indian tribes kept records called winter counts: pictorial calendars in which each year was marked by a single image of its most memorable event, painted on hide. A year might be remembered for a meteor shower, an epidemic, or a great hunt. Keepers of the count could recite the history of the community year by year from the images. The counts are calendars, but they are also arguments about what mattered — history as a community chose to remember it.

As described in the passage, which statement about the winter count is accurate?

answers.text: Algae living inside coral tissues supply much of the corals' food
The return journey north from Mexico takes several generations of butterflies
Each year in a winter count was marked by an image of its most memorable event
Deaths in Semmelweis's ward fell dramatically after hand washing was required

questions.explanation: The passage states this directly: Each year in a winter count was marked by an image of its most memorable event. The other choices are statements drawn from other passages.

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'assess'?

answers.text: hardworking
stray
collect
evaluate

questions.explanation: 'Evaluate' is a synonym for 'assess', which means: to evaluate or estimate the nature, value, or quality of something. Synonyms share essentially the same meaning.

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'delicate'?

answers.text: fragile
traditional
exhaust
modern

questions.explanation: 'Fragile' is a synonym for 'delicate', which means: easily broken or damaged; requiring careful handling. Synonyms share essentially the same meaning.

questions.question: Round 1908 to the nearest hundred.
questions.explanation: Look at the digit to the right of the hundreds place in 1908; rounding to the nearest hundred gives 1900.

questions.question: Which statement about chromosomes is accurate?

answers.text: Ribosomes are the sites where amino acids are linked together to build proteins
The cytoskeleton is a network of protein fibers that gives the cell its shape and helps move materials within it
Meiosis is cell division that produces gametes with half the chromosome number of the parent cell
Human body cells normally contain 46 chromosomes arranged in 23 pairs

questions.explanation: One chromosome of each pair comes from each parent, giving 46 in total. This is a standard fact at the high-school and early-college level covered by the entrance examination.

questions.question: Which description of bacteria and disease is correct?

answers.text: Not all bacteria cause disease; many live harmlessly on the skin and in the intestines and aid digestion
Mental health includes emotional and social well-being and affects how people think, feel, handle stress, and relate to others
Screening tests are used in people without symptoms to detect diseases early, when treatment is most effective
Brushing and flossing remove plaque, a bacterial film whose acids cause tooth decay and gum disease

questions.explanation: Helpful gut bacteria also compete with harmful microbes for space and nutrients. This is a standard fact at the high-school and early-college level covered by the entrance examination.

questions.question: A trip lasts 5 hours and 45 minutes. How many minutes is that in total?
questions.explanation: Convert the hours first: 5 × 60 = 300 minutes, then add the extra minutes: 300 + 45 = 345 minutes.

questions.question: Which statement about chloroplasts is accurate?

answers.text: The nucleus stores the cell's DNA and controls the cell's activities by directing protein synthesis
In the carbon cycle, carbon moves between the atmosphere, living organisms, oceans, and rocks through processes such as photosynthesis and respiration
Chloroplasts are the organelles in plant cells where photosynthesis takes place
The cell wall is a rigid layer outside the cell membrane that supports and protects plant cells

questions.explanation: Only cells with chloroplasts can capture sunlight to make food. This is a standard fact at the high-school and early-college level covered by the entrance examination.

questions.question: A trip lasts 1 hours and 30 minutes. How many minutes is that in total?
questions.explanation: Convert the hours first: 1 × 60 = 60 minutes, then add the extra minutes: 60 + 30 = 90 minutes.

questions.question: Which description of glucagon's role in raising glucose is correct?

answers.text: Bones support the body, protect organs, allow movement, store minerals such as calcium, and produce blood cells
Glucagon is a hormone that raises blood glucose by signaling the liver to release stored glucose
Ventilation is the physical movement of air into and out of the lungs, driven by pressure differences
Hormones are chemical messengers released into the blood by endocrine glands that regulate activities in target organs

questions.explanation: Insulin and glucagon work in opposition to keep blood glucose in a narrow range. This is a standard fact at the high-school and early-college level covered by the entrance examination.

questions.question: How should the immune response in biology be described?

answers.text: White blood cells are the cells of the immune system that identify and destroy pathogens
Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria or stop them from growing, and they are not effective against viruses
An adaptation is an inherited trait that improves an organism's ability to survive and reproduce in its environment
Vaccines train the immune system by exposing it to a harmless form or part of a pathogen

questions.explanation: Some white blood cells engulf invaders while others produce antibodies against them. This is a standard fact at the high-school and early-college level covered by the entrance examination.

c-efm.quiz_title: Electronic Fetal Monitoring (C-EFM) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What happens to placental exchange surface as a pregnancy passes its due date?

answers.text: It gradually declines as the placenta ages, with calcification and infarction reducing reserve — the physiology behind postterm surveillance
The ductus venosus, which streams oxygenated umbilical-vein blood past the liver toward the fetal heart
The ductus arteriosus, which diverts blood from the pulmonary artery into the aorta, bypassing the fluid-filled fetal lungs
Maternal blood delivered by the spiral arteries into the intervillous space, where it bathes the chorionic villi and exchanges gases with fetal blood

questions.explanation: Placental senescence is slow but real: past 41–42 weeks the margin for error narrows, amniotic fluid falls, and late decelerations appear with less provocation. Postterm testing schedules exist because reserve is shrinking.

questions.question: A rise at 30 weeks reaches 11 beats per minute and lasts 9 seconds. Which judgment applies?

answers.text: A prolonged acceleration — a rise above baseline lasting at least 2 minutes but less than 10 minutes
An acceleration — an abrupt rise of at least 15 beats per minute above the baseline, lasting at least 15 seconds, at 32 weeks or beyond
It falls just short of the preterm criterion, which requires at least 10 beats per minute sustained for at least 10 seconds
A baseline change — a rise that persists 10 minutes or more stops being an acceleration and becomes the new baseline

questions.explanation: Near-misses are charted as near-misses. The 9-second rise suggests a system trying to respond; the correct move is continued testing, not a promoted label.

questions.question: Why are premature ventricular contractions documented more anxiously than atrial ones?

answers.text: Supraventricular tachycardia — a sustained, very fast fetal rhythm, typically 220 to 300 beats per minute, driven by a reentry circuit
Premature ventricular contractions — early beats arising from the ventricles, less common than atrial ectopy and evaluated more carefully
Premature atrial contractions — isolated early beats, sometimes conducted and sometimes blocked, the most common and usually benign fetal dysrhythmia
Congenital heart block — a fixed slow ventricular rate that ignores autonomic commands, classically linked to maternal anti-Ro (SSA) antibodies

questions.explanation: Origin changes the prior probabilities: ventricular ectopy associates more often with structural disease, electrolyte disturbance, or myocardial problems. The anxiety is statistical, expressed as evaluation rather than alarm.

questions.question: Which tracing feature can auscultation never report, no matter how experienced the listener?

answers.text: Auscultation hears rate and rhythm only: it cannot judge variability, because beat-to-beat differences are below what the ear can resolve
The auscultated rate is counted for a full interval and compared with the maternal pulse, so a maternal signal is never charted as fetal
Intermittent auscultation — listening to the fetal heart with a Doppler or fetoscope at set intervals, before, during, and after contractions, for eligible low-risk patients
Palpating the contraction while listening links what is heard to what the uterus is doing, which is what makes each scheduled check interpretable

questions.explanation: Variability is a beat-to-beat measurement measured in single beats per minute. The ear integrates over counts and simply cannot resolve it, which is why auscultation findings are charted as rate and rhythm only.

questions.question: Why can an early deceleration be deep — 40 beats — yet remain benign?

answers.text: An abrupt catastrophe — cord prolapse, placental abruption, uterine rupture, or profound maternal hypotension — cutting fetal oxygen delivery suddenly
Uteroplacental insufficiency, in which the placenta cannot keep the fetus oxygenated through the stress of contractions
Umbilical cord compression, which abruptly throttles blood flow through the cord
Fetal head compression, which squeezes the head during contractions and triggers a vagal slowing

questions.explanation: Benignity lives in the mechanism, not the depth. A vagal reflex can pull the rate far down while oxygen delivery never wavers — which is why depth alone never classifies or condemns a deceleration.

questions.question: Which chronic condition most classically produces a fetus with high hemoglobin and thickened blood as an oxygenation adaptation?

answers.text: Cord compression that intermittently strangles umbilical flow, first the vein and then the arteries
A drug effect that stimulates the fetal heart and produces a sustained rise in baseline rate
Maternal diabetes, in which fetal hyperinsulinemia drives increased oxygen consumption and compensatory red-cell production
Excessive uterine activity that shortens relaxation time and progressively drains fetal oxygen reserve

questions.explanation: The diabetic fetus burns oxygen faster (hyperinsulinemia) and compensates with polycythemia — an adaptation that helps in utero and complicates the newborn transition. Its placenta may be large yet functionally insufficient.

questions.question: When oxygen delivery fails briefly, the fetus's first blood-gas abnormality is carbon dioxide retention. Which disorder does that produce?

answers.text: Metabolic acidemia, in which anaerobic metabolism consumes buffer and the base deficit climbs as acid accumulates
Respiratory acidemia, in which retained carbon dioxide lowers pH while the base deficit stays near normal
The umbilical artery sample, which reports the fetus's own acid-base state at birth
The umbilical vein sample, which reports the blood the placenta was delivering and therefore reflects placental function
