Electrical power in watts equals volts times amps (P = V x I)
It regulates voltage

questions.explanation: P = V x I gives watts for DC and resistive AC loads — the basis for load and heat calculations.

uscg-able-seaman.quiz_title: USCG Able Seaman Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures bitts and chocks?

answers.text: Displacement is the maximum cargo weight the vessel can lift
Bitts are fairleads on the mast
Bitts are paired vertical posts for securing mooring lines; chocks are fittings that guide lines through the rail
A vessel with sport-fishing rods out is engaged in fishing under the Rules

questions.explanation: Lines are made fast to bitts or cleats; chocks give the line a fair lead and protect it from chafe at the rail.

questions.question: Which description of lookout duty matches accepted maritime practice?

answers.text: Only the master, never the vessel, answers for wake damage
Radar alone satisfies the lookout requirement on a clear day
The lookout may also run errands below during quiet periods
Every vessel must at all times maintain a proper lookout by sight and hearing and by all available means, so as to fully appraise the situation and the risk of collision

questions.explanation: The lookout rule has no off switch. On the AB's watch that means eyes up, hearing unobstructed, reports crisp — radar and AIS assist but never replace the human lookout.

questions.question: A trainee asks about hawsepipe. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: The hawsepipe carries fuel to the bow thruster
The hawsepipe is the pipe through which the anchor chain runs from the deck to the hawse opening in the bow
Trim is the angle of the rudder at rest
Constrained by draft applies only to vessels at anchor

questions.explanation: Chain travels from windlass through the hawsepipe to the anchor. The spurling pipe leads chain down into the chain locker.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes masthead light arc?

answers.text: A masthead light shows over 360 degrees
A masthead light shows over 135 degrees like a sternlight
A masthead light is red on the port side
A masthead light is a white light showing over an arc of 225 degrees, visible from ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam on each side

questions.explanation: Masthead (225°), sidelights (112.5° each), and sternlight (135°) together cover the full circle without overlap confusion.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding anchor light?

answers.text: A vessel at anchor shows an all-round white light where it can best be seen (two, the forward one higher, if 50 meters or more), and by day a single black ball
A vessel at anchor shows a black diamond by day
An anchored vessel shows its sidelights and masthead light
An anchored vessel under 50 meters shows two white lights vertically

questions.explanation: Anchor lights are all-round white; deck lighting may be added on larger vessels but the anchor lights/shapes remain the legal signal.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how power-driven underway lights is handled at sea.

answers.text: A flashing light is any aid to navigation that flashes
A power-driven vessel underway shows a masthead light forward, a second masthead light abaft and higher if 50 meters or more, sidelights, and a sternlight
A second masthead light is shown forward of and lower than the first
A power-driven vessel under 50 meters must show two masthead lights

questions.explanation: Length drives the second masthead light (≥50 m). Under 50 m she may show one masthead light plus sidelights and sternlight.

questions.question: How would an experienced able seaman best explain compass points: full circle?

answers.text: The compass card is divided into 32 points; each point equals 11.25 degrees
Variation is the same everywhere on earth
The helmsman trims sails without orders
Each point equals 10 degrees

questions.explanation: 32 × 11.25° = 360°. Cardinal (N/E/S/W), intercardinal (NE/SE/SW/NW), and the by-points (N by E, etc.) make up the 32.

questions.question: How would an experienced able seaman best explain iALA Region B returning from sea?

answers.text: Returning from sea, red aids are kept to port
Private aids may use any colors the owner likes
In U.S. waters (IALA Region B), returning from sea the mariner keeps red aids to starboard and green aids to port — 'red, right, returning'
All datums give identical positions

questions.explanation: Red-right-returning is the U.S. (Region B) convention; most of the rest of the world (Region A) is the reverse. The AB sailing foreign-flag itineraries must know both exist.

questions.question: How would an experienced able seaman best explain fiber rope construction?

answers.text: Traditional fiber rope is laid (twisted) in three strands, usually right-laid (strands spiral to the right, 'Z' twist); most modern synthetic line is braided or plaited, which does not unlay like laid rope
Synthetic rope ends need no finishing (they are heat-sealed or whipped — never left raw)
All rope is braided today
6x19 means 6 wires of 19 strands

questions.explanation: Know your material: laid rope splices by strands; braided rope splices by its own fid-and-bury methods. Right-laid is the standard for wire rope too.

questions.question: Which description of windlass operation basics matches accepted maritime practice?

answers.text: Limits may be overridden for the last meter
The brake is left off while heaving
The stopper stays on while the windlass heaves through it

Before heaving anchor the windlass is engaged to the wildcat, the brake and clutch checked, chain stopper/compressor controlled, and the operation is conned from the bridge — the anchor detail never heaves or lets go except on the bridge's orders

questions.explanation: Anchoring is a bridge evolution executed on deck. Orders, reports (chain direction/strain, links at the waterline), and readiness states flow in a closed loop.

questions.question: How would an experienced able seaman best explain lifeboat types and capacity?

answers.text: Enclosed motor lifeboats (totally/partially enclosed as required) are the primary survival craft on cargo ships, each side's boats together able to carry all persons aboard; capacity is marked on the boat and never exceeded
Checks are visual only, engines run annually
Lifeboats are sized for the crew only, passengers use rafts
Helicopter winching areas need no preparation

questions.explanation: Count heads against marked capacity at muster, not at the davit. Boats are provisioned and engined for the full complement marked.

questions.question: Which description of fire triangle and tetrahedron matches accepted maritime practice?

answers.text: Removing oxygen is the only extinguishing method
The chain reaction cannot be interrupted by agents
Ear protection is needed only in the engine room

Fire needs heat, fuel, and oxygen (the triangle); the modern model adds the self-sustaining chemical chain reaction (tetrahedron) — extinguishment removes one element: cooling, smothering, starving, or interrupting the chain

questions.explanation: Every extinguisher and tactic maps to an element: water cools, foam/CO2 smother, closing valves starves, dry chemical interrupts the chain.

questions.question: On a pre-departure walkthrough, the topic of windlass and wildcat comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The wildcat is the sprocketed wheel of the windlass that engages the links of the anchor chain
The wildcat is the drum used only for mooring lines
A shot is the length from the windlass to the hawsepipe
Frames run fore and aft and strakes run across

questions.explanation: The wildcat's pockets grip each chain link as the windlass heaves or pays out. Smooth drums (gypsy heads / warping heads) handle line instead.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers sidelight arcs. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Each sidelight shows over 112.5 degrees, from ahead to 22.5 degrees abaft the beam on its own side — green to starboard, red to port
Sidelights show from astern around to ahead
A composite unit shows two full sets of towing lights
The green light is on the port side

questions.explanation: Seeing red means you are on the other vessel's port side; green, her starboard side — the first clue to aspect and crossing geometry.

questions.question: A new ordinary seaman needs to understand sternlight arc. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: A fishing vessel shows no sidelights even when making way
A sternlight is yellow and shows over 225 degrees
A sternlight is a white light showing over 135 degrees, centered astern (67.5 degrees each side of dead astern)
A composite unit shows two full sets of towing lights

questions.explanation: An overtaking vessel sees the sternlight of the vessel ahead. A special yellow towing light is shown above the sternlight when towing astern (Inland).

questions.question: A lookout reports a light 8 points from dead ahead. What is the relative bearing in degrees? (One point = 11.25 degrees.)
questions.explanation: 8 x 11.25 = 90 degrees.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about stand-on vessel's two-stage duty earns credit?

answers.text: The stand-on vessel's duty is to sound signals and nothing more
The stand-on vessel may never alter course under any circumstance
The stand-on vessel keeps course and speed, but must act when the give-way vessel clearly is not acting in time, and must act at the last when collision cannot be avoided by the give-way vessel alone
The stand-on vessel acts only after collision is inevitable and then only to port

questions.explanation: Stand-on is not stand-still-forever: first hold, then (when the other's failure is apparent) you may act, and finally you must act — avoiding, if possible, turning to port for a vessel on your port side.

questions.question: The water depth at the anchorage is 60 feet and the master orders a scope of 6 to 1 based on depth. How many feet of chain must be paid out?
questions.explanation: Chain = 6 x 60 = 360 feet.

questions.question: The true course is 150 degrees, variation is 11 degrees E, and deviation is 6 degrees E. Uncorrecting (reversing the signs), what compass course must be steered, in degrees?
questions.explanation: True 150 - variation +11 - deviation +6 = compass 133 degrees.

questions.question: On a heading, variation is 7 degrees E and deviation is 3 degrees W. Taking easterly error as positive, what is the total compass error in degrees (give a negative number for westerly)?
questions.explanation: Total error = variation +7 + deviation -3 = +4 degrees.

uscg-qmed.quiz_title: USCG QMED Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures lubricating oil levels?

answers.text: Oil levels are checked once a month
Remote control removes the need for an engine room watch
Sump and header tank oil levels are kept within the marked working range and checked on every round
Calipers measure temperature

questions.explanation: Too little oil starves bearings; too much causes foaming, overheating, and leaks. Levels falling steadily mean consumption or a leak to find.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding hand tools care?

answers.text: Damaged tools are kept in service until they break
Tools are stowed loose on top of machinery
Hand tools are cleaned, inspected, and returned to their stowage after use so they are ready and accounted for
Gate and globe valves are identical inside

questions.explanation: A tool left in machinery spaces can fall into equipment or be impossible to find in an emergency; damaged tools injure people.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding trunk piston and crosshead designs?

answers.text: Large slow-speed engines use a crosshead to take side thrust, keeping it off the cylinder liner, while smaller engines use trunk pistons
A crosshead engine has no connecting rod
Side thrust does not exist in diesel engines
Trunk pistons are used only in steam engines

questions.explanation: The crosshead guide absorbs piston side thrust so the liner sees only vertical motion; trunk pistons take the thrust on the liner wall through the skirt.

questions.question: How would an experienced QMED best explain steering gear types?

answers.text: Steering gear moves the rudder by hydraulic rams or a rotary vane actuator, driven by electric-hydraulic power units, with emergency local control
Static generation during washing is not a hazard
A centrifugal pump delivers the same flow at any head
The rudder is moved by the main engine directly

questions.explanation: Two independent power units are the norm; if remote control fails, the gear is worked locally in the steering flat on orders by phone.

questions.question: Which statement best captures flanged joints?

answers.text: Flanged joints use no gasket
A leaking flange is fixed by overtightening one bolt
Flange bolts are tightened fully one at a time around the circle
A flanged pipe joint is sealed by a gasket compressed evenly between the flange faces as the bolts are tightened in sequence

questions.explanation: Even, cross-pattern tightening compresses the gasket uniformly; one-sided tightening cocks the flange and guarantees a leak.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how measuring with a micrometer is handled at sea.

answers.text: A micrometer measures small dimensions such as shaft journals and clearances to about a thousandth of an inch
A micrometer measures electrical resistance
Expansion is absorbed by tightening flanges harder
Grease and oil are interchangeable in every bearing

questions.explanation: Micrometers (and calipers for larger work) are the precision measuring instruments of the engine room; feeler gauges measure clearances between parts.

questions.question: Which description of calipers matches accepted marine engineering practice?

answers.text: Calipers measure temperature
Calipers transfer or take inside and outside dimensions of parts such as bores, journals, and pipe
Calipers are used only on electrical work
Calipers are cutting tools

questions.explanation: Inside calipers read bores, outside calipers read shafts; the measurement is then read against a rule or micrometer.

questions.question: Which description of diesel engine principle matches accepted marine engineering practice?

answers.text: Compression in a diesel is lower than in a gasoline engine
A diesel engine ignites its fuel by the heat of compression alone, with no spark plug
Diesel fuel ignites from a glow of the exhaust
Injection timing is fixed and unrelated to load

questions.explanation: Air compressed to a small fraction of its volume gets hot enough (well above the fuel's ignition temperature) to ignite the injected spray.

questions.question: Regarding diesel fuel injection purpose, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The injection system meters the fuel, atomizes it, and injects it at the correct time for the load and speed
Injection only stores fuel near the cylinder
Liners wear most at the bottom of the stroke
An engine is started at full fuel without turning it first

questions.explanation: Meter, atomize, time: those three jobs of the injection system decide how completely and smoothly the fuel burns.

questions.question: How would an experienced QMED best explain water tube boiler advantage?

answers.text: Water circulates outside the tubes in a water-tube boiler
Boiler interiors are never inspected
A water-tube boiler holds a small water inventory, raises steam quickly, and suits high pressures, with water inside the tubes and hot gas outside
One gauge reading describes plant efficiency completely

questions.explanation: Small inventory means fast response and less stored energy in a tube failure; fire-tube boilers are the reverse arrangement.

questions.question: Which description of vapor compression cycle matches accepted marine engineering practice?

answers.text: Expansion creates the cooling effect by generating cold
The vapor-compression cycle moves heat by evaporating refrigerant at low pressure, compressing the vapor, condensing it at high pressure, and expanding it back down
The compressor lowers the refrigerant pressure
Set points are changed by the engine room at will

questions.explanation: Evaporator absorbs heat, compressor raises pressure and temperature, condenser rejects heat, expansion valve drops pressure — the four legs of every plant aboard.

questions.question: Which description of lathe purpose matches accepted marine engineering practice?

answers.text: Turning produces only flat surfaces
A lathe turns workpieces against a cutting tool to produce round parts — shafts, pins, bushings — to measured diameters
A lathe cannot cut threads in any setup
A tested item is marked or recorded as such

questions.explanation: Turning, facing, boring, and thread cutting on rotating work: the lathe is the machine shop's foundation machine.

questions.question: For safe and correct engineering practice, which statement about feeler gauge use holds true?

answers.text: A feeler gauge measures the small gap or clearance between two surfaces, such as valve clearance or bearing clearance
Temperature is measured only by hand feel
A feeler gauge measures shaft speed
A feeler gauge tightens pipe flanges

questions.explanation: The blade that slips in with light drag is the clearance. Valve lash, ring gaps, and coupling checks all depend on it.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers four-stroke cycle. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: The four-stroke cycle completes intake, compression, power, and exhaust in four piston strokes and two crankshaft revolutions
Low compression raises that cylinder's exhaust temperature sharply
Four-stroke means four cylinders
The four-stroke cycle has no separate exhaust stroke

questions.explanation: One power stroke per cylinder every two revolutions; separate valve events handle charging and scavenging across the four strokes.

questions.question: Which description of voltage current resistance matches accepted marine engineering practice?

answers.text: Current is stored in a conductor
Resistance is measured in amperes
A single ground must trip propulsion power immediately
Voltage is the electrical pressure that pushes current through a resistance; current is the flow, resistance is the opposition to it

questions.explanation: The water analogy holds: voltage is pressure, current is flow rate, resistance is the restriction. Ohm's law ties the three together.

questions.question: Which description of centrifugal pump operation matches accepted marine engineering practice?

answers.text: The impeller of a centrifugal pump seals positively against the casing
Centrifugal pressure is independent of speed
A hydrostatic level signal is unaffected by liquid density changes
A centrifugal pump adds velocity with its impeller and converts it to pressure in the volute; flow depends on the head it works against

questions.explanation: No positive sealing means no fixed delivery: the pump finds its point where its curve crosses the system's resistance curve.

questions.question: A circuit carries 20 amperes through a resistance of 11 ohms. What voltage is applied, in volts?
questions.explanation: V = I x R = 20 x 11 = 220 volts.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers pipe threads and fittings. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Tapered pipe threads seal by the wedging action of the threads themselves, usually with thread compound or tape
Pipe size names give the exact outside diameter
Pipe threads seal only with a gasket
Straight and tapered pipe threads are interchangeable

questions.explanation: National pipe taper threads tighten and seal as they wedge; nominal pipe size is a name, not the measured diameter.

questions.question: An instructor is checking understanding, the topic of two-stroke cycle comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A two-stroke fires once every two revolutions
A two-stroke engine completes its cycle in one crankshaft revolution, using ports uncovered by the piston for exhaust and charging
A two-stroke engine needs four revolutions per cycle
Two-stroke engines have no lubrication concerns

questions.explanation: Ports in the liner and a scavenge blower or turbocharger clear exhaust and refill the cylinder each revolution — a power stroke every turn.

questions.question: Which description of the fire triangle and fire tetrahedron matches accepted marine engineering practice?

answers.text: Cooling a burn is stopped after thirty seconds in all cases
A fire continues without oxygen if fuel is present
Removing heat has no effect on a fire
Fire needs fuel, oxygen, heat, and (in the modern model) the chemical chain reaction; extinguishing removes one of them

questions.explanation: Cool it, smother it, starve it, or break the chain — every extinguishing method is one of those four sentences.

indiana-plumbing-contractor.quiz_title: Indiana Plumbing Contractor Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures the trade-experience route?

answers.text: Trade experience must be proven only by tax records
Temporary licenses renew without limit
A resident may instead present a notarized statement evidencing at least four years of experience in the plumbing trade
State licensure eliminates all local permit duties

questions.explanation: Experience outside a formal apprenticeship counts if it reaches the four-year floor and is sworn to in the notarized statement the statute requires.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the Commission's verification power?

answers.text: Only the applicant may be contacted during review
Verification ends once affidavits are filed
The Commission must accept application papers at face value
The Commission may seek additional information from the applicant, any employer, or any third party to decide whether examination requirements are met

questions.explanation: Eligibility is actively verified. The Commission's authority to go to employers and third parties is written into the admission rule.

questions.question: Select the accurate statement about the weekly counting cap.

answers.text: There is no weekly cap on counted hours
No more than 40 hours may be counted in any calendar week toward the apprenticeship or experience requirement
The rule binds journeymen but not contractors
Overtime hours count double toward the requirement

questions.explanation: The 40-hour weekly cap is why the requirement cannot be compressed: even heavy overtime stretches across the full four years.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes employer affidavits?

answers.text: A contractor's later reinstatement fee is $100
The Indiana building commissioner licenses plumbers county by county
An examination applicant must submit affidavits from employers verifying all experience claimed in the application
Employer verification is optional if the applicant signs the form

questions.explanation: Every claimed period of experience must be verified by the employer who supervised it; the Commission does not take the applicant's word alone.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes water closet flush volume?

answers.text: Dual-flush closets are prohibited
A standard water closet is limited to a maximum flush of 1.6 gallons per flush, with high-efficiency models flushing less
Water closets may flush up to 3.5 gallons as new fixtures
Flush volume has no maximum for commercial closets

questions.explanation: The 1.6 gallon maximum made the modern closet; older 3.5 and 5 gallon tanks are replacement-only history, not a new-installation option.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about urinal flush volume earns credit?

answers.text: Urinals may flush 1.6 gallons like water closets
A urinal is limited to a maximum flush of 1.0 gallon per flush
Ice machine drains connect directly to a branch
Clinic sinks are drained like lavatories

questions.explanation: Urinals carry their own, tighter maximum; waterless designs satisfy it by using no water at all where they are approved.

questions.question: When checking a journeyman's knowledge of showerhead flow, which response is correct?

answers.text: Flush controls may be placed behind the user in all cases
Sealing the base is prohibited because it hides leaks
Showerheads may flow 5 gallons per minute as new fixtures
A showerhead is limited to a maximum flow of 2.5 gallons per minute at the standard test pressure

questions.explanation: The 2.5 gpm cap applies per shower compartment's outlet arrangement; body-spray designs must account for the combined flow the code allows.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how kitchen faucet flow is handled in practice.

answers.text: Kitchen faucets are limited to 1.5 gpm in all cases
Pull-out sprays are measured differently and unlimited
Rough-in dimensions never vary between brands
A kitchen sink faucet is limited to 2.2 gallons per minute at the standard test pressure

questions.explanation: Kitchen faucets share the lavatory-class maximum; temporary higher-flow features on some models are an engineered exception, not the rating.

questions.question: Which description of purpose of venting matches the Indiana plumbing code as adopted?

answers.text: Vents pressurize the drainage system
Vents are only for odor at the property line
Aggregate venting is not a code concept
Vent piping protects trap seals by admitting and releasing air so drainage flows without siphoning or blowing the seals, and it vents sewer gas to the outdoors

questions.explanation: Every trap seal is a small water plug in a pressure system; venting equalizes that pressure and gives the system's gases an exit that is not a fixture.

questions.question: Which description of maximum static pressure matches the Indiana plumbing code as adopted?

answers.text: Fixture stops are required only for water closets
Where static water pressure exceeds 80 psi, a pressure-reducing valve is installed to bring the building pressure to 80 psi or less
A PRV is required only on commercial services
High pressure is corrected at each fixture instead

questions.explanation: Eighty psi is the system's ceiling: above it, valves chatter, supplies hammer, heaters relieve, and fixture life collapses — the PRV is code, not comfort.

questions.question: Which description of what an isometric drawing is matches the Indiana plumbing code as adopted?

answers.text: Orientation symbols are drafting decoration
Isometrics show only vertical piping
An isometric is drawn without any fittings shown
An isometric plumbing drawing shows the piping system in three dimensions on a single drawing, with pipe runs drawn at 30-degree angles, so lengths, rises, and offsets can be visualized and measured

questions.explanation: The isometric is the plumber's working sketch of the DWV or water system: one drawing that carries the whole run's geometry.

questions.question: Which description of copper pipe types matches the Indiana plumbing code as adopted?

answers.text: Any copper type may be buried in any service
Old insulation may be ripped off freely
Types differ only in color of marking
Copper water tube comes in types K, L, and M in descending wall thickness; underground and high-demand service uses the heavier types as the code's material tables require

questions.explanation: K-L-M is a wall-thickness ladder: the marking color tells the inspector which rung was installed, and the tables assign each rung its permitted duties.

questions.question: For code-compliant Indiana practice, which statement about the work-under-a-contractor route holds true?

answers.text: Working in a plumbing business under the direction of a licensed plumbing contractor for at least four years is a qualifying route for the contractor examination
Any testing company may administer the Indiana plumbing exam
Only work performed as a journeyman counts toward the contractor exam
Business employment without field work qualifies by itself

questions.explanation: The contractor exam recognizes time spent in a real plumbing business under a licensed contractor's direction — the journeyman-to-owner pathway.

questions.question: A journeyman asks the contractor, the topic of lavatory faucet flow comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Lavatory faucets have no flow limit
Public faucets flow more than private by rule
Metering faucets are prohibited in public restrooms
A private lavatory faucet is limited to 2.2 gallons per minute at the standard test pressure, and public lavatory faucets are limited much lower or are metering types

questions.explanation: Public lavatories are the conservation frontier: low maximum flows or self-closing metering faucets that deliver a fixed dose per cycle.

questions.question: Which description of minimum drainage slope for small pipe matches the Indiana plumbing code as adopted?

answers.text: Small pipe requires one-half inch per foot minimum
Horizontal drainage pipe of 2.5 inches and smaller is installed at a slope of not less than one-quarter inch per foot
Failed sections need not be retested after patching
Small pipe requires one-eighth inch per foot

questions.explanation: Quarter-inch per foot is the self-scouring grade for small drains; flatter runs let solids settle out of the carrying water.

questions.question: Which description of temperature and pressure relief valve purpose matches the Indiana plumbing code as adopted?

answers.text: Only commercial heaters need relief protection
Every storage water heater has a temperature and pressure (T&P) relief valve that opens on excessive temperature or pressure, discharging water so the tank cannot become a pressure bomb
Pans are optional above finished ceilings
A pressure-only valve is an equal substitute

questions.explanation: The T&P is the heater's last safety device, sensing both the pressure rise and the far more dangerous temperature rise toward steam.

questions.question: A horizontal drain is laid at a slope of 1/4 inch per foot for a run of 36 feet. What is the total fall, in inches?
questions.explanation: Fall = 1/4 x 36 = 9 inches.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers when an employer affidavit cannot be obtained. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: An applicant who cannot obtain a required employer affidavit must file an affidavit stating the inability and the reason for it
A coworker's letter replaces the required affidavit automatically
The application is automatically denied without every employer affidavit
The applicant may simply omit that period with no explanation

questions.explanation: A defunct employer does not end an application — but the gap must be sworn to and explained, and the Commission may still investigate.

questions.question: A pipe's center-to-center dimension is 60 inches. The fitting take-out is 2 inches at one end and 2 inches at the other. What is the cut length, in inches?
questions.explanation: Cut length = 60 - 2 - 2 = 56 inches.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers prior-experience credit in an apprenticeship. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: A failed candidate must wait four years before any retake
There is no weekly cap on counted hours
Prior credit may cover 100 percent of the apprenticeship
Credit for previous education, training, or experience toward an approved apprenticeship may not exceed 75 percent of the total required hours

questions.explanation: Credit is generous but capped: at most three-quarters of the program may be credited, and the credit must be granted through the federal apprenticeship bureau and approved by the Commission.

massachusetts-journeyperson-sheet-metal.quiz_title: Massachusetts Journeyperson Sheet Metal Worker Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures what is not sheet metal work?

answers.text: Sheet metal work is limited to cutting flat stock in a shop
Residential duct systems are not sheet metal work
Duct or air exhaust systems for refrigeration and combustion units are not sheet metal work
J-1 eligibility has no minimum years, only total hours

questions.explanation: The refrigeration and combustion carve-out is express; ordinary commercial duct and remodeling ductwork are inside the definition.

questions.question: Which statement best captures parallel line development?

answers.text: Layout is the final inspection of installed duct
Parallel line development works only on round pipe
Parallel line development requires a single apex point
Parallel line development suits prismatic shapes such as rectangular duct and square elbows, where element lines stay parallel

questions.explanation: When the fitting's edges run parallel, the pattern wraps those parallel elements onto the flat sheet.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes what duct sizing must satisfy?

answers.text: Velocity may be ignored if the fan is large
A duct system is sized to deliver the required airflow to each space at acceptable pressure loss, noise, and velocity
Pressure loss is set by the installer after the fact
Ducts are sized by the building's square footage alone

questions.explanation: Design airflow, loss, and noise together fix the sizes; an undersized system cannot be cured by fan speed alone.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding non-metal roof coverings?

answers.text: Roof coverings are sheet metal work when a sheet metal worker installs them
Experience counts if the worker later gets licensed
Non-metal roof coverings and their associated flashing are not sheet metal work
Metal flashing on a shingle roof makes the whole roof sheet metal work

questions.explanation: Watershed roof systems are in the definition, but roof coverings and associated metal flashing within them are excepted, and non-metal coverings are outside entirely.

questions.question: Regarding other trades' work boundary, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Any trade may perform any other trade's work on a commercial job
Plumbing and gasfitting are included in the sheet metal license
A sheet metal license overrides every other trade license on a job
Work of a licensed pipe fitter, oil burning technician, refrigeration technician, plumber, or gasfitter under those trades' own laws is not sheet metal work

questions.explanation: Each licensed trade's statutory work stays with that trade; the sheet metal definition yields to the neighboring licenses.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts journeyperson best explain tasks needing no license?

answers.text: No license is required for paid duct repair by a handyman
No license is required for any work under a set dollar amount
All licenses expire December 31
No license is required for transporting or non-professional handling of sheet metal fixtures, or operating heavy machinery to move fixtures to the installation point

questions.explanation: Logistics and rigging support are carved out; installing or repairing the work for the public is not.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts journeyperson best explain purpose of layout?

answers.text: Layout is the shop process of developing flat patterns from drawings so fittings can be cut, formed, and assembled to finished size
Layout means marking duct routes on the building floor only
Standing seams are nailed through the pan
True length is guessed from the nearest view

questions.explanation: Every fitting starts as a flat pattern; layout converts the drawing's finished geometry into cuttable metal.

questions.question: When checking an apprentice's knowledge of radial line development, which response is correct?

answers.text: The Pittsburgh lock is a soldered corner joint
Radial line development suits cones and pyramids, whose element lines radiate from one apex point
Radial line development suits long straight duct runs
Caps are cut exactly to the opening with no allowance

questions.explanation: All surface lines of a cone meet at the apex, so the pattern is struck from that center.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how triangulation is handled in practice.

answers.text: Wired edges are glued
Triangulation develops irregular transitions by dividing the surface into triangles and finding each edge's true length
Triangulation avoids finding true lengths
Triangulation works only on cylinders

questions.explanation: Square-to-rounds and offset transitions have no parallel or radial order, so the surface is broken into triangles.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts journeyperson best explain shearing sheet metal?

answers.text: Shears cut straight lines through sheet metal; the squaring shear is the shop's basic straight-cutting machine
Sequencing is a field concern only
Firestopping is the ceiling trade's problem alone
Shears are used only for curves

questions.explanation: One blade passes another and the sheet parts along the line — the foundation cut of the shop.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts journeyperson best explain reading a title block?

answers.text: The title block identifies the project, sheet, scale, and revision — the first check before using any drawing
Details may be improvised without consequence
The title block is decorative
Snow retention is never needed on metal

questions.explanation: Wrong revision, wrong work; the title block is where a sheet proves it is current.

questions.question: Which description of galvanized steel matches the governing Massachusetts rules and standards?

answers.text: Galvanized steel never corrodes in any service
It is the required material for grease duct in all cases
All solders suit all metals
Galvanized steel is carbon steel coated with zinc, the standard duct material for most comfort systems

questions.explanation: Zinc sacrifices itself for the steel beneath — the workhorse sheet of the trade.

questions.question: A new apprentice needs to understand who may perform sheet metal work for the public. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: J-1 eligibility requires 4,800 hours over three years
Only a master or journeyperson licensed by the Board, with the proper permit from the local building inspector, may perform sheet metal work for the public
A business license alone authorizes an individual to do the work
An unlicensed person may work if a licensee inspects afterward

questions.explanation: Both the license and the permit are required before a licensee performs work for the public.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the three pattern development methods. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Fittings are developed by parallel line development, radial line development, or triangulation, chosen by the fitting's shape
Patterns are developed by freehand sketching only
A cone's pattern is a rectangle
One method serves every fitting shape

questions.explanation: Rectangular-to-round transitions triangulate, elbows radiate from a center, and straight duct develops on parallel lines.

questions.question: Which description of volume damper construction matches the governing Massachusetts rules and standards?

answers.text: Damper blade action has no effect on control
Pooling grease is harmless
Single-blade dampers are used only in small duct
An opposed-blade damper disturbs flow more evenly than a parallel-blade damper at partial settings, making it the better balancing and control damper

questions.explanation: Opposed blades throttle symmetrically; parallel blades skew the air to one side of the duct.

questions.question: Which description of fall protection trigger heights matches the governing Massachusetts rules and standards?

answers.text: The trigger is the same for all industries at four feet for construction
No protection is needed under fifteen feet
Exposure ends at the task boundary
In construction, fall protection is generally required at six feet above a lower level

questions.explanation: Six feet is construction's line — sheet metal roof and duct work routinely happens above it.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts journeyperson best explain purpose of testing adjusting balancing?

answers.text: TAB proves the installed system delivers design airflow to every outlet and adjusts it until measurements match design within tolerance
Pressure falls as speed rises
Parallel fans double pressure
TAB is the fan manufacturer's startup only

questions.explanation: Design intent is a claim; the traverse and the hood readings are the evidence.

questions.question: A rectangular duct measures 24 inches by 12 inches. What is its cross-sectional area, in square feet? (144 square inches = 1 square foot.)
questions.explanation: Area = 24 x 12 = 288 square inches = 2 square feet.

questions.question: A duct carries 1500 cubic feet per minute through a cross-sectional area of 2.5 square feet. What is the air velocity, in feet per minute?
questions.explanation: Velocity = 1500 / 2.5 = 600 feet per minute.

questions.question: A fitting requires 30 square feet of sheet that weighs 1.6 pounds per square foot. What is the sheet weight, in pounds?
questions.explanation: Weight = 30 x 1.6 = 48 pounds.

massachusetts-master-plumber.quiz_title: Massachusetts Master Plumber Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures separate gas fitter licenses?

answers.text: An apprentice license may be renewed forever with no time limit.
Only Part One must be passed because Part Two is not scored.
Massachusetts has separate gas fitter licenses, including journeyman gas fitter, master gas fitter, and liquefied petroleum gas installer credentials.
Massachusetts has no gas fitter license separate from plumbing licenses.

questions.explanation: Gas fitting has its own license types alongside the plumbing ladder.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding plumber seeking gas fitter license?

answers.text: A plumber must repeat the full plumbing apprenticeship to get a gas fitter license.
A plumber is barred from ever holding a gas fitter license.
A licensed plumber who wants a journeyman gas fitter license must still apply, pay the required fees, and pass that exam, but needs no added education or experience for it.
Hydronic work for an HVAC firm counts double toward plumbing hours.

questions.explanation: The plumbing background satisfies education and experience, but the separate application and exam still apply.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding polyethylene pipe underground only?

answers.text: Polyethylene gas pipe is used underground only and is never run inside a building as interior gas piping.
Polyethylene pipe may rise through a floor and connect directly to an appliance indoors.
Polyethylene pipe is approved exposed inside a living room.
Polyethylene pipe is the standard material for interior manifolds.

questions.explanation: Plastic gas pipe is an underground material, with the transition to approved material made as the code requires.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes two opening combustion air method?

answers.text: One opening at the ceiling alone satisfies the two-opening method.
The two-opening method provides combustion air through two permanent openings, one high in the space and one low in the space.
Combustion air openings may be closed whenever the room feels drafty.
Two openings both placed at floor level satisfy the method.

questions.explanation: One opening near the top and one near the bottom let air circulate to the appliance as the method intends.

questions.question: Regarding master exam journeyman prerequisite, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: A high school diploma alone qualifies a person for the master exam.
Working for a supply house qualifies a person for the master exam.
Any apprentice may sit for the master exam without a journeyman license.
Eligibility for the master plumber exam requires holding a Massachusetts journeyman plumber license.

questions.explanation: Master eligibility builds on the journeyman license already earned.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts master plumber best explain tier five course requirement?

answers.text: No course work of any kind is required for the master exam.
The Board must personally warn each licensee many times before acting.
The Tier Five course is a one-hour online orientation.
Master exam eligibility includes completing the 110-hour Tier Five course, unless it was already finished during the apprenticeship.

questions.explanation: Tier Five is the final education tier and its 110 hours are part of master eligibility.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts master plumber best explain black steel gas piping?

answers.text: Black steel pipe is an approved material for fuel gas piping inside buildings.
Black steel pipe is banned from all fuel gas use.
Accessibility matters only for the meter valve and no others.
Gas pipe may share an elevator shaft if it is labeled.

questions.explanation: Black steel is a standard fuel gas piping material, joined mainly with threaded or welded joints.

questions.question: A journeyman asks the master, the topic of copper tubing for gas comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Copper tubing may be joined for gas with any solder found on the truck.
Copper tubing may be used for fuel gas where the gas and the code allow it, using approved joints for gas service.
Copper tubing is required for all underground gas piping.
Copper tubing is the only material ever allowed for gas piping.

questions.explanation: Copper has a limited, conditional place in gas work rather than a universal one.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how tracer wire for plastic piping is handled in practice.

answers.text: A tracer wire is needed only if the installer expects to dig the line up.
Underground plastic gas piping must be installed with a tracer wire so the line can be located later.
Painting the ground above plastic pipe replaces the tracer wire.
An elevator shaft is an approved vertical chase for gas piping.

questions.explanation: Because plastic cannot be found with a metal locator, the tracer wire provides the locating path.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts master plumber best explain purpose of plumbing venting?

answers.text: Plumbing venting protects trap seals so sewer gases stay out of occupied space.
Plumbing venting exists mainly to increase drainage speed.
Capillary action only happens in metal traps.
Island fixtures are vented by omitting the vent entirely.

questions.explanation: A vent system admits and releases air at the right points so the water seal in each trap is not pulled or pushed out of place.

questions.question: Which description of dwelling minimum fixture set matches the Massachusetts uniform state plumbing code?

answers.text: A bathtub or shower is optional in a dwelling if a lavatory is provided.
Fixtures should be set out of level so waste runs toward the room drain.
A dwelling may share a single toilet among separate dwelling units without limit.
Every dwelling needs at least one toilet, one lavatory, one kitchen-style sink, and one bathtub or shower.

questions.explanation: The Massachusetts uniform state plumbing code sets a basic sanitary minimum for every dwelling. That minimum covers toileting, hand washing, food preparation, and bathing.

questions.question: How would an experienced Massachusetts master plumber best explain isometric drawing purpose?

answers.text: An isometric drawing shows a three-dimensional piping run on two-dimensional paper so lengths, fittings, and elevations can be taken off.
In a 45-degree offset, set means the length of the offset fitting itself.
An isometric drawing is a decorative rendering that carries no measurable piping information.
A material list is built from the plan view alone because isometrics hide fittings.

questions.explanation: Part of the real exam is isometric analysis, built around reading a single drawing accurately. The isometric packs direction, length, fittings, and elevation into one view.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers corrugated stainless steel tubing. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Corrugated stainless steel tubing is an approved gas piping system when it is installed according to its listing and the manufacturer instructions.
Corrugated stainless steel tubing never needs any fittings from its own system.
A low-pressure system may be tested at one-half pound because that is its working pressure.
Corrugated stainless steel tubing is approved only for underground burial.

questions.explanation: CSST is a listed system, so its listing and instructions control how it is routed, supported, and terminated.

questions.question: Which description of drainage design against fouling matches the Massachusetts uniform state plumbing code?

answers.text: Sewage may use the storm system when the sanitary is busy.
Protection against fouling applies only to water supply piping.
Fouling inside drainage piping is a design goal.
The drainage system is designed and maintained to protect against fouling of its interior surfaces.

questions.explanation: The basic principles of the Massachusetts uniform state plumbing code treat a clean-running interior as a health and performance requirement, not an afterthought.

questions.question: Which description of potable protection core principle matches the Massachusetts uniform state plumbing code?

answers.text: Only non-potable piping needs backflow protection.
Potable water must be protected from contamination at every point where a hazard can reach it.
Contamination protection is optional once water enters a building.
Friction loss adds pressure as water travels farther.

questions.explanation: Backflow protection is the core of this portion because the distribution system is only as safe as its weakest connection.

questions.question: Which description of approved listed materials principle matches the Massachusetts uniform state plumbing code?

answers.text: Approval and listing apply only to fixtures, never to pipe or fittings.
The standard water test head for drainage is 100 feet.
A material listed only for drainage may be used for drinking water supply.
Plumbing materials must be approved and listed for the use they serve, with potable water materials kept distinct from drainage materials.

questions.explanation: Listing ties a material to the duty it was tested for, such as pressure, temperature, or waste. Using a material outside its listing defeats that protection.

questions.question: A building drain runs 22 feet at a pitch of 1/2 inch per foot. How many inches does it fall over the run?
questions.explanation: Fall = 1/2 x 22 = 11 inches.

questions.question: Using the standard method (50 cubic feet of room volume per 1,000 BTU per hour of appliance input), what minimum room volume is needed for appliances totaling 180,000 BTU per hour, in cubic feet?
questions.explanation: Volume = 180 x 50 = 9000 cubic feet.

questions.question: A piping material grows 0.04 inches per foot for the design temperature change. By how many inches does a run of 90 feet grow?
questions.explanation: Growth = 0.04 x 90 = 3.6 inches.

questions.question: Using the standard method (50 cubic feet of room volume per 1,000 BTU per hour of appliance input), what minimum room volume is needed for appliances totaling 160,000 BTU per hour, in cubic feet?
questions.explanation: Volume = 160 x 50 = 8000 cubic feet.

ase-a1-engine-repair.quiz_title: ASE A1 — Engine Repair Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: An engine is covered in old oil from the valve cover down to the oil pan. What should be done first to locate the actual source of the oil leak?

answers.text: Clean the engine thoroughly, run it, and then inspect for the highest fresh oil trail
Replace the oil pan gasket because oil always settles at the lowest gasket
Add two quarts of oil and watch which seal drips first while cranking
Replace the valve cover gasket without cleaning because it is the highest seal

questions.explanation: Oil migrates down and back from its source, so old residue hides the origin. Cleaning first, then running the engine, lets fresh oil reveal the highest point of leakage, which is the source to repair.

questions.question: A technician plans to use power balance results alone to authorize an engine teardown for a weak cylinder. What is missing from that plan?

answers.text: Nothing; a weak drop is sufficient proof for teardown
A second power balance test is the only missing step
Power balance only localizes the weak cylinder; compression and leak-down (or equivalent) are required to establish a mechanical cause before teardown
Teardown is justified if the drop is the smallest by any amount

questions.explanation: Authorizing internal repairs requires evidence of an internal fault. The balance test cannot distinguish a dead injector or plug from a burnt valve, so confirmatory mechanical tests must precede any teardown decision.

questions.question: A valve stem tip shows uneven wear and mushrooming. Which related parts must also be inspected?

answers.text: The rocker arm contact surface, retainer, and locks that bear on or locate at the tip
Only the valve spring
Only the valve guide
Only the head gasket surface

questions.explanation: Tip damage comes from the parts that contact it and hold it: the rocker or follower contact, retainer, and locks. A new valve installed against a worn rocker or damaged locks will wear the same way. Spring, guide, and deck checks are separate inspections.

questions.question: A flat (non-roller) lifter face shows a concave wear pattern and edge chipping. What does the concave face tell about its operation?

answers.text: The lifter was rotating correctly
The lifter face should be concave when new
The lifter was not rotating in its bore, wearing in one orientation against the lobe
The lifter is a roller type

questions.explanation: Flat lifter faces are slightly crowned when new and the lobe taper spins the lifter to distribute wear. A concave, chipped face shows rotation stopped, so one area took all the sliding wear. That lifter and its lobe are condemned and lifter bore freedom is checked.

questions.question: A PCV valve is removed and shaken. It rattles freely. What does the rattle test by itself establish, and what does it not establish?

answers.text: It establishes the pintle is not stuck solid; it does not establish correct flow rate or sealing, so a flow/vacuum check is still needed
It proves the valve is fully good and needs no further testing
It proves the valve is bad because good valves are silent
It measures crankcase pressure in the crankcase

questions.explanation: A free rattle only shows the internal pintle moves. A valve can rattle yet flow the wrong amount or leak, which is why inspection continues with a vacuum/flow check rather than ending at the shake test.

questions.question: An engine starts hard when hot but cranks and starts normally cold. During the hot fault, cranking speed is normal, spark is present, and fuel pressure is below the specification stated in the procedure. What is the best-supported cause category?

answers.text: A heat-related fuel subsystem fault (such as vapor formation or a heat-sensitive pump) rather than a mechanical compression fault
Piston rings that expand and lose seal only when hot in a way that also lowers fuel pressure
A timing belt that slips only when hot
Valve guides causing the low fuel pressure

questions.explanation: The measured fault during the symptom is low fuel pressure, and it is temperature dependent — that places the cause in the fuel subsystem. Rings and guides in B and D cannot lower fuel pressure, which is the documented abnormal reading.

questions.question: A vacuum needle is steady and normal at idle, but as rpm rises past about 2,500 the needle begins to vibrate rapidly and the engine develops a misfire only in that rpm range. Which valve-train fault fits an rpm-dependent needle breakdown?

answers.text: A weak or broken valve spring allowing valve float at higher rpm
Retarded ignition timing, which is rpm-independent in effect
A restricted exhaust, which improves at higher rpm
An intake leak that seals only at high rpm

questions.explanation: Valve float from a weak spring appears when rpm exceeds the spring's control ability, disturbing both the needle and combustion only in that range. Idle behavior stays normal because the spring still controls the valve at low speed.

questions.question: A four-cylinder engine reads 182, 90, 180, and 184 psi. Cylinder 2's spark plug is oil-fouled and that cylinder smokes on acceleration. Wet compression in cylinder 2 rises to 170 psi. What repair direction do these results support?

answers.text: Replace the exhaust valve in cylinder 2
Replace the head gasket between cylinders 2 and 3
Cylinder 2 ring and bore service, because oil fouling, smoke, and a large wet-test recovery all point to oil passing the rings
No repair; a single low cylinder is acceptable if the others are high

questions.explanation: Dry 90 psi versus about 182 psi elsewhere is a major loss. The wet rise to 170 psi shows oil sealing the ring gap is the variable, and oil fouling plus smoke under load are consistent with oil control loss at the rings and bore in that cylinder.

questions.question: Freeze-frame and mode data show a misfire code for cylinder 6 set at idle only. Swapping coils between cylinders 6 and 3 does not move the misfire. Relative compression shows cylinder 6 low. What is the strongest conclusion?

answers.text: The coil from cylinder 3 is also faulty
The misfire is caused by the fuel trim on the opposite bank
The fault follows the cylinder, not the coil, and the low relative compression identifies it as mechanical sealing loss in cylinder 6, to be confirmed with gauge and leak-down tests
The scan tool code must be cleared and ignored because coils were swapped

questions.explanation: Component swapping separates part faults from cylinder faults: the misfire stayed at cylinder 6. The scope's relative compression then supplies the mechanical evidence. Together they justify gauge compression and leak-down testing on cylinder 6 rather than more parts swapping.

questions.question: Carbon and varnish build up inside a guide and the valve begins to stick intermittently when hot. Clearance was correct at assembly. What is the best first service action?

answers.text: Replace the cylinder head
Install a stronger spring to force the valve closed
Grind the valve face deeper
Clean the guide bore and stem with the correct guide cleaner/reamer without oversizing, and verify free movement

questions.explanation: Deposits can close up correct clearance and cause hot sticking. Cleaning the bore to its original size and verifying the stem moves freely addresses the cause. A stronger spring masks sticking and adds load, and head replacement is not the first step for a deposit problem.

questions.question: A crank/no-start engine has 60 psi fuel pressure (specification 55-62 psi), good spark and even compression, but a noid light shows no injector pulse. What subsystem should be diagnosed next as the cause?

answers.text: The injector control circuit / engine control output for the injectors
The piston rings
The exhaust system
The fuel pump

questions.explanation: Delivery pressure, spark and compression are all proven, so the missing link is injector actuation shown by the noid light. The pump is already proven by pressure, and rings/exhaust faults do not stop injector pulse.

questions.question: A belt squeal begins a week after a coolant hose leak was repaired, and the belt and pulleys are found glazed with dried coolant residue. The alternator and pump bearings test smooth. The correct repair sequence is to:

answers.text: Install a new belt without cleaning the pulleys, since residue wears off
Sand the belt surface to restore its grip and reuse it
Replace the alternator because its pulley is the most glazed
Clean the residue from all pulleys, confirm the coolant leak is fully repaired, and install a new belt

questions.explanation: Coolant residue makes a belt slip and squeal and ruins its friction surface. Cleaning the pulleys, verifying the original leak is fixed so the new belt is not contaminated again, and fitting a new belt corrects the noise at its cause.

questions.question: Spring pressure at installed height tests low on several springs from the same head. What is the most likely effect at high engine speed?

answers.text: Valve sealing improves at high speed
Oil consumption decreases
Deck warpage increases
Valve float, where the valve does not follow the cam lobe and loses control

questions.explanation: Spring pressure holds the valve train in contact with the cam. Low pressure lets inertia carry the valve off the lobe at speed, causing float, power loss, and possible valve-to-piston contact. It does not improve sealing or affect the deck.

questions.question: A slapping noise is loudest at the front timing cover at idle. With the cover removed, the inside of the cover is scored and pieces of plastic guide material are found in the oil pan pickup area. What is the most likely cause?

answers.text: Excessive valve lash at the top of the head
A failed timing chain guide allowing the chain to slap the cover
A worn valve guide in the rearmost cylinder
Normal chain operation that requires no repair

questions.explanation: The evidence localizes the fault: scoring inside the timing cover plus broken plastic guide fragments means the chain is no longer controlled on its slack side and is striking the cover. The guide (and the chain set and tensioner, inspected together) must be replaced and the pickup cleaned. Valve lash noise comes from the valve train at the top of the engine and leaves no guide debris or cover scoring.

questions.question: Technician A says all external sensors, brackets and wiring that will transfer to a replacement engine should be moved and inspected on the stand. Technician B says transferred parts should be installed after the engine is in the vehicle to save time. Who is correct?

answers.text: Technician B only
Both Technician A and Technician B
Neither Technician A nor Technician B
Technician A only

questions.explanation: Transferring and inspecting parts on the stand is easier, safer and catches damaged connectors before installation. Doing it in the vehicle (Technician B) makes access worse and delays finding defects.

questions.question: Technician A says cylinder wall glazing should be broken with a proper hone to restore a crosshatch for ring seating. Technician B says a mirror-smooth bore is ideal for new rings. Who is correct?

answers.text: Both Technician A and Technician B
Neither Technician A nor Technician B
Technician B only
Technician A only

questions.explanation: New rings need a crosshatch pattern to seat and to retain oil; a glazed mirror finish prevents seating and causes oil consumption. Technician B's mirror finish is exactly the condition honing corrects.

questions.question: What does a polished, mirror band in the center of a rod journal combined with an hourglass wear pattern most likely indicate?

answers.text: Normal oil film appearance that needs no measurement
A correctly finished journal ready for standard bearings
Evidence that the journal was ground oversize at the factory
Journal wear / distortion that must be measured for taper and out-of-round before reuse

questions.explanation: Appearance is a prompt to measure, not a verdict. Uneven polish patterns suggest the journal is no longer cylindrical; only micrometer readings in multiple positions confirm whether it is within limits.

questions.question: On a turbocharged gasoline engine in A1 scope, oil is found in the intercooler piping, consumption is high, and crankcase pressure is normal with a healthy PCV system. Shaft play at the turbocharger compressor is excessive per the stem limit. What is the indicated oil path?

answers.text: Oil drawn past the valve guides into the intercooler
Oil leaking past the turbocharger shaft seals into the intake tract
Oil entering through the PCV system despite normal pressure and function
Coolant leaking into the intake through the intercooler

questions.explanation: With ventilation ruled out by normal pressure and PCV function, oil pooled in the charge piping plus excessive shaft play points to the turbocharger's shaft seals. Location of the oil, upstream in the intake tract, is the localizing evidence.

questions.question: During leak-down of cylinder 3, no air is heard at the intake, exhaust, or oil fill, leakage reads 35%, and the radiator is not bubbling, but a hiss is heard near the spark plug tube and the plug is found finger-loose with a damaged seat washer. What is the correct action?

answers.text: Condemn the head gasket
Replace the piston rings in cylinder 3
Machine the valve seats in cylinder 3
Correct the external leak at the plug (proper plug and washer, correctly seated and torqued per service information) and repeat the test before diagnosing internal leakage

questions.explanation: Not all air loss is internal. A loose plug with a damaged sealing washer vents test air to the atmosphere at the plug tube, producing percentage loss with no internal escape sounds. Fix the test setup fault and retest; only then judge the cylinder.

questions.question: Low hot oil pressure began right after an oil service. The invoice shows the engine, which the manufacturer specifies as 5W-30, was filled with 0W-16 oil. Cold pressure is normal, but hot pressure falls below the given minimums at both idle and 2,500 rpm, and the complaint disappears when the correct oil is installed for a verification test. What caused the low pressure?

answers.text: Oil of too low a viscosity for the application, which thins further when hot and leaks past bearing clearances too easily to hold pressure
A relief valve that the oil service jammed closed
A sending unit damaged by the drain plug being removed
A pickup screen that clogged during the oil change

questions.explanation: The pattern fits thin oil, not a mechanical failure: cold, thicker oil holds normal pressure, hot oil falls below both given minimums, and restoring the specified 5W-30 restores pressure — a controlled A/B result. A jammed-closed relief valve, the strongest distractor, raises pressure rather than lowering it, and neither the sender nor the pickup was disturbed in a way that would track the oil grade so exactly.

ase-a2-automatic-transmission.quiz_title: ASE A2 — Automatic Transmission/Transaxle Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which feature most reliably distinguishes a stepped planetary automatic from a CVT during a road test?

answers.text: The vehicle moves when Drive is selected
Distinct, repeatable ratio steps and shift events
The unit contains automatic transmission fluid
The shift lever has a Drive position

questions.explanation: Stepped automatics change between fixed ratios with perceptible shifts; CVTs vary ratio continuously. Having a Drive position is shared by both, so it cannot distinguish them.

questions.question: Which enabling condition is commonly required before many transmission monitors will run?

answers.text: Fluid temperature, speed, and throttle within specified windows with no inhibiting faults present
The fuel tank completely empty
The parking brake applied at highway speed
The scan tool disconnected for the entire drive

questions.explanation: Monitors run only when temperature, speed, load, and related inputs are inside calibrated windows and no blocking faults exist. The strongest distractor D is wrong because the scan tool connection does not prevent monitors from running.

questions.question: Which test sequence best distinguishes a stator fault from an engine performance fault when launch is sluggish?

answers.text: Replace the stator before any engine checks
Measure line pressure in Park only
Verify engine power first (vacuum, exhaust restriction, fuel), then perform a stall test — low stall with a proven engine points to the stator clutch
Road test only at highway speed

questions.explanation: Both a weak engine and a freewheeling stator cause sluggish launch and low stall, so engine health must be proven before the converter can be condemned. Replacing the stator first risks installing a good part on an engine-caused complaint.

questions.question: Why do road test procedures often specify monitoring transmission fluid temperature during the test?

answers.text: Many strategies — lockup enable, shift scheduling, and pressure adaptation — are temperature-dependent, and overheating itself is diagnostic information
Temperature data is recorded for warranty paperwork only
Fluid temperature only matters for dipstick reading
Cold fluid shifts better in all cases

questions.explanation: Temperature gates real control decisions and reveals cooling faults, so it belongs in the data set. 'Paperwork only' is the strongest distractor — the module itself uses this input to decide lockup and scheduling.

questions.question: CAN high and CAN low are accidentally swapped at a repaired connector for one module. The expected result is:

answers.text: Only that module's power is affected
Faster communication
That module cannot communicate correctly and may disrupt bus messages
No effect because the lines are interchangeable

questions.explanation: CAN signaling depends on the correct differential polarity at each transceiver, so swapped lines corrupt that module's messaging. Interchangeable lines are wrong because high and low carry opposite signal swings.

questions.question: During a stall-related concern verification, which observation is a safety/repair red flag requiring stopping the test?

answers.text: The engine reaching normal operating temperature
Burning smell, smoke, or rapidly rising temperature/noise during testing
The parking brake holding
Scan tool connecting normally

questions.explanation: Smoke, burning, or escalating noise/temp indicate active damage and the test should stop. Normal warm-up is expected and not a stop condition.

questions.question: A wiring diagram test shows continuity from the controller to a solenoid, but a loaded voltage-drop test drops 2.5 volts on the feed wire. Why did continuity alone miss the fault?

answers.text: Continuity testing uses high current that repairs the wire
Voltage drop cannot be measured on a feed wire
A few remaining strands can pass continuity but cannot carry operating current without a large drop
The solenoid must be defective if voltage drop is high

questions.explanation: A beep test passes through even one or two strands, but those strands act as a resistor under load, causing the 2.5 volt drop. The strongest distractor D is wrong because the drop was measured in the wire itself, locating the resistance there, not in the solenoid.

questions.question: Exposure to coolant-contaminated fluid has swollen and softened multiple internal seals and the friction material is delaminating. Why is a fluid change alone insufficient here?

answers.text: Coolant in fluid evaporates completely at operating temperature with no residue
Only the radiator needs service and the transmission will recover
The contamination affects only the pan gasket
Glycol contamination attacks seals and friction bonding throughout the unit, so contaminated soft parts must be replaced during overhaul

questions.explanation: Coolant/glycol degrades elastomers and friction adhesives everywhere the fluid circulated, not just in the pan. 'It evaporates away' is wrong because the chemical damage to seals and lining remains after any water portion boils off.

questions.question: A pressure gauge on the forward clutch tap reads 0 psi in Drive while main line pressure reads normal at the main tap. What has this two-tap comparison proven?

answers.text: The gauge on the main tap is inaccurate
The pump is worn out
The fault is between the main line and the forward clutch tap — valve, seal, or passage — not in the pump supply
The torque converter is slipping

questions.explanation: Normal supply pressure with zero element pressure localizes the loss to the circuit between the taps. A worn pump is the strongest distractor, but a worn pump could not produce normal pressure at the main tap.

questions.question: What distinguishes the pressure accumulator's role from the shift-feel accumulators found in a conventional valve body?

answers.text: Pressure accumulators work only in Reverse
Shift accumulators store energy for restarts
The pressure accumulator stores energy for system pressure support during engine-off events; shift accumulators only cushion a single element's apply
There is no difference in role or size

questions.explanation: One stores system energy for engine-off support; the others meter apply feel for individual elements. 'No difference' is the strongest distractor, but their purpose, size, and test procedures are entirely different.

questions.question: How do the engine control and transmission control functions interact in an integrated powertrain control architecture?

answers.text: The engine module moves the shift valves directly
They share sensor data and coordinate actions — for example the engine reduces torque briefly during a shift the transmission is executing
They operate in total isolation with no shared data
The transmission module controls fuel injection

questions.explanation: Integrated control means shared inputs and coordinated torque management during shifts. 'Total isolation' is the strongest distractor — shared throttle, speed, and temperature data are the foundation of the architecture.

questions.question: A transmission is supported on a jack but still will not separate from the engine after all bellhousing bolts are removed. What should the technician check next?

answers.text: A missed dowel-pin bind, a forgotten converter bolt, or a harness or cooler line still attached
That the pan bolts were torqued in sequence
That the output shaft speed sensor has been relearned
That the torque converter has been drained completely

questions.explanation: Separation resistance almost always means something still connects the units or the dowels are cocked. Draining the converter does not hold the case to the engine, so that choice misses the mechanical cause.

questions.question: A technician finds two procedures: a generic video and the OEM service information for the exact unit. For torque values and fluid type, priority goes to:

answers.text: The generic video
Social media comments
The OEM service information for that exact unit
The oldest forum post

questions.explanation: OEM data is unit-specific and authoritative for specs. A generic video may cover a different variant, making it risky for specs.

questions.question: Stall speed is 600 rpm above specification and the vehicle launches weakly, but highway cruise is normal once moving. What is most likely?

answers.text: A stuck closed thermostat
A slipping forward element or low apply pressure at launch
A locked torque converter clutch at launch
Correct stall for a performance converter in all cases

questions.explanation: High stall means the engine revs against an element that is not holding — a slipping forward clutch or low apply pressure — while cruise can feel normal once another element carries load. The strongest distractor C is wrong because a locked converter clutch at launch would stall or kill the engine, not raise stall speed.

questions.question: An engine stalls every time the vehicle comes to a stop in Drive, but restarts easily and idles fine in Park/Neutral. The most likely converter-related cause is:

answers.text: The stator clutch freewheels both ways
The converter is low on balance weights
The converter clutch is stuck applied, mechanically tying the engine to the wheels as they stop
The impeller has lost its fins

questions.explanation: A stuck-applied TCC makes the drivetrain act like a manual transmission with the clutch never released — the engine is dragged to a stall at stops. A freewheeling stator affects launch torque, not stopping behavior, and would never stall the engine.

questions.question: A scan tool shows the module reducing EPC current (commanding higher pressure) as throttle increases from 20% to 80%, and a gauge confirms pressure rising smoothly. A harsh-shift complaint exists only at light throttle. What does this data do to the diagnosis?

answers.text: It shows pressure control is irrelevant
It proves the pump is worn
It clears the EPC command/response for load-based pressure rise, steering diagnosis toward light-throttle-specific items such as accumulator condition or base idle pressure calibration
It proves the EPC solenoid must be replaced

questions.explanation: A system proven across the load range is unlikely to be the light-throttle-only culprit. Replacing the EPC anyway is the strongest distractor — it ignores data that just exonerated that part.

questions.question: What does a 5-volt reference that measures only 2.5 volts at multiple sensors most likely indicate?

answers.text: Normal operation, because references vary from 2 to 12 volts by sensor
Low transmission fluid, which loads the reference circuit
A shorted sensor or wiring fault dragging the shared reference down, or a failing module reference supply
One burned-out dashboard bulb sharing the reference

questions.explanation: A shared reference low at many points means a common cause: something on that line pulling it down or the supply itself failing. Testing sensors one by one by disconnecting them finds which one restores the reference.

questions.question: A calculation: a service drain removes 4.0 quarts and the service fill spec is 4.5 quarts including a new cooler line allowance of 0.5 quart. If the cooler was NOT replaced, the initial fill before level check should be based on:

answers.text: 4.5 quarts regardless
4.0 quarts, then adjust by the level procedure
9.0 quarts
2.0 quarts

questions.explanation: Subtract the 0.5-quart cooler allowance when the cooler was not serviced: 4.5 - 0.5 = 4.0 quarts, then verify by level procedure. Using 4.5 blindly overfills initially.

questions.question: A customer complaint of harsh 1–2 shift is paired with line pressure 30 psi above specification at light throttle only; pressure is normal at idle and at heavy throttle. The most focused suspect is:

answers.text: The load-signal/boost control in the light-throttle region — e.g., modulator, TV, or EPC control at that operating point
A worn pump producing low pressure
A slipping direct clutch
A restricted cooler

questions.explanation: Pressure error confined to one load region points to the signal device operating in that region, not base pump output, which the normal idle/heavy readings prove. A worn pump is wrong because its fault would lower, not raise, pressure.

questions.question: Customer complaint: fuel economy dropped and highway rpm is about 300 rpm higher than it used to be at 65 mph, with no other symptoms.
