TCC duty reads 0% at cruise and coolant temperature reads normal, but transmission fluid temperature reads 90°F after an hour of driving. What is the likely chain of cause?

answers.text: The engine lost power
The speedometer is miscalibrated
The converter lining suddenly wore out with no other symptom
The fluid temperature sensor reads falsely low, so the module inhibits lockup as if the fluid were cold — costing the ~300 rpm of converter slip and the fuel economy

questions.explanation: An hour of driving cannot leave fluid at 90°F, so the sensor lies, the module obeys cold-fluid inhibit logic, and the unlocked converter explains both rpm and economy. Sudden lining wear is the strongest distractor, but duty at 0% proves the clutch was never even commanded.

ase-a3-manual-drive-train-and-axles.quiz_title: ASE A3 — Manual Drive Train and Axles Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A pedal pivot shaft shows a worn groove where the bushing rides, and new bushings alone still leave side play. What is the correct repair?

answers.text: Pack the pivot with grease to fill the groove
Tighten the pivot nut until side play disappears
Replace the worn pivot shaft (and bushings as needed) so the pedal tracks straight
Bend the pedal arm to center it

questions.explanation: A grooved shaft is undersized at the contact area, so new bushings cannot restore a straight, play-free pivot; the shaft must be replaced. Grease or overtightening cannot rebuild worn metal and bending the arm does not fix pivot clearance.

questions.question: A rod linkage transmission has a bent shift rod discovered after underbody impact. The driver reports 3rd gear cannot be fully engaged. The best repair is to:

answers.text: Straighten the rod by eye and skip adjustment
Replace or properly repair the rod and perform the full linkage adjustment procedure
Lengthen the clutch cable to compensate
Grind the shift gate to allow more travel

questions.explanation: A bent rod changes linkage geometry, so it must be repaired or replaced and the linkage fully readjusted to restore full engagement. Straightening by eye without adjustment leaves geometry unverified and risks continued incomplete engagement.

questions.question: A synchronizer hub has a visible crack running from a keyway corner toward the outer splines. The sleeve slides smoothly. What is the correct action?

answers.text: Reuse the hub, because the sleeve slides smoothly
Replace the hub, because a cracked hub can fail and lose synchronizer function
Weld the crack and return the hub to service
Reuse the hub if the blocking rings measure in specification

questions.explanation: A crack at the keyway is a stress-riser failure that can progress until the hub breaks apart. Reuse based on smooth sleeve travel is wrong because sliding feel does not restore the hub's structural strength.

questions.question: A shift fork's pads are correct thickness but the fork is loose on its rail because its roll pin hole is elongated. What is the effect?

answers.text: Increased synchronizer speed
A change in gear tooth count
Lost motion between rail and fork causing delayed/incomplete sleeve movement
Case pressurization

questions.explanation: An elongated pin hole decouples rail movement from fork movement, losing sleeve travel. It cannot change tooth count or pressurize the case.

questions.question: A half-shaft vibration appears after an engine replacement. The powertrain sits visibly tilted and one mount bracket is bent. The best first repair is to:

answers.text: Replace both half-shafts
Restore correct powertrain position by repairing the bracket and mounts
Add a thicker shaft damper
Change transaxle gear oil viscosity

questions.explanation: A tilted powertrain changes half-shaft angles, so restoring its position addresses the root cause. New shafts installed at the same wrong angles would still vibrate, so that distractor fails.

questions.question: All of the following are reasons to flush clutch hydraulic fluid EXCEPT:

answers.text: The fluid is dark and contaminated with debris
Moisture content is above the limit given in the service information
The pedal pad rubber shows normal wear from use
Rubber particles from a deteriorating seal are suspended in the fluid

questions.explanation: Dark contaminated fluid, excess moisture, and seal debris all compromise the hydraulics and justify flushing. Pedal pad wear is a cosmetic pedal part condition with no connection to fluid condition.

questions.question: A dual-mass flywheel can be rocked by hand and shows excessive free play with a clunk well beyond the manufacturer's rotational free-play limit, and grease is leaking from its damper area. What is the correct action?

answers.text: Pack the damper with chassis grease and reuse it
Replace the dual-mass flywheel as an assembly
Weld the two masses together to stop the play
Tighten the flywheel bolts an extra quarter turn to reduce play

questions.explanation: Excessive rotational free play plus grease loss indicates internal damper failure, and dual-mass units are serviced as a complete assembly. Adding grease cannot restore worn springs or stops, which is why regreasing and reuse is wrong.

questions.question: A shift shaft seal leaks only when that shaft is moved during shifts, and the shaft shows side play in its bore. Replacing the seal alone will likely fail because:

answers.text: Seals cannot seal moving shafts under any condition
The worn bore/bushing lets the shaft move eccentrically and work the lip open; the support wear must also be repaired
The fluid level is at the specified height
The shaft moves too fast for any seal

questions.explanation: Excess shaft play from a worn bore lets the shaft orbit and lift the lip, so the support wear must be fixed with the seal. Seals are specifically designed to seal moving shafts when the shaft runs true, so that distractor is false.

questions.question: A shift cable bracket on the transaxle is loose by one bolt. What symptom is most likely?

answers.text: Lost motion at the lever, vague gates and possible incomplete engagement
A gear whine in 5th only
Low fluid level
Clutch chatter

questions.explanation: A loose bracket lets the cable housing move instead of the inner cable, creating lost motion and vague/incomplete shifts. It cannot create a 5th-only whine.

questions.question: After transaxle replacement the vehicle pulls and the steering wheel is off-center. The subframe was removed and reinstalled without regard to its prior position. What likely happened?

answers.text: Subframe shift changed suspension/steering geometry; alignment must be checked and corrected
The synchronizers were installed backwards
The clutch is dragging
The final drive ratio changed

questions.explanation: Subframe position locates suspension pickup points, so shifting it alters alignment and steering center. Internal gear parts do not affect steering wheel center.

questions.question: A carrier has a visible crack through a side bearing journal area and distortion that prevents a new bearing from seating squarely. Gears themselves are serviceable and can be transferred. What should be done?

answers.text: Reuse the carrier because the bearing press fit will hold the crack closed
Weld the crack and machine the journal without further inspection
Replace the cracked, distorted carrier and transfer or replace the internal gears as inspected
Install oversize shims to compensate for the distortion

questions.explanation: A cracked, distorted carrier cannot support bearings squarely and must be replaced; serviceable internals may be transferred after inspection. Press-fit reuse (strongest distractor) lets the crack grow under load until the carrier fails.

questions.question: On a part-time 4WD truck, fluid is found only at the front output seal, and only after trips where 4WD was used. The seal is dry after weeks of 2WD driving. Why does the pattern fit that seal?

answers.text: The front seal leaks only when the fluid is cold
The front output only turns under drive when 4WD is engaged, so a marginal seal leaks mainly then
The rear seal leak runs forward along the case
The vent only opens in 2WD

questions.explanation: On a part-time system the front output is driven in 4WD and idle in 2WD, so a marginal front seal can stay dry for weeks and weep only after 4WD use. A rear leak running forward is the strongest distractor, but gravity and airflow carry leaks rearward, and the rear area is dry.

questions.question: Grease is found slung from the release bearing area onto the inside of the bell housing, and the disc shows early slip. What is the most likely source and fault?

answers.text: Normal bearing lubrication level
Hydraulic fluid from the reservoir
Engine oil from the intake manifold
An over-lubricated or failed release bearing seal throwing grease that can reach the disc facings

questions.explanation: Grease thrown from the bearing area that reaches the facings lowers friction and causes slip, indicating a failed bearing seal or overlubrication at assembly. Hydraulic fluid is thin and would show as a wet leak with a falling reservoir level, not slung grease.

questions.question: During shift cover installation, a detent spring is found slightly shorter than the others and its rail has the weakest in-gear feel. The springs are specified as identical. The technician should:

answers.text: Stretch the short spring back to length and reuse it
Swap it to the reverse rail where feel matters less
Replace the weak/short spring with a new specified spring and verify detent feel
Add a second spring on top of it

questions.explanation: A shortened, weak spring has lost tension and must be replaced with the specified part to restore detent force. Stretching a fatigued spring does not restore its rate or durability, so it will weaken again quickly.

questions.question: A cluster gear is heated excessively with a torch during a previous repair and shows blue discoloration on several teeth, though no teeth are broken. What should the technician do?

answers.text: Reuse the gear, because discoloration is only cosmetic
Quench the gear in oil to restore its original hardness
Grind the discoloration off and reuse the gear
Replace the gear, because the heat has altered the tooth hardness and fatigue strength

questions.explanation: Blueing indicates temperatures that temper the hardened tooth surface, leaving it soft and prone to rapid wear. Grinding the color off is wrong because it removes more material without restoring hardness through the tooth.

questions.question: A bearing retainer bolt hole in the case is stripped. The technician proposes using a longer bolt that reaches deeper threads of questionable engagement. The better repair is:

answers.text: Any longer bolt is acceptable
Leave that bolt out; others will hold
A specified thread repair (e.g. thread insert) or case repair restoring full clamping, verified by torque
Use sealant as thread

questions.explanation: Retainer clamping must be reliable; a proper thread insert restores it, while partial-engagement bolts or omitting a bolt risk bearing movement.

questions.question: Technician A says low axle lubricant can cause overheating and accelerated wear of gears and bearings. Technician B says overfilling an axle well above the fill plug can cause foaming, overheating, and seal leakage. Who is correct?

answers.text: Technician A only
Technician B only
Both Technician A and Technician B
Neither Technician A nor Technician B

questions.explanation: Both are correct: too little oil starves and overheats parts, while gross overfill churns and foams the oil and raises pressure at seals. Treating only one level error as harmful, as the single-technician options do, is incomplete.

questions.question: Technician A says a disc should be slid onto the input shaft splines during inspection to check for binding or excessive play. Technician B says spline condition cannot affect clutch release because the disc is clamped when driving. Who is correct?

answers.text: Technician B only
Both Technician A and Technician B
Neither Technician A nor Technician B
Technician A only

questions.explanation: Technician A is correct because the disc must slide freely to separate and can rock if splines are worn, both found by a trial fit on the shaft. Technician B is wrong because release depends on that sliding movement even though drive depends on clamping.

questions.question: Before pressing the mainshaft assembly apart, the technician records the order and direction of every gear, hub, washer, and spacer. At reassembly, a hub installed facing the wrong way would most likely show up as:

answers.text: A bench shift check failure or incorrect sleeve travel for that hub's two gears
Correct operation because hub direction never matters
A speedometer error only
Low fluid level after filling

questions.explanation: A reversed hub alters sleeve travel and strut function, which a bench shift check reveals as failed or abnormal engagement for its gears. Recording direction exists precisely because hub orientation does matter, contradicting the no-effect option.

questions.question: Technician A says synchronizer springs must be installed in their specified direction/position (e.g. tangs/ends as shown) to load the keys evenly. Technician B says mixing up hub orientation can put the key/spring geometry wrong even if parts fit. Who is correct?

answers.text: A only
B only
Neither
Both A and B

questions.explanation: Spring placement and hub orientation determine how keys are loaded; both affect function even when parts physically fit — both correct.

ase-a4-suspension-and-steering.quiz_title: ASE A4 — Suspension and Steering Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A recirculating-ball gear leaks fluid into the dust cap at the end of the sector shaft housing and the cap is swollen with fluid. This indicates:

answers.text: The sector shaft seal has failed and is leaking into the cap area; the seal requires renewal
The cap is supposed to hold a reserve of fluid
The gear is overfilled from the reservoir
The pitman arm nut is loose

questions.explanation: The dust cap is only a protective cover; finding it full of fluid means the sector shaft seal behind it has failed and is passing fluid into the cap. The cap holds no reserve by design, reservoir level does not pressurize the cap, and nut tightness does not seal the shaft.

questions.question: After overhauling a recirculating-ball gear, the technician adjusts worm preload with the sector shaft removed. Why is this sequence required?

answers.text: The sector shaft blocks access to the fluid passages during preload checks
Worm preload can only be measured at full lock with the sector removed
With the sector removed, the torque reading is worm bearing preload alone, without sector mesh drag added
Removing the sector prevents air from entering the gear during adjustment

questions.explanation: Accurate worm preload requires isolating the worm bearings. Any sector engagement adds mesh drag and would cause the worm bearings to be set too loose. The sector is installed and its lash set afterward.

questions.question: A tie rod end with a grease fitting has been over-greased until its boot ballooned and split at the seam. The joint itself is tight. What service is needed and why?

answers.text: Replace the boot (or the end if the boot is not serviced separately); a split boot will admit contamination and ruin a currently good joint
No service; a tight joint needs no boot
Remove grease through the fitting until the boot returns to shape
Seal the split with adhesive and continue greasing on schedule

questions.explanation: The boot is the joint's only contamination defense. Once split — even by over-greasing a good joint — water and grit will destroy it. Boot service now preserves the joint; technique correction (grease only until the boot firms) prevents recurrence.

questions.question: A technician is fitting a coil-spring compressor before removing a strut-type front spring. Where should the compressor hooks be positioned?

answers.text: Both hooks on the same side so the spring tilts toward the technician
Only on the top two coils, leaving the lower coils unengaged
On the insulator and the mount rather than on the coils themselves
On opposite sides of the spring, engaging coils as evenly as possible so the spring compresses straight

questions.explanation: Hooks placed opposite each other load the spring evenly so it compresses straight and stays captive. One-sided or partial engagement lets the spring bow and slip, which is both unsafe and likely to damage the spring finish.

questions.question: Technician A says wander can be caused by loose steering linkage. Technician B says wander can be caused by insufficient positive caster. Who is correct?

answers.text: Both Technician A and Technician B
Technician A only
Technician B only
Neither technician

questions.explanation: Both are established wander causes: looseness lets wheels steer without input, and insufficient positive caster reduces the self-centering force that keeps the vehicle tracking straight.

questions.question: While performing an EPS torque sensor calibration, the procedure requires the steering wheel to be untouched and the vehicle on a level surface with wheels straight. The reason the wheel must be completely unloaded is that:

answers.text: The assist motor would overheat during the procedure
The steering angle sensor would be damaged
Any torque applied during the learn would be recorded as the zero point and bias assist afterward
The calibration drains the battery

questions.explanation: The learn records the sensor's current output as 'no driver torque'; a hand on the wheel or a slope loading the linkage writes that load into the zero reference, and the module then applies a constant unwanted assist afterward. The brief stationary learn does not overheat the motor, damage the angle sensor, or drain the battery.

questions.question: A vehicle's rack is retained by bolts that also pass through the subframe heat shield and a brace. On reassembly, what must be preserved about these stacked parts?

answers.text: The shield may be discarded to save weight
The brace goes wherever it fits last
The original stack order and orientation of shield and brace, with all parts in place before final torque
Stack order never affects a bolted joint

questions.explanation: Shields and braces in a bolted stack contribute to clamp distribution and heat protection, and reversing or omitting them changes the joint and can leave the rack under-clamped. The stack is reassembled exactly as it was removed.

questions.question: EPS assist feels notchy at low speed, like detents as the wheel turns. Motor position sensor data shows a repeating dropout at the same motor angle each revolution, while torque data is smooth. What component is implicated?

answers.text: The torque sensor, despite its smooth data
The rack teeth, which have a damaged section
The steering column bearing, which has flat spots
The motor position (resolver) sensor, whose repeated same-angle dropout disrupts motor commutation at that position

questions.explanation: Motor control needs continuous position feedback to commutate smoothly. A dropout repeating at the same motor angle each revolution points to that sensor's track, producing a torque disturbance at the same spot every turn — the notchy feel.

questions.question: Bonded rubber control arm bushings are being installed. Why must the pivot bolts be final-torqued with the vehicle at normal ride height rather than with the suspension hanging?

answers.text: Because torque wrenches only work at ride height
Because the bushings are larger at ride height
So the bolts can be reached more easily
So the rubber is not locked in a twisted position at ride height, which would shorten bushing life and can hold the suspension incorrectly

questions.explanation: Bonded bushings flex by twisting the rubber between the shells. Clamping them at full droop pre-twists the rubber at normal height, causing early tearing and possibly affecting ride position.

questions.question: A front wheel shows radial (side-to-side at the joint) ball joint movement of 0.028 inch measured at the joint with a dial indicator. The limit on the work order is 0.050 inch, and the boot is intact. What is the correct call?

answers.text: Replace the joint because any measurable movement is a failure
Replace both front joints as a precaution
The measurement method is invalid for radial play
The joint is within its stated radial limit, so it should not be condemned on this measurement; record the reading and continue the inspection

questions.explanation: 0.028 inch is less than the stated 0.050-inch maximum, so this measurement does not condemn the joint. Replacing in-limit parts on a number that passes would be guessing, not diagnosis.

questions.question: After a front hub assembly replacement, the wheel-speed sensor that is integral to the hub reads erratically at low speed on a scan tool road test. The harness connector is fully seated. What hub-related cause should be checked?

answers.text: The front alignment toe setting
The strut mount bearing tightness
The replacement hub's tone ring/sensor orientation and whether the correct hub (with the proper sensor configuration for that corner) was fitted
The stabilizer link torque

questions.explanation: Integral-sensor hubs must match the vehicle's sensor configuration and be oriented correctly; a wrong or mis-oriented hub gives erratic low-speed readings with a good connection. Alignment and mount torque do not generate wheel-speed signals.

questions.question: Tires rotated for the first time at 40,000 miles reveal the two that were on the front are worn evenly but 3/32 inch lower than the rears, with no abnormal patterns anywhere. The best action is:

answers.text: Replace all four tires immediately because depths differ
Complete the rotation, record the depths, and set a shorter rotation interval going forward
Adjust front camber to slow the even front wear
Add 5 psi to the front tires to equalize wear rates

questions.explanation: Even wear with a depth difference is the normal front-versus-rear wear-rate gap that rotation manages; there is no fault pattern to correct and no reason to replace tires with serviceable, evenly worn tread. The fix is procedural — rotate on a shorter interval and document depths.

questions.question: Steering effort on a rack and pinion vehicle is normal, but there is a rhythmic pulsing felt in the wheel during turns that matches engine speed and a matching pressure gauge fluctuation at the rack inlet. The pulsation is most likely generated by:

answers.text: Worn rack teeth at equal intervals
A bent rack bar
Worn inner tie rod sockets
The power steering pump (a damaged vane or flow control fault) sending pressure pulses that the rack is transmitting, not originating in the rack

questions.explanation: A pulse locked to engine speed with a matching inlet pressure fluctuation is arriving at the rack from the pump; the rack is transmitting, not creating, it. Rack teeth, bar straightness and tie rod sockets produce symptoms tied to steering position or road inputs, not to engine rpm.

questions.question: Two technicians discuss a pump that leaks at the pressure fitting. Technician A says a leaking threaded fitting may only need the correct new O-ring and proper torque. Technician B says any pump with a fitting leak must be replaced as an assembly. Who is correct?

answers.text: Technician A only
Technician B only
Both technicians
Neither technician

questions.explanation: Many pressure fittings seal with a replaceable O-ring, and renewing it and torquing correctly repairs the leak without pump replacement. Technician B's blanket replacement ignores the serviceable seal, so only Technician A is correct.

questions.question: A customer reports a creaking noise from the front when turning into driveways at low speed. The noise does not occur when bouncing the front end straight up and down in the shop. What does the driveway condition add that helps diagnosis?

answers.text: Higher road speed than a shop bounce test
Body twist and steering angle together, which load bushings and joints differently than straight vertical movement
Brake application, which is the only load in a driveway entry
Cold tires, which only occur in driveways

questions.explanation: Entering a driveway combines steering input, one-wheel suspension movement, and body twist. A noise that needs that combination points toward parts loaded by twist and steering, guiding where to inspect while an assistant reproduces it.

questions.question: A front strut shows a bent piston rod after the vehicle struck a deep pothole, and the tire on that corner shows rapid wear on one shoulder. Besides the strut, what must the technician check before returning the vehicle?

answers.text: Only the tire pressure on the damaged corner
The steering knuckle, control arm, and wheel for bending, and then alignment angles on that corner
Only the strut mount bearing for noise
The rear alignment, because front damage always shifts it first

questions.explanation: Impact force strong enough to bend a rod often bends other locating parts. The knuckle, arm, and wheel must be inspected and alignment measured, or the replacement strut will be installed into a still-bent geometry that keeps wearing the tire.

questions.question: A customer reports a rattle over washboard roads that disappears on smooth pavement and during turns. The front stabilizer links check tight, but the bar bushings show a visible gap between bar and rubber when the bar is pried. What is the likely cause?

answers.text: A loose steering gear mounting bolt
Worn, shrunken frame bushings allowing the bar to rattle in its brackets
Worn strut bearings that only rattle on rough roads
Excessive caster causing a road-speed rattle

questions.explanation: Clearance between the bar and its frame bushings lets the bar knock over repeated small inputs, matching a washboard rattle, while tight links rule themselves out. The worn bushings are renewed to restore the bar's snug mounting.

questions.question: A steering system passes every pressure and flow test, yet the customer still reports heavy steering on cold mornings that fades as the vehicle warms. Which test condition was most likely missing from the workshop tests?

answers.text: The tests should have been run with the wheels removed
The tests were run on warm fluid; the fault only appears with cold, thick fluid and should be retested cold
The tests should have been run at highway speed on a lift
No test can ever reproduce a temperature complaint

questions.explanation: Viscosity and worn clearances behave differently cold, and a classic cold-only assist loss will pass every test once the fluid is warm. Reproducing the customer's condition — testing first thing on a cold system — is essential before declaring the hydraulics healthy.

questions.question: An idler arm is the frame-mounted type with a threaded bushing that sets arm tension. After replacement, the center link requires excessive force to move by hand with the pitman arm disconnected; service information specifies the link should move with moderate hand force and no binding. What is wrong?

answers.text: The center link is bent and must be replaced without further checks
The pitman arm is causing the binding even though disconnected
New idler arms are always stiff and must be driven to break in
The threaded idler bushing is over-tightened, binding the pivot and adding steering friction

questions.explanation: A disconnected link isolates the idler pivot as the resistance source. Threaded-bushing idlers have an adjustment: too tight binds the pivot and raises steering effort/return problems. Backing it to the specified freedom of movement is the correction.

questions.question: Load-leveling rear shocks with air fittings are fitted. The vehicle sits level unloaded at minimum pressure but sags heavily with a trailer, and adding air to the specified maximum raises it only slightly while the gauge shows pressure building normally. What is suspect?

answers.text: The compressor on a manual-fill system is faulty
Sag with a trailer is normal at any amount
The air shocks' internal air chambers are leaking or the shocks are beyond their load capacity for the tongue weight in use
The leaf/coil springs carry none of the load on this design

questions.explanation: Manual air shocks assist the springs within a rated capacity. Pressure that builds but does not lift indicates chamber leakage or a load beyond capacity; the springs still carry the base load, and a manual-fill system has no onboard compressor to blame.

ase-xev-level-1-electrified-vehicle-safe.quiz_title: ASE xEV Level 1 — Electrified Vehicle Safety (Electrically Aware Person) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A detailer asks whether the shock hazard is the only electrical hazard the standards name for work around xEVs. How should the lead answer?

answers.text: No; the hazards named include shock along with arc flash and arc blast
Yes; shock is the single hazard the standards recognize
No; the other named hazard is static discharge from carpeting
Yes; burns from hot exhaust are counted as the electrical hazard

questions.explanation: The standards name shock, arc flash, and blast as the electrical hazards, so limiting awareness to shock alone understates the risk.

questions.question: Two electrified vehicles sit side by side in the holding area, one energized and one non-energized. How must their toppers read?

answers.text: Each topper must identify its own vehicle's condition, one as energized and the other as non-energized
Both toppers should read energized to be safe and simple
Only the energized vehicle needs a topper at all
The toppers can be swapped because the vehicles are the same model

questions.explanation: Identification is per vehicle: the topper states whether that vehicle is energized or non-energized, and a wrong state misleads everyone nearby.

questions.question: Two Level One coworkers disagree at lunch: one says the prohibition covers only the battery pack itself. What settles the disagreement?

answers.text: Seniority in the shop, with the longer-serving worker prevailing
A vote of the technicians present that day
The parts catalog, which groups some items as accessories

The standard's own wording: a Level One person shall not touch a Manual Service Disconnect or any of the high-voltage components — inverters, orange cables, motors, compressors, converters, and the rest of the listed hardware included

questions.explanation: The prohibition names the disconnect and then sweeps in all high-voltage components. The listed hardware leaves no battery-only reading available.

questions.question: A Level One receptionist sees vapor and then flame under a parked electric car in the showroom. What sequence is correct?

answers.text: Get people out, call 911 and state that the vehicle is an electrified vehicle, and stay out, because the battery appearing to be the fire source means everyone leaves the area immediately
Move the car outside by pushing it through the showroom doors
Announce a sale event to clear the floor indirectly
Ask the sales team to photograph the car for the insurer first

questions.explanation: Showroom or shop, the sequence is the same: evacuate, call with the xEV fact, and do not re-enter for property or pictures.

questions.question: A trainer must justify including toxic and flammable gases in a drill that involves no fire. What justification matches the element?

answers.text: Gases only matter after a fire is fully developed

A damaged or overheating cell may generate toxic and flammable gases before or without ignition, so crews drill recognizing the hazard, moving people away, and avoiding ignition sources even when nothing is burning
The drill teaches crews to smell batteries at close range
Gas training is about the shop's heating system instead

questions.explanation: Gases precede flames in many battery events. The element trains recognition and distance on the strength of the gas hazard alone, not as a fire footnote.

questions.question: A technician-in-training asks why the motor-generator matters for identification beyond driving the wheels. What extra role should the mentor mention?

answers.text: It steers the vehicle when the wheel is disconnected
It also generates electricity during regenerative braking, recovering energy for the high-voltage battery
It burns fuel to warm the cabin in winter
It inflates the tires to the correct pressure

questions.explanation: Motor-generators are listed HV components whose regenerative braking role is part of how the standards describe them.

questions.question: A rescue scenario in training involves a person shocked where the source is the HV battery itself. The instructor's key caution about step 2 is:

answers.text: A disconnect is always mounted on the battery case
A disconnect may not be available when the source is the HV battery itself
The battery can be switched off at its own ignition
The MSD is stored inside the battery pack

questions.explanation: The standard is explicit: when the HV battery is the source, a disconnect may not be available, and responders must plan around that exception.

questions.question: Orange cabling is visible along the frame of an electric delivery truck, outside its electrical protection barriers. What conclusion should a Level One observer draw?

answers.text: The cabling marks a high-voltage circuit that he can identify but must not touch
The cabling marks a safe low-voltage circuit he may handle freely
The cabling is a tow strap stored along the frame
The cabling proves the truck is de-energized

questions.explanation: High-voltage circuits are identified by orange cabling outside electrical protection barriers; identification never permits touching.

questions.question: A fire-service liaison visiting a bus garage asks the Level One host what single voltage fact most changes responder thinking about the fleet. Which fact is it?

answers.text: That bus packs are interchangeable with car packs
That larger trucks and buses can exceed 1200 volts DC in their high-voltage lithium-ion systems, dwarfing the typical passenger pack range of 100 to 400 volts DC
That buses store their energy at 60 volts DC
That bus voltage drops to zero when parked

questions.explanation: Responders plan around scale. The over-1200-volt fact is the one that separates a bus-garage briefing from a car-shop briefing.

questions.question: A quality reviewer asks what three battery conditions the standard names as creating accident risk despite protective design. What is the accurate set?

answers.text: A battery that is punctured, crushed, or has damaged internal components
A battery that is dusty, warm, or recently charged
A battery that is old, leased, or out of warranty
A battery that is painted, labeled, or roof-mounted

questions.explanation: The named trio is punctured, crushed, or internally damaged. Ordinary age, dirt, or mounting style is not the accident-risk trigger.

questions.question: A qualified technician removes the Manual Service Disconnect from a plug-in hybrid before lunch. Where must that disconnect be while the vehicle stays de-energized?

answers.text: On the driver's seat where the next person will see it
In the glove box with the owner's manual
In a secured location under lock and key, if possible, controlled by the technician who removed it, so no other person can reinstall it unknowingly
On top of the battery pack so it stays with the vehicle

questions.explanation: Removed disconnects, fuses, and relays belong in a secured location under lock and key if possible, under the removing technician's control.

questions.question: A shop's job safety planning form has a blank where the hazard analysis summary belongs, and leads routinely skip it. What does that habit do to the program?

answers.text: It strengthens planning by making forms shorter
It converts planning into the training element automatically
It has no effect because forms are not part of a program
It severs job safety planning from risk assessment, two separate named elements the program expects to connect on every job, so plans are made without the analysis that should shape them

questions.explanation: The form is where two elements meet. Skipping the analysis leaves planning uninformed, which is a program defect an audit should catch and correct.

questions.question: Maya, a Level One porter, is asked to pull the manual service disconnect on a hybrid SUV so the bay will be 'safe' before a technician arrives. What must Maya do?

answers.text: Pull it slowly while wearing shop gloves, since porters move vehicles all day
Pull it only if a supervisor is watching from the doorway
Pull it after switching the ignition off, which makes the action low-voltage work
Stop and hand the task to a Level Two or Level Three technician, because a Level One person shall not touch a manual service disconnect

questions.explanation: The Level One limit is absolute: a Level One person shall not touch the MSD. Disconnect work belongs to a Level Two or Level Three technician.

questions.question: During onboarding, a tire technician who will service only conventional tires on plug-in hybrids is offered xEV safety training. How does the standard treat that training?

answers.text: xEV safety training is forbidden until Level Two
xEV safety training is a SHALL proficiency about opening battery packs
xEV safety training is a MAY topic: a Level One person may be trained and tested in it
xEV safety training applies only to sales staff

questions.explanation: C1.1 names xEV safety training itself as one of the MAY training topics for the electrically aware person.

questions.question: A safety lead counts a dozen non-working crossings of the xEV bay in one hour by staff fetching coffee and paperwork. The lead's report to the owner should frame this as:

answers.text: A failure of the employer's foot-traffic limits for the work area, to be fixed with routing, signage, and supervision — not as twelve individual acts of carelessness to be disciplined one by one
A reason to ban coffee in the building entirely
Proof the bay is in the wrong building and must move
A compliment on how popular the new bay has become

questions.explanation: Traffic volume is an environment property. The employer's duty is to limit it by design, which is a management fix, not a dozen personal ones.

questions.question: A Level One inspector records that an exposed high-voltage cable outside its barrier has correct orange covering, then notices the covering stops halfway and the rest of the run is black. What is the proper record?

answers.text: A pass, because partial orange is enough once any orange is present
A note to add orange tape over the black half at the next service
An incomplete identification finding for a Level Two or Level Three person, because the exposed run outside the barrier should be identified by orange covering along the run others may encounter
No record, because the first half satisfied the inspection point

questions.explanation: A half-identified exposed run still leaves workers guessing for the other half. Recording and handing off beats passing it or taping it.

questions.question: An assessment identifies an arc flash hazard at a service panel. The owner asks what kinds of mitigation the framework expects the shop to consider. What answer is complete?

answers.text: Mitigation by design, by work practices, or by PPE: the hazard can be engineered down, worked around with safer methods, or protected against with equipment, and the assessment drives that choice
Mitigation by ignoring the hazard until an incident occurs
Mitigation only by telling workers to be careful verbally
Mitigation only by buying the most expensive option available

questions.explanation: The framework names three mitigation routes. A real assessment selects among design, practices, and PPE instead of defaulting to a warning.

questions.question: A wash attendant hears a parked EV's systems come alive as its owner approaches with a fob. Recognizing this as the named risk of unexpected turn-on, the attendant's sound move is to:

answers.text: Reach in and switch it off through the window
Stand in front of it so the owner notices the staff
Ignore it, since automatic wake-ups are harmless
Stay clear of the vehicle's path and treat it as ready to move until its state is confirmed

questions.explanation: Awareness plus distance is the Level One response to a vehicle that wakes on its own; reaching into it is not.

questions.question: A Level One employee identifies an electrified sedan in the service lane purely from its badging and then confirms with underhood labels and cables. Why is the confirmation step good practice?

answers.text: Identification uses multiple named cues: badging, underhood high-voltage warning labels, and cables together confirm the high-voltage system
Badging alone is forbidden as a cue
Confirmation authorizes him to open the battery
Underhood labels are unrelated to identification

questions.explanation: Combining badging with underhood warning labels and cables follows the standard's set of identification cues.

questions.question: During de-energizing preparation, a Level Two technician asks a Level One assistant to verify the parking brake. The assistant finds the brake indicator lit but one rear wheel still turns freely on the lift check. How is the verification reported?

answers.text: As a failed element: the brake is reported as not holding despite the indicator, and securing is not declared complete until the discrepancy is resolved per the maker's instructions
As complete, because the indicator is the official brake record
As complete for the braked side of the vehicle only
As a reason to rely on chocks alone and proceed regardless

questions.explanation: Verification tests reality, not lamps. A turning wheel defeats an indicator, and honest reporting stops the line.

praxis-core.quiz_title: Praxis Core Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Ms. Okafor reads the following to her class. When the high school jazz band began rehearsing at 7 a.m., few students liked the hour. The early slot, however, was the only time the shared music room was free, and it changed the group in unexpected ways. Students arrived, set up without reminders, and listened more closely because there was no hallway noise. Sections began trading recordings during breakfast. By spring, their director said the band's discipline and attentiveness — not extra talent — explained its sharper performances. Which statement best states the main idea?

answers.text: Early rehearsal is the only way any school band can improve
The jazz band performed better because new, more talented students joined
An inconvenient early schedule fostered discipline and focus that improved the band's playing
Students traded recordings because they disliked rehearsing

questions.explanation: The early hour removed distractions and built routines and listening, which the director credits for improvement. Talent is explicitly not the explanation.

questions.question:
The sewing circle at the Harborview Senior Center meets on Thursdays around a table covered with donated fabric. Some members mend their own clothes; others sew quilts for the children's hospital or hem curtains for neighbors who can no longer manage a needle. Newcomers are handed the simplest task first, usually sewing on buttons. Gradually, as their stitches grow steadier, they graduate to the quilting frames. Last winter the circle finished its hundredth quilt, and the hospital hung it in the lobby rather than on a bed. The members, most of them in their eighties, voted to start the next hundred immediately.

In the passage, the word "Gradually" is used to show that newcomers

answers.text: finish their first quilt within a single meeting
are eventually put in charge of the whole circle
lose interest in sewing as the weeks pass
take on harder sewing tasks slowly, as their skill improves

questions.explanation: The word marks a slow progression from buttons to quilting frames as stitches grow steadier. It does not suggest speed, promotion to leadership, or fading interest.

questions.question: A principal claims that adding a late bus will increase participation in after-school clubs, since students will have a ride home. Which finding would most weaken the principal's claim?

answers.text: A survey shows that most students who skip clubs do so because they must care for younger siblings at home, not because they lack a ride
The late bus would also be available to students attending tutoring
Several popular clubs meet in rooms near the bus loop
Some students who attend clubs live within walking distance of the school

questions.explanation: If most nonparticipants stay home for sibling care rather than for lack of a ride, a late bus does not address their reason for skipping clubs. Tutoring riders are a distractor because extra passengers say nothing about why club participation would or would not rise.

questions.question: Read the draft passage. (1) Volunteers gathered at the trailhead on a cool October morning. (2) They cleared fallen branches and repaired a wooden bridge. (3) The trail is popular. (4) Hikers use it in every season. (5) By noon, the group had restored the muddiest section near the creek. (6) Walkers will now find the path safer and easier to follow. Which revision best combines sentences 3 and 4 of the passage above?

answers.text: The trail is popular, hikers use it in every season.
The trail is popular and hikers, they use it in every season.
The popular trail is used by hikers in every season.
Popular, hikers use the trail in every season it.

questions.explanation: Folding the season detail into a single statement about the popular trail produces one clear, complete sentence. A comma splice and a doubled subject both leave the combined sentence ungrammatical.

questions.question: What is the prime factorization of 96?

answers.text: 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3
2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3
2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3
2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 3

questions.explanation: Dividing 96 by 2 five times and then by 3 gives 96 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3, and every factor is prime. The factors 2, 2, 2, 3, and 3 multiply to 72, not 96.

questions.question: The following describes a school experiment. Students in a biology class placed identical bean seedlings in three locations: a sunny windowsill, a shaded corner, and under a grow light for twelve hours a day. All seedlings received the same amount of water. After two weeks, the grow-light seedlings were tallest, the windowsill seedlings were slightly shorter and leaned toward the glass, and the shaded seedlings were pale and thin. The students concluded that light conditions, not water, explained the differences they observed. Which detail supports that conclusion?

answers.text: The seedlings were all bean plants of the same kind
All the seedlings received the same amount of water, so water did not vary among groups
The shaded seedlings were planted in larger pots
The windowsill seedlings were measured first each day

questions.explanation: Holding water constant removes it as an explanation for differing growth, leaving light as the varied factor. Pot size and measurement order are not mentioned.

questions.question:
On Tuesday afternoons, a calm golden retriever named Biscuit pads through the children's ward at St. Anne's Hospital, a volunteer handler at the other end of the leash. Children who have refused their walking exercises will often cross a whole hallway if they are allowed to hold that leash. However, the visits are carefully scheduled, because some patients are allergic to dogs and others are frightened of them. Staff therefore post Biscuit's route each morning, so families can choose a different corridor or enjoy a visit, as they prefer. Between stops, Biscuit rests on a mat, tail thumping whenever a door opens.

The author's attitude toward the therapy dog visits is best described as

answers.text: enthusiastic without any reservations at all
warmly supportive while acknowledging their limits
doubtful that the visits do patients any good
focused mainly on the risks the dog creates

questions.explanation: The hallway walks show clear approval, while the scheduling for allergies and fear shows the approval is measured rather than blind. Doubt is undercut by children walking who had refused to, and risk is treated as manageable, not central.

questions.question:
When the city replaced its glaring white streetlights with amber, shielded fixtures, the council's stated reason was the electricity bill, and the savings have indeed been real. Walk through a neighborhood at midnight now, though, and residents mention something else first: they sleep better. The new fixtures aim their light at the pavement instead of into bedroom windows and across the night sky. Astronomers at the community college report fainter skyglow for their evening classes, and migrating birds, drawn off course by bright towers of light, pass over the city in greater safety. The mayor calls it the rare project that pleased the accountants and the stargazers at once.

The relationship between the fixtures' shielding and residents' sleep is best described as

answers.text: residents sleep better because the amber light is brighter
aiming light downward keeps it out of bedrooms, which lets residents sleep better
the shielding was installed after residents complained about noise
better sleep caused the city to choose shielded fixtures

questions.explanation: The passage says the fixtures aim light at the pavement instead of into bedroom windows, and residents report sleeping better, a direct mechanism. Brightness is reduced rather than raised, noise is never mentioned, and the sleep reports followed the installation.

questions.question:
Passage 1: Protected bicycle lanes, separated from car traffic by a curb, make city cycling far safer. In the year after the city installed protected lanes on Elm Avenue, bicycle crashes on that street fell by nearly half, even as the number of riders grew.
Passage 2: As a parent, I opposed nothing about the new protected lanes on Elm Avenue, and the results have convinced me further. My children now ride to the library along a lane where no car can drift into their path, and I no longer worry about that trip.
The authors of the two passages agree that

answers.text: Protected bicycle lanes make cycling safer
Every street in the city should have a protected lane
All children should ride bicycles to school
Bicycles are a better form of transportation than cars

questions.explanation: The engineer-style evidence about falling crashes and the parent's account of children riding without cars drifting into their path both support safer cycling from protected lanes. A lane on every street is tempting, but neither author claims the lanes belong everywhere.

questions.question: Consider the sentence "In light of the fact that enrollment rose, the school hired two more teachers." Its underlined portion is: "In light of the fact that" Which of the following best replaces the underlined portion?

answers.text: In light of the fact that
On account of the fact that
Due to the circumstance that
Because

questions.explanation: A single causal word carries the same meaning as the five-word opener without weakening the sentence. The other wordy openers preserve the bloat they were meant to cure.

questions.question: After a 15% discount, a bicycle sells for $51. What was the original price before the discount?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 85% of the original, so the original is 51 ÷ 0.85 = $60. Multiplying 51 by 0.85 gives $43.35, which discounts the sale price a second time instead of recovering the original.

questions.question: A data set has a mean of 17.5. If every value in the set is multiplied by 4, what is the mean of the new data set?
questions.explanation: Multiplying every value by 4 multiplies the mean by 4 as well, giving 17.5 x 4 = 70. Adding 4 to the mean would give 21.5, which describes a shift rather than a scaling.

questions.question: Passage: By the 1990s, the one-screen Palace Theater was losing money, its seats torn and its roof leaking whenever it rained. Closure seemed certain. The response came from an unlikely alliance: the high school drama club, which needed a stage, and a retired projectionist, who knew the building's equipment. Students raised money through car washes, a local bank matched the total, and volunteers repaired the roof. The Palace reopened in 1998 and now hosts plays as well as films. The overall organization of this passage is best described as

answers.text: a problem — a failing, leaking theater — followed by the community response that solved it
a cause — a bank donation — followed only by its effects on ticket sales
a description of a theater arranged by spatial order
an argument against showing films in old theaters

questions.explanation: A theater facing closure is presented first, then the alliance, fundraising, and repairs that saved it. That is a problem followed by its solution.

questions.question:
On weekday mornings, a folding repair stand appears beside the entrance to the Marston Street train station, staffed by two mechanics from a nearby bike shop. Riders can get a flat fixed, a chain oiled, or brakes adjusted while they wait for their train, and every repair is free during the first month. The shop's owner admits the stand costs more than it earns. Nevertheless, she keeps setting it up at dawn, saying that a rider whose commute is rescued once tends to trust the shop with bigger jobs later. Regulars now bring coffee for the mechanics, and one rider painted a small sign that reads, 'Saved my 8:10 again.'

It can most reasonably be inferred from the passage that the shop owner

answers.text: plans to begin charging for flat repairs next month
believes most riders will never need a bike shop
intends to move her shop beside the station entrance
expects free small repairs to bring the shop larger paid work in time

questions.explanation: The owner says a rider whose commute is rescued once tends to trust the shop with bigger jobs later, which points to larger paid work as the expected payoff. No plan to charge, move, or dismiss riders' future needs is stated.

questions.question: A farmers market that has operated only on Saturdays is often crowded. Its organizers conclude that adding a Wednesday session will be just as successful, and they plan to rent the same lot for Wednesdays. Their conclusion depends on which assumption?

answers.text: Saturday shoppers enjoy buying fresh produce
The market lot is large enough to hold more stalls
Wednesday shoppers will prefer produce that was picked the same morning
The vendors and shoppers who make the Saturday market succeed are available and willing to come on a weekday as well

questions.explanation: Saturday success transfers to Wednesday only if the same vendors can staff stalls and enough shoppers can attend on a weekday. A larger lot is tempting, but space was not the stated reason for expecting success.

questions.question: A board that is 11.36 meters long is shortened by removing a piece 4.58 meters long. How many meters of board remain?

answers.text: 15.94 meters
6.78 meters
6.68 meters
6.88 meters

questions.explanation: Subtracting with borrowing across the decimal point gives 11.36 - 4.58 = 6.78 meters. Adding the two lengths gives 15.94 meters, which answers a different question.

questions.question: A stem-and-leaf plot shows page counts with stem 3 and leaves 1, 4, 9; stem 4 and leaves 0, 2, 2, 7; and stem 5 and leaf 3. The values are 31, 34, 39, 40, 42, 42, 47, and 53. How many of the values are less than 42?
questions.explanation: The values below 42 are 31, 34, 39, and 40, which is 4 values. Counting 6 includes the two values equal to 42, but the question asks for values strictly less than 42.

questions.question: Read the passage. The ferry company's rigid schedule frustrated commuters: the boat left at six whether it was full or nearly empty, and no appeal to the captain could add a sailing on a busy morning. As used in the passage, 'rigid' most nearly means

answers.text: made of stiff material
inflexible and unchanging
precisely on time by accident
harsh toward passengers

questions.explanation: The schedule cannot be altered — no added sailings, no exceptions — which is inflexibility of a rule, not stiffness of a material.

questions.question: A theater's price table lists tickets as follows: children under 12 pay $6, students with identification pay $9, adults pay $14, and seniors pay $10. A group made up of two adults and one child under 12 would pay how much in total?
questions.explanation: Two adult tickets at $14 each plus one child ticket at $6 total $34. The $28 figure counts only the two adults and omits the child's ticket.

questions.question: A drink mix uses juice concentrate and water in the ratio 1:5. If a batch uses 15 cups of water, how many cups of juice concentrate does it use?

answers.text: 3 cups
5 cups
15 cups
75 cups

questions.explanation: The water is 5 parts totaling 15 cups, so each part is 3 cups, and the juice is 1 part, or 3 cups. Multiplying the two given numbers gives 75, which ignores the parts structure of the ratio.

aws-certified-welding-inspector.quiz_title: AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Two plates meet at their edges to form an L shape for the corner of a box. Which term names this joint?

answers.text: A lap joint
A tee joint
An edge joint
A corner joint

questions.explanation: A corner joint joins two members at right angles at their edges, as at the corner of a box. A tee joint involves one member meeting the flat surface of the other instead.

questions.question: At the end of a bead, where the arc was broken, a shallow bowl-like depression remains in the weld. That depression is called a:

answers.text: Keyhole
Puddle mark
Crater
Dimple pass

questions.explanation: A crater is the depression at the end of a weld bead where the arc was terminated. Unfilled craters shrink and crack, so proper technique fills the crater before breaking the arc.

questions.question: A weld contains a crack, and the applicable standard prohibits cracks of any size. Because it makes the weld rejectable, the crack is classified as a:

answers.text: Benign discontinuity
Cosmetic indication
Defect
Relevant artifact

questions.explanation: A defect is a discontinuity that exceeds the acceptance criteria of the governing standard and renders the weld rejectable. Cracks are prohibited outright in most structural standards.

questions.question: On an adjustable alternating-current gas tungsten arc power source, shifting more of the cycle to electrode positive will generally increase which effect?

answers.text: Cleaning action on the work surface, with more heat into the tungsten and less penetration
Penetration with no effect on the tungsten
Wire feed speed from the feeder
Flux melting in the joint

questions.explanation: More electrode-positive time strengthens oxide cleaning but dumps more heat into the tungsten and reduces penetration, while more electrode-negative time does the opposite by heating the work more deeply.

questions.question: A shop proposes eddy current testing on a glass-reinforced plastic tank seam. Why will the method not work on that seam?

answers.text: The seam is too smooth for a probe to follow
The seam is above room temperature
Plastic reflects ultrasound too strongly
Eddy currents can only be induced in electrically conductive materials

questions.explanation: Eddy current testing depends on inducing circulating electrical currents in the part, which requires an electrically conductive material such as a metal. Nonconductive plastics cannot support the induced currents the method measures.

questions.question: A single-bevel preparation is cut at 30 degrees measured from a line perpendicular to the plate surface, on one member only. The 30-degree figure describes the:

answers.text: Included groove angle
Work angle
Travel angle
Bevel angle

questions.explanation: The bevel angle is the angle between the prepared edge of one member and a plane perpendicular to its surface. The groove angle is the total included angle between both groove faces.

questions.question: A procedure requires fusion through the entire thickness of the joint, with weld metal completely filling the groove from face to root. This condition is known as:

answers.text: Partial joint penetration
Intermittent welding
Seal welding
Complete joint penetration

questions.explanation: Complete joint penetration means the weld metal fully penetrates the joint thickness with complete root fusion. Partial joint penetration intentionally leaves part of the joint unfused.

questions.question: A visual examination is planned in a shadowed corner of a fabrication shop where the inspector can barely read a gauge. What must be corrected before the examination can be trusted?

answers.text: Adequate illumination must be provided at the examination surface
The weld must be painted before it is examined
The examination must be done from farther away
Only a mirror may be used in shadowed areas

questions.explanation: Visual examination depends on the inspector actually seeing fine surface detail, so adequate light at the surface is a basic precondition. Examining in poor light makes small cracks and shallow undercut easy to miss.

questions.question: During a pipe test, the pipe is turned on rollers so the welder always welds near the top while the joint rotates under the arc. Which position does this represent?

answers.text: 1G, the flat rotated pipe position
5G, because the pipe is horizontal
6G, because pipe is round
4G overhead plate

questions.explanation: When the pipe rotates and welding stays in the flat position at the top, the test is the rotated flat pipe position. The welder does not have to change body position around a fixed joint.

questions.question: Before joining a dissimilar-metal joint, a layer of compatible weld metal is deposited on one joint face and then welded to. What is this layer called and why is it used?

answers.text: Buttering, used to provide a transition surface that makes the final joint weldable and sound
Tacking, used only to hold parts during fit-up
Gouging, used to remove defective metal
Sealing, used only to stop leaks visually

questions.explanation: Buttering coats a joint face with a layer that is metallurgically compatible with both sides, easing dissimilar-metal joining and sometimes limiting dilution or cracking in the final weld.

questions.question: Before using a gauge to measure weld dimensions on an acceptance check, the inspector notices its calibration sticker shows a past-due date. What should the inspector do?

answers.text: Use the gauge anyway because mechanical gauges do not drift
Borrow the welder personal gauge without checking its status either
Set that gauge aside and use equipment with current calibration for the acceptance measurements
Measure by eye and record the gauge number on the report

questions.explanation: Acceptance measurements must come from equipment with current calibration so the recorded values can be trusted. Recording a gauge that was not actually used would misstate how the measurement was made.

questions.question: Above a fillet weld symbol, a curved line bowed outward away from the symbol is drawn touching the top of the triangle. What finished weld face does this contour symbol require?

answers.text: A flush face even with the symbol outline
A concave face dished inward
No requirement; contour symbols describe the groove only
A convex face bulging outward

questions.explanation: An outward-bowed contour line calls for a convex weld face, an inward-curved line calls for concave, and a straight line calls for a flush face. The contour symbol is placed with the weld symbol on the reference line.

questions.question: The face of a fillet weld bulges outward with excess metal rather than lying flat or slightly concave. The maximum distance from the face to a line between the toes describes the weld's:

answers.text: Convexity
Concavity
Throat size
Leg size

questions.explanation: Convexity is the maximum distance from a convex weld face to the line joining the weld toes. Concavity is the corresponding measurement for a face curving inward.

questions.question: At the junction where the arrow meets the reference line, a small circle is drawn around the joint of the two lines. No other supplementary symbol is present. What does the circle instruct?

answers.text: The weld is to be made in the shop only
The weld requires radiographic examination around the joint
The weld extends all the way around the joint
The weld is a plug weld through a round hole

questions.explanation: A circle at the arrow-to-reference-line junction is the all-around symbol, meaning the weld continues around the entire joint. A flag at that junction, by contrast, denotes a field weld.

questions.question: A gas metal arc weld runs at 28 volts and 250 amperes with a travel speed of 10 inches per minute. Using heat input = volts × amperes × 60 ÷ travel speed in inches per minute, what is the heat input?

answers.text: 42.0 kilojoules per inch
70.0 kilojoules per inch
25.2 kilojoules per inch
4.2 kilojoules per inch

questions.explanation: Heat input = 28 × 250 × 60 ÷ 10 = 420,000 ÷ 10 = 42,000 joules per inch, or 42.0 kilojoules per inch.

questions.question: A vessel filled completely with water is pressurized above its operating pressure and held while joints are examined for weeping. Beyond leak detection, what does this hydrostatic test demonstrate?

answers.text: The electrical conductivity of the shell
The magnetic permeability of the welds
The internal soundness of every weld pass
The pressure-containing strength and integrity of the vessel under load

questions.explanation: A hydrostatic test loads the whole vessel with pressure, demonstrating overall strength and tightness under conditions beyond normal service. It does not characterize individual weld passes, conductivity, or permeability.

questions.question: A constant-voltage wire welding station shows voltage set correctly at the source but the arc behaves as if voltage at the arc is low. Long, undersized leads are found in the circuit. What is the likely problem?

answers.text: Too much inductance stored in the shielding gas
Voltage drop in the welding circuit from excessive or undersized cable length
The wire classification is expired
The contact tube is too new

questions.explanation: Long or undersized welding cables add resistance that drops voltage along the circuit, so the arc receives less than the voltage set and displayed at the power source.

questions.question: At the point where a welder stopped and broke the arc, a small star-shaped crack is found in the depression left at the end of the bead. This is most likely a:

answers.text: Longitudinal crack
Underbead crack
Crater crack
Toe crack

questions.explanation: A crater crack forms in the depression left when the arc is terminated without filling the crater, often with a star-like pattern. It is located in the crater itself, not along the toe or beneath the bead.

questions.question: A low-alloy steel containing chromium and molybdenum is scheduled for welding with the same thickness and joint as a mild steel job that needed no preheat. Why does the alloy steel typically require preheat anyway?

answers.text: Alloy steels melt at twice the temperature of mild steel
Alloying elements make the steel nonmagnetic
Alloying elements raise hardenability, so the heat-affected zone can harden and crack without heat control
Alloy steels cannot be welded with standard processes

questions.explanation: Chromium, molybdenum, and similar elements increase hardenability, meaning even moderate cooling rates can produce hard heat-affected zones in alloy steels, so preheat and controlled cooling become necessary at thicknesses where mild steel welds easily. Such steels are routinely welded with the standard arc processes.

questions.question: Visual examination reveals a faint, tight linear indication that could be a surface crack or could be a tool mark, and the distinction decides acceptance. What is the most appropriate next examination step?

answers.text: Accept the weld without further checks
Measure the weld size again with a fillet gauge
Apply a surface method such as liquid penetrant or magnetic particle examination to confirm the indication
Grind the area deeply until the question disappears

questions.explanation: When visual examination leaves a crack-like indication uncertain, a surface examination method sensitive to fine cracks can confirm whether a real surface break exists. Grinding first would destroy the evidence and may not remove a real crack fully.

biochemistry.quiz_title: Biochemistry Practice Exams FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A monosaccharide is best defined as which of the following?

answers.text: A chain of two sugar units joined by a glycosidic bond
A single sugar unit that cannot be hydrolyzed into a smaller carbohydrate
A polymer of many sugar units
A sugar unit joined to a lipid by an ester bond

questions.explanation: A monosaccharide is one sugar unit, so it cannot be broken down into a smaller carbohydrate by hydrolysis. Two units form a disaccharide and many units form a polysaccharide.

questions.question: The shorthand 18:1 for oleic acid indicates a fatty acid with which composition?

answers.text: 18 carbons and no double bonds
16 carbons and one double bond
18 double bonds and one methyl group
18 carbons and one double bond

questions.explanation: In fatty acid shorthand the first number is the chain length in carbons and the second is the number of double bonds. Oleate is an 18-carbon monounsaturated fatty acid.

questions.question: What is the central claim of the chemiosmotic theory of oxidative phosphorylation?

answers.text: Oxygen binds directly to ATP synthase to phosphorylate ADP
NADH transfers its phosphate group directly to ADP
Electron transport pumps protons across the inner membrane, and the resulting proton-motive force drives ATP synthesis
ATP is made only by substrate-level phosphorylation in the matrix

questions.explanation: Chemiosmosis couples electron transport to ATP synthesis indirectly: proton pumping stores energy in an electrochemical gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane, and proton flow back through ATP synthase drives phosphorylation.

questions.question: What is the central reaction catalyzed by aminotransferases in amino acid catabolism?

answers.text: They oxidize amino acids directly to CO2 and free ammonia using oxygen
They transfer the alpha-amino group of an amino acid to an alpha-keto acid, most often alpha-ketoglutarate, forming glutamate and a new alpha-keto acid
They hydrolyze peptide bonds to release free amino acids from proteins
They attach amino groups to fatty acids for disposal as urea

questions.explanation: Aminotransferases reversibly move amino groups between amino acids and alpha-keto acids; collecting nitrogen on alpha-ketoglutarate to form glutamate funnels amino groups from many amino acids into a single carrier.

questions.question: What are the three components of a nucleotide?

answers.text: A nitrogenous base and a pentose sugar, with no phosphate group
A nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and at least one phosphate group
A nitrogenous base and a phosphate group, with no sugar
An amino acid, a pentose sugar, and a fatty acid

questions.explanation: A nucleotide consists of a nitrogenous base attached to a pentose sugar that also carries one or more phosphate groups. Removing the phosphate leaves a nucleoside.

questions.question: An enzyme that joins two molecules together in a reaction coupled to ATP hydrolysis belongs to which class?

answers.text: Ligases
Lyases
Isomerases
Hydrolases

questions.explanation: Ligases form new covalent bonds between two substrates at the expense of a nucleoside triphosphate such as ATP. DNA ligase sealing a nick in a backbone is a familiar example.

questions.question: A reaction occurring in a cell at constant temperature and pressure has a negative ΔG. What does this sign establish?

answers.text: It is endergonic and requires a net input of energy to proceed forward.
It is exergonic and is thermodynamically able to proceed in the forward direction.
The reaction must already be at equilibrium.
The reaction can only occur if it is coupled to ATP hydrolysis.

questions.explanation: A negative ΔG defines an exergonic reaction: the forward direction is thermodynamically favorable under the actual conditions present. It says nothing by itself about how fast the reaction will occur.

questions.question: Glycolysis takes place in which cellular location, in both aerobic and anaerobic cells?

answers.text: The mitochondrial matrix
The lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum
The cytosol
The peroxisome

questions.explanation: All ten glycolytic enzymes are soluble cytosolic proteins, and the pathway runs in the cytosol of essentially all cell types. Only later stages of glucose oxidation move into the mitochondrion.

questions.question: In eukaryotic cells, where do the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex and most citric acid cycle enzymes operate?

answers.text: In the mitochondrial matrix
In the cytosol
In the intermembrane space
In the lysosome

questions.explanation: Pyruvate is transported into mitochondria, and the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex and the soluble cycle enzymes are located in the matrix, close to the respiratory chain that reoxidizes NADH.

questions.question: In the oxidative pentose phosphate pathway, the carbon dioxide released comes from which step?

answers.text: The hydrolysis of 6-phosphogluconolactone by lactonase
The isomerization of ribulose-5-phosphate to ribose-5-phosphate
The transketolase transfer of a two-carbon unit
The oxidative decarboxylation of 6-phosphogluconate by 6-phosphogluconate dehydrogenase

questions.explanation: 6-Phosphogluconate dehydrogenase oxidatively removes carbon 1 of the six-carbon substrate as CO2, yielding the five-carbon ribulose-5-phosphate and the second NADPH of the oxidative branch.

questions.question: Which description best summarizes the integrated action of insulin in the fed state?

answers.text: It promotes mobilization of all stored fuels simultaneously
It lowers blood glucose mainly by forcing the kidney to excrete glucose
It promotes fuel storage and synthesis: glucose uptake in muscle and adipose tissue, glycogen and fat synthesis, and protein synthesis, while suppressing fuel mobilization
It acts only on the brain to suppress appetite and has no peripheral metabolic effects

questions.explanation: Insulin is the hormone of fuel abundance; its coordinated peripheral actions move glucose out of the blood into storage and synthesis pathways and restrain the release of stored fuels.

questions.question: A fraction contains 240 units of enzyme activity and 60 milligrams of total protein. What is its specific activity?

answers.text: 4 units per milligram
0.25 units per milligram
300 units per milligram
14,400 units per milligram

questions.explanation: Specific activity is total activity divided by total protein: 240 units / 60 mg = 4 units per milligram.

questions.question: Glucose is classified as an aldose and fructose as a ketose because glucose contains which functional group and fructose contains which other group?

answers.text: An aldehyde group in glucose and a ketone group in fructose
A ketone group in glucose and an aldehyde group in fructose
A carboxylic acid group in glucose and an aldehyde group in fructose
An alcohol group in glucose and an ester group in fructose

questions.explanation: Aldoses carry an aldehyde group, as in glucose. Ketoses carry a ketone group, as in fructose.

questions.question: During fasting, triacylglycerols stored in adipose tissue are mobilized primarily because which hormonal signal activates lipolysis there?

answers.text: Aldosterone acting on hormone-sensitive lipase
High insulin acting on adipose lipases
Glucagon and epinephrine signaling through cyclic AMP, with low insulin removing its antilipolytic brake
Thyroxine directly hydrolyzing triacylglycerol in the droplet

questions.explanation: Catecholamine and glucagon signaling raises adipocyte cyclic AMP and activates the lipase cascade, while falling insulin releases its normal suppression of lipolysis.

questions.question: Several hours into a fast, adipose tissue releases large amounts of free fatty acids and glycerol into the blood. Which change in the adipocyte is the direct cause?

answers.text: Insulin rises and activates hormone-sensitive lipase by dephosphorylation
Falling insulin removes its restraint while protein kinase A phosphorylates perilipin and hormone-sensitive lipase, opening the lipid droplet's stored triacylglycerol to hydrolysis
Glucagon receptors on adipocytes directly hydrolyze triacylglycerol extracellularly
Fatty acids leave because their membrane transporters are induced by glucose

questions.explanation: Triacylglycerol mobilization (Ch 12) is gated hormonally (Ch 14). In the fed state insulin keeps the lipolytic machinery dephosphorylated and quiet. As insulin falls and catecholamine/PKA signaling rises, perilipin and hormone-sensitive lipase are phosphorylated, lipolysis proceeds, and fatty acids plus glycerol (a gluconeogenic substrate for the liver) enter the blood.

questions.question: At a given chain length, a saturated fatty acid has a higher melting point than an unsaturated one mainly because saturated chains can do what?

answers.text: Form hydrogen bonds with water more readily
Pack tightly together, maximizing van der Waals contacts
Bend into rings that stack closely
Carry a negative charge that attracts neighboring chains

questions.explanation: Straight saturated chains align closely, so many van der Waals contacts must be broken to melt them. Double bonds, especially cis, disrupt this packing.

questions.question: In poorly controlled diabetes, adipose tissue becomes insulin-resistant. The downstream hepatic consequences include increased VLDL output and ketogenesis. The connecting sequence is:

answers.text: Insulin resistance in adipose raises glucose uptake, starving the liver of fatty acids

Unrestrained adipose lipolysis delivers excess fatty acids to the liver, which re-esterifies part into triacylglycerol for VLDL export and oxidizes the rest, with acetyl-CoA overflow forming ketone bodies
The liver secretes VLDL in order to manufacture ketone bodies from it in the blood
Hepatic VLDL output falls because fatty acids cannot reach the liver

questions.explanation: One tissue's signaling failure becomes another's substrate flood (Ch 14 integration). Insulin-resistant adipocytes cannot suppress hormone-sensitive lipase (Ch 12 mobilization), so fatty acid flux to the liver rises; the liver partitions the surplus between re-esterification (VLDL triacylglycerol, raising blood lipids) and oxidation (acetyl-CoA, overflowing to ketones). Two hallmark blood abnormalities of diabetes are thus one upstream defect read out by hepatic fuel partitioning.
