questions.explanation: The second service route is unlicensed or cadet service in either department of a certified tank vessel.

questions.question: When checking cargo work against the tankerman requirements, which statement about combining officer and rating service is right?

answers.text: The service leg is waived for experienced Assistants.
An applicant may combine officer service and rating or cadet service to reach the 90-day total.
Totals alone satisfy every part of the pattern.
The 90 days must come from a single service type only.

questions.explanation: The rule offers three ways to reach 90 days: officer service, rating/cadet service, or a combination of the two.

questions.question: On a tank barge alongside a products terminal, the topic of the STCW tanker endorsements comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: STCW tanker endorsements for oil, chemical, and liquefied-gas cargo operations are a separate international track from the national tank vessel endorsements.
Yes — a PIC may serve as chief engineer on tank barges.
PIC applicants are exempt from medical examination.
STCW tanker endorsements replaced the national endorsements in 2025.

questions.explanation: National and STCW tanker credentials run in parallel; this program prepares for the national PIC endorsements.

questions.question: On a course assessment, a question covers whether a PIC endorsement authorizes officer service. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: No — a tank vessel endorsement credentials transfer duties only and does not qualify the holder to serve as a deck or engineer officer.
Yes — PIC holders may navigate the vessel as officer of the watch.
Yes — a PIC may serve as chief engineer on tank barges.
A PIC endorsement upgrades automatically to a mate's license.

questions.explanation: The endorsement is deliberately narrow: cargo-transfer responsibility, not watchstanding officer authority.

questions.question: A tank vessel loads 120 barrels of a dangerous-liquid cargo. At 42 gallons per barrel, how many gallons is that?
questions.explanation: Gallons = 120 x 42 = 5040.

questions.question: When checking cargo work against the tankerman requirements, which statement about who must supervise qualifying transfers is right?

answers.text: No supervision is required for the last five transfers.
Transfers supervised by any licensed officer qualify.
Qualifying transfers are performed under the supervision of a Tank Vessel-PIC — for barge applicants, a Tank Vessel-PIC or a Tank Barge-PIC.
Transfers supervised by the facility alone qualify for PIC.

questions.explanation: The apprentice PIC learns under an endorsed PIC; that supervision is what makes the transfers creditable.

colorado-master-plumber.quiz_title: Colorado Master Plumber Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures what counts as plumbing under Colorado law?

answers.text: The record needs only the years worked, with no dates or job descriptions.
The master examination has 100 scored items and 240 minutes.

Plumbing includes potable water supply and distribution piping, fixtures and traps, drainage and vent pipes, connected water conditioning appliances, and building drains, within the building or extending five feet from the building foundation.
Plumbing stops at the interior wall; nothing outside the building counts.

questions.explanation: The statutory reach is the building plus five feet from the foundation, excluding the service line from the first joint to the property line.

questions.question: A safety talk turns to slope for large building sewers. Which point is correct?

answers.text: Garage floor drains must always connect to the sanitary sewer in Colorado.
Large sewers are installed level because their size prevents clogging.
Horizontal drainage piping of 8 inches and larger may be installed at a slope as low as one-sixteenth inch per foot where the design supports it.
Large sewers slope one-quarter inch per foot, the same as a lavatory drain.

questions.explanation: Diameter buys grade relief: 8-inch and larger piping can run at a sixteenth inch per foot.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes master plumber experience requirement?

answers.text: A master plumber applicant needs 9,780 hours computed from sixty months at 163 hours.
A formula sheet is handed out with the examination.
A master plumber applicant must furnish evidence of five full-time years, or 8,500 hours, of practical plumbing experience.
Out-of-state experience never counts toward a Colorado license.

questions.explanation: Five full-time years and 8,500 published hours is the master standard; the 9,780 figure is a secondary-source error the Board does not publish.

questions.question: A trainee asks about the 163-hour month. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Military plumbing service counts month-for-month without any cap.
Colorado counts one month of full-time plumbing experience as equivalent to 163 hours when experience is measured in months.
Appointments can only be scheduled at least thirty days in advance.
Colorado counts one month of full-time experience as 200 hours.

questions.explanation: 163 hours is the Board's month — a conversion for measuring experience, not a way to recompute the published grade totals.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the job of the drainage system?

answers.text: The drainage system treats wastewater to drinking quality inside the building.
The drainage system stores wastewater until a pump truck removes it monthly.
The drainage system pressurizes waste so it can flow uphill without slope.

The sanitary drainage system collects wastewater and waterborne waste from fixtures and conveys it by gravity to the building drain, building sewer, and the public sewer or an approved private disposal system.

questions.explanation: Drainage is a gravity conveyor to an approved disposal point — slope and venting make it work.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how why drainage slope matters is handled in practice.

answers.text: Steeper is always better, so drains should be pitched as sharply as possible.

Proper slope keeps the liquid stream moving at a self-scouring pace that carries solids along; too little slope lets solids settle, and excessive slope can let liquid outrun solids and leave them behind.
One air admittance valve can replace the entire vent system of a building.
Slope is a cosmetic concern handled by the finish grade of the floor.

questions.explanation: Grade is a balance — scour without separation is the goal on every horizontal run.

questions.question: Which description of what an isometric drawing shows matches accepted Colorado practice?

answers.text: An isometric drawing is a photograph of the finished system.
Vents may turn horizontal at any height, including below the rim.
An isometric drawing lists materials without showing any piping.

An isometric plumbing drawing shows the piping system in three dimensions on a single view — runs, rises, drops, and fittings — drawn at 30-degree axes so the installer can count fittings, measure developed lengths, and see how stacks and branches relate.

questions.explanation: One drawing, whole system: isometrics are the working language of layout and material takeoff.

questions.question: How would an experienced Colorado master plumber best explain the job of the water distribution system?

answers.text: The water distribution system delivers potable water at adequate pressure and flow from the service through the building to every fixture, while protecting that water from contamination at every connection.
The distribution system stores a day's supply in open tanks in the attic.
Doubling a run's length has no effect on pressure at the end.
The water service may share a trench wall-to-wall with the sewer at the same level in all cases.

questions.explanation: Adequate, potable, protected: delivery and defense are the same system's two duties.

questions.question: How would an experienced Colorado master plumber best explain approved materials requirement?

answers.text: Materials are approved if they look like listed products.
Lead solder is still standard on drinking water lines.

Every pipe, fitting, fixture, and material installed in a Colorado plumbing system must be approved and listed for its intended use under the Colorado Plumbing Code's referenced standards; unlisted look-alikes are not approved by resemblance.
Sewer gas is only a nuisance odor, never a health hazard.

questions.explanation: Listed for the use, or it does not go in — approval is a property of the product, not the pitch.

questions.question: Which description of the purpose of a fixture trap matches accepted Colorado practice?

answers.text: A trap pressurizes the vent system to keep it clear.

A trap holds a seal of water in the drainage path that blocks sewer gases, vermin, and odors from entering the building while letting wastewater pass — it is the single most important fitting in the system.
A trap slows drainage so solids can settle out.
Hot waste cools itself in the trap sufficiently.

questions.explanation: A cup of water standing guard: the trap seal is the border between the sewer and the room.

questions.question: Which description of fixture approval and listing matches accepted Colorado practice?

answers.text: Classroom lavatories count double toward fixture counts.
Listing is required only for commercial fixtures.
Manufacturer instructions may be ignored where they conflict with habit.

Plumbing fixtures must be approved, listed products made of approved materials, installed per their manufacturers' instructions and the code, with smooth, impervious, easily cleanable surfaces where sanitation demands them.

questions.explanation: Approved fixtures, maker's instructions, code installation: three authorities, no substitutions.

questions.question: How would an experienced Colorado master plumber best explain the Colorado Fuel Gas Code?

answers.text: Colorado's fuel gas rules are the Colorado Fuel Gas Code: the Board's adoption of the 2021 International Fuel Gas Code chapters and appendices, with exceptions, together with the fuel gas chapters of the 2021 residential code — the minimum standards for fuel gas piping and systems statewide.
Colorado uses the Uniform Plumbing Code for all fuel gas work.
Bonding is the electrician's concern alone, never verified by the plumber.
Leaders are sized by their height.

questions.explanation: One code for gas as for water: the IFGC as Colorado adopted it, plus the residential fuel gas chapters.

questions.question: An apprentice is unsure about journeyworker plumber experience requirement. Which statement should the master plumber confirm?

answers.text: The journeyworker license requires two years, or 3,400 hours, like the residential license.
The journeyworker license requires five full-time years, or 8,500 hours.
The maximum experience the Board requires for a journeyworker license is four years, or 6,800 hours, of practical experience.
The journeyworker license requires ten years, or 17,000 hours, of experience.

questions.explanation: Four years and 6,800 hours caps the journeyworker requirement — the Board's own word for it is maximum.

questions.question: On a commercial service call in Colorado, the topic of the affidavit of experience comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Examination applicants verify their plumbing installation experience with an Affidavit of Experience form submitted from current and former employers who are plumbing contractors.
Incomplete applications are retained for five years at no charge.
Military plumbing service counts month-for-month without any cap.
Applicants verify experience with a notarized statement they write and sign themselves.

questions.explanation: The affidavit comes from the employing contractors — the people who supervised the work being claimed.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers minimum slope for small horizontal drains. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Horizontal drainage piping of 2 inches and smaller must be installed with a uniform slope of not less than one-quarter inch per foot toward the direction of flow.
Small drains may slope back toward the fixture if a trap is installed.
Small drains require one inch of slope per foot to stay clean.
The building sewer is any pipe the owner calls a sewer, regardless of location.

questions.explanation: A quarter inch per foot is the floor for small drains — enough velocity to carry solids without outrunning the liquid.

questions.question: A licensed Colorado master plumber asks a journeyworker, the topic of the responsible master rule comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Any journeyworker may serve as the responsible supervisor for a contractor.
Contractors without a master may supervise their own work for one year.
The responsible master may be a part-time consultant.

To act as a plumbing contractor, the organization must either be a master plumber itself or employ full-time a master plumber who is in charge of the supervision of all plumbing work the contractor performs.

questions.explanation: Full-time, in charge of all the work: the responsible master is the contractor's license made flesh.

questions.question: A test column on a Colorado job stands 24 feet tall. At 0.433 psi per foot of head, what psi presses at the bottom?
questions.explanation: Pressure = 24 x 0.433 = 10.39 psi.

questions.question: A licensed Colorado master plumber asks a journeyworker, the topic of slope for a four-inch building drain comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A 4-inch drain must be installed dead level to slow the flow.
A 4-inch horizontal building drain may be installed at a slope of one-eighth inch per foot, the standard grade for mid-size drainage piping.
A 4-inch drain must slope one-half inch per foot in all cases.
A 4-inch drain requires two inches of slope per foot.

questions.explanation: Mid-size drains run at an eighth inch per foot; larger diameter carries the load at a gentler grade.

questions.question: A drain of 2 inches or smaller in a Colorado building falls 1/4 inch per foot along a run of 96 feet. Compute the total drop in inches.
questions.explanation: Drop = 96 x 0.25 = 24 inches.

questions.question: A Colorado tempering mix blends 38 gallons at 136 degrees F with 18 gallons at 60 degrees F. Find the resulting temperature in degrees F.

maryland-master-plumber-gas-fitter.quiz_title: Maryland Master Plumber/Gas Fitter Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures the experienced-master track for Baltimore County and WSSC holders?

answers.text: Local-system holders transfer to the state master license automatically.
Public works accept any state's plumbing license.

A Baltimore County or WSSC journey holder applying toward the master paper certifies 7,500 hours under a master licensed by written examination plus 3,750 hours worked as a licensed master over two years since receiving the home master license.
Experimental items come with extra time on the master paper.

questions.explanation: The local track is an experienced-master track: both hour legs are certified, not waived.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the master's drainage design duty before rough-in?

answers.text: Design verification happens at final inspection only.
Drainage design needs no review if the materials are already bought.
The journey crew sizes drainage by habit without master review.
The directing master verifies the drainage design — sizes, grades, venting, and cleanout access — before rough-in begins, because corrections after concealment fall on the master's license.

questions.explanation: The master designs and checks first; the crew builds to the checked design.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the master's response to a back-graded building drain?

answers.text: A building drain found back-graded is rejected on the master's review and re-laid to grade before cover — a directing master does not sign off on reverse fall.
Back-graded drains are noted and left for the owner.
A back grade corrects itself once flow begins.
A back grade is acceptable if the drain is oversized.

questions.explanation: Re-lay it. Reverse fall is a reject, never a sign-off.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the master's materials approval duty?

answers.text: Unmarked pipe may be used where it will be buried.
The master approves every material that enters a Maryland system against the adopted code's lists and the product's listing — a bargain pipe without the right marking never reaches the trench.
Price is the master's primary materials criterion.
A supplier's assurance replaces a product listing.

questions.explanation: Listed, marked, approved — the master gates materials before the job does.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the references a Maryland master candidate brings?

answers.text: Master candidates use a master-only code edition from a different year.
Only 1,875 journey hours are required for the master grade.

The master candidate's shelf mirrors the journey shelf: the 2018 plumbing code, the 2018 fuel gas code, a plumbing mathematics text, any standard backflow text, and the federal construction safety standards.
Loose paper inserts may tab the master candidate's code book.

questions.explanation: Same published shelf at both grades — the master paper tests deeper use of it.

questions.question: For safe, code-compliant Maryland master practice, which statement about the master examination's book rule holds true?

answers.text: The master examination is open book: candidates bring their own unmarked code and reference books under the same rules as the journey paper.
Natural gas fitter credentials are grades of the plumbing inspector card.
Master candidates may bring any book including study guides.
The testing center lends master candidates a shared set of books.

questions.explanation: Open book at both grades — bring your own, unmarked, no study guides.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the Maryland vent stack a master must recognize on plans is handled at master level.

answers.text: Grease is the health department's problem, not the design's.

In Maryland a vent stack is a pressure-relief device at the base of an individual drain stack serving five or more branch intervals — the master reads the term with the Maryland meaning, not the generic one.
The Maryland vent stack definition matches the generic vent-pipe meaning exactly.
Maryland abolished vent stacks in its code.

questions.explanation: Five or more branch intervals, pressure relief at the base — Maryland's own definition.

questions.question: How would an experienced Maryland master plumber best explain the master's gas design responsibility in Maryland?

answers.text: A generator's starting surge needs no pressure consideration.
Both openings belong at the ceiling.

Because gas carries 40 of the master paper's 100 items and the gravest hazards in the trade, the directing master owns the gas design: sizing, materials, venting, combustion air, and testing, all proven before an appliance fires.
Gas design may be left to the appliance supplier.

questions.explanation: Forty items and the highest stakes — gas design is master work.

questions.question: Which description of the master's cross-connection duty at design matches accepted Maryland master practice?

answers.text: A check valve anywhere in the building protects every hazard.

Every water design the master signs is screened for cross-connections: wherever potable water meets a hazard, the design names the protection — air gap, reduced-pressure assembly, or the device the hazard's degree requires.
Hazards are the fixture manufacturer's concern, not the design's.
The below-grade bar applies only to drainage.

questions.explanation: Screen at design, protect by degree — the master's first water duty.

questions.question: Which description of the master's grease interceptor sizing duty matches accepted Maryland master practice?

answers.text: A lab system may be signed with neutralization pending.
The master sizes a grease interceptor from the connected fixtures' flow and the retention the separation needs — an undersized interceptor passes grease to the sewer and the bill to the owner.
Any interceptor passes if the water runs clear on day one.
Retention time is irrelevant to grease separation.

questions.explanation: Flow plus retention — separation is a sizing calculation.

questions.question: Which description of the master's fixture approval standard matches accepted Maryland master practice?

answers.text: Yard hydrants need no protection review.
Flow rate is a marketing figure with no code standing.
Unlisted fixtures may be installed where the owner insists.
Fixtures enter the master's design on their listings and their code compliance — flow rates, backflow provisions, and trap compatibility — not on a showroom photograph.

questions.explanation: Listed and compliant, then beautiful — in that order.

questions.question: How would an experienced Maryland master plumber best explain the master's insured-to-contract status?

answers.text: The certificate holder is the testing vendor.
Any licensee may contract; insurance is a formality recorded later.
A Maryland licensee's record shows one of two postures — not insured, or insured to contract — and only the insured-to-contract licensee may contract for plumbing work in their own or another's name.
Scope assignments are exempt from audit.

questions.explanation: Status first, signature second — contracting follows the insurance record.

questions.question: On the master written examination, a question covers the tab rule on a master candidate's books. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Only permanent self-adhesive plastic tabs may mark a master candidate's books; removable flags are unacceptable and any tab a proctor can lift without tearing the page comes off.
Loose paper inserts may tab the master candidate's code book.
Tabs of any kind are banned on the master examination.
Paper flags are preferred on the master paper.

questions.explanation: Permanent tabs only — the rule does not soften at the master grade.

questions.question: On the master written examination, a question covers grade for smaller drainage piping the master lays out. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Drainage piping two and one-half inches and smaller is laid out at one-quarter inch of fall per foot so solids move with the liquid stream.
Smaller drainage is laid out at one inch per foot for speed.
Grade for small drainage is whatever the trench allows.
Existing drains are assumed adequate for any added load.

questions.explanation: Quarter-inch per foot for the small sizes — the master's layout standard.

questions.question: A drain of two and one-half inches or smaller in a Maryland building falls 1/4 inch per foot along a run of 36 feet. Compute the total drop in inches.
questions.explanation: Drop = 36 x 0.25 = 9 inches.

questions.question: Two fittings on a Maryland run sit 55 inches apart center to center, and their take-outs total 8 inches. How long is the piece to cut, in inches?
questions.explanation: Cut length = 55 - 8 = 47 inches.

questions.question: On the master written examination, a question covers the verification letter for the 11,250 out-of-state hours. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: A journey licensee directs apprentices independently of any master.
A photocopied license satisfies the verification-letter rule.
Master candidates may substitute a manufacturer's catalog for the fuel gas code.

The out-of-state master applicant files an original letter of verification that all 11,250 required hours were worked under a licensed master whose own license was obtained by passing a written competency examination.

questions.explanation: Original letter, full 11,250 hours, supervising master licensed by written examination.

questions.question: On a commercial service call under a Maryland master, the topic of the one master-outline area the journey paper lacks comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The master outline adds a Special Topics area of three items that the journey outline does not carry — the only content area unique to the master paper.
The master examination is an untimed practical only.
The master outline adds a second mathematics area.
A photocopied license satisfies the verification-letter rule.

questions.explanation: Special Topics, three items — the master paper's signature addition.

questions.question: A Maryland journey licensee asks the directing master, the topic of grade for mid-size drainage piping the master lays out comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Mid-size drainage grade is set by the fixture count alone.
Mid-size drainage piping in the three-to-eight-inch range is laid out at one-eighth inch of fall per foot under the adopted drainage table.
Mid-size drainage may be laid back-graded toward fixtures.
Mid-size drainage requires one-half inch per foot.

questions.explanation: Eighth-inch per foot for the mid sizes — checked on the master's grade layout.

questions.question: When signing off work against the Maryland State Plumbing Code, which statement about the Maryland master examination's item count and time is right?

answers.text: The Master Plumber/Gas Fitter examination carries 100 questions with 240 minutes allowed — the same size and clock as the journey paper.
The master examination carries 80 questions in 180 minutes.
The master examination is an untimed practical only.
The master examination carries 150 questions in 300 minutes.

questions.explanation: 100 items, 240 minutes — master and journey papers share the format.

arkansas-master-plumber.quiz_title: Arkansas Master Plumber Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures the journeyman holding year before the Arkansas master examination?

answers.text: A license transfers to a spouse automatically.
Both vents and drains are drawn in black pencil only.
A person who obtains an Arkansas Journeyman Plumber License must hold that license for one full year before becoming eligible for the master plumber examination.
A new journeyman may sit for the master examination the next month.

questions.explanation: One full year licensed as a journeyman stands between the two examinations.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes what an isometric DWV riser diagram shows a master reviewer?

answers.text: An isometric shows only the building's front elevation.
An isometric hides pipe sizes by design.
An isometric is a materials price list in drawing form.

An isometric riser diagram shows the drainage and vent piping in three-dimensional relationship — stacks, branches, vents, and fixture connections — so sizes, slopes, and vent paths can be checked from one drawing.

questions.explanation: One drawing, whole system in relief — the master's review tool.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding the slope a master checks first on a horizontal drain in the drawing?

answers.text: A master reviewing the riser checks that horizontal drainage is drawn to fall at the code grade for its size — drainage moves by gravity, and a flat or back-pitched run in the drawing becomes a clogged run in the wall.
Horizontal drains are drawn level for appearance.
Slope matters only on the building sewer.
Drainage slope is optional if the pipe is oversized.

questions.explanation: Gravity is the pump: the drawing's fall is the system's future performance.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the longest length method's core measurement?

answers.text: Lengths are averaged across the system.
Each segment is sized by its own length alone.
The shortest run sets the size for all segments.

The longest length method sizes every gas piping segment using the length of the longest run from the meter or regulator to the farthest appliance, so the farthest appliance still receives its required pressure.

questions.explanation: Size the whole tree by its longest branch — the farthest burner is the design case.

questions.question: How would an experienced Arkansas master plumber best explain the P-trap's working principle?

answers.text: Pump at total capacity.
Full-bore slugs improve separation.
A P-trap holds a standing water seal in its U-bend between the fixture and the drainage system, passing waste while blocking sewer gas — the seal, not the pipe shape alone, is the protection.
A P-trap filters solids from waste.

questions.explanation: Water standing in the bend is the barrier — shape serves the seal.

questions.question: A journeyman asks about the minimum experience for the Arkansas journeyman examination. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: An applicant for the Arkansas journeyman plumber examination must have a minimum of four years of experience or its equivalent.
No minimum experience applies to the master examination.
The journeyman examination requires six years of experience.
The journeyman examination has no experience floor.

questions.explanation: Four years or equivalent for journeyman; five for master.

questions.question: How would an experienced Arkansas master plumber best explain what a current Arkansas journeyman files for experience proof?

answers.text: Fixture spacing is never tested.
A current journeyman files only a photograph of the license.
A current journeyman files no work history at all.
A current Arkansas journeyman applying for the master examination need only provide work history for the length of their journeymanship.

questions.explanation: Journeymanship-length history suffices for the in-state journeyman — the earlier record already stands.

questions.question: In a master examination review, which statement about why the Arkansas drawing separates vents and drains by color earns credit?

answers.text: Colors are decorative and carry no meaning.
Vent connection height is cosmetic.
A stack is the horizontal run under the slab.
Coloring vents blue and drains red lets the grader — and later the crew — follow each system's path through the riser without confusing a vent for a drain at a shared stack.

questions.explanation: Blue vent, red drain: two systems, instantly separable on the page.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the minimum fall for small horizontal drainage piping is handled at master level.

answers.text: Candidates draw any building they prefer.
Horizontal drainage piping of two and one-half inches and smaller is laid at a minimum fall of one-quarter inch per foot under the adopted plumbing code.
Small drainage falls one-sixteenth inch per foot.
Small drainage falls one inch per foot minimum.

questions.explanation: Quarter-inch per foot for the small sizes — the classic drainage grade.

questions.question: Which description of the purpose of venting, stated at master level matches accepted Arkansas master practice?

answers.text: Existing lines are assumed sound.
Venting is a water-supply function.
Venting increases drainage velocity.
Venting protects trap seals by keeping drainage-system air pressure near atmospheric, so discharge momentum neither siphons a seal out nor blows sewer gas back through it.

questions.explanation: Pressure balance is seal protection — the vent's whole job.

questions.question: How would an experienced Arkansas master plumber best explain copper's joining methods a master commands?

answers.text: Copper water tube is joined by soldering, brazing, press fittings, or listed mechanical joints — each with its own temperature, flux, and preparation discipline the master enforces on the crew.
Tools calibrate themselves.
Bins sort themselves.
Copper is joined with solvent cement.

questions.explanation: Solder, braze, press, mechanical — matched to duty and done by the book.

questions.question: How would an experienced Arkansas master plumber best explain the water closet's rough-in dimensions a master verifies?

answers.text: Before a closet is set, the master verifies the rough-in: flange position from the finished wall, water supply location, and the clearances the code's spacing rules demand — errors here are discovered by the bowl, expensively.
Rough-in is checked after the bowl is set.
Grates sit proud for visibility.
Removing aerators improves efficiency.

questions.explanation: Measure the rough-in before the fixture arrives — bowls do not forgive.

questions.question: When signing off work against the Arkansas codes, which statement about the hardship exception to the Arkansas one-year holding rule is right?

answers.text: In cases of extreme hardship, the Committee of Plumbing Examiners may waive the one-year journeyman holding requirement in whole or in part.
The one-year rule is waived whenever the fee is doubled.
Any employer letter automatically waives the one-year rule.
The one-year rule can never be waived for any reason.

questions.explanation: Extreme hardship only, Committee's call, in whole or in part.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how the professional-engineer route to the Arkansas master examination is handled at master level.

answers.text: The Committee may consider applicants for the master plumber examination who are registered professional engineers with special expertise in plumbing engineering.
Engineers are barred from the master examination.
Only a nickname and email are required.
A new journeyman may sit for the master examination the next month.

questions.explanation: Registered professional engineer plus plumbing-engineering expertise — a consideration route, not an automatic license.

questions.question: For safe, code-compliant Arkansas master practice, which statement about how an Arkansas master applicant proves the five years holds true?

answers.text: Experience is proven with documentation submitted with the application: records, affidavits, bona fide evidence from licensing agencies, or qualified former employers who can attest to the work background.
Documentation may be mailed separately months after the application.
Only a college diploma can prove plumbing experience.
Re-examination after a failure is free.

questions.explanation: Paper proof travels with the application — records, affidavits, agency or employer evidence.

questions.question: On the master examination, a question covers what an out-of-state Arkansas master applicant adds. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: An out-of-state application must include a completed Verification of License Form or its equivalent, alongside the experience documentation.
Out-of-state applicants file only a resume.
Out-of-state applicants skip license verification.
Out-of-state verification is handled after licensure.

questions.explanation: Verification of the home license is part of the out-of-state file, not an afterthought.

questions.question: How would an experienced Arkansas master plumber best explain what the code's water-sizing appendix method is designed to deliver?

answers.text: Sizing assumes all fixtures run continuously.
Surveys are new-construction only.

Water sizing by the code's appendix method delivers each fixture's needed flow at adequate residual pressure during the building's probable peak demand — not every fixture at once, and not a trickle at the far end.
Hose bibbs need RP assemblies indoors.

questions.explanation: Probable peak, adequate pressure — the appendix method's promise.

questions.question: On a commercial service call under an Arkansas master, the topic of the affidavit rule for an unlicensed Arkansas applicant comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: An applicant who is not enrolled in the Arkansas apprenticeship program files affidavits from current or former employers attesting to the plumbing and gas fitting background — notarized and on company letterhead — and only legal work history is considered.
The master license is free after the first year.
Unnotarized notes from coworkers prove an unlicensed applicant's history.
Candidates may work two sections simultaneously.

questions.explanation: Notarized, on letterhead, legal history only — the unlicensed route is documented, not casual.

questions.question: An Arkansas journeyman asks the superintending master, the topic of what a size-change notation on a riser tells the installer comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Notations mark only the stack base.
A size-change notation marks exactly where the piping changes diameter along the run, so the installer orders and sets the right fittings at the right point.
Notations record the pipe's color.
Size changes are left to the installer's preference.

questions.explanation: The notation is the instruction: here the diameter changes.

questions.question: A drain of two and one-half inches or smaller in an Arkansas building falls 1/4 inch per foot along a run of 80 feet. Compute the total drop in inches.
questions.explanation: Drop = 80 x 0.25 = 20 inches.

uscg-lifeboatman.quiz_title: USCG Lifeboatman Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures what the lifeboat operator fulfils aboard?

answers.text: A lifeboat counts as a survival craft only when it is motor driven.
Only a center examination counts, even after an approved course is passed.
A Lifeboat Operator is the person who fulfils the manning requirement as lifeboat operator aboard the vessel.
A Lifeboat Operator is a passenger assigned to count lifejackets during drills.

questions.explanation: The endorsement exists because the vessel's manning calls for a qualified person in that role.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes rocket parachute flare height and color?

answers.text: A rocket parachute flare sinks in the water and burns orange under the surface.
A rocket parachute flare rises a few feet and burns white for cooking light.
A rocket parachute flare stays low, burns green, and is seen only at close range.
A rocket parachute flare rises high, burns red, and can be seen for miles.

questions.explanation: Height and a bright red parachute-suspended light give this signal the range to reach distant ships and aircraft.

questions.question: Which statement best captures general rule for unrigged vessels?

answers.text: Unrigged vessels require the full endorsement from every deck hand aboard.
Every person on an unrigged vessel must hold a lifeboat endorsement.
The unrigged vessel rule was removed and no longer applies to anyone.
As a general rule, no lifeboat endorsement is required of a person employed on an unrigged vessel.

questions.explanation: Unrigged vessels are the general exception to the endorsement requirement.

questions.question: Regarding vessels that call for the limited endorsement, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Lifeboat Operator-Limited serves only vessels that carry free-fall lifeboats.
Lifeboat Operator-Limited serves vessels that carry neither liferafts nor any other lifesaving gear.
Lifeboat Operator-Limited serves vessels that carry lifeboats but no liferafts.
Lifeboat Operator-Limited serves vessels that are fitted with liferafts but are not fitted with lifeboats.

questions.explanation: The limited scope follows the vessel's outfit, which has rafts and no lifeboats.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes limited holder charge of a liferaft?

answers.text: Lifeboat Operator-Limited has always carried exactly that printed title.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may watch a liferaft but never take charge of one.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may take charge of a liferaft.
Able Seafarer qualification replaces the lifeboat endorsement entirely.

questions.explanation: Taking charge of a liferaft is central to the limited role.

questions.question: A trainee asks about everyday name still used for the endorsement. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Mariners and industry still commonly call the Lifeboat Operator endorsement lifeboatman in everyday speech.
Using the word lifeboatman now refers to a completely different rating.
Certificated persons are assigned to boats only to complete paperwork after drills.
Only retired mariners are permitted to use the word lifeboatman.

questions.explanation: The old word remains the familiar spoken name even though the printed title changed.

questions.question: Which description of minimum age for the lifeboat family matches accepted survival-craft practice?

answers.text: The minimum age is 21 for every endorsement in the lifeboat family.
The minimum age is 18 for Lifeboat Operator, Lifeboat Operator-Limited, Proficiency in Survival Craft, and Proficiency in Survival Craft-Limited.
The limited examination pass mark is 100 percent on a practical test only.
There is no minimum age if the applicant has completed an approved course.

questions.explanation: One age floor of 18 covers all four endorsements in the family.

questions.question: On a course assessment, a question covers prescribed medical examination. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: An applicant must pass the prescribed physical and medical examination for the endorsement.
Citizenship is never checked for rating endorsements of any kind.
Only applicants over 40 need a medical examination for this endorsement.
A sports physical from any school satisfies the prescribed examination automatically.

questions.explanation: Medical fitness is examined, not assumed, before issuance.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how drug test timing and first endorsement is handled in practice.

answers.text: Taking charge is demonstrated only by a written essay about leadership.
Drug testing compliance must fall within 6 months, and the test is required for the first Lifeboat Operator endorsement unless the applicant is also renewing.
A mariner renewing nothing still never needs drug test evidence for a first endorsement.
The drug test is required only at the second renewal of the endorsement.

questions.explanation: Fresh compliance within 6 months is what the first endorsement calls for.

questions.question: How would an experienced boat commander best explain totally enclosed lifeboat protection?

answers.text: Signaling gear in a lifeboat is stowed ashore and brought down at abandonment.
Buoyancy tanks are removed whenever the boat is loaded to full capacity.
A totally enclosed lifeboat surrounds its occupants with a rigid cover that shields them from exposure and from water shipped aboard.
A totally enclosed lifeboat has no cover over its occupants at all.

questions.explanation: A rigid full enclosure is what sets the totally enclosed boat apart from open and partially enclosed designs.

questions.question: Which description of gravity davits operation matches accepted survival-craft practice?

answers.text: On gravity davits the lifeboat floats off its cradle when the deck floods.
On gravity davits the lifeboat moves down inclined skids or tracks by its own weight once the brake is released.
Tricing pendants secure the boat in its stowed position for a voyage.
On gravity davits the lifeboat is lifted outboard by a crane before lowering.

questions.explanation: Gravity does the launching work on this davit type, controlled by the brake.

questions.question: How would an experienced boat commander best explain engine starting checks for fuel?

answers.text: Trail oars orders the crew to throw the oar looms inboard and sleep.
Oar handling knowledge is not examined at all for the endorsement.
Before starting a lifeboat engine the crew checks that fuel is available and the fuel supply is open to the engine.
Before starting a lifeboat engine the crew drains the fuel tank to check its color.

questions.explanation: A starved engine will not start, so fuel state and supply come first.

questions.question: On a course assessment, a question covers limited holder charge of other apparatus. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may take charge of other lifesaving apparatus besides a rescue boat or liferaft.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder is limited to paperwork about lifesaving apparatus.
A Lifeboat Operator-Limited holder may touch no apparatus beyond a single named raft.
Other lifesaving apparatus may be handled only by unlicensed crew members.

questions.explanation: The limited charge extends to other lifesaving apparatus, not just rafts and rescue boats.

questions.question: A boat commander briefs the boat crew, the topic of valid medical certificate held comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: An expired Medical Certificate is acceptable if renewal papers were mailed.
An applicant must hold a valid Medical Certificate when qualifying for the endorsement.
The Medical Certificate is needed only after the endorsement is issued.
A first aid card substitutes for the Medical Certificate.

questions.explanation: A current Medical Certificate is part of a complete application.

questions.question: When checking boat work against the lifeboat requirements, which statement about evidence of a passed drug test is right?

answers.text: A letter from an employer saying the applicant seems reliable replaces the drug test.
An applicant must provide evidence of having passed a chemical test for dangerous drugs or of qualifying for an exemption from that test.
The first topic area covers radio watchkeeping procedures.
STCW assessments may be signed by any shipmate who watched the task.

questions.explanation: Passed test evidence, or a genuine exemption, is the standard.

questions.question: Which description of securing the painter before a manual liferaft launch matches accepted survival-craft practice?

answers.text: A rescue boat tows liferafts at full speed to reach shore quickly.
The painter is secured to a fixed object on the ship before the raft container is thrown overboard.
The painter is tied to a movable item of deck cargo before launch.
The painter is cut free before the raft container leaves the ship.

questions.explanation: Securing the painter first keeps the inflating raft under control and prevents it from drifting away from the ship.

questions.question: A lifeboat is approved for 45 persons and its water outfit is 3 litres per person. How many litres of water does the outfit total?
questions.explanation: Water = 45 x 3 = 135 litres.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes first action to clear the ship after boarding?

answers.text: The craft waits alongside so survivors can return aboard for forgotten gear.
Once boarding is complete, the survival craft is cut or slipped clear of the ship without delay.
The craft stays tied alongside until the ship has fully settled in the water.
The craft is paddled clear only after the sea anchor has been streamed.

questions.explanation: Getting clear quickly removes the danger of being dragged down, struck by debris, or fouled on the sinking ship.

questions.question: A motor lifeboat carries 132 litres of fuel and its engine burns 11 litres per hour at cruising speed. How many hours can it run on that fuel?
questions.explanation: Endurance = 132 / 11 = 12 hours.

questions.question: A PSC holder renewing by sea service has 290 days within the last 5 years toward the 360 days that evidence continued competence. How many days remain?
questions.explanation: Remaining = 360 - 290 = 70 days.

ampp-cip1.quiz_title: AMPP Certified Coating Inspector Level 1 Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures supervision required in a shop setting?

answers.text: In a shop setting a Basic Coatings Inspector works entirely without supervision.
Total seat time for the theory exam is 90 minutes.
In a shop setting a Basic Coatings Inspector works under the supervision of a Level 2 or a Level 3 inspector.
A Basic Coatings Inspector certifies pressure vessels for service.

questions.explanation: Shop work at Level 1 is supervised by a Certified or Senior inspector.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding confined space hazard awareness?

answers.text: Confined spaces can hold oxygen-deficient, toxic, or flammable atmospheres and require controlled entry procedures.
A confined space is any room with a closed door.
Confined space rules apply only to underground mines.
Confined spaces are safe whenever a ladder is present.

questions.explanation: Atmosphere and entry control are why confined spaces get special procedures.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes work experience required before the course?

answers.text: There is no level above Basic in the coating inspector family.
Two years of coating inspection experience is required before the course.
No prior work experience is required before taking the CIP Level 1 course.
Total seat time for the theory exam is 5 hours.

questions.explanation: Experience is a renewal requirement, not an entry requirement at Level 1.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the purpose of a safety data sheet?

answers.text: A safety data sheet replaces the product data sheet for application values.
A safety data sheet is the inspector's daily production log.
A safety data sheet is the coating's color chart and gloss record.
A safety data sheet communicates a chemical product's hazards, handling, storage, and emergency measures.

questions.explanation: The SDS is the hazard-communication document for the product.

questions.question: In an examination review, which statement about what HazCom requires earns credit?

answers.text: Hazard communication requires workers to memorize every product formula.
Old coatings may be dry-blasted into the open air without controls.
Welding fumes from coatings are harmless by default.
Hazard communication requires that chemical hazards be identified and communicated through labels and safety data sheets.

questions.explanation: Labels and SDSs are the backbone of hazard communication.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how checking the atmosphere before entry is handled in practice.

answers.text: A single test a week before entry covers the whole job.
The atmosphere of a confined space is tested before and during entry for oxygen, flammables, and toxics.
Atmosphere testing is needed only after work finishes.
Fall protection is needed only above one hundred feet.

questions.explanation: Testing precedes entry and continues while people are inside.

questions.question: How would an experienced coatings inspector best explain the purpose of coating inspection?

answers.text: Visual inspection is unnecessary where instruments are available.
Inspection exists to slow the contractor's production down.
Inspection verifies that surface preparation and coating application meet the specification so the system can deliver its intended service life.
A Level 1 inspector may cut the film anywhere at any time.

questions.explanation: Inspection is verification against the specification, aimed at service life.

questions.question: Which description of the definition of corrosion matches accepted coating inspection practice?

answers.text: Corrosion is damage caused only by mechanical impact or abrasion.
Corrosion is the deterioration of a material, usually a metal, by chemical or electrochemical reaction with its environment.
Temperature has no effect on the speed of any corrosion reaction.
Corrosion is a protective film that a metal forms to stop all deterioration.

questions.explanation: Corrosion is an environmental reaction process, not purely mechanical wear or a protective treatment.

questions.question: Which description of the meaning of dew point matches accepted coating inspection practice?

answers.text: The wet bulb should be read only once, several minutes after whirling stops.
Dew point is the difference between wet-bulb and dry-bulb thermometer readings.
Dew point is the highest temperature recorded on a surface during a sunny day.
Dew point is the temperature at which air becomes saturated and water vapor begins to condense into liquid.

questions.explanation: Condensation begins when saturated air is cooled to its dew point, so that temperature marks the condensation threshold.

questions.question: How would an experienced coatings inspector best explain why surface preparation matters for adhesion?

answers.text: Proper surface preparation creates a clean surface that allows the coating to bond tightly to the substrate.
Poor surface preparation extends coating life by trapping moisture under the film.
Solvent cleaning is carried out by soaking steel in water until oil floats away.
Surface preparation matters only because it makes steel look brighter before coating.

questions.explanation: A clean, sound surface is the foundation for coating adhesion.

questions.question: Which description of what surface profile is matches accepted coating inspection practice?

answers.text: Light flash rust means the steel has rusted through its full thickness.
Surface profile is the color change that blasting leaves on the steel.
Surface profile is the thickness of rust removed from the steel in total.
Surface profile is the pattern of peaks and valleys left on steel by abrasive blasting or other preparation, measured from peak to valley.

questions.explanation: Profile describes the anchor pattern texture, not gloss, rust loss, or color.

questions.question: How would an experienced coatings inspector best explain the purpose of the inspector's log book?

answers.text: The daily report records materials ordered for future projects instead of materials used that day.
A non-conformance report records praise for work that exceeded the specification.
The inspector's log book provides a chronological and permanent record of daily activities, observations, and decisions made during the project.
The inspector's log book is a private diary that is never shared with anyone on the project.

questions.explanation: A log book preserves what happened each day so the work can be reviewed and traced later.

questions.question: Which of these statements about education required to enter the pathway would a senior coatings inspector agree with?

answers.text: A bachelor's degree in engineering is required to enter the pathway.
Approval is granted by the course instructor on the final day.
A Level 1 candidate is expected to know nothing before the exam by design.
No education requirement is published for entering the CIP Level 1 pathway.

questions.explanation: Entry to Level 1 carries no published education gate.

questions.question: On a written examination, a question covers the first course required for certification. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Certification requires successful completion of the CIP Level 1 Course.
Certification requires the Level 2 course taken before Level 1.
Certification requires only a self-study reading of the course manual.
Certification requires a manufacturer's product course instead of CIP Level 1.

questions.explanation: The CIP Level 1 Course is a named certification requirement.

questions.question: On a shop walkdown of coated steel, the topic of the ethics course requirement comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Certification requires the Ethics for the Corrosion Professional Course or an equivalent training.
References to NACE CIP Level 1 describe a program that was cancelled with no successor.
Certification requires a law degree module on contract ethics.
The course purchase includes a lifetime AMPP membership.

questions.explanation: An ethics course (or equivalent) is one of the two required courses.

questions.question: Which description of the function of the binder or resin in a coating matches accepted coating inspection practice?

answers.text: The binder or resin exists only to thin the coating so it can be sprayed.
The binder or resin forms the continuous film, holds the other constituents together, and provides adhesion to the substrate.
The binder or resin provides color and hiding power while the pigment holds the film together.
A moisture-cure coating cures only by being baked in an oven with completely dry air.

questions.explanation: The binder is the film former that binds pigment and additives into an adherent, continuous coating.

questions.question: A coating is applied at a wet film thickness of 6 mils and has a volume solids of 60 percent. Compute the resulting dry film thickness in mils.
An experienced coatings inspector explains a point to a trainee, the topic of the inspector's personal safety responsibility comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Safety is solely the responsibility of the site owner.
Every inspector bears personal responsibility for working safely and stopping to address an unsafe condition.
Personal responsibility ends once a safety talk has been attended.
An inspector may ignore unsafe conditions outside the coating area.

questions.explanation: Personal responsibility is an explicit element of the safety domain.

questions.question: At a work check the steel surface temperature is 88 degrees Fahrenheit and the dew point is 66 degrees Fahrenheit. Compute how many degrees the surface is above the dew point.
questions.explanation: Margin = 88 - 66 = 22 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.question: An area average measures 9.9 mils against a specified 9 mils dry film thickness. Compute by what percent the measured average exceeds the specification.
questions.explanation: Percent over = (9.9 - 9) / 9 x 100 = 10 percent.

wonderlic.quiz_title: Wonderlic Cognitive Ability Test Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What position is the letter O in the alphabet?
questions.explanation: O is letter number 15 in the alphabet, counting A as number 1.

questions.question: mountain is to valley as peak is to:

answers.text: trail
base
slope
rock

questions.explanation: The relation is 'high to low pair': mountain relates to valley the same way peak relates to base.

questions.question: 40% of 40 equals:
questions.explanation: Convert the percent to a fraction of 100: 40% of 40 = 40 × 40/100 = 16.

questions.question: What position is the letter U in the alphabet?
questions.explanation: U is letter number 21 in the alphabet, counting A as number 1.

questions.question: KEEN is most nearly the same in meaning as:

answers.text: calm
sharp
eager
reluctant

questions.explanation: The word most nearly the same in meaning as 'keen' is 'eager'.

questions.question: What does the proverb "A watched pot never boils" mean?

answers.text: Patience cooks food better
Watching a pot is dangerous
Time seems to pass slowly when you wait anxiously
Pots boil faster when covered

questions.explanation: The proverb means: time seems to pass slowly when you wait anxiously

questions.question: Which of these numbers is the largest? 0.75, 0.045, 0.8, 0.3
A ribbon costs $52.38 and a spool costs $15.72. What is the total cost?
questions.explanation: Add the two prices column by column: $52.38 + $15.72 = $68.10.

questions.question: What number comes next in the series? 18, 28, 46, 74, 120, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 74 + 120 = 194.

questions.question: Which number does not belong with the others? 84, 39, 30, 37
questions.explanation: 84, 39, 30 are all multiples of 3; 37 is not.

questions.question: Which number completes the series 9, 68, 13, 66, 17, 64, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: one rises by 4 each time it appears (9, 13, 17, ...) while the other starts at 68; the next term belongs to the first series, so it is 21.

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly opposite to poverty:

answers.text: debt
hardship
misery
wealth

questions.explanation: Of the options, only 'wealth' runs against the meaning of 'poverty', so it is the opposite.

questions.question: Follow the instructions: Start with 20. Then double it, then double it, then subtract 1. What is the final number?
questions.explanation: Step by step from 20: applying double it, double it, subtract 1 gives 79.

questions.question: Sam, a technician, sees a small puddle of water on the floor of a busy walkway. What is the best course of action?

answers.text: Wait for the cleaning staff at the end of the week
Wipe it up or place a warning sign and report it
Step over it and continue working
Tell customers to walk around it without marking it

questions.explanation: For Sam, working as a technician, the responsible action is to wipe it up or place a warning sign and report it; the other choices ignore the problem, conceal it, or act without checking.

questions.question: Which choice arranges the words into a proper sentence? Scrambled: glided across the marsh at dawn the heron

answers.text: The heron across the marsh glided at dawn the.
At dawn the across marsh heron glided.
The heron glided across the marsh at dawn.
Across the heron glided the marsh at dawn.

questions.explanation: The only grammatically complete arrangement is: The heron glided across the marsh at dawn.

questions.question: In a code where each letter is shifted forward by 2 in the alphabet, BOOK becomes:

answers.text: GTTP
DQQM
ERRN
FSSO

questions.explanation: Shifting each letter of BOOK forward by 2 gives DQQM.

questions.question: How many players from one soccer team are on the field at once (standard)?
questions.explanation: There are 11 players from one soccer team in the field at once (standard).

questions.question: Three of the following belong together. Which one does NOT belong? — Paris, London, Rome, Canada

answers.text: Paris
London
Rome
Canada

questions.explanation: Paris, London, Rome are all European capital cities; Canada is not.

questions.question: A rectangular garden is 25 feet long and 13 feet wide. What is its area in square feet?
questions.explanation: Area = length × width = 25 × 13 = 325 square feet.

questions.question: A packer packs 4 gift boxes per hour. A coworker works 3 times as fast. How many boxes does the coworker assemble in 8 hours?
questions.explanation: A packer packs 4 boxes per hour, so the coworker's rate is 4 × 3 = 12 per hour; in 8 hours: 12 × 8 = 96 boxes.

parapro.quiz_title: ParaPro Assessment Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: An aide asks, while drafting a sports-day summary: Which word has three syllables?

answers.text: apple
dog
cat
banana

questions.explanation: The correct choice is 'banana' — it is the only option that matches the sound pattern asked for; the other words have different vowel or consonant sounds. [Practice variant 3 — Phonics and Decoding.]

questions.question: What is 8.3 + 3.0? (Give the decimal sum.)
questions.explanation: Align decimal points and add: 8.3 + 3.0 = 11.3.

questions.question: If x − 10 = 13, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Add 10 to both sides: x = 13 + 10 = 23. Working the step shown in the question, in order, gives this result.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct? (Grammar check set while writing a pet-care guide page.)

answers.text: Neither the teacher nor the students were late.
Neither the teacher nor the students has been late every days.
Neither the teacher nor the students was being late yesterday tomorrow.
Neither the teacher nor the students is been late.

questions.explanation: The correct sentence is "Neither the teacher nor the students were late." — it follows standard subject–verb agreement, pronoun, and verb-form rules, while each other choice breaks at least one of those rules.

questions.question: Find the median of: 8, 11, 14, 26, 28
questions.explanation: In order, the middle (third) value of the five numbers is 14, which is the median.

questions.question: Sam asks: as used in "A peculiar smell came from the old cabinet." the word "peculiar" means

answers.text: impossible to determine
strange
familiar
pleasant

questions.explanation: In context, "peculiar" means strange — the surrounding details in the sentence point to that meaning, while the other choices contradict or ignore those clues. [Practice variant 3 — Vocabulary in Context.]

questions.question: Read: "Sam set two alarms before his early flight." What can reasonably be inferred?

answers.text: Nothing at all can be inferred from the passage
Sam does not want to oversleep
Sam collects alarm clocks
The flight is at noon

questions.explanation: The details in the passage support the inference that sam does not want to oversleep. The other choices either contradict the details or go far beyond anything the passage suggests.

questions.question: A clock shows a start time, and 4 hours and 40 minutes pass. How many minutes is that in total?
questions.explanation: 4 hours = 240 minutes; adding 40 minutes gives 280 minutes.

questions.question: Aisha helps students find the perimeter of a square tile with sides of 16 cm. What is the perimeter?
questions.explanation: A square has four equal sides: 4 × 16 = 64 cm.

questions.question: A graph of books read by a class shows 17 books in week 1 and 27 books in week 2. Adam asks what trend the graph shows.

answers.text: The graph shows no information about change
Reading stayed exactly the same
Reading increased from week 1 to week 2
Reading decreased from week 1 to week 2

questions.explanation: 27 is greater than 17, so the trend over the two weeks is an increase in reading.

questions.question: A teacher asks Mona to arrange 210 chairs into 15 equal rows. How many chairs go in each row?
questions.explanation: 210 ÷ 15 = 14 chairs per row. Working the step shown in the question, in order, gives this result.

questions.question: An aide asks, in a community-helpers unit: Choose the correct word: You are ___ late to start the test.

answers.text: to
that
too
two

questions.explanation: 'too' is the word that fits the sentence's meaning and grammar; the other choices are sound-alike or look-alike words whose meanings do not fit here.

questions.question: Which sentence needs a comma added? (Choose the correctly punctuated version.) (Punctuation check set in a weather-forecast exercise.)

answers.text: After the rain stopped we went, outside.
After, the rain stopped we went outside.
After the rain, stopped we went outside.
After the rain stopped, we went outside.

questions.explanation: The correct version is "After the rain stopped, we went outside." — its commas, apostrophes, end marks, and capital letters all follow standard written English; each other version misplaces or omits at least one of them. [Practice variant 4 — Punctuation and Capitalization.]

questions.question: In 'The book is on the table', the word 'on' is (Grammar drill set while writing a lunch-menu notice.)

answers.text: a verb
a preposition
an adjective
a conjunction only

questions.explanation: In that sentence the word functions as a preposition — its job in the sentence (naming, acting, describing, or relating) is what determines its part of speech. [Practice variant 2 — Parts of Speech.]

questions.question: What is the verb in 'The soup simmered on the stove all afternoon'? (Sentence drill set while drafting a lost-and-found notice.)

answers.text: simmered
afternoon
it cannot be determined from any sentence
soup

questions.explanation: The answer is 'simmered': a complete sentence needs a subject and a predicate expressing a complete thought, and fragments and run-ons fail that test in opposite ways.

questions.question: A paraprofessional checks a word list during a recycling-campaign activity. Which word is spelled correctly? (Practice variant 2.)

answers.text: all three spellings are equally correct
definately
definitly
definitely

questions.explanation: 'definitely' is the standard spelling; the other forms misplace, double, or drop letters compared with the accepted spelling of the word. [Practice variant 5 — Spelling.]

questions.question: An aide supports a young writer during a recycling-campaign activity. Talking with a partner before writing helps a writer to

answers.text: avoid writing anything at all
generate and clarify ideas to write about
skip the revision stage entirely
hand the student a finished essay to copy

questions.explanation: The supported step is: generate and clarify ideas to write about. Prewriting comes before drafting and is about generating and organizing ideas, not about correctness or copying. [Practice variant 4 — Prewriting and Planning.]

questions.question: Read this passage: 'The school orchard was pruned by volunteers in spring, so the apple trees produced more fruit. Earlier changes had been tried, but this step made the biggest difference.' Which sentence best summarizes the passage?

answers.text: Why the school orchard should be closed next year
A problem that the school orchard caused for visitors
The history of the school orchard since it was founded
The benefit of the change at the school orchard

questions.explanation: The passage centers on one change — the school orchard was pruned by volunteers in spring — and its benefit: the apple trees produced more fruit. The other choices name topics the passage never discusses, so the main idea is the benefit of that change at the school orchard. [Practice variant 3 — Main Idea and Purpose.]

questions.question: In a passage read in a classroom-jobs chart task, a writer states that the public pool's swim team practices before school, competes on Saturday mornings, and welcomes swimmers aged eight to fourteen. According to the passage, which of the following is true of the public pool's swim team? (Reader: Felix)

answers.text: It practices before school
It was founded by Felix
It received a national award last spring
It is the largest of its kind in the state

questions.explanation: The passage states directly that the public pool's swim team practices before school. The other choices add claims — about a founder, an award, or a ranking — that the passage never makes, so only the stated detail is supported.

questions.question: Consider this text, used during a story-writing workshop: "On the left side of the hall hang portraits; on the right, landscapes fill the wall from floor to ceiling." Its main organizational pattern is

answers.text: time order
spatial order
a collection of opinions with no pattern
cause and effect

questions.explanation: The passage's structure is spatial order: its sentences are arranged to show exactly that relationship, which the other labels do not describe. [Practice variant 5 — Organization of a Selection.]

ccat.quiz_title: Criteria Cognitive Aptitude Test (CCAT) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Of the choices, which is the best antonym for VICTORY?

answers.text: ornate
rough
reckless
defeat
precise

questions.explanation: 'Defeat' is the best antonym here: victory and defeat carry opposed meanings, while the other choices offered (ornate, precise, reckless, rough) do not reverse the meaning of victory.

questions.question: The sequence 1, 2, 4, 8 continues with which number?
questions.explanation: Each term multiplies by 2: the sequence runs 1, 2, 4, 8, so the next term is 8 × 2 = 16.

questions.question: Of the choices, which is the best antonym for CHEAP?

answers.text: decrease
descend
costly
confident
distant

questions.explanation: 'Costly' is the best antonym here: cheap and costly carry opposed meanings, while the other choices offered (confident, decrease, descend, distant) do not reverse the meaning of cheap.

questions.question: Which word is most nearly a synonym of DARING?

answers.text: shy
separate
rich
solid
bold

questions.explanation: 'Bold' is closest in meaning to daring: the two words can substitute for each other in most contexts, unlike the remaining choices offered (rich, separate, shy, solid).

questions.question: Choose the word most nearly SAME in meaning as COMPLEX.

answers.text: inspect
intricate
harm
idea
leave

questions.explanation: 'Intricate' is closest in meaning to complex: the two words can substitute for each other in most contexts, unlike the remaining choices offered (harm, idea, inspect, leave).

questions.question: Choose the completion: shoe is to foot as glove is to ___

answers.text: hand
fire
sand
hospital
leg

questions.explanation: The relation is covering and body part (shoe:foot :: glove:hand): shoe relates to foot in the same way glove relates to hand, so hand completes the pair; the other completions offered (fire, leg, sand, hospital) break that relation.

questions.question: A word meaning 'calm, peaceful and untroubled' is ___

answers.text: eloquent
ancient
serene
severe
abundant

questions.explanation: 'Serene' matches the definition exactly — calm, peaceful and untroubled — while each other choice names a different concept (definition 14).

questions.question: 115 items are shared equally among 5 people. How many items does each person get?
questions.explanation: Working the operation directly gives 23: each distractor results from a common slip such as adding instead of averaging or misplacing a digit, and none equals the computed value 23.

questions.question: Clara is 26 years old. Tara is 6 years older than Clara. How old is Tara?
questions.explanation: '6 years/inches older/taller' means add: 26 + 6 = 32. Subtracting would give the younger/shorter value, which answers the reverse question.

questions.question: Cubes are stacked 3 long, 2 wide and 4 layers high, with no gaps. How many cubes are in the stack?
questions.explanation: The stack is a rectangular solid: 3 × 2 × 4 = 24 unit cubes.

questions.question: Choose the completion: smile is to happy as frown is to ___

answers.text: sad
rope
drink
body
hunger

questions.explanation: The relation is expression and emotion (smile:happy :: frown:sad): smile relates to happy in the same way frown relates to sad, so sad completes the pair; the other completions offered (drink, body, hunger, rope) break that relation.

questions.question: Statements: (1) All tickets include parking. (2) This is a ticket. Which conclusion necessarily follows?

answers.text: The first statement must be false
The opposite of the second statement follows necessarily
Nothing at all can be concluded from the two statements
The conclusion holds only on weekdays
The second statement's subject has the property named in the first statement (it follows necessarily)

questions.explanation: From (1) and (2) together, the property in the first statement applies to the subject of the second, so the necessary conclusion is the one that restates that application; the negated version ('This ticket excludes parking') contradicts the premises rather than following from them.

questions.question: Because the road was ___, the delivery van took a different route. Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.

answers.text: paved
rural
blocked
straight
mapped

questions.explanation: 'Blocked' is the only choice that fits the sentence that begins 'ill in the blank with the most suitable word.': it matches the context clues in that sentence, while the alternatives contradict or ignore them.

questions.question: In a row of three, the pencil sits directly left of the mug, and the lamp is rightmost. What is in the middle position?

answers.text: Cannot be determined from the information given
mug
pencil
lamp
None of the three objects

questions.explanation: The lamp is fixed at the far right, and the pencil is immediately left of the mug; the only arrangement is pencil, mug, lamp, so the middle object is the mug.

questions.question: In a set where four figures are a red pentagon and one figure differs only in color, which figure is the odd one out?

answers.text: The red pentagon in the top-left position
The red pentagon drawn largest
The red pentagon in the center
The blue pentagon
The red pentagon drawn smallest

questions.explanation: Color is the only property that varies: four figures are red and one is blue, so the blue pentagon is the odd one out regardless of size or position.

questions.question: A class of 240 students has 15% absent one day (use the class size as the whole). How many students is that?
questions.explanation: 15% of 240 = 240 × 15/100 = 36. The other values come from using the wrong percentage or dropping a zero.

questions.question: The figure 'LETTER L' is reflected in a horizontal edge (flip top-to-bottom)2. What happens to it?

answers.text: Its top and bottom swap places, but its left and right stay the same
It stays exactly identical in every respect, including any lettering
It rotates 180 degrees in its plane
It becomes twice its original size
Its left and right sides swap places, but its top and bottom stay the same

questions.explanation: A flip over a horizontal edge is a top-bottom reversal of 'LETTER L': top and bottom exchange, left and right do not. That is different from a left-right mirror flip or a 180-degree rotation of 'LETTER L'.

questions.question: If 6 items cost the same ratio as 48 items scaled by 7, and the first group is 6, the second group is how many when the first becomes 42? (Solve the proportion 6:48 = 42:x)
questions.explanation: In the ratio 6:48, each step multiplies by 48/6 = 8; 42 × 8 = 336.

questions.question: A circle grows and shrinks in the pattern: small circle, medium circle, large circle, ___. If the size pattern (small, medium, large, medium) repeats, which figure comes next?

answers.text: medium triangle
small circle
medium circle
large circle
tiny circle

questions.explanation: The size cycle is small, medium, large, medium, then back to small, and the shape stays a circle throughout, so the next figure is a small circle.

questions.question: A sapling is 22 inches tall and grows to 13 inches taller than a second plant that is 22 inches. (Read carefully:) Priya's plant is 22 inches; Eli's is 13 inches taller. How tall is Eli's plant, in inches?
questions.explanation: Taller by 13 inches means add: 22 + 13 = 35. Subtracting would answer the reverse comparison.

parapathways.quiz_title: ParaPathways Assessment Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which sentence is correct? (Grammar and usage check set while writing a museum-visit report.)

answers.text: Whom did you invites to the ceremony?
Whom did you invite to the ceremony?
Who did you invite to the ceremony to whom's?
Who's invitation did you whom?

questions.explanation: The correct sentence is: "Whom did you invite to the ceremony?" It follows the rules of standard English grammar and usage — agreement, tense, pronoun case, and word choice — while each other sentence breaks one of those rules in a way a paraeducator should be able to spot. The setting for this item is the activity while writing a museum-visit report.

questions.question: During a library research lesson in a pen-pal letter exchange: A secondary source is

answers.text: ignore sources and evidence entirely
the original experiment data
a diary written at the time of the event
a work that analyzes or describes primary sources, such as a biography or history book

questions.explanation: In the activity in a pen-pal letter exchange, the supported answer is: a work that analyzes or describes primary sources, such as a biography or history book. Credible sources are authored, current, and evidence-based (journal articles and .edu/.gov sites over blogs, social posts, and tabloids), exact words require quotation and credit, and paraphrases still require citation.
