The date of the act, a description of the document and the type of act, the printed full name, address and signature of each person served, the type of satisfactory evidence presented and its description with its issuance or expiration date, the thumbprint where the law requires one, and the fee charged per signature
The document's full text, copied into the journal

questions.explanation: Electronic journals must be permanent and tamper-evident.

questions.question: How many kinds of notarial act does the New Jersey list name for a suburban signing in Vineland?

answers.text: Two kinds only — acknowledgments and oaths
Four kinds, with protests excluded
Nine kinds, including drafting documents
Six kinds, from acknowledgments to protests of negotiable instruments

questions.explanation: The list runs to six: acknowledgment, oath or affirmation, verification, witnessing or attesting, copy or deposition certification, and protest.

questions.question: Which of these is an approved identity-proofing method for a remote act at a harbor office in Franklin Township?

answers.text: The individual's promise that they are who they claim
Dynamic knowledge-based authentication provided online by a third party
A social media profile check by the officer
A utility bill photographed by the individual

questions.explanation: Knowledge-based authentication by a third party is one of the three named methods.

questions.question: May an officer sign a certificate before performing the act, to save time for a signing in East Orange?

answers.text: Yes — pre-signing is permitted for regular customers
Yes — if the act happens later the same day
Yes — for copy certifications only
No — the officer may not affix or logically associate a signature with a certificate until the act has been performed

questions.explanation: Signing before performance is barred outright.

questions.question: An agent or attorney-in-fact signing for a principal acts in what capacity at a bank branch in Jersey City?

answers.text: In an individual capacity
In a notarial capacity
In no recognized capacity
In a representative capacity

questions.explanation: An agent or attorney-in-fact for a principal is a named representative-capacity case.

questions.question: May a credible witness appear by communication technology at a credit union in Woodbridge?

answers.text: No — witnesses must always be physically present
Yes — the witness may personally appear before the officer or use communication technology to appear
Yes — and the witness need not be identified at all
No — witnesses are not used in New Jersey

questions.explanation: Communication-technology appearance is expressly allowed for the witness.

questions.question: An agent or attorney-in-fact signing for a principal acts in what capacity for a military family signing in Bayonne?

answers.text: In an individual capacity
In a representative capacity
In a notarial capacity
In no recognized capacity

questions.explanation: An agent or attorney-in-fact for a principal is a named representative-capacity case.

questions.question: A notary is asked to administer an oath to a witness. Which power covers this at a courthouse desk in Clifton?

answers.text: No power — oaths belong only to judges
Administering an oath or affirmation is an enumerated notarial act
The copy-certification act
The protest act

questions.explanation: Oath and affirmation administration is its own enumerated act.

questions.question: A certificate in a form permitted by the law of the jurisdiction where the act was performed — can it be sufficient for a military family signing in Bayonne?

answers.text: No — only the manual's short forms can ever be used
Yes — that is one of the recognized sufficiency routes
No — foreign forms void the act
Yes — but only for protests

questions.explanation: Sufficiency runs three ways: short form, this State's law, or the law of the place of performance.

questions.question: A public officer or guardian signing in the capacity stated in a record acts in what capacity for a suburban signing in Vineland?

answers.text: In a personal capacity only
In a witnessing capacity
In a representative capacity
In a certifying capacity

questions.explanation: Public officers, personal representatives, and guardians acting as stated act representatively.

questions.question: A qualified applicant lives outside New Jersey but is regularly employed at an office in this State. May the applicant be commissioned at a courthouse desk in Clifton?

answers.text: No — only legal residents may ever be commissioned
Yes — a nonresident with a place of employment or practice in this State may qualify
Yes — but only if the applicant also owns New Jersey property
No — nonresidents must first become residents

questions.explanation: The eligibility criteria admit a legal resident or a person with employment or practice in the State.

questions.question: A record for acknowledgment is in the notary's possession during a remote session. What must happen at a law office in Toms River?

answers.text: The record must be displayed to and identified by the remotely located individual during the audio-visual session
The notary may acknowledge it without showing it
The individual must mail a second copy first
The acknowledgment converts to a verification

questions.explanation: Display and identification during the session support that acknowledgment route.

questions.question: A notary never took the oath after receiving the commission, missing the required window entirely. Is that a discipline ground for a hospital signer in Paterson?

answers.text: Yes — failure to take and subscribe the oath within the required window is an enumerated ground
No — the oath is a formality with no ground attached
Yes — but only if a customer complained
No — the commission simply pauses

questions.explanation: Missing the oath is enumerated among the grounds.

questions.question: A notary performs an act on a record in which the notary's civil union partner holds a direct beneficial interest. What is the act's status at a courthouse desk in Clifton?

answers.text: The act is fully valid because the partner is not the notary
The act converts to a different act type
The act is voidable under the interest prohibition
The act is valid if the fee was standard

questions.explanation: The prohibition reaches the spouse's and civil union partner's interests, and the act is voidable.

questions.question: In a single transaction to finance real estate, the officer administers oaths and takes acknowledgments of the mortgagors repeatedly. What is the total fee for a home signing in Edison?

answers.text: Twenty-five dollars per service
A flat fifteen dollars
Two dollars and fifty cents in total
A flat twenty-five dollars, regardless of the number of such services in the single financing transaction

questions.explanation: Mortgagor services in one financing transaction are capped at the flat twenty-five dollars.

questions.question: A commissioning desk completes 4 notary applications in one week, and holds that pace for 314 weeks. Using total applications = applications per week x number of weeks, how many applications are completed?

answers.text: 1252 applications
1570 applications
1256 applications
1264 applications

questions.explanation: Total applications = 314 x 4 = 1256 applications. The weekly pace is repeated for every week in the run.

agacnp.quiz_title: Adult-Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner (AGACNP) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: During a case review at a medical-surgical unit, a question about acute care practice comes up. Regarding fluid shift and third spacing, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Third spaced fluid remains fully available to support circulating blood volume.
Third spacing occurs when fluid moves from the intravascular space into interstitial or body cavity spaces where it does not support circulating volume.
Third spacing describes fluid moving from tissues back into vessels to expand volume.
Third spacing occurs only when total body fluid is reduced with no redistribution.

questions.explanation: Counting third spaced fluid as circulating volume can lead to underrecognition of hypoperfusion, which is why the correct statement best fits practice. The other choices distort the principle behind fluid shift and third spacing.

questions.question: During a case review at an emergency department, a question about acute care practice comes up. Regarding cultural factors in care planning, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: A group label reliably predicts what an individual patient believes and prefers.
Care planning should ask the individual patient about cultural practices and preferences that matter to them rather than assuming beliefs from a group label.
Cultural preferences are relevant only to diet and never to treatment decisions.
Qualified interpreter services can be replaced by family members for complex discussions.

questions.explanation: This statement is right because individualized cultural assessment is a core part of inclusive care planning in acute care. That is the sound approach to cultural factors in care planning.

questions.question: In an interdisciplinary team meeting at a hospital step-down unit, clinicians raise a question about standard practice. Which statement about neurogenic shock distinction correctly resolves the issue presented?

answers.text: Neurogenic shock reliably presents with tachycardia and cool clammy skin in every case.

Neurogenic shock after spinal cord injury is distinguished by hypotension with bradycardia and warm skin from loss of sympathetic tone, unlike hypovolemic shock which typically presents with tachycardia and cool skin.
Neurogenic shock and hypovolemic shock cannot occur together after spinal trauma.
Neurogenic shock assessment does not require evaluation of the level of spinal injury.

questions.explanation: Overlooking the neurogenic pattern can lead to misclassification of shock or a flawed plan, which is why the correct statement best fits practice. The other choices distort the principle behind neurogenic shock distinction.

questions.question: Hana is reviewing the plan of care for a young adult admitted after a serious motor vehicle collision at a medical-surgical unit. Which of the following best describes payment models reward outcomes not volume?

answers.text: Value-oriented payment models pay more whenever more services are delivered, regardless of outcomes.
Under value-oriented models, quality measurement is unnecessary because payment ignores results.
Value-oriented payment models aim to reward quality and patient outcomes rather than simply paying for a greater volume of services.
Volume-based and value-oriented payment models are identical in the incentives they create.

questions.explanation: This statement is right because linking payment to quality and outcomes rather than volume alone is the core principle of value-oriented models. This is the standard acute care practice whenever payment models reward outcomes not volume is at issue.

questions.question: Ingrid is reviewing the plan of care for an adult recovering from an acute stroke on a monitored unit at an intensive care unit. Which of the following best describes confidentiality in everyday acute care?

answers.text: Discussing patient details in public areas is acceptable if names are spoken quietly.
Family members are automatically entitled to all patient information.
Patient information should be shared only with those involved in care or authorized by the patient, and discussed in private settings.
Sharing information for teaching never requires attention to patient privacy.

questions.explanation: This statement is right because privacy in information handling is a core professional and ethical duty in acute care. The other choices distort the principle behind confidentiality in everyday acute care.

questions.question: A unit manager at an emergency department reviews a practice question with nurse practitioner Oscar. Regarding beta blocker class effect principle, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: A beta blocker raises heart rate by stimulating sympathetic receptors directly.
Beta blockade increases contractility in all acute care situations without exception.
A beta blocker has no effect on heart rate, rhythm, or blood pressure control.
A beta blocker reduces heart rate and contractility by blocking sympathetic stimulation, which can be harmful when cardiac output depends on compensatory tachycardia.

questions.explanation: A beta blocker slows rate and reduces contractility by blocking sympathetic drive, so use requires caution when compensation depends on tachycardia. The other choices distort the principle behind beta blocker class effect principle.

questions.question: Yusuf is a newly certified adult-gerontology acute care nurse practitioner being mentored at a cardiac care unit. Regarding shared decision making within standards of care, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Standards of care remove any role for patient preference in choosing among reasonable options.
Shared decision making means offering options that fall outside accepted standards without explanation.
Within the range of options supported by standards of care, the informed preferences of the patient should guide which option is chosen.
Discussing preferences is unnecessary when a patient appears to agree quickly.

questions.explanation: Overlooking patient preference among reasonable options can lead to unwanted treatment or a flawed plan, which is why the correct statement best fits practice. That is the sound approach to shared decision making within standards of care.

questions.question: During a case review at an academic medical center ward, a question about acute care practice comes up. Regarding health promotion counseling during acute episodes, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Health promotion has no place in an acute care episode under any circumstances.
Brief counseling during an acute episode about activity, diet, sleep, and chronic disease self-management can reinforce prevention when it is linked to follow-up support after discharge.
Chronic disease self-management is unrelated to why many acute episodes occur.
A brief conversation about activity and diet is too trivial to influence later habits.

questions.explanation: This statement is right because weaving health promotion into acute episodes is a core part of comprehensive, cost-effective care. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about health promotion counseling during acute episodes.

questions.question: A unit manager at an intensive care unit reviews a practice question with nurse practitioner Tessa. Regarding central line infection prevention principle, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Central line infection prevention allows routine replacement of lines on a fixed schedule to reduce infection.
Daily review of central line necessity has no effect on infection risk.
Sterile barrier precautions at central line insertion are optional when the insertion is urgent in every circumstance.

Central line infection prevention includes maximal sterile barrier precautions at insertion, chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, daily review of line necessity, and prompt removal when the line is no longer needed.

questions.explanation: Line infection prevention depends on sterile insertion, skin antisepsis, and daily necessity review with prompt removal, so this practice helps reduce bloodstream infection. The other choices distort the principle behind central line infection prevention principle.

questions.question: A care team at a hospital step-down unit is discussing how to handle a recurring situation. Regarding scope expands only with added education, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: A practitioner's scope expands legitimately only through additional formal education, supervised experience, and demonstrated competence in the new area.
Health care policy shapes acute care practice by influencing staffing models, available technology, service lines, and the resources a practitioner can offer patients.
Policies governing staffing levels, work hours, and required competencies directly affect patient safety in acute care units.
A practitioner's scope expands automatically with each year of employment regardless of new preparation.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Growth in scope must be earned and verified, so requiring added education and demonstrated competence helps keep expanded practice well supported and safe.

questions.question: Casper is a newly certified adult-gerontology acute care nurse practitioner being mentored at a cardiac care unit. Regarding chunking teaching into small steps, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Covering every topic in one session ensures that a patient will retain more.
Checking understanding between steps interrupts learning and should be avoided.
Breaking teaching into small steps and checking understanding between steps helps an acutely ill patient retain essential information.
Small steps are helpful only for teaching children about a care task.

questions.explanation: Breaking teaching into small steps with checks between steps supports retention, so this practice helps the clinician educate an acutely ill patient effectively. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about chunking teaching into small steps.

questions.question: At a medical-surgical unit, a nurse practitioner considers the best way to proceed with a complex case. The situation turns on distributive shock vasodilation principle. Which proposition states the sound approach?

answers.text: In distributive shock, intense vasoconstriction is the main reason tissue perfusion fails.
Distributive shock impairs perfusion only by reducing total circulating blood volume.
In distributive shock, vessel tone increases so much that vessels cannot relax at all.
In distributive shock, widespread vasodilation and maldistribution of blood flow impair tissue perfusion even though cardiac output may be preserved or increased.

questions.explanation: Overlooking maldistribution in distributive shock can lead to missed recognition of ongoing tissue hypoperfusion, which is why the correct statement best fits practice. This is the standard acute care practice whenever distributive shock vasodilation principle is at issue.

questions.question: Priya is reviewing the plan of care for a frail elderly patient whose family helps coordinate decisions during a hospital stay at an emergency department. Which of the following best describes delirium assessment distinguishing features?

answers.text: Delirium develops gradually over years as a permanent progressive condition.
Fluctuating attention is a hallmark of dementia rather than of delirium.
Delirium is an acute, fluctuating disturbance of attention and awareness that differs from dementia, which develops gradually and progresses over a longer course.
Delirium involves clear awareness with fully intact attention throughout the day.

questions.explanation: Mistaking delirium for dementia or aging can delay treatment of a reversible cause, which is why the correct statement best fits practice. That is the sound approach to delirium assessment distinguishing features.

questions.question: In an interdisciplinary team meeting at an intensive care unit, clinicians raise a question about standard practice. Regarding matching imaging modality to the clinical question, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: The imaging modality should be matched to the specific question being asked, the urgency, and the patient's stability rather than defaulting to the most advanced study.
The most advanced imaging study is the right first choice for every clinical question.
When infection is suspected and organ dysfunction is present, the clinician should treat the patient as high risk and act promptly rather than waiting for complete diagnostic certainty.
Antimicrobial stewardship means starting therapy promptly when infection is likely, then narrowing or stopping it as culture results and the clinical course clarify the picture.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Matching modality to question, urgency, and stability yields timely answers safely, so this practice helps the clinician reach a well supported conclusion.

questions.question: In an interdisciplinary team meeting at a cardiac care unit, clinicians raise a question about standard practice. Regarding acute pancreatitis supportive care principle, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: In acute pancreatitis, early fluid resuscitation, pain control, antiemetic therapy, and early enteral nutrition when tolerated are central supportive principles, with evaluation for gallstone or alcohol related causes.
In acute pancreatitis, prolonged fasting for many days is preferred even when enteral feeding is tolerated.

Prevention of contrast associated kidney injury includes assessing baseline renal function, ensuring adequate hydration when appropriate, and reviewing nephrotoxic medications before contrast imaging.
Palliative care can be integrated alongside curative treatment in serious acute illness to address symptoms, support decision making, and align care with patient values and goals.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Supportive pancreatitis care depends on fluids, symptom control, and early enteral nutrition when tolerated, so this practice helps the clinician support recovery.

questions.question: Goran and another nurse practitioner disagree about the right approach and check the standard practice. Regarding fall prevention through risk assessment, which choice states the practice an adult-gerontology acute care nurse practitioner should follow?

answers.text: A single standard intervention prevents falls equally well for every hospitalized adult.
Risk factors such as medications, mobility, and cognition contribute little to fall planning.
Fall prevention begins with assessing each patient's individual risk factors and matching interventions to those factors rather than applying one intervention to everyone.
Reassessment of fall risk is unnecessary because risk stays constant throughout a stay.

questions.explanation: This statement is right because individualized risk assessment and reassessment are core parts of fall prevention in acute care practice. The other choices distort the principle behind fall prevention through risk assessment.

questions.question: Nadia and another nurse practitioner disagree about the right approach and check the standard practice. Regarding quality action calculation 7, which choice states the practice an adult-gerontology acute care nurse practitioner should follow?

answers.text: A unit quality review counts 50 eligible patients who received a stated safety action out of 33 eligible patients in the measure, giving a quality action rate of 151.52 percent, computed as 50 divided by 33 and multiplied by 100.

A unit quality review counts 33 eligible patients who received a stated safety action out of 50 eligible patients in the measure, giving a quality action rate of 83 percent, computed as 33 plus 50 and multiplied by 100.

A unit quality review counts 33 eligible patients who received a stated safety action out of 50 eligible patients in the measure, giving a quality action rate of 66 percent, computed as 33 divided by 50 and multiplied by 100.

A unit quality review counts 33 eligible patients who received a stated safety action out of 50 eligible patients in the measure, giving a quality action rate of 33 percent, computed as the count of 33 alone without regard to the total.

questions.explanation: A quality-measure rate compares the eligible patients who received the stated safety action with every eligible patient in the measure denominator. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about quality action calculation 7.

questions.question: Marta, an adult-gerontology acute care nurse practitioner, is coordinating care for an older adult admitted with an acute exacerbation of chronic heart failure at an academic medical center ward. Regarding assessment completion calculation 8, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: A unit audit counts 93 patients who received a completed structured assessment out of 100 patients who were due for that assessment in the same period, giving an assessment completion rate of 93 percent, computed as 93 divided by 100 and multiplied by 100.
In hypovolemic shock, sympathetic activation raises heart rate and constricts peripheral vessels to preserve perfusion to vital organs despite reduced circulating volume.

A unit audit counts 100 patients who received a completed structured assessment out of 93 patients who were due for that assessment in the same period, giving an assessment completion rate of 107.53 percent, computed as 100 divided by 93 and multiplied by 100.
When oxygen delivery is inadequate, cells shift to anaerobic metabolism, which yields far less energy and produces lactic acid as a byproduct.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. An assessment completion rate compares the patients who actually received the completed structured assessment with all patients who were due for it in the same audit period. This is the standard acute care practice whenever assessment completion calculation 8 is at issue.

questions.question: Yusuf and another nurse practitioner disagree about the right approach and check the standard practice. Regarding unstable dysrhythmia immediate intervention, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: An unstable dysrhythmia causing hypotension, altered mentation, chest pain, or acute heart failure requires immediate synchronized cardioversion or defibrillation as appropriate to the rhythm.
In suspected aortic dissection, urgent imaging, heart rate and blood pressure control with careful sequencing of therapy, and immediate surgical consultation are central principles.
An unstable dysrhythmia should be observed for several hours before any intervention is attempted.
In hemorrhagic stroke, management includes careful blood pressure control, reversal of anticoagulation when present, neurosurgical consultation, and monitoring for increased intracranial pressure.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Urgent care of unstable dysrhythmia depends on immediate electrical therapy matched to the rhythm, so this practice helps the clinician restore perfusion without delay.

questions.question: Dalia is a newly certified adult-gerontology acute care nurse practitioner being mentored at an emergency department. Regarding asking an answerable clinical question, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: A focused clinical question identifies the patient population, the intervention, a comparison, and the outcome of interest.
Searching reputable peer reviewed databases and selecting sources by relevance and quality strengthens an evidence review.
A focused clinical question should be kept as vague as possible to capture more studies.
After an evidence based change is implemented, outcomes should be measured and compared with the goals set before the change.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Naming population, intervention, comparison, and outcome focuses a search, so this practice helps the clinician reach a well supported conclusion efficiently.

bcba.quiz_title: BCBA (Board Certified Behavior Analyst) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which of the following best describes empiricism in behavior analysis?

answers.text: Knowledge claims rest on objective observation and measurement of behavior and its environmental relations
Knowledge claims rest on intuition and personal conviction
Unobservable mental events are the preferred unit of analysis
A single anecdote outweighs repeated objective measurement

questions.explanation: Empiricism requires objective, repeatable observation rather than subjective impression.

questions.question: Regarding ecological assessment, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Ecological assessment tests the client's skills directly
Environmental demands are irrelevant to goal selection
The environments where the client lives and learns are inventoried — demands, routines, and available reinforcers — so goals fit real life
Only the clinic room is examined in an ecological assessment

questions.explanation: Ecological assessment examines the settings themselves so intervention fits their real demands.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the matching law?

answers.text: Learners always choose the option reinforced most recently
Matching applies only when both options deliver identical schedules
Allocation is unrelated to obtained reinforcement rates
Relative response allocation matches the relative rate of reinforcement obtained from each option

questions.explanation: Matching describes how behavior distributes across options in proportion to reinforcement from each.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes overcorrection procedures?

answers.text: Practice activities are unrelated to the disruption caused
Overcorrection is the first procedure to try for any behavior
Restitutional or positive-practice activities follow the behavior, contingent on it, beyond simply correcting the disruption
Overcorrection means apologizing verbally for the behavior

questions.explanation: Overcorrection adds contingent restitution or practice beyond the natural correction of the act.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes non-discrimination (Section 1)?

answers.text: Harmless jokes about a group fall outside this standard
The analyst does not discriminate against clients, stakeholders, supervisees, or colleagues on protected or personal grounds
Discrimination is defined only by the analyst's intent
Preference-based caseload selection is always permissible

questions.explanation: The non-discrimination standard bars biased treatment regardless of stated intent.

questions.question: A behavior analyst working in an adult day program must apply differential reinforcement of incompatible behavior for a young learner. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: A response that can occur simultaneously with the target is reinforced
The target response itself is reinforced at a lower rate
Incompatibility between responses is irrelevant to this procedure
A response that cannot occur at the same time as the target is reinforced while the target is on extinction

questions.explanation: DRI selects a replacement that is physically incompatible with the target response.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the second core principle — compassion, dignity, and respect?

answers.text: Respect is owed only to paying stakeholders
Self-determination ends where the analyst's preference begins
Cultural values are irrelevant to respectful practice
Clients, families, and colleagues are treated with compassion and dignity, with their values, privacy, and self-determination respected

questions.explanation: The second principle requires compassionate, dignified, respectful treatment of all others.

questions.question: During a case review for a new client in a preschool inclusion classroom, the team discusses training loosely to promote generalization. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Every feature of every trial is held rigidly identical
Variation is introduced only after generalization fails
Loose training varies the defining features of the target
Noncritical features of instruction are varied deliberately so control attaches to the critical features of the task

questions.explanation: Training loosely varies the irrelevant so the learner responds to what actually matters.

questions.question: Regarding conforming with professional and legal requirements (Section 1), which statement is correct?

answers.text: Employer policy excuses violating the Ethics Code
An analyst follows only the rules they agree with
The analyst follows the law and the rules of the BACB, licensure boards, funders, and employers that govern their practice
Certification rules override all state law automatically

questions.explanation: Analysts must conform to applicable law and to every governing body's requirements.

questions.question: A behavior analyst working in a telehealth-supported home program must apply latency-based functional analysis for a teenage client. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: Latency cannot differentiate conditions in an analysis
Ending at first occurrence removes the safety benefit
The measure is how quickly the behavior occurs in each condition, and the trial ends at the first occurrence for safety
Total counts across long sessions are the required measure

questions.explanation: Latency-based analyses shorten exposure by measuring time to the first response.

questions.question: When planning services for a young learner in a middle school resource room, the analyst considers verbal behavior — the tact. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: A response controlled by a motivating operation that names its reinforcer
A written response to a verbal stimulus without correspondence
A verbal operant evoked by a nonverbal stimulus and maintained by generalized conditioned reinforcement
A repetition of a heard word with point-to-point correspondence

questions.explanation: Tacts are evoked by nonverbal stimuli — labeling what is present — and maintained socially.

questions.question: In a public elementary school classroom, a behavior analyst is addressing intraverbal training methods with an adolescent learner. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: Point-to-point correspondence is required in intraverbal targets
Question-answering and conversational responses are taught by starting from supported forms — fill-ins and choices — toward independent answers
Intraverbals are taught only by repeating the question back
Conversation skills need no antecedent verbal stimulus control

questions.explanation: Intraverbal teaching scaffolds from supported answers to independent responses to verbal stimuli.

questions.question: Across three observations in a summer camp program, an episode by a preschool learner lasts 7 minutes, then 8 minutes, then 3 minutes. What is the total duration across the three observations?
questions.explanation: Total duration adds the three episode lengths: 7 + 8 + 3 = 18 minutes.

questions.question: A behavior analyst working in a high school life-skills class must apply behavioral momentum in intervention design for a preschool learner. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: Embedding high-rate reinforced responding before a demand increases persistence through the demand
Momentum procedures begin with the hardest demand
Momentum is built by withholding all reinforcement first
Persistence is unrelated to recent reinforcement history

questions.explanation: Momentum interventions front-load reinforced success so behavior carries through disruption.

questions.question: Two observers agree on occurrence or nonoccurrence in 23 of 27 recording intervals for a preschool learner in a transition program for young adults. What is the interval-by-interval agreement percentage?
questions.explanation: Interval-by-interval agreement divides agreeing intervals (23) by total intervals (27): the result is 85 percent.

questions.question: A behavior analyst working in a telehealth-supported home program must apply schedules for skill acquisition versus maintenance for a preschool learner. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: New skills earn dense, continuous reinforcement; mastered skills shift to intermittent, natural schedules that maintain them
Acquisition proceeds best on the leanest schedule available
Maintenance requires continuous reinforcement forever
Schedule changes between stages are never planned

questions.explanation: Dense schedules build behavior; thinned, natural schedules keep it alive.

questions.question: In an after-school social skills group, a behavior analyst is addressing scatterplot recording in assessment with a learner in transition. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: A scatterplot requires experimental conditions to interpret
Occurrences are plotted by time of day and day, exposing temporal patterns in the behavior
Scatterplots identify the reinforcer maintaining behavior directly
Time patterns are irrelevant to assessment planning

questions.explanation: Scatterplots reveal when behavior clusters, guiding where to look for controlling variables.

questions.question: During a case review for a teenage client in a preschool inclusion classroom, the team discusses carryover and sequence effects in alternating designs. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Exposure to one condition can influence responding in the next, so counterbalancing and distinct signals are used to limit the contamination
Carryover is impossible when sessions alternate quickly
Sequence effects strengthen every conclusion automatically
Counterbalancing removes the need for discriminative signals

questions.explanation: Alternating designs must manage carryover through design features such as counterbalancing.

questions.question: When planning services for a teenage client in a home-based early intensive program, the analyst considers ongoing personnel performance management. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: Annual review alone manages performance adequately
Coaching follows only formal discipline
Performance is monitored with data, reinforced when it meets standard, and coached when it does not — continuously, not only at annual review
Reinforcement for staff performance is unprofessional

questions.explanation: Managing personnel is a contingency system: monitor, reinforce, coach — on a short loop.

questions.question: A supervisor in a transition program for young adults is teaching a trainee about using group supervision effectively using the case of a teenage client. Which of the following is correct?

answers.text: Cases are discussed without data in group sessions
Group sessions are structured around case data, skill practice, and peer learning, complementing — never replacing — individual observation
Group supervision substitutes fully for individual supervision
Peer presence makes rehearsal unnecessary

questions.explanation: Group supervision multiplies learning through shared cases and practice, alongside individual oversight.

arrt-mammo.quiz_title: ARRT Mammography Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Devon is a newly credentialed mammography technologist being mentored at a diagnostic breast imaging clinic. Regarding social risk and access to care, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Access to care has no effect on screening patterns and should not be noted.
Transportation problems are a private matter that the care team should always ignore.
Access barriers matter only for billing staff and never for the clinical team.
Access to care is a social risk factor, so barriers such as delayed screening, limited transportation, or gaps in follow-up care should be noted when the patient shares them.

questions.explanation: Noting gaps in care without blame helps the team arrange follow-up and understand why prior imaging or results may be unavailable. This is the standard mammography practice whenever social risk and access to care is at issue.

questions.question: Goran is a mammography technologist at an outpatient breast imaging center reviewing a sampled case file. Which of the following best describes viewing conditions for softcopy reading?

answers.text: Bright room lighting improves softcopy reading by washing out display contrast.
Glare on the display has no effect on perception of low contrast lesions.
Ambient light should be brighter than the display for comfortable interpretation.
Softcopy reading is performed in low ambient light with controlled glare so that subtle contrast differences remain visible on the display.

questions.explanation: Controlled lighting, clean screens, and glare management are simple defenses for diagnostic accuracy. The other choices distort the principle behind viewing conditions for softcopy reading.

questions.question: A team at a community screening mammography unit is discussing how to handle a recurring imaging situation. The situation turns on quality control rate calculation 7. Which proposition states the sound approach?

answers.text: Of 180 cases in which medical physicist survey items were due for completion in the cycle, 135 met the standard, a rate of 133.33 percent, computed as 180 divided by 135 and multiplied by 100.
Of 180 cases in which medical physicist survey items were due for completion in the cycle, 135 met the standard, a rate of 75 percent, computed as 135 divided by 180 and multiplied by 100.
Of 180 cases in which medical physicist survey items were due for completion in the cycle, 135 met the standard, a rate of 315 percent, computed as 135 plus 180 and multiplied by 100.
Of 180 cases in which medical physicist survey items were due for completion in the cycle, 135 met the standard, a rate of 70 percent, computed as 135 divided by 180 and multiplied by 100.

questions.explanation: Rates are compared across periods only when the denominator is the full scheduled or audited set, drawn the same way each time. This is the standard mammography practice whenever quality control rate calculation 7 is at issue.

questions.question: Farah is a mammography technologist at an outpatient breast imaging center reviewing a sampled case file. Which of the following best describes calcifications associated with ductal carcinoma in situ?

answers.text: Calcifications linked to ductal carcinoma in situ often appear as fine, linear, or branching specks following the course of ducts, reflecting material formed within involved duct spaces.
Calcifications of in situ disease are always large, round, and smoothly rimmed like eggshells.
In situ disease never produces calcifications and is visible only as a skin change.
Ductal calcifications form in lymph nodes and then migrate into the duct system.

questions.explanation: The distribution of calcifications helps estimate disease extent when in situ carcinoma is confirmed. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about calcifications associated with ductal carcinoma in situ.

questions.question: Casper is a newly credentialed mammography technologist being mentored at an outpatient breast imaging center. Regarding small breast adaptations, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: For a small breast, the largest paddle is used so the breast cannot shift during compression.
Small breasts cannot be imaged with standard projections under any circumstances.

For a small breast, a smaller compression paddle and careful use of surrounding tissue movement help place enough tissue on the detector, and spot or rolled approaches may help when standard placement is difficult.
For a small breast, compression is omitted because the paddle cannot contact the tissue.

questions.explanation: Paddle size matched to the breast improves contact and compression control when tissue volume is limited. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about small breast adaptations.

questions.question: Emil has asked Dalia, an experienced mammography technologist, a question about a case under review. Regarding explaining compression purpose, which choice states the practice a mammography technologist should follow?

answers.text: Compression exists only to hold the breast still and has no effect on dose or detail.
Faster and harder compression is always better, so gradual pressure is discouraged.
The technologist explains that compression spreads breast tissue, reduces motion and dose, and improves detail, and that pressure is applied gradually while the patient can report discomfort.
The purpose of compression should be kept from patients to avoid worry.

questions.explanation: Compression spreads tissue so structures overlap less, motion drops, and detail improves, which is why skipping compression undermines the examination. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about explaining compression purpose.

questions.question: Mina and another mammography technologist disagree about the right approach and check the standard practice. Regarding tomosynthesis sweep motion and blur, which choice states the practice a mammography technologist should follow?

answers.text: Patient motion during the tomosynthesis sweep improves slice sharpness through averaging.
Tomosynthesis sweeps are instant, so motion never affects reconstructed images.
Patient motion during the tomosynthesis sweep degrades reconstructed slices, so firm compression and clear stillness instructions are essential.
Loose compression is preferred during tomosynthesis to allow natural breast movement.

questions.explanation: Because the sweep takes longer than a single contact exposure, even small movement can blur multiple projections. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about tomosynthesis sweep motion and blur.

questions.question: During a case review at a community screening mammography unit, a question about mammography practice comes up. Regarding phantom evaluation purpose and scoring, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Phantom evaluation uses a patient volunteer to judge image quality subjectively.
Phantom evaluation images a standardized test object and scores visible fibers, speck groups, and masses to track system image quality over time.
A phantom image is evaluated once at installation and never compared with later results.
Phantom evaluation measures room lighting rather than imaging system performance.

questions.explanation: Declining scores warn of detector, processing, or exposure problems before clinical images suffer visibly. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about phantom evaluation purpose and scoring.

questions.question: Clara has asked Mateo, an experienced mammography technologist, a question about a case under review. Regarding menstrual cycle effects on breast tissue, which choice states the practice a mammography technologist should follow?

answers.text: Across a menstrual cycle, shifting estrogen and progesterone levels can bring fullness, tenderness, and nodularity that are often most noticeable in the days before a period and ease afterward.
Breast tissue does not change at all across the menstrual cycle in any patient.
Cyclic breast tenderness is strongest immediately after a period ends and absent before it.
Hormonal fluctuation causes permanent new lobes to form with every menstrual cycle.

questions.explanation: Cyclic change explains why some patients report a lump that seems to appear and fade with the cycle. That is the sound approach to menstrual cycle effects on breast tissue.

questions.question: A training session for mammography technologists at a community screening mammography unit takes up a practice scenario. Which statement about breast abscess appearance and disposition correctly resolves the issue presented?

answers.text: A breast abscess is a simple cyst of clear fluid that always resolves without any treatment.

A breast abscess is a contained collection of pus that can appear as an irregular or partly circumscribed density with surrounding edema and skin thickening, and management generally combines antibiotics in words with drainage of the collection when one is present.
A breast abscess is a benign fatty tumor that grows slowly over many years.
Abscess formation rules out infection and points instead to a purely hormonal cause.

questions.explanation: Recurrent abscess in the same location prompts a search for an underlying duct or skin cause. The other choices distort the principle behind breast abscess appearance and disposition.

questions.question: At a diagnostic breast imaging clinic, a mammography technologist considers the best way to proceed with a complex examination. The situation turns on spot compression purpose and technique. Which proposition states the sound approach?

answers.text: Spot compression uses a small paddle to apply focused compression over a region of interest, spreading overlapping tissue and pressing the area closer to the detector for clearer evaluation.
Spot compression uses a large paddle to compress the whole breast more forcefully than a standard view.
Spot compression is performed without any compression so tissue keeps a natural thickness.
Spot compression works by magnifying tissue with an air gap rather than by focused pressure.

questions.explanation: Bringing the region closer to the detector also improves sharpness for the spot compression view. That is the sound approach to spot compression purpose and technique.

questions.question: Nadia has asked Hana, an experienced mammography technologist, a question about a case under review. Regarding labeling and identification in words, which choice states the practice a mammography technologist should follow?

answers.text: Each view carries accurate identification and labeling in words and markers covering patient identity, date, side, and projection, placed so markers do not obscure breast tissue and laterality is never reversed.
Side markers may be added later from memory if they were forgotten during positioning.
Projection labeling is optional on additional views because the standard views are labeled.
Identification is verified only at scheduling, not again at the time of the examination.

questions.explanation: Markers belong near the axilla side of the field by convention, keeping them clear of breast tissue in most projections. This is the standard mammography practice whenever labeling and identification in words is at issue.

questions.question: During a case review at a diagnostic breast imaging clinic, a question about mammography practice comes up. Regarding documenting physical findings during assessment, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Findings should be documented with personal opinions about likely causes.

Physical findings noted during assessment, such as a palpable area reported by the patient, visible skin change, or tenderness, are documented objectively with location and shared with the interpreting team.

Clinical experience requires independently completing mammographic imaging on seventy-five patients, covering screening or diagnostic examinations and the associated patient care tasks, with verification through the designated process.
Registration is renewed annually, and continuing education is completed across a two-year biennium cycle, with compliance subject to audit and ethics standing maintained throughout.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Objective notes with clear location turn assessment observations into useful information for positioning, added views, and physician interpretation.

questions.question: Tessa is reviewing the worksheet for a patient returning for a short-interval follow-up study at an accredited mammography facility. Which of the following best describes image quality evaluation before patient release?

answers.text: Each image is evaluated for positioning, compression, exposure, contrast, sharpness, noise, and artifacts before the patient is released.
Image evaluation occurs only after the patient leaves and the report is issued.
Only exposure needs checking because digital processing fixes all other attributes.
A noisy or blurred image should be sent for reading without comment to save time.

questions.explanation: Releasing a patient with a known deficiency risks recall, delay, and loss of diagnostic confidence. That is the sound approach to image quality evaluation before patient release.

questions.question: Tomas is a mammography technologist at an accredited mammography facility reviewing a sampled case file. Regarding glandular fatty and fibrous tissue mix, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Breast tissue is a mix of glandular tissue that makes secretions, fatty tissue that gives volume, and fibrous connective tissue that provides structure, in proportions that vary widely among patients.
The inframammary fold is the crease where the lower breast meets the chest wall, and it serves as a key landmark for positioning and for describing the lower extent of breast tissue.
Healthy breast tissue is composed almost entirely of glandular tissue with almost no fat at any age.

The male breast normally contains a small amount of ductal and stromal tissue behind the nipple with little lobular development and mostly fatty tissue, and it can still develop benign enlargement and, uncommonly, malignancy.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. The balance of fat and glandular tissue determines mammographic density, which affects how easily masses stand out.

questions.question: A department manager at a diagnostic breast imaging clinic reviews a practice question with mammography technologist Nadia. Regarding craniocaudal symmetry comparison, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: The paired craniocaudal views must be mirror identical in every patient for the examination to be adequate.
A difference in size between breasts on the craniocaudal views always means one side was mispositioned.
The paired craniocaudal views are compared only for exposure, never for tissue inclusion.
The paired craniocaudal views are compared for roughly symmetric tissue distribution and depth, while recognizing that genuine anatomic differences between breasts can occur.

questions.explanation: Asymmetry prompts a second look for rotation or cutoff, while natural size differences remain a normal finding. That is the sound approach to craniocaudal symmetry comparison.

questions.question: Vera and another mammography technologist disagree about the right approach and check the standard practice. Regarding infection control for interventional procedures, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Infection control for breast interventional procedures includes hand hygiene, skin antisepsis at the entry site, sterile gloves and supplies, and maintaining a sterile field throughout sampling.
When clinically significant tissue is missed and the view cannot answer the examination purpose, the view is repeated with a specific positioning change rather than accepted or repeated identically.

The technologist consults the interpreting physician when a finding or symptom needs direction, when positioning limits prevent adequate tissue inclusion, when a device or surgical change is unclear, or when a patient condition may change the examination plan.
Skin antisepsis is optional when the needle passes through clothing-free skin that looks clean.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Breast procedures breach the skin, so sterile technique protects the sampling tract and deeper tissue from contamination.

questions.question: A department manager at a university breast center reviews a practice question with mammography technologist Clara. Regarding mqsa as a parallel federal system in words, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: The Mammography Quality Standards Act is a federal system, separate from professional certification, that sets facility, personnel, quality, and reporting standards under federal mammography regulations.
Privacy and dignity are protected by exposing only the area needed, using draping and private changing space, limiting observers, and keeping health information confidential in every setting.
The Mammography Quality Standards Act is a voluntary marketing program run by facilities.

Of 160 cases in which patients with a documented family-history risk assessment were due for review at the visit, 144 met the standard, a rate of 90 percent, computed as 144 divided by 160 and multiplied by 100.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Certification shows individual competence while the federal system governs facility practice, so the two systems operate in parallel by design.

questions.question: Nadia, a mammography technologist, is performing a study for a patient whose prior images are unavailable at the time of the visit at a community screening mammography unit. Regarding deodorant and powder artifact mimic, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Deodorant residue appears as large soft masses rather than tiny bright specks.
Skin products never reach the imaged area and cannot affect mammograms.
Cleansing the skin before a repeat view is discouraged because residue confirms findings.
Deodorant, powder, and skin products in the axilla or breast area can appear as tiny bright specks resembling calcifications, so skin is cleansed when such products are suspected.

questions.explanation: A repeat view after cleansing that clears the specks spares the patient unnecessary recall and biopsy anxiety. The other choices distort the principle behind deodorant and powder artifact mimic.

questions.question: Nadia, a mammography technologist, is performing a study for a patient with a strong family history of breast cancer at a first screening visit at a university breast center. Regarding oblique nipple in profile, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: On the mediolateral oblique view, the nipple should be shown in profile, and a nipple pointing downward suggests the breast was allowed to sag during positioning.
On the mediolateral oblique view, the nipple should point downward to prove the breast hung naturally.
For the mediolateral oblique view, the arm on the imaged side rests relaxed on the detector housing or handle with the shoulder dropped, keeping muscle soft and tissue mobile.
To limit motion on the mediolateral oblique view, the patient is instructed to hold still and breathe quietly or hold a breath as directed while compression maintains the breast position.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. A profile nipple on the oblique view indicates the breast was lifted and supported rather than left to droop under compression.

cpnp-pc.quiz_title: Certified Pediatric Nurse Practitioner — Primary Care (CPNP-PC) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Sana is a newly certified pediatric nurse practitioner being mentored at a pediatric primary care practice. Regarding toddler tantrum response guidance, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: For toddler tantrums, caregivers should use long detailed explanations during peak crying to teach reasoning skills.
For toddler tantrums, caregivers should ignore safety concerns and leave the room until the crying stops completely.
For toddler tantrums, caregivers should stay calm, ensure safety, use brief simple language, and reconnect once the child settles.
For toddler tantrums, caregivers should expect a toddler to negotiate rules calmly like an older school-age child.

questions.explanation: Rewarding a tantrum with the sought item can reinforce the behavior, while reconnection afterward supports learning. The other choices distort the principle behind toddler tantrum response guidance.

questions.question: Mina is a pediatric nurse practitioner at a school-based health center reviewing a sampled case file. Which of the following best describes developmental surveillance at every visit?

answers.text: Developmental surveillance is a continuing process at every health supervision visit, not a one time milestone check.
Developmental surveillance is completed once in infancy and then no longer needed at later visits.
Developmental surveillance means asking only whether a child is walking, regardless of age.
Developmental surveillance can be replaced entirely by physical growth plotting at each visit.

questions.explanation: Surveillance elicits caregiver concerns, observes the child, and reviews milestones across all visits over time. That is the sound approach to developmental surveillance at every visit.

questions.question: Mateo is a newly certified pediatric nurse practitioner being mentored at a rural pediatric clinic. Regarding screening completion calculation 5, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A primary care pediatric practice audit counts 60 children who completed developmental screening on schedule out of 57 children who were due for screening in the same period, giving a screening completion rate of 105.26 percent, computed as 60 divided by 57 and multiplied by 100.

A primary care pediatric practice audit counts 57 children who completed developmental screening on schedule out of 60 children who were due for screening in the same period, giving a screening completion rate of 117 percent, computed as 57 plus 60 and multiplied by 100.

A primary care pediatric practice audit counts 57 children who completed developmental screening on schedule out of 60 children who were due for screening in the same period, giving a screening completion rate of 95 percent, computed as 57 divided by 60 and multiplied by 100.

A primary care pediatric practice audit counts 57 children who completed developmental screening on schedule out of 60 children who were due for screening in the same period, giving a screening completion rate of 90 percent, computed as 57 divided by 60 and multiplied by 100.

questions.explanation: A rate above the raw screened count would be impossible here, because the screened children are a subset of the children who were due. That is the sound approach to screening completion calculation 5.

questions.question: Marta is reviewing the plan of care for a newborn at a first office visit after hospital discharge at a rural pediatric clinic. Which of the following best describes coordinating durable medical equipment and supplies?

answers.text: For durable medical equipment, the practitioner submits an order and assumes delivery, fit, and family training all occurred as planned.
For durable medical equipment, the practitioner orders the same size at each renewal without checking growth or current fit.
For durable medical equipment, the practitioner documents functional need, follows up on delivery and fit, and reassesses equipment as the child grows or condition changes.
For durable medical equipment, the practitioner documents the equipment brand preference but omits the functional reason it is needed.

questions.explanation: An order alone does not guarantee the child received equipment that fits, works, and that caregivers can use safely. This is the standard pediatric primary care practice whenever coordinating durable medical equipment and supplies is at issue.

questions.question: A care team at a school-based health center is discussing how to handle a recurring situation. The situation turns on pubertal growth spurt monitoring. Which proposition states the sound approach?

answers.text: Growth velocity during puberty should stay flat, and any acceleration signals a disorder.
Pubertal staging adds nothing to growth interpretation once chronological age is known.
All adolescents begin and complete the growth spurt at exactly the same age.
During puberty, growth velocity normally accelerates and is interpreted alongside pubertal staging and overall tempo.

questions.explanation: A pubertal spurt is expected, and its timing relative to staging helps judge whether tempo is typical. The other choices distort the principle behind pubertal growth spurt monitoring.

questions.question: A training session for pediatric nurse practitioners at a community children's health clinic takes up a practice scenario. Which statement about growth chart trajectory tracking correctly resolves the issue presented?

answers.text: Growth should be assessed from a single weight measurement without regard to prior trajectory or length.
A percentile line crossing should always be labeled failure to thrive without further assessment.
Head circumference tracking can stop in the first month because brain growth is complete by then.
Growth should be assessed by plotting weight, length or height, and head circumference in infancy on appropriate growth charts and following trajectory over time.

questions.explanation: Head circumference in infancy reflects brain growth and belongs with weight and length in routine growth surveillance. The other choices distort the principle behind growth chart trajectory tracking.

questions.question: Dario is a newly certified pediatric nurse practitioner being mentored at a suburban pediatric office. Regarding preventive visit completion calculation 3, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A pediatric primary care practice audit counts 240 children who completed their scheduled preventive visits out of 168 children who were due for a preventive visit in the same period, giving a preventive visit completion rate of 142.86 percent, computed as 240 divided by 168 and multiplied by 100.

A pediatric primary care practice audit counts 168 children who completed their scheduled preventive visits out of 240 children who were due for a preventive visit in the same period, giving a preventive visit completion rate of 168 percent, computed as the count of 168 alone without regard to the total.

A pediatric primary care practice audit counts 168 children who completed their scheduled preventive visits out of 240 children who were due for a preventive visit in the same period, giving a preventive visit completion rate of 70 percent, computed as 168 divided by 240 and multiplied by 100.

A pediatric primary care practice audit counts 168 children who completed their scheduled preventive visits out of 240 children who were due for a preventive visit in the same period, giving a preventive visit completion rate of 65 percent, computed as 168 divided by 240 and multiplied by 100.

questions.explanation: Dividing by the number due, rather than by the number seen, is what makes the figure a completion rate instead of a raw visit count. The other choices distort the principle behind preventive visit completion calculation 3.

questions.question: Priya has asked Oscar, an experienced pediatric nurse practitioner, a question about a case under review. Regarding nichq vanderbilt adhd rating scales, which choice states the practice a pediatric nurse practitioner should follow?

answers.text: The NICHQ Vanderbilt scales collect parent and teacher reports of attention and behavior symptoms plus performance, helping evaluate attention-deficit hyperactivity concerns across settings.
A single Vanderbilt form completed at home diagnoses attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder alone.
Teacher input is unnecessary because symptoms at school rarely inform the evaluation.
The Vanderbilt scales measure medication blood levels for stimulant therapy.

questions.explanation: Cross-setting evidence matters because diagnostic thinking requires symptoms and impairment in more than one environment. That is the sound approach to nichq vanderbilt adhd rating scales.

questions.question: Clara is a newly certified pediatric nurse practitioner being mentored at a school-based health center. Regarding staple removal technique and wound check, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Staples should be removed by twisting each staple sideways with fingers until metal tears free from skin.
A dedicated staple remover is optional because straight pulling causes no additional pain or wound disruption.
Staple removal uses a dedicated remover placed under the staple center, squeezing to bend the staple upward and lift ends free, after confirming adequate wound approximation and healing.
Remaining staples should be cut flush at skin level and left embedded when removal is difficult.

questions.explanation: Counting removed staples and inspecting the line afterward confirm complete removal and early detection of problems. That is the sound approach to staple removal technique and wound check.

questions.question: Marta is a pediatric nurse practitioner at a rural pediatric clinic reviewing a sampled case file. Which of the following best describes contacting child protective services for suspected maltreatment?

answers.text: When findings raise reasonable suspicion of maltreatment, the practitioner contacts child protective services as required, documents objective findings, and does not delay the report to investigate independently.
When findings raise reasonable suspicion of maltreatment, the practitioner waits for proof beyond doubt before contacting child protective services.
When findings raise reasonable suspicion of maltreatment, the practitioner asks the family to self-report and takes no further action.
When findings raise reasonable suspicion of maltreatment, the practitioner reports only if a second clinician independently reaches the same suspicion.

questions.explanation: Delaying a report to confront anyone or gather proof can place a child at further risk and interfere with the agency response. This is the standard pediatric primary care practice whenever contacting child protective services for suspected maltreatment is at issue.

questions.question: A nurse manager at a pediatric primary care practice reviews a practice question with pediatric nurse practitioner Clara. Regarding growth chart trajectory tracking, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: Growth should be assessed from a single weight measurement without regard to prior trajectory or length.
Growth should be judged mainly by comparing a child with siblings at the same age in the family.
A percentile line crossing should always be labeled failure to thrive without further assessment.
Growth should be assessed by plotting weight, length or height, and head circumference in infancy on appropriate growth charts and following trajectory over time.

questions.explanation: Using appropriate charts and accurate technique prevents mislabeling normal variation as abnormal growth in childhood. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about growth chart trajectory tracking.

questions.question: During a case review at a pediatric primary care practice, a question about pediatric primary care practice comes up. Regarding patient health questionnaire adolescent depression, which statement states the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: A Patient Health Questionnaire result alone establishes major depressive disorder as a final diagnosis.
A Patient Health Questionnaire adapted for adolescents screens for depressive symptoms and functional impact, and any report of self-harm thoughts requires a prompt safety assessment.
The adolescent depression questionnaire is scored by parents because adolescents cannot report mood.
A positive depression screen should be filed without discussion until the next annual visit.

questions.explanation: Self-harm items act as a safety trigger that changes the visit priority regardless of the total symptom picture. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about patient health questionnaire adolescent depression.

questions.question: Lena, a pediatric nurse practitioner, is coordinating care for a school-age child with asthma seen for a routine follow-up at a school-based health center. Regarding natural immunity misconception counseling, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Counseling should explain that infection can produce immunity but carries the full risks of disease, while vaccination produces protection with far lower risk.
Getting a preventable disease is always a safer route to immunity than vaccination.
Natural infection never causes serious complications in otherwise healthy children.
Immunity from infection and immunity from vaccination carry identical risks for a child.

questions.explanation: The comparison that matters is risk: disease carries risks of hospitalization, disability, and death that vaccination largely avoids. That is the sound approach to natural immunity misconception counseling.

questions.question: Goran and another pediatric nurse practitioner disagree about the right approach and check the standard practice. Regarding medication history reconciliation, which choice states the practice a pediatric nurse practitioner should follow?

answers.text: Medication history covers prescription products only and excludes supplements and remedies used at home.
Adherence should be assumed when a prescription was filled, without asking about actual use.
Medication history reconciliation verifies current prescription and nonprescription products, supplements, adherence, and perceived effects at each visit.
Perceived side effects are not part of medication history and belong only in laboratory review.

questions.explanation: Asking nonjudgmentally about actual use reveals missed doses and barriers that a fill record cannot show. This is the standard pediatric primary care practice whenever medication history reconciliation is at issue.

questions.question: Dario has asked Alba, an experienced pediatric nurse practitioner, a question about a case under review. Regarding constipation maintenance education and follow-up, which choice states the practice a pediatric nurse practitioner should follow?

answers.text: Families are counseled that an osmotic laxative is often continued for months after cleanout, with regular toilet sits and prompt follow-up for blood in stool, vomiting, or worsening pain.
Families are counseled to stop maintenance treatment as soon as one soft stool occurs to avoid lazy bowel.
Families are counseled that withholding stool is mainly defiance and should be addressed with strict punishment.
Families are counseled that follow-up is unnecessary even if soiling, pain, or withholding continues for weeks.

questions.explanation: Explicit return thresholds help families seek care for obstruction signs rather than waiting through worsening symptoms. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about constipation maintenance education and follow-up.

questions.question: Anders, a pediatric nurse practitioner, is coordinating care for an infant brought in for a scheduled well-child visit at a pediatric primary care practice. Regarding follow-up completion calculation 1, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A primary care pediatric practice audit counts 81 children who completed their recommended follow-up visits out of 90 children who were due for follow-up in the same period, giving a follow-up completion rate of 90 percent, computed as 81 divided by 90 and multiplied by 100.

A primary care pediatric practice audit counts 90 children who completed their recommended follow-up visits out of 81 children who were due for follow-up in the same period, giving a follow-up completion rate of 111.11 percent, computed as 90 divided by 81 and multiplied by 100.

A primary care pediatric practice audit counts 81 children who completed their recommended follow-up visits out of 90 children who were due for follow-up in the same period, giving a follow-up completion rate of 171 percent, computed as 81 plus 90 and multiplied by 100.

A primary care pediatric practice audit counts 81 children who completed their recommended follow-up visits out of 90 children who were due for follow-up in the same period, giving a follow-up completion rate of 81 percent, computed as the count of 81 alone without regard to the total.

questions.explanation: A follow-up completion rate compares the children who actually returned as recommended with all children due for follow-up, so both counts come from the same recall list and period. That is the sound approach to follow-up completion calculation 1.

questions.question: Alba and another pediatric nurse practitioner disagree about the right approach and check the standard practice. Regarding interval history at follow up visits, which choice states the practice a pediatric nurse practitioner should follow?

answers.text: An interval history repeats the entire birth history in full at every follow up visit.
Changes in school, home, or routines are irrelevant to an interval health history update.
An interval history focuses on changes since the last visit, including new symptoms, treatments, adherence, and life events.
Interval history should ignore whether a prior treatment plan was actually followed at home.

questions.explanation: Interval history keeps follow up visits efficient while capturing what has changed and what needs action. Remembering this principle resolves most questions about interval history at follow up visits.

questions.question: At a rural pediatric clinic, a pediatric nurse practitioner considers the best way to proceed with a complex case. Regarding dehydration warning signs in illness, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: During vomiting or diarrhea, families should watch for markedly fewer wet diapers or urination, no tears, a dry mouth, sunken eyes, and unusual sleepiness as signs needing prompt care.
A child with vomiting and diarrhea who has not urinated for many hours can safely continue without evaluation.
Sun and heat counseling covers shade and protective clothing, sunscreen on exposed skin with reapplication, hydration, and never leaving a child alone in a parked vehicle.

A pediatric primary care practice audit counts 114 children who completed their scheduled preventive visits out of 150 children who were due for a preventive visit in the same period, giving a preventive visit completion rate of 76 percent, computed as 114 divided by 150 and multiplied by 100.

questions.explanation: The keyed statement is the wrong one. Output, tears, mouth moisture, and alertness give families observable markers that track fluid status better than guessing.

questions.question: Vera is a pediatric nurse practitioner at a pediatric primary care practice reviewing a sampled case file. Regarding urinalysis and urine culture decisions, which statement does NOT state the sound practice correctly?

answers.text: A positive bagged urine culture alone confirms urinary tract infection and its organism reliably.

In a febrile young child, urinalysis and urine culture obtained by a reliable collection method support the diagnosis of urinary tract infection, while a bagged specimen is useful mainly when the result is negative.

Pulse oximetry adds objective data about oxygenation in a child with respiratory distress, but readings are checked against probe fit, motion, perfusion, and the child overall appearance before decisions are made.

An elevated capillary blood lead result is confirmed with a venous sample because skin contamination can falsely raise capillary values, and management follows the confirmed result plus exposure history.
