questions.explanation: Simple chart math is part of the skill being tested and used in the field. Adding each deduction in turn and checking the total against the gross value keeps errors visible and prevents an overload by arithmetic slip.

questions.question: Which of the following is most consistent with safe practice in confirming the landing area can take the load?

answers.text: A load can be landed on stacked pallets or loose material if the ground at the destination looks too soft to use.
The landing area can be prepared while the load is in the air to save time between picks at a busy customer site.
Before lifting, the operator should confirm the landing area is clear, level, and strong enough to receive the load where it will be set.
Before lifting, the operator only needs the pick area checked because a load can be set down almost anywhere flat.

questions.explanation: A pick is not finished until the load rests safely, and a weak or cluttered landing spot can tip the load or trap a helper at the end. Checking the destination first keeps the final, often rushed, phase controlled.

questions.question: Regarding voice signal required elements, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: Voice signals work best as single words shouted quickly without naming the crane function involved.
The operator should begin moving as soon as any part of a voice signal is heard over the radio.
A voice signal of only a distance is enough because the operator can infer the function and direction.
Each voice signal should name the function and the direction before the distance or speed, so the operator moves the intended motion the intended way.

questions.explanation: A complete voice signal removes guesswork about which control to work and which way to move it. Giving function and direction first lets the ground operator confirm the move before adding distance or speed.

questions.question: A service crew is discussing inspecting hook latch and block. Which statement should guide the crew's work?

answers.text: The operator inspects the hook only when a sling has already slipped off it during a lift.
The operator inspects the hook, its latch, and the hook block for damage, distortion, and free movement before lifting.
The operator ties a hook latch open so rigging can be placed faster during repeated lifts.
The operator checks the hook block paint color but never tests whether the latch closes fully.

questions.explanation: The hook and latch keep rigging captured while the load moves, so checking them for damage and proper closing before lifting prevents rigging from rolling out under load.

questions.question: A service crew is discussing correct shackle use in a lift. Which statement should guide the crew's work?

answers.text: A shackle is loaded across its bow sideways to make a wide load fit the available rigging.
Shackles are loaded in line with their pin and bow, with the pin fully secured, and are never side-loaded or point-loaded in the rigging.
A shackle pin is replaced with a bolt of similar size when the original pin cannot be found.
A shackle pin is left partly backed out so the rigging can be removed faster after landing.

questions.explanation: A shackle is strongest when the load pulls in line through its pin and bow as designed, so correct orientation and a fully secured pin keep the connection from bending or opening.

questions.question: A service crew is discussing hook block function. Which statement should guide the crew's work?

answers.text: A hook block houses sheaves for reeving and provides the hook connection that carries the rigging and load.
A hook block is a solid counterweight with no sheaves, reeving, or moving internal components.
A hook block houses batteries for the radio remote and provides power to the transmitter unit.
A hook block houses the hydraulic pump and provides pressure for all of the crane functions.

questions.explanation: The block is where parts of line come together at the load end, and its sheaves, hook, and latch condition directly affect both reeving performance and the security of the rigging connection.

questions.question: Regarding anti two block protection, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: An anti-two-block device measures the distance between the truck and the nearest overhead building.
An anti-two-block device warns of and can limit hoisting when the hook block nears the boom tip sheaves.
An anti-two-block device locks the two hook block halves together so the block can be stored safely.
An anti-two-block device warns of and can limit extension when the stabilizers near the ground.

questions.explanation: Contact between the block and the tip can damage rope and components or part the line, so sensing that closing distance is a dedicated protective function on telescopic service truck cranes.

questions.question: Regarding capacity falls as radius grows, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: As load radius increases on a given chart and boom length, the charted gross capacity generally increases.
As load radius increases on a given chart and boom length, radius stops mattering once lifting begins.
As load radius increases on a given chart and boom length, the charted gross capacity generally decreases because the load is farther from the center of rotation.
As load radius increases on a given chart and boom length, the charted gross capacity stays exactly the same.

questions.explanation: Distance drives the chart. Moving the same load farther out puts more overturning effect on the crane, so the printed capacities step down as radius grows, and the operator must recheck the chart at the largest radius.

questions.question: A service crew is discussing planning the drive-in path under lines. Which statement should guide the crew's work?

answers.text: The truck can drive under a low line with the boom rest slightly raised if the operator moves through very slowly.
The access path matters only for the boom, because a truck body can safely brush a service drop without harm.
The operator should choose the shortest drive-in path even if it passes directly beneath a sagging overhead line.
The access path into a site should be planned so the truck, its body, and any raised equipment stay clear of overhead lines while driving in.

questions.explanation: Contact hazards begin before the lift, while the truck is moving and the operator is watching the road and mirrors. Planning the entry path keeps the vehicle profile clear of lines that sag or cross driveways.

questions.question: During a pre-lift review of leveling the truck before lifting, which of the following should a service truck crane operator affirm?

answers.text: The operator levels the service truck with the stabilizers before lifting so the crane works within its intended geometry.
The operator levels the truck by eye from the driver's seat and never checks any level indicator.
The operator lifts first and levels the truck afterward if the load begins to drift sideways.
The operator accepts a noticeably tilted truck when the load is light and the lift is very short.

questions.explanation: A level truck keeps the boom centered over its base and the load hanging true, while an out-of-level setup adds side pull and reduces the stability the chart assumes.

questions.question: A service crew is discussing hoisting carefully near the boom tip. Which statement should guide the crew's work?

answers.text: As the block approaches the tip, the operator speeds the winch to finish the hoist in one motion.
As the block approaches the tip, the operator watches the load instead of the block's position.
As the block approaches the tip, the operator relies on momentum to carry the block the last distance.
As the hook block approaches the boom tip, the operator slows the winch and stops before the block contacts the tip.

questions.explanation: Contact between the hook block and the boom tip can damage the rope, block, and tip, so slowing and stopping with clearance keeps a routine hoist from becoming a repair and a hazard.

questions.question: During a pre-lift review of sheave diameter and rope life, which of the following should a service truck crane operator affirm?

answers.text: A sheave that is too small for the rope increases line pull by gripping the rope more tightly.
A sheave that is too small for the rope bends the rope sharply and shortens its service life through added fatigue.
A sheave that is too small for the rope reduces bending and greatly extends its service life.
A sheave that is too small for the rope has no effect on the rope as long as the groove is smooth.

questions.explanation: Rope fatigue comes from repeated bending over sheaves at the boom tip and hook block, so matching sheave size to rope size is a basic design feature that protects the line on a service truck crane.

questions.question: During a pre-lift review of select chart for exact configuration, which of the following should a service truck crane operator affirm?

answers.text: The operator must select the load chart that matches the exact crane configuration planned for the lift, including stabilizer setup, boom length, and working area.
The operator may use a chart for a different stabilizer setup if the load looks light.
The operator should select the chart with the highest capacities when several charts are available.
The operator may select any chart for the same crane model as long as the boom length is similar.

questions.explanation: Chart selection is configuration specific. A capacity printed for one stabilizer setup, boom length, or working area does not transfer to another setup, so the chart header must match the machine as it will actually be used.

questions.question: Grace Liu, a service truck crane operator working at a rural wellhead site, is working on operator watches for people entering. Which of the following reflects sound practice?

answers.text: While operating from the ground remote, the operator keeps scanning for people entering the work area and stops motion if anyone approaches the load path.
Once a lift starts, the operator should focus only on the load and ignore surrounding activity.
People entering the area are the signalperson's sole responsibility to notice and redirect.
The operator may rely on the barricade alone and stop scanning once lifting has begun.

questions.explanation: The ground operator's wide view is an advantage of remote operation, but only if it is used. Scanning between control inputs catches the delivery driver or customer walking in before they reach the fall zone.

questions.question: Sarah Osei, a service truck crane operator working at the municipal water plant, is working on plan around lines before setup. Which of the following reflects sound practice?

answers.text: Line locations are the customer's responsibility, so the operator need not look for them at setup.
Overhead lines only need to be considered after the truck is parked and the first load is rigged.
The operator should park for the shortest load travel first and deal with lines if they interfere.
Before parking and setting up the service truck, the operator identifies overhead lines and plans truck position and boom path to keep clear of them.

questions.explanation: Truck position decides which arcs the boom can reach for the whole job. Spotting lines before setup lets the operator choose a parking spot and swing path that never bring the crane into the hazard area.

questions.question: Grace Liu, a service truck crane operator working at a customer's equipment yard, is working on electric winch motor duty. Which of the following reflects sound practice?

answers.text: An electric winch motor on a service truck crane runs directly from household power through the truck cab.
An electric winch motor on a service truck crane is built for intermittent duty and can overheat under sustained pulling.
An electric winch motor on a service truck crane produces more power as its temperature continues to climb.
An electric winch motor on a service truck crane is built for continuous duty at maximum pull without heating.

questions.explanation: Electric units draw heavy current from the truck system and heat quickly, so duty limits are a defining difference between electric and hydraulic drives on compact service truck cranes.

abim-internal-medicine.quiz_title: ABIM Internal Medicine Board Certification Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement best captures role of SGLT2 inhibitors in heart failure?

answers.text: Direct oral anticoagulants are preferred over warfarin for mechanical valve anticoagulation.
Primary prevention ICD should be implanted within 10 days of myocardial infarction routinely.
SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure hospitalization and cardiovascular death in HFrEF regardless of diabetes status.
SGLT2 inhibitors benefit heart failure only in patients with poorly controlled diabetes.

questions.explanation: Trials of dapagliflozin and empagliflozin showed benefit in HFrEF patients with and without diabetes, establishing SGLT2 inhibitors as heart failure therapy.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding diagnosis of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction?

answers.text: HFpEF is diagnosed only when diastolic dysfunction is absent on echocardiography.
Anticoagulation for 3 weeks is required before cardioversion in a hemodynamically unstable patient.
HFpEF is characterized by heart failure symptoms with left ventricular ejection fraction of 50 percent or higher.
A normal B-type natriuretic peptide level excludes HFpEF in an obese patient.

questions.explanation: HFpEF is defined by clinical heart failure with preserved ejection fraction of at least 50 percent, often with diastolic dysfunction and elevated filling pressures.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes type 2 diabetes diagnosis by hba1c?

answers.text: A fasting glucose of 100 mg per deciliter or higher on one occasion confirms diabetes.
A hemoglobin A1c of 5.7 percent or higher on a single test confirms diabetes in all adults.
A random glucose of 140 mg per deciliter or higher alone confirms diabetes without symptoms.
A hemoglobin A1c of 6.5 percent or higher on two separate occasions confirms diabetes in the absence of conditions that distort red cell turnover.

questions.explanation: An A1c at or above 6.5 percent is one accepted diagnostic criterion, and confirmation on repeat testing avoids mislabeling when no unequivocal hyperglycemia is present.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes asthma diagnosis spirometry?

answers.text: Asthma is supported by variable expiratory airflow limitation, shown by an increase in forced expiratory volume after bronchodilator on spirometry.
Asthma requires a reduced diffusion capacity on pulmonary function testing to be diagnosed.
A normal chest radiograph alone is sufficient to confirm a diagnosis of asthma.
Asthma is confirmed when spirometry shows a fixed obstructive defect that never changes over time.

questions.explanation: Asthma involves variable airflow limitation, so demonstrating reversibility or variability over time is central to confirming the diagnosis.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes iron deficiency anemia labs?

answers.text: Iron deficiency anemia is defined by a normal mean corpuscular volume and elevated reticulocyte count alone.
Iron deficiency anemia typically shows low total iron-binding capacity and normal ferritin in all cases.
Iron deficiency anemia typically shows low ferritin, low serum iron, high total iron-binding capacity, and microcytic hypochromic red cells.
Iron deficiency anemia typically shows high ferritin, high serum iron, and macrocytic red cells with hypersegmented neutrophils.

questions.explanation: Ferritin reflects iron stores and falls in iron deficiency, while transferrin rises as the body attempts to capture more iron.

questions.question: How would an experienced internist best explain aortic stenosis murmur characteristics?

answers.text: Aortic stenosis murmur intensity reliably increases as stenosis becomes critical and flow falls.
The murmur of aortic stenosis is holosystolic and radiates to the axilla.
Medical therapy with statins reverses severe calcific aortic stenosis and avoids valve replacement.
Severe aortic stenosis produces a harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur radiating to the carotids.

questions.explanation: Turbulent flow across a stenotic aortic valve during systole creates a crescendo-decrescendo murmur that radiates to the carotid arteries.

questions.question: A resident asks about severe aortic stenosis intervention threshold. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: Asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis with normal exercise tolerance always requires immediate surgery.
Aortic valve replacement is indicated for severe aortic stenosis with exertional dyspnea, angina, or syncope.
Secondary causes should never be considered in resistant hypertension after age 60.
Oral PCSK9 inhibitors are taken daily as the standard formulation for all patients.

questions.explanation: Onset of classic symptoms in severe aortic stenosis marks a poor prognosis without valve replacement, making symptoms a clear indication for intervention.

questions.question: A study group briefing turns to infective endocarditis prophylaxis indication. Which point is correct?

answers.text: Gastrointestinal procedures routinely require endocarditis prophylaxis in moderate-risk patients.
All patients with any murmur require endocarditis prophylaxis before dental cleaning.
Antibiotic prophylaxis for endocarditis is reserved for high-risk patients such as those with prosthetic valves undergoing dental procedures.
Prophylaxis is recommended for all patients with mitral valve prolapse without regurgitation.

questions.explanation: Current guidelines limit prophylaxis to those at highest risk of adverse outcomes, including prosthetic valves and prior endocarditis, for dental procedures.

questions.question: How would an experienced internist best explain cardioversion in unstable atrial fibrillation?

answers.text: Immediate synchronized electrical cardioversion is indicated for atrial fibrillation with hypotension or acute heart failure.
Thyroid dysfunction does not occur with amiodarone because it contains no iodine.
Anticoagulation replaces the need for antiplatelet therapy after coronary stenting.
Unstable atrial fibrillation should be treated with oral rate control and observation for 48 hours.

questions.explanation: Hemodynamic instability from AF requires urgent restoration of sinus rhythm with synchronized cardioversion without delay for anticoagulation.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes gerd typical presentation and first therapy?

answers.text: Uncomplicated reflux should be treated initially with urgent endoscopic dilation in all patients.
Typical reflux presents with painless jaundice and pale stools treated first with antibiotics alone.

Typical gastroesophageal reflux presents with heartburn and regurgitation worsened after meals or lying flat, and uncomplicated cases are treated with a trial of once daily proton pump inhibitor therapy.
Heartburn that improves with a proton pump inhibitor confirms esophageal cancer as the cause.

questions.explanation: Classic symptoms without alarm features allow an empiric acid suppression trial, while weight loss, dysphagia, or bleeding would prompt endoscopy instead.

questions.question: How would an experienced internist best explain community-acquired pneumonia most common pathogen?

answers.text: Valve surgery is never indicated during active infective endocarditis under any circumstance.
Formed stool from asymptomatic patients should routinely be tested for difficile toxin.
Streptococcus pneumoniae remains the most commonly identified bacterial cause of community-acquired pneumonia in adults.
Mycoplasma pneumoniae causes most cases of community-acquired pneumonia in older adults.

questions.explanation: Pneumococcal disease is the leading identified bacterial etiology of community-acquired pneumonia, although many cases have no pathogen isolated.

questions.question: How would an experienced internist best explain aki definition and staging principle?

answers.text: Acute kidney injury is defined solely by a chronic fall in estimated glomerular filtration rate over years.
Acute kidney injury is defined by a rise in serum creatinine, a fall in urine output, or both occurring over hours to days.
Nephrotic syndrome is defined by hematuria with red cell casts and rapidly rising creatinine as required features.
A normal anion gap acidosis occurs with lactic acidosis in nearly every affected patient.

questions.explanation: AKI is an acute decline in kidney function detected by creatinine trends and urine output, distinct from chronic kidney disease.

questions.question: Regarding management of acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary edema, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Beta-blockers should be newly started at high dose during acute pulmonary edema.
Intravenous fluids are first-line for acute heart failure with pulmonary edema and hypoxia.
Morphine is the preferred first-line therapy to improve outcomes in acute pulmonary edema.
Intravenous loop diuretics are first-line therapy for acute decompensated heart failure with volume overload and pulmonary edema.

questions.explanation: Loop diuretics reduce preload and pulmonary congestion rapidly and are the cornerstone of treatment for volume-overloaded acute decompensated heart failure.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how atrial fibrillation rate control first line is handled in practice.

answers.text: Immediate cardioversion is required for all hemodynamically stable patients with rapid AF.
Beta-blockers or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are first-line for rate control in atrial fibrillation with rapid response.
Amiodarone is the routine first-line chronic rate control agent for all patients with AF.
Digoxin alone is the preferred first-line agent for rate control during exercise in AF.

questions.explanation: Atrioventricular nodal blocking agents control ventricular rate effectively, with beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers preferred for most patients.

questions.question: In a board review, which statement about wolff-Parkinson-White with atrial fibrillation management earns credit?

answers.text: Acute pericarditis shows ST elevation in a single coronary territory with reciprocal depression.
Resistant hypertension is diagnosed after failure of a single antihypertensive agent.
Intravenous beta-blockers are the treatment of choice for pre-excited atrial fibrillation.
AV nodal blockers should be avoided in pre-excited atrial fibrillation because they may accelerate accessory pathway conduction.

questions.explanation: Blocking the AV node in pre-excited AF can shunt impulses down the accessory pathway, precipitating ventricular fibrillation, so procainamide or cardioversion is used.

questions.question: Which description of rheumatoid arthritis early morning stiffness matches accepted internal medicine practice?

answers.text: Morning stiffness that is worst in the evening after rest is characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis.
Prolonged morning stiffness lasting more than one hour that improves with activity is characteristic of rheumatoid arthritis.
Rheumatoid arthritis protects against cardiovascular disease and risk factor treatment is unnecessary.
Absence of any morning stiffness is required to diagnose rheumatoid arthritis in early disease.

questions.explanation: Inflammatory arthritis causes prolonged morning stiffness that eases with movement, unlike osteoarthritis where stiffness is brief and worsens with use.

questions.question: Which description of colorectal cancer screening start age matches accepted internal medicine practice?

answers.text: Average-risk adults should begin colorectal cancer screening at age 45 and continue regularly through age 75.
Cervical cancer screening should begin at age 16 for all sexually active adolescents.
Average-risk adults need colorectal screening only if they develop rectal bleeding or weight loss.
Average-risk adults should begin colorectal screening at age 30 with annual colonoscopy for life.

questions.explanation: Screening starting at 45 for average-risk adults reduces colorectal cancer incidence and mortality, with routine screening recommended through age 75.

questions.question: A colleague is unsure about contraindication to beta-blockers in acute heart failure. Which statement should the internist confirm?

answers.text: Acute pulmonary edema alone is an absolute permanent contraindication to beta-blockers.
Beta-blockers must be continued at the same dose in cardiogenic shock from heart failure.
Beta-blockers should be held or reduced in acute decompensated heart failure with signs of low output or cardiogenic shock.
Beta-blockers should be started de novo during an episode of cardiogenic shock.

questions.explanation: Negative inotropic effects can worsen low-output states, so beta-blockers are temporarily held in decompensated heart failure with hypoperfusion or shock.

questions.question: At a hospital medicine conference, the topic of mitral regurgitation in ischemic heart disease comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Ischemic mitral regurgitation results from papillary muscle displacement and leaflet tethering after myocardial infarction.
CRT is indicated for HFpEF with narrow QRS and normal ejection fraction.
Acute pulmonary edema alone is an absolute permanent contraindication to beta-blockers.
Ischemic mitral regurgitation is caused primarily by leaflet perforation from endocarditis.

questions.explanation: Ventricular remodeling after infarction displaces the papillary muscles, tethering structurally normal leaflets and preventing proper coaptation.

questions.question: Which of these statements about anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation with high stroke risk would an experienced attending agree with?

answers.text: Oral anticoagulation is recommended for atrial fibrillation when CHA2DS2-VASc score indicates elevated stroke risk.
Aspirin alone provides equivalent stroke protection to anticoagulation in high-risk AF.
Rate control eliminates the need for anticoagulation in high-risk atrial fibrillation.
Anticoagulation is unnecessary if atrial fibrillation episodes last less than 24 hours and risk is high.

questions.explanation: Anticoagulation substantially reduces ischemic stroke in AF and is guided by validated risk scores rather than rhythm pattern alone.

cssbb.quiz_title: Certified Six Sigma Black Belt (CSSBB) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: On the subject of deployment reviews by senior leadership, which statement is right?

answers.text: Senior leadership reviews sustain deployment by keeping resources fixed even when evidence shows priorities shifted.
Senior leadership reviews sustain deployment by celebrating reported activity without comparing results to goals.
Senior leadership reviews sustain deployment by punishing teams for surfacing obstacles that need executive help.
Senior leadership reviews sustain deployment by examining results against goals, removing obstacles, and redirecting resources when evidence warrants change.

questions.explanation: Regular evidence-based review closes the loop between planning and execution, so deployment learns as it proceeds.

questions.question: On the subject of p-value meaning, which statement is right?

answers.text: A p-value expresses how compatible the observed data are with the null hypothesis, with smaller values indicating data that would be less expected if that null position were true.
A p-value above the significance level proves that no effect of any kind exists.
A p-value measures the size or practical importance of the effect that was found.
A p-value is the probability that the null hypothesis itself is true.

questions.explanation: The value gauges strength of evidence against a stated position, and it must be read alongside effect size and context.

questions.question: Examined closely, six sigma focus on variation reduction comes down to one correct statement. Which is it?

answers.text: Six Sigma treats variation as a problem only in final inspection results and ignores variation in process inputs.
Six Sigma treats variation around a target as a central cause of defects, rework, and unpredictable performance.
Six Sigma treats variation as harmless whenever average performance looks acceptable on a summary report.
Six Sigma treats variation as something to increase so processes can demonstrate flexibility under load.

questions.explanation: Averages can hide harmful spread, so reducing variation makes performance more predictable as well as better on average.

questions.question: Of the statements offered on waste analysis during analyze, which one is accurate?

answers.text: Waste analysis is finished when waste categories have been named, with no need to locate them in the process.
Waste analysis during Analyze consists of urging staff to work faster at every step of the process.
Waste analysis treats all inventory, waiting, and checking as equally harmless parts of any process.
Waste analysis during Analyze examines where waiting, extra movement, rework, and other non-value-adding activity appear in the data, and links those patterns to causes the project can address.

questions.explanation: Locating waste in evidence rather than in opinion shows where process design, not individual effort, is creating delay and cost.

questions.question: On the subject of gage repeatability and reproducibility study design in words, which statement is right?

answers.text: A gage repeatability and reproducibility study has several appraisers measure a set of parts that span the usual process range, each part measured more than once, with the order arranged so appraisers do not simply remember earlier readings.
A gage study tells appraisers each earlier reading so they can match it closely.
A gage study uses a single part measured once by the most experienced appraiser available.
A gage study selects only parts known to be identical so appraiser differences cannot appear.

questions.explanation: Parts spanning the real range and repeated blind readings let the study separate part differences from appraiser and equipment variation.

questions.question: In a competency review at an automotive supplier, a question addresses process ownership at the organizational level. Which answer is right?

answers.text: At the organizational level, a process owner is accountable for end-to-end process performance, improvement priorities, and the resources the process needs.
At the organizational level, a process owner approves project reports but holds no accountability for ongoing performance.
At the organizational level, process ownership rotates daily so no one stays accountable for sustained results.
At the organizational level, a process owner is accountable only for tasks inside a single department of the process.

questions.explanation: End-to-end accountability prevents each function from optimizing its own segment while the overall process fails its customers.

questions.question: In a competency review at a hospital system, a question addresses lead time as total elapsed time from request to delivery. Which answer is right?

answers.text: Lead time is the time between two successive units leaving the end of the process.
Lead time is set by the customer as a target and does not need to be measured from data.
Lead time is the total elapsed time from when a request enters the process until the completed result is delivered to the customer.
Lead time is only the hands-on processing time, excluding all waiting and transport time.

questions.explanation: Lead time captures the full customer experience of delay, including queues and handoffs, so it is usually far longer than touch time alone.

questions.question: During a project tollgate review at an automotive supplier, a decision turns on handover to the process owner in control. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Handover to the process owner in Control leaves responsibility with the Black Belt, who continues to own daily monitoring.
Handover to the process owner in Control transfers responsibility for monitoring, reaction, and further refinement to the person who owns the process in daily operations.
Handover to the process owner in Control is complete when the final presentation ends, with no transfer of duties.
Handover to the process owner in Control means the owner accepts the results but not the control plan duties.

questions.explanation: Improvement becomes permanent only when the person who lives with the process owns its care, with support agreed for the transition.

questions.question: When a situation involving interview method for voice of the customer needs resolving at a hospital system, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Interviews are useful only when the interviewer already knows the solution the customer should request.
Interviews replace all other voice methods because a single conversation represents every customer.
Interviews gather voice of the customer through open conversation that lets customers explain needs, problems, and context in their own words.
Interviews gather voice of the customer by reading a fixed sales script and recording only yes answers.

questions.explanation: Skilled interviewing follows up on vague statements to uncover the underlying need behind what a customer first says.

questions.question: An improvement problem at an automotive supplier makes median as the middle value resistant to extremes the central issue. Which statement is right?

answers.text: The median changes as much as the mean whenever one extreme value appears.
The median is the middle value of ordered data, so half the observations fall at or below it and half fall at or above it, and extreme values move it far less than they move the mean.
The median is the most frequently occurring value in a set of observations.
The median is the arithmetic average of all observations in a data set.

questions.explanation: Comparing the median with the mean in Measure hints at skewness, and the median often describes a typical lead time better when a few cases take exceptionally long.

questions.question: A champion at a food-processing operation asks why a step involving interrelationship digraph purpose and use matters. Which explanation is correct?

answers.text: An interrelationship digraph maps how factors influence one another and identifies which factors drive many others or are driven by them.
An interrelationship digraph breaks a goal into ever smaller tasks in a branching structure.
An interrelationship digraph displays project activities against time to show the schedule.
An interrelationship digraph groups similar ideas into themes without considering influence.

questions.explanation: Counting arrows in and out helps a team find leverage points where action affects much of the system.

questions.question: In a competency review at a food-processing operation, a question addresses overproduction waste in an improve project. Which answer is right?

answers.text: Overproduction waste in an Improve project is making more output, or making it sooner, than the next step or the customer actually needs.
Overproduction waste in an Improve project is having highly skilled staff spend time on tasks far below their capability.
Overproduction waste in an Improve project is moving finished goods between buildings more often than needed.
Overproduction waste in an Improve project is any pause in work while an operator waits for material.

questions.explanation: Producing ahead hides defects and ties up space and cash, which is why lean improvement treats it as a leading waste to remove.

questions.question: A fellow Black Belt double-checking Omar's work at a manufacturing plant raises value of constructive disagreement in teams. Which statement settles it?

answers.text: Constructive disagreement means attacking the competence of whoever proposed an unpopular idea.
Constructive disagreement matters only at the start of a project and harms the team in later phases.
Constructive disagreement weakens a team, so strong teams avoid questioning one another's proposals.
Constructive disagreement improves team decisions by testing assumptions, exposing risks, and bringing alternative explanations into the open before commitment.

questions.explanation: A proposal that survives honest challenge is more robust than one protected from it, provided the challenge targets ideas rather than people.

questions.question: At a staff in-service drawn from a hospital system's cases, the instructor quizzes staff on screening trial purpose in improve. Which statement earns the point?

answers.text: A screening trial in Improve aims to set final operating tolerances for a process ready for full production.
A screening trial in Improve aims to prove to customers that the improved process meets every specification.
A screening trial in Improve aims to replace the pilot by testing the chosen solution at full scale at once.
A screening trial in Improve aims to identify which of many candidate factors matter most, so later work can focus on the vital few.

questions.explanation: Screening trades depth for breadth, narrowing a long list of suspects before the team spends effort refining settings.

questions.question: Marcus, a Black Belt at a manufacturing plant, is handling a problem involving process owner accountability for sustained results. Which statement should guide the work?

answers.text: The process owner is accountable for how the process performs every day and for holding the gains after an improvement team hands the process back.
The process owner becomes involved only during the final celebration and has no ongoing accountability.
The process owner may change improved procedures at will without telling the team or updating documents.
The process owner hands daily accountability to the Black Belt permanently once a project ends.

questions.explanation: Improvements decay when nobody owns daily performance, so naming the owner early ensures the handover lands with someone who accepts it.

questions.question: During a Black Belt mentoring session at an electronics assembly plant, a decision turns on motion waste in an improve project. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Motion waste in an Improve project is cured mainly by asking staff to move faster during their shifts.
Motion waste in an Improve project is unnecessary movement by people, such as walking, reaching, or searching, that adds effort without adding value.
Motion waste in an Improve project is the movement of pallets between sites on a delivery vehicle.
Motion waste in an Improve project is any physical effort by an operator, including the handling the task truly requires.

questions.explanation: Redesigning layout and point of use storage removes wasted motion at its source instead of demanding more exertion.

questions.question: A Master Black Belt reviewing project practice at a food-processing operation asks about type one error consequence in analyze. Which response is correct?

answers.text: A type one error means the team collected more data than the test strictly required.
A type one error in Analyze means concluding that a difference or effect is real when it is not, which can send a project chasing a cause that does not exist.
A type one error means the correct cause was found but the solution was implemented poorly.
A type one error means missing a real effect that the project needed to find and address.

questions.explanation: This false-alarm risk is the risk controlled directly by the significance level the team chooses before testing.

questions.question: At a staff in-service drawn from a logistics and distribution operation's cases, the instructor quizzes staff on interview method for voice of the customer. Which statement earns the point?

answers.text: Interviews are useful only when the interviewer already knows the solution the customer should request.
Interviews gather voice of the customer through open conversation that lets customers explain needs, problems, and context in their own words.
Interviews replace all other voice methods because a single conversation represents every customer.
Interviews gather voice of the customer by reading a fixed sales script and recording only yes answers.

questions.explanation: Skilled interviewing follows up on vague statements to uncover the underlying need behind what a customer first says.

questions.question: Something has gone wrong during a project selection workshop at a manufacturing plant, and dmadv methodology phase logic is at the centre of it. Which statement points the right way?

answers.text: DMADV begins with building the design and gathers customer needs only after a prototype exists.
DMADV moves through Define, Measure, Analyze, Design, and Verify, ending by confirming that the new design actually meets the customer needs it was built from.
DMADV moves through Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, and Control, improving an existing process step by step.
DMADV ends at the Design step, because verification of a new design belongs to ordinary operations alone.

questions.explanation: The Verify step closes the loop for a new design, testing whether the design as built delivers the performance its earlier analysis promised.

questions.question: Something has gone wrong during a project selection workshop at a financial services back office, and sampling discipline for ongoing monitoring in control is at the centre of it. Which statement points the right way?

answers.text: Sampling discipline for ongoing monitoring in Control changes the sampling method whenever results look unfavourable.
Sampling discipline for ongoing monitoring in Control lets collectors choose convenient units that are likely to look good.
Sampling discipline for ongoing monitoring in Control keeps sample timing, selection, and handling consistent with the plan, so chart results stay comparable over time.
Sampling discipline for ongoing monitoring in Control matters only during the pilot and not during normal running.

questions.explanation: Inconsistent sampling manufactures false signals and hides real ones, undermining every judgement the chart supports.

abfm-family-medicine-board-certification.quiz_title: ABFM Family Medicine Board Certification Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement about Long QT syndrome with torsades risk is correct?

answers.text: A prolonged QT interval — congenital or drug-induced — predisposes to torsades de pointes, and management removes the culprit drugs, corrects electrolytes, and uses magnesium
Myocarditis often follows a viral illness in a young patient and can mimic infarction, with chest pain, troponin elevation, and a non-ischemic pattern of injury on cardiac MRI
A pericardial effusion without tamponade physiology is managed by finding and treating its cause with imaging surveillance, reserving drainage for tamponade or diagnostic need
Costochondritis causes localized chest pain that is reproducible on palpation of the costochondral junctions, and this reproducibility is its most discriminating feature

questions.explanation: Delayed repolarization allows early afterdepolarizations to trigger polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. Syncope with exertion or auditory triggers and a family history of sudden death suggest the congenital form. The remaining statements describe other topics in this area and do not apply here.

questions.question: For Osteoporosis, which is known for low bone density with a fragility fracture, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Cushing syndrome is chronic cortisol excess causing central obesity, purple striae, proximal myopathy, hypertension, and hyperglycemia, and exogenous steroids are its most common cause overall
Primary adrenal insufficiency causes fatigue, weight loss, postural symptoms, and hyperpigmentation from high ACTH, with hyponatremia and hyperkalemia from aldosterone loss
Osteoporosis is a T-score of -2.5 or lower or the presence of a fragility fracture, and bisphosphonates are first-line therapy to reduce further fractures
Vitamin D deficiency impairs mineralization, causing bone pain and proximal weakness with compensatory secondary hyperparathyroidism

questions.explanation: Bone resorption outpaces formation, thinning trabeculae until trivial trauma fractures them. A fragility fracture alone establishes clinical osteoporosis. The remaining statements describe other topics in this area and do not apply here.

questions.question: Regarding Fibromyalgia — a topic whose hallmark is widespread pain with fatigue, unrefreshing sleep, and tender areas — which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Anemia of CKD is mainly erythropoietin deficiency with iron restriction, and iron status must be assessed and corrected before erythropoiesis-stimulating agents are used
Polymyalgia rheumatica causes bilateral girdle pain and prolonged morning stiffness with raised inflammatory markers in patients over fifty, and it responds dramatically to moderate-dose steroids
Chronic gout with frequent flares or tophi is treated with urate-lowering therapy titrated to a target urate, and treatment is lifelong and continued during flares once established
Fibromyalgia is a centralized pain condition with widespread pain, fatigue, and unrefreshing sleep without inflammation, and graded exercise is its most effective foundation therapy

questions.explanation: Central pain processing amplifies signals so ordinary input hurts. Normal investigations with diffuse tenderness and multisystem symptoms fit the pattern. The remaining statements describe other topics in this area and do not apply here.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Placental abruption is correct?

answers.text: A ruptured ectopic pregnancy bleeds into the peritoneum causing shock and shoulder-tip pain from diaphragmatic irritation, and emergency surgery is lifesaving
A tubo-ovarian abscess complicating PID presents with fever, pelvic pain, and a complex adnexal mass, and rupture causes life-threatening peritonitis requiring surgery
Placental abruption causes a painful, tense uterus with bleeding that may be concealed, and maternal blood loss is often underestimated because much blood is retained behind the placenta
Ovarian torsion is a time-critical emergency because ovarian viability declines with ischemia duration, so surgical detorsion should not be delayed by prolonged observation

questions.explanation: Premature separation bleeds into the decidua, tetanizing the uterus and compromising the fetus. Concealed hemorrhage explains shock out of proportion to visible loss. The remaining statements describe other topics in this area and do not apply here.

questions.question: Which preventive service is being delivered when a clinician arranges food and water precautions with a diarrhea self-treatment plan?

answers.text: Travel health consultation
Latent tuberculosis screening
Food and water safety counseling for travelers
Post-exposure prophylaxis for HIV (PEP)

questions.explanation: Most cases are bacterial, acquired from contaminated food and water. Standby antibiotics are reserved for defined situations rather than routine prophylaxis. Recognising traveler needing enteric illness prevention advice links the finding or treatment back to the condition.

questions.question: Which condition is most likely when repeated inhaled bronchodilator with systemic corticosteroids is started for a presentation dominated by wheeze with prolonged expiration after a viral trigger?

answers.text: Lung cancer (new presentation)
Pertussis
Tuberculosis (active pulmonary)
Acute asthma exacerbation

questions.explanation: Bronchospasm, edema, and mucus narrow the airways and prolong expiration. Severity signs — short phrases, accessory muscle use, falling peak flow — guide escalation. Recognising wheeze with prolonged expiration after a viral trigger links the finding or treatment back to the condition.

questions.question: A clinician chooses immediate intravenous antibiotics without delay, with admission and resuscitation for a presentation dominated by fever with neck stiffness, photophobia, and altered consciousness. Which condition are they treating?

answers.text: Ménière disease
Bacterial meningitis
Vestibular neuritis
Vertigo — benign paroxysmal positional vertigo

questions.explanation: Bacterial invasion of the meninges triggers intense inflammation and raised intracranial pressure. The petechial rash reflects meningococcal endotoxin-driven vasculitis and coagulopathy. Recognising fever with neck stiffness, photophobia, and altered consciousness links the finding or treatment back to the condition.

questions.question: A 47-year-old patient with COPD continues smoking despite breathlessness. They are willing to set a quit date with support. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: Long-term oxygen therapy assessment
Smoking cessation (chronic support)
Pulmonary rehabilitation in chronic lung disease
Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

questions.explanation: Nicotine dependence is a chronic relapsing condition driven by receptor adaptation. Dual-form nicotine replacement covers both baseline and breakthrough craving. In this presentation, ongoing tobacco dependence needing pharmacotherapy and follow-up again identifies the correct answer.

questions.question: Treatment with cardiac monitoring with rhabdomyolysis and compartment assessment is begun after a presentation dominated by burns at entry and exit with arrhythmia and muscle injury risk. The treatment targets which condition?

answers.text: Fracture with neurovascular compromise
Carbon monoxide poisoning
Major hemorrhage and hemorrhagic shock
Electrical injury

questions.explanation: Current follows nerves and vessels, cooking muscle between modest entry and exit wounds. Dark urine signals myoglobin from that deep injury. Recognising burns at entry and exit with arrhythmia and muscle injury risk links the finding or treatment back to the condition.

questions.question: A 2-year-old with a viral illness has a two-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure at a temperature of 39.4°C. They recover fully within twenty minutes and are alert. Which diagnosis best explains this presentation?

answers.text: Pediatric dehydration (gastroenteritis)
Croup with respiratory distress
Bronchiolitis
Febrile seizure (simple)

questions.explanation: The immature brain seizes at lower thermal thresholds during rapid temperature rises. Focal, prolonged, or repeated features reclassify it as complex. The discriminating feature here is brief generalized seizure with fever in a young child.

questions.question: A 30-year-old attends alone for headaches and anxiety. She has never been asked about safety at home. Which preventive service is most appropriate here?

answers.text: Prenatal preventive care
Adolescent preventive care (confidential interview)
Intimate partner violence screening
Postpartum preventive care

questions.explanation: Screening must never occur with the partner present. The response matters more than the disclosure: validation and options, not rescue. The discriminating feature here is patient of reproductive age needing private safety screening.

questions.question: A screening program reports that its test misses 5% of true cases and falsely labels 10% of healthy people positive. This scenario is used in teaching to illustrate sensitivity and specificity. Which action best reflects it?

answers.text: Screen for and act on social needs — food, housing, transport, cost — with referrals to community resources, and examine practice systems for inequitable barriers
Perform medication reconciliation at every transition — comparing the best possible medication history against orders — and resolve discrepancies before harm occurs
Use structured approaches — standardized criteria, perspective-taking, and cultural humility with interpreter services — to reduce bias effects and rebuild trust
Explain that sensitivity is the proportion of diseased patients testing positive and specificity the proportion of non-diseased testing negative, while predictive values depend on prevalence

questions.explanation: A sensitive test rules out when negative (few false negatives); a specific test rules in when positive. The same test yields different predictive values in clinic versus screening populations. That is why the management described is the appropriate next step for this condition.

questions.question: A 44-year-old patient develops steady right upper quadrant pain radiating to the right shoulder after a fatty meal, with fever. Examination shows inspiratory arrest on palpation under the right costal margin. Which diagnosis best explains this presentation?

answers.text: Diverticulitis
Bowel obstruction (small bowel)
Cholecystitis
Peptic ulcer perforation

questions.explanation: An obstructing stone traps bile and inflames the gallbladder wall, producing sustained rather than colicky pain. Inspiratory arrest on palpation — Murphy's sign — reflects the inflamed organ meeting the examiner's hand. The discriminating feature here is right upper quadrant pain after a fatty meal with a positive Murphy sign.

questions.question: A patient whose presentation was dominated by blood pressure uncontrolled on three agents including a diuretic is started on cause and adherence review with spironolactone as the preferred fourth agent. Which condition is being treated?

answers.text: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Atrial fibrillation (chronic rate/rhythm care)
Resistant hypertension
Secondary hypertension — primary aldosteronism

questions.explanation: Volume and aldosterone mechanisms dominate truly resistant cases, explaining spironolactone's advantage. Apparent resistance from nonadherence or white-coat effect must be excluded first. Recognising blood pressure uncontrolled on three agents including a diuretic links the finding or treatment back to the condition.

questions.question: A 66-year-old patient with confirmed PE remains hypotensive despite fluids. Their troponin and BNP are elevated with right heart strain on imaging. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: Massive pulmonary embolism
Pericardial tamponade (emergency)
Aortic rupture / symptomatic aneurysm
Acute limb ischemia

questions.explanation: A large clot burden abruptly raises pulmonary resistance beyond the thin-walled right ventricle's capacity. Shock, not hypoxemia, defines the massive category. In this presentation, obstructive shock with right heart strain after venous thromboembolism again identifies the correct answer.

questions.question: A 59-year-old with a urinary source of sepsis is hypotensive with a wide pulse pressure initially, now cold and oliguric despite resuscitation. What is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.text: Septic shock
Acetaminophen poisoning
Salicylate poisoning
Tricyclic antidepressant poisoning

questions.explanation: Dysregulated host response vasodilates and leaks the circulation while injuring organs. Lactate marks tissue hypoperfusion beyond blood pressure alone. In this presentation, infection with hypotension persisting despite fluids and a high lactate again identifies the correct answer.

questions.question: A healthy 30-year-old wonders if staying up to date still matters for them. They work in a school. The clinician decides this patient should receive covid-19 vaccination (up to date). Which approach is most appropriate?

answers.text: Vaccinate routinely at 11–12 years (can start at 9), with catch-up through age 26 and shared decision-making for ages 27–45
Reconstruct the record, use the catch-up schedule without restarting series, and give all due vaccines at the visit using combination products where appropriate
Vaccinate adults younger than 60 (universally recommended) and older or at-risk adults including healthcare workers and people with diabetes, checking post-vaccination immunity for healthcare workers
Recommend staying up to date with the current season's COVID-19 vaccine per the schedule for their age and risk, especially with diabetes

questions.explanation: Immunity wanes and variants evolve, so updated formulations target circulating strains. Risk concentrates in older and chronically ill patients. That is why the management described is the appropriate next step for this condition.

questions.question: A 19-year-old military recruit reports progressive shin pain with a discrete tender spot on the tibia after weeks of marching. Pain eases with rest. The working diagnosis of Stress fracture is confirmed and the team turns to treatment. Which is the most appropriate next step in management?

answers.text: Offer splinting and activity advice, with corticosteroid injection into the tendon sheath as effective next-step treatment
Reassure, advise staying active and avoiding bed rest, offer NSAIDs, and avoid routine imaging without red flags
Stop the impact activity, arrange protected weight-bearing, check vitamin D and energy availability, and image with MRI if radiographs are negative but suspicion persists
Offer a neutral wrist splint at night and activity advice, arrange nerve studies if uncertain, and refer for injection or surgical release if persistent or motor signs develop

questions.explanation: Repetitive load outpaces bone remodeling, creating a crack that hurts precisely at one spot. Point tenderness with a training-load history is the clinical key. That is why the management described is the appropriate next step for this condition.

questions.question: A 30-year-old patient with schizophrenia smokes heavily and has not had lipids or glucose checked in two years. Their mental state is stable. The working diagnosis of Schizophrenia (primary-care monitoring) is confirmed and the team turns to treatment. Which is the most appropriate next step in management?

answers.text: Monitor weight, pulse, blood pressure, and electrolytes closely, coordinate with specialist eating-disorder care, and escalate urgently for medical instability
Institute regular metabolic and cardiovascular monitoring — weight, glucose, lipids, blood pressure — and support smoking cessation and antipsychotic adherence
Normalize grief, provide supportive listening and practical guidance, and watch for prolonged grief disorder or depression needing specific treatment
Offer support, problem-solving and brief psychological therapy, monitor for progression to major depression, and usually avoid medication as first line

questions.explanation: Antipsychotic metabolic effects, smoking, and poverty compound cardiovascular risk. Stable mental state makes the physical-health work the priority. That is why the management described is the appropriate next step for this condition.

questions.question: A 61-year-old with hypertension wants to start exercising but is unsure how much is enough or safe. The clinician decides this patient should receive physical activity prescription. Which approach is most appropriate?

answers.text: Counsel a Mediterranean- or DASH-style pattern — vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, fish, olive oil; limited sodium, processed meat, and added sugar — with dietitian support
Ask, advise clearly to quit, assess readiness, assist with pharmacotherapy and referral to cessation support, and arrange follow-up (the 5 As)
Deliver a brief intervention linking drinking to health, advise cutting below guideline limits, agree on goals, and arrange follow-up — referring dependent drinkers for specialist treatment
Prescribe at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly plus muscle strengthening twice weekly, built up gradually from the patient's baseline

questions.explanation: Dose-response benefits begin well below the full target, so starting small succeeds. Brisk walking at a talk-but-not-sing pace defines moderate intensity. That is why the management described is the appropriate next step for this condition.

nyc-sanitation-worker-dsny.quiz_title: NYC Sanitation Worker (DSNY) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Sanitation Worker Kowalski is unsure of an assignment detail at roll call. What is the right move?

answers.text: Skip the uncertain stop
Assume the printed sheet is complete despite the doubt
Ask at roll call, in the garage, before departure — roll call exists to confirm the assignment while questions can still be answered cheaply
Ask a resident at the first stop

questions.explanation: The passage of the work itself teaches this: roll call is where assignments are confirmed; street improvisation is the expensive substitute. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: Sanitation Worker Delgado detects a change in the truck's fuel consumption. Which response is best?

answers.text: Top up from another truck to hide the numbers
Report the change; a sudden rise in consumption is a symptom that can point to a mechanical problem worth checking
Drive less carefully to save fuel personally
Say nothing because fuel is not the crew's budget

questions.explanation: Inductive reasoning connects a consumption change to a possible underlying fault; reporting the pattern is how small problems stay small. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: The published passing standard for the Sanitation Worker written test is what?

answers.text: A score in the top 10% only
At least 70%
At least 60%
At least 80%

questions.explanation: The Notice of Examination states it directly: a candidate must achieve a score of at least 70% to pass the test. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Ice from freezing rain coats Canal Street. Which statement guides Sanitation Worker Baptiste's response?

answers.text: Freezing rain bonds ice to every surface including wires and limbs, making traction, falling-branch, and surface-bond problems that salting and caution — not ordinary plowing — address
Branches are safer when ice-weighted
Freezing rain is just wet snow and plows the same
Traction improves because rain washes salt in

questions.explanation: Ice storms are a different emergency class: bonded surfaces, loaded limbs and wires, and traction loss everywhere at once. Choosing well here depends on the details in front of you, not on habit.

questions.question: Broken glass dominates a set-out on Route 26. Which handling is right?

answers.text: Handle the bin as sharps-bearing material: gloves, controlled movement, and no reaching into the bin
Dump the bin from shoulder height to empty it fast
Refuse the bin and leave it untagged
Reach in and compress the glass by hand

questions.explanation: Broken glass changes the bin's handling class: gloved, controlled, and never hand-compressed or reached into.

questions.question: Heat-stroke signs appear in a crew member on Route 21. What should Sanitation Worker Donnelly do? The matter comes up on Route 21 during the 6 a.m.-to-2 p.m. shift.

answers.text: Offer them coffee for energy
Finish the block first, then decide
Treat it as a medical emergency: stop work, get the worker to shade, cool them, and get medical help immediately
Tell them to sit in the hot cab until the shift ends

questions.explanation: Confusion plus stopped sweating in heat is heat stroke until proven otherwise — minutes matter and the route does not.

questions.question: Moving a heavy drum at the Manhattan district garage, Sanitation Worker Delgado should rely on what? The question arises near Riverside Drive during the day shift.

answers.text: Tipping it end over end solo
Carrying it against the chest
A drum handler or dolly and a second worker as needed — heavy drums are equipment moves, not grip tests
Rolling the drum on its side across the floor alone

questions.explanation: Drums are moved with the devices made for them; improvised rolling, tipping, and dragging spill chemicals and injure backs. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: An overweight container sits at a stop on Route 9. What is Sanitation Worker Baptiste expected to do? The question arises near Maple Street during the 4 p.m.-to-midnight shift.

answers.text: Lift it alone quickly before the weight registers
Empty half of it onto the sidewalk and take the rest
Not strain to lift it alone; handle it as procedures direct for overweight or improper material, using the crew and equipment as assigned and reporting it
Tip it into the street and load it from there

questions.explanation: Overweight and improper loads are handled by procedure and teamwork, not by a solo strain injury or by dumping material on the sidewalk. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: A coworker in the truck's path on Summit Avenue cannot hear warnings. What should Sanitation Worker Kaminski do? The situation develops at 4:05 a.m. on Route 15.

answers.text: Let the operator decide without warning
Throw a light object near the coworker to startle them clear
Shout louder until the truck's movement finishes
Stop the truck's movement first, then get the coworker's visual attention — safety communication that cannot be received has not happened

questions.explanation: If the message cannot land, movement stops; a warning shouted at headphones is no warning at all.

questions.question: Sanitation Worker Whitaker is working on Riverside Drive when a strong chemical smell and visible vapor rise from a storm drain after an illegal dumping. What is the crew's course?

answers.text: Pour water in to flush it away
Cover the drain and continue working beside it
Send the newest worker to check it
Move upwind and clear, keep others away, and report it as a hazardous-material event; drains concentrate unknown chemicals and their vapors

questions.explanation: Unknown vapors are never identified by nose at close range; upwind distance and a hazmat report are the response. It is the response a supervisor would expect on this fact pattern.

questions.question: While preparing the truck at the Bronx district garage, Sanitation Worker Donnelly smells fuel strongly near the vehicle. What is the first concern?

answers.text: Ignore it because fuel smells are normal at garages
Start the truck to see if the smell clears
Wash the area down and depart
Keep ignition sources away, do not start the truck, and report the suspected leak at once

questions.explanation: Fuel vapor plus ignition is a fire scenario; the truck stays off and the leak is reported before anything else happens. It is the response a supervisor would expect on this fact pattern.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences about sanitation work is written correctly? This is discussed at roll call before the 6 a.m.-to-2 p.m. shift.

answers.text: By the time the plows reached the avenue, the snow already had covered the crosswalks under it.
By the time the plows reached the avenue, the snow had already covered the crosswalks.
By the time the plows reached the avenue, the snow had already covered the crosswalks it.
By the time the plows reached the avenue the snow had already cover the crosswalks.

questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had covered' correctly orders the earlier event before the plows' arrival. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: After plowing, meltwater on Canal Street will refreeze overnight into black ice at a shaded dip. Sanitation Worker Reyes passes it in the afternoon. What foresight applies? The question arises near Canal Street during the midnight-to-8 a.m. shift.

answers.text: Close the street personally for the night
Treat or report the spot now — salt the dip or flag it for the night operation — because meltwater plus a cold shaded surface is a known black-ice recipe
Tell residents to warn each other
Ignore it because it is currently just water

questions.explanation: Combining today's meltwater with tonight's cold and the shade pattern predicts the hazard; acting in the afternoon is cheaper than the night crash. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Sanitation Worker Reyes is assigned a litter basket route on Cedar Street: public litter baskets are overflowing. What is the work? The question arises near Cedar Street during the night shift.

answers.text: Empty and reline the baskets and clean the litter spilled around them so the corner is left tidy
Swap full baskets with emptier ones down the block
Push overflow down into the basket to make room
Empty only the fullest basket on each corner

questions.explanation: Basket service includes the spill around the basket; compressing, removing, or ignoring overflow defeats the assignment.

questions.question: In Sanitation Worker Kowalski's report for Lakeshore Road, a witness disagrees with the crew. What should the report do? This is discussed at roll call before the 6 a.m.-to-2 p.m. shift.

answers.text: Leave the event out of the report entirely
Record both accounts as accounts, attributed to who said them, without resolving the conflict personally
Rewrite the crew's account to match the witness
Omit the witness's account because it conflicts

questions.explanation: Reports attribute statements to their makers; deciding between accounts is the investigator's job, not the writer's.

questions.question: An oil-slick floor is found at the Manhattan district garage. What should Sanitation Worker Marchetti do? This is worked through at the Manhattan district garage on the 6 a.m.-to-2 p.m. shift.

answers.text: Walk carefully and say nothing
Clean it only if a supervisor tours the garage
Pour water on it to thin it
Warn others and mark or guard the slick, then clean it or report it for cleaning — in that protective order

questions.explanation: Slip hazards are controlled first (warn and guard) and removed second; silence makes the next person's fall your doing.

questions.question: Sanitation Worker Salazar sees a coworker on Route 12 lifting heavy bags with a twisting motion and no leg drive. What is the helpful, correct response? The scenario is set at the Queens East district garage during the 4 p.m.-to-midnight shift.

answers.text: Speak up, show or suggest the safer lifting method, and help with the heaviest items as a crew
Tell the coworker injuries are part of the job
Take over all of the coworker's lifting for the rest of the route
Film the coworker for the supervisor instead of helping

questions.explanation: Crews protect each other: correct the method in the moment and share the heavy work, rather than watching an injury develop.

questions.question: The Physical Work. Sanitation work is lifting work: bags, cans, containers, and bulk items, hundreds of times a shift, in weather that ranges from ice to extreme heat. The safe method is consistent — size up the load before lifting, get help or equipment for the heaviest items, lift with the legs, and avoid twisting under load. Fatigue is part of the hazard: technique that is sound in the first hour degrades by the sixth, which is why crews pace themselves and rotate the heaviest stops. An injury reported early is a strain treated; the same injury hidden for a week of shifts can become a surgery. Reporting pain is not weakness in this work; it is maintenance of the only equipment that cannot be replaced. According to the passage, why does fatigue matter to technique?

answers.text: Rotation is a reward for senior workers
Fatigue improves focus
Sound technique degrades as the shift wears on, so crews pace and rotate heavy stops
Technique matters only in the first hour

questions.explanation: Degrading technique under fatigue is why pacing and rotation exist.

questions.question: A load weighs 4,000 pounds. Using 2,000 pounds per ton, how many tons is the load?

answers.text: 2 tons
3 tons
1 tons
4 tons

questions.explanation: 4,000 ÷ 2,000 = 2 tons. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: After the Storm. When snowfall ends, snow work does not. Plowed snow must be pushed back from intersections where banks block sight lines, cleared from bus stops and crosswalks where people board and cross, and removed from around hydrants and catch basins. Melting is its own operation: as temperatures rise, meltwater must reach the basins, or it ponds and refreezes at night into sheets of ice on the same streets the plows cleared. Supervisors keep crews on snow duty through this phase because the hazards of the melt — flooding, refreeze, and hidden ice at crossings — injure as many people as the storm itself. According to the passage, why must meltwater reach the catch basins? Consider the passage carefully.

answers.text: Basins filter the melt for reuse
Otherwise it ponds and refreezes at night into sheets of ice
Refreeze improves traction
Meltwater damages the plows

questions.explanation: Ponding and refreeze are the stated consequences. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

corrections-officer-ntn-react.quiz_title: Corrections Officer Entrance — NTN REACT Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Resident Zimmer tells Officer Tom Beckett he has been having thoughts of harming himself and asks that nobody else be told. What should Officer Tom Beckett do?

answers.text: Stay with him, take the statement seriously, and notify Sergeant Nguyen and medical or mental-health staff immediately, explaining that this kind of report cannot be kept secret
Promise complete secrecy and check on him again next week
Tell him only staff with a counseling title may hear such reports, so he should wait
Tell him to think about his family and return him to the general population without reporting

questions.explanation: Any statement about self-harm is acted on at once: stay with the resident, notify the supervisor and clinical staff, and be honest that safety reports cannot be kept confidential. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: A formal count in Granite Unit comes up one resident short, and movement records do not explain the difference. What must happen next?

answers.text: Residents are asked to account for the missing resident
The roster is corrected to match the physical count
The count is cleared and rechecked at the next scheduled count
Movement stays stopped, a recount is taken, and Sergeant Nguyen is notified while the discrepancy is resolved

questions.explanation: An unexplained shortage holds movement, triggers a recount, and goes to the sergeant at once — a count is never cleared on an assumption. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Scores from a REACT administration are used by —

answers.text: The candidate's academy class
The agencies the candidate designates through NTN, which make their own hiring decisions
NTN, which hires officers directly
No one; scores are for the candidate only

questions.explanation: NTN administers and reports; the designated hiring agencies decide. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: The sentence below comes from study material for corrections officers. Choose the best word for the blank: After the disturbance, staff ___ the area before residents were allowed to return.

answers.text: searched
decorated
painted
assigned to residents

questions.explanation: Areas are checked for hazards and contraband — staff 'searched' the area. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: Two officers disagree in front of residents about whether recreation should be cut short because of an approaching storm. What should Officer Grace Donnelly do first?

answers.text: Debate it in front of the residents until one prevails
Split the group: half stay out with one officer, half go in
One officer takes the lead per the post orders and the weather guidance, the disagreement is settled away from the residents, and the decision is communicated as a single staff position
Let the residents vote on staying out

questions.explanation: Residents see one staff position; disagreements are resolved off-stage through post orders and the chain, never auctioned in the yard. The other choices fail on the facts given, on the standard, or on both.

questions.question: Officer Marcus Doyle is double-checking a count with a colleague and their two tallies differ by one resident. What is the soundest course of action for Officer Marcus Doyle?

answers.text: Clear the count and recount at the next scheduled count
Assume a resident is in the shower and clear the count
Ask residents whether anyone is missing
Stop movement, recount both areas carefully, and reconcile against the roster and movement records before declaring the count clear — and notify Sergeant Osei if it does not reconcile promptly

questions.explanation: A one-resident discrepancy is never averaged or assumed away: movement stops, the recount is methodical, and supervision is involved until it reconciles. It is the response a supervisor would expect on this fact pattern.

questions.question: The sentence below comes from study material for corrections officers. Choose the best word for the blank: A backup officer should be ___ before staff enter a cell to move a non-compliant resident.

answers.text: off duty
a resident
uninformed
present

questions.explanation: Safety practice requires backup 'present'. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Officer Tom Beckett records this observation while on post in the kitchen at 6:30 p.m.. A resident wearing a brown coat and blue sweatpants is seated near the television area, carrying a book. According to the observation, where is the resident?

answers.text: Near the television area
Near the officer's desk
Near the phone bank
Near the stairs

questions.explanation: The scene places the resident near the television area; the location is stated in the observation. This follows directly from the information given in the stem.

questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly in this sentence: 'The officer kept the ___ until the end of the shift.' Staff in Granite Unit consider the matter on the morning shift.

answers.text: resceipt
reciept
receippt
receipt

questions.explanation: 'Receipt' follows the 'i before e except after c' pattern reversed after c: r-e-c-e-i-p-t.

questions.question: Resident Zimmer complains that Officer Julia Brandt always searches his cell and never searches the cell across the hall, and says he will file a grievance. Which action handles this situation most professionally?

answers.text: Apologize and offer to skip his next scheduled search
Warn him that grievances affect how staff view him
Tell him which officer ordered the search pattern
Respond evenly, explain that searches follow the schedule and orders rather than personal choice, and tell him how to file the grievance if he wishes
