questions.question: An association executive faces this situation: routine approvals and informational reports are grouped for a single vote so the board can spend its meeting on strategy and policy questions. Which concept does this situation primarily illustrate?

answers.text: a portion of a board meeting held without staff present, used for sensitive matters such as chief executive evaluation, litigation, or personnel concerns
a meeting practice that groups routine, noncontroversial items for approval in a single motion so board time can focus on deliberation and strategy
the requirement that a minimum number of voting members be present for official action, together with fair procedures that make votes valid and binding
the official record of board proceedings that documents decisions, votes, and assigned actions as the legal memory of the organization

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on consent agenda. A meeting practice that groups routine, noncontroversial items for approval in a single motion so board time can focus on deliberation and strategy — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Board time is the scarcest governance resource, and the consent agenda protects it for questions only the board can answer. The practice works only when directors receive material in advance and any member can pull an item for discussion. Used well, it signals trust in preparation while keeping oversight intact. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: An association executive faces this situation: contributions are thanked specifically and promptly, in forms the volunteers themselves value, from public honor to quiet personal gratitude. Which concept does this situation primarily illustrate?

answers.text: the definition of ethical standards for professional conduct that align with the organization's vision and mission and the interests of its stakeholders
the recognition of volunteer contributions in specific, timely, and personally meaningful ways that sustain engagement
the accountable management of volunteer performance, addressing missed commitments directly and respectfully to protect the work and other volunteers
the raising of awareness of ethical standards through education, discussion, and guidance so members understand and adhere to them

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on volunteer recognition. The recognition of volunteer contributions in specific, timely, and personally meaningful ways that sustain engagement — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Recognition works when it is specific: people treasure being seen for what they actually did. Matching the form to the person, public or private, grand or simple, matters more than the budget. Executives build recognition into the rhythm of service rather than reserving it for annual ceremonies that arrive after enthusiasm has cooled. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: Consider what happens when leadership opens planning sessions by examining emerging trends and possible futures, rewarding staff who surface uncomfortable signals early. The practice being demonstrated here is best understood as which of these ideas?

answers.text: the development of people through mentoring and coaching that builds judgment, confidence, and leadership capacity across the organization
a culture of inquiry that assesses the impact of trends, future scenarios, challenges, and opportunities on the organization
the modeling of self care and wellness behaviors by leaders to encourage workforce satisfaction, health, and sustained productivity
the practice of seeking new perspectives and growth opportunities to increase the executive's own effectiveness and build team capacity

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on culture of inquiry. A culture of inquiry that assesses the impact of trends, future scenarios, challenges, and opportunities on the organization — this is what the described practice demonstrates. A culture of inquiry treats the future as something to be studied together rather than feared or ignored. Regular scanning, scenario thinking, and welcome for uncomfortable signals keep strategy honest. Executives build it by asking future focused questions often and by thanking, visibly, the people who bring inconvenient evidence. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: Consider what happens when former members are approached with curiosity about what changed and offers matched to their answers, rather than with generic discount pressure. The practice being demonstrated here is best understood as which of these ideas?

answers.text: the definition of goals and key performance indicators for membership recruitment and retention, monitored so performance can be managed
the recovery of lapsed members through inquiry into their reasons and offers matched to their current needs
the determination of the membership business model and value proposition so they align with the mission and strategic goals
the clear statement of the distinctive value members receive, which explains why joining and renewing are worth their cost

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on lapsed member recovery. The recovery of lapsed members through inquiry into their reasons and offers matched to their current needs — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Lapsed members are a research asset and a recoverable relationship in one. Asking what changed, and answering it genuinely, wins back some and teaches how to keep the rest. Executives resist pure discounting, because a member recovered only by price is a member rented, not regained. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: An association executive faces this situation: the conference is designed so remote participants gain real learning and connection rather than a passive window into a room designed for others. Which concept does this situation primarily illustrate?

answers.text: the design of events that serve in person and remote participants with genuine learning and engagement for both audiences
the management of relationships with exhibitors through clear communication, fair practices, and honest expectations
the design of certification renewal requirements that maintain certificant competence through relevant continuing learning and fair process
the design of continuing education from identified learning needs, with clear objectives, qualified instruction, and evaluation of learning

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on hybrid events. The design of events that serve in person and remote participants with genuine learning and engagement for both audiences — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Hybrid done honestly is two designed experiences sharing content, not one experience and one broadcast. Remote participants need their own facilitation, interaction, and pacing. Executives budget for that reality or choose a single format deliberately, because a neglected remote audience pays full price for the lesson that it was an afterthought. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: An association executive faces this situation: the executive uses board and staff sessions to teach the reasoning behind strategy, building the organization's capacity to decide well without her. Which concept does this situation primarily illustrate?

answers.text: the executive's visible, accessible presence across the organization and membership, balanced with delegation so presence does not become dependence
leadership that develops organizational capacity by teaching reasoning, context, and judgment rather than only issuing decisions
the willingness of executives to make and defend necessary decisions that are unpopular, grounded in evidence and mission
the executive's practice of keeping the board and chair well informed, presenting problems with options, and preventing surprises

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on leader as teacher. Leadership that develops organizational capacity by teaching reasoning, context, and judgment rather than only issuing decisions — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Teaching leaders leave behind organizations that think, not merely comply. Explaining the reasoning behind choices builds the judgment others need when the leader is absent. The habit compounds: every well taught decision raises the quality of the next hundred decisions the leader will never see. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: During a planning review, a senior manager observes that renewal requirements are designed to keep certificants current through relevant learning, with processes that are rigorous and navigable. The executive explains that this is an example of which concept?

answers.text: the expansion of programs and services to international audiences with adaptation to local needs, contexts, and regulations
the evaluation of educational or professional programs against established standards by a recognized body, resulting in accredited status
the deliberate redesign of how the organization creates and captures value, tested through new models of membership, pricing, and delivery
the design of certification renewal requirements that maintain certificant competence through relevant continuing learning and fair process

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on credential renewal design. The design of certification renewal requirements that maintain certificant competence through relevant continuing learning and fair process — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Renewal is where a credential proves it means current competence rather than a past event. Requirements tied to real practice change, administered fairly and clearly, sustain employer confidence. Executives balance rigor with navigability, because a renewal process that is merely burdensome teaches avoidance instead of learning. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: At a growing membership organization, an experienced executive points to a moment where content is planned against audience needs and organizational goals across channels, with ownership, calendars, and quality standards. How should this practice be classified?

answers.text: the planning and governance of content across channels so it serves audience needs and organizational goals coherently
the planning of marketing activities as an integrated system in which channels reinforce one another toward shared goals
the analysis of digital behavior to understand audience needs, improve experience, and guide communication and marketing decisions
the governance of social media activity through guidance on voice, responsiveness, escalation, and boundaries that protects the organization

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on content strategy. The planning and governance of content across channels so it serves audience needs and organizational goals coherently — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Content strategy replaces random publishing with an intentional system: what, for whom, where, and why, owned and calendared. The discipline raises quality while lowering total volume, a trade audiences reward. Executives audit content against the strategy periodically, because drift toward internal convenience is constant and silent. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: An association executive faces this situation: significant agreements are reviewed for obligations, term, termination, and liability before signature, and a register tracks what the organization has promised. Which concept does this situation primarily illustrate?

answers.text: the alignment of facilities and physical resources with organizational objectives and the requirements of a changing workplace
the systematic retention and disposal of organizational records according to a schedule that reflects legal, operational, and historical needs
the determination of the organization's ongoing technology strategy, aligning systems and investment with organizational goals
the disciplined review and tracking of contracts so the organization's commitments, protections, and deadlines are known and honored

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on contract discipline. The disciplined review and tracking of contracts so the organization's commitments, protections, and deadlines are known and honored — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Organizations are bound by what they sign long after the signers forget. Review before signature and a living register of commitments prevent surprise obligations and missed renewals. Executives scale the rigor to the stakes, keeping small agreements light and large ones unmistakably careful. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: During a planning review, a senior manager observes that a new service launches with a comprehensive plan covering audience, pricing, staffing, promotion, and success measures, all tied to the mission. The executive explains that this is an example of which concept?

answers.text: the setting of prices for programs and services based on value, cost, market conditions, and organizational needs
the management of offerings across their lifecycle, using evidence to invest, refresh, reposition, or retire them at the right time
the development of comprehensive implementation plans that ensure programs, products, and services are mission driven and ready to succeed
the development of revenue from sources other than dues, including programs, publications, sponsorship, and services, to strengthen the organization

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on program implementation planning. The development of comprehensive implementation plans that ensure programs, products, and services are mission driven and ready to succeed — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Good ideas fail in underplanned launches more often than in conception. A comprehensive plan connects audience, economics, staffing, and promotion before the public promise is made. Executives review the plan against the mission explicitly, because drift enters most easily through launches nobody tested against purpose. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: At a growing membership organization, an experienced executive points to a moment where inventories, access controls, and maintenance schedules protect the equipment, furnishings, and materials the organization owns. How should this practice be classified?

answers.text: the compliance duties attached to tax exempt status, including permitted activities, reporting obligations, and protection of the exemption
the planning and operation of technology that supports meetings and events, tested and staffed to perform reliably for participants
the protection of physical assets through inventory, access control, and maintenance practices proportionate to their value and risk
the consideration of environmental sustainability in operational decisions about purchasing, travel, events, and facilities

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on asset protection. The protection of physical assets through inventory, access control, and maintenance practices proportionate to their value and risk — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Physical assets are easy to neglect because they fail quietly and walk away quietly. Proportionate inventory and access practices keep small losses from becoming a culture of carelessness. Executives scale the effort to value and risk, protecting what matters without building a bureaucracy around staplers. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: A leadership team's working notes describe a case in which training, clear reporting channels, and prompt impartial investigation define how the organization prevents and responds to harassment. What the notes chiefly show is which underlying principle?

answers.text: the structured process of integrating new employees into their roles, teams, and the organization's culture and expectations
the organizational duty to prevent harassment through policy, training, accessible reporting, and prompt impartial response
the forward planning of staffing levels and capabilities so the workforce matches the organization's strategy and workload
the management of employment practices in compliance with applicable laws and regulations across hiring, pay, leave, and separation

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on harassment prevention. The organizational duty to prevent harassment through policy, training, accessible reporting, and prompt impartial response — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Prevention is a system, not a poster: policy people know, channels people trust, and responses people believe. Prompt impartial investigation protects complainants, respondents, and the organization alike. Executives measure success partly by willingness to report, since silence in a large organization is rarely evidence of health. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: A leadership team's working notes describe a case in which two associations weigh cooperating on shared services against combining fully, comparing control, cost, culture, and member benefit before choosing. What the notes chiefly show is which underlying principle?

answers.text: research into members' evolving needs, work, and pressures, used as the evidentiary foundation for strategy
the evaluation of cooperation options between organizations, from shared services and alliances to full combination, against mission, cost, and culture
the identification of developments that could undermine the organization's strategy or model, and the preparation of responses before they arrive
an organizational culture that habitually looks ahead, surfaces future signals, and tests assumptions before events force the issue

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on alliances and mergers. The evaluation of cooperation options between organizations, from shared services and alliances to full combination, against mission, cost, and culture — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Structural cooperation ranges from light alliances to full merger, and the right answer depends on what problem is being solved. Comparing options against mission benefit, cost, control, and culture prevents both timid half measures and irreversible leaps. Executives lead these conversations with unusual candor, because partners discover hidden reservations eventually regardless. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: During a planning review, a senior manager observes that the association periodically judges whether each coalition it joins is advancing its advocacy goals enough to justify the investment of time and reputation. The executive explains that this is an example of which concept?

answers.text: the assessment of the efficacy of each coalition relative to the organization's advocacy goals and investment
participation in regulatory processes through informed comment grounded in member experience and evidence
the determination of strategies to achieve public policy goals, matched to the venue and the nature of each issue
the establishment of prioritized public policy positions, adopted through governance, that support the organization's goals

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on coalition assessment. The assessment of the efficacy of each coalition relative to the organization's advocacy goals and investment — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Coalition membership consumes time, money, and reputational capital, and deserves the same portfolio discipline as any program. Periodic assessment against advocacy goals surfaces partnerships to deepen, redirect, or leave. Executives conduct it diplomatically, because today's peripheral coalition may hold tomorrow's essential ally. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: During a planning review, a senior manager observes that the association gathers member research and environmental evidence, debates choices about its future, and adopts a plan with goals, priorities, and measures. The executive explains that this is an example of which concept?

answers.text: the analysis of economic and other external factors to guide long term financial planning and performance
the preparation of business plans that align resources, activities, and operations with the organization's core purpose and strategy
the structured process of assessing the environment, making choices about direction, and setting goals and priorities that advance the organization's vision and mission
the systematic monitoring of external factors and trends that could affect the organization, used to inform planning and decisions

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on strategic planning process. The structured process of assessing the environment, making choices about direction, and setting goals and priorities that advance the organization's vision and mission — this is what the described practice demonstrates. A real strategic plan is a set of choices, not a list of aspirations. The process matters because evidence and debate are what turn preferences into commitments the whole organization can execute. Executives protect the process from becoming ceremonial by insisting on research, real tradeoffs, and measures that will later judge the plan honestly. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: At a growing membership organization, an experienced executive points to a moment where a plan names spokespeople, approval paths, and first messages for foreseeable crises, so the organization can speak quickly and truthfully under pressure. How should this practice be classified?

answers.text: advance planning for communication during crises, including roles, approvals, and prepared approaches that enable fast, truthful response
the use of authentic member and mission stories to communicate value and meaning in ways data alone cannot
the planning and governance of content across channels so it serves audience needs and organizational goals coherently
communication within the organization that keeps staff informed, explains reasoning, and provides genuine two way channels

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on crisis communication. Advance planning for communication during crises, including roles, approvals, and prepared approaches that enable fast, truthful response — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Crisis communication quality is decided before the crisis, in the plan and the rehearsals. Named roles, clear approvals, and honest first messages buy the credibility that improvisation spends. Executives review the plan as people and risks change, because a plan naming the departed is a fiction with a logo. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: A leadership team's working notes describe a case in which a senior staff member who serves on a vendor's advisory panel discloses the relationship and takes no part in evaluating that vendor's proposal. What the notes chiefly show is which underlying principle?

answers.text: an organizational climate in which people can report suspected misconduct or concerns without fear of retaliation, supported by clear channels and fair follow up
the embodiment of ethical principles in behavior and decisions especially when honoring them carries a personal or organizational cost
the identification, disclosure, and management of situations where a person's outside interests could influence, or appear to influence, their duties to the organization
the leadership responsibility of communicating the importance of ethical behavior throughout the organization so expectations shape everyday decisions

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on conflict of interest. The identification, disclosure, and management of situations where a person's outside interests could influence, or appear to influence, their duties to the organization — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Conflicts of interest are managed, not merely avoided, because experienced leaders naturally have outside relationships. Disclosure, recusal, and documentation keep decisions clean and visibly clean. Executives maintain living policies and model disclosure themselves, since a process used only against others quickly loses legitimacy. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: At a growing membership organization, an experienced executive points to a moment where shared costs such as technology and occupancy are distributed to programs by a consistent, explainable method so program economics can be compared honestly. How should this practice be classified?

answers.text: a documented process for evaluating employees that supports teamwork, performance, growth, and professional development
the consistent assignment of shared organizational costs to programs and activities so their true economics are visible
the delineation of job roles and responsibilities through clear, current position descriptions supported by policies and procedures
recruiting and hiring practices that ensure fair and equitable treatment and comply with applicable law, reducing organizational risk

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on cost allocation. The consistent assignment of shared organizational costs to programs and activities so their true economics are visible — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Programs cannot be judged fairly when shared costs land arbitrarily. A consistent allocation method makes comparisons honest and cross subsidies deliberate rather than hidden. Executives keep the method explainable, because a system nobody understands will be gamed or ignored, and both outcomes corrupt the decisions it feeds. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: During a planning review, a senior manager observes that an institute's executive reminds directors of the notice, quorum, and record keeping duties that surround board meetings and elections so the organization's acts remain valid. The executive explains that this is an example of which concept?

answers.text: the alignment of parent organization policies, procedures, and resources so they genuinely support healthy affiliate and chapter relationships
the use of formal agreements to delineate the lines of authority and responsibility between a parent organization and its affiliates or chapters
the obligation to conduct board activities, meetings, and governance in compliance with the laws and regulations that apply to the organization
the periodic evaluation of how affiliates and chapters are structured and how they function, judged by their contribution to the organization's mission

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on board legal compliance. The obligation to conduct board activities, meetings, and governance in compliance with the laws and regulations that apply to the organization — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Governance decisions can be challenged when the process behind them ignores legal requirements, even when the substance was sound. Executives protect the organization by building compliant habits around notice, voting, conflicts, and records. That diligence also models seriousness for volunteers, reinforcing that fiduciary care is part of leadership rather than paperwork imposed on it. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

questions.question: At a growing membership organization, an experienced executive points to a moment where expense reports, credit for others' work, and promises to return calls are handled by leadership with the same care as major policy, because staff watch the small things. How should this practice be classified?

answers.text: the deliberate management of roles between the chief staff executive and volunteer leadership so decision making is effective and authority is respected
the creation of organizational performance measures that show whether the association is achieving its goals and where attention is needed
an organizational culture in which people own their commitments, report progress honestly, and expect follow through from one another
the demonstration of integrity through consistent care in small matters, which stakeholders read as evidence of character in large ones

questions.explanation: The situation in the stem centers on integrity in small things. The demonstration of integrity through consistent care in small matters, which stakeholders read as evidence of character in large ones — this is what the described practice demonstrates. Stakeholders cannot observe most large decisions directly, so they infer character from visible small ones. Care with expenses, credit, and small promises is therefore not fussiness but evidence. Leaders whose small conduct is impeccable rarely need to assert their integrity when large questions arise. The other choices describe different concepts from the same study area; each names a real idea, but none of them matches the specific practice, finding, or responsibility described in the stem, so they do not answer the question that was asked.

asis-app-associate-protection-profession.quiz_title: ASIS APP Associate Protection Professional Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes security program definition?

answers.text: A security program consists only of the insurance arrangements of an organization.
A security program is a single electronic device installed at a main entrance.
A security program is the coordinated set of policies, people, procedures, and technology an organization uses to protect its assets.
A security program is the unwritten habits of whichever officers are on duty.

questions.explanation: Protection fails when its parts work in isolation, so a program deliberately joins management direction, staffing, daily practice, and equipment into one effort.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes vendor staff turnover management?

answers.text: High turnover among vendor officers should be treated as a service risk, prompting review of screening, training completion, and familiarity with the site before problems surface.
A manager should avoid asking a vendor about turnover to preserve the relationship.
New vendor officers need no site orientation if they have worked at any other location.
Turnover among vendor officers has no effect on site knowledge or service quality.

questions.explanation: Frequent personnel change erodes site specific knowledge and consistency. Monitoring turnover and orientation keeps contracted service aligned with what was promised.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes psychological first aid concept?

answers.text: Psychological first aid requires untrained helpers to provide formal therapy to affected employees.
Psychological first aid offers calm presence, listening, practical assistance, and connection to further support, without forcing people to recount traumatic details before they are ready.
Psychological first aid replaces professional mental health care for those who need it.
Psychological first aid means pressing people to relive the event in detail immediately afterward.

questions.explanation: Early support should stabilize and comfort rather than treat. Respecting readiness and linking people to professional care keeps early help safe and appropriate.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding criminal history review consideration?

answers.text: When criminal history is reviewed, its relevance to the duties and trust involved in the specific position should be considered.
When criminal history is reviewed, the candidate favorite explanation should be accepted without checking any records at all.
When criminal history is reviewed, any past offense of any kind should automatically end consideration for every position.
When criminal history is reviewed, only offenses committed in the same building as the workplace should ever be considered.

questions.explanation: A thoughtful review weighs the nature and age of an offense against what the job actually involves. Blanket approaches can be both unfair to candidates and unhelpful for genuine risk decisions.

questions.question: Which statement best captures functional exercise concept?

answers.text: A functional exercise tests specific operations by having participants only talk about what they might do.
A functional exercise tests specific operations by surveying customers about their brand preferences.
A functional exercise tests specific operations by reviewing historical documents from past decades.
A functional exercise tests specific operations, systems, or teams in action without fully deploying the entire organization.

questions.explanation: Functional exercises go beyond discussion by making teams perform real tasks under simulated conditions. They expose practical problems with equipment, communications, and procedures.

questions.question: How would an experienced protection professional best explain visitor badge use to a trainee?

answers.text: A visitor badge should be visible, temporary, and distinct from employee badges so staff can quickly recognize someone who is visiting.
Visitor badges should look identical to regular employee badges in every way.
Visitor badges work best when they are hidden underneath outer clothing.
A visitor badge grants permanent access and never needs to expire.

questions.explanation: A clearly different badge turns every employee into a sensor, because anyone can spot a visitor in the wrong place or without an escort.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes favorable and unfavorable variance meaning?

answers.text: A favorable spending variance always means the security program performed better than planned.
A variance can only be favorable when spending is higher than the amount that was planned.
Underspending on security is always desirable even when required services were not delivered.
A favorable spending variance is not automatically good, because underspending may reflect missed patrols, vacant posts, or deferred maintenance that increased risk.

questions.explanation: Money saved by not delivering needed protection is not a genuine gain. Managers should examine what service or risk outcome accompanied any underspending.

questions.question: When reviewing the concept with a class, which statement about alternate work arrangement is right?

answers.text: Alternate work arrangements let employees perform critical tasks remotely or through manual methods when systems or sites fail.
Alternate work arrangements let employees choose any task they prefer regardless of organizational priorities.
Alternate work arrangements let employees perform only optional tasks while critical work remains stopped.
Alternate work arrangements let employees abandon critical tasks until normal systems return on their own.

questions.explanation: Manual procedures and remote access keep essential output moving during a disruption. These arrangements must be planned and practiced in advance to work under pressure.

questions.question: A trainee is asked about fence top guard purpose. Which response is accurate?

answers.text: A top guard makes a fence easier to climb by providing firm handholds.
A top guard eliminates any need for fence fabric along a perimeter.
An outward angled top guard with barbed strands makes climbing over a fence harder and increases delay.
A top guard is installed at the bottom of a fence to block digging.

questions.explanation: Reaching outward and upward over angled strands is awkward and slow, which raises the effort and exposure involved in crossing the barrier.

questions.question: On a written exercise, a question covers video verification benefit. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: Video verification lets monitoring personnel change the access rights of employees at the protected premises during an alarm.
Video verification lets monitoring personnel erase recordings from before an alarm so responders see only the alarm itself.
Video verification lets monitoring personnel view the protected premises in connection with an alarm to judge what is actually happening.
Video verification lets monitoring personnel unlock all doors at the protected premises remotely whenever an alarm occurs.

questions.explanation: Seeing the scene adds context that a bare sensor signal cannot provide, such as the presence of an intruder or an employee who forgot to disarm. That context informs the response decision and the information passed to responders.

questions.question: A study group briefing turns to survey purpose in risk assessment. Which point is correct?

answers.text: A security survey is a financial review of invoices submitted by security service providers.
A security survey is a marketing study of how customers view the organization brand.
A security survey is a thorough on site examination of a facility, its operations, and its existing protection measures.
A security survey is a brief opinion poll asking employees whether they feel safe at work.

questions.explanation: Surveys gather firsthand facts about conditions, procedures, and controls at a specific location. Their observations feed directly into vulnerability identification and risk analysis.

questions.question: In a practice exercise, which statement about restoration of essential services earns credit?

answers.text: Restoration of essential services should follow a priority order based on life safety, legal obligations, and operational impact, with progress communicated to affected employees and customers.
Restoration of essential services should keep progress secret until everything is fully complete.
Restoration of essential services should follow the order in which complaints are received loudest first.
Restoration of essential services should prioritize executive convenience over safety systems.

questions.explanation: Prioritized restoration directs limited crews and parts to what matters most first. Regular communication about progress helps people plan around what is and is not yet available.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how electric strike versus magnetic lock is understood in security management.

answers.text: An electric strike releases the latch bolt in the frame, while a magnetic lock holds the door shut using a heavy mechanical bolt.
An electric strike photographs the latch bolt in the frame, while a magnetic lock records video of the door itself.
An electric strike generates the power for the whole door, while a magnetic lock generates power for the alarm panel.
An electric strike releases the latch bolt in the frame, while a magnetic lock holds the door itself shut with an electromagnet.

questions.explanation: The two devices differ in how they secure the opening and how they behave when power is lost. Life safety requirements govern which arrangement is permitted and how free egress is preserved.

questions.question: Pick the statement that correctly states how asset valuation concept is understood in security management.

answers.text: Asset valuation considers replacement difficulty, operational importance, and sensitivity when judging how much an asset matters.
Asset valuation considers only the original purchase receipt and ignores operational importance entirely.
Asset valuation considers only whether an asset is visually appealing to visitors and customers.
Asset valuation considers only the personal preference of the assessor conducting the review.

questions.explanation: Value is broader than purchase history because some assets are hard to replace or vital to operations. Information and reputation may carry high value with no simple replacement path.

questions.question: On a written exercise, a question covers proprietary security staffing. Which statement is the correct one?

answers.text: A proprietary security force answers only to an external service vendor.
A proprietary force is staffed by workers the organization never hires.
A proprietary security force is employed directly by the organization it protects and works under that organization management.
A proprietary security force is supplied to a site by an outside firm.

questions.explanation: Direct employment gives the organization control over hiring, training, and daily direction, along with direct responsibility for those officers.

questions.question: A newly certified practitioner is unsure about staffing level cost impact. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: Adding a post costs only the wage of the single officer standing at that post.
Staffing changes can be approved on coverage grounds alone without considering full cost.
Extending coverage hours has no effect on supervision or relief staffing needs.
Adding a post or extending coverage hours increases labor, supervision, relief, and training burdens, so staffing changes should be costed as a full package.

questions.explanation: Coverage is delivered by a system of officers, relief, and supervisors working together. Costing only the visible post understates the true commitment.

questions.question: Which of these statements about assembly point selection would an experienced protection professional agree with?

answers.text: Assembly points should be inside parking structures beneath the building for shelter from weather.
Assembly points should be placed in the main driveway so managers can watch arriving fire apparatus.
Assembly points should be located a safe distance from the building, clear of responder access lanes, and large enough to hold occupants while accountability checks occur.
Assembly points should change daily without notice so occupants stay alert by searching for them.

questions.explanation: A well chosen assembly point keeps evacuees safe and out of the way of emergency operations. It also gives wardens a known place to count people and report missing occupants.

questions.question: A newly certified practitioner is unsure about identity verification in screening. Which statement gives the right idea?

answers.text: Identity verification confirms that a candidate will perform well by comparing their handwriting with successful employees.
Identity verification confirms that application documents were printed on the correct color of paper for the department.
Identity verification confirms that application documents and background records actually belong to the candidate being screened.
Identity verification confirms that a candidate lives near the workplace by checking the distance on a road map.

questions.explanation: Without this step, a clean record belonging to someone else could be mistaken for the candidate own history. Reliable documents and consistent details across sources build that confidence.

questions.question: In a review class for protection practitioners, the topic of liaison officer function comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: The liaison officer commands the personnel of every other agency that arrives on scene.
The liaison officer serves as the point of contact for assisting and cooperating agencies, helping coordinate their involvement with the incident organization.
The liaison officer replaces the incident commander when media are present at the scene.
The liaison officer handles only internal scheduling and never speaks with outside agencies.

questions.explanation: Outside agencies need a clear contact who understands the incident organization. The liaison keeps communication flowing without giving the liaison command over other agencies.

questions.question: In a review class for protection practitioners, the topic of policy exceptions and waivers comes up. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: An exception, once granted informally, should expand automatically to all similar situations.
Any exception to a security policy should be authorized at the proper level, documented, time bound where appropriate, and reviewed for the risk it creates.
Exceptions should be kept undocumented so auditors cannot question them later.
Individual officers may grant themselves permanent exceptions whenever a policy is inconvenient.

questions.explanation: Undocumented exceptions quietly become the real policy. Controlled, recorded exceptions allow flexibility while keeping risk visible and accountable.

asnt-ndt-level-iii.quiz_title: ASNT NDT Level III Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: What is the correct definition of recommended practice basis for employer certification?

answers.text: The maintained file for each certified person holding their training, experience, examination results, vision records and certification status, kept current for the life of the certification so any grant of authority can be traced to the evidence that supported it.

The minimum formal instruction time a candidate must complete in each NDT method before certification, set by the governing basis the employer adopts and scaled to the method and level, covering the theory, equipment, techniques and interpretation the candidate will be examined on.

The widely used ASNT recommended practice that gives employers a model framework for qualifying and certifying their own NDT personnel, recommending minimum training, experience and examination content by level and method while leaving the employer responsible for its own written practice and certification decisions.

The entry status of a person gaining NDT experience under the direct guidance of certified personnel, who works only under supervision, performs no independent evaluation of results, and whose hours count toward qualification only when gained under the conditions the written practice specifies.

questions.explanation: By definition, recommended practice basis for employer certification is the widely used ASNT recommended practice that gives employers a model framework for qualifying and certifying their own NDT personnel, recommending minimum training, experience and examination content by level and method while leaving the employer responsible for its own written practice and certification decisions. The other descriptions define different concepts in personnel qualification programs and the written practice.

questions.question: Tracer gas safety and ventilation oversight in leak testing can be defined as:

answers.text: Directing thermographic surveys of operating equipment, where abnormal heating patterns reveal loose connections, overloads, friction and insulation failures, with load conditions, safety distances and follow-up criteria under Level III control.
Managing the safety of tracer gas work, including asphyxiation awareness in confined areas, flammability where hydrogen mixtures are used, ventilation and monitoring, as part of leak test planning.

Planning acoustic emission examinations, including sensor selection and placement, coverage of the structure, background noise characterization and the loading sequence, since the method listens to flaws under stress rather than examining at rest.

Verifying leak detection systems against calibrated standard leaks at the sensitivity the work requires, before and during testing, so a reported leak rate or a tight result rests on demonstrated detector response.

questions.explanation: Tracer gas safety and ventilation oversight in leak testing is managing the safety of tracer gas work, including asphyxiation awareness in confined areas, flammability where hydrogen mixtures are used, ventilation and monitoring, as part of leak test planning. The remaining options are definitions of other concepts in visual, leak, acoustic emission, infrared and flux leakage testing oversight.

questions.question: Assisting material failure investigations with ndt evidence can be defined as:

answers.text: Understanding that detection is statistical, that capability is properly expressed as the likelihood of finding flaws of a given size under stated conditions, and that demonstrations and trials should be sized and interpreted accordingly.

Assessing whether a method or technique, proven elsewhere, will perform on a new material, geometry or flaw population, through literature, trials and probability considerations, before committing the application to it.

Having multiple technicians, teams or candidate techniques examine the same specimen sets and comparing their results against known truth, to measure real-world performance spread and identify best practice.

Contributing inspection evidence to engineering investigations of failed components, preserving indications and records, examining the failed part and its siblings, and reporting findings in a form that supports root cause determination.

questions.explanation: Assisting material failure investigations with ndt evidence is contributing inspection evidence to engineering investigations of failed components, preserving indications and records, examining the failed part and its siblings, and reporting findings in a form that supports root cause determination. The remaining options are definitions of other concepts in failure investigation, product research and method evaluation.

questions.question: Which statement defines specific examination in ndt personnel certification?

answers.text: The Level III duty of setting, for every method the employer performs, the specific training content, experience conditions and examination elements a candidate must complete, reflecting the method's techniques and the governing basis the program follows.

The written examination covering the equipment, techniques, procedures and specifications a candidate will actually use in the employer's operations, testing applied knowledge of the documents and acceptance standards governing that workplace's inspections.

The Level III's ongoing assessment of whether certified personnel remain able to perform their methods to the required standard, drawing on work observation, result quality, audit findings and complaint history rather than examination scores alone.

The periodic internal review of the employer's qualification and certification program, checking personnel files, examination integrity, written practice currency and actual floor practice against the governing basis, with findings tracked to closure.

questions.explanation: Specific examination in ndt personnel certification is the written examination covering the equipment, techniques, procedures and specifications a candidate will actually use in the employer's operations, testing applied knowledge of the documents and acceptance standards governing that workplace's inspections. The other choices state the meanings of different concepts in certification examinations, competency evaluation and program audits.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of infrared thermography emissivity and reflection oversight?

answers.text: Applying the simplest leak technique, pressurizing and watching for bubble formation under liquid or solution film, with honest recognition of its limited sensitivity and its dependence on pressure, time and observer attention.

Controlling the surface emissivity knowledge and reflected background effects that determine whether thermal images mean what they appear to mean, including reference emitters, viewing angle and environmental conditions.

Planning acoustic emission examinations, including sensor selection and placement, coverage of the structure, background noise characterization and the loading sequence, since the method listens to flaws under stress rather than examining at rest.

Overseeing thermographic techniques that apply controlled heating or cooling and watch surface temperature evolution to reveal subsurface disbonds, delaminations and inclusions in composites and bonded structures.

questions.explanation: By definition, infrared thermography emissivity and reflection oversight is controlling the surface emissivity knowledge and reflected background effects that determine whether thermal images mean what they appear to mean, including reference emitters, viewing angle and environmental conditions. The other descriptions define different concepts in visual, leak, acoustic emission, infrared and flux leakage testing oversight.

questions.question: In an NDT Level III course, developing certification examinations as a level iii duty means:

answers.text: The Level III work of writing and maintaining the general, specific and practical examination content for the employer's program, drawing questions from the method's body of knowledge and the employer's procedures at a depth matched to the level being certified.

The Level III's ongoing assessment of whether certified personnel remain able to perform their methods to the required standard, drawing on work observation, result quality, audit findings and complaint history rather than examination scores alone.

The controlled conduct of certification examinations by the responsible Level III or delegate, covering identity, conditions, permitted materials, timing and collection of papers, so every candidate's result is earned under the same defensible conditions.

The Level III's documented assessment of whether a candidate's earlier training or experience, gained under another employer or program, satisfies the written practice's requirements in whole or in part, and what remains to be completed.

questions.explanation: The correct explanation is that developing certification examinations as a level iii duty is the Level III work of writing and maintaining the general, specific and practical examination content for the employer's program, drawing questions from the method's body of knowledge and the employer's procedures at a depth matched to the level being certified. The other explanations describe different concepts in this topic area.

questions.question: Which definition belongs to magnetic particle technique sheet and shot sequence oversight?

answers.text: Enforcing the timed steps of the penetrant process, adequate dwell for flaw entry, removal that cleans the surface without emptying shallow flaws, and development that draws penetrant back out for viewing, since each step's timing decides sensitivity.

Overseeing electromagnetic array and field-measurement techniques used to detect and size surface cracks without removing coatings, including their calibration on known flaws and the limits of their sizing claims.

Controlling the condition of magnetic particle suspensions and dry powders, including concentration, contamination and settling checks, so the medium that makes indications visible remains capable of forming them.

Approving the documented magnetization sequence for a part, the shots, directions, currents and coverage, so every region is magnetized in the orientations its likely flaws require and no area is left unexamined by assumption.

questions.explanation: Magnetic particle technique sheet and shot sequence oversight is approving the documented magnetization sequence for a part, the shots, directions, currents and coverage, so every region is magnetized in the orientations its likely flaws require and no area is left unexamined by assumption. The remaining options are definitions of other concepts in electromagnetic, magnetic particle and liquid penetrant testing oversight.

questions.question: Pick the accurate statement about refresher training for infrequently used techniques:

answers.text: Watching for the signals that a certified person's skills need renewal, long absence from a method, repeated evaluation errors, audit findings or changed procedures, and assigning targeted refresher work before competence gaps reach product.

Renewing skill in techniques a technician is certified for but rarely performs, through scheduled practice on specimens and supervised live work, since infrequent performance erodes fluency even in experienced personnel.

Structured practical experience in which a trainee performs real inspection work under the direct guidance of certified personnel, with defined tasks, observation and sign-off, converting supervised hours into genuine skill rather than mere attendance.

The deliberate staging of a trainee's duties from observation through assisted performance to independent work under decreasing supervision, matched to demonstrated readiness at each step rather than to time served.

questions.explanation: The accurate statement is that refresher training for infrequently used techniques is renewing skill in techniques a technician is certified for but rarely performs, through scheduled practice on specimens and supervised live work, since infrequent performance erodes fluency even in experienced personnel. The other statements describe different concepts in this topic area.

questions.question: An instructor explains calibration systems and traceability for ndt equipment as:

answers.text: Assembling the inspection documentation that accompanies or supports delivered product, procedures and revisions used, personnel certifications, calibration status and results, complete enough for a customer to verify quality without visiting.

The routine checks woven into daily inspection work, equipment function verifications, process checks, record reviews and supervisory sampling, that catch drift and error while correction is still cheap.

Reviewing accumulated inspection data for patterns, rising reject rates, clustering by shift, product or process step, that signal a manufacturing or inspection drift long before any single result alarms.

The program that keeps inspection instruments and reference standards on defined calibration intervals with traceability to recognized references, status identification and recall discipline, so no result rests on an instrument of unknown state.

questions.explanation: The correct explanation is that calibration systems and traceability for ndt equipment is the program that keeps inspection instruments and reference standards on defined calibration intervals with traceability to recognized references, status identification and recall discipline, so no result rests on an instrument of unknown state. The other explanations describe different concepts in this topic area.

questions.question: In NDT Level III study, recertification of ndt personnel at interval is understood as:

answers.text: The periodic renewal of a person's certification under the written practice, requiring evidence of continued satisfactory performance and currency in the method, and re-examination where performance, interruption of service or the governing basis demands it.

The graded structure of NDT personnel qualification, running from trainee through Level I and Level II technicians of increasing independence to the Level III, with each level defined by what its holder may do, from working under supervision to performing and evaluating tests to establishing techniques and certifying others.

The written practice's provisions for withdrawing a person's certification, temporarily or permanently, for causes such as failed re-examination, loss of vision qualification, unethical conduct or demonstrated incompetence, together with the conditions under which certification may be reinstated.

The principle that NDT certification is granted method by method rather than as a general license, so a person certified in one method holds no authority in another until that method's training, experience and examinations are separately completed and documented.

questions.explanation: The correct explanation is that recertification of ndt personnel at interval is the periodic renewal of a person's certification under the written practice, requiring evidence of continued satisfactory performance and currency in the method, and re-examination where performance, interruption of service or the governing basis demands it. The other explanations describe different concepts in this topic area.

questions.question: Which statement defines surface preparation requirements for surface methods oversight?

answers.text: Directing flux leakage applications such as tank floor scanning and tubular inspection, where magnetized material and sensor arrays map metal loss, with oversight of coverage, speed, lift-off and verification digs.

Specifying and verifying cleaning and surface condition before magnetic particle, penetrant or eddy current work, since coatings, scale, oil and smeared metal can seal flaws or mask fields and signals.

Understanding specialized electromagnetic techniques for ferromagnetic tubing and plate, where through-wall energy transmission or saturation reveals wall loss and flaws that conventional eddy current cannot reach in magnetic materials.

Confirming that magnetization in magnetic particle testing is strong enough and correctly directed for the flaws sought, using field indicators, known-flaw specimens or measurement, since an inadequate or misdirected field leaves cracks invisible.

questions.explanation: Surface preparation requirements for surface methods oversight is specifying and verifying cleaning and surface condition before magnetic particle, penetrant or eddy current work, since coatings, scale, oil and smeared metal can seal flaws or mask fields and signals. The other choices state the meanings of different concepts in electromagnetic, magnetic particle and liquid penetrant testing oversight.

questions.question: Which claim about essential and nonessential variables in ndt procedures is true?

answers.text: Distinguishing the procedure elements whose change can affect inspection results and therefore requires requalification or re-approval, from those that may be adjusted without it, a discipline borrowed from welding procedure control and applied to inspection rigor.

Stating plainly how much of a part or population must be examined, full coverage, defined zones or a sampling plan, and the basis for any partial coverage, so the inspection's scope is a decision rather than an accident.

Crafting procedure documents that working technicians can follow under real conditions, clear sequence, unambiguous language, the necessary detail without burying the critical steps, and formatting that survives the bench.

Reading the inspection obligations a code, standard or specification imposes, the methods, extent, techniques, personnel and acceptance criteria it demands, and translating them faithfully into what the shop must actually do.

questions.explanation: The accurate statement is that essential and nonessential variables in ndt procedures is distinguishing the procedure elements whose change can affect inspection results and therefore requires requalification or re-approval, from those that may be adjusted without it, a discipline borrowed from welding procedure control and applied to inspection rigor. The other statements describe different concepts in this topic area.

questions.question: A candidate reads about a case: watching a routine examination, the Level III notices the technician's scanning pattern skips the overlap the procedure requires, a drift no paperwork review would ever have revealed. The concept is:

answers.text: Conducting NDT Process Audits in Operations
Method Selection Based on Flaw Type and Location
Documenting Inspection Results for Traceability
Evaluating NDT Equipment Performance Over Time

questions.explanation: The situation shows Conducting NDT Process Audits in Operations: observing inspection work as it is actually performed and comparing it with the governing procedure, covering setup, calibration checks, technique, evaluation and reporting, to find where practice has drifted from the written method. questions.question: Suppose that a qualification file is held up because a course completion certificate names the subject but not the hours or the instructor, and the training record standard is tightened to capture all three. The principle at work is:

Providing NDT Instruction as the Level III
Adapting Training to Candidate Education and Experience
Evaluating Training Effectiveness After Courses End

questions.question: An NDT Level III encounters this situation: two readers initially parse a code paragraph differently, and the Level III works the text, its references and its intent until one documented interpretation governs the job. The concept involved is:

Interpreting NDT Requirements of Codes and Standards
Specifying Extent and Coverage of Examination in Procedures
Resolving Conflicts Between Codes, Specifications and Drawings

questions.explanation: The situation shows Interpreting NDT Requirements of Codes and Standards: reading the inspection obligations a code, standard or specification imposes, the methods, extent, techniques, personnel and acceptance criteria it demands, and translating them faithfully into what the shop must actually do. Naming the concept correctly is the first step to applying it well.

questions.question: In a problem-solving exercise, a surface method flags an indication whose depth matters for the acceptance decision, so the Level III calls for a volumetric method to characterize it before the part is dispositioned. The exercise demonstrates:

answers.text: Creating Inspection Plans from Expected Flaw Types
Inspecting Components Based on the Manufacturing Process
Supplemental Examinations with Additional Methods
Method Selection Based on Flaw Type and Location

questions.explanation: The principle at work is Supplemental Examinations with Additional Methods: deciding when a finding, a limitation or an unresolved indication requires confirmation or characterization by a different NDT method, and specifying that additional examination so the final evaluation rests on converging evidence. The other options name different concepts in method selection and inspection planning that work differently.

questions.question: In a worked NDT example, two parts of the same alloy give markedly different magnetic and electromagnetic responses, and the Level III traces the difference to their different heat treatments before questioning the equipment. Which concept does this most directly illustrate?

answers.text: Material Grain Structure Influence on Ultrasonic Testing
Characterizing Flaws from Casting Processes
Heat Treatment Effects on Material Condition
Characterizing Welding Discontinuities

questions.explanation: This illustrates Heat Treatment Effects on Material Condition: understanding how hardening, tempering, annealing, normalizing and related treatments change a material's structure, hardness and residual stress, and therefore both its service behavior and its response to inspection methods. The other options are different concepts in materials, manufacturing processes and flaw characterization that work differently.

questions.question: An NDT Level III reference states: "Approving phased array applications, including focal law design, aperture and steering choices, encoding and data display, and verifying that the encoded record supports reviewable, repeatable evaluation of the examination volume" Which concept is being described?

answers.text: Ultrasonic Calibration and Reference Standard Oversight
Radiation Safety Oversight in Radiographic Operations
Radiographic Artifact Recognition Oversight
Phased Array Ultrasonic Technique Oversight

questions.explanation: The description matches Phased Array Ultrasonic Technique Oversight: approving phased array applications, including focal law design, aperture and steering choices, encoding and data display, and verifying that the encoded record supports reviewable, repeatable evaluation of the examination volume. Precise terminology matters in NDT Level III study.

questions.question: One study resource defines a concept this way: "Understanding how hardening, tempering, annealing, normalizing and related treatments change a material's structure, hardness and residual stress, and therefore both its service behavior and its response to inspection methods" The concept is:

answers.text: Corrosion Damage Forms and Inspection Implications
Characterizing Welding Discontinuities
Heat Treatment Effects on Material Condition
Surface Condition Effects Across NDT Methods

questions.explanation: The description matches Heat Treatment Effects on Material Condition: understanding how hardening, tempering, annealing, normalizing and related treatments change a material's structure, hardness and residual stress, and therefore both its service behavior and its response to inspection methods. Precise terminology matters in NDT Level III study.

questions.question: In an inspection vignette, a Level III observes this: a crew's results look inconsistent between shifts, and the Level III traces the difference to a calibration practice that skipped the transfer correction the technique demands.
