Bianca follows the special documentation comment format used by Java tools. Which of the following statements about documentation comments for methods is correct?

answers.text: Documentation comments describe a class or method for readers and can be processed into external documentation.
Documentation comments are executed before a method runs to prepare its parameters.
Documentation comments must be written in a separate file away from the source code.
The compiler requires a documentation comment on every method or the program fails.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is accurate because documentation comments are a standardized form of comment whose content describes an interface and can be extracted by documentation tools into browsable pages. The first wrong statement fails because like all comments they are ignored at execution. The second wrong statement fails because they live in the source directly above the element they document. The third wrong statement fails because they are a professional convention and a tooling aid rather than a language requirement. In the situation described, the keyed statement is the one consistent with this reasoning.

questions.question: Jae maintains an ArrayList of library book objects for a school collection and needs to pull out every book marked as overdue for a reminder mailing. His program visits each book object in turn, asks whether it meets the overdue condition, and gathers the matching books while leaving the original collection intact. He explains why the original list still holds every book afterward. With traversing an ArrayList of objects to filter a data set in mind, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Filtering an ArrayList removes the objects that satisfy the condition and keeps the ones that fail it.
A filter traversal can skip elements after the first match because all later elements will match as well.
Filtering an ArrayList of objects means traversing every element, testing each object against a condition, and collecting the objects that satisfy the condition.
Filtering requires the ArrayList to be sorted by the tested field before traversal begins.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is right because filtering is defined by testing all elements and keeping the ones that pass. The first wrong statement fails because it inverts the outcome, describing removal of matches instead of collection of matches. The second wrong statement fails because matches can appear anywhere, so stopping early loses later matches scattered through the list. The third wrong statement fails because a condition test works element by element in any order; sorting is unrelated to whether an object satisfies the test. Applied to this new situation, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: A Song method that builds a duet description documents that both song references it receives must refer to actual song objects, not absent references. A caller who passes an absent reference triggers a failure inside the method. Instructors use the incident to teach that preconditions state what must be true before a call, and honoring them is the responsibility of the calling code. With preconditions for methods and constructors in mind, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A precondition describes the state that a method guarantees after it finishes running successfully.
Preconditions are promises the caller makes about what the method will return to it.
A method must produce correct results even when its preconditions are violated by the caller.
A precondition is a condition that must be true before a method is called for the method to work as documented.

questions.explanation: The correct statement gives the standard before-the-call meaning of a precondition. The first wrong statement actually defines a postcondition, which concerns the state after execution. The second wrong statement reverses the parties, since preconditions constrain the caller inputs rather than promising caller anything about returns. The third wrong statement fails because documented behavior is conditional on the requirements being met, and violating callers cannot demand guaranteed results. Applied to this new situation, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: Ingrid is extending a greeting program so that qualifying visitors receive both a welcome line and a map offer under the same condition. She groups the two outputs together, tests qualifying and nonqualifying visitors, and confirms that both outputs appear together or not at all, unlike an earlier draft where the second output appeared for everyone who visited. Which of the following statements about blocks and braces for if bodies is correct?

answers.text: Braces around an if body are purely decorative and never affect which statements the condition controls.
Braces group statements so that only the first statement in the block is controlled by the condition.
Braces cause every statement in the block to run twice, once for the check and once for the action.
Braces group multiple statements into a single block so that all of them are controlled together by an if condition.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is right because a block is treated as one compound statement wherever a single statement is expected. The first wrong statement fails because removing braces observably changes behavior when a body contains multiple statements. The second wrong statement fails because control applies to the block as a whole, not to its first line alone. The third wrong statement fails because grouping affects selection, not repetition, and each statement in a taken branch runs exactly once in order. In the situation described, the keyed statement is the one consistent with this reasoning.

questions.question: A weather station grid holds temperature readings by day row and hour column, and the evening news wants to announce not just the hottest reading but when it happened. Luis must report the day and hour of the peak, not merely the peak value. He explains why his search remembers two extra pieces of information every time it finds a new hottest reading. Which of the following statements about locating the position of the largest value in a grid is correct?

answers.text: Locating the position of the maximum requires recording the row and column indices whenever a new largest value replaces the current best.
The position of the maximum can be worked out afterward from the maximum value alone without recording indices.
Recording only the row of the maximum is enough because the column can be assumed to be the first column.
The position tracking search can stop at the first element that exceeds the starting element.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is right because value and location are separate facts, and the location is known only at the moment a new best is found during the scan. The first wrong statement fails because the same maximum value could appear in several places or its place could be unrecoverable later. The second wrong statement fails because the column of the maximum is arbitrary and must be captured too. The third wrong statement fails because beating the starting element does not make an element the overall maximum. In the situation described, the keyed statement is the one consistent with this reasoning.

questions.question: A candidate reviewing practice material before the examination encounters this description in one of the study sets: Zoe is comparing ages, scores, and counts throughout a school records program using equality and relational operators directly on the stored numbers. She tests equal numbers, ordered numbers, and negative numbers where they occur, and she finds the comparisons behave exactly as ordinary arithmetic comparisons would suggest in every case she tries. The accompanying item offers four statements about the case, only one of which is accurate. Which statement accurately states the rule or principle this case presents?

answers.text: Primitive values must first be converted into objects before any comparison operator can be applied to them.
Two primitive variables holding the same integer value compare as unequal because they are different variables.
Primitive values such as integers can be compared directly with relational and equality operators because the operators examine the values themselves.
Relational operators on primitives compare the names of the variables alphabetically rather than their values.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is right because primitives carry their values directly, so operators have immediate access to what is being compared. The first wrong statement fails because no conversion is needed, and direct comparison of primitives is among the most basic operations in the language. The second wrong statement fails because variable identity is irrelevant for primitives, where only the held values matter. The third wrong statement fails because names are compile time labels for the programmer and play no role at all in runtime numeric comparison. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: Alma helps maintain a scoreboard that starts blank before a trivia contest begins. The conversation keeps circling back to default values in newly created numeric arrays, with Alma insisting that every claim survive a careful trace before it is believed. In the setting of the scoreboard that starts blank before a trivia contest begins, Alma wants to know exactly what is stored, exactly how it is reached, and exactly what a full review would touch. The details Alma remembers are a folded paper crane and a wooden bead necklace, and picturing them helps the entries stay separate rather than blurring together. Which of the following statements about default values in newly created numeric arrays is correct?

answers.text: A newly created integer array starts with every element set to one so counting can begin right away.
A newly created numeric array starts with random leftover values from earlier programs.
Reading a slot that was never assigned causes an error because the slot is completely empty.
Every element of a newly created array of integers starts with the value zero.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is right because a fresh numeric array is fully initialized by the runtime, with integer slots holding zero and decimal slots holding zero in decimal form, so every slot can be read safely. The first false statement fails because it contradicts that behavior and describes an outcome the structure never produces in ordinary use. The second false statement fails because it confuses a related operation, limit, or default with the one actually being described here. The third false statement fails because a careful trace through the positions and values, done in order and in words, shows the opposite result. Keeping these distinctions straight lets a programmer predict output, protect valid indices, and avoid runtime errors when storing, reading, and updating values in classroom programs of this kind. In the situation described, the keyed statement is the one consistent with this reasoning.

questions.question: During a seminar devoted to common examination traps, a presenter displays the following case and explains that three of the statements offered about it are accurate while one is not, and that spotting the single inaccurate statement among sound ones is precisely the skill being practiced: Karen is sorting single letter grades by comparing character values directly, relying on their underlying ordered numeric codes. She tests pairs of letters in alphabetical order, reversed order, and identical letters, and she finds the comparisons follow alphabetical order for the uppercase letters she uses throughout her grading program. With comparing character values as primitives in mind, and checking each statement against the facts of the case rather than against first impressions, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

answers.text: Character values cannot be compared with relational operators and must always be converted to strings first.
Character values are primitives that can be compared with relational operators according to their underlying ordered numeric codes.
For uppercase letters, character comparison order matches ordinary alphabetical order.
Two character variables holding the same character compare as equal with the equality operator.

questions.explanation: The first wrong statement is false because the band validation in the scenario succeeds precisely by using direct relational comparison on characters. The correct statement is accurate because the numeric code explanation accounts for the observed ordering. The second true statement is accurate because the encoding preserves alphabetical sequence within the uppercase range. The third true statement is accurate because character equality follows the same exact value rule as other primitives. Because the other three statements are accurate as written, the keyed statement is the single incorrect one.

questions.question: A candidate reviewing practice material before the examination encounters this description in one of the study sets: A yearbook adviser needs a seating grid printed with row numbers and seat numbers beside every name, so plain value by value printing is not enough. Sam writes nested loops whose control variables track positions as the grid is visited. He explains to the adviser why knowing the position of each name, not just the name itself, changes which loop style the task requires. The accompanying item offers four statements about the case, only one of which is accurate. Which statement accurately states the rule or principle this case presents?

answers.text: Index based nested loops are needed when a task requires knowing the row and column position of elements during traversal.
Index loops and enhanced for loops provide exactly the same information at every step of a traversal.
An index loop over a grid must always start its indices at one to match printed position labels.
Index based traversal visits elements in no predictable order because the indices change as the loops run.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is right because only index loops expose the current row and column values while visiting, which location reporting tasks depend on. The first wrong statement fails because enhanced loops supply values without positions, so the information available differs. The second wrong statement fails because Java indices begin at zero, and any printed labels can be adjusted from those indices. The third wrong statement fails because index loops advance in a completely predictable pattern governed by their update expressions. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: During a seminar devoted to common examination traps, a presenter displays the following case and explains that three of the statements offered about it are accurate while one is not, and that spotting the single inaccurate statement among sound ones is precisely the skill being practiced: Talia cleans up user input with a program for a newsletter signup form on a club website. She first extracts part of a String and then converts that part to uppercase for display purposes. Talia writes the two calls in a chain with one following the other directly. She reasons about which call runs first and what the second call receives. With chaining String method calls in mind, and checking each statement against the facts of the case rather than against first impressions, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

answers.text: In a chain the rightmost method call is always evaluated before the others.
In a chain of method calls each call operates on the value returned by the previous call.
Chaining is possible when a method returns an object of a type that has further methods.
The calls in a chain are evaluated from left to right.

questions.explanation: The first wrong statement is false because chained calls proceed from left to right with each result feeding the next call. The correct statement is accurate for that pipeline reason. The second true statement is accurate because a returned object is what makes the next call possible. The third true statement is accurate because left to right evaluation matches the reading order and determines which object each method acts upon. Because the other three statements are accurate as written, the keyed statement is the single incorrect one.

questions.question: Ines helps maintain a judge identifying the highest score in a talent contest. Since the lesson is really about finding the maximum element in an array, Ines sets the surface details aside and follows the underlying rule wherever it leads. The judge identifying the highest score in a talent contest supplies the details Ines reasons with, so a claim that fails for those entries fails outright, however plausible it sounds in general. To keep the picture vivid, Ines notes a roll of masking tape and a frayed shoelace sitting off to one side of the work. Which of the following statements about finding the maximum element in an array is correct?

answers.text: Finding a maximum keeps a running best value and replaces it whenever a larger element is encountered.
Finding a maximum requires the array to be sorted before the search can begin.
The maximum of an array is always stored at the last index because traversal ends there.
Initializing the best value to zero always works, even when every element in the array is negative.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is right because the search compares each element against a running best that starts from an actual element, so the value left standing after a full traversal is the largest one present. The first false statement fails because it contradicts that behavior and describes an outcome the structure never produces in ordinary use. The second false statement fails because it confuses a related operation, limit, or default with the one actually being described here. The third false statement fails because a careful trace through the positions and values, done in order and in words, shows the opposite result. Keeping these distinctions straight lets a programmer predict output, protect valid indices, and avoid runtime errors when storing, reading, and updating values in classroom programs of this kind. In the situation described, the keyed statement is the one consistent with this reasoning.

questions.question: In a different setting, Omar is responsible for a coach recording the fastest finishing time in a practice race. A partner suggests handling the entries with the same structure, and the two of them talk through what the structure guarantees, what it forbids, and what a careful traversal would visit. Their discussion focuses on predicting behavior in words before trusting any result the program might produce later. With finding the minimum element in an array in mind, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Finding a minimum works by repeatedly removing the largest element until one element remains.
Finding a minimum keeps a running best value and replaces it whenever a smaller element is encountered.
Initializing the best value to zero always works, even when every element in the array is positive.
The minimum of an array is always stored at index zero after any traversal completes.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is right because the search compares each element against a running best seeded from the first element, replacing it only when a smaller element appears, so the survivor is the smallest value present. The first false statement fails because it contradicts that behavior and describes an outcome the structure never produces in ordinary use. The second false statement fails because it confuses a related operation, limit, or default with the one actually being described here. The third false statement fails because a careful trace through the positions and values, done in order and in words, shows the opposite result. Keeping these distinctions straight lets a programmer predict output, protect valid indices, and avoid runtime errors when storing, reading, and updating values in classroom programs of this kind. Applied to this new situation, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: A candidate reviewing practice material before the examination encounters this description in one of the study sets: Priya prints name tags for a robotics workshop using a counter that starts at the first guest, continues while guests remain unprinted, and advances to the next guest after each tag. She can predict the whole run by reading the starting setup, the continuing test, and the advance step in the order they take effect during printing. The accompanying item offers four statements about the case, only one of which is accurate. Which statement accurately states the rule or principle this case presents?

answers.text: In a for loop, initialization runs once at the start, the condition is tested before each pass, and the update runs after each pass.
In a for loop, the update runs before the condition is ever tested and before the body runs for the first time.
In a for loop, initialization runs again at the start of every pass through the body.
In a for loop, the condition is tested only after the body has finished its final pass.

questions.explanation: The correct statement gives the true order: initialize once, test, run the body, update, then test again. The first wrong claim places the update before any test or body run, but the update only follows a completed body pass. The second wrong claim repeats initialization on every pass, which would reset the counter endlessly and contradicts its once-only role. The third wrong claim moves the test to after the final pass, yet the test is what permits each pass in the first place, including the first. The companion true statements correctly describe the starting value and the purpose of the update. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: A candidate reviewing practice material before the examination encounters this description in one of the study sets: Maya is building a grade book program for her homeroom teacher at school. The program records quiz scores for each student and calculates a class average at the end of the week. Before writing the calculations Maya lists every value the program will need. She wonders why each value must be introduced before it can be used in later statements. The accompanying item offers four statements about the case, only one of which is accurate. Which statement accurately states the rule or principle this case presents?

answers.text: A variable can be used anywhere in a program even if it is declared later in the file.
Declaring a variable automatically fills it with a meaningful value chosen by the compiler.
A variable must be declared with a type and a name before it can be used in a program.
The type in a declaration is optional whenever the variable name is descriptive enough.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is accurate because Java is a strongly typed language and the compiler must know the type and name of every variable before any statement refers to it. The first wrong statement fails because a later declaration does not rescue an earlier use and the compiler reports the unknown name. The second wrong statement fails because declaring a whole number variable does not give it a usable value until an assignment occurs. The third wrong statement fails because the type is a required part of the declaration and a descriptive name cannot replace it. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: During a seminar devoted to common examination traps, a presenter displays the following case and explains that three of the statements offered about it are accurate while one is not, and that spotting the single inaccurate statement among sound ones is precisely the skill being practiced: Elena is working with a row of lockers numbered for students in one hallway. Elena keeps returning to the length field of an array, asking what changes, what stays fixed, and what would break if a boundary were crossed. The row of lockers numbered for students in one hallway supplies the details Elena reasons with, so a claim that fails for those entries fails outright, however plausible it sounds in general. Elena can picture the scene down to a frayed shoelace and a folded linen napkin resting nearby, and that concreteness keeps the reasoning honest. With the length field of an array in mind, and checking each statement against the facts of the case rather than against first impressions, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

answers.text: The length of an array reports how many elements the array holds, and that value never changes after creation.
Reading the length of an array is done through a field, not through a method call with parentheses.
The length of an array grows by one each time a new value is assigned into one of its slots.
The length counts every slot in the array, including slots that still hold default values.

questions.explanation: The first wrong statement is false because length is a field that counts all slots of the array object, it is fixed at creation, and it includes slots that still hold default values. The correct statement, by contrast, matches the actual behavior exactly, and the two additional true statements are accurate as well because they describe consequences that follow from the same rule. A learner who tests the claim on a small example described in words, position by position, will watch the false claim break down while each true claim continues to hold for every valid position and every stored value in the collection being discussed here today. Because the other three statements are accurate as written, the keyed statement is the single incorrect one.

questions.question: Iris numbers the seats in a small theater row for a seating chart program. She wants a label for every seat in the row, starting with the first seat. When her counter begins one seat too late, the chart silently omits the opening seat, and the usher finds a guest holding a ticket for a seat the chart never printed. Which of the following statements about off-by-one errors from the starting value is correct?

answers.text: The starting value of a loop never affects which items get processed, only how fast they are processed.
An off-by-one error always doubles the amount of work a loop performs.
If a loop starts at the wrong value, the update step automatically compensates and fixes the range.
Starting a loop control variable one step too high or too low shifts which values are processed and causes an off-by-one error.

questions.explanation: The correct statement links the starting value directly to the processed range: shift the start and the whole window of values shifts. The first wrong claim denies that link, but Iris missing first seat proves the start decides inclusion. The second wrong claim exaggerates the effect into doubling, whereas the classic symptom is a single extra or missing pass. The third wrong claim trusts the update to compensate, but a steady update preserves the initial shift from beginning to end rather than erasing it. The companion true statements suggest boundary checking and name the typical size of the error. In the situation described, the keyed statement is the one consistent with this reasoning.

questions.question: Olive checks login names with a program for a library computer reservation system at school. A typed name must match the stored name character by character before access is granted to a student. Olive compares the two Strings with a method designed for content comparison. She avoids a shortcut operator that her classmate suggested for the job. Which of the following statements about comparing Strings with the equals method is correct?

answers.text: The double equals operator is the recommended way to compare the content of two Strings.
The equals method returns a number showing how many characters the two Strings share.
The equals method compares the character content of two Strings rather than their identities.
The equals method ignores capitalization and spacing when it compares two Strings.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is accurate because equals is defined on String to test whether both sequences of characters are identical regardless of whether the objects are distinct. The first wrong statement fails because the double equals operator compares references and can report false for equal content held by different objects. The second wrong statement fails because equals returns a boolean verdict and not a count. The third wrong statement fails because the comparison is exact and case and spacing differences make Strings unequal. In the situation described, the keyed statement is the one consistent with this reasoning.

questions.question: During a study session, an instructor presents the following case to the class and asks the students to reason carefully from the facts it contains, reminding everyone that a single deciding detail in a case like this usually separates the sound statement from the merely plausible ones surrounding it: A Thermometer class needs to convert its stored reading into a friendly verbal description for several different public reports. Rather than repeating the conversion logic in each report method, the programmer writes a single private helper that performs the conversion. Public methods call the helper internally, while outside classes never see it and simply enjoy the polished reports it helps produce. With private helper methods in mind, and weighing the whole case rather than any one phrase in isolation, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Private helper methods must be callable from every other class to be useful.
A private helper method automatically becomes part of the public interface of the class.
Helper methods are forbidden from accessing the instance variables of their own class.
A private helper method supports the internal work of a class and is not accessible to client code.

questions.explanation: The correct statement is right because private helpers exist for internal reuse while staying hidden from clients. The first wrong statement reverses the visibility rule, since usefulness inside the class does not require outside access. The second wrong statement fails because private members are excluded from the public interface by definition. The third wrong statement fails because helpers are ordinary members of the class and routinely read and use its instance variables to do their supporting work. Weighing the whole case rather than any one phrase in isolation, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: During a seminar devoted to common examination traps, a presenter displays the following case and explains that three of the statements offered about it are accurate while one is not, and that spotting the single inaccurate statement among sound ones is precisely the skill being practiced: Marco demonstrates a counted loop that calls out exhibit numbers in a museum tour. He shows his students that the current exhibit is always described first, and only afterward does the tour advance to the next exhibit number. A student who expected the advance to happen first predicts the wrong opening exhibit and corrects the prediction after watching. With when the for loop update runs in mind, and checking each statement against the facts of the case rather than against first impressions, which of the following statements is INCORRECT?

answers.text: In a for loop, the body runs with the current control value before the update changes that value for the next pass.
In a for loop, the update runs first so the body never sees the initialization value.
The first pass of a for loop uses the initialization value in the body, not the value after one update.
After the update runs, the condition is tested again with the new control value.

questions.explanation: The first wrong statement is false because the body demonstrably uses the initialization value on the opening pass; the advance to the next exhibit happens only after that exhibit has been described. The correct statement is accurate that the body precedes the update on each pass, and the other true statements are accurate as well: the first pass uses the starting value, and the updated value faces a fresh condition test before another pass is allowed. Because the other three statements are accurate as written, the keyed statement is the single incorrect one.

arizona-real-estate-broker.quiz_title: Arizona Real Estate Broker Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: On a practice test, a candidate encounters this fact pattern: A brokerage advertises a home as having features it plainly does not have, reasoning that advertising is expected to exaggerate. Which statement accurately states the rule that governs here?

answers.text: Advertising exaggeration is fully protected and can never support discipline.
Only advertising that names the wrong brokerage can violate Arizona law.
False or misleading advertising by a licensee is prohibited and can be grounds for discipline.
Misleading statements are permitted in advertising if the contract documents are accurate.

questions.explanation: Arizona holds licensees to truthful advertising because consumers rely on listings and promotions when deciding where to spend time and money. Materially false claims about a property features, terms, or availability mislead the public even if later contract paperwork is accurate, since the deception shaped the consumer decision to engage. The prohibition is not limited to errors about brokerage identity. Puffery about subjective appeal differs from factual misstatements, which are disciplinable. Judged for accuracy, only the keyed statement survives the test this explanation applies.

questions.question: A lender and an insurer both refuse to serve an entire neighborhood because of its racial composition rather than individual property risk. Which statement correctly describes that pattern?

answers.text: Redlining is a pricing discount offered to buyers who choose a preferred neighborhood.
Refusing service to a whole area is lawful if each company applies the refusal consistently.
Refusing housing related services to an area because of the protected composition of its residents is redlining and is prohibited.
Redlining describes only the act of drawing a literal red line on a paper map.

questions.explanation: Redlining grew from maps that marked minority neighborhoods as too risky for loans and insurance, but the violation is the area based denial itself, not the color of the ink. Consistent application makes the discrimination systematic rather than legal. Decisions must rest on legitimate, individual, property and applicant factors, not on who lives nearby. Brokers encounter redlining when financing or coverage collapses for a location, and they should not repeat or endorse area judgments tied to protected traits. Equal access to credit and insurance is part of equal access to housing itself. In the situation described, the keyed statement is the one consistent with this reasoning.

questions.question: While married, an Arizona wife inherits a cabin from her aunt and keeps it titled in her name alone, never mixing it with marital funds, and her husband asks whether he owns part of it. Which statement is correct?

answers.text: A spouse's separate property becomes community property whenever the couple lives in the home together.
Property a spouse acquires during marriage by gift, devise, or inheritance, and property owned before marriage, is generally that spouse's separate property in Arizona.
Everything either spouse acquires during marriage is community property no matter how it was acquired.
An inheritance becomes community property automatically as soon as the inheriting spouse records a deed.

questions.explanation: Community property law sorts assets by source and timing: what a spouse owned before marriage, and what a spouse later receives alone by gift, devise, or inheritance, remains separate property unless that spouse takes steps to change its character. Keeping the cabin separate and unmixed preserves that status, which defeats the sweeping claim that everything acquired during marriage is community property. Recording a deed or sharing a roof does not by itself transmute separate property into community property; a clear intent or a commingling that destroys traceability is what endangers the separate character of an asset. In the situation described, the keyed statement is the one consistent with this reasoning.

questions.question: In a continuing education discussion, licensees consider a case with these facts: A successful sales team has an experienced team leader who mentors newer members. Which of the following statements correctly states the applicable rule?

answers.text: A team leader automatically becomes a co-broker of the firm once the team reaches a certain size.
A team leader who is not the designated broker cannot replace the designated broker's supervision, hold the brokerage license, or authorize brokerage-level decisions.
Team members may follow the team leader instead of the designated broker whenever instructions conflict.
A team leader may open a branch office for the team without the designated broker's involvement.

questions.explanation: Teams exist inside brokerages, so leadership is mentorship and organization, not licensure authority, which remains with the designated broker alone. The wrong choices fail because team size confers no broker status, because conflicting instructions are resolved in favor of the broker who bears legal responsibility, and because branch offices are brokerage decisions under the broker's control. Clear lines keep talented teams productive without blurring accountability. A candidate who applies this reasoning will select the statement that states the rule correctly.

questions.question: On a practice test, a candidate encounters this fact pattern: A community claims it may lawfully limit occupancy based on age as housing for older persons. Which statement accurately states the rule that governs here?

answers.text: Any community may claim the exemption simply by calling itself an adult community in an ad.
The exemption allows a qualified community to discriminate based on race if residents vote for it.
Once claimed, the exemption permanently removes the community from all fair housing duties.
The older persons exemption is narrow and depends on the community actually qualifying and operating under the specific legal requirements for that category, not on marketing language alone.

questions.explanation: Familial status law contains a defined path for genuine housing for older persons, but the exemption must be earned through qualifying occupancy, published intent, and compliance with the governing requirements. A label in an advertisement creates nothing by itself. The exemption is also limited in scope: it concerns familial status and does not authorize discrimination on race or other protected grounds, and it does not erase every other housing duty. A manager marketing such a community should verify qualification with the designated broker and counsel rather than repeating an owner assurance, because a failed claim exposes every rejected family to a discrimination complaint. Judged for accuracy, only the keyed statement survives the test this explanation applies.

questions.question: In a continuing education discussion, licensees consider a case with these facts: A salesperson working under a brokerage mishandles a client matter within the scope of the salesperson's work for the brokerage. Which of the following statements correctly states the applicable rule?

answers.text: Each salesperson is entirely unsupervised once licensed, and the designated broker bears no responsibility.
Supervision is the responsibility of the clients, who must monitor their own salesperson's work.
The designated broker is responsible only for salespersons who share the broker's last name.
The designated broker is responsible for supervising the salespersons affiliated with the brokerage and for the brokerage's compliance with the law.

questions.explanation: Arizona brokerages operate under a designated broker who must supervise affiliated licensees, review their work, and maintain systems that keep the brokerage compliant. The wrong choices fail because licensure does not free a salesperson from brokerage oversight, because clients hire representation rather than agreeing to police it, and because supervision turns on affiliation and authority, not family ties. Active supervision includes training, file review, and prompt correction when problems appear. A candidate who applies this reasoning will select the statement that states the rule correctly.

questions.question: A designated broker uses a training example with new licensees: A borrower signs two documents at closing on a financed purchase and asks what each document does. One of the following statements about promissory note versus deed of trust misstates the rule. Which one is the incorrect statement?

answers.text: The promissory note transfers ownership to the borrower, while the deed of trust guarantees that the property has marketable title.
The promissory note pledges the real property as security, while the deed of trust is the personal promise to repay the debt.
The promissory note is the evidence of the debt and the promise to repay, while the deed of trust pledges the real property as security for that debt.
The promissory note and the deed of trust are identical documents that both transfer ownership of the property to the lender.

questions.explanation: Keeping the note and the security instrument separate prevents many exam errors. The note creates the personal obligation to repay on stated terms and is the instrument a lender may endorse and transfer. The deed of trust creates the lien interest in the land that allows foreclosure if the note is not paid. The first wrong option reverses those functions. The second wrongly merges them and overstates the lender interest as ownership. The third confuses the security instrument with a deed of conveyance and with title assurance, which serve different purposes. The keyed choice is the statement that fails this explanation's test and is therefore the incorrect one.

questions.question: On a practice test, a candidate encounters this fact pattern: A salesperson affiliated as an independent contractor argues that contractor status means the designated broker cannot direct or review the salesperson's licensed work. Which statement accurately states the rule that governs here?

answers.text: No, because contractors are supervised by their clients rather than by the brokerage.
Yes, because a contractor licensee is legally unsupervised and answers to no broker at all.
No, because independent contractor status affects tax and business treatment, but the licensee remains subject to the designated broker's supervision for licensed activity.
Yes, because supervision would instantly convert every contractor into a part-time employee for licensing purposes.

questions.explanation: Contractor classification and licensing supervision operate on different tracks: a salesperson may be a contractor for tax purposes while still practicing only under a designated broker who must review files, advertising, and trust handling. The wrong choices fail because no affiliated licensee is unsupervised, because lawful broker supervision is required by licensing law regardless of tax labels, and because clients are principals to serve, not supervisors of licensure. Both realities coexist in a properly documented affiliation. Judged for accuracy, only the keyed statement survives the test this explanation applies.

questions.question: In a continuing education discussion, licensees consider a case with these facts: A buyer asks for objective data about schools, commute routes, and crime statistics for several areas the buyer selected. Which of the following statements correctly states the applicable rule?

answers.text: The agent must refuse to discuss any neighborhood topic under all circumstances.
The agent may share personal opinions about where a buyer kind will feel comfortable.
The agent may provide factual, objective information and reliable public sources for areas the buyer chooses, without ranking neighborhoods by the protected makeup of their residents.
The agent should warn the buyer away from any area the agent considers demographically changing.

questions.explanation: Fair housing law does not require an agent to be useless; it requires the agent to be neutral. Objective facts, public data sources, and property specific information help a buyer evaluate areas the buyer has selected. The violation begins when the agent steers by praising or condemning an area in protected class terms or by substituting demographic comfort opinions for buyer choice. A total refusal to provide any factual help is unnecessary and can itself produce uneven service. The disciplined method is consistent information, cited sources, and respect for the buyer stated criteria across every neighborhood. A candidate who applies this reasoning will select the statement that states the rule correctly.

questions.question: On a practice test, a candidate encounters this fact pattern: A broker wants to thank an unlicensed friend by paying him a share of the commission every time a referred friend lists a home. Which statement accurately states the rule that governs here?

answers.text: A broker may share commission with an unlicensed person as long as the share is called a gift.
Unlicensed persons may receive a percentage of commission if they do not attend the closing.
Referral fees to unlicensed persons are allowed if the referred customer consents in writing.
A broker may not pay compensation for real estate referral or brokerage activity to a person who is not properly licensed.

questions.explanation: Arizona reserves compensation for brokerage activity, including procuring and referring clients for a fee tied to transactions, to persons who hold the proper license. Calling the payment a gift, obtaining customer consent, or keeping the unlicensed person away from closing does not change its substance as a commission share for referrals. A broker who pays such fees risks discipline, and the arrangement can also expose the unlicensed recipient for acting without a license. Judged for accuracy, only the keyed statement survives the test this explanation applies.

questions.question: A designated broker uses a training example with new licensees: An appraiser needs a quick value check for a small residential rental using only its rent and a market factor. One of the following statements about gross rent multiplier method misstates the rule. Which one is the incorrect statement?

answers.text: The gross rent multiplier method estimates value by dividing net operating income by the gross rent and subtracting accrued depreciation.
The gross rent multiplier method estimates value by multiplying net operating income by the property tax rate for the current year.
The gross rent multiplier method estimates value by adding all operating expenses to the loan balance and dividing by the number of rental units.
The gross rent multiplier method estimates value by multiplying the gross rent of the subject property by a multiplier derived from comparable properties that relate price to gross rent.

questions.explanation: The multiplier is extracted from comparable rentals by relating each sale price to its gross rent, then applying a representative multiplier to the subject gross rent on the same monthly or annual basis. It is a shortcut that works best for small residential rentals with similar expense patterns, because it does not adjust for differing expenses the way full capitalization does. The first wrong option mixes net income and depreciation into a gross rent tool. The second uses a tax rate with no market basis. The third builds a formula from expenses and debt that the method never uses. The keyed choice is the statement that fails this explanation's test and is therefore the incorrect one.

questions.question: During a broker prelicensing study session, an instructor presents the following situation to the class: Salespersons in a brokerage create their own flyers, posts, and signs for listings. With broker supervision and approval of advertising in mind, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Advertising is each salesperson's private business, and the designated broker may not review it.
Broker review of advertising is needed only after a consumer complains about a specific piece.
A salesperson may publish advertising under a made-up brokerage name if the design looks professional.
The designated broker must supervise and review licensee advertising to ensure it identifies the brokerage and contains no false or misleading content.

questions.explanation: Because advertising speaks for the brokerage, the designated broker's supervision extends to reviewing it for identification, accuracy, and compliance before the public relies on it. The wrong choices fail because affiliated advertising is brokerage activity rather than a private side venture, because waiting for complaints abandons preventive supervision, and because an invented firm name misidentifies the responsible licensee entirely. A simple pre-publication review routine prevents most advertising discipline cases. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: During a broker prelicensing study session, an instructor presents the following situation to the class: A buyer receives a counteroffer and replies with enthusiasm but adds a new demand that the seller leave all appliances behind. With unqualified acceptance in mind, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: An acceptance must be unqualified and match the offer on material terms, or the reply operates as another counteroffer.
Enthusiastic language turns any reply into an acceptance even when new material demands are added.
Adding a material demand merely creates a side note that never affects contract formation.
A reply that changes material terms binds the other party unless that party objects within an hour.

questions.explanation: Acceptance must assent to the offer as made on its material terms. Adding a demand about appliances changes what must be delivered, so the reply is a further counteroffer rather than a completed acceptance. The wrong choices fail because tone cannot replace agreement, material additions alter the bargain instead of annotating it, and no rule binds a party to changed terms simply because a short period passes without objection. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: During a broker prelicensing study session, an instructor presents the following situation to the class: A brokerage advertises a home as having features it plainly does not have, reasoning that advertising is expected to exaggerate. With false or misleading advertising in mind, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Misleading statements are permitted in advertising if the contract documents are accurate.
False or misleading advertising by a licensee is prohibited and can be grounds for discipline.
Advertising exaggeration is fully protected and can never support discipline.
Only advertising that names the wrong brokerage can violate Arizona law.

questions.explanation: Arizona holds licensees to truthful advertising because consumers rely on listings and promotions when deciding where to spend time and money. Materially false claims about a property features, terms, or availability mislead the public even if later contract paperwork is accurate, since the deception shaped the consumer decision to engage. The prohibition is not limited to errors about brokerage identity. Puffery about subjective appeal differs from factual misstatements, which are disciplinable. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: A designated broker uses a training example with new licensees: An investor values an apartment building primarily for the income it produces rather than for its construction cost. One of the following statements about income capitalization approach concept misstates the rule. Which one is the incorrect statement?

answers.text: The income capitalization approach converts expected net operating income into a value indication by applying a capitalization rate derived from the market.
The income capitalization approach values income property by adding land cost to replacement cost and subtracting physical depreciation only.
The income capitalization approach converts gross sales prices of comparable homes into value by adjusting for bedroom count differences only.
The income capitalization approach values income property by assuming its income has no effect on what an investor will pay for it.

questions.explanation: Investors buy an income stream, so this approach focuses on what the property is expected to earn after vacancy and operating expenses, but before debt service and income taxes, which yields net operating income. Capitalizing that income at a market extracted rate expresses the present value of the future benefit. The first wrong option describes a narrow version of sales comparison. The second describes the cost approach. The third contradicts the premise of investment value, because expected income is the central driver of price for this property type. The keyed choice is the statement that fails this explanation's test and is therefore the incorrect one.

questions.question: In a continuing education discussion, licensees consider a case with these facts: After a binding purchase contract is signed but before closing, the house is damaged by an accidental fire and the contract is silent about the risk. Which of the following statements correctly states the applicable rule?

answers.text: A signed contract has no effect on ownership interests until the buyer physically moves into the home.
Equitable conversion means the seller remains full owner for every purpose until the deed is recorded years later.
Under equitable conversion the buyer is treated as the equitable owner once a valid contract is signed, which can place the risk of loss on the buyer unless the contract or law provides otherwise.
Risk of loss always stays with the seller no matter what the contract says or the doctrine provides.

questions.explanation: Equity regards as done what ought to be done, so once a specifically enforceable contract exists the buyer holds equitable title while the seller holds legal title tied to receiving the price. That shift is why risk of loss may fall on the buyer when the agreement is silent. The wrong choices fail because they deny the buyer present equitable interest, ignore that parties may allocate risk by agreement, and confuse physical possession with the legal interests created by the contract itself. A candidate who applies this reasoning will select the statement that states the rule correctly.

questions.question: During a broker prelicensing study session, an instructor presents the following situation to the class: A licensee places a license on inactive status during a career break but continues to negotiate a sale for a neighbor for a fee. With inactive license consequences in mind, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Inactive status suspends only the continuing education duty while preserving full practice rights.
An inactive licensee may earn commissions if a licensed friend agrees to lend supervision informally.
Inactive licensees may negotiate occasional sales as long as they do not advertise.
A licensee on inactive status may not engage in licensed real estate activity until the license is properly reactivated through a broker.

questions.explanation: Inactive status preserves the credential in a nonpracticing state; it does not preserve practice rights. While inactive, the licensee lacks an employing broker relationship for active work and may not negotiate transactions or earn commissions for licensed activity. Informal supervision from a friend is not employment, and doing an occasional unadvertised deal is still licensed activity. Returning to practice requires proper reactivation and employment through a broker. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: A designated broker uses a training example with new licensees: A married couple living in Arizona buys a home during their marriage using wages both earned while married, and the deed says nothing special about how they hold title. One of the following statements about Arizona community property presumption misstates the rule. Which one is the incorrect statement?

answers.text: Property acquired during marriage is presumed to be community property in Arizona, with each spouse owning an equal undivided interest in it.
Property acquired during marriage in Arizona is presumed to be held in joint tenancy with survivorship.
Property acquired during marriage in Arizona belongs to whichever spouse paid the larger share of the price.
Property acquired during marriage in Arizona is presumed to belong only to the spouse who signed the deed.

questions.explanation: Arizona is a community property state, and its central presumption is that property acquired during the marriage belongs to the marital community, with each spouse holding an equal undivided interest regardless of whose name or whose wages were most visible in the transaction. That presumption defeats the claims favoring the signing spouse or the larger contributor, because contribution size does not reorder community ownership. Joint tenancy is a separate, expressly chosen form of title and is never created by the marital presumption alone, so a deed must clearly state a survivorship form when the couple wants one instead of community property. The keyed choice is the statement that fails this explanation's test and is therefore the incorrect one.

questions.question: During a broker prelicensing study session, an instructor presents the following situation to the class: An Arizona buyer needs terms for a homeowners association transfer, a septic system, and a domestic well that the main purchase form does not fully cover. With Arizona purchase contract addenda in mind, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: The parties should use the appropriate signed addenda for those subjects and incorporate them into the purchase contract so the added terms become part of the agreement.
Special subjects should be handled by oral promises so the written contract stays short and simple.
A broker may attach unsigned addenda after acceptance and treat them as binding on both parties.
Addenda for association, septic, and well matters replace the need for any disclosures the law requires.

questions.explanation: Arizona practice relies on subject specific addenda to supply terms the base purchase form does not contain, covering matters such as association documents and fees, septic transfer, and well rights. Signed and incorporated addenda become contract terms. The wrong choices fail because oral side promises invite statute of frauds and proof problems, unsigned papers imposed later lack mutual agreement, and contractual addenda work alongside rather than erase independent disclosure duties. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

questions.question: During a broker prelicensing study session, an instructor presents the following situation to the class: A creditor wins a money judgment against a landowner in court and takes the proper steps to make that judgment reach the landowner's real estate in the county. With judgment lien on real property in mind, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A judgment lien attaches only to the single parcel the debtor was living in on the day of the trial.
A judgment lien disappears from the records the moment the debtor lists the property for sale with a broker.
A court judgment never affects real property unless the debtor voluntarily signs a mortgage to the creditor.
A properly recorded or docketed judgment can become a general lien on the judgment debtor's real property in that county, clouding title until it is paid or expires.

questions.explanation: A money judgment becomes a lien on real estate through the recording or docketing process the law prescribes, and once attached it operates as a general lien reaching the debtor's real property in that county rather than only the home occupied on one particular day. No voluntary mortgage is needed, because the lien arises from the court's judgment and the creditor's filing steps, and listing the property for sale does nothing to remove it. In practice the lien surfaces in the title search and must be paid, settled, or otherwise cleared at or before closing, which is why brokers treat judgments as title problems and not merely as personal debts. Asked directly, the same reasoning identifies the single correct statement among the choices.

social-psychology.quiz_title: Social Psychology Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Problem review time: the topic is planning Fallacy. Which statement is sound?

answers.text: The planning fallacy is the tendency of town councils to approve building plans that fail to meet the published safety code for new housing.
The planning fallacy is the tendency to underestimate how long a task will take to complete, even by people who know that similar tasks have run over time in the past.

The planning fallacy is the tendency to overestimate completion times in order to guarantee that every deadline is comfortably met ahead of schedule. Students return to this point whenever a classic finding is reviewed.
The planning fallacy is the logical error of assuming that because a plan is detailed, every event it describes is certain to occur as written.

questions.explanation: Planners focus on the inside view of the current project and its best-case sequence, while neglecting the outside view of how long comparable projects actually took.

questions.question: Of the statements offered on alcohol And Aggression, which one is accurate?

answers.text: Alcohol and aggression are related only because aggressive people choose to drink, and controlled experiments show no effect of alcohol itself.
Alcohol decreases aggression in all drinkers, because its sedative properties reliably calm every social gathering it enters.

Alcohol increases aggression by directly creating hostile intentions in people who had none, a pharmacological effect independent of attention. This is one of the ideas experienced instructors check first.
Alcohol increases aggression partly by impairing the cognitive processes that normally restrain it, narrowing attention to provocative cues and weakening consideration of consequences.

questions.explanation: Alcohol myopia names the attentional mechanism: intoxicated attention locks onto the insult and loses the mitigating context that sobriety would weigh.

questions.question: Of the statements offered on resisting Unjust Authority, which one is accurate?

answers.text: Resistance to unjust authority is supported by allies, by distance from the authority and closeness to the victim, by public commitment to values and by knowledge that obedience paradigms exist and can be recognised.
Resistance to unjust authority depends only on physical courage, and social support has never been shown to affect it.

Resistance to unjust authority is impossible once an order has been given, because the agentic state cannot be interrupted by knowledge or allies. Students return to this point whenever a classic finding is reviewed. This is one of the ideas experienced instructors check first.
Resistance to unjust authority is most likely when the dissenter is alone and uninformed, because ignorance concentrates the will.

questions.explanation: Teaching the obedience literature is itself an intervention: students who know the paradigm report recognising its shape in real hierarchies.

questions.question: Of the statements offered on negativity In Person Perception, which one is accurate?

answers.text: In person perception, positive and negative behaviours are weighted by their alphabetical order in a report, a convention evaluators follow strictly. The point holds for beginning students as much as for advanced learners.
In person perception, negative behaviours are treated as more diagnostic than positive ones, especially in the domain of morality, where one dishonest act can define a reputation.
In person perception, positive behaviours are always more diagnostic, so one generous act permanently outweighs any number of dishonest ones.
In person perception, behaviour is ignored entirely, and reputation is decided solely by the opinions of the persons oldest friends.

questions.explanation: Diagnosticity differs by domain: for ability, a success at a hard task is most informative, while for morality, a failure of honesty speaks loudest.

questions.question: Knowledge check: on empathy Altruism Hypothesis, which statement passes?

answers.text: The empathy-altruism hypothesis is a doctrine of charity law, governing the tax status of organisations that relieve poverty.

The empathy-altruism hypothesis proposes that all helping is selfish, and that empathic concern is merely a strategy for relieving personal distress. This idea supports consistent explanations across the whole subject. Classes come back to this idea when practice questions arise.

The empathy-altruism hypothesis proposes that feeling empathic concern for a person in need produces genuinely altruistic motivation to help, with the goal of relieving that persons need rather than ones own distress.
The empathy-altruism hypothesis proposes that empathy prevents helping, because feeling with a victim is so painful that witnesses leave the scene.

questions.explanation: Experiments that make escape from the situation easy separate the motives: if helping persists when escape is free, egoistic distress relief cannot be the whole story.

questions.question: A classmate at the seminar room asks James about global And Specific Causes. Which guidance is correct?

answers.text: Causes can be classified as global, affecting many domains of life, or specific, affecting only a narrow domain, and global explanations for setbacks carry wider emotional consequences.
Causes can be classified as global if they are written in general terms on a form, or specific if the form asks for dates and addresses.
Causes can be classified as global if they are shared by a group, or specific if they are held by one person, and numbers decide the class.

Causes can be classified as global if they are reported in international news, or specific if they appear only in a local newspaper column. Students return to this point whenever a classic finding is reviewed.

questions.explanation: Explaining one rejection as evidence about every domain of life generalises the damage, which is why scope is a separate dimension from stability.

questions.question: While preparing at the classroom, Daniel reviews team Diversity Effects. Which statement applies?

answers.text: Team diversity always improves performance automatically, because variety of background mechanically produces variety of useful ideas. This principle travels across systems, settings and patient populations alike.

Team diversity brings a wider pool of information and perspectives but can also activate categorisation and conflict, so its effects on performance depend on how differences are managed and integrated.
Team diversity has no effects of any kind, because professional training erases every difference members bring to a team.
Team diversity always damages performance, because categorisation and conflict are unavoidable whenever backgrounds differ in a team.

questions.explanation: The dual potential is the finding: diversity is an information resource and a social faultline at once, and leadership decides which face dominates.

questions.question: New student orientation covers attribution Of Blame today. Which statement belongs in the teaching?

answers.text: Blame attribution is assigned by lot in everyday life, with perceivers drawing names to decide who will carry responsibility for an event.

Blame attribution weighs only the status of the person blamed, so low-status people are blamed for every harm and high-status people for none. The principle is part of how sound mechanistic reasoning is judged.
Blame attribution weighs only the size of the harm, so intention and control are never considered by perceivers judging a bad outcome.
Blame attribution weighs cause, control and intention, so harm seen as intended and controllable draws far more blame than the same harm seen as accidental and unavoidable.

questions.explanation: The graded nature of blame shows attribution doing moral work: perceivers are not only explaining an event but deciding what response it deserves.

questions.question: At the study lounge, the discussion turns to cyberbullying Features. Which statement earns agreement?

answers.text: Cyberbullying differs from traditional bullying through the permanence and reach of digital content, the possibility of anonymity and the absence of refuge, since the harassment can follow the victim home through their devices.
Cyberbullying requires physical co-presence, because online aggression is counted only when the parties are in the same room.

Cyberbullying is identical to traditional bullying in every feature, because the medium through which aggression travels changes nothing at all. This principle applies across everyday social situations alike. The idea is revisited whenever the quality of a research explanation is discussed.
Cyberbullying is always less harmful than traditional bullying, because words on a screen cannot distress a victim in any lasting way.

questions.explanation: The same features that complicate harm complicate intervention: content can be copied beyond the original audience, but it also leaves evidence that face-to-face cruelty does not.

questions.question: Review rounds bring up perseverance Of Impressions this week. Which statement does the reasoning support?

answers.text: Impressions never persevere, because the mind automatically deletes any impression whose evidence base is later shown to be faulty.
Impressions can persevere only when they are written in a diary, because unwritten impressions fade within minutes of being formed. The point comes up in teaching for new psychology students.
Impressions can persevere because perceivers generate explanations and stories that support them, and those self-generated supports remain even when the original information is withdrawn.
Impressions can persevere because other people keep repeating them, and private explanation plays no part in their survival at all.

questions.explanation: Debriefing research showed the pattern clearly: telling participants that feedback was fabricated did not fully undo the impression the feedback had created.

questions.question: Focus on realistic Conflict Theory for a moment - which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: Realistic conflict theory holds that intergroup hostility arises from imagined differences alone, and that real competition over resources plays no part in it. The point holds for beginning students as much as for advanced learners.
Realistic conflict theory is an economic doctrine about price wars between firms, with no application to relations between social groups.

Realistic conflict theory holds that intergroup hostility arises from competition over scarce resources and incompatible goals, and recedes when groups must cooperate toward goals neither can reach alone.
Realistic conflict theory holds that competition always improves intergroup relations, because contact during contests builds mutual respect.

questions.explanation: The Robbers Cave study is its classic field demonstration: tournament competition manufactured hostility between stranger boys, and superordinate goals dissolved it.

questions.question: Instructors use stereotype Definition as a teaching point for the class. Which statement should be taught?

answers.text: A stereotype is a verified fact about every member of a group, checked individually and never applied beyond the evidence that supports it. The principle stays relevant across a survey course in this subject.
A stereotype is a private nickname given to one individual, used by close friends and unknown to anyone outside that small circle.
A stereotype is a sound system with two speakers that produces a fuller audio image than a single-speaker system can achieve alone.
A stereotype is a generalised belief about the attributes of a social group, applied to individual members on the basis of their group membership.

questions.explanation: Stereotypes are cognitive structures, which separates them from prejudice, an affective response, and discrimination, an overt behaviour.

questions.question: Robert is handling a question involving heuristic Systematic Model while working through a topic review. Which statement should guide the work?

answers.text: The heuristic-systematic model proposes that systematic processing occurs only during examinations, when candidates are required to show workings.
The heuristic-systematic model proposes that heuristics are a kind of printed checklist issued to jurors before they retire to deliberate.

The heuristic-systematic model proposes that people process messages only heuristically, because systematic processing is beyond ordinary capacity. This principle applies across everyday social situations alike. The idea is revisited whenever the quality of a research explanation is discussed.

The heuristic-systematic model proposes that people process messages systematically when motivated, and otherwise rely on heuristics such as the rule that experts are usually right or that longer messages are stronger.

questions.explanation: The model shares the dual-process insight with the elaboration likelihood model while giving heuristics a more explicit, rule-like form.

questions.question: When a situation involving behavioural Confirmation needs resolving during a social_psychology seminar discussion, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Behavioural confirmation occurs when an employee signs a form to acknowledge that a new workplace procedure has been read and understood.
Behavioural confirmation occurs when a perceiver acts toward a target in ways that lead the target to behave in line with the perceiver expectations, making the expectation come true.
Behavioural confirmation occurs when a target behaviour is rewarded every time it appears, so the behaviour gradually becomes a stable habit.

Behavioural confirmation occurs when a laboratory result is repeated by an independent team and published as a verified finding in a journal. The concept is woven through ordinary study of how disorders progress.

questions.explanation: Expectations can create their own evidence: treating someone as hostile can provoke the very hostility that then seems to confirm the original expectation.

questions.question: When a situation involving dual Identity Approach needs resolving while preparing notes for a tutoring session, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The dual identity approach denies that a superordinate identity can ever develop, holding that subgroup loyalties exhaust social identity. The point holds for beginning students as much as for advanced learners.
The dual identity approach requires members to abandon their subgroup identity completely as the price of belonging to the larger group.
The dual identity approach maintains subgroup and superordinate identities simultaneously, so that people can belong to a common group without surrendering the distinct identity of their own group.
The dual identity approach is a security practice in which a person carries two identity documents for use in different jurisdictions.

questions.explanation: Dual identity often outperforms pure recategorisation where subgroup identities are strong and valued, because it asks for addition rather than surrender.

questions.question: While helping a classmate understand the material, Robert explains authority Principle. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The authority principle is the tendency to question every request from authority, scrutinising credentials before any compliance is considered. The idea is revisited whenever the quality of a research explanation is discussed.
The authority principle is the tendency to comply only with requests made in writing, because spoken requests lack legal standing.

The authority principle is the tendency to comply with requests from people perceived as legitimate authorities, whose symbols, titles and uniforms can trigger compliance with little scrutiny of the request itself.
The authority principle is a rule of grammar governing the use of titles before names in formal correspondence and official documents.

questions.explanation: Authority cues work peripherally: the trappings of expertise can substitute for expertise, which is why uniforms and titles feature in studies of compliance.

questions.question: Rachel is handling a question involving person Schema while working through a topic review. Which statement should guide the work?

answers.text: A person schema is a first impression formed in a single glance, which can never be revised even when years of later experience contradict it completely. This remains a central point in the study of how people think, feel and act in social situations.
A person schema is a mental structure that organises knowledge about the traits and typical behaviour of a particular individual whom the perceiver knows.
A person schema is a category label applied to a whole social group, which treats every member as identical regardless of their individual history.
A person schema is a legal file that an employer keeps on a worker, recording formal warnings and used only when a contract is about to be ended.

questions.explanation: Person schemas are about specific known individuals, which separates them from stereotypes, which are beliefs about groups rather than about one known person.
