questions.question: The statement below describes which concept? "Taking direction through established supervisors and routing concerns upward rather than bypassing authority or acting outside orders"

answers.text: Honesty in Reports and Testimony
Following the Chain of Command
Accepting Gifts and Gratuities Limits
Social Media Conduct About the Job

questions.explanation: The description matches Following the Chain of Command: taking direction through established supervisors and routing concerns upward rather than bypassing authority or acting outside orders. Precise terminology matters in security work.

questions.question: A service vignette describes this: appearance shaping public confidence. Which concept does this most directly illustrate?

answers.text: Handling Complaints From the Public
First Impressions and Guard Appearance
Interagency Communication During Incidents
Professional Radio Communication Procedure

questions.explanation: This illustrates First Impressions and Guard Appearance: the initial perception formed from a guard uniform, grooming, posture, and demeanor when meeting the public. The other options are different concepts in communication and public relations that work differently.

qei-elevator-inspector.quiz_title: QEI Elevator Inspector Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: During a team meeting on hoistway entrance lighting, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: Landing lighting lets passengers see the entrance, sill and car floor as they board
Poor entrance lighting hides the sill step and misleveling from boarding passengers
The inspector notes lighting that makes the entrance unsafe to use
Passengers can judge the sill step by feel in the dark

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Boarding is a visual task performed at a moving threshold; light at the entrance is part of the safety system the inspector walks through.

questions.question: Which statement about car door gate switch is accurate?

answers.text: The gate switch locks every hoistway door in the building
Gate switches and interlocks are the same device with two names
The car door or gate switch proves the car door is closed before the car will run in normal operation
The car may run normally with the gate switch open

questions.explanation: Two proofs guard two different doors: interlocks for the hoistway door, the gate switch for the car door — and confusing them hides real defects.

questions.question: Regarding governor tripping and inspection, which statement is inaccurate?

answers.text: Governor operation is never demonstrated at any test
Governor tripping speeds are set and sealed so they cannot be casually changed
A governor test demonstrates tripping at the witnessed periodic test
The inspector verifies governor rope condition, jaw operation and switch action

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Tripping speed is a sealed promise: the inspector checks the seal, the rope and the mechanism, and witnesses the trip when the test program calls for it.

questions.question: During a preparation class on guards on moving machinery, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Guards are decorative covers removed at installation
Rotating shafts need no guard if they turn slowly
A missing guard is a finding only after someone is injured
The inspector reports missing guards as safety deficiencies even if no incident has occurred

questions.explanation: Guarding is preventive: the deficiency exists when the protection is missing, not when the accident happens.

questions.question: In a study group on the hoistway enclosure purpose, one assertion is false. Which one?

answers.text: The hoistway enclosure separates the moving equipment from building occupants and other building areas
Hoistway enclosure walls exist mainly to carry the building structure above
Openings in the hoistway enclosure are limited so the shaft stays a protected vertical space
Hoistway enclosure walls protect people outside the shaft from contact with the car and counterweight

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. The enclosure turns the shaft into a guarded space: it keeps people and objects away from moving equipment and keeps the travel path free of interference.

questions.question: Concerning ropeway and other regulated conveyances boundary, which assertion is inaccurate?

answers.text: Working outside one's certified scope is itself a professional violation
Scope boundaries are advisory for experienced inspectors
The inspector recognizes which conveyances fall under the elevator code family and which under other standards
Ski lifts and amusement rides, for example, are governed by their own standards and programs

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Knowing where the credential ends is part of the credential; adjacent industries have their own standards and their own inspectors.

questions.question: A junior colleague makes several claims about safety gear types in words. Which claim should a mentor correct?

answers.text: The type fitted must match the car's speed, load and the code's requirements for that duty
Instantaneous safeties wedge or clamp the rail abruptly and suit lower speeds
Safeties with buffered or gradual action spread the stop over a distance for higher speeds
Gradual safeties stop the car with no travel distance at all

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Stopping energy decides the safety type: gentle, progressive application for fast, heavy cars and abrupt application only where speeds are low.

questions.question: A junior colleague makes several claims about emergency hoistway lighting checks. Which claim should a mentor correct?

answers.text: The inspector confirms pit and hoistway work lighting functions before relying on it
Lamp guards in the pit are prohibited because they dim the light
Failed pit lighting is corrected before routine work proceeds in the pit
Lighting guards protect lamps in the pit from damage by equipment or workers

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Light is safety equipment in the pit: guards keep it working and the inspector treats a dark pit as a stop-and-fix condition, not an inconvenience.

questions.question: During a team meeting on escalator safety switch family, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: Any operated safety switch stops the escalator and requires investigation before restart
Restart after a safety stop is automatic and immediate
The inspector verifies a representative, code-directed set of these devices by function
Escalator safety switches guard comb impact, skirt intrusion, step level, chain sag and handrail entry among other points

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. An escalator is ringed with trip points because its hazards are distributed; each switch is a small inspector in permanent attendance, and the human inspector audits them.

questions.question: During a team meeting on governor rope tension device in the pit, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: The tension device keeps the governor rope taut so it faithfully follows car speed
The governor rope runs in a loop between the governor and a tension sheave in the pit
A tension sheave switch can stop the car if the governor rope breaks or slackens excessively
The pit tension sheave drives the governor rope to move the car

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. The governor can only sense speed if its rope is taut and intact; the pit tension device and its switch guard both of those conditions.

questions.question: Among these statements on sidewalk and basement elevators awareness, one is incorrect. Identify it.

answers.text: The inspector checks the sidewalk doors and their operation as public protection
Street-level hazards are the city's problem, not the inspection's
Sidewalk elevators serve freight between basement and street level through a sidewalk opening
Their gates, covers and street-level protection guard the public way above

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. A machine that opens in a public sidewalk exports its hazards to strangers; its covers and gates are public-safety equipment.

questions.question: In a study group on broken rope and rope slack protection, one assertion is false. Which one?

answers.text: Rope slack or broken-rope switches stop the car if suspension ropes lose tension abnormally
A car resting on an obstruction should keep driving its ropes off
Such switches protect against a car resting on an obstruction while ropes unwind
The inspector verifies these switches on installations where they are fitted

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. A machine that keeps turning against a stalled car unloads its ropes into a tangle or a drop; slack protection is the switch that notices.

questions.question: Peter Lindqvist is studying hoistway and machine room material in a review session. On guide shoes and rollers, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Worn guide liners improve the ride by letting the car float freely
Worn guide shoe liners let the car ride loosely and can cause noisy, uneven running
Damaged roller tires are ignored because rollers are purely cosmetic
Guide shoes grip the rail tightly at all times to hold the car still

questions.explanation: The car rides on its guides: their wear shows up as play, noise and poor leveling, and the inspector treats worn liners and damaged rollers as genuine deficiencies.

questions.question: While practicing integration questions under time pressure, Ingrid Bauer considers escalator speed and overspeed protection. Which statement holds true?

answers.text: Overspeed protection is the passenger's responsibility to notice
A fully loaded descending escalator that loses drive control is the event this protection addresses
Reversal under load is a normal operating mode
Escalators cannot overspeed because they are slow

questions.explanation: Gravity works on a loaded band exactly as on a car; the escalator's overspeed and anti-reversal devices are its governor-and-safety equivalent.

questions.question: Chris Delacroix, who is building a study schedule for the inspector examination, reviews hoistway door unlocking zone. Which of these statements is accurate?

answers.text: Outside the zone, the hoistway door must remain locked against opening from the landing side
A hoistway door may be opened from the landing whenever the power is off
Zone limits are set by passenger preference
The unlocking zone extends the full hoistway height

questions.explanation: The zone defines where an open door meets a car floor rather than a void; verifying its discipline at each landing is a core entrance test.

questions.question: What should an elevator inspector candidate understand about protection against hoistway access enablement faults? Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Unexpected car movement from landing controls is a minor fault
Access circuits are convenience wiring with no safety role
Access enablement is tested only at installation
Hoistway access enabling circuits ensure access movement only occurs with the proper key sequence

questions.explanation: Controls that move a car from outside the shaft are powerful by design; their enabling logic is safety logic.

questions.question: While working through an elevator inspection study set, Laura Chen considers machine room fire and safety provisions. Which statement holds true?

answers.text: A telephone or communication means in the machine room supports emergency coordination
Sprinklers may discharge directly onto open live equipment by design intent
Communication from the machine room is unnecessary because workers shout down the hoistway
Machine rooms are exempt from all fire provisions

questions.explanation: Fire, communication and water protection in a machinery space are coordinated systems; the inspector notes provisions that are missing or in conflict.

questions.question: Ingrid Bauer, an elevator inspector candidate, is reviewing notes for the qualified elevator inspector examination and reads a summary of landing system devices in the hoistway. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: The inspector checks hoistway position devices for secure mounting along the travel
Landing system switches or sensors in the hoistway tell the controller when the car approaches a floor
Landing sensors are mounted on the car operating panel
Loose vanes or sensors cause leveling errors and unexpected stops

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. The hoistway is lined with the controller's senses; their mounting security is checked along the ride, not just at the controller.

questions.question: Anders Holm, an elevator inspector candidate, is studying hoistway and machine room material in a review session and reads a summary of hydraulic control and leveling valves. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: Down speed is governed by the valve so descent stays controlled even with varying load
A car that repeatedly relevels without demand can signal valve leakage or oil viscosity problems
Releveling is a fault that should be disabled permanently
Leveling valves creep the car back to floor level as load changes or oil contracts

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Anti-creep leveling is normal in small doses and diagnostic in large ones; the valve block is where controlled descent is actually decided.

questions.question: Nadia Hassan, an elevator inspector candidate, is reviewing notes for the qualified elevator inspector examination and reads a summary of door system behavior on power restoration. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: On power return the car immediately resumes full speed wherever it is
A car should not move with doors in an unknown state when power returns
After a power failure, doors and car state are re-established in a controlled sequence
The inspector verifies restoration behavior as part of emergency operation checks

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Restoration is a designed restart, not a resumption by momentum; unknown door state must be resolved before movement.

preact.quiz_title: PreACT Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which of these assertions about subjective pronoun case fails to hold up?

answers.text: The sentence she and I presented the report correctly uses subjective pronouns as subjects
In a compound subject, each pronoun should be in the subjective case when it acts as a subject
In a compound subject, each pronoun should be in the objective case when it acts as a subject
Pronouns used as subjects take the subjective case, such as I, she, he, we, and they

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Case shows a pronoun role in a sentence, and subjects perform the action so they need the subjective forms. Testing a compound subject by removing the other person quickly reveals whether I or me, she or her, sounds and functions correctly.

questions.question: During a preparation class on commas in a series, which statement is correct?

answers.text: A comma before the final conjunction in a series always creates confusion and is never used
The sentence we bought apples oranges and grapes uses commas to separate items in a list
A comma before the final conjunction in a series is standard in most style guides for clarity
Commas join three or more items in a series into one blended item

questions.explanation: Series commas act as dividers that prevent items from running together and being misread as combined phrases. Without them, readers may pair the wrong words, while consistent commas make every item in the list stand out as separate.

questions.question: For heredity from parents to offspring, which statement holds true?

answers.text: Heredity is the passing of traits from parents to their offspring through reproduction
Siblings must be identical in every trait because they share the same two parents
Heredity is the passing of learned skills from parents to offspring through daily lessons
Inherited traits appear only after long practice and involve no material passed on

questions.explanation: Heredity passes traits through reproduction by way of inherited material from the parents, and siblings vary because they receive different combinations, while learned skills are not inherited in this way.

questions.question: Which statement about informational text features is wrong?

answers.text: An index at the end of a book lists topics alphabetically with page references so readers can find specific information quickly
A glossary is a list of chapter titles in the order in which the chapters appear in the book
A glossary defines key terms used in a text and is usually placed near the end of the work
Informational text features such as headings, subheadings, captions, bold terms, and a table of contents help readers locate and understand information

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Text features are working tools that preview structure, highlight key terms, and route readers to definitions and topics, with the index pointing to locations alphabetically and the glossary supplying meanings, so none of them are mere decoration or substitutes for the text.

questions.question: Regarding evaluating expressions, which statement is inaccurate?

answers.text: Evaluating an expression means finding its value after replacing each variable with a given number
Operations in an expression are carried out first and substitution is done at the very end
Substitution must be done before the operations in an expression are carried out
The same expression can have different values when different numbers are substituted for its variable

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. An expression has no single value until numbers stand in for its letters, substitution comes first, and different substituted numbers can lead to different final values from the same expression.

questions.question: Which of these assertions about surface area meaning for solid figures fails to hold up?

answers.text: Opening a solid into a net can help find its surface area
Surface area is the total area of all faces of a solid figure
Surface area counts only one face of a solid figure
Surface area is measured in square units

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Surface area covers the outside of a solid by adding the areas of every face, so it uses square units like ordinary area. A net lays those faces flat to make the total easier to see, unlike volume which fills the inside.

questions.question: During a preparation class on interpolating between data points, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Interpolating means estimating a value far beyond all of the data that was collected
Interpolation assumes the change between nearby points follows the pattern they suggest
An interpolation is generally less secure than an estimate far beyond the collected data
Interpolation assumes there is no pattern at all between the two nearby known points

questions.explanation: Interpolation estimates a value between known points using the pattern those points suggest, and because it stays inside the collected range it is generally more secure than estimating far beyond the data.

questions.question: Hannah Kim is reviewing briefing material on multiplying polynomials. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: The distributive property is the basis for multiplying polynomials
When multiplying powers with the same base, the exponents are added
Multiplying polynomials requires every term of one polynomial to be multiplied by every term of the other
Multiplying polynomials requires only the first terms of each polynomial to be multiplied together

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Each term of one polynomial must reach each term of the other through distribution, missing a pairing loses terms, and repeated multiplication of one base adds the counts of its factors as exponents.

questions.question: During a team meeting on dependent events in probability, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: Two events are dependent when the outcome of one affects the probability of the other
After a dependent first draw the counts for the second draw change
Drawing from a bag without putting the item back creates dependent draws
Drawing from a bag and putting the item back before the next draw makes the draws dependent because the contents changed

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Dependence means the first outcome reshapes what remains possible. Drawing without replacement removes an item and changes the totals for the next draw, while replacing the item restores the original setup and independence.

questions.question: Which statement about evaluating expressions would a well-prepared PreACT student endorse?

answers.text: An expression has one fixed value no matter what number replaces its variable
Evaluating an expression means solving for the variable so the variable disappears forever
Operations in an expression are carried out first and substitution is done at the very end
Substitution must be done before the operations in an expression are carried out

questions.explanation: An expression has no single value until numbers stand in for its letters, substitution comes first, and different substituted numbers can lead to different final values from the same expression.

questions.question: During a preparation class on triangle classification by side length, which statement is correct?

answers.text: A scalene triangle has all sides the same length
A scalene triangle has no sides the same length
An isosceles triangle must have all three sides different
An equilateral triangle has no sides the same length

questions.explanation: Triangles are named by side length in a consistent way. Equilateral means all sides match, isosceles means at least two sides match, and scalene means no sides match, so swapping those meanings makes a statement false.

questions.question: A study group turns to extrapolating beyond collected data. Which statement should the candidate stand behind?

answers.text: An extrapolation is more certain than any value that lies within the collected data range
Extrapolating assumes that a trend seen in the data continues in a similar way beyond it
Extrapolating assumes that a trend stops completely as soon as collected data ends
Extrapolating means reporting a value that was directly measured during the study

questions.explanation: Extrapolation estimates beyond the collected range by extending a trend, which makes it less certain than values inside the data because the trend might not continue in the same way outside the study.

questions.question: Samuel Ortiz, who is preparing a study plan for the PreACT, reviews adding polynomials. Which of these statements is accurate?

answers.text: Polynomials are added by multiplying every pair of terms together
Only like terms are combined when two polynomials are added
The sum of two polynomials is never a polynomial
Any two terms can be combined when adding polynomials, even if they are unlike

questions.explanation: Adding polynomials is bookkeeping with like terms, matching variable parts are combined and unlike terms stay separate, and the result remains a polynomial because no new kind of term is created.

questions.question: A visitor repeats something they read online about arcs and central angles in a circle. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: The measure of an arc matches the measure of its central angle
A central angle has its vertex at the center of a circle
An arc is a part of the circumference of a circle
An arc is a straight line across the inside of a circle

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. A central angle opens from the center of the circle, and the piece of the edge cut off by its sides is an arc. The arc and its central angle share the same measure, linking the angle at the center to the curve.

questions.question: Tom Becker is drilling English, math, reading and science questions. On audience purpose and tone, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Word choice and sentence style should shift randomly with no regard for the effect on readers
A writer explaining a process to beginners should avoid defining terms and use a mocking tone
Tone should ignore the audience and purpose, with formal writing using a slang filled casual voice
A writer explaining a process to beginners should define terms and use a helpful tone

questions.explanation: Audience and purpose govern tone because the same content must sound different in a formal report and in a friendly guide for beginners. Matching diction, detail, and attitude to the readers needs is what makes writing feel appropriate and effective.

questions.question: Omar Haddad is reviewing briefing material on bar graph comparing categories. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Taller or longer bars represent larger values when all bars use the same scale
The scale on a bar graph must be read before deciding how large a difference really is
A bar graph uses bars of different heights or lengths to compare values across categories
A bar graph uses bars that must all be the same height so categories cannot be compared

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. A bar graph compares categories through bar height or length on a shared scale, so taller bars mean larger values and reading the scale is essential before judging the size of any difference.

questions.question: A visitor repeats something they read online about cause and effect text structure. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: Signal words such as consequently and as a result show that two ideas are being compared for similarity
A cause and effect structure explains why something happens and what results from it, linking reasons to outcomes
A single cause can produce several effects, and a single effect can grow out of several combined causes
Signal words for cause and effect include because, since, as a result, consequently, and therefore

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Cause and effect organization is built on the logic of reasons and results, marked by signals like because and therefore, and the relationship can branch in both directions, while mere listing or comparison follows a different logic and effects cannot precede their causes.

questions.question: On the subject of metaphor, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: Metaphors highlight a shared quality between the two things compared, such as describing time as a thief to stress that time steals moments
An extended metaphor carries a single comparison through several sentences or across a whole passage
Metaphors are literal statements that should be understood as plain physical facts
A metaphor directly compares two unlike things by stating that one thing is another, without using like or as

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. A metaphor asserts an identity between unlike things to transfer qualities from one to the other, and it does so without the like or as of a simile, which is why examples like time as a thief are figurative comparisons rather than literal claims or near identical pairings.

questions.question: While comparing answer choices on a practice assessment, Julia Santos double-checks notes on third person limited point of view. Which statement should be corrected?

answers.text: In third person limited point of view, an outside narrator focuses on the thoughts and feelings of mainly one character
Because the view is limited, readers learn about other characters only through what the focal character observes or is told
Third person limited narration uses pronouns such as he, she, and they for the characters rather than having a character narrate as I
In third person limited point of view, the narrator reveals the inner thoughts of every character equally throughout the story

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. The word limited is the key to this viewpoint, because an outside narrator stays close to one character and withholds the inner lives of the rest, which separates it from both first person narration by a participant and all knowing narration that ranges everywhere.

questions.question: While studying English and math material in a review session, Peter Lindqvist double-checks notes on irregular verb past forms. Which statement should be corrected?

answers.text: Irregular verbs form their past tense by adding a regular ending to the present form
Irregular verbs form their past tense by changing spelling rather than by adding a regular ending
The past tense of go is went and the past tense of bring is brought
Using the past participle with a helping verb is correct, as in she has chosen the topic

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Irregular verbs do not follow the regular pattern of adding an ending, so their past and participle forms must be learned individually. Forms such as goed or bringed sound plausible to the ear but are never accepted in standard written English.

icc-fire-inspector-i.quiz_title: ICC Fire Inspector I Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding fire protection report and special inspection documents, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The fire inspector accepts a test certificate for a different building's system.
The fire inspector treats acceptance documents as unnecessary once the system operates.

Where the approval relied on fire protection reports, test certificates, or special inspections, the fire inspector verifies those documents are on file and correspond to the systems actually installed.
The fire inspector files certificates without reading what system they describe.

questions.explanation: Approvals rest on evidence — tests witnessed, materials certified, installations specially inspected — and evidence filed for the wrong system is evidence that does not exist. Matching the documents to the building and system in front of the inspector is a basic but decisive verification step. This is the governing rule for fire protection report and special inspection documents.

questions.question: A storage room holds 20 containers of 5 gallons each. What total quantity is stored in the room?

answers.text: 210 gallons
100 gallons
50 gallons
45 gallons

questions.explanation: Total quantity is container count times unit size: 20 x 5 = 100 gallons. The fire inspector verifies this computed figure against the conditions found in the field.

questions.question: While inspecting a mid-rise office building, the fire inspector is reviewing key boxes for emergency entry. Which condition is a violation that must be corrected?

answers.text: The fire inspector checks a required key box and finds keys for a tenant who left two years ago, with none fitting the current locks.
The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering key boxes for emergency entry
The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering access to fire protection equipment rooms
The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering standpipe and hose connection access

questions.explanation: A key box earns its place by giving firefighters immediate, non-destructive entry, and stale keys turn it into a false promise that costs time at the door. Verifying current, working keys after tenant and lock changes is a small check with outsized value during a night alarm. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for key boxes for emergency entry; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: Regarding inspecting mixed construction in one building, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The fire inspector ignores the separation between an original building and its addition.
The fire inspector treats mixed construction as a classification error to be resolved by choosing one type.

Where a building combines construction types or has additions of a different type, the fire inspector identifies each portion's construction and the separations between them, applying the inspection focus each portion requires.
The fire inspector assigns the whole building the type of its newest addition.

questions.explanation: Mixed construction concentrates risk at the seams, where a fire in the combustible portion attacks the protected portion through openings nobody maintained. Inspecting each portion by its own logic — and the joint between them most carefully of all — matches the inspection to how such buildings actually burn. This is the governing rule for inspecting mixed construction in one building.

questions.question: Regarding sprinkler inspection and service tags, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The fire inspector checks that sprinkler systems carry current inspection and testing documentation from qualified service providers and reports overdue inspection, testing, and maintenance as a deficiency.
The fire inspector treats sprinkler testing as the owner's private arrangement outside inspection scope.
The fire inspector accepts a tag from any year as current if the system looks clean.
The fire inspector requires the tag to be framed and displayed in the lobby.

questions.explanation: Sprinkler reliability is created by the inspection, testing, and maintenance cycle, not by the installation alone, because valves get closed, gauges fail, and components corrode invisibly. Current documentation from qualified providers is the inspector's evidence that the cycle is alive; a years-old tag is evidence it is not. This is the governing rule for sprinkler inspection and service tags.

questions.question: During an inspection of a care facility, the fire inspector is reviewing an accessory use versus a separate occupancy. Which condition is a violation that must be corrected?

answers.text: The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering classifying day care and child care uses
The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering a change of occupancy discovered in the field
The fire inspector accepts a full-scale commercial kitchen and dining operation occupying a third of an office building as a mere accessory use with no occupancy requirements of its own.
The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering an accessory use versus a separate occupancy

questions.explanation: The accessory concept exists for incidental spaces that cannot drive the building's risk; a use that occupies a third of the floor and concentrates cooking hazards plainly can. Judging accessory status by size, function, and hazard keeps the exception from swallowing the classification system. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for an accessory use versus a separate occupancy; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: During a fire inspection of a mixed-use building, a deficiency involving the purpose of occupant load calculation must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected condition satisfy?

answers.text: The fire inspector treats occupant load as a real estate marketing figure.
The fire inspector assumes occupant load matters only for theaters.
The fire inspector considers the owner's expected attendance as the occupant load in all cases.

The fire inspector understands the occupant load as the number of people a space must safely serve in an emergency, from which exit number, exit width, aisle width, and plumbing and alarm provisions are derived.

questions.explanation: Occupant load is the single input that sizes the entire escape system, so an understated load silently undersizes every exit the occupants will use. Inspectors treat the figure as a physical commitment the room must honor, not as an estimate of who usually shows up. Correction is complete only when the corrected condition satisfies the rule for the purpose of occupant load calculation.

questions.question: During an inspection of a care facility, the fire inspector is reviewing classifying factory and industrial occupancies. Which condition is a violation that must be corrected?

answers.text: The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering classifying storage occupancies
The fire inspector records a plant manufacturing foam products with flammable processes as a low-hazard storage occupancy.
The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering classifying factory and industrial occupancies
The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering classifying residential occupancies

questions.explanation: Industrial risk lives in the process and its contents, not in the building's shell, and grading that risk correctly is what scales the protection, separation, and materials controls the inspection enforces. A foam plant wearing a warehouse's classification is a hazard whose paperwork conceals it. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for classifying factory and industrial occupancies; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: During a fire inspection of a manufacturing plant, the fire inspector is reviewing hot work operations and their fire watch. Which condition should the fire inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: The fire inspector verifies that hot work — welding, cutting, grinding, and similar operations — is performed under the required permit and precautions, including a fire watch during and after the work and the removal or protection of nearby combustibles.
The fire inspector checks hot work only in dedicated welding shops.
The fire inspector treats the fire watch as ending the moment the torch is shut off.
The fire inspector permits hot work to proceed wherever the welder finds it convenient.

questions.explanation: Hot work manufactures ignition continuously, and its fires characteristically smolder in concealed or adjacent fuel long after the work ends, which is why the fire watch outlasts the torch. Permits force the precautions — surveyed area, protected combustibles, watch assigned — to exist before the first spark rather than after the first smoke. Applied here, the complying condition is the one that matches the rule for hot work operations and their fire watch.

questions.question: While walking a hospital wing with facility staff, the fire inspector is reviewing an exit stair enclosure kept clear. Which condition is a violation that must be corrected?

answers.text: The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering fire escape ladders and exterior stairs condition
The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering an exit passageway used for storage
The fire inspector finds cleaning chemicals, mops, and a spare desk stored inside an enclosed exit stair serving three floors.
The observed conditions conform to the requirement covering an exit stair enclosure kept clear

questions.explanation: Storage inside an exit enclosure introduces fuel and obstruction into the one space that must stay tenable for every floor's evacuation, and combustible storage under stairs has started fires that cut off the escape route itself. The enclosure's emptiness is a deliberate design feature, not wasted space. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for an exit stair enclosure kept clear; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: While inspecting a mid-rise office building, the fire inspector is reviewing structural damage affecting fire resistance. Which condition should the fire inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: The fire inspector reports structural damage — from fire, vehicle impact, corrosion, or alteration — that could compromise a building's fire-resistive construction and refers it for qualified evaluation.
The fire inspector delays reporting structural damage until the next annual inspection.
The fire inspector ignores spalled concrete and exposed reinforcement as routine aging in all cases.
The fire inspector certifies visibly damaged structural elements as sound based on a visual glance.

questions.explanation: Fire resistance assumes the structure arrives at the fire intact, and damage from impact or corrosion means it may not. Inspectors are not asked to engineer the repair, but they are responsible for surfacing the damage promptly so qualified evaluation happens before a fire tests the weakness. Applied here, the complying condition is the one that matches the rule for structural damage affecting fire resistance.

questions.question: While inspecting a mid-rise office building, the fire inspector is reviewing access roads obstructed by construction or events. Which condition should the fire inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: The fire inspector permits excavations to sever the only access road with no alternative provided.
The fire inspector suspends access requirements for the duration of any construction project.
During construction, demolition, or special events, the fire inspector verifies that required fire access is maintained or that approved temporary arrangements keep the site reachable by apparatus.
The fire inspector treats event barricades blocking access as a traffic matter outside inspection.

questions.explanation: Fire risk does not pause for construction or festivals — it usually rises — so access must be maintained or deliberately replaced with approved alternatives. Inspectors who encounter severed access during temporary activities are protecting the occupants who remain in the buildings behind the blockage. Applied here, the complying condition is the one that matches the rule for access roads obstructed by construction or events.

questions.question: While inspecting a warehouse storing mixed commodities, a deficiency involving floor finish and covering requirements must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected condition satisfy?

answers.text: The fire inspector treats a floor's rating as surviving any covering change automatically.
The fire inspector requires laboratory certificates for every carpet square in every occupancy.
Where floor finishes are regulated — in exits and corridors of certain occupancies — the fire inspector verifies the installed coverings meet the required ratings and reports unrated replacements.
The fire inspector assumes floor coverings are never regulated.

questions.explanation: Floor finishes in egress paths are tested because a corridor fire attacks them under the feet of evacuating occupants, including occupants moved in beds and wheelchairs. Cosmetic replacements are the usual way rated floors disappear, which is why inspectors ask for the rating when coverings change. Correction is complete only when the corrected condition satisfies the rule for floor finish and covering requirements.

questions.question: During a fire inspection of an occupied warehouse, the fire inspector is reviewing when a change of occupancy triggers a new plan. Which condition should the fire inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: The fire inspector recognizes that a change of occupancy or a major change in operations can create a plan requirement where none existed, and refers the new use so its plan obligation is established.
The fire inspector lets a new assembly use inherit a warehouse's lack of a plan.
The fire inspector treats change of occupancy as a zoning matter with no fire planning consequence.
The fire inspector assumes plan requirements never change after a building opens.

questions.explanation: Plan requirements follow the risk of the use, not the history of the building, and use changes are the classic path by which crowded or vulnerable occupancies appear inside envelopes planned for storage. Connecting the change of occupancy to its plan obligation is a core applicability judgment. Applied here, the complying condition is the one that matches the rule for when a change of occupancy triggers a new plan.

questions.question: Regarding occupant load of a portion of a building, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The fire inspector ignores mezzanine loads when checking the floor's exits.

The fire inspector calculates the load of the portion under consideration — a room, a floor, a tenant space — and also considers the loads that share its exits, since exit capacity serves the combined demand placed on it.
The fire inspector evaluates each room's load as if it alone used the exits.
The fire inspector assigns a whole building's load to each of its rooms.

questions.explanation: Exits are shared infrastructure, and their adequacy is a question about everyone who will arrive at them in the same minutes. Evaluating loads room by room in isolation manufactures capacity that the corridor will not have when all three rooms empty at once. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for occupant load of a portion of a building: the fire inspector calculates the load of the portion under consideration — a room, a floor, a tenant space — and also considers the loads that share its exits, since exit capacity serves the combined demand placed on it.

questions.question: While inspecting a mid-rise office building, a deficiency involving an inspection focused on combustible construction must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected condition satisfy?

answers.text: The fire inspector treats fireblocking as uninspectable and omits it entirely.

In combustible construction, the fire inspector emphasizes concealed spaces, fireblocking, vertical openings, and added separations, because hidden fire spread is the type's characteristic failure mode.
The fire inspector checks only the exterior of wood-frame buildings.
The fire inspector inspects combustible buildings exactly as noncombustible ones, with no change of emphasis.

questions.explanation: Combustible buildings burn from the inside of their own structure, through voids and channels that finished surfaces hide. An inspection that never looks into attics, basements, and chases has not inspected the construction type's real hazard at all. Correction is complete only when the corrected condition satisfies the rule for an inspection focused on combustible construction.

questions.question: Regarding special event plan applicability, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The fire inspector checks event plans only for events held outdoors.
The fire inspector treats event planning as the promoter's public relations task.
The fire inspector verifies that temporary events with large crowds, special hazards, or altered layouts have the emergency planning the jurisdiction requires for the event's actual configuration.
The fire inspector assumes annual building plans automatically cover any temporary event layout.

questions.explanation: Temporary layouts rewrite a room's egress geometry — booths, stages, and crowds where the permanent plan assumes open floor — so the permanent plan no longer describes the building people must escape. Event-specific planning matched to the actual configuration is what restores that description. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for special event plan applicability: the fire inspector verifies that temporary events with large crowds, special hazards, or altered layouts have the emergency planning the jurisdiction requires for the event's actual configuration.

questions.question: Regarding identifying the five types of construction in the field, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The fire inspector assumes every masonry building is the most restrictive construction type.
The fire inspector classifies construction by the building's exterior paint and siding appearance alone.

The fire inspector identifies a building's construction type from its structural frame, bearing walls, and floor and roof assemblies — distinguishing protected noncombustible, unprotected combustible, heavy timber, and ordinary construction by their materials and fire-resistance characteristics.
The fire inspector treats construction type as determined by the building's age rather than its assemblies.

questions.explanation: Construction type drives allowable height, area, and many protection requirements, so misidentifying it cascades into wrong conclusions across the whole inspection. The classification lives in the structural assemblies themselves, not in finishes chosen to look substantial. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for identifying the five types of construction in the field: the fire inspector identifies a building's construction type from its structural frame, bearing walls, and floor and roof assemblies — distinguishing protected noncombustible, unprotected combustible, heavy timber, and ordinary construction by their materials and fire-resistance characteristics.

questions.question: Regarding safety cans and portable containers for flammable liquids, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The fire inspector permits unlabeled drink bottles as solvent containers in workshops.

The fire inspector verifies that flammable liquids in use are kept in approved safety cans or original containers with closures maintained, and cites open or improvised containers holding such liquids.
The fire inspector accepts cut-open drums as portable containers for gasoline.
The fire inspector treats the container as irrelevant once the liquid is inside the building.

questions.explanation: Approved containers limit vapor release, resist tipping and spilling, and announce their contents — three protections improvised containers abandon at once, with misidentification adding a poisoning and misuse hazard. The container is the smallest unit of flammable liquid control, and inspectors hold it to standard everywhere liquids are used. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for safety cans and portable containers for flammable liquids: the fire inspector verifies that flammable liquids in use are kept in approved safety cans or original containers with closures maintained, and cites open or improvised containers holding such liquids.

questions.question: Regarding extinguisher inspection tags and monthly checks, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The fire inspector checks that extinguishers show current monthly inspections and annual maintenance by their tags and condition, and reports extinguishers that are overdue, discharged, or damaged.
The fire inspector ignores an extinguisher's pressure gauge reading in the red.
The fire inspector accepts a tag initialed for future months as thoroughness.
The fire inspector treats extinguisher maintenance as purely the service company's concern.

questions.explanation: Extinguishers fail quietly — pressure leaks, hoses crack, contents settle — and the monthly check plus annual maintenance cycle is what stands between storage and readiness. Tags and gauges are the inspector's quick evidence of that cycle, and a neglected extinguisher is worse than none because people will rely on it. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for extinguisher inspection tags and monthly checks: the fire inspector checks that extinguishers show current monthly inspections and annual maintenance by their tags and condition, and reports extinguishers that are overdue, discharged, or damaged.

icc-electrical-plans-examiner.quiz_title: ICC Electrical Plans Examiner Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding fault current at feeder taps and transformers, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Fault current is identical at every point in the building by definition
The documents must account for how available fault current changes through transformers and along feeders when ratings are assigned at downstream equipment
Downstream equipment may be rated from the service fault current with no adjustment or study
Transformer impedance never affects the fault current on its secondary

questions.explanation: Impedance between the source and a panel changes the available current; copying service values downstream documents ratings nobody has verified. This is the governing rule for fault current at feeder taps and transformers.

questions.question: Regarding storable versus permanently installed pool distinction, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Any pool drawn on the plans may use storable-pool provisions regardless of its construction
Storable and permanently installed pools have identical electrical requirements and need not be distinguished
The distinction is made by the owner after installation and never affects the documents
The documents must make clear whether a pool is a storable pool or a permanently installed pool, because the pump, protection, and receptacle requirements shown depend on that distinction

questions.explanation: Construction decides the category; documents that borrow the lighter storable rules for a permanent pool understate every protection that pool requires. This is the governing rule for storable versus permanently installed pool distinction.

questions.question: Regarding boxes in rated assemblies detailed to preserve the rating, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Boxes may be placed back-to-back in a rated wall with no protective detail
Where boxes are shown in fire-resistance-rated walls or ceilings, the details must show the protection, spacing, and putty or enclosure treatment that preserves the assembly rating
Membrane penetrations by boxes never affect a rated assembly as documented
Rated-wall box details are an architectural concern with no electrical documentation

questions.explanation: Every box is a hole in the fire barrier; the documents must show how each penetration is protected so the assembly keeps its rating. This is the governing rule for boxes in rated assemblies detailed to preserve the rating.

questions.question: During review of a service upgrade submittal, a deficiency involving receptacle load calculation for commercial occupancies is cited. Which requirement must the corrected documents satisfy?

answers.text: Receptacle load is included only for dwelling units
The calculation must include receptacle loads for the occupancy at the documented unit values, with demand applied only as permitted for those loads
Receptacles in commercial buildings carry no load in the calculation
Every receptacle is calculated at its maximum possible appliance load with no demand ever

questions.explanation: Receptacle loads are a defined part of commercial calculations; omitting them understates the service the building will actually draw. Correction is complete only when the resubmitted documents satisfy the rule for receptacle load calculation for commercial occupancies.

questions.question: Regarding current-limiting devices credited in the documents, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Where current-limiting overcurrent devices are relied on to protect downstream equipment, the documents must identify the devices and the basis for the let-through values claimed
Current limitation never needs documentation in the submittal
Any fuse may be credited with limiting fault current to any value the designer states
Downstream equipment ratings are irrelevant whenever fuses are used

questions.explanation: Current limitation is a property of specific listed devices; an undocumented claim cannot substitute for equipment ratings. This is the governing rule for current-limiting devices credited in the documents.

questions.question: While reviewing the panel schedules of a mixed-use submittal, the plans examiner is checking feeder demand factors for specific occupancies. Which documented condition should the plans examiner accept as complying?

answers.text: Feeder demand factors are prohibited in commercial buildings
Any feeder may take the most favorable demand factor from any occupancy table
Feeder calculations may apply the demand factors the code provides for the specific occupancy and load type, such as marinas, hospitals, and lodging, where the documents establish that occupancy
The occupancy basis for a feeder demand factor never needs to be documented

questions.explanation: Demand factors belong to specific occupancies; borrowing another occupancy's factor produces a feeder sized for a building that is not this one. Applied here, the complying condition is the one that matches the rule for feeder demand factors for specific occupancies.

questions.question: While verifying classified-area details in an industrial submittal, a deficiency involving health care essential electrical system branches shown is cited. Which requirement must the corrected documents satisfy?

answers.text: Branch assignment for essential loads is optional and need not appear on the one-line
All essential loads may be shown on a single undifferentiated emergency panel

The one-line for a facility with an essential electrical system must show the life safety branch, the critical branch, and the equipment branch as separate branches with their loads assigned as the documents detail
Equipment loads, life safety loads, and patient care loads must all be combined to simplify the documents

questions.explanation: Each branch has its own permitted and required loads and its own transfer arrangement; combining them on the documents hides overloads and prohibited load mixing. Correction is complete only when the resubmitted documents satisfy the rule for health care essential electrical system branches shown.

questions.question: During a plan review of a new service for an office building, the plans examiner is checking demand factors applied in the load calculation. Which documented condition should the plans examiner accept as complying?

answers.text: A single overall demand factor may be applied to the entire connected load
Demand factors may reduce fire alarm and emergency loads on the calculation
Demand factors may be applied in the calculation only to the load types and portions the code permits, and the calculation must show each factor's application
The factors used never need to be shown in the submitted calculation

questions.explanation: Diversification is load-specific; a blanket reduction hides exactly the loads that must never be reduced and cannot be verified. Applied here, the complying condition is the one that matches the rule for demand factors applied in the load calculation.

questions.question: During a plan check of a health care project's electrical design, the plans examiner is checking class division and group identification on plans. Which documented condition should the plans examiner accept as complying?

answers.text: The material group never affects which equipment may be documented for a classified area
Where a classified area is shown, the documents must state its class, its division or zone, and the material group or the specific flammable material involved so equipment suitability can be verified
Stating only that an area is hazardous is sufficient for approval of any equipment shown there
Division and zone designations are interchangeable and need not be distinguished on the plans

questions.explanation: Equipment is approved for a specific class, division or zone, and group; a submittal that omits those designations cannot demonstrate that the listed equipment matches the hazard. Applied here, the complying condition is the one that matches the rule for class division and group identification on plans.

questions.question: While reviewing the pool and special-equipment sheets of a submittal, a deficiency involving electric vehicle charging equipment documentation is cited. Which requirement must the corrected documents satisfy?

answers.text: Charging equipment loads may be treated as noncontinuous in every calculation as noted
Multiple fast chargers may be documented on one small shared branch circuit without a load basis

Electric vehicle charging documents must show a dedicated branch circuit for each charging load as required, the disconnecting provisions where required, and protection and location provisions for the charging equipment as drawn
Charging equipment never requires any disconnecting provision regardless of its rating as documented

questions.explanation: Charging is a large continuous load at a vehicle the public handles; the documents must circuit it, size it, and disconnect it as a dedicated system. Correction is complete only when the resubmitted documents satisfy the rule for electric vehicle charging equipment documentation.

questions.question: During review of a fuel-dispensing facility design, the plans examiner is checking intrinsically safe wiring separation documented. Which documented condition is a deficiency that must be corrected before the plans can be approved?

answers.text: The documents conform to the requirement covering ventilation basis for a reduced classification
The drawings route intrinsically safe instrument conductors in the same raceway as motor power conductors, with no control drawing and no separation detail in the submittal
The documents conform to the requirement covering temperature class of equipment in classified areas
The documents conform to the requirement covering intrinsically safe wiring separation documented

questions.explanation: Intrinsic safety depends on keeping energy-limited circuits from picking up energy from other wiring; documents that mix them without the control drawing defeat the protection. The deficient condition is the one that breaches the rule for intrinsically safe wiring separation documented; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: While reviewing the one-line diagram of a commercial submittal, the plans examiner is checking service load diversity shown in calculations. Which documented condition should the plans examiner accept as complying?

answers.text: Demand factors may be applied to any load at the designer's preference without documentation
Where the calculation applies demand factors, the documents must show the basis for each factor so the examiner can verify the diversified load is permitted for that load type
The examiner approves demand factors without seeing their basis
Continuous loads may be reduced by a demand factor on the calculation

questions.explanation: Demand factors are permissions with conditions, not discounts; each one applied must be traceable to a load type the code allows to be diversified. Applied here, the complying condition is the one that matches the rule for service load diversity shown in calculations.

questions.question: While verifying raceway and box details in a hotel submittal, the plans examiner is checking cable protection where passing through framing. Which documented condition is a deficiency that must be corrected before the plans can be approved?

answers.text: The documents conform to the requirement covering cable and raceway support shown on the details
The documents conform to the requirement covering cable protection where passing through framing
The typical wall detail runs cable through bored holes at the face of the studs and through unbushed punched metal studs, with no protective plate or bushing note
The documents conform to the requirement covering branch circuit identification at outlets and panels

questions.explanation: Screws, nails, and sharp framing edges are predictable damage sources; the documents must detail the protection before the walls are closed. The deficient condition is the one that breaches the rule for cable protection where passing through framing; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: While verifying standby-power design in a health care submittal, the plans examiner is checking emergency lighting and exit sign documentation. Which documented condition is a deficiency that must be corrected before the plans can be approved?

answers.text: The documents conform to the requirement covering fire pump power supply documentation
The egress drawings show exit signs and corridor emergency lights fed from ordinary lighting circuits with no generator connection, transfer provision, or unit battery equipment identified
The documents conform to the requirement covering emergency system selective coordination documentation
The documents conform to the requirement covering emergency lighting and exit sign documentation

questions.explanation: Egress lighting is the load the emergency system exists to serve first; documents that leave it on normal power alone defeat the system. The deficient condition is the one that breaches the rule for emergency lighting and exit sign documentation; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: While verifying equipment nameplate data in a multifamily submittal, the plans examiner is checking motor conductor sizing from full-load current values. Which documented condition is a deficiency that must be corrected before the plans can be approved?

answers.text: The documents conform to the requirement covering motor conductor sizing from full-load current values
The documents conform to the requirement covering overload protection based on nameplate running current
The motor schedule sizes every motor's conductors at exactly its tabulated full-load current, with no margin applied to any continuous-duty motor
The documents conform to the requirement covering branch short-circuit protection separate from overload protection

questions.explanation: Motor conductors carry full-load current for long periods and must have thermal headroom; the documents must apply the sizing margin to the prescribed current values. The deficient condition is the one that breaches the rule for motor conductor sizing from full-load current values; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: While verifying the branch-circuit design in a school submittal, the plans examiner is checking branch circuit conductor size versus breaker shown. Which documented condition is a deficiency that must be corrected before the plans can be approved?

answers.text: The documents conform to the requirement covering branch circuit conductor size versus breaker shown
The schedule pairs the smallest branch-circuit conductors in the project with breakers rated at twice their ampacity
The documents conform to the requirement covering multiwire branch circuits on the panel schedule
The documents conform to the requirement covering branch circuit voltage drop on long runs

questions.explanation: Light load today does not protect a conductor from the fault or overload its breaker would let through; the pairing must be correct on the documents. The deficient condition is the one that breaches the rule for branch circuit conductor size versus breaker shown; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: While checking the feeder schedule of a retail project, the plans examiner is checking feeder conductor ampacity versus its calculated load. Which documented condition is a deficiency that must be corrected before the plans can be approved?

answers.text: The documents conform to the requirement covering voltage drop addressed on long feeders
The documents conform to the requirement covering feeder overcurrent device coordination with conductor size
The feeder schedule pairs a feeder carrying a large continuous lighting load with conductors whose ampacity equals only the running load
The documents conform to the requirement covering feeder conductor ampacity versus its calculated load

questions.explanation: A feeder is sized from its own load, with the continuous portion margined; matching conductors to the raw running load documents an overheated feeder. The deficient condition is the one that breaches the rule for feeder conductor ampacity versus its calculated load; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: Regarding generator disconnecting means and shutdown controls located, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: Emergency shutdown controls are optional decorations on generator plans
A generator may be documented with its only disconnect inside a locked room unknown to responders

The plans must show the generator disconnecting means and, where the installation requires them, remote emergency shutdown controls at the locations the documents designate for responders and operators
Disconnect location for a generator is verified only after a fault event

questions.explanation: Responders and operators must be able to stop a generator without hunting for it; the documents must place and identify its disconnect and shutdown controls. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for generator disconnecting means and shutdown controls located: the plans must show the generator disconnecting means and, where the installation requires them, remote emergency shutdown controls at the locations the documents designate for responders and operators

questions.question: A panel's calculated branch load is 24000 volt-amperes, served by 120-volt, 20-ampere circuits each supplying 2400 volt-amperes. Rounding up, how many branch circuits are required?

answers.text: 11 circuits
13 circuits
10 circuits
9 circuits

questions.explanation: Circuits are total load divided by circuit capacity, rounded up: 24000 / 2400 = 10, so 10 circuits. The plans examiner verifies this computed figure against the governing requirement shown in the documents before approving the plans.

questions.question: Regarding overload protection based on nameplate running current, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: Overload devices are sized from the branch breaker rating as drawn
Service factor and temperature rise information on the nameplate never affect overload selection
One overload setting may be scheduled for all motors of the same horsepower regardless of nameplate data
Motor overload protection shown in the documents must be selected from each motor's nameplate current rating and service factor information, not from the general sizing values used for conductors

questions.explanation: Overloads protect a specific motor's windings; using generic values instead of the motor's own nameplate data leaves individual motors unprotected or nuisance-tripping. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for overload protection based on nameplate running current: motor overload protection shown in the documents must be selected from each motor's nameplate current rating and service factor information, not from the general sizing values used for conductors

icc-commercial-electrical-inspector.quiz_title: ICC Commercial Electrical Inspector Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding certificates and energizing a new service, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Utility connection alone proves the installation complies

A new or altered commercial service is energized and the space occupied only after the required inspections are approved, because energizing unapproved work removes the chance to correct hidden hazards safely
Occupancy approval has no connection to electrical approval in a commercial space
A contractor may energize a new service on their own schedule regardless of inspection status

questions.explanation: Approval before energizing and occupancy is the control point that keeps uninspected, possibly defective work from becoming an occupied hazard. This is the governing rule for certificates and energizing a new service.

questions.question: Regarding recreational and exhibition vehicle exhibition areas, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Public temporary power is governed by exhibitor preference
Exhibition and trade-show power distribution must use approved distribution equipment, protected cords, and ground-fault provisions suited to dense public temporary use
Trade-show booths may be powered by any cords the exhibitor brings
Distribution on an exhibition floor needs no protection planning

questions.explanation: A trade-show floor is a temporary city grid; its distribution is engineered or it is improvised, and the rules require the former. This is the governing rule for recreational and exhibition vehicle exhibition areas.

questions.question: Regarding disconnecting means must disconnect all ungrounded conductors, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Opening one pole of a three-phase disconnect is sufficient
Simultaneous disconnection is required only for motors
A disconnect may leave one phase connected for convenience loads
The service disconnect must simultaneously disconnect all ungrounded service conductors, so no part of the premises wiring remains energized from the service when it is open

questions.explanation: Partial disconnection is a trap: equipment looks dead while one conductor remains live for the next person who trusts the switch. This is the governing rule for disconnecting means must disconnect all ungrounded conductors.

questions.question: While inspecting a place of assembly, the inspector is checking carnivals and traveling shows. Which finding should the inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: Carnival and fair installations require ground-fault protection, proper grounding and bonding of rides and generators, and clearances maintained despite constant setup and teardown
Constant reassembly exempts carnival wiring from rules
Ride power may be grounded to each ride's frame alone
Generators for public rides need no bonding coordination

questions.explanation: Equipment assembled weekly by traveling crews in public mud is held to explicit rules precisely because nothing about it is permanent or familiar. Applied here, the complying finding is the one that matches the rule for carnivals and traveling shows.

questions.question: Regarding neutral-to-case bonding downstream of the service, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Isolation of the neutral downstream is only a residential rule
Bonding neutral to case at every panel improves safety
Neutral current on conduit and enclosures is normal and harmless

Downstream of the service disconnect, the grounded conductor must be isolated from equipment enclosures and grounding conductors, so neutral current returns only on the neutral and never on metal parts

questions.explanation: Neutral current on metal parts is a shock and fire hazard and defeats fault clearing; separation downstream of the one service bond is the rule that prevents it. This is the governing rule for neutral-to-case bonding downstream of the service.

questions.question: At the meter and service equipment inspection for an office building, the inspector is checking service equipment location. Which finding should the inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: Service equipment must be located so it is accessible to the building's occupants and responders, protected from damage, and as close as practicable to where the service conductors enter
Service equipment may be buried deep inside a tenant space far from the point of entry
Long runs of unprotected service conductors inside a building are unrestricted
Location of the service equipment is purely an architectural choice

questions.explanation: Service conductors have no overcurrent protection upstream; keeping their indoor run short and the equipment accessible limits the unprotected exposure. Applied here, the complying finding is the one that matches the rule for service equipment location.

questions.question: At a commercial kitchen equipment check, the inspector is checking luminaire support and listing. Which observed condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The work conforms to the requirement covering luminaires in damp and wet locations
The work conforms to the requirement covering luminaire temperature and combustible materials
The work conforms to the requirement covering luminaire support and listing
Heavy pendant fixtures hang from their supply cords in a retail space

questions.explanation: Support keeps fixtures off people for decades of vibration and maintenance; conductor-supported weight is a slow mechanical failure. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for luminaire support and listing; the other findings describe work that conforms.

questions.question: During a standby system inspection, a deficiency involving smoke control and damper power must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected work satisfy?

answers.text: Damper power failure positions need no coordination
Smoke dampers may be powered from ordinary local circuits with no reliability provisions
Smoke control power design is outside electrical inspection entirely
Power for smoke control systems, dampers, and related life-safety mechanical equipment must come from the sources and with the reliability their systems' designs specify

questions.explanation: Smoke control is a choreographed system; random power sources scramble the choreography exactly when the building is on fire. Correction is complete only when the work satisfies the rule for smoke control and damper power.

questions.question: At a wiring-methods check in a commercial building, a deficiency involving copper versus aluminum conductor properties must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected work satisfy?

answers.text: Terminations listed for copper alone are fine for aluminum
Aluminum conductors require larger sizes than copper for the same ampacity and demand terminations listed for aluminum, proper torque, and attention to oxide at connections
Aluminum and copper of the same size have the same ampacity
Aluminum terminations need no special practice

questions.explanation: Different metals behave differently at connections; aluminum's oxide and creep are managed by listed hardware and practice, not ignored. Correction is complete only when the work satisfies the rule for copper versus aluminum conductor properties.

questions.question: During a final electrical inspection of a commercial space, a deficiency involving group motor installations must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected work satisfy?

answers.text: Group conductors are sized by adding breaker ratings
Any motors may be grouped on any circuit without conditions
Where several motors are fed from one feeder or branch circuit, the protection and conductor rules for groups apply — sized from the largest motor's allowance plus the others' full-load currents
Group circuits protect every motor as if it were alone at full allowance

questions.explanation: Group rules share the starting allowance once — on the largest motor — because motors do not all start at the same instant. Correction is complete only when the work satisfies the rule for group motor installations.

questions.question: At a wiring-methods check in a commercial building, the inspector is checking raceway bends and pull points. Which finding should the inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: Unlimited bends are acceptable if a strong enough pull rope is used
Runs of raceway are limited in total bends between pull points — the equivalent of four quarter-bends — so conductors can be installed and removed without damage
Junction boxes inserted for pulling reset nothing and are decorative
Bend limits apply only to the first pull, not to future conductor replacement
