questions.question: A healthcare professional, an experienced healthcare interpreter studying for certification, is evaluating developmental milestones in movement before the certification examination. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Movement milestones include skills such as reading chapter books and writing essays.
Movement milestones include skills such as rolling over, sitting without support, crawling, standing, and walking as a young child develops.
Movement milestones include the ability to name colors in two languages by infancy.
Movement milestones include memorizing multiplication tables during toddler years.

questions.explanation: Motor milestones track physical abilities that emerge in early childhood, not academic skills expected much later. The correct statement is: Movement milestones include skills such as rolling over, sitting without support, crawling, standing, and walking as a young child develops.

icc-b1.quiz_title: ICC Residential Building Inspector Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: A proposed habitable room measures 10 feet by 11 feet. What is its floor area?

answers.text: 90 square feet
21 square feet
130 square feet
110 square feet

questions.explanation: Floor area is length times width: 10 x 11 = 110 square feet, the figure checked against the minimum area for the room's use. The inspector verifies this computed figure against the governing requirement in the field before approving that stage of the work.

questions.question: An emergency escape window has a net clear opening 26 inches wide by 34 inches high. What is its net clear opening area?

answers.text: 6.1 square feet
884 square feet
7.6 square feet
3.0 square feet

questions.explanation: Net clear area is 26 x 34 = 884 square inches; dividing by 144 gives 6.1 square feet, checked against the minimum for escape openings. The inspector verifies this computed figure against the governing requirement in the field before approving that stage of the work.

questions.question: Regarding moisture content and framing condition, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Decayed studs may be enclosed if they are dry today
Framing lumber must be in sound condition at enclosure — excessive splits, warp that prevents proper bearing or sheathing, and decayed pieces must be corrected
Severely bowed studs are corrected by the drywall, in the inspector's view
Condition of lumber is never grounds for correction

questions.explanation: Enclosure hides condition forever; the framing inspection is the only moment a rotten or failed member can still be replaced. This is the governing rule for moisture content and framing condition.

questions.question: Regarding engineered wood product limits, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Manufacturer instructions do not apply to engineered products
Engineered joists such as I-joists may be cut or drilled only where and as the manufacturer permits, because their thin webs and flanges work differently from solid lumber
Any hole may be cut in an I-joist web at any location
I-joist flanges may be notched like solid-sawn lumber

questions.explanation: An I-joist's flange carries the bending load; cutting it is like cutting a solid joist in half, which is why manufacturers strictly limit field modifications. This is the governing rule for engineered wood product limits.

questions.question: Regarding weep screed and stucco terminations, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Weep screeds are decorative grounds only
Stucco must terminate at its base with a weep screed or equivalent that lets the wall drain and keeps plaster clear of grade and paving as required
Stucco may run into the soil to hide the foundation line
Terminations need no clearance from paving

questions.explanation: The screed is the wall's drain spout and its rot break; burying stucco traps moisture and invites decay and pest entry. This is the governing rule for weep screed and stucco terminations.

questions.question: A footing is 26 inches wide and the foundation wall it supports is 12 inches thick, centred on the footing. How far does the footing project beyond each face of the wall?

answers.text: 7 inches
6 inches
14 inches
9 inches

questions.explanation: With the wall centred, the total projection is 26 - 12 = 14 inches, split evenly: 7 inches on each side. The inspector verifies this computed figure against the governing requirement in the field before approving that stage of the work.

questions.question: At a roofing inspection, a deficiency involving rafter ties and collar ties must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected work satisfy?

answers.text: Rafter ties and collar ties must be present, sized, connected, and located as the code requires — ties at the plate line resist spread, collar ties in the upper roof resist uplift separation
Collar ties at the ridge may replace rafter ties at the plate in all cases
Tie connections need only a single nail
Ties are optional where walls look strong

questions.explanation: Each tie has its own job at its own height; substituting the upper tie for the lower one leaves thrust unopposed where it acts. Correction is complete only when the work satisfies the rule for rafter ties and collar ties.

questions.question: At a footing inspection on a sloping lot, the inspector is checking footing projection and thickness relationship. Which finding should the inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: Projection rules apply only to commercial footings
Thickness may be reduced wherever the footing widens
A thin footing may project any distance beyond the wall
Footing thickness and its projection beyond the wall face are related: the projection cannot exceed what the thickness can structurally support unreinforced

questions.explanation: Plain concrete spreads load at a limited angle; too much projection on too little thickness cracks the footing edge off. Applied here, the complying finding is the one that matches the rule for footing projection and thickness relationship.

questions.question: While checking egress at a framing inspection, a deficiency involving stair width and headroom must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected work satisfy?

answers.text: Stairways must meet the minimum width and provide the required headroom along the whole stair, measured as the code directs
Stair width may pinch at the handrail below the minimum in all cases
Headroom is measured only at the top step
A beam may cross the stair at head height if padded

questions.explanation: Headroom and width protect the tall, the hurried, and the furniture-carrying; a low beam in a dark stair is an injury placed at head height. Correction is complete only when the work satisfies the rule for stair width and headroom.

questions.question: During a foundation walk-through with the builder, the inspector is checking eccentric and offset footings. Which finding should the inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: Footings must be positioned under the walls they support so loads transfer concentrically, unless the design specifically provides otherwise
A wall may bear on the outer inch of its footing with no design
Offset footings are standard practice without engineering
Load path does not matter below the first floor

questions.explanation: Eccentric bearing twists and cracks footings; the wall belongs over its footing unless a design says otherwise. Applied here, the complying finding is the one that matches the rule for eccentric and offset footings.

questions.question: While checking egress at a framing inspection, the inspector is checking exterior stair and deck guards. Which finding should the inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: Weather exposure relaxes opening limits
Exterior guards may be lower than interior ones in all cases
Exterior stairs, decks, and porches open to the weather need guards and handrails under the same safety logic as interiors, built of materials that survive the exposure
A rope railing is a guard

questions.explanation: Gravity works the same outdoors; exterior guards add weather durability to the same height and opening rules. Applied here, the complying finding is the one that matches the rule for exterior stair and deck guards.

questions.question: While checking exterior walls before siding, the inspector is checking cripple walls. Which finding should the inspector accept as complying?

answers.text: Cripple walls are unregulated filler framing
Tall cripple walls need no bracing regardless of height or area conditions
Cripple studs may be toe-nailed scraps
Short cripple walls between the foundation and the first floor must be framed and braced as the code requires for their height and the loads above

questions.explanation: Cripple walls are a storey in miniature and a known seismic weak link; their framing and bracing rules scale with that risk. Applied here, the complying finding is the one that matches the rule for cripple walls.

questions.question: Regarding crawl space ventilation, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: One small vent serves any size crawl space
Vents may be blocked by insulation and storage permanently
Ventilation area is calculated from the attic size
Crawl spaces must be ventilated by openings of the required net area, distributed as required, or built as an approved unvented assembly

questions.explanation: Vent area is proportional to the space it serves; undersized or blocked vents leave ground moisture nowhere to go. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for crawl space ventilation: crawl spaces must be ventilated by openings of the required net area, distributed as required, or built as an approved unvented assembly

questions.question: On a site visit to a new single-family home, a deficiency involving final grade slope away from foundation must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected work satisfy?

answers.text: Water ponding against the foundation is acceptable for new work
Finished grade must fall away from the foundation walls so surface water drains away from the structure rather than toward it
Grade may slope toward the foundation if the soil looks dry
Grade slope is checked only on commercial sites

questions.explanation: Drainage away from the foundation protects footings, walls, and interior spaces from water the site work was supposed to shed. Correction is complete only when the work satisfies the rule for final grade slope away from foundation.

questions.question: While checking an attic before insulation is covered, the inspector is checking roof truss installation. Which observed condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The work conforms to the requirement covering purlins and struts
The work conforms to the requirement covering birdsmouth and rafter bearing
The work conforms to the requirement covering roof truss installation
A truss web was cut out to make storage room and the truss 'fixed' with a nailed 2x4

questions.explanation: Trusses are the most engineered thing on the site; every member and brace is calculated, and field edits without engineering are structural guesses. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for roof truss installation; the other findings describe work that conforms.

questions.question: While checking exterior walls before siding, the inspector is checking control joints in stucco. Which observed condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The work conforms to the requirement covering metal lath type and fastening
The work conforms to the requirement covering stucco curing and weather
The work conforms to the requirement covering control joints in stucco
A very large uninterrupted stucco wall has no control joints and is already map-cracked

questions.explanation: Stucco will move and shrink; joints choose where. Without them the wall chooses — in random cracks. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for control joints in stucco; the other findings describe work that conforms.

questions.question: While checking exterior walls before siding, the inspector is checking siding clearances to grade and roofs. Which observed condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The work conforms to the requirement covering siding clearances to grade and roofs
The work conforms to the requirement covering sheathing thickness and fastening on walls
The wood siding is buried an inch into the soil along the whole elevation
The work conforms to the requirement covering exterior wall covering at projections

questions.explanation: Clearances are rot prevention measured in inches; buried or touching siding wicks water continuously and fails early. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for siding clearances to grade and roofs; the other findings describe work that conforms.

questions.question: Regarding cripple and jack stud lumber, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: Short studs may be any scrap because they are short
Cripples carry no load by definition
Jack, cripple, and king studs are structural lumber subject to the same grade expectations as other framing, because they carry header and plate loads
Jack studs may be finger-jointed remnants in all positions

questions.explanation: Short members carry concentrated loads; scrap cripples crush and settle, taking the header's bearing with them. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for cripple and jack stud lumber: jack, cripple, and king studs are structural lumber subject to the same grade expectations as other framing, because they carry header and plate loads

questions.question: A slab measures 20 feet by 20 feet and is 4 inches thick. Approximately how many cubic yards of concrete does it contain?

answers.text: 9.8 cubic yards
2.5 cubic yards
7.9 cubic yards
4.9 cubic yards

questions.explanation: Volume is 20 x 20 x 1/3 ft = 133 cubic feet; dividing by 27 gives about 4.9 cubic yards. The inspector verifies this computed figure against the governing requirement in the field before approving that stage of the work.

questions.question: A chimney passes through the roof, and the ridge 10 feet away stands 3 feet above the penetration point. Using the rule that a chimney must extend at least 3 feet above its penetration and at least 2 feet above any roof part within 10 feet, how high above the penetration must this chimney reach at minimum?

answers.text: 5 feet
4 feet
7 feet
3 feet

questions.explanation: The two tests give 3 feet and 3 + 2 = 5 feet; the greater governs, so the chimney must reach at least 5 feet above the penetration. The inspector verifies this computed figure against the governing requirement in the field before approving that stage of the work.

icc-plumbing-plans-examiner.quiz_title: ICC Plumbing Plans Examiner Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding buried piping protection detailing, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The submitted details must show protective wrapping, coating, or sleeving for metallic piping installed underground where soil conditions could corrode it, together with the bedding that keeps the pipe from point loading.
The submitted details need only protect buried piping at the point where it enters the building, with the rest of the run unaddressed.
The submitted details may show metallic piping buried directly in any soil with no wrapping or coating regardless of soil condition.
The submitted details satisfy buried-pipe protection by specifying deeper burial alone, with no corrosion treatment required.

questions.explanation: Buried piping cannot be inspected or repaired without excavation, so the documents must demonstrate that soil corrosion and uneven bearing were addressed in the design itself. The plans examiner verifies the wrapping and bedding details at review, because approving an unprotected buried run defers an expensive failure to the building owner. This is the governing rule for buried piping protection detailing.

questions.question: Regarding vent stack and stack vent distinction, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The plans satisfy review when a vent collecting vents from several floors is sized like a single stack vent.
The plans may omit connection details where branch vents join a vent stack on each floor.

The plans must distinguish a vent stack serving multiple floors from a stack vent continuing a single drainage stack, applying the sizing and connection rules of each as drawn for the plans examiner to verify.
The plans may label every vertical vent a stack vent regardless of how many drainage stacks it serves.

questions.explanation: A vent stack accumulates air demand from every floor it collects, while a stack vent serves only its own drainage stack, so confusing the two understates required capacity. Clear labeling and sizing on the riser let the plans examiner apply the correct load basis to each vertical vent. This is the governing rule for vent stack and stack vent distinction.

questions.question: Regarding floor drain placement in fixture areas, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The submitted plans must show floor drains where the adopted plumbing code and the design require them, located so the floor can be sloped to drain and the drain remains accessible for cleaning and trap maintenance.
The submitted plans satisfy floor drain review by showing one drain per building, regardless of how many areas require drainage.
The submitted plans may omit floor drains in restrooms and mechanical areas if the floors are described as waterproof.
The submitted plans need only locate floor drains on the plumbing schedule, with their positions never shown on the floor plans.

questions.explanation: Floors in wet areas are washed down and fixtures in them eventually leak, and without a drain that water ponds, damages finishes, and migrates into adjoining construction. The plans examiner verifies drain locations and the implied floor slopes on the plans because adding a drain after the slab is poured means cutting concrete and reworking the drainage below it. This is the governing rule for floor drain placement in fixture areas.

questions.question: Regarding vent connection height above fixture flood level, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The plans may run a horizontal vent at drain height immediately beside the fixture it vents.
The plans satisfy connection height review when vent tie-in heights are never shown on any section or riser.
The plans may connect a fixture vent below the flood rim of its fixture whenever space is tight.

The plans must show each fixture vent connecting to its vent system at a height above the flood level of the fixture served, or otherwise as permitted, so the plans examiner can verify waste cannot enter the vent during a backup.

questions.explanation: If a drain backs up, waste rises to the flood level of the fixture, and any vent opening below that level becomes a waste passage that clogs the vent. Tie-in height shown on sections lets the plans examiner keep vent openings in the safe zone above foreseeable backups. This is the governing rule for vent connection height above fixture flood level.

questions.question: During review of a plumbing submittal for a school, a deficiency involving chemical feeder protection showing must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected documents satisfy?

answers.text: Where a chemical feeder or similar device connects to the potable system, the plans must show backflow protection suited to that documented chemical hazard at the point of connection.
Where a chemical feeder connects, the plans may rely on the feeder's internal check as the only protection shown.
Where a chemical feeder connects, protection is only needed while the feeder is operating and not as a permanent showing.
Where a chemical feeder connects, a hose bibb downstream satisfies the protection requirement for the feeder itself.

questions.explanation: A feeder holds concentrated chemicals against the pressure of the potable main, and any pressure reversal can drive those chemicals into the drinking water. The examiner requires protection documented at that exact connection, rated for the hazard the feeder presents. Correction is complete only when the corrected documents satisfy the rule for chemical feeder protection showing.

questions.question: While checking fixture schedules for a school project, the plans examiner is reviewing lavatory and faucet material approval. Which documented condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering drinking fountain fixture listing
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering lavatory and faucet material approval
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering bathtub and shower fixture standard
The submitted fixture schedule shows lavatories and faucets with no materials identified and no fitting compliance information provided.

questions.explanation: Restroom fixtures are wetted and cleaned constantly, so absorbent or unapproved materials harbor contamination and deteriorate, while unapproved faucets can allow contaminated water back into the supply. The plans examiner checks materials and fittings in the schedule because those properties are established by the product selected, not by how carefully it is installed. The violating documented condition is the one that breaches the rule for lavatory and faucet material approval; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: While verifying a drainage plan set before approval, the plans examiner is reviewing condensate drain disposal showings. Which documented condition should the plans examiner accept as complying?

answers.text: The plans may terminate condensate lines directly into a drainage pipe with a hard connection and no air gap.
The plans satisfy condensate review when the lines are drawn ending above a finished floor with no receptor.
The plans must show condensate drains from cooling and refrigeration equipment discharging through an air gap to an approved receptor or drain, with pipe size and route documented.
The plans may omit condensate drain routes entirely because the volume of water is small.

questions.explanation: Condensate forms continuously while equipment runs, and a hard connection exposes the unit to sewer backflow while an unterminated line damages finishes. Documenting size, route, and air-gapped termination lets the plans examiner verify a safe and complete disposal path. Applied here, the complying documented condition is the one that matches the rule for condensate drain disposal showings.

questions.question: While checking storm sizing calculations in a submittal, a deficiency involving leader material approval notation must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected documents satisfy?

answers.text: Submitted plans must identify leader and conductor materials that are approved for storm drainage service and compatible with the rest of the system shown.
Submitted plans must specify the same leader material for every project regardless of height or exposure.
Submitted plans are complete when leader material is described only as metal or plastic with no specific product type.
Submitted plans may specify any piping material for leaders including materials not approved for drainage use.

questions.explanation: Leaders endure weather, impact, and continuous wet service, and unapproved materials deteriorate or fail under those conditions. A clear material notation lets the examiner verify the chosen product is listed for this use and matches the connected piping. Correction is complete only when the corrected documents satisfy the rule for leader material approval notation.

questions.question: The submitted water distribution layout runs in three sections of 60 feet, 35 feet, and 15 feet from the meter to the most remote outlet. What developed length must the sizing documentation use?

answers.text: 135 feet
60 feet
90 feet
110 feet

questions.explanation: Developed length is the sum of the sections: 60 + 35 + 15 = 110 feet. The plans examiner verifies this computed figure against the submitted documents before approving the plans.

questions.question: While verifying a drainage plan set before approval, the plans examiner is reviewing hub drain and floor sink placement. Which documented condition should the plans examiner accept as complying?

answers.text: The plans may show indirect waste piping passing through a food storage area to reach a distant receptor without comment.
The plans satisfy placement review when equipment drains must run uphill to reach the receptor as drawn.
The plans may place the only floor sink across the room from the equipment with a long flat indirect run.
The plans must place floor sinks and hub drains where the equipment they serve can reach them by gravity with short, properly sloped indirect waste runs as shown on the floor plan.

questions.explanation: Indirect waste flows by gravity in open piping, so distance and slope decide whether it reaches the receptor or ponds and spills along the way. Placement reviewed on the floor plan keeps runs short, sloped, and inside the area the receptor is meant to serve. Applied here, the complying documented condition is the one that matches the rule for hub drain and floor sink placement.

questions.question: During review of a hotel water heating plant submittal, the plans examiner is reviewing water heater vent height showing. Which documented condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering water heater vent height showing
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering combustion air for multiple heaters showing
The submitted set sizes the water heater vent from a stated height but includes no section or dimension establishing that height anywhere in the drawings.
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering gas piping plan legend and load schedule

questions.explanation: Draft strength is produced by the height of the warm column of gas, so the sizing stands or falls on the height actually available in the building. Requiring the height to be shown lets the examiner confirm the building can deliver the vent performance the calculation claims. The violating documented condition is the one that breaches the rule for water heater vent height showing; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: During plan review of a hotel's DWV drawings, a deficiency involving relief vent showings for long stacks must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected documents satisfy?

answers.text: For tall stacks, relief vent locations may be left to field judgment after the stack is installed.
For tall stacks, the plans may omit relief vents whenever the stack vent itself is generously sized.
For tall stacks, a single relief vent at the top satisfies every floor regardless of building height as drawn.

For tall stacks and stacks receiving load over many stories, the plans must show relief or yoke vents where required to equalize pressure, with their size and connection floors identified for the plans examiner.

questions.explanation: Falling waste in a tall stack creates positive and negative pressure waves that a roof vent alone cannot equalize at distant floors. Relief connections shown at their floors let the plans examiner verify pressure protection where traps are most at risk. Correction is complete only when the corrected documents satisfy the rule for relief vent showings for long stacks.

questions.question: During review of a hotel water heating plant submittal, the plans examiner is reviewing temperature and pressure relief valve specification. Which documented condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering temperature and pressure relief valve specification
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering relief valve discharge piping detail
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering water heater drain pan provision
The submitted water heater schedule and details contain no temperature-and-pressure relief valve specification for any storage heater in the project.

questions.explanation: A storage heater whose controls fail can turn its tank into a pressure vessel, and the combined temperature-and-pressure valve is the last safeguard against a catastrophic tank rupture. The plans examiner verifies the specified valve and its rating against each heater because a mismatched or missing valve leaves that safeguard entirely to chance. The violating documented condition is the one that breaches the rule for temperature and pressure relief valve specification; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: While checking interceptor details in a parking structure submittal, the plans examiner is reviewing grease interceptor sizing documentation. Which documented condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The submitted restaurant plans show a single grease interceptor serving the full kitchen with no sizing basis, fixture list, or flow information provided.
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering grease interceptor sizing documentation
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering trap seal depth showing
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering trap arm length and slope showing

questions.explanation: Grease interceptors only separate effectively when their capacity matches the actual discharge they receive, so an undocumented size cannot be reviewed for adequacy. Requiring the sizing basis on the submittal lets the examiner confirm that peak kitchen flows will be retained long enough for separation before discharge. The violating documented condition is the one that breaches the rule for grease interceptor sizing documentation; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: While checking water heater schedules and gas piping plans, the plans examiner is reviewing outdoor combustion air method showing. Which documented condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering vent connector sizing showing
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering mechanical combustion air showing
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering outdoor combustion air method showing
The submitted plan notes that outdoor combustion air will be provided for the water heater room but shows no openings, ducts, or louvers anywhere in the set.

questions.explanation: Outdoor air methods work only through the specific openings or ducts they rely on, so a label without the physical provisions proves nothing. The examiner verifies that the identified method and the drawn provisions match, and returns a set where the air path exists only in a note. The violating documented condition is the one that breaches the rule for outdoor combustion air method showing; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: While checking interceptor details in a parking structure submittal, a deficiency involving indirect waste connection through trap protection must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected documents satisfy?

answers.text: Submitted plans may connect an indirect waste receptor directly to the drainage system with no trap shown.
Submitted plans must show indirect waste receptors protected by a properly trapped and vented connection as required by the adopted plumbing code.
Submitted plans are complete when the receptor trap is shown but its vent connection is left off the drawings.
Submitted plans must show indirect waste receptors trapped only when they receive food waste.

questions.explanation: A receptor is an open point in the drainage system, and without a trap it becomes a direct opening for sewer gas at floor level. Showing the trapped and vented receptor connection lets the examiner confirm both drainage and air protection at that opening. Correction is complete only when the corrected documents satisfy the rule for indirect waste connection through trap protection.

questions.question: Regarding backwater valve location showings, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The plans may place the backwater valve requirement in a general note without showing any valve location on the drawings.
The plans satisfy backwater review when a valve is drawn only on fixtures located well above street level.
The plans may omit a backwater valve for all below-grade fixtures as long as the building has a sump pump.

The plans must show a backwater valve on the building drain or on branches serving fixtures whose flood level is below the elevation of the next upstream manhole cover or other point of relief identified on the documents.

questions.explanation: When public sewer levels rise, sewage flows backward toward the lowest fixtures unless a backwater valve blocks that path. Showing the valve where the elevation relationship requires it lets the plans examiner protect below-grade spaces before a surcharge floods them. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for backwater valve location showings: the plans must show a backwater valve on the building drain or on branches serving fixtures whose flood level is below the elevation of the next upstream manhole cover or other point of relief identified on the documents.

questions.question: Regarding hose bibb valving and protection showing, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The plans may show hose bibbs as plain outlets with no protective provisions regardless of their use.
The plans must show hose bibbs and similar outlets with the valving and protective provisions documented for outlets that connect to hoses and external uses.
The plans only need hose bibb provisions on the building's front elevation and not at service yards.
The plans may omit hose bibbs from the plumbing drawings entirely when they are shown on the architectural elevations.

questions.explanation: A hose connection can submerge an outlet in nonpotable water and pull contamination back toward the supply, which is why these outlets carry specific documented provisions. The examiner reconciles the plumbing plans with the elevations so no outlet escapes the protection review. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for hose bibb valving and protection showing: the plans must show hose bibbs and similar outlets with the valving and protective provisions documented for outlets that connect to hoses and external uses.

questions.question: During review of patient-room plumbing in a care facility submittal, the plans examiner is reviewing handwashing station documentation in care areas. Which documented condition is a violation that must be corrected before approval?

answers.text: The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering health care fixture material approval showing
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering scrub sink installation detail in procedure areas
The submitted documents conform to the requirement covering handwashing station documentation in care areas
The submitted patient floor plans show care rooms with sinks scheduled for general use and no dedicated handwashing station identified in any room.

questions.explanation: Hand hygiene depends on a fixture that is always available and never used for waste disposal, which is a planning distinction that must be visible in the submittal. Identifying dedicated stations room by room lets the examiner confirm infection control functions are actually plumbed into the design. The violating documented condition is the one that breaches the rule for handwashing station documentation in care areas; the other conditions describe documents that conform.

questions.question: Regarding roof drain strainer detail documentation, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: Submitted roof drain details must show a strainer or dome with the free inlet area required by the adopted plumbing code so debris cannot readily block the drain opening.
Submitted roof drain details are acceptable when the strainer is mentioned in a catalog cut but not in the detail itself.
Submitted roof drain details must show a flat strainer flush with the roof surface for every drain type.
Submitted roof drain details may omit the strainer whenever the roof is described as normally clean.

questions.explanation: Leaves and roofing debris migrate to drain openings during every storm, and an unguarded opening clogs at the moment drainage is most needed. Showing the strainer in the detail confirms the installed drain will keep its inlet open under real roof conditions. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for roof drain strainer detail documentation: submitted roof drain details must show a strainer or dome with the free inlet area required by the adopted plumbing code so debris cannot readily block the drain opening.

icc-permit-technician.quiz_title: ICC Permit Technician Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding handling requests for another persons project information, which statement is correct?

answers.text: When a person requests another party project information, the permit technician provides the information only if the requester explains a reason staff approve of.
When a person requests another party project information, the permit technician releases the entire file including private contact and security details.

When a person requests information about another party project, the permit technician provides the portions that are public record and withholds protected personal or security information under disclosure rules.
When a person requests another party project information, the permit technician refuses all access solely because the requester is not the owner.

questions.explanation: Public records law generally does not require a requester to be the owner or to justify the request for disclosable material. At the same time, third-party files contain details that disclosure rules protect regardless of who asks. Applying both principles item by item is the technician responsibility at the point of release. This is the governing rule for handling requests for another persons project information.

questions.question: Regarding recording an easement release in a permit file, which statement is correct?

answers.text: When an easement is released, the permit technician destroys the original plat to keep the file current.
When an easement is released, the permit technician relies on the applicant's verbal assurance and keeps no documentation.
When an easement affecting a project has been formally released or vacated, the permit technician records that documentation in the file before treating the area as available for construction.
When an easement is released, the permit technician records the release of a different parcel's easement as sufficient.

questions.explanation: A release changes the legal usability of the land, so the file must show the recorded evidence rather than a recollection. Documenting it protects future reviewers and buyers who will rely on the permit history to understand why construction was allowed in that area. This is the governing rule for recording an easement release in a permit file.

questions.question: Regarding maintaining impartiality when serving competing applicants, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The permit technician maintains impartiality by expediting a relative application ahead of earlier submittals without disclosure.
The permit technician maintains impartiality by sharing one applicant confidential project plans with a direct competitor at the counter.
The permit technician maintains impartiality by applying stricter document demands to an applicant they personally dislike.

The permit technician maintains impartiality by processing applications in established order, applying the same requirements and fees to competing applicants, and disclosing any personal interest in a project.

questions.explanation: Public permitting works only if every applicant believes the process is neutral and their information is safe. Queue order, uniform requirements, and disclosure of personal interests are the practical mechanics of that neutrality. Even the appearance of favoritism damages trust in approvals that competitors and the public must accept. This is the governing rule for maintaining impartiality when serving competing applicants.

questions.question: Regarding verifying mixed occupancies are each designated, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The permit technician records only the largest occupancy for a mixed-use building and omits the others.
The permit technician tells the applicant mixed occupancies need not be designated if the building is small.
The permit technician combines all uses in a mixed-use building under a single generic designation of their choosing.
When a project involves more than one occupancy group in the same building, the permit technician verifies that each occupancy is designated in the plans or permit documents.

questions.explanation: Each use in a mixed building carries its own considerations, and reviewers need every one of them identified. Verifying that all occupancies are designated prevents a use from escaping the review it requires. This is the governing rule for verifying mixed occupancies are each designated.

questions.question: During intake work at a building department, a deficiency involving handling public records requests for permit files must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected handling satisfy?

answers.text: The permit technician handles public records requests by allowing requesters to browse original files unsupervised and remove pages they need.

The permit technician handles requests for permit files through the public records process, providing access to disclosable records within the required timeframe and noting any portions withheld under an exemption.
The permit technician handles public records requests by providing records immediately to friends while making other requesters wait months without explanation.
The permit technician handles public records requests by denying access to all permit records because they contain owner names and addresses.

questions.explanation: Permit records are largely public, and orderly access supports transparency, property research, and accountability. Supervised or copied access protects originals that the jurisdiction must retain for the life of the building. Applying the same process and timeframe to everyone prevents favoritism and unlawful delay. Correction is complete only when the corrected handling satisfies the rule for handling public records requests for permit files.

questions.question: Regarding confirming required forms are signed and dated, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The permit technician confirms required submittal forms are signed and dated by the appropriate party before accepting the package as complete.
The permit technician accepts unsigned forms and adds a signature stamp kept at the counter.
The permit technician backdates a form to the day the applicant first visited the counter.
The permit technician dates forms themselves with the expected review completion date.

questions.explanation: A signature ties the submittal's statements to a responsible party and the date fixes the filing in the project timeline. Checking both at intake is a small step that supports fees, deadlines, and accountability throughout the process. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for confirming required forms are signed and dated: the permit technician confirms required submittal forms are signed and dated by the appropriate party before accepting the package as complete.

questions.question: While checking a plan submittal at the permit counter, a deficiency involving documenting deficiencies found in a submittal must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected handling satisfy?

answers.text: The permit technician holds an incomplete submittal without notifying the applicant at all.
When a submittal is incomplete, the permit technician documents the specific missing or deficient items and provides that list to the applicant for correction and resubmittal.
The permit technician tells the applicant the submittal is incomplete without identifying what is missing.
The permit technician corrects deficient documents personally instead of returning them to the applicant.

questions.explanation: A specific deficiency list is the fastest path to a complete resubmittal, for both the applicant and the department. Documenting it also creates a record of what was requested, which prevents disputes on the next visit. Correction is complete only when the corrected handling satisfies the rule for documenting deficiencies found in a submittal.

questions.question: Regarding checking documents when occupancy and construction type interact in fees, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: The permit technician finalizes fees before the occupancy and construction type are designated in the documents.
The permit technician uses the designated occupancy group and construction type recorded in the documents when calculating permit fees, and verifies both before finalizing the calculation.
The permit technician lets the applicant select the construction type for fee purposes regardless of the plans.
The permit technician calculates fees using whichever occupancy produces the lowest charge.

questions.explanation: Fee schedules commonly key charges to occupancy and construction type, so those entries must come from the documents, not negotiation. Verifying both before calculating keeps fees consistent between similar projects and defensible if questioned. The incorrect statement is the one that contradicts the rule for checking documents when occupancy and construction type interact in fees: the permit technician uses the designated occupancy group and construction type recorded in the documents when calculating permit fees, and verifies both before finalizing the calculation.

questions.question: While checking a plot plan submitted with an application, a deficiency involving verifying a required side setback on a site plan must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected handling satisfy?

answers.text: The permit technician verifies a side setback by comparing the lot width to the street frontage.
The permit technician verifies a required side setback by comparing the distance shown between each side lot line and the nearest part of the proposed structure to the required side yard.
The permit technician verifies a side setback by averaging the front and rear yards shown on the plan.
The permit technician verifies a side setback by measuring only to the structure's front corner and ignoring projections.

questions.explanation: Side yards provide separation for light, air, fire safety, and maintenance access between neighboring properties. Measuring to the closest part of the structure, including projections the ordinance counts, ensures the check reflects how the building will actually sit on the lot. Correction is complete only when the corrected handling satisfies the rule for verifying a required side setback on a site plan.

questions.question: At the permit counter of a building department, the permit technician is reviewing researching certificates and final approvals. Which condition is a violation that must be corrected?

answers.text: A buyer asks whether a finished basement was finaled and the technician confirms it based on the listing description without checking the records.
The handling conforms to the requirement covering cross-referencing parcel and address information
The handling conforms to the requirement covering researching code compliance history and violations
The handling conforms to the requirement covering researching certificates and final approvals

questions.explanation: Occupancy and financing decisions often hinge on whether prior work received its final approval. Checking the record before answering protects buyers and owners from relying on an assumption that the file does not support. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for researching certificates and final approvals; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: At the permit counter with a set of construction drawings, a deficiency involving confirming project valuation and scope documents align must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected handling satisfy?

answers.text: The permit technician checks that the stated project valuation and scope documents submitted are consistent with the plans for purposes of fee calculation and routing.
The permit technician ignores a stated valuation that plainly conflicts with the size of work shown on the plans.
The permit technician adjusts the applicant's stated valuation downward to lower the fee without any basis.
The permit technician calculates fees from the contractor's verbal estimate instead of the submitted documents.

questions.explanation: Fees and review routing both scale with the actual scope of work, so an understated valuation distorts both. Flagging an obvious mismatch at intake keeps fee calculation honest without the technician redesigning or re-estimating the project. Correction is complete only when the corrected handling satisfies the rule for confirming project valuation and scope documents align.

questions.question: While logging a plan submittal in the permit system, a deficiency involving maintaining occupancy information in the historical record must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected handling satisfy?

answers.text: The permit technician ensures the final occupancy and construction type designations are preserved in the project record so future research reflects what was actually approved.
The permit technician records only the proposed occupancy and discards the designation that was finally approved.
The permit technician updates historical occupancy entries to match a later tenant without preserving the original designation.
The permit technician deletes the construction type from closed files during routine cleanup.

questions.explanation: Buildings change uses over decades, and each approved designation is a chapter in that history. Preserving the final approved designations lets future staff reconstruct the sequence instead of finding only the latest entry. Correction is complete only when the corrected handling satisfies the rule for maintaining occupancy information in the historical record.

questions.question: At the permit counter with a subdivision plat, the permit technician is reviewing explaining utility clearance from an easement holder. Which handling should the permit technician accept as complying?

answers.text: The permit technician explains that paying the permit fee serves as the utility's clearance for the encroachment.
The permit technician explains that the utility holder's clearance is never needed if the building is small.
The permit technician explains that building within a utility easement may require written clearance from the utility that holds the easement before a permit can be issued.
The permit technician explains that the permit technician can sign the clearance on the utility's behalf at the counter.

questions.explanation: The easement holder's rights cannot be bargained away by the permitting office, and the holder may need access or separation for safety and maintenance. Requiring the holder's written clearance before issuance aligns the permit with the private rights that already burden the land. Applied here, the complying handling is the one that matches the rule for explaining utility clearance from an easement holder.

questions.question: During records work in a building department office, the permit technician is reviewing noting gaps and limitations found during research. Which condition is a violation that must be corrected?

answers.text: The handling conforms to the requirement covering noting gaps and limitations found during research
The handling conforms to the requirement covering researching who performed and designed past work
The handling conforms to the requirement covering researching fees and payments tied to past projects
A research summary covers only recent permits and presents itself as a complete history even though archived records for earlier decades were never checked.

questions.explanation: Every archive has limits, and overstating a search misleads the people relying on it. Disclosing gaps keeps expectations honest and tells the requester where additional diligence, such as a title or site investigation, may be needed. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for noting gaps and limitations found during research; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: While logging a plan submittal in the permit system, the permit technician is reviewing recording the occupancy designation on the issued permit. Which condition is a violation that must be corrected?

answers.text: The handling conforms to the requirement covering checking occupancy designation for temporary uses and events
An issued permit shows no occupancy group even though the approved plans designate one, leaving the official record incomplete.
The handling conforms to the requirement covering explaining that the technician verifies rather than classifies occupancy
The handling conforms to the requirement covering recording the occupancy designation on the issued permit

questions.explanation: The issued permit is the document owners, buyers, and other agencies read first, often without the plans in hand. Recording the approved designation accurately makes the permit a reliable summary of what was authorized. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for recording the occupancy designation on the issued permit; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: While assisting an applicant with a site plan submittal, the permit technician is reviewing identifying a drainage easement at intake. Which condition is a violation that must be corrected?

answers.text: The handling conforms to the requirement covering explaining a temporary encroachment in the right-of-way
The handling conforms to the requirement covering checking for easements before issuing a permit
The handling conforms to the requirement covering identifying a drainage easement at intake
An application proposes filling and building within a drainage easement, and the permit is issued without engineering review of the obstruction.

questions.explanation: Blocked drainage paths redirect water onto neighboring lots and streets, creating flooding and liability beyond the single parcel. Flagging drainage easements at intake ensures engineering reviewers evaluate any proposal that could interrupt the designed flow. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for identifying a drainage easement at intake; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: While checking a plan submittal at the permit counter, the permit technician is reviewing confirming required forms are signed and dated. Which handling should the permit technician accept as complying?

answers.text: The permit technician dates forms themselves with the expected review completion date.
The permit technician accepts unsigned forms and adds a signature stamp kept at the counter.
The permit technician backdates a form to the day the applicant first visited the counter.
The permit technician confirms required submittal forms are signed and dated by the appropriate party before accepting the package as complete.

questions.explanation: A signature ties the submittal's statements to a responsible party and the date fixes the filing in the project timeline. Checking both at intake is a small step that supports fees, deadlines, and accountability throughout the process. Applied here, the complying handling is the one that matches the rule for confirming required forms are signed and dated.

questions.question: While assisting a resident with a permit question, the permit technician is reviewing handling research requests that require extensive searching. Which handling should the permit technician accept as complying?

answers.text: The permit technician starts extensive research without logging it, so no one can follow up on its status.
The permit technician declines any research that cannot be finished while the requester waits at the counter.
The permit technician promises extensive research results by the end of the same hour without checking the workload.
For research requests that require extensive searching, the permit technician explains the process, any applicable fees, and the expected timeframe, and logs the request for follow-up.

questions.explanation: Large research jobs compete with daily counter work and may involve archived material that takes time to retrieve. Setting expectations and logging the request ensures the work is tracked, completed, and delivered as promised. Applied here, the complying handling is the one that matches the rule for handling research requests that require extensive searching.

questions.question: While assisting an applicant with a site plan submittal, the permit technician is reviewing verifying an accessory structure location on a site plan. Which condition is a violation that must be corrected?

answers.text: The handling conforms to the requirement covering verifying an accessory structure location on a site plan
A shed is permitted directly on the side lot line in a district that requires accessory structures to observe a side setback.
The handling conforms to the requirement covering confirming lot dimensions before site verification
The handling conforms to the requirement covering explaining a site plan correction to an applicant

questions.explanation: Accessory buildings are frequent sources of neighbor complaints and easement conflicts precisely because they are often treated as informal. Applying the district's accessory placement rules at intake gives sheds, garages, and similar structures the same lawful siting check as the main building. The violating condition is the one that breaches the rule for verifying an accessory structure location on a site plan; the other conditions describe situations that conform.

questions.question: While assisting a resident with a permit question, the permit technician is reviewing retaining records for projects that were never completed. Which handling should the permit technician accept as complying?

answers.text: The permit technician returns all submitted documents for an expired permit and keeps no copies at all.
The permit technician retains abandoned project files only if the applicant pays a storage fee.
The permit technician destroys the file for an abandoned project as soon as the permit expires.
The permit technician retains applications, plans, and correspondence for expired or abandoned projects for the required period rather than destroying them when the permit lapses.

questions.explanation: An expired project often returns as a new application, and its prior reviews and comments shape the next submittal. Retaining the file for the required period also preserves the record of fees, decisions, and notices if questions arise later. Applied here, the complying handling is the one that matches the rule for retaining records for projects that were never completed.

st-augustine-tour-guide.quiz_title: St. Augustine Tour Guide Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: In a tour review, a question addresses carolina raids destroying the missions. Which answer is right?

answers.text: The mission destroying raids were led by Spanish friars who burned their own churches to protest low wages.
After seventeen oh two, Carolina led raids rebuilt every Florida mission in stone and staffed them with English clergy.
After seventeen oh two the mission provinces grew richer and more populous than ever under Carolina protection.
In the years after seventeen oh two, Carolina led raids with Native allies destroyed the Apalachee and Timucua mission provinces, killing and enslaving many residents.

questions.explanation: The raids collapsed a mission world built over more than a century in a few violent seasons. Survivors fled toward Saint Augustine, Pensacola, or French settlements to the west.

questions.question: On the subject of nombre de dios mission founding, which statement is right?

answers.text: The mission of Nombre de Dios, founded near the first landing grounds north of the town, is regarded as the first mission in what is now the continental United States.
The mission of Nombre de Dios was founded in New Mexico by English settlers a century after Saint Augustine began.
The mission of Nombre de Dios was built by British troops in the seventeen hundreds as a barracks and stable.
The mission of Nombre de Dios was a French trading post that sold beaver pelts and never held religious services.

questions.explanation: Nombre de Dios grew on the ground tied to the landing and the village of Seloy. Its church and shrine kept that northern ground sacred in local memory for centuries.

questions.question: Regarding telling the fort mose story honestly, which statement is correct?

answers.text: A guide presents Fort Mose as a Spanish prison built to punish enslaved people who ran away.
A guide presents Fort Mose as a settlement of formerly enslaved people who won freedom under Spanish rule, and describes both that freedom and the dangers surrounding it.
A guide presents Fort Mose as a resort where enslaved people spent holidays from plantation work.
A guide presents Fort Mose as a legend with no archaeological or documentary basis at all.

questions.explanation: In the seventeen hundreds, people escaping slavery in the English colonies reached Spanish Florida and built a free Black town north of the city. Its story complicates simple narratives, which is exactly why guides should tell it fully and accurately.

questions.question: On the subject of lightner museum inside the alcazar, which statement is right?

answers.text: The Lightner Museum is housed inside the old Spanish fort on the bay.
The Lightner Museum now fills the former Alcazar Hotel, displaying collections of art, glass, and everyday objects from Americas Gilded Age.
The Lightner Museum now fills the former lighthouse tower on the inlet.
The Lightner Museum occupies a replica pirate ship anchored offshore.

questions.explanation: Visitors tour galleries where hotel guests once lodged and amused themselves. The great empty pool, now lined with tables and a small cafe setting, recalls the casino era.

questions.question: Consider hardships at new smyrna disease and insects. Which statement holds true?

answers.text: At New Smyrna, the main hardship was heavy snow and frozen canals in winter.
At New Smyrna, settlers lived in stone houses provided on arrival and did little manual labor.
At New Smyrna, settlers suffered terribly from malaria and other diseases, biting insects, and clearing dense hammock land in extreme heat.
At New Smyrna, the mild climate meant disease was almost unknown among the settlers.

questions.explanation: Mosquito-borne illness and poor sanitation killed settlers at an alarming rate, especially in the first years. Grief and exhaustion, as much as any single event, steadily turned the colonists against the enterprise.

questions.question: A trainee asks why a point involving coquina hardening after quarrying holds. Which explanation is correct?

answers.text: Freshly cut coquina stays soft forever and was held together only by iron bands.
Freshly cut coquina is hardest underground and turns to powder in sunlight.
Freshly cut coquina must be fired in kilns for a month before it can be used.
Freshly cut coquina is soft and easy to shape, then hardens as it dries in air, which made it practical to quarry with simple tools.

questions.explanation: Quarrymen exploited the brief soft stage to saw blocks to size. Once cured in the sun, the stone resisted weather and, as battles proved, even cannonballs.

questions.question: Focus on king arrest at the monson motor lodge restaurant for a moment - which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: In June of nineteen sixty-four, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was arrested at the Monson Motor Lodge restaurant in St. Augustine after seeking service at the segregated business.
In June of nineteen sixty-four, Dr. King was arrested at the Monson Motor Lodge for failing to pay a lodging bill.
In June of nineteen sixty-four, Dr. King was arrested inside the Castillo for climbing its walls after hours.
In June of nineteen sixty-four, Dr. King was arrested at the Monson Motor Lodge for pouring chemicals into its pool.

questions.explanation: King and companions asked to be served, were refused, and were arrested on the steps of the restaurant. The arrest of the nation most famous civil rights leader in a small Florida city became a defining image of the campaign.

questions.question: While preparing at the City Gate, Alicia reviews treaty of paris seventeen sixty-three terms. Which statement applies?

answers.text: The Treaty of Paris in seventeen sixty-three gave Florida to France in exchange for Louisiana.
The Treaty of Paris in seventeen sixty-three divided Florida equally between Britain and France.
The Treaty of Paris in seventeen sixty-three ended the Seven Years War and Spain ceded Florida to Great Britain in exchange for the return of Havana.
The Treaty of Paris in seventeen sixty-three made Florida an independent republic under Spanish protection.

questions.explanation: Britain had captured Havana during the war, and Spain valued that port more than sparsely settled Florida. The exchange explains why a Spanish city suddenly became British without a battle fought in St. Augustine itself.

questions.question: At the bayfront seawall, the discussion turns to plaza de armas central courtyard. Which statement earns agreement?

answers.text: The Castillo central courtyard was a public market where townspeople sold goods every day.
The Castillo central courtyard, the plaza de armas, was the open heart of the fort where troops assembled, drilled, and drew water under protection.
The Castillo central courtyard was flooded as a reservoir for visiting warships.
The Castillo central courtyard held the governors palace and his family residence.

questions.explanation: Rooms for soldiers, stores, and worship open off the courtyard on every side. In a siege the whole life of the garrison contracted into this sheltered square of ground.

questions.question: Focus on st augustine as military base in the seminole war for a moment - which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: The Second Seminole War never affected life in St. Augustine in any way.
During the Second Seminole War, St. Augustine was abandoned by the army and left empty.
During the Second Seminole War, the town sided with the Seminoles against the United States.
During the Second Seminole War, St. Augustine served as an important United States Army post and supply point, with soldiers, hospitals, and anxious refugees filling the town.

questions.explanation: Regiments rotated through the city, wounded men were treated there, and military spending propped up the local economy. At the same time, residents feared attacks so much that travel beyond town limits could be dangerous.

questions.question: A guest at the Bridge of Lions asks Daniel about castillo construction begun sixteen seventy-two. Which guidance is correct?

answers.text: Construction of the Castillo de San Marcos began in seventeen forty, during the siege led by James Oglethorpe.
Construction of the Castillo de San Marcos began in fifteen sixty-five, the same year the town was founded.
Construction of the Castillo de San Marcos began in sixteen seventy-two after earlier wooden defenses proved too weak to protect the town.
Construction of the Castillo de San Marcos began in eighteen twenty-one, after Florida passed to the United States.

questions.explanation: Work on the stone fort started in sixteen seventy-two under Governor Manuel de Cendoya. The project replaced a long line of wooden forts that fire, rot, and attack had repeatedly destroyed.

questions.question: Looked at closely, tolomato cemetery tours only when open comes down to one correct statement. Which is it?

answers.text: A guide takes a group into Tolomato Cemetery only during its authorised open times, following the stewards rules and treating the burial ground with quiet respect.
A guide takes a group into Tolomato Cemetery whenever the route passes, whether it is open or not.
A guide takes a group into Tolomato Cemetery at night without permission for a more dramatic atmosphere.
A guide takes a group into Tolomato Cemetery and lets guests sit on tombstones while listening to stories.

questions.explanation: Tolomato holds centuries of burials, including Native, African and European residents, under the care of dedicated stewards. Entering only when open, staying on paths and speaking softly honour both the dead and the volunteers who protect them.

questions.question: When a situation involving adams-onis treaty signed eighteen nineteen needs resolving while preparing tour commentary, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The Adams-Onis Treaty was signed by Britain and Spain to divide Florida between them.
The Adams-Onis Treaty gave Texas to the United States and kept Florida Spanish forever.
The Adams-Onis Treaty, signed in eighteen nineteen, sold Florida to France for a second time.
The Adams-Onis Treaty, signed in eighteen nineteen, agreed that Spain would cede Florida to the United States and settled the boundary between Spanish territory and Louisiana.

questions.explanation: Secretary of State John Quincy Adams and Spanish minister Luis de Onis negotiated for years amid raids, filibusters, and border disputes. Florida was the centerpiece, but the treaty also drew a continental line all the way to the Pacific Ocean.

questions.question: Sofia is asked to justify a statement involving fort mose community departs for cuba. Which statement provides the correct basis?

answers.text: When Britain took Florida, the people of Fort Mose moved to Fort Matanzas island.
When Britain took Florida, the people of Fort Mose stayed and joined the British garrison.
When Britain took Florida in seventeen sixty-three, the free people of Fort Mose sailed away with the Spanish to Cuba rather than risk enslavement under British rule.
When Britain took Florida, the people of Fort Mose returned to Carolina as free landowners.

questions.explanation: The Mose families had built their freedom under Spanish law and Spanish protection. Rather than trust a slaveholding empire, they chose exile and began again near Matanzas in Cuba.

questions.question: While helping a trainee understand the material, Tom explains burning of the town in the seventeen oh two siege. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The burning of the town in seventeen oh two was caused by a cooking fire in the governor kitchen on a calm day.
In seventeen oh two the town escaped all damage and Moore left behind gifts of food, tools, and building stone.
As Spanish relief ships arrived, Moore forces withdrew in seventeen oh two after setting fire to much of Saint Augustine, including its church and many homes.
As relief ships arrived, Moore forces rebuilt Saint Augustine in brick at their own expense before leaving.

questions.explanation: Burning denied the returning Spanish shelter, stores, and a working town around their fort. Rebuilding from ashes became a recurring burden in the final Spanish decades.

questions.question: Tom is asked to justify a statement involving correcting a guest misconception politely. Which statement provides the correct basis?

answers.text: When a guest states a misconception, a good guide stops the tour and demands the guest leave the group.
When a guest states a misconception, a good guide mocks the guest so the group learns to stay silent.
When a guest states a misconception, a good guide agrees with it to keep the tour pleasant at any cost.
When a guest states a misconception, a good guide corrects it politely, thanks the guest for raising it and offers the documented version without embarrassment.

questions.explanation: Correction works best as shared curiosity, for instance by noting what records show and why the myth is so persistent. The guest keeps dignity, the group keeps trust and the accurate version is more likely to be remembered.

questions.question: In St. Augustine guiding, charlotte street historic character often shapes what a visitor takes away. Which statement about it is correct?

answers.text: Charlotte Street is a modern interstate bypass west of the city.
Charlotte Street runs through the historic district past inns and old homes, parallel to the bayfront a block away.
Charlotte Street is the service road inside the lighthouse grounds.
Charlotte Street is a boardwalk built on pilings over the ocean.

questions.explanation: The street took shape in the Spanish town plan and kept its intimate scale. Walking it shows how homes, commerce, and the harbor stayed closely woven together.

questions.question: Alicia is working while leading a walking tour and must apply the knowledge on fresnel lens of the lighthouse. Which statement gives the correct guidance?

answers.text: The lighthouse beam came from a bonfire lit on the tower roof nightly.
A first order Fresnel lens, made of hundreds of prisms, focused the lighthouse beam so it could be seen far out at sea.
Mirrors made of polished coquina focused the lighthouse beam seaward.
A plain magnifying glass from a drugstore focused the lighthouse beam.

questions.explanation: The French designed Fresnel lens wrapped the lamp in rings of precision glass. Its rotating flash gave St. Augustine a signature that ships learned to trust.

questions.question: Grace is handling a matter involving aviles street among the oldest streets while answering a guest question. Which statement should guide the work?

answers.text: Aviles Street was paved in the nineteen sixties as a brand new suburb road.
Aviles Street was built on a bridge above the Matanzas River.
Aviles Street is counted among the oldest streets in the city, lined with galleries, old houses, and the early hospital museum.
Aviles Street is a railway line that never held any houses.

questions.explanation: Spanish maps show a street on this line from the earliest centuries of the town. Its narrow scale and art galleries make it a favorite quiet walk for visitors.

questions.question: Before finalizing the tour commentary, Priya tests the treatment of coquina material properties for building. Which statement shows the right grasp?

answers.text: Coquina melts in rain and dissolves in sea air, so builders avoided it for any building near the coast.
Coquina is soft when first cut and hardens on exposure to air, and its spongy shell texture could absorb cannon fire rather than shattering like hard stone.
Coquina is a metal alloy smelted from iron ore that Spanish smiths poured into molds for fort walls.
Coquina shatters more easily than glass, which is why cannonballs passed through it without slowing.

questions.explanation: Quarrymen could shape the fresh stone with saws and axes before it hardened in place. In siege, its give under impact proved an unexpected advantage for the fortress walls.

icc-m3.quiz_title: ICC Mechanical Plans Examiner Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Regarding decorative appliance showing, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Decorative appliances may be shown without identifying their fuel type in the submittal.
A decorative gas appliance needs no venting information because it is not a heating appliance.
A vented decorative appliance and an unvented one require identical showings, so the arrangement never needs to be identified.

A decorative fuel-fired appliance shown on the submitted documents must be identified as decorative, with its location, fuel supply, and venting or direct-vent arrangement indicated, for the plans examiner to review.

questions.explanation: Decorative appliances burn real fuel and produce real combustion products. Identifying the appliance and its venting arrangement in the documents lets the examiner verify the design matches the type proposed. This is the governing rule for decorative appliance showing.

questions.question: While reviewing commercial gas piping plans, a deficiency involving allowable pressure drop stated must be corrected. Which requirement must the corrected documents satisfy?

answers.text: Any pressure drop is acceptable if the pipe sizes look generous.
Pressure drop allowance never needs to be stated in a submittal.
The drop may be stated only as a final measured value after installation.
The sizing documentation must state the pressure drop the designer allowed across the piping system so the examiner can see the margin built into the sizes chosen.

questions.explanation: Pressure drop is the budget the sizing spends along each run, and without the stated budget the examiner cannot tell whether the smallest sizes still deliver enough pressure. Correction is complete only when the corrected documents satisfy the rule for allowable pressure drop stated.

questions.question: Regarding duct not reduced in run, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The duct may reduce in size near the appliance to fit available space if the wall opening is oversized.
A fire damper or shutoff device that can fully close is an acceptable standard note for a combustion air duct.

The drawings must show the combustion air duct maintaining at least the required cross-sectional area throughout its run, with no reductions, dampers, or obstructions noted that would shrink the air path.
A volume damper may be installed and throttled in a combustion air duct to balance it with other systems.

questions.explanation: Anything that can close or narrow the path can starve the burners while the drawings still claim full area. The examiner flags dampers and reductions in the run and requires an unobstructed path of full size as documented. This is the governing rule for duct not reduced in run.

questions.question: Regarding return air path documented, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The plans examiner must approve a system even when the return path is blocked by a rated wall with no opening shown.
Return air may be assumed to find its own way, so no return path ever needs to appear on any drawing.
Plenum return is documented by deleting the ceiling plan and noting only the supply duct sizes.
The submitted drawings document the return air path from occupied spaces back to the air handler, including return grilles, transfer openings, or return ducts where relied upon.
