The statement that holds here is that configuration records are stored with the job documentation rather than only in installer memory.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes why a stand-alone system needs energy storage?

answers.text: A stand-alone system needs storage mainly to export energy to the utility grid.
Storage in a stand-alone system exists only to raise array voltage.
Storage lets a stand-alone array produce power after dark without any prior charging.
Without storage, a stand-alone system can power loads only while the array is producing.

questions.explanation: Sunlight is intermittent while loads occur around the clock, so stored energy bridges the gaps between production and use. The statement that holds here is that without storage, a stand-alone system can power loads only while the array is producing.

questions.question: For an installer explaining series connection behavior for current to a new colleague, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: A break anywhere in a series path stops current flow through the entire path.
A series circuit splits current into separate branches at each component.
Opening a series path in the middle leaves the rest of the path with current flowing normally.
Adding resistance in series reduces total resistance of the path.

questions.explanation: Charge follows a shared path without branches, so the flow rate must match at every point along that path. The statement that holds here is that a break anywhere in a series path stops current flow through the entire path.

questions.question: Thinking about how a central inverter serves a large array, which of these statements holds true?

answers.text: A central inverter eliminates the need for combiner equipment in every large array.
A central inverter converts power without receiving any direct current input.
A central inverter can serve only a tiny rooftop array and fails on larger systems.
Central inverters are typically used where array capacity is large, such as utility-scale plants.

questions.explanation: Large arrays benefit from consolidating conversion, because many strings can feed shared heavy-duty equipment at a common point. The statement that holds here is that central inverters are typically used where array capacity is large, such as utility-scale plants.

questions.question: A new candidate wants to understand net metering explained by concept. Which explanation should they be given?

answers.text: Net metering eliminates all fixed charges and fees on the bill.
A customer with net metering never draws energy from the grid at night.
Net metering lets exported solar energy offset energy the customer later draws from the grid.
Net metering means the utility pays the customer cash for every unit ever produced.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: Crediting exports against later imports turns the grid into a balancing mechanism, which is why the policy terms matter so much to value. The statement that holds here is that net metering lets exported solar energy offset energy the customer later draws from the grid.

questions.question: Decide which statement is sound. Which statement about why final approval matters before operation is correct?

answers.text: Final approval is a ceremony with no practical effect.
A system should operate for years before anyone seeks final approval.
Final approval signals that the authority found the installation acceptable under applicable requirements.
Final approval transfers ownership of the array to the city.

questions.explanation: Final approval is the checkpoint where review, construction, and inspection converge, so other parties rely on it as proof the process completed. The statement that holds here is that final approval signals that the authority found the installation acceptable under applicable requirements.

questions.question: In the area of keeping conduit runs neat and securely supported, which of the following is accurate?

answers.text: Loose fittings will seat themselves once the conduit warms in the sun.
Support spacing is purely aesthetic and can be skipped on long runs.
Extra sharp bends are harmless because wire pulling force does not increase.
Neat conduit routing avoids unnecessary bends that make pulling conductors difficult.

questions.explanation: Conduit is both a protective raceway and a pulling path, so support and gentle routing preserve its alignment, keep joints intact, and let conductors be installed without damage. The statement that holds here is that neat conduit routing avoids unnecessary bends that make pulling conductors difficult.

questions.question: Focus on the principle tested here. Which statement about the role of overcurrent protection is correct?

answers.text: Overcurrent protection increases current to help loads start faster.
A breaker that trips frequently should be replaced with a much larger rating to stop trips.
Overcurrent protection interrupts a circuit when current exceeds a safe level for the conductors.
Overcurrent protection is designed to protect the load from receiving too little current.

questions.explanation: Limiting current duration prevents conductor insulation from overheating, so protection acts as a guard between fault energy and fire risk. The statement that holds here is that overcurrent protection interrupts a circuit when current exceeds a safe level for the conductors.

questions.question: On the subject of understanding rate schedule influence on usage value, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Solar energy that displaces expensive grid energy is worth more than energy that displaces cheap grid energy.
The rate schedule shown on the bill is unrelated to how savings are calculated.
A customer on any plan saves the same amount from the same system.
Rate schedules never change and never affect a solar proposal.

questions.explanation: Savings come from avoided purchases, and the price of what is avoided is set by the rate schedule rather than by the panels. The statement that holds here is that solar energy that displaces expensive grid energy is worth more than energy that displaces cheap grid energy.

questions.question: During a study group, the topic of irradiance and electrical output comes up. Which statement by the experienced installer is accurate?

answers.text: Irradiance stays constant from dawn to dusk on a clear day.
Irradiance describes the power of sunlight arriving on a surface.
Cloud cover has no effect on irradiance reaching a module.
Irradiance describes the temperature of a module surface.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: More arriving light energy frees more charge carriers, so electrical output tracks the strength of sunlight reaching the cells. The statement that holds here is that irradiance describes the power of sunlight arriving on a surface.

questions.question: In a briefing on matching system size to available budget without overselling, which statement by the instructor is correct?

answers.text: A smaller system sold honestly will always cover the entire electric bill.
A responsible proposal can be scaled to fit the budget the customer states.
Financing pressure is an acceptable substitute for a system the customer can afford.
The largest possible system is always the right recommendation regardless of budget.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: A system the customer can actually buy and keep delivers real value, while an unaffordable design delivers nothing at all. The statement that holds here is that a responsible proposal can be scaled to fit the budget the customer states.

questions.question: While preparing for the test, a candidate reviews mounting choices for pitched shingle roofs. Which statement reflects the correct position?

answers.text: Rafters are avoided because decking alone is stronger.
Pitched shingle roofs commonly use flashed attachments fastened into rafters or structural members.
Flashing is unnecessary on shingle roofs because shingles seal bolt holes automatically.
Shingle roof attachments should be screwed only into the shingles themselves.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: A lag fastener gains strength from the wood fibers of a rafter, while decking alone is too thin to resist pull out under uplift. The statement that holds here is that pitched shingle roofs commonly use flashed attachments fastened into rafters or structural members.

questions.question: This item checks applied understanding. Which statement about comparing expected and actual output by concept is correct?

answers.text: Expected output is a guaranteed promise the system must meet hourly.
Comparing a winter week to a summer week fairly judges system health.
Expected output is estimated from irradiance, temperature, orientation, and system size.
Actual output above expectation on a cool bright day indicates a fault.

questions.explanation: A model of expected production turns raw data into a meaningful gap, and that gap is what distinguishes weather driven variation from equipment or site problems. The statement that holds here is that expected output is estimated from irradiance, temperature, orientation, and system size.

questions.question: For an installer explaining function of a dc disconnect in a photovoltaic system to a new colleague, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Opening a dc disconnect interrupts direct current flow from the array toward downstream equipment.
A dc disconnect stores energy that the array produces at noon.
A dc disconnect tracks energy production for the system owner.
A dc disconnect boosts array voltage during cloudy weather.

questions.explanation: Service and emergency work require a clear way to separate energized array wiring from equipment being handled. The statement that holds here is that opening a dc disconnect interrupts direct current flow from the array toward downstream equipment.

questions.question: Think about what the candidate must know. Which of the following statements about why a stand-alone system needs energy storage is NOT correct?

answers.text: Without storage, a stand-alone system can power loads only while the array is producing.
A stand-alone system needs storage mainly to export energy to the utility grid.
A stand-alone system needs storage because solar production and load demand rarely align in time.
Batteries in a stand-alone system supply loads at night and during cloudy weather.

questions.explanation: Sunlight is intermittent while loads occur around the clock, so stored energy bridges the gaps between production and use. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that a stand-alone system needs storage mainly to export energy to the utility grid.

questions.question: This item rewards careful reading. Which of the following statements about ground mount as an alternative to roof mount is NOT correct?

answers.text: Ground mounting requires available land and protection from damage at ground level.
A ground mounted array can be placed where sunlight is best when the roof is shaded or unsuitable.
Ground mounts allow easier access for cleaning and service than roof mounts.
Ground mounts need no foundation or support structure at all.

questions.explanation: Moving the array off the building trades roof constraints for land and foundation considerations, which suits some properties far better. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that ground mounts need no foundation or support structure at all.

questions.question: Test each statement for accuracy. Which of the following statements about glove selection for electrical and mechanical work is NOT correct?

answers.text: Gloves that are punctured, cracked, or contaminated are removed from service.
Gloves are selected according to the task, balancing protection against cuts, abrasion, and electrical hazards.
Any work glove protects equally against electrical shock and sharp metal.
Electrical work requires gloves rated for the voltage exposure and inspected before use.

questions.explanation: Different hazards demand different materials and ratings, so matching gloves to the task protects hands without creating new risks. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that any work glove protects equally against electrical shock and sharp metal.

ib-history.quiz_title: IB History Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: When it comes to the impact of conquest on conquered cities and populations, which statement holds up?

answers.text: Cities that surrendered early often fared better, retaining local elites, property, and religious life under new rulers in return for tribute and loyalty, so the experience of conquest varied sharply from place to place.
Conquered populations experienced no change in taxation, garrisoning, or government, because invaders collected no tribute and left administration entirely in the hands of defeated rulers.
Deportation of skilled workers never occurred under the Mongols, who left all artisans in their home cities and made no use of captive expertise anywhere else in the empire.
Every conquered city was completely destroyed regardless of whether it resisted or surrendered, and no city ever retained local elites, worship, or property after Alexander or Mongol conquest.

questions.explanation: Impact depended heavily on whether a city resisted or submitted. Resisting cities risked massacre, enslavement, and deportation, while surrender could preserve local life under tribute. Recovery varied, with the worst-hit regions suffering economic and demographic damage for generations. The statement that holds here is that cities that surrendered early often fared better, retaining local elites, property, and religious life under new rulers in return for tribute and loyalty, so the experience of conquest varied sharply from place to place.

questions.question: Thinking about the treatment of minorities in Nazi Germany, which of these statements holds true?

answers.text: Roma, homosexual men and Jehovah's Witnesses faced no persecution in Nazi Germany and retained all civil rights throughout the period.
Persecution ended with the Nuremberg Laws, after which Jewish life in Germany returned to normal until emigration became compulsory in 1945.
The euthanasia programme was a voluntary medical scheme with family consent required and verified in every documented case.

Kristallnacht, organized after the assassination of a German diplomat in Paris, destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses across Germany and sent around thirty thousand Jewish men to concentration camps.

questions.explanation: The treatment of minorities shows persecution as a process driven by ideology, bureaucracy and wartime radicalization. Stages of exclusion taught perpetrators and bystanders to accept escalating violence, culminating in the Holocaust, in which six million Jews were murdered, alongside millions of other victims. The statement that holds here is that kristallnacht, organized after the assassination of a German diplomat in Paris, destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses across Germany and sent around thirty thousand Jewish men to concentration camps.

questions.question: On the subject of the causes of the United States Civil War in overview, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Both North and South agreed before 1861 that slavery should expand into all new territories, and fought instead over control of western gold mines.
Lincoln was elected in 1860 promising immediate emancipation in all states, and northern voters gave him a majority in every southern state.

Economic and social differences between an industrializing North and a slave-based agricultural South deepened disagreements over tariffs, internal improvements and the power of the federal government relative to the states.
Southern states seceded because the federal government had already abolished slavery nationwide by an executive order issued in 1859.

questions.explanation: Historians emphasize slavery, and especially its expansion westward, as the central cause of sectional crisis. Compromises failed during the 1850s, the Democratic Party split, and Lincoln's election triggered secession in the Deep South. Confederate state declarations explicitly cited protection of slavery among their principal reasons for leaving. The statement that holds here is that economic and social differences between an industrializing North and a slave-based agricultural South deepened disagreements over tariffs, internal improvements and the power of the federal government relative to the states.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the command term Discuss in history essay questions?

answers.text: Discussion implies balance without neutrality: different views are examined fairly, but the essay still moves toward a conclusion about which view the evidence best supports.
Discuss requires the candidate to describe everything known about a topic in chronological order, with no need to consider alternative interpretations.
A discuss essay should present only the candidate own opinion from the start and ignore other viewpoints, because considering them shows uncertainty.
The command term discuss is satisfied by a conversation style introduction that mentions debate, even if the rest of the essay is pure narrative.

questions.explanation: Discuss is an invitation to weigh interpretations. The essay surveys relevant viewpoints, tests each against evidence, and ends with a judgement. Fair treatment of alternatives strengthens rather than weakens the conclusion that the discussion finally reaches. The statement that holds here is that discussion implies balance without neutrality: different views are examined fairly, but the essay still moves toward a conclusion about which view the evidence best supports.

questions.question: Which description of economic crisis as a condition for authoritarian emergence is the soundest?

answers.text: Economic crisis always produces authoritarian government, and every country hit by the Depression abandoned democracy during the 1930s without exception.
Germany's economy was booming in 1932 with near full employment, which explains why voters turned to extremist parties out of satisfaction.
Authoritarian movements generally promised to deepen free trade and cut state intervention, and voters supported them mainly as defenders of laissez-faire economics.

Economic crisis helped authoritarian movements by radicalizing voters, bankrupting businesses, straining welfare systems and making promises of jobs, protection and national economic revival more appealing.

questions.explanation: Economic crisis was a powerful catalyst but not a sufficient cause: Britain, France and the United States endured the Depression without dictatorship. Crisis mattered through its political effects, destroying confidence in governments and making anti-system movements plausible to voters and elites alike. The statement that holds here is that economic crisis helped authoritarian movements by radicalizing voters, bankrupting businesses, straining welfare systems and making promises of jobs, protection and national economic revival more appealing.

questions.question: For a teacher explaining the Munich Agreement and the Sudetenland crisis of 1938 to a class, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: British prime minister Neville Chamberlain defended Munich as securing peace for our time, believing Hitler's demands were limited to ethnic German areas and that concessions could satisfy Germany and avoid a war Britain was unprepared to fight.
Chamberlain returned from Munich expecting immediate war and told Parliament that the agreement had failed completely, urging instant general mobilization against Germany that same evening.
Germany honoured Munich by making no further territorial demands in Europe, and the occupation of Prague in March 1939 was carried out by Soviet rather than German forces.
The Munich Agreement transferred no territory to Germany and instead required Hitler to withdraw all claims to the Sudetenland permanently in exchange for British trade concessions alone.

questions.explanation: Munich in September 1938 gave Hitler the Sudetenland while excluding Czechoslovakia from the talks. Chamberlain presented it as peace, but Germany's seizure of the remaining Czech lands in March 1939 discredited appeasement and shifted British and French policy. The statement that holds here is that british prime minister Neville Chamberlain defended Munich as securing peace for our time, believing Hitler's demands were limited to ethnic German areas and that concessions could satisfy Germany and avoid a war Britain was unprepared to fight.

questions.question: One option fits the principle best. Which statement about the Night of the Long Knives in 1934 is correct?

answers.text: The Night of the Long Knives was an SA coup attempt that briefly seized Berlin before the army restored Hitler to power after a week of fighting.
Roehm survived the purge and remained SA chief until 1939, when he retired with honours after a public reconciliation with Hitler.
On 30 June 1934 Hitler ordered the SS and police to murder Ernst Roehm and other SA leaders, claiming they planned a coup, thereby destroying the SA as a potential rival power centre.
The purge targeted only communist deputies, and no Nazi or conservative figures were killed during the events of June and July 1934.

questions.explanation: The purge showed Hitler ruling by murder with legal impunity, since a law retroactively declared the killings lawful. It secured the army's loyalty, satisfied conservatives who feared SA radicalism, and demonstrated that no institution, including the party itself, stood above the leader. The statement that holds here is that on 30 June 1934 Hitler ordered the SS and police to murder Ernst Roehm and other SA leaders, claiming they planned a coup, thereby destroying the SA as a potential rival power centre.

questions.question: Regarding proxy wars as a characteristic practice of the Cold War, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: The superpowers provided no weapons or funding to any local conflict after 1945, keeping all regional wars entirely separate from Cold War rivalry.
Proxy wars were fought mainly in western Europe, where American and Soviet clients battled repeatedly while Asia and Africa remained untouched by the rivalry.
Local actors in proxy wars had no independent aims of their own and acted only as passive instruments carrying out detailed superpower instructions.
Korea, Vietnam and Afghanistan all functioned partly as proxy conflicts, as did wars in Angola and the Horn of Africa where superpower backing prolonged and internationalized local struggles.

questions.explanation: Proxy warfare let the superpowers compete without risking direct nuclear confrontation. The costs were displaced onto Korea, Vietnam, Afghanistan and other arenas, where local conflicts became longer and deadlier because external patrons sustained both sides. The statement that holds here is that korea, Vietnam and Afghanistan all functioned partly as proxy conflicts, as did wars in Angola and the Horn of Africa where superpower backing prolonged and internationalized local struggles.

questions.question: The stem below tests one idea. Which statement about the creation of modern Turkey and Ataturk's reforms is correct?

answers.text: Ataturk preserved the caliphate and Islamic law as the basis of the Turkish state, rejecting secular reforms throughout his presidency of the republic.
The Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 restored the Ottoman sultan as ruler of Turkey and returned all territories demanded under the Treaty of Sevres to foreign control.

Mustafa Kemal, later Ataturk, led Turkish national resistance after the First World War, defeated the Sevres settlement, and secured recognition of a Turkish state within roughly its modern borders by the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923.
Turkey adopted the Arabic script for the first time in 1928 as part of Ataturk's campaign to strengthen traditional religious education in state schools.

questions.explanation: Modern Turkey emerged from national resistance to postwar partition, not simply from Ottoman collapse. Ataturk used one-party authority to carry out rapid secular, legal, educational and cultural change. Historians debate the reforms' depth in rural society, but their institutional legacy shaped the Turkish republic for generations. The statement that holds here is that mustafa Kemal, later Ataturk, led Turkish national resistance after the First World War, defeated the Sevres settlement, and secured recognition of a Turkish state within roughly its modern borders by the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923.

questions.question: On the subject of the first section of the investigation: identification and evaluation of two sources, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The two sources chosen for detailed evaluation should be the two longest sources in the bibliography, regardless of their relevance to the question.
Origin, purpose, and content are irrelevant in this section, which is concerned only with whether the author of each source was famous.
Evaluation in this section examines each source in terms of its origin, purpose, and content, and draws out both the value and the limitations that follow for this investigation.
Evaluation in this section means deciding whether each source is completely reliable or completely unreliable, with no middle position allowed.

questions.explanation: The first section selects two relevant sources and evaluates each by origin, purpose, and content, noting value and limitations for the specific question. Contrasting sources work well because their differences sharpen the enquiry and prepare the analysis that follows. The statement that holds here is that evaluation in this section examines each source in terms of its origin, purpose, and content, and draws out both the value and the limitations that follow for this investigation.

questions.question: At a study session on the German invasion of Poland and the outbreak of war in 1939, which statement on the slides is correct?

answers.text: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939 using fast-moving combined arms tactics often called Blitzkrieg, while the staged Gleiwitz incident was used by Nazi propaganda to present Germany as the victim of Polish aggression.
The Soviet Union defended Poland against Germany in September 1939 by declaring war on Berlin and fighting alongside Polish forces to preserve Polish independence in the east.
German forces avoided combined arms tactics in Poland and advanced slowly on foot over six months, allowing Poland's allies ample time to organize an effective relief expedition.
Poland invaded Germany on 1 September 1939 after the genuine Polish attack at Gleiwitz, and Britain and France declared war on Poland in fulfilment of their guarantees to Berlin.

questions.explanation: In class, precision matters: Germany's invasion on 1 September 1939, justified by staged border incidents, destroyed Poland with Soviet help from 17 September. Britain and France declared war on 3 September but could not save Poland. The European war had begun, soon to become global. The statement that holds here is that germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939 using fast-moving combined arms tactics often called Blitzkrieg, while the staged Gleiwitz incident was used by Nazi propaganda to present Germany as the victim of Polish aggression.

questions.question: Picture the exam task behind this item. Which statement about limited war as a practice in the nuclear age is correct?

answers.text: Limited war means wars fought with unlimited objectives and weapons, including unrestricted nuclear strikes, whenever a state believes it can win quickly.
Nuclear weapons made limited war impossible, so every conflict after 1945 involving a nuclear power immediately escalated into general nuclear war without exception.
The Korean War was unlimited in scope, with the United States invading China and the Soviet Union openly declaring war on the United States in 1951.

Limited war involves deliberate restraint in objectives, weapons or geography to avoid escalation, a practice shaped after 1945 by the existence of nuclear weapons and fear of superpower confrontation.

questions.explanation: Nuclear weapons encouraged states to limit wars rather than risk annihilation. Korea exemplifies the pattern: fierce fighting combined with geographic and political restraint, negotiated settlement and acceptance of stalemate instead of pursuit of unconditional victory at any cost. The statement that holds here is that limited war involves deliberate restraint in objectives, weapons or geography to avoid escalation, a practice shaped after 1945 by the existence of nuclear weapons and fear of superpower confrontation.

questions.question: This is a foundational item. Which of the following statements about the value of a primary source for a historian is NOT correct?

answers.text: A primary source is valuable because it is always completely accurate and unbiased, since people living through events cannot misunderstand, exaggerate, or misrepresent what they experienced directly.

Value is always relative to the question asked: a source valuable for studying public attitudes may be weak evidence for battlefield facts, so historians state value in relation to a particular inquiry.

A primary source can be valuable because it comes from the period studied, offering direct evidence of contemporary language, beliefs, experiences, and what its creator wanted others to think or do at the time.

Primary sources can reveal detail unavailable elsewhere, such as a participant's description of conditions, decisions, or atmosphere, and their specific wording may itself be evidence, for example in propaganda or official statements.

questions.explanation: Primary sources offer closeness to events, contemporary language, and evidence of beliefs and intentions. Their value depends on the question: a poster strongly evidences a regime's message but weakly evidences public reaction. Evaluation must tie each strength to the inquiry. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that a primary source is valuable because it is always completely accurate and unbiased, since people living through events cannot misunderstand, exaggerate, or misrepresent what they experienced directly.

questions.question: While preparing for the exam, a candidate reviews the Korean War: causes and the stalemate outcome. Which statement reflects the correct position?

answers.text: China remained neutral throughout the war and sent no troops across the Yalu River, despite UN forces reaching the Chinese border in late 1950.
The Soviet Union led the UN intervention in Korea by contributing the largest contingent of combat troops under a Soviet commanding general.
North Korea invaded the south in 1950 with no support or approval from any communist power and using only weapons captured from Japanese stores in 1945.
Korea was divided at the 38th parallel after 1945 into a Soviet-backed north and a United States-backed south, and in June 1950 North Korea invaded the south seeking reunification by force.

questions.explanation: In class, precision matters: The Korean War began as an attempt at forced reunification within a divided Cold War state. Superpower and Chinese intervention internationalized it, but neither side could achieve full victory, so the 1953 armistice preserved division near the original boundary. The statement that holds here is that korea was divided at the 38th parallel after 1945 into a Soviet-backed north and a United States-backed south, and in June 1950 North Korea invaded the south seeking reunification by force.

questions.question: Stay with the published framework. Which of the following statements about conditions in Imperial Russia before 1917 is NOT correct?

answers.text: Defeats and strain in the First World War exposed military, transport and food supply failures, causing inflation, shortages in cities and loss of confidence in the tsarist government by early 1917.

Imperial Russia remained an autocracy under Tsar Nicholas II, with limited reform after 1905; the Duma had little power, political parties were restricted, and censorship and the secret police constrained opposition to the regime.
Russia before 1917 was a constitutional democracy in which the Duma controlled the government and the tsar reigned only as a ceremonial figurehead.

Rapid industrialization created a concentrated urban working class living and working in poor conditions, while most peasants remained poor, short of land and resentful of landlords and redemption burdens in the countryside.

questions.explanation: Pre-revolutionary Russia combined autocracy, land hunger, harsh industrial conditions and ethnic diversity under strain. The 1905 revolution forced limited concessions that satisfied few. War after 1914 magnified every weakness: military failure, inflation and food shortages destroyed the regime's remaining authority and set the stage for 1917. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that russia before 1917 was a constitutional democracy in which the Duma controlled the government and the tsar reigned only as a ceremonial figurehead.

questions.question: The facts below are the whole basis. Which statement about perspective and empathy in the IB approach to historical study is correct?

answers.text: Historical empathy means agreeing with and approving of everything people in the past did, however harmful their actions may have been.
Perspective is a defect that good historians eliminate entirely, after which their accounts contain no viewpoint or selection of any kind.
Perspective in historical study means recognizing that accounts of the past are shaped by the position, values, and context of those who produced the sources and interpretations being used.
Understanding past perspectives requires imagining feelings freely without evidence, since beliefs and circumstances of the period cannot be recovered.

questions.explanation: Perspective and empathy are disciplined habits. Students recognize how position shapes sources and interpretations, reconstruct past viewpoints from evidence rather than present assumptions, and compare perspectives to reach better supported judgements, not automatic approval or relativism. The statement that holds here is that perspective in historical study means recognizing that accounts of the past are shaped by the position, values, and context of those who produced the sources and interpretations being used.

questions.question: A tutor is covering indoctrination through culture, art and architecture in authoritarian states in a study session. Which statement from the session is accurate?

answers.text: Authoritarian regimes policed culture through chambers, exhibitions and patronage, promoting art that celebrated the nation, the leader and approved values while stigmatizing modernist work as degenerate or decadent.
Fascist Italy banned references to ancient Rome in public building, regarding imperial imagery as incompatible with its forward-looking programme.
Authoritarian regimes treated culture as unimportant and left artists, filmmakers and architects entirely free of registration or supervision.
Nazi cultural policy protected modernist art with state funding and prosecuted traditional artists whose work the regime considered subversive.

questions.explanation: In class, precision matters: Culture was a serious instrument of rule: it defined national identity, rewarded conformity with careers and commissions, and made ideology visible in everyday surroundings. Yet private tastes persisted, jazz and foreign fashions survived underground, showing again the gap between ambition and control. The statement that holds here is that authoritarian regimes policed culture through chambers, exhibitions and patronage, promoting art that celebrated the nation, the leader and approved values while stigmatizing modernist work as degenerate or decadent.

questions.question: Think about what the candidate must know. Which of the following statements about the weakness of the Weimar Republic and the rise of Hitler is NOT correct?

answers.text: Adolf Hitler rebuilt the Nazi Party after 1925 as a legal mass movement with strong propaganda and paramilitary organization, waiting for economic and political crisis to make its message attractive to voters.
The Weimar Republic collapsed mainly because its constitution gave the chancellor unlimited personal powers, which Hitler simply inherited when he entered office.

The Weimar Republic faced lasting burdens including defeat in war, reparations, hyperinflation in 1923 and political violence, while many judges, officials and army officers remained hostile to democratic government.

Proportional representation and fragmented parties made stable coalition government difficult, and frequent use of presidential emergency decrees under Article 48 weakened parliamentary habits, especially after 1930.

questions.explanation: Weimar's weakness was structural and cultural: economic shocks, institutional flaws and hostile elites eroded democratic legitimacy. Hitler exploited these weaknesses, but historians stress that the republic survived crises in the 1920s and that its final collapse also depended on decisions taken after 1929. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that the Weimar Republic collapsed mainly because its constitution gave the chancellor unlimited personal powers, which Hitler simply inherited when he entered office.

questions.question: Apply the standard approach here. Which of the following statements about the FLN and Algeria's struggle for independence from France is NOT correct?

answers.text: The war ended through the Evian Accords of 1962 followed by a referendum, after the conflict had destabilized France and settler and army resistance produced the OAS terrorist campaign.
The FLN achieved independence through purely parliamentary methods within the French National Assembly, never resorting to armed action at any stage.
The FLN, founded in 1954, combined guerrilla warfare in the countryside with urban attacks and diplomacy, building a provisional government to press Algeria's claim to independence internationally.
France responded with large-scale counterinsurgency involving hundreds of thousands of troops, resettlement of Algerian villagers and systematic use of torture, notably during the Battle of Algiers.

questions.explanation: Algeria's independence required both armed struggle and international diplomacy against a state that considered Algeria part of France. The FLN prevailed politically despite military containment, and the war's brutality left deep scars in both countries. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that the FLN achieved independence through purely parliamentary methods within the French National Assembly, never resorting to armed action at any stage.

questions.question: One option fits the principle best. Which of the following statements about the impact of conquest on conquered cities and populations is NOT correct?

answers.text: Longer-term effects included new garrisons, settlers, tax demands, and rebuilt urban centres, alongside disruption to trade and agriculture that in badly devastated regions such as parts of Khwarezmia took generations to repair.

Conquest in the Mongol and Macedonian periods never harmed urban populations, because both empires had strict laws forbidding any killing, enslavement, or deportation of civilians under all circumstances.

Conquest could bring massacre, enslavement, and deportation to cities that resisted, as at Tyre after its fall and in several Khwarezmian cities, where populations were killed or dispersed and skilled workers were taken away.

Cities that surrendered early often fared better, retaining local elites, property, and religious life under new rulers in return for tribute and loyalty, so the experience of conquest varied sharply from place to place.

questions.explanation: Impact depended heavily on whether a city resisted or submitted. Resisting cities risked massacre, enslavement, and deportation, while surrender could preserve local life under tribute. Recovery varied, with the worst-hit regions suffering economic and demographic damage for generations. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that conquest in the Mongol and Macedonian periods never harmed urban populations, because both empires had strict laws forbidding any killing, enslavement, or deportation of civilians under all circumstances.

microsoft-azure-solutions-architect-expe.quiz_title: Microsoft Azure Solutions Architect Expert Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Retail, outlet, and online divisions each need subscriptions, but group-wide security baselines must apply to every one of them. Which governance structure fits?

answers.text: A management group hierarchy above the subscriptions, with baseline Azure Policy assigned at the higher management group
Unrelated subscriptions with baselines emailed to each division
One resource group containing every division's workloads
Tagging alone, with no policy enforcement anywhere

questions.explanation: Management groups let policy and RBAC inherit across subscriptions, which is how a baseline reaches every division. Tags describe resources but enforce nothing.

questions.question: Dozens of small merchant databases each spike briefly at different times, and buying peak capacity for every database wastes money. Which design pools their capacity?

answers.text: Provision each database at its individual peak all day
Move merchant data into one shared table with no isolation
Use a single Basic database for all merchants
Use an Azure SQL elastic pool so the merchant databases share provisioned capacity

questions.explanation: Elastic pools exploit the fact that peaks do not coincide, sharing capacity across many databases. Per-database peak provisioning pays for idle headroom in every database.

questions.question: Research sensor readings arrive as JSON with varying fields per experiment and need global low-latency reads for collaborating campuses. Which storage design fits?

answers.text: Azure SQL with a fixed schema requiring alterations per experiment
Azure Cosmos DB with an API and partition design matched to the query patterns, using multi-region reads for collaborators
Blob Storage files listed and parsed by every reader
Azure Files shares mounted by each campus

questions.explanation: Cosmos DB handles schema-varying JSON with partitioned scale and multi-region distribution suited to the collaboration pattern. A rigid relational schema would need constant alteration as experiments change fields.

questions.question: Leadership dashboards must refresh in minutes from warehouse data during enrolment week, not overnight. Which design decision enables that freshness?

answers.text: Full reload of all history before every dashboard refresh
Dashboards querying raw lake files directly with no curated layer
An analysis design with incremental loading into Synapse dedicated or serverless structures and a semantic layer tuned for dashboard queries
Static PDF reports generated each morning

questions.explanation: Incremental loads and curated structures keep dashboard data current without reprocessing years of history per refresh. Full reloads make minute-level freshness computationally impossible at this volume.

questions.question: Tokenisation webhooks arrive unpredictably, run for under a second each, and must integrate privately with the payment virtual network. Which Functions design fits?

answers.text: Use the Consumption plan while requiring virtual network integration it cannot provide as specified
Run a dedicated VM polling for webhooks every minute
Process webhooks in a nightly batch job
Host the functions on an Azure Functions Premium plan with virtual network integration for private, burst-capable execution

questions.explanation: The Premium plan combines elastic burst scaling with virtual network integration for private dependencies. Polling or nightly batching breaks the event-driven timing webhooks require.

questions.question: A legacy warehouse application expects an SMB file share it can mount with drive-letter semantics, and rewriting it is out of scope this year. Which Azure storage service fits unmodified?

answers.text: Blob Storage with a gateway the team must build themselves
Azure Table Storage holding file contents as entities
Azure Files, providing fully managed SMB shares the application can mount
Cosmos DB storing files as document attachments

questions.explanation: Azure Files is the managed service that presents genuine SMB shares to unmodified legacy applications. A self-built blob gateway is the strongest alternative, because it replaces a managed service with bespoke machinery.

questions.question: Regulators require that no payment storage account in any current or future subscription accepts public blob access. Which governance mechanism enforces that continuously?

answers.text: A guidance document asking teams not to enable public access
An Azure Policy deny assignment at the management group scope for public network access on storage accounts
A one-time script that fixes existing accounts today
A tag named compliant applied to approved accounts

questions.explanation: A deny policy at management group scope blocks the configuration in every subscription, including future ones. Guidance and one-time scripts do not stop the next misconfiguration.

questions.question: Decoupling appointment booking from downstream notifications so booking succeeds even if the notification system is down is the design goal. Which pattern achieves it?

answers.text: Call the notification API synchronously inside the booking transaction
Store notifications in the booking database and send them during checkout
Require the notification system to be upgraded before booking launches
Publish the booking to a Service Bus queue or topic, letting notification consumers process it independently when they are available

questions.explanation: Asynchronous messaging isolates the booking path from downstream availability, which is the decoupling requested. Synchronous calls chain the two systems' uptime together.

questions.question: A consumer of plant downtime messages is offline each weekend, and messages must not expire before Monday processing. Which Service Bus design property should be configured?

answers.text: Send messages only when the consumer is confirmed online by phone
Use volatile in-memory queues that clear nightly
Reduce message importance so loss is acceptable by definition
Set appropriate message time-to-live and rely on durable queue storage so weekend messages persist until the consumer returns

questions.explanation: Durable queues with suitable TTL are the designed answer to intermittently offline consumers. Volatile queues guarantee the weekend loss the requirement forbids.

questions.question: Routing platform logs from a multi-site clinic network to both real-time analysis and a seven-year archive is required by the compliance team. Which routing design meets both needs?

answers.text: Send logs only to the workspace and delete them when workspace retention expires
Print quarterly log summaries and store the paper copies as the archive
Configure diagnostic settings on each resource to send logs to the Log Analytics workspace and to an archive storage account for long-term retention
Route logs to a single administrator's mailbox for manual filing

questions.explanation: Diagnostic settings support multiple destinations, so analysis and long-term archive are satisfied in one design. A workspace-only route loses records once its retention expires, failing the seven-year requirement.

questions.question: Thousands of small-business tenants self-onboard monthly, and building a separate directory for each would overwhelm the two-person platform team. Which identity management design scales?

answers.text: One Microsoft Entra ID tenant for the application, with each customer organisation represented and isolated inside the app's tenancy model and external identity sign-up flows
A separate Entra ID tenant per customer, administered by hand
One shared account that all small tenants sign in with
Spreadsheets tracking which tenant each user belongs to

questions.explanation: External identity sign-up within a single application tenant scales onboarding through automation while the app enforces tenant isolation. Hand-administered directories per customer collapse under the stated volume.

questions.question: Internal state services communicate over raw TCP and UDP with very high throughput and need load balancing without HTTP inspection. Which balancer matches that layer-4 profile?

answers.text: Use Azure Load Balancer for the high-throughput layer-4 distribution of the internal TCP and UDP traffic
Use Application Gateway and convert the protocols to HTTP
Use Front Door for internal non-HTTP traffic
Balance the traffic manually by assigning users to servers

questions.explanation: Azure Load Balancer operates at layer 4 for TCP and UDP at high throughput, matching the protocol profile. Layer-7 services require HTTP semantics the internal traffic does not have.

questions.question: Hybrid file and application servers in county offices have modest objectives: a day of data loss is tolerable and recovery within two days is acceptable, at the lowest cost. Which design is proportionate?

answers.text: Use Azure Backup for those servers rather than continuous Site Recovery replication
Replicate every county server continuously to two regions
Buy duplicate hardware for every county office
Provide no protection because the offices are small

questions.explanation: When RPO and RTO are loose, scheduled backup is the cost-proportionate protection. Continuous multi-region replication buys recovery speed the stated objectives do not require.

questions.question: Production file shares holding a streaming company's edit-project data need scheduled protection with restore of whole shares or single files after accidental changes, managed centrally rather than by share owners. Which design provides it?

answers.text: Azure Backup for Azure Files, protecting the shares with policy-driven snapshots and file-level restore
Manual share snapshots taken by each project lead before big edits
Blob versioning applied to the file shares
A robocopy mirror of the shares to a workstation under a producer's desk

questions.explanation: Azure Backup for Azure Files gives centrally managed, policy-based share protection with granular restore. Manual snapshots depend on memory, and a workstation mirror shares the office's risks rather than removing them.

questions.question: The spare-parts relational database must stay available for reads and writes if its region fails, with automatic failover and minimal data loss for dealers nationwide. Which data HA design fits?

answers.text: Schedule nightly exports to the secondary region as the failover plan
Accept regional loss as a multi-day outage for dealers
Use an auto-failover group for Azure SQL with a secondary region so failover is managed and the endpoint stays stable
Replicate by emailing transaction logs to the secondary plant hourly

questions.explanation: Auto-failover groups provide managed, near-continuous replication with automatic failover for exactly this requirement. Nightly exports leave a full day's transactions behind on failure.

questions.question: Cosmos DB data for a care-coordination app was corrupted by a bad deployment two hours ago; the design must support restoring the account to before the deployment. Which backup mode provides that?

answers.text: Continuous backup mode on the Cosmos DB account, enabling point-in-time restore to any moment within the retention window
Periodic backup with a minimum interval of several hours, accepted as sufficient
Manual exports of containers taken at each release, when remembered
Multi-region writes, treated as a substitute for backup

questions.explanation: Continuous backup captures changes as they happen, so a restore point two hours ago exists; periodic backup's coarsest interval may skip over it entirely. Replication propagates the corruption rather than undoing it.

questions.question: Restricted criminal-justice case systems in a state police records programme must be logged, yet their log data may not be queryable by general agency analysts. How should the logging architecture handle that boundary?

answers.text: Mix the restricted logs into the shared workspace and rely on analysts not to open them
Disable logging on the restricted systems so no sensitive records are created
Export the restricted logs to a public storage account for separation
Send those systems' diagnostic logs to a dedicated Log Analytics workspace whose access is limited to cleared personnel

questions.explanation: A dedicated workspace with restricted access preserves both the audit trail and the confidentiality boundary. Disabling logging destroys accountability, and mixing the data into a shared workspace relies on behaviour rather than access control.

questions.question: Every time an episode file lands in a streaming platform's origin storage, a thumbnail and preview set must be generated within moments, and the code runs for seconds per file with long quiet gaps overnight. Which compute design fits?

answers.text: A dedicated VM polling the storage account every minute around the clock
An Azure Function with a Blob trigger, running the generator only when new files arrive
An AKS deployment holding warm replicas for the nightly gaps
A Logic App that emails the file's location to the design team

questions.explanation: A Blob-triggered function is the canonical event-driven fit: it wakes on arrival, runs briefly, and costs nothing while idle. A polling VM pays all night to discover that nothing happened.

questions.question: Checkout-equivalent flows in the SaaS product — tenant admins inviting users — fail silently in the browser tier while server metrics look healthy. Which monitoring addition closes that gap?

answers.text: More frequent ping tests against the home page
Larger virtual machines for the web tier
Application Insights for the web application, capturing end-to-end transactions and browser-side failures tied to each tenant's session
A status page updated manually by support

questions.explanation: Application Insights traces the full transaction including client-side steps, which is where these invite failures occur. Ping tests only prove the home page loads, not that a tenant workflow completes.

questions.question: Overnight, thousands of tenant report renders must crunch through a compute-heavy queue with a hard morning deadline and no daytime use. Which batch design fits?

answers.text: A fixed fleet of rendering servers idling all day
Rendering reports on demand inside tenant page loads
One worker machine racing the deadline alone
Azure Batch pools that scale out for the rendering queue overnight and scale back when the queue drains

questions.explanation: Batch pools align parallel compute with queue depth and release it afterwards, meeting the deadline without a standing fleet. Page-load rendering would make tenants wait for their heaviest reports.

questions.question: What is accurate about canon and whose voices get studied?

answers.text: Questions about the canon ask only for the correct order in which famous works should be memorised.
Questions about the canon assume the set of valued works was formed with no influence from culture or power.
Questions about the canon ask which works have been valued and preserved over time, whose voices have been centred or excluded, and how those judgements can be reconsidered.
Questions about the canon mean older valued works should never be read or discussed again.

questions.explanation: The canon is a product of cultural judgement, not a natural fact. Examining it helps students think critically about value, tradition, and inclusion in their own reading. The correct statement is: Questions about the canon ask which works have been valued and preserved over time, whose voices have been centred or excluded, and how those judgements can be reconsidered.

questions.question: Concerning the bildungsroman, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A bildungsroman follows an elderly ruler's final day with no change at all.
A bildungsroman is a detective form centred only on solving a crime.
A bildungsroman is a travel guide written in the form of a novel.
A bildungsroman follows a young protagonist's growth toward maturity through experience, error, and self-discovery.

questions.explanation: Formation of the self is the central arc. Events matter chiefly for how they shape the developing character. The correct statement is: A bildungsroman follows a young protagonist's growth toward maturity through experience, error, and self-discovery.

questions.question: What is accurate about research skills as an approach to learning?

answers.text: Research skills mean collecting as many sources as possible, regardless of quality or relevance.
Research skills mean trusting the first search result, since ranking guarantees accuracy.
Research skills are only about finding facts, never about judging whether a source is credible.
Research skills involve framing questions, finding and evaluating sources, and using what is found ethically and purposefully in the student work.

questions.explanation: Good research is selective and critical; the value lies in what is chosen and how it is used, not in volume. The correct statement is: Research skills involve framing questions, finding and evaluating sources, and using what is found ethically and purposefully in the student work.

questions.question: Regarding the refrain, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A refrain is a line that appears only once and is never repeated anywhere.
A refrain is a line or phrase repeated at intervals through a poem, often at the end of stanzas, creating emphasis and unity.
A refrain is the name of the poet printed on a book cover.
A refrain means avoiding repetition so no phrase ever returns in a poem.

questions.explanation: Return creates familiarity and pressure, and small changes to a repeated line can signal a shift in feeling or understanding. The correct statement is: A refrain is a line or phrase repeated at intervals through a poem, often at the end of stanzas, creating emphasis and unity.

questions.question: Which statement about comparing techniques across works is correct?

answers.text: Comparing techniques across works means examining how similar or different methods, such as narration, imagery, or structure, function in each work and serve its meaning.
Comparing techniques across works means checking which work uses more techniques and awarding it the stronger discussion.
Comparing techniques across works means describing a technique in one work and assuming it works identically in the other.
Comparing techniques across works is worthwhile only when both works use exactly the same technique in the same way.

questions.explanation: The same method can produce different effects in different contexts, so function and effect must be compared, not just presence. The correct statement is: Comparing techniques across works means examining how similar or different methods, such as narration, imagery, or structure, function in each work and serve its meaning.

questions.question: In a study group for the language and literature course, a teacher asks about the multimodal text. Which statement is true?

answers.text: A multimodal text uses only written language and excludes every other mode of communication.
A multimodal text combines two or more modes, such as written language, image, sound, layout, and movement, that work together to create its overall meaning.
A multimodal text is a text that has been translated into many languages for a global audience.
A multimodal text combines modes that never interact, so each mode must be understood entirely alone.

questions.explanation: Much modern communication is deliberately multimodal. Analysis must consider how modes reinforce, extend, or complicate each other, not just the words. The correct statement is: A multimodal text combines two or more modes, such as written language, image, sound, layout, and movement, that work together to create its overall meaning.

questions.question: A student preparing a study plan studies props as symbols. Which statement reflects how it works?

answers.text: A prop becomes symbolic only when it is too heavy for an actor to lift.
A prop becomes symbolic when it is mentioned in the title of the programme.
A prop becomes symbolic when a handled object carries meaning beyond its practical use, such as power, memory, or guilt.
A prop becomes symbolic when it is removed from the stage before the play begins.

questions.explanation: Objects gain weight through repeated use and context. A simple item can concentrate a theme in visible form. The correct statement is: A prop becomes symbolic when a handled object carries meaning beyond its practical use, such as power, memory, or guilt.

questions.question: Regarding comparing techniques across works, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Comparing techniques across works means checking which work uses more techniques and awarding it the stronger discussion.
Comparing techniques across works means describing a technique in one work and assuming it works identically in the other.
Comparing techniques across works means examining how similar or different methods, such as narration, imagery, or structure, function in each work and serve its meaning.
Comparing techniques across works is worthwhile only when both works use exactly the same technique in the same way.

questions.explanation: The same method can produce different effects in different contexts, so function and effect must be compared, not just presence. The correct statement is: Comparing techniques across works means examining how similar or different methods, such as narration, imagery, or structure, function in each work and serve its meaning.

questions.question: Concerning sponsored content and disclosure, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Sponsored content is editorial material that a publication produces with no payment or brand involvement.
Sponsored content is material paid for by a brand but presented in the style of editorial content, and disclosure labels exist so audiences know it is paid promotion.
Sponsored content and disclosure mean brands must hide any payment so audiences treat promotion as independent reporting.
Sponsored content is content that a brand sponsors for a sports team with no published material involved.

questions.explanation: Blending promotion with editorial style can mislead readers about independence. Disclosure protects audience trust by making the commercial relationship visible. The correct statement is: Sponsored content is material paid for by a brand but presented in the style of editorial content, and disclosure labels exist so audiences know it is paid promotion.

questions.question: Regarding the rhetorical situation of a speech, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: The rhetorical situation refers only to the room size and the seating plan for a speech.
The rhetorical situation means a speech has no audience and no purpose beyond filling time.
The rhetorical situation links a speaker, an audience, a purpose, and a context that together shape the choices in a speech.
The rhetorical situation is the set of spelling rules a speaker follows when writing notes.

questions.explanation: Analysis starts by asking who speaks, who listens, why they speak, and what surrounds the moment, because those factors guide tone, evidence, and structure. The correct statement is: The rhetorical situation links a speaker, an audience, a purpose, and a context that together shape the choices in a speech.

questions.question: Before a practice assessment, a student studies visual elements in a Paper One text. Which statement reflects how it works?

answers.text: Visual elements in a Paper One text should be described in detail but never linked to meaning or purpose.
Visual elements in a Paper One text are decoration and should be ignored in favour of the written words alone.
Visual elements such as layout, image, colour, and typography should be analysed for how they direct attention and reinforce or complicate the verbal message.
Visual elements in a Paper One text matter only when there are no written words to analyse.

questions.explanation: Many Paper One texts communicate through image and design as well as language, so visual choices are part of how the text makes meaning. The correct statement is: Visual elements such as layout, image, colour, and typography should be analysed for how they direct attention and reinforce or complicate the verbal message.

questions.question: A student preparing a study plan studies the portfolio as evidence of growth. Which statement reflects how it works?

answers.text: The portfolio shows growth only when every early entry is deleted and replaced with later work.
Across the course, portfolio entries show growth as early tentative responses develop into more precise, confident, and independent analysis.
The portfolio shows growth when entries become longer, regardless of how the thinking develops.
The portfolio shows growth when the student writes only about texts they already understand fully.

questions.explanation: Keeping earlier work visible makes change traceable, which is what turns a folder of entries into a record of learning. The correct statement is: Across the course, portfolio entries show growth as early tentative responses develop into more precise, confident, and independent analysis.

questions.question: A student, a Diploma Programme student preparing for the English A assessments, is reviewing the rhetorical situation of a speech. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The rhetorical situation refers only to the room size and the seating plan for a speech.
The rhetorical situation links a speaker, an audience, a purpose, and a context that together shape the choices in a speech.
The rhetorical situation means a speech has no audience and no purpose beyond filling time.
The rhetorical situation is the set of spelling rules a speaker follows when writing notes.

questions.explanation: Analysis starts by asking who speaks, who listens, why they speak, and what surrounds the moment, because those factors guide tone, evidence, and structure. The correct statement is: The rhetorical situation links a speaker, an audience, a purpose, and a context that together shape the choices in a speech.

questions.question: In a study group for the language and literature course, a teacher asks about formal register in analytical writing. Which statement is true?

answers.text: Analytical writing sounds stronger when it uses casual slang to show a personal voice.
Analytical writing should use the most complex vocabulary available, even when the meaning becomes unclear.
Analytical writing should be written in the first person as a diary of how the writer felt while reading.
Analytical writing uses a formal, precise register with clear sentences and subject-specific vocabulary used accurately.

questions.explanation: A formal register keeps attention on the text and the argument, and precise vocabulary lets the writer make fine distinctions about effect. The correct statement is: Analytical writing uses a formal, precise register with clear sentences and subject-specific vocabulary used accurately.

questions.question: In a study group for the language and literature course, a teacher asks about culture as a course concept. Which statement is true?

answers.text: Culture as a course concept invites study only of food and festivals and excludes values and beliefs.
Culture as a course concept means only texts from unfamiliar countries count as cultural texts.
Culture as a course concept treats culture as a single viewpoint shared identically by everyone in a group.
Culture as a course concept invites study of how texts reflect, preserve, challenge, and pass on the values, practices, and beliefs of communities.

questions.explanation: Every text emerges from and speaks to cultural contexts. The concept helps students examine norms, traditions, and tensions within and between communities. The correct statement is: Culture as a course concept invites study of how texts reflect, preserve, challenge, and pass on the values, practices, and beliefs of communities.

questions.question: For an English A candidate, a future IB graduate reviewing textual analysis ideas, reviewing conventions of comedy matters. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Conventions of comedy require the action to end in irreversible ruin for all characters.
Conventions of comedy forbid mistaken identity and wordplay of any kind.
Conventions of comedy mean characters never face embarrassment or confusion.
Conventions of comedy include misunderstanding, disguise, and social confusion that are typically resolved in a reconciling or celebratory ending.

questions.explanation: Comic plots tangle relationships and expectations. Resolution usually untangles them and restores social harmony. The correct statement is: Conventions of comedy include misunderstanding, disguise, and social confusion that are typically resolved in a reconciling or celebratory ending.

questions.question: For an English A candidate, a future IB graduate reviewing textual analysis ideas, reviewing a visual body of work in the oral matters. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: When the body of work is visual, the student can only describe what is pictured, since images have no craft to analyse.
When the body of work is visual, a single advertisement automatically counts as a rich body of work on its own.
When the body of work is visual, the student can analyse composition, colour, framing, and imagery as authorial choices that explore the issue.
When the body of work is visual, the student should avoid mentioning the issue and discuss taste in art instead.

questions.explanation: Images are made texts too; their formal choices carry meaning that can be analysed just as language can. The correct statement is: When the body of work is visual, the student can analyse composition, colour, framing, and imagery as authorial choices that explore the issue.

questions.question: During a revision session, students including a student studying language and literature concepts before an assessment discuss speaker versus poet in a poem. Which statement is true?

answers.text: The speaker in a poem is the voice created within the text and should not automatically be treated as the poet themselves.
The speaker in a poem is always the poet speaking directly about their own life.
The speaker and the poet are identical in every poem ever written.
A poem has no speaker because poems contain no voice at all.

questions.explanation: Keeping voice and author separate allows for persona, irony, and invention, and prevents a reading from resting on biography alone. The correct statement is: The speaker in a poem is the voice created within the text and should not automatically be treated as the poet themselves.

questions.question: During a revision session, students including a student studying language and literature concepts before an assessment discuss what makes an issue a global issue. Which statement is true?

answers.text: An issue counts as global only when every country in the world is affected in exactly the same way.
An issue counts as global when it is mentioned briefly in a single local news report with no wider reach.
An issue counts as global when it has significance that reaches across cultures and places and can be explored meaningfully through texts from different contexts.
An issue counts as global whenever a student finds it interesting, even if it matters nowhere beyond their own life.

questions.explanation: A global issue needs significance beyond one setting plus clear textual evidence, not universal sameness or personal interest alone. The correct statement is: An issue counts as global when it has significance that reaches across cultures and places and can be explored meaningfully through texts from different contexts.

questions.question: While reviewing course material, a group including a Diploma Programme candidate reviewing how texts create meaning discusses the epistolary form. Which statement is true?

answers.text: The epistolary form tells a story through a single omniscient voice with no documents.
The epistolary form tells a story through documents such as letters, diary entries, or messages, giving the narrative an intimate and piecemeal quality.
The epistolary form is a novel written entirely as stage directions.
The epistolary form forbids any gaps or delays between pieces of writing.

questions.explanation: Documents create immediacy and limitation at once. Readers piece events together from partial, dated, personal records. The correct statement is: The epistolary form tells a story through documents such as letters, diary entries, or messages, giving the narrative an intimate and piecemeal quality.

series-30.quiz_title: Series 30 (Branch Manager Examination) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Jordan is working on a one-to-one review with a designated branch supervisor. new staff handles options orders It is the first week of a new product increment. Which statement about written procedures options on futures is the one to remember?

answers.text: The branch must follow written procedures covering options on futures, including order handling, exercise, assignment, and customer risk disclosure.
The branch must let each customer invent personal procedures for options exercise and assignment without any firm involvement at all.
The branch may ignore written procedures for options on futures whenever options volume at the branch happens to be light.
The branch must follow unwritten customs covering options on futures, changing approach whenever a confident salesperson prefers something different today.

questions.explanation: Options involve exercise and assignment mechanics that differ from outright futures, so written procedures ensure consistent disclosure, order handling, and expiration processing rather than improvised treatment that varies by employee.

questions.question: Ivy is working on a curriculum review with the course instructor. branch transmits order to carrier A retrospective is scheduled for later that afternoon. A colleague asks about forwarding customer orders through carrying firm. Which answer is correct?

answers.text: Customer orders from an introducing broker are forwarded to the carrying firm for execution and clearing rather than executed by the introducing broker.
An introducing broker executes orders on its own informal exchange among customers, matching buyers and sellers internally without carrying firm involvement.
Orders may be held at the branch until staff feel market timing is attractive, because discretion over timing supposedly improves every customer outcome.
Forwarding is optional for urgent orders, which associates should instead shout to neighboring offices in hopes someone can arrange execution informally.

questions.explanation: Forwarding orders to the carrying firm connects introduced customers to actual markets through the firm carrying their accounts, preserving execution, clearing, margin, and confirmation within the regulated account structure.

questions.question: Devon is working on a discussion at the compliance desk whiteboard. vague explanations lead to compliance escalation The front desk logged the training room for the afternoon. Which of the following is true of unusual transactions require careful follow up?

answers.text: Follow up is complete once the customer gives any explanation, however vague or contradictory it sounds.
Transactions with no apparent lawful or business purpose, or inconsistent with a customer's known profile, require careful follow up and possible escalation.
Unusual transactions should be processed faster so the firm does not inconvenience important customers.
Inconsistency with a customer profile is meaningless and should never prompt any follow up questions.

questions.explanation: Unexplained or inconsistent activity is a classic warning sign; thoughtful follow up either resolves the concern with credible information or strengthens the case for escalation.

questions.question: Luis is working on a coordination meeting with carrying firm staff. associate pauses to explain margin The practitioner is revising notes after a long study block. Which of the following is true of explaining risk disclosure in plain language?

answers.text: Handing over paperwork silently always suffices, because customers who fail to read dense documents bear complete responsibility for misunderstanding futures.
Risk should be described as modest and manageable regardless of the actual disclosure, so customers feel comfortable funding accounts quickly.
Associates should explain the risk disclosure in plain language and invite questions rather than merely handing over paperwork without discussion.
Plain language explanations are discouraged since technical jargon impresses customers and discourages them from asking probing questions about potential losses.

questions.explanation: Delivery alone may not create understanding, especially for inexperienced customers, so a plain explanation and a chance to ask questions make the disclosure meaningful rather than a purely formal step.

questions.question: Tara is working on a supervisory awareness session for new branch staff. customer asks what trader may decide A planning session is planned for the following morning. In a discussion of discretionary authority scope explained to customer, which claim holds up?

answers.text: Scope explanations are best given after trading begins, when concrete examples from the account make the arrangement easier for the customer to understand fully.
Scope explanations may omit what remains outside the grant, since customers naturally assume authority covers everything related to the account without further clarification needed.
Before granting authority, the customer should understand exactly what decisions the authorized person may make, what remains outside the grant, and what records the customer will receive.

Before granting authority, the customer needs only a general assurance that the authorized person is experienced, because detailed scope explanations tend to overwhelm ordinary customers unnecessarily.

questions.explanation: Understanding scope prevents the most common discretionary disputes, where customers claim they approved far less than the trader believed was granted. Explaining boundaries and reporting before trading begins aligns expectations on both sides of the relationship.
