An introducing firm makes no records because its carrying firm makes them all.

questions.explanation: Rule 17a-3 is the making rule — if it is not made, it cannot be kept. The statement that holds here is that making the required records is the first step in the recordkeeping framework the FINOP administers.

questions.question: In the area of assessing market, liquidity and credit risks in financial reporting, which of the following is accurate?

answers.text: Credit risk is assessed only for customers whose accounts the firm carries.
Liquidity risk matters because assets not readily convertible into cash affect the firm's financial strength.
Risk assessment is complete once any one of the three risks has been considered.
Liquidity risk disappears whenever an asset appears on the balance sheet.

questions.explanation: Market, liquidity, credit: unusual deals get all three lenses. The statement that holds here is that liquidity risk matters because assets not readily convertible into cash affect the firm's financial strength.

questions.question: A candidate asks a mentor about the units in which securities are delivered. Which reply is accurate?

answers.text: The FINRA Uniform Practice Code addresses the units of delivery for securities transactions.
The introducing firm physically breaks up certificates in its own vault to meet delivery units.
Delivery units matter only for the firm's own proprietary inventory.
Any quantity a seller chooses counts as a proper delivery unit.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: Proper units make a delivery good — wrong units make it rejectable. The statement that holds here is that the FINRA Uniform Practice Code addresses the units of delivery for securities transactions.

questions.question: With respect to standards of commercial honor and principles of trade under FINRA Rule 2010, which statement is correct?

answers.text: FINRA Rule 2010 is a rule about the format of customer confirmations.
A firm complies with FINRA Rule 2010 by advertising that it has high standards.
Conduct that falls short of just and equitable principles of trade can violate FINRA Rule 2010 even in areas covered by other rules.
Standards of commercial honor under FINRA Rule 2010 apply only to carrying firms.

questions.explanation: Rule 2010: just and equitable principles govern all member conduct. The statement that holds here is that conduct that falls short of just and equitable principles of trade can violate FINRA Rule 2010 even in areas covered by other rules.

questions.question: Weigh the four options carefully. Which statement about commodities adjustments in the haircut framework is correct?

answers.text: Commodities positions receive the standard equity haircut in every case.
Appendix B applies to customer accounts rather than firm positions.
A commodities position is deducted only when it shows a loss at year end.
Commodities positions receive adjustments in the haircut framework.

questions.explanation: Commodities follow Appendix B in the haircut framework. The statement that holds here is that commodities positions receive adjustments in the haircut framework.

questions.question: This item rewards careful reading. Which statement about hindsight deficiency notifications is correct?

answers.text: Hindsight deficiencies are among the regulatory notifications the FINOP may need to file.
A hindsight deficiency never requires notice because the period has passed.
Hindsight deficiencies are corrected by restating history with no filing.
Notice is required only for deficiencies the firm knew about in advance.

questions.explanation: Found later still counts — a past deficiency gets noticed. The statement that holds here is that hindsight deficiencies are among the regulatory notifications the FINOP may need to file.

questions.question: Concerning confirmations of transactions under SEA Rule 10b-10, which of these statements is sound?

answers.text: A confirmation replaces the need to keep any other record of a trade.
Customers of an introducing firm receive no confirmations because the firm is small.
SEA Rule 10b-10 lets the introducing firm confirm trades it never executed.
A confirmation gives the customer a written record of the transaction that was executed.

questions.explanation: Every trade gets confirmed — Rule 10b-10 makes the paper trail real. The statement that holds here is that a confirmation gives the customer a written record of the transaction that was executed.

questions.question: Under the heading of electing and applying the firm's chosen net capital method, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The firm's elected method is chosen by its customers at account opening.
An introducing firm never elects a method because the carrying firm elects for it.
A firm applies both methods and reports whichever result it prefers each month.
A firm computes its minimum under its elected method, either the basic method or the alternative method.

questions.explanation: Know the elected method and apply its test, not the easier one. The statement that holds here is that a firm computes its minimum under its elected method, either the basic method or the alternative method.

questions.question: Answer from the underlying concept. Which of the following statements about form custody for FOCUS filings is NOT correct?

answers.text: The principal oversees custody of reporting forms as part of compiling and filing FOCUS reports.
Form custody concerns keeping the proper forms and filed copies within the firm's records framework.
Filed FOCUS copies may be discarded once the filing is submitted.
Retaining filed FOCUS information supports the firm's ability to answer later regulatory inquiries.

questions.explanation: Keep the filed forms; a filing you cannot produce is a problem. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that filed FOCUS copies may be discarded once the filing is submitted.

questions.question: Judge each option against the concept. Which statement about preservation duties of an introducing firm that does not carry accounts is correct?

answers.text: An introducing firm preserves nothing because the carrying firm holds customer assets.
An introducing firm must preserve its own books and records even though it does not carry customer accounts.
Preservation duties attach only to firms that hold customer funds or securities.
The introducing firm may rely entirely on the carrying firm's filing cabinets for its own records.

questions.explanation: Fully disclosed is not record-free — the introducer preserves its own books. The statement that holds here is that an introducing firm must preserve its own books and records even though it does not carry customer accounts.

questions.question: A workshop speaker is covering discretionary liabilities as an adjustment to net worth. Which statement from the talk is accurate?

answers.text: Discretionary liabilities require an adjustment to net worth in the computation.
Only involuntary liabilities ever adjust net worth.
The FINOP may omit a discretionary liability until it comes due.
Discretionary liabilities are excluded because the firm chose to incur them.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: Chosen or not, a real liability reduces net worth. The statement that holds here is that discretionary liabilities require an adjustment to net worth in the computation.

questions.question: A trainee reads a summary of requests for extensions of time under Regulation T and asks a mentor to check it. Which statement in the summary is accurate?

answers.text: FINRA Rule 4230 addresses requests for extensions of time under Regulation T and SEA Rule 15c3-3.
An introducing firm may extend Regulation T deadlines on its own authority whenever a customer asks.
Requests for extensions of time eliminate the underlying margin obligation of the customer.
Extensions of time under Regulation T are granted automatically without any request or approval process.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: More time under Regulation T is requested, never just assumed. The statement that holds here is that fINRA Rule 4230 addresses requests for extensions of time under Regulation T and SEA Rule 15c3-3.

questions.question: During a back-office training talk, the topic of keeping preserved records accurate and complete during retention comes up. Which statement by the trainer is accurate?

answers.text: A firm may lend out its only copy of a preserved record indefinitely.
Records must remain accurate and complete throughout their preservation period.
Accuracy during retention is the customer's concern rather than the firm's.
Preserved records may be corrected silently at any time to match new facts.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: Preservation protects content, not just paper — accurate and complete throughout. The statement that holds here is that records must remain accurate and complete throughout their preservation period.

questions.question: This is a foundational item. Which of the following statements about internal control over financial responsibility rules is NOT correct?

answers.text: Internal control over financial responsibility rules is optional for introducing firms.
The principal's audit-related duties include understanding the firm's internal control structure.
The firm's internal control structure includes compliance over the financial responsibility rules.
Internal control supports accurate net capital computations and reliable financial reporting.

questions.explanation: Controls over the financial responsibility rules protect every filing. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that internal control over financial responsibility rules is optional for introducing firms.

questions.question: Weigh the four options carefully. Which of the following statements about the 2 percent of aggregate debit items standard under the alternative method is NOT correct?

answers.text: A firm on the alternative method compares its net capital with the amount produced by the 2 percent standard.
Under the alternative method, the minimum net capital standard is 2 percent of aggregate debit items arising from customer transactions.
The alternative-method standard is 20 percent of aggregate debit items.
The 2 percent figure is applied to aggregate debit items, not to aggregate indebtedness.

questions.explanation: Alternative standard: 2 percent of aggregate debit items from customers. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that the alternative-method standard is 20 percent of aggregate debit items.

questions.question: Ground your answer in the concept. Which of the following statements about expense management and liquidity preservation is NOT correct?

answers.text: The FINOP reviews whether expense arrangements are documented so that obligations of the firm are clear.
Managing expenses helps preserve the liquidity the firm needs to operate and to maintain capital.
Expense management means shifting firm expenses onto customer accounts at the carrying firm.
Affiliate transactions and expense-sharing agreements affect how much cash the firm must supply for its own costs.

questions.explanation: Clear, controlled expenses keep liquidity from leaking away. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that expense management means shifting firm expenses onto customer accounts at the carrying firm.

hspt.quiz_title: HSPT - High School Placement Test Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: "Dull" most nearly means:

answers.text: fullness
boring
sad
unassuming

questions.explanation: A dull lesson fails to hold attention, and boring means exactly that lack of interest or excitement in it.

questions.question: Of the fractions 1/5 and 1/2, which one is greater?
questions.explanation: Written as decimals, 1/5 is about 0.200 and 1/2 is about 0.500. Comparing the values shows 1/2 is greater.

questions.question: How is context clue by synonym correctly described?

answers.text: A stated detail is given directly in the text, while an inference is a conclusion the reader draws from it.
Paraphrasing restates an idea in completely new words while keeping the original meaning the same.
A synonym clue places a word with a similar meaning near the unfamiliar word to hint at its sense.
A cause effect text structure explains why things happen and what results follow from them.

questions.explanation: When two nearby words seem to say almost the same thing, the familiar one often unlocks the meaning of the harder one.

questions.question: What is the correct end punctuation for this sentence: Where is my book

answers.text: A question mark
A period
An exclamation point
A comma

questions.explanation: The sentence asks a question, so it ends with a question mark.

questions.question: What is covering the streets in this passage: Snow fell during the night, covering the quiet streets.

answers.text: Parked cars
Snow
Fallen leaves
Thick fog

questions.explanation: The passage says snow fell and covered the streets.

questions.question: "Despair" is most nearly the opposite of:

answers.text: attack
rough
hope
enormous

questions.explanation: Despair is the complete loss of expectation for good, while hope is the expectation that good may come, its opposite.

questions.question: What number comes next in the series? 67, 73, 79, 85, 91, ___
questions.explanation: Each term increases by 6: the differences between consecutive terms are all 6, so the next term is 91 + 6 = 97.

questions.question: Maria bakes bread on Saturdays for her family. Maria bakes bread on

answers.text: Wednesdays
Saturdays
Sundays
Fridays

questions.explanation: The passage states that Maria bakes bread on Saturdays.

questions.question: Using 3.14 for pi, what is the circumference of a circle with radius 10?
questions.explanation: Circumference is 2 x pi x radius: 2 x 3.14 x 10 = 62.8. Estimating the size of the answer first is a quick way to notice when a computed result cannot be right.

questions.question: Noah scored 75, 90, and 90 on three tests. What is the mean score?
questions.explanation: Add the scores: 75 + 90 + 90 = 255. Divide by 3: 255 / 3 = 85. Showing the steps in order makes it possible to catch an arithmetic slip before it becomes a wrong answer.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes capitalization marks sentence starts?

answers.text: A good title hints at the content and invites the reader to begin.
Paragraph unity means every sentence in a paragraph relates to the same main idea.
An apostrophe shows possession or marks letters left out of a contraction.
Capitalization marks the start of a sentence and sets proper nouns apart.

questions.explanation: These signals help readers parse text quickly, distinguishing names and fresh starts from the ordinary flow of words.

questions.question: Regarding the area of a figure, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The area of a figure is the number of square units needed to cover its surface.
A quadrilateral is a polygon with four sides and four angles that add to 360 degrees.
The radius of a circle is the distance from the center of the circle to any point on the circle.
A right angle measures exactly 90 degrees and forms a square corner.

questions.explanation: Area is measured in square units because it counts how many unit squares fit inside the figure. Showing the steps in order makes it possible to catch an arithmetic slip before it becomes a wrong answer.

questions.question: Which pair does NOT fit the relationship shown by 'hot : cold'?

answers.text: wet : dry
up : down
warm : hot
big : small

questions.explanation: Hot and cold are opposites, like the other pairs, but warm and hot are similar in meaning, not opposites.

questions.question: A number is multiplied by 5 and then increased by 3. If the starting number is 7, what is the result?
questions.explanation: Multiply first: 7 x 5 = 35. Then increase by 3: 35 + 3 = 38. These items reward careful reading: the relationship between the numbers matters more than the numbers themselves.

questions.question: Two numbers add to fifty-two, and the larger number is four more than twice the smaller number, so the two values can be found by careful reasoning with the given facts. The smaller number is
questions.explanation: If the smaller number is 16, the larger is 2 x 16 + 4 = 36, and 16 + 36 = 52.

questions.question: Then shows time or a next step in order - which statement is true?

answers.text: You're is a contraction of you are, as in: You're the first student to finish the puzzle that the teacher placed on the board today.
The title of a book, film, or other work takes a singular verb even if the title contains a plural word, because the title names one work.
Every pronoun should refer clearly to one specific antecedent, so readers never have to guess which noun the pronoun is meant to replace.
Then shows time or the next step in a sequence, as in: First we mixed the batter, and then we poured it into the warm pan.

questions.explanation: Then belongs to timelines and instructions, answering the question of when something happens, and it has nothing to do with comparing two things.

questions.question: A baker arranges muffins in rows on a wide tray, placing six muffins in each row and filling seven full rows before the tray is taken to the display case. The number of muffins on the tray is
questions.explanation: Six muffins in each of seven rows gives 6 x 7 = 42 muffins.

questions.question: A teacher sorts a set of word cards into groups on the board and places apple, banana, and grape together in one group, explaining to her student that every word in a group must share the same category and that a word from a different category, even a familiar one, does not belong no matter how often it appears in daily conversation around the classroom. Which word is the most appropriate choice to add to the group containing apple, banana, and grape?

answers.text: pencil
peach
carrot
chair

questions.explanation: Apple, banana, and grape are all fruits, so peach, another fruit, is the word that belongs in the group.

questions.question: A student encounters this sentence in a geography book: 'From the top of the tower, the travelers could see the vast desert stretching to the horizon in every direction, with no town, river, or patch of green anywhere in sight.' Her teacher suggests she weigh how the phrases about the horizon and the empty view in every direction shape the meaning of the size word that the author chose for the desert. Which meaning is the most appropriate for 'vast' as it is used in this sentence?

answers.text: Completely dry
Dangerously hot
Far from home
Very large

questions.explanation: A desert stretching to the horizon in every direction is vast, meaning very large.

questions.question: A student is proofreading a paragraph about a school trip and pauses at the sentence: 'The bus could not accomodate every student who signed up, so a second bus was ordered for the remaining riders.' Her teacher reminds the class that this frequently misspelled word contains two sets of double letters, and that checking each syllable against that pattern is the surest way to catch the error before the paragraph is published. Which spelling is the most appropriate correction for the underlined word in the student's sentence?

answers.text: accomodate
acommodate
accommodate
accommadate

questions.explanation: Accommodate is spelled with double c and double m: accommodate.

cdr-cso-oncology-nutrition.quiz_title: CDR CSO - Certified Specialist in Oncology Nutrition Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: For tumor biology and uncontrolled growth, which statement holds true?

answers.text: A tumor is a mass formed by abnormal and uncontrolled cell growth.
Cancer cells are unable to travel through blood or lymph to distant sites.
A tumor is a mass formed only by healthy cells growing in a controlled pattern.
Cancer cells never invade nearby tissue beyond where they started.

questions.explanation: Tumor biology centers on uncontrolled growth, local invasion, and the ability of cancer cells to spread, all of which distinguish cancer from benign growth.

questions.question: Among these statements on monitoring nutrition outcomes, one is incorrect. Identify it.

answers.text: Outcome monitoring includes tracking weight trends, intake, and functional status over time.
When a plan is not working, the correct response is to continue it unchanged indefinitely.
Reassessment compares current status against the goals set in the nutrition care plan.
Persistent decline despite intervention should trigger escalation and plan revision.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Monitoring weight, intake, symptoms, and function against stated goals shows whether interventions are working and signals when the plan needs escalation or revision.

questions.question: For weight management for prevention, which statement fails to hold up?

answers.text: Excess body fatness influences hormone and inflammation pathways that are relevant to cancer development.
Maintaining a healthy body weight across adulthood is associated with lower risk for several cancers.
Weight counseling should rely on shame to motivate lasting behavior change.
Weight management counseling should focus on sustainable habits rather than rapid restrictive dieting.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Healthy weight maintenance is a prevention priority because excess body fatness affects metabolic and hormonal pathways, and respectful habit based counseling supports lasting change without stigma.

questions.question: Concerning edema and fluid shifts, which assertion is inaccurate?

answers.text: Edema can mask loss of muscle and fat by keeping measured weight artificially elevated.
Fluid accumulation may result from treatment effects, low protein status, or disease related changes.
Documenting the presence and location of edema helps the team interpret weight and physical findings accurately.
Noting edema is unnecessary when interpreting weight change in a patient with cancer.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Retained fluid distorts weight and hides tissue loss, so recognizing edema and its possible causes protects the assessment from misleading conclusions about nutrition status.

questions.question: A candidate reviews reflux and heartburn relief. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Eating a large spicy meal right before bed is recommended for reflux relief.
Smaller meals and avoiding lying down soon after eating can reduce reflux symptoms.
Peppermint and chocolate are prescribed to tighten control of reflux symptoms.
Tight belts and lying flat after meals are encouraged to improve digestion.

questions.explanation: Explanation: Reflux worsens with large fatty meals and lying flat, so smaller meals, trigger awareness, and staying upright after eating help reduce heartburn during treatment.

questions.question: Grace Mbeki is reviewing briefing material on surgery role in cancer treatment. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Surgery may also be used to relieve symptoms caused by a tumor.
Surgery can remove a tumor and nearby tissue affected by cancer.
Surgery can never remove a tumor or any tissue affected by cancer.
Nutrition status before surgery matters for healing and recovery afterward.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Surgery can remove disease and ease symptoms, and sound nutrition before and after the procedure supports wound healing and overall recovery.

questions.question: During a team meeting on avoiding unproven restrictive diets, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: Highly restrictive diets can worsen weight loss and nutrient inadequacy during treatment.
Patients considering alternative diets should discuss risks and benefits with the care team.
Evidence based nutrition care prioritizes adequate energy and protein during treatment.
Eliminating major food groups always improves cancer treatment outcomes.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Restrictive regimens promoted without evidence can accelerate malnutrition in patients already at risk, so dietitians emphasize adequate nourishment and open discussion of alternatives.

questions.question: Which statement about food aversions and smell sensitivity would an experienced oncology dietitian endorse?

answers.text: Strong smelling foods should be served piping hot to intensify aroma for sensitive patients.
Trying new bland foods during treatment can avoid linking favorite foods with nausea.
Food aversions mean a patient is being difficult and counseling should be withheld.
Favorite foods should be eaten during nausea so they become associated with treatment.

questions.explanation: Explanation: Treatment can heighten smell sensitivity and create lasting aversions, so reducing food odors and protecting favorite foods from nausea episodes helps preserve enjoyment of eating.

questions.question: Kevin Doyle is reviewing briefing material on immunotherapy immune activation. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Immune related side effects can involve inflammation in organs such as the bowel.
Immunotherapy works by permanently shutting down the immune system response to cancer.
Immunotherapy helps the immune system recognize and attack cancer cells.
Immunotherapy works differently from chemotherapy that directly damages cells.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Immunotherapy engages the patient own immune defenses against cancer, and that immune activation can also inflame healthy organs including the bowel.

questions.question: What should an oncology dietitian understand about estimating energy needs principles? Which statement is correct?

answers.text: Metabolic stress from cancer and healing lowers energy needs below usual resting requirements.
Energy needs in cancer vary with tumor burden, inflammation, activity, and treatment related stress.
An initial energy estimate should never be adjusted even when weight trends show it is missing the mark.
Energy needs are identical for every patient with cancer regardless of illness burden or activity.

questions.explanation: Energy estimation in oncology is individualized and provisional, rising with metabolic stress and healing demands, then refined by monitoring weight, intake, and clinical response.

questions.question: An oncology care team is evaluating evaluating alternative nutrition therapies. Which statement accurately describes it?

answers.text: Natural products are always safe and never interact with cancer treatment.
Checking reliable evidence sources helps distinguish helpful supportive care from harmful claims.
Patients should hide supplement use from the oncology team to avoid criticism.
Testimonials alone prove that an alternative therapy cures cancer.

questions.explanation: Explanation: Alternative therapies vary widely in safety and evidence, so open disclosure and checking claims against reliable sources protect patients from harm and false promises.

questions.question: During a team meeting on bone health in survivorship, one statement is wrong. Which one?

answers.text: Adequate calcium and vitamin D from food and appropriate sources support skeletal health in survivors.
Survivors on hormone therapy should avoid calcium rich foods to protect their bones.
Certain cancer treatments and hormone therapies can weaken bones, making bone health part of survivorship care.
Weight bearing activity complements nutrition in maintaining bone strength after treatment.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Bone health deserves attention in survivorship because some therapies accelerate bone loss, and nutrition, activity, and monitoring together help preserve strength and reduce fracture risk over time.

questions.question: Anders Holm, who is planning a group class on eating well during cancer treatment, reviews laboratory testing interpretation. Which of these statements is accurate?

answers.text: A laboratory marker can diagnose malnutrition on its own without any clinical information.
An isolated laboratory result is always more informative than a trend over time.
Inflammation and hydration status can distort laboratory markers often linked with nutrition.
Inflammation and hydration have no effect on laboratory markers related to nutrition.

questions.explanation: Laboratory data support rather than replace clinical judgment in oncology nutrition, because inflammation, hydration, and illness shift many markers away from pure nutrition meaning.

questions.question: A stakeholder repeats something they read online about supplement and herb interaction risks. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: The oncology team and pharmacist can review supplements for safety during treatment.
Megadose nutrient supplements are not routinely recommended during treatment without review.
Taking many supplements together eliminates the risk of interactions.
Some antioxidant supplements and herbs can interfere with chemotherapy or radiation effects.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Explanation: Supplements and herbs can change how treatments work or add side effects, so reviewing every product with the oncology team and pharmacist is an important safety step.

questions.question: An oncology nutrition case review turns to immune suppression in cancer. Which statement should the dietitian stand behind?

answers.text: The oncology dietitian should disregard infection risk when advising about food handling.
Some cancers strengthen the immune system so infection risk always falls.
The oncology dietitian considers infection risk when advising a patient with cancer about food handling.
A weakened immune system makes food safety practices less important for patients.

questions.explanation: When cancer suppresses immunity, infection risk rises and careful food handling becomes a meaningful part of nutrition counseling and daily care.

questions.question: Michael Novak, who is planning a group class on eating well during cancer treatment, reviews fiber adjustments for bowel changes. Which of these statements is accurate?

answers.text: Fiber should be eliminated permanently for every patient with any bowel change.
The same high fiber plan is appropriate regardless of bowel symptoms.
Fluid intake has no relationship to tolerance of a higher fiber eating pattern.
Soluble fiber foods can be helpful for some patients with loose stools.

questions.explanation: Bowel effects vary widely during treatment, so fiber type and amount are tailored to the dominant symptom and adjusted gradually with attention to fluid and tolerance.

questions.question: While reviewing a tube feeding tolerance note with the care team, Julia Santos double-checks notes on managing appetite loss in palliative care. Which statement should be corrected?

answers.text: Appetite stimulants are considered selectively in palliative care and are not helpful for every patient.
Declining appetite is a common and expected part of advanced illness and the dying process.
Explaining expected appetite changes can ease family worry that a loved family member is being starved.
Appetite loss in advanced illness always signals a reversible nutrition problem that must be fixed.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Understanding that appetite loss is expected in advanced illness helps clinicians respond with comfort measures and compassionate explanation rather than pressure, supporting both patient and family.

questions.question: Chris Delacroix, who is reviewing a patient's diet history before an oncology clinic visit, reviews fat loss and weight change interpretation. Which of these statements is accurate?

answers.text: Fat stores cannot be examined as part of a nutrition focused physical assessment.
Loss of subcutaneous fat can be assessed by examining areas such as the orbital region and upper arm.
A weight trend should be interpreted without considering fluid retention or reduced intake.
Intentional and unintentional weight loss carry the same clinical meaning in a patient with cancer.

questions.explanation: Unintentional loss and visible fat depletion point toward depleted reserves, yet interpretation stays sound only when intake, symptoms, inflammation, and fluid status are considered together.

questions.question: Marta Kowalski, an oncology dietitian, is reviewing food safety practices with an immunosuppressed patient. Regarding cultural humility in palliative nutrition care, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Language barriers are best handled by guessing at family preferences about feeding.
Cultural humility means treating every family the same regardless of their traditions.
Clinicians should correct families whose food customs differ from standard guidance.
Respecting cultural food practices can coexist with comfort focused goals in palliative care.

questions.explanation: Culturally humble palliative care honors diverse food traditions and beliefs, uses qualified language support, and invites families to share what food means to them during a deeply personal time.

questions.question: While preparing a nutrition counseling session for a patient starting cancer treatment, Julia Santos double-checks notes on appetite stimulant role. Which statement should be corrected?

answers.text: Appetite stimulants work alongside, not instead of, nutrition counseling and monitoring.
Medication choices for appetite weigh benefits against side effects and patient goals.
Appetite stimulants guarantee restoration of lean body mass in every patient.
Appetite stimulants may be considered when poor appetite contributes to weight loss.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Appetite stimulants can help selected patients eat more, but they carry side effects and do not replace counseling, symptom management, and monitoring of weight and intake.

ae-c-certified-asthma-educator.quiz_title: AE-C Certified Asthma Educator Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: For asthma mucus hypersecretion effect, which statement fails to hold up?

answers.text: Goblet cell changes in asthma produce thinner mucus that is always effortless for the patient to clear.
Goblet cell changes in asthma contribute to thicker mucus that is harder for the patient to clear.
Mucus hypersecretion in asthma can plug narrowed airways and worsen airflow limitation for the patient.
Excess mucus production in asthmatic airways often increases during exacerbations and contributes to cough.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Excess and thickened mucus narrows already inflamed asthmatic airways, adding to obstruction and cough during flare periods.

questions.question: Regarding cleaning and replacing spacers, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Spacers for asthma inhalers should be cleaned gently as directed and allowed to air dry without toweling the inside.
Spacers for asthma inhalers should be scrubbed harshly and dried by rubbing the inside with a rough towel.
Regular inspection of a valved holding chamber is unnecessary because valve damage never affects asthma inhaler delivery.
A cracked or cloudy spacer that no longer seals well should be kept indefinitely because damage improves asthma delivery.

questions.explanation: Gentle cleaning, air drying, inspection, and timely replacement keep a spacer sealing and functioning well so inhaled delivery is not compromised.

questions.question: Which statement about confidentiality and documentation standards is accurate?

answers.text: Learner health information shared during asthma education must be kept confidential and shared only as permitted and necessary for care.
Documentation of asthma education can be completed from memory long afterward with invented details added as needed.
Details a learner shares in asthma education may be discussed freely with neighbors and coworkers for interest.
Writing judgmental opinions about a learner character is preferred over objective notes in an asthma education record.

questions.explanation: Confidential handling and accurate objective documentation protect learner privacy, support the care team, and provide a reliable record of asthma education delivered.

questions.question: On the subject of allergy testing referral concept, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Confirmed allergic triggers should be kept out of education sessions because avoidance teaching never uses that information.
Allergy testing is required for every person with asthma even when the history shows no allergic pattern at all.
When history suggests allergic triggers, the educator can encourage discussion with the clinician about possible allergy testing.
Allergy testing is a casual curiosity with no connection to avoidance teaching or to follow up discussion with the clinician.

questions.explanation: Allergy testing is a referral consideration when the history suggests allergic triggers, and confirmed sensitivities help the educator tailor avoidance teaching within the clinician directed plan.

questions.question: Among these statements on collaborative goal setting, one is incorrect. Identify it.

answers.text: Effective goal setting with the patient produces goals that are specific and described in clear everyday words.
Goals should be set far beyond what the patient believes is achievable to force faster behavior change.
Goals should feel achievable to the patient so early success can build confidence in asthma self-management.
The educator and patient choose goals together and review progress on those goals at later visits.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Specific, achievable goals chosen with the patient turn broad intentions into steps the patient can attempt, review, and adjust with educator support over time.

questions.question: Kevin Doyle is reviewing briefing material on asthma air pollution trigger effect. Which claim in the material is wrong?

answers.text: Air pollution can irritate asthmatic airways and provoke symptoms on high pollution days.
A patient with asthma may benefit from checking air quality guidance before outdoor exertion.
Particulate matter and ozone in polluted air may worsen asthma control for exposed patients.
Air pollution soothes asthmatic airways and prevents symptoms on high pollution days.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Pollutants such as ozone and particles inflame and irritate asthmatic airways, linking poor air quality to symptom worsening.

questions.question: A stakeholder repeats something they read online about combination inhaler concept. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: Patients using a combination inhaler for asthma still need a separate quick-relief plan as directed by the prescribing clinician.
Using a combination inhaler as prescribed allows a patient with asthma to discard the written action plan entirely.
Using a combination inhaler as prescribed can simplify an asthma regimen by pairing controller components in a shared device.
A combination inhaler delivers a corticosteroid and a long-acting bronchodilator together in the same device for asthma control.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Combination inhalers join anti-inflammatory and long-acting bronchodilator therapy in the same device, simplifying the regimen while a separate reliever plan remains necessary.

questions.question: An asthma program team is evaluating demonstration and return demonstration. Which statement accurately describes it?

answers.text: Return demonstration is unnecessary because patients can correct their own inhaler technique without observation.
During return demonstration, the educator should stay silent even when the patient skips a critical step.
Demonstration paired with return demonstration helps confirm that device skills are performed correctly, not just described correctly.
Watching a device demonstration once guarantees the patient can perform the technique correctly at home.

questions.explanation: Seeing a skill and then performing it under observation are different learning steps, and return demonstration exposes technique errors that verbal recall can miss.

questions.question: In a study group on asthma air pollution trigger effect, one assertion is false. Which one?

answers.text: Air pollution can irritate asthmatic airways and provoke symptoms on high pollution days.
Particulate matter and ozone in polluted air always improve asthma control for exposed patients.
A patient with asthma may benefit from checking air quality guidance before outdoor exertion.
Particulate matter and ozone in polluted air may worsen asthma control for exposed patients.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Pollutants such as ozone and particles inflame and irritate asthmatic airways, linking poor air quality to symptom worsening.

questions.question: An asthma program team is evaluating fears and misconceptions about medicines. Which statement accurately describes it?

answers.text: Fears about inhaled steroids should be suppressed because voicing them makes a learner less likely to follow the plan.
Another misconception is that needing a rescue inhaler often is a normal sign that asthma management is working well.
Frequent rescue inhaler need is the clearest sign that asthma management is excellent and needs no further review.
Daily controller medicines are meant to be stopped as soon as symptoms ease, since quiet days prove they are unnecessary.

questions.explanation: Surfacing steroid fears, dependence myths, and misunderstandings about controller and rescue medicines lets the educator correct misconceptions gently and share persistent concerns with the clinician.

questions.question: During an asthma education team training session on green zone daily control, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The educator helps the patient link green zone days with steady habits such as trigger avoidance and correct inhaler technique.
The green zone means asthma has resolved and daily controller medicines can be stopped without clinician direction.
A patient in the green zone should skip daily medicines and save them for worsening symptoms.
The green zone describes severe breathing difficulty that requires emergency care right away.

questions.explanation: The green zone signals usual control, so teaching emphasizes continuing daily clinician-directed therapy and the habits that help maintain that control.

questions.question: In a study group on evaluating asthma program outcomes, one assertion is false. Which one?

answers.text: Program evaluation for asthma education can examine changes in knowledge, inhaler skills, asthma control, and health care utilization.
Emergency visits and hospital use are never relevant when evaluating outcomes of an asthma education program.
Learner satisfaction alone is not a complete measure of whether an asthma education program improved self management.
Collecting outcome information before and after an asthma education program helps show whether the program made a difference.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Meaningful evaluation looks beyond attendance to knowledge, demonstrated skills, asthma control, and utilization, giving a fuller picture of whether education changed outcomes.

questions.question: While observing a patient demonstrate inhaler technique at a clinic visit, Ingrid Bauer considers family roles in childhood asthma. Which statement holds true?

answers.text: Only one parent should ever be assessed for a child asthma plan, even when several caregivers give medicines daily.
Shared management means responsibilities shift gradually toward the child as age, maturity, and skills allow.
Care arrangements in a second household are irrelevant and should never be asked about during family assessment.
Young children should be given full independent responsibility for medicines as soon as they can name their inhaler.

questions.explanation: Mapping which caregivers do what, how responsibility can shift toward the maturing child, and how care works across households prevents gaps that undermine a child asthma management plan.

questions.question: A stakeholder repeats something they read online about travel planning and reliever access. Which repeated claim is inaccurate?

answers.text: The action plan should be left at home during travel because unfamiliar places rarely trigger asthma symptoms.
Travel planning for asthma includes packing medicines and devices in carry-on baggage so they stay accessible during the trip.
Family members traveling with the patient should know where the reliever and the action plan are kept during the trip.
The patient should travel with the action plan and reliever medicine within easy reach rather than stored out of reach.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Accessible medicines, devices, and the written plan during travel protect the patient when triggers, delays, and unfamiliar settings make asthma harder to manage.

questions.question: David Osei, who is preparing plain-language asthma handouts for a family session, reviews asthma airway remodeling changes. Which of these statements is accurate?

answers.text: Airway remodeling in asthma refers to temporary mucus clearing that restores the airway wall to normal within hours.
Remodeling in a patient with asthma can include thickening of airway walls and increased smooth muscle.
Persistent uncontrolled asthma inflammation prevents remodeling and guarantees airflow limitation stays fully reversible.
Remodeling in a patient with asthma always thins airway walls and reduces smooth muscle to improve breathing.

questions.explanation: Remodeling reflects structural change from chronic inflammation, underscoring why sustained asthma control matters for lung health.

questions.question: While reviewing peak-flow diary entries with a patient, Laura Chen double-checks notes on biologic therapies for severe asthma. Which statement should be corrected?

answers.text: Biologic therapy is considered by specialists for severe asthma that remains uncontrolled despite optimized controller treatment.
Patients receiving biologic therapy for asthma continue prescribed controller medicines unless the specialist directs otherwise.
Biologic therapies for severe asthma target specific immune pathways involved in airway inflammation.
Biologic therapies for severe asthma are over-the-counter relievers used during a sudden attack at home.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Biologics are specialist-directed options for severe asthma with specific inflammatory patterns, and they supplement rather than replace prescribed controller therapy.

questions.question: Michael Novak, who is preparing a trigger-control checklist for a home visit discussion, reviews wood smoke and strong fragrances. Which of these statements is accurate?

answers.text: The stronger and more heavily scented a cleaning spray is, the safer it is for someone whose asthma reacts to fragrances.
Strong fragrances from scented sprays, candles, and cleaning products trigger symptoms in some people with asthma and may need to be reduced.
An asthma educator should dismiss reports that fragrances trigger symptoms because scented products never affect asthma.
Wood smoke is soothing for inflamed airways and should be inhaled deliberately by a person with asthma.

questions.explanation: Wood smoke and strong fragrances are common airway irritants, and reducing exposure when they provoke symptoms is a practical part of individualized asthma trigger control.

questions.question: Fatima Al-Sayed, a certified asthma educator, is following up with a patient after an urgent care visit for asthma and reads a summary of poor control versus severity distinction. Which claim in it is inaccurate?

answers.text: Asthma severity describes the underlying intensity of the condition and the level of treatment needed to achieve control.
Asthma that is severe can become well controlled, and asthma that is mild can be poorly controlled when treatment or adherence falters.
Poor control describes how much symptoms, waking, and activity limitation a person is currently experiencing.
Severity and control mean exactly the same thing, so the two words can be swapped freely in every assessment.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Severity reflects the underlying condition and treatment intensity required, while control reflects current symptom burden, and keeping the distinction clear prevents mistaken conclusions during assessment.

questions.question: Fatima Al-Sayed, a certified asthma educator, is reviewing peak-flow diary entries with a patient. Regarding occupational exposures and clinician discussion, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: An asthma educator can encourage a worker to describe job tasks and exposures in detail when reviewing asthma control with the clinician.
Workers with asthma should hide their condition and exposures from their clinician to avoid workplace discussion.
An asthma educator should independently decide that a workplace exposure caused asthma and order the employer to change the job.
Symptoms that appear only on workdays should never be mentioned to the clinician caring for a person with asthma.

questions.explanation: Occupational exposures can drive poor asthma control, and the educator supports care by prompting detailed reporting to the clinician rather than making workplace determinations independently.

questions.question: On the subject of matching device to patient ability, which statement is NOT correct?

answers.text: A patient with limited hand strength may need an asthma device or spacer arrangement that is easier to actuate and hold.
Device choice for asthma should be reassessed when a patient cannot demonstrate correct technique despite teaching and support.
Device choice for asthma should never be reassessed even when a patient repeatedly cannot use the device correctly.
Matching an asthma device to patient ability considers dexterity, inspiratory strength, and age when the clinician selects therapy.

questions.explanation: That statement is inaccurate. Device success depends on fit with patient abilities and developmental stage, so reassessment is needed whenever correct use cannot be achieved.

ts-c.quiz_title: TS-C — Tech in Surgery — Certified (NCCT) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How is checking suction function during setup correctly described?

answers.text: The planned anesthesia type is reviewed because it affects positioning, warming, and equipment needed in the room.
The count board or record is prepared before the case so sponge, sharp, and instrument counts can be posted.
Bony prominences are padded during positioning to protect skin and underlying nerves from pressure injury.
Suction is turned on and tested during setup to confirm strong, continuous vacuum at the tip.

questions.explanation: Weak suction discovered after incision leaves blood pooling in the wound. A setup test with water or air confirms the whole pathway works.

questions.question: How is room temperature and patient warmth correctly described?

answers.text: The technologist supports patient warmth by limiting unnecessary exposure and alerting the team when the room feels excessively cold for the patient.
Formalin used for specimens is handled with gloves and eye protection and kept capped to limit vapor exposure.
Powder and dust in the operating room can carry allergens and particles onto surfaces and into the air the team breathes.
Suction canisters are changed with gloves worn, ports capped, and care taken to avoid splashing the surrounding surfaces.

questions.explanation: Anesthetized patients lose heat quickly and cannot report feeling cold, so attention to exposure, covers, and room conditions is part of protecting the patient during long cases.

questions.question: Regarding suction handling at breakdown, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Suction tubing and canisters are handled as contaminated at breakdown, with care to avoid splashing fluids onto staff or clean surfaces.
Adhesive drapes and incise films are removed gently at case end to avoid skin injury, especially on fragile or elderly skin.
Specimens for culture are handled to avoid contamination and are sent promptly so organisms remain viable for the laboratory.
The initial amount and appearance of drain output are observed and shared with the circulating nurse for documentation.

questions.explanation: Suction contents are infectious waste, so slow, controlled handling with eye protection awareness protects the team during one of the messiest parts of turnover.

questions.question: How is interlaced fingers during scrub correctly described?

answers.text: Powder free gloves are used and any glove surface that contacts the wound is kept free of foreign material.
Fingers are kept separated and scrubbed on all surfaces, including the web spaces, during hand antisepsis.
Sterile solutions are poured into containers on the field without the bottle lip touching the container rim.
Instrument and sponge counts are performed on an organized field so every item is visible and accounted for.

questions.explanation: Microorganisms collect between fingers, and scrubbing only the palms and backs leaves those hidden surfaces as a source of contamination.

questions.question: Regarding irrigation fluid disposal, which statement is correct?

answers.text: A specimen container is never labeled from memory alone when the source can still be confirmed with the surgeon.
The technologist assists with securing the dressing by holding it in place while tape or a bandage is applied by the team.
Leftover irrigation fluid in basins is disposed of carefully during breakdown without splashing and without pouring it into hand washing sinks.
The final instrument check includes looking for bent tips, dull edges, and loose joints that need repair.

questions.explanation: Splashing spreads contaminated fluid and sinks for hand hygiene must stay clean, so the technologist uses the designated disposal point and pours slowly and close.

questions.question: Room temperature awareness for exposure - which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Room temperature and patient exposure are kept in mind, and only the area needed is uncovered at any one time.
The concentration of a medication is confirmed with the circulator from the original container before it is used.
A patient who has received sedation or feels dizzy is accompanied to the bathroom rather than sent alone.
Pooled alcohol based solution is wicked away and soaked materials are removed because pooled fuel raises fire risk.

questions.explanation: Every exposed area radiates heat, so uncovering only what is needed for each step is a quiet but real temperature safeguard.

questions.question: Regarding insulation integrity testing, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Electrosurgical instruments are inspected and tested for breaks in insulation that could allow current to stray and burn tissue.
Used instruments are kept moist after the case with an approved method so that residual soil stays soft until decontamination begins.
An implant package is opened only after the surgeon confirms the size and type, because an opened implant generally cannot be returned to stock.
A biological indicator contains highly resistant living spores that are used to test whether a sterilizer cycle actually killed microorganisms.

questions.explanation: Even a pinhole defect can cause a serious injury at an unseen site, so suspect instruments are removed from service for evaluation.

questions.question: Antibiotic irrigation handling awareness - which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: A stapler is never fired as a test on the sterile field because firing consumes the reload and wastes the device load.
Basins on the sterile field are filled without splashing and are refilled or replaced before they run dry.
When antibiotic irrigation is requested, it is prepared, labeled, and kept separate from plain irrigation fluids.
The technologist anticipates the next step of the procedure and readies its supplies before the surgeon has to ask.

questions.explanation: Mixing it into the general basin would change every use of that fluid. A separate labeled container keeps its use deliberate and traceable.

questions.question: Wiping down surfaces before opening sterile items - which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Clean unused instruments are kept apart from instruments that have been used and returned during setup checks.
Backup bulbs, batteries, and spare parts for key equipment are confirmed available during setup.
Horizontal surfaces in the room are damp wiped before sterile supplies are opened onto them.
Preference card items that are no longer stocked or no longer used are flagged for correction.

questions.explanation: Dust settles on tables and equipment between cases and overnight. Wiping first prevents that dust from being disturbed onto freshly opened sterile items.

questions.question: Electrosurgery tip holster when idle - which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: Hair removal, when ordered, is done with clippers rather than a razor to reduce skin injury before surgery.
The temperature of warmed irrigation is confirmed with the team rather than assumed from the warmer setting alone.
The electrosurgical pencil is returned to its holster whenever it is not actively in the surgeon hand.
A safety strap is placed across the patient after final positioning and checked to be snug without being overly tight.

questions.explanation: An active tip resting on drapes or skin can burn or ignite material if activated, so the holster is its only safe resting place.

questions.question: Passing ties and ligatures - which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: An implant is handled as little as possible, kept in its packaging until needed, and passed without contact with skin or nonsterile surfaces.
Ties are passed at the length and on the instrument the surgeon prefers, ready for immediate placement around a vessel.
During an anastomosis the technologist keeps fine sutures, suction, and sponges precisely staged because the work is delicate and sequential.
The specimen label is checked against the surgeon's stated site and the requisition before the container leaves the room.

questions.explanation: A tie that arrives too short or poorly mounted slows hemostasis, so preparing the preferred length and carrier in advance supports quick and secure vessel control.

questions.question: Curved needle general use - which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: A curved needle is used for most suturing because its arc lets the surgeon sew in confined spaces with wrist rotation.
Retention sutures are heavy strands placed to support a closure that is under unusual strain or healing poorly.
Suction canisters are checked for capacity and replaced before they overfill during a high-fluid case.
A tourniquet cuff is selected in a width and length suited to the limb so pressure is distributed evenly.

questions.explanation: The curve follows the natural turn of the needle holder and wrist. Straight needles are reserved for surfaces that are easily reached, such as skin in some closures.

questions.question: Riley, a surgical technologist assisting during the procedure, Regarding self reporting a break, which statement is correct?

answers.text: Protective eyewear and loupes are positioned before hand antisepsis begins.
A scrubbed person who notices their own glove brush a nonsterile surface reports it and changes the glove.
Instrument and sponge counts are performed on an organized field so every item is visible and accounted for.
The label of a sterile solution is verified aloud with the circulator before it is accepted onto the field.

questions.explanation: Self reporting models sterile conscience and prevents a known defect from being carried silently through the rest of the case.

questions.question: Robin, a surgical technologist preparing for the next case, Regarding energy setting confirmation, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Energy device settings that affect the patient are confirmed verbally with the surgeon before activation begins.
Fire risk factors present in a case, such as open oxygen and alcohol-based preparation, are voiced during the time-out discussion.
When a surgeon preference changes during a case, the technologist notes the change so the preference card can be updated afterward.
A technologist who is falling behind or unsure during setup asks for help early rather than struggling silently until the case is affected.

questions.explanation: A quick verbal confirmation prevents a setting carried over from a prior case or a bumped control from delivering unintended energy at the first activation of the device.

questions.question: Riley, a surgical technologist assisting during the procedure, Regarding delayed hemorrhage awareness, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The operative report details shared verbally are kept consistent with what was documented in the record.
Bleeding can begin hours after an initially stable recovery, so concerns are reported whenever they appear, not only in the first minutes.
A sharps injury sustained during or after the case is reported immediately and follow up care is obtained without delay.
A dressing that rapidly saturates with blood after surgery is recognized as a possible sign of hemorrhage and is reported immediately.

questions.explanation: A calm first hour does not guarantee the hours that follow, and the technologist who notices later drainage changes during follow up tasks still reports them promptly.

questions.question: Casey, a surgical technologist checking the sterile supplies, Which statement correctly describes susceptible host concept?

answers.text: The prefix hyper means above normal or excessive while the prefix hypo means below normal or deficient.
Anterior describes the front of the body or a structure while posterior describes the back of the body or a structure.
A susceptible host is a person whose defenses are weakened enough that exposure to a microorganism is more likely to cause infection.
The pelvic floor is a sling of muscles and connective tissue that supports the bladder, uterus, and rectum within the pelvis.

questions.explanation: Age, chronic disease, poor nutrition, and immune suppression all raise susceptibility, prompting extra protective measures for those surgical patients.

questions.question: Jordan, a surgical technologist scrubbed for the case, Regarding hemorrhage sign expanding swelling, which statement is correct?

answers.text: The type of dressing applied is included in the completed documentation so the recovery team knows what covers the wound.
During transfer, intravenous lines, monitoring cables, drains, and catheters are watched and given slack so none are pulled or disconnected.
Rapidly expanding swelling or firmness near the operative site is reported at once as a possible sign of internal bleeding.
A blood or fluid exposure to eyes, skin, or mucous membranes is washed promptly and reported for follow up evaluation.

questions.explanation: Swelling that grows before the eyes can mean blood collecting under the skin or in a body space, and early reporting gives the surgical team the chance to intervene sooner.

questions.question: Harper, a surgical technologist preparing the suction and electrosurgery setup, Which statement correctly describes local anesthesia overview?

answers.text: Local anesthesia numbs a small specific area at the surgical site while the patient remains fully awake and aware.
Medications on the sterile field are handled only with sterile technique and are drawn up or poured without contaminating the container or the solution.
The sagittal plane divides the body into right and left portions and a cut exactly on the midline is called midsagittal.
Normal flora are microorganisms that normally live on skin and mucous membranes without causing disease and help crowd out harmful organisms.

questions.explanation: Cases done this way still require a fully sterile setup and monitoring, and the technologist watches for signs that the patient is uncomfortable.

questions.question: Sage, a surgical technologist monitoring the sterile field boundaries, Regarding anticipating imaging in the case, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The technologist watches the assistant's signals as well, since exposure and suction requests may come from either pair of hands.
When intraoperative imaging is expected the technologist anticipates protective draping and clearing the field for the imaging equipment.
During an anastomosis the technologist keeps fine sutures, suction, and sponges precisely staged because the work is delicate and sequential.
The technologist watches that retractor blades rest where placed and do not press on delicate structures the surgeon has not exposed.

questions.explanation: Imaging equipment entering the field must remain sterile or protected, and preparing drapes and space beforehand keeps the sterile boundary intact during the study.

questions.question: Harper, a surgical technologist preparing the suction and electrosurgery setup, Regarding implant verification before opening, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Delicate instruments are kept separated from heavy instruments on the back table to prevent damage to their tips.
Normal saline is the most common irrigation fluid on the sterile field because it is gentle to tissues.
The electrosurgical generator is checked before the case so its settings, alarms, and connections are working.
An implant is verified by type and size with the team before its sterile packaging is opened.

questions.explanation: Once opened, an implant generally cannot be returned to stock. Confirming first prevents waste of a costly item and ensures the correct device is on the field.

vts-internal-medicine.quiz_title: Veterinary Technician Specialist - Internal Medicine (VTS) Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: How is gi foreign body imaging and monitoring correctly described?

answers.text: Alterations in small intestinal microbiota can accompany chronic enteropathy and contribute to diarrhea and cobalamin deficiency, but they are usually secondary to an underlying intestinal disorder.
Fasting status before abdominal ultrasound and endoscopy should be confirmed and documented, because food in the stomach limits visualization and increases aspiration risk.
Hepatic dysfunction can prolong drug metabolism and increase sensitivity to sedatives and other hepatically cleared medications, so doses and drug choices are adjusted by the veterinarian.
Suspected gastrointestinal obstruction is monitored for repeated vomiting, abdominal pain, and deteriorating perfusion, because obstructed bowel can become devitalized and perforate.

questions.explanation: Pressure and distension compromise bowel wall blood flow over time, changing urgency; serial examinations by the team detect deterioration between imaging studies.

questions.question: How is cytology versus histopathology correctly described?

answers.text: Cytology examines individual cells from a needle sample, while histopathology examines tissue architecture in a biopsy section.
Unintentional weight loss in an oncology patient is recorded at every visit using the same scale and technique.
Tumor measurements are recorded with the method used so later measurements remain comparable across visits.
Staging describes how far a tumor has spread in the body at the time of evaluation.

questions.explanation: Histopathology is often needed for grading and margins, and technicians help clients understand why a second sample may be recommended.

questions.question: How is advanced skills mastery concept correctly described?

answers.text: Documentation uses objective, observable language and avoids speculation about cause or intent
Nursing care plans are updated as patient status changes rather than left as written on admission.
Discharge instructions are given in plain language, in writing, and checked by asking the owner to explain them back
Mastery of an advanced skill means performing it safely, consistently, and with understanding of indications and complications

questions.explanation: True mastery includes knowing when a skill is appropriate and when to stop or escalate, not merely completing the technique once.

questions.question: How is cardiology heart failure forward signs correctly described?

answers.text: A quiet examination room improves the accuracy of heart auscultation and blood pressure measurement.
An electrocardiogram is the test of choice for characterizing an irregular heart rhythm.
Signs of poor forward cardiac output can include weakness, exercise intolerance, pale mucous membranes, and weak peripheral pulses.
Owners should seek urgent care if a heart patient develops open mouth breathing, collapse, blue tongue color, or sudden rear limb pain.

questions.explanation: These signs reflect reduced delivery of oxygenated blood to tissues even before obvious fluid accumulation develops in a heart patient.

questions.question: How is fine needle aspirate support correctly described?

answers.text: Contrast studies use an administered agent to outline structures such as the gastrointestinal tract, urinary tract, or vessels on imaging.
Fine needle aspiration collects cells from a mass or organ with minimal invasiveness before more invasive biopsy is considered.
Packed cell volume reflects the proportion of blood occupied by red cells and is read alongside total protein for context.
A reticulocyte count shows whether the marrow is releasing young red cells in response to red cell loss or destruction.

questions.explanation: Aspirates sample cells without tissue architecture, so the technician prepares multiple good slides and the veterinarian decides if biopsy is still needed.

questions.question: Pheochromocytoma rhythm risk - which statement describes it correctly?

answers.text: Bursts of catecholamine release from a phaeochromocytoma can provoke dangerous fast or irregular heart rhythms
Non steroidal anti inflammatory drugs can reduce protective blood flow within the kidney, especially in dehydrated or kidney compromised patients
Casts in urine sediment form inside renal tubules, so their presence localises at least part of the problem to the kidney itself
A careful history of when leakage occurs, water intake, and voluntary voiding helps the veterinarian work up urinary incontinence

questions.explanation: Cardiac monitoring matters during suspected episodes, and pulse quality, rhythm, and blood pressure changes are recorded and reported to the veterinarian promptly.

questions.question: Regarding facial nerve deficit clues, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Rehabilitation goals for neurologic patients are set by the veterinarian and advanced gradually as function returns.
Spinal pain is assessed by posture, vocalization, reluctance to move, and response to gentle palpation performed as directed.
Body weight, appetite, and water intake are tracked in hospitalized neurologic patients as part of overall nursing care.
Facial nerve deficits cause drooping of the ear and lip, inability to blink fully, and food dropping on the affected side.

questions.explanation: An incomplete blink threatens the eye surface, so technicians report it promptly and apply eye lubrication only as directed by the veterinarian.

questions.question: Respiratory acid base concept - which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Cystocentesis provides the cleanest urine sample for culture, while free catch samples are more prone to contamination.
Coagulation screening tests assess how well the clotting cascade forms a clot before invasive procedures or when bleeding is seen.
Diagnostic samples collected before treatment starts preserve information that therapy can quickly erase.
A respiratory acid-base change begins with altered ventilation changing carbon dioxide levels in the blood.

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is controlled by breathing, so ventilation history and examination findings help the veterinarian confirm a respiratory origin.

questions.question: Regarding urine protein ratio principle, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: As kidney function falls, phosphorus is retained in the blood and contributes to further harm to bone and kidney tissue
An Addisonian crisis presents with collapse, profound weakness, vomiting, diarrhoea, and poor circulation requiring urgent veterinary care
Daily body weight is one of the most sensitive nursing tools for detecting fluid retention or ongoing fluid losses in hospitalised kidney patients
Comparing urine protein to urine creatinine on a single sample helps quantify how much protein the kidney is losing

questions.explanation: A ratio corrects for urine concentration, giving the veterinarian a repeatable way to track proteinuria over time without collecting urine over a full day.

questions.question: Regarding aspiration pneumonia risk, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Blood donor animals should be screened for infectious diseases and general health to protect both donor safety and recipient safety.
A well-made blood smear supports evaluation of red cell morphology, platelet estimates, and white cell appearance by the veterinary team.
Aspiration pneumonia can follow inhalation of food, liquid, or vomited material, especially in patients with swallowing or esophageal disorders.
When zoonotic disease is suspected, staff should use gloves and other protective equipment and follow hand hygiene and waste handling protocols.

questions.explanation: Aspiration introduces material into the airways and lungs. Technicians watch at-risk patients closely when feeding and report coughing or breathing changes.

questions.question: Mei, a veterinary technician on an internal medicine team, How is ppid laminitis link correctly described?

answers.text: Horses with pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction have an increased risk of laminitis, so hoof comfort and digital pulses are monitored routinely.
The neurologic form of equine herpesvirus infection can cause hindlimb weakness, incoordination, and bladder dysfunction and demands strict isolation.
In a horse with suspected renal disease, monitoring urine production and concentration helps the veterinarian assess kidney function over time.
Before fluids or medication are given by nasogastric tube in a horse, placement in the esophagus is confirmed to avoid delivery into the airway.

questions.explanation: Hormonal changes in affected horses alter insulin regulation, which is linked to lamellar injury, making regular foot checks part of ongoing care.

questions.question: Follow up scheduling support - which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: Perfusion assessment combines mucous membrane appearance, capillary refill observation, pulse quality, and extremity warmth
Before discharge, follow up arrangements, warning signs, and emergency contact routes are explained clearly to the owner
Food offered, amount eaten, water intake, and appetite changes are recorded accurately for hospitalized patients
Blood pressure measurement uses a calm environment, consistent positioning, an appropriate cuff, and repeated readings

questions.explanation: Owners leaving with a clear plan and knowing when to seek help are less likely to delay care if recovery stalls.

questions.question: Aisha, a veterinary technician specialist in a teaching hospital, How is itp immune platelet destruction correctly described?

answers.text: Disorders of platelet function or number commonly cause mucosal surface bleeding such as gum bleeding and nosebleeds.
Patients with contagious enteric disease require prompt cleanup of fecal contamination, dedicated equipment, and careful hand hygiene after handling.
Complete and accurate nursing notes support continuity of care for complex internal medicine patients.
Immune-mediated thrombocytopenia occurs when the immune system destroys platelets, increasing risk of spontaneous bleeding and bruising.

questions.explanation: Platelet destruction impairs normal clot formation at vessel injury sites. Technicians watch for bruising and bleeding and use gentle handling and restraint.

questions.question: Ruth, a veterinary technician specialist mentoring junior technicians, How is nutrition support anorectic patient correctly described?

answers.text: Foal diarrhea nursing focuses on hydration status, continued nursing where advised, skin care of the hindquarters, and strict hygiene.
An anorectic horse or ruminant is supported with small, palatable, veterinarian approved offerings, intake records, and monitoring for refeeding complications.
Temperature, pulse, and respiration are recorded at consistent times of day to make trend comparisons in large animal patients meaningful.
For equine abdominal ultrasound the technician clips or wets the hair coat as directed, applies coupling contact, and restrains the horse for a systematic scan.

questions.explanation: Prolonged inappetence worsens many internal medicine conditions, so quantifying what is actually eaten guides timely nutritional intervention.

questions.question: Beth, a veterinary technician specialist supporting a multi-doctor practice, How is lymphangiectasia role in protein loss correctly described?

answers.text: Successful elimination diet trials require feeding only the prescribed diet and water, avoiding treats, table food, and flavored supplements for the full trial period set by the veterinarian.
Nutritional plans for chronic liver and intestinal disease work best when one diet is fed consistently and all household members follow the same instructions.
Acute gastroenteritis management centers on hydration, nausea and pain control as directed, and gradual reintroduction of a digestible diet once vomiting is controlled.
Intestinal lymphangiectasia causes protein losing enteropathy when dilated lacteals leak lymph rich in protein, fat, and lymphocytes into the intestinal lumen.

questions.explanation: Dilated lacteals rupture and lose lymph, which depletes protein and lymphocytes; dietary fat restriction is often part of the veterinarian directed management plan.

questions.question: Lucia, a veterinary technician working with exotic companion animals, How is cerebellar ataxia hypermetria correctly described?

answers.text: Body weight, appetite, and water intake are tracked in hospitalized neurologic patients as part of overall nursing care.
Weak patients with swallowing or esophageal problems need close watching for coughing, fever, and breathing changes suggesting aspiration.
Cerebellar ataxia features exaggerated, high-stepping movements and intention tremor that worsens as the patient reaches for a target.
Gait assessment describes symmetry, stride, limb placement, dragging, crossing, and willingness to bear weight on each limb.
