answers.text: An assignment of mortgage transfers the mortgage lien and the secured debt from the original holder to a new holder who then stands in the holder place of record.
An assignment of mortgage cancels the lien and leaves the debt unsecured.
An assignment of mortgage transfers ownership of the land to the new holder.
An assignment of mortgage can be made only by the borrower who granted the mortgage.

questions.explanation: Examiners test this because loans change hands often and the abstract must show who currently holds the mortgage lien. The correct statement is: An assignment of mortgage transfers the mortgage lien and the secured debt from the original holder to a new holder who then stands in the holder place of record.

questions.question: Regarding revocation of a kansas abstracter license, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: The Board may warn a licensee but has no power to suspend or revoke a Kansas abstracter license.
Revocation of a Kansas abstracter license affects only the firm's name, while the examined manager may keep practicing alone.
The Board may revoke or suspend a Kansas abstracter license for cause under the Act, and a person whose license has been revoked may no longer lawfully make or sell abstracts in Kansas.
A revoked Kansas abstracter may keep selling abstracts already in stock until the supply runs out.

questions.explanation: Examiners test revocation because it is the Board's strongest tool and candidates must understand that losing the license ends the right to practice. The correct statement is: The Board may revoke or suspend a Kansas abstracter license for cause under the Act, and a person whose license has been revoked may no longer lawfully make or sell abstracts in Kansas.

questions.question: Concerning reference to a recorded plat incorporating it, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A deed that refers to a recorded plat makes the plat a private document unavailable to later searchers.
A deed that refers to a recorded plat incorporates only the lot numbers and none of the plat boundaries.
A deed that describes land by reference to a recorded plat incorporates that plat into the description as if the plat were fully set out in the deed.
A deed that refers to a recorded plat is void unless the plat is copied word for word into the deed.

questions.explanation: Examiners test this because the incorporated plat supplies dimensions, streets, and easements that the short deed description omits. The correct statement is: A deed that describes land by reference to a recorded plat incorporates that plat into the description as if the plat were fully set out in the deed.

questions.question: On the subject of name variations and spelling in searching, which statement is correct?

answers.text: A careful searcher checks only the exact spelling shown on the most recent deed.
A careful searcher checks name variations, alternate spellings, initials, and married or former names because an index entry under a variant can hide an instrument affecting title.
A careful searcher treats a middle initial difference as proof that two entries concern different land.
A careful searcher ignores earlier names of an owner who later changed names by marriage.

questions.explanation: Examiners test this because Kansas indexes are name based, and a missed variant is a missed instrument. The correct statement is: A careful searcher checks name variations, alternate spellings, initials, and married or former names because an index entry under a variant can hide an instrument affecting title.

questions.question: In a study group for licensing candidates, a mentor asks about matters outside the record search. Which statement is true?

answers.text: Matters that lie outside the public records, such as an unrecorded private agreement between strangers to the record, are beyond what the certificate of abstract certifies.
An abstracter must certify private agreements learned through neighborhood gossip as if they were matters of record.
Matters outside the record search are the abstracter's chief responsibility and outweigh the recorded instruments.
If a matter is outside the records, the abstracter must invent a showing for it so the abstract looks complete.

questions.explanation: Examiners test off-record limits because candidates must know where record certification ends and other forms of inquiry begin. The correct statement is: Matters that lie outside the public records, such as an unrecorded private agreement between strangers to the record, are beyond what the certificate of abstract certifies.

questions.question: Regarding covenants carried by a general warranty deed in kansas, which of the following statements is correct?

answers.text: A general warranty deed warrants only defects the grantor personally created after acquiring the land.
A general warranty deed contains no covenants at all and is identical in effect to a quitclaim deed.
A general warranty deed carries broad covenants by the grantor, warranting the title against defects arising through anyone, whether before or during the grantor's ownership.
A general warranty deed warrants the future market value of the land rather than the title conveyed.

questions.explanation: Examiners test general warranty covenants because abstracters must recognize the broadest deed warranty when they show the instrument in a chain. The correct statement is: A general warranty deed carries broad covenants by the grantor, warranting the title against defects arising through anyone, whether before or during the grantor's ownership.

questions.question: Studying for the abstracter license, a candidate reviews administrator deed in intestate estate. Which statement reflects how it works?

answers.text: An administrator deed is signed by the county treasurer to collect delinquent taxes.
An administrator deed is a deed from a business administrator conveying company offices.
An administrator deed requires the decedent to have left a will naming that administrator as a beneficiary.
An administrator deed is used when a court-appointed administrator conveys real estate of a decedent who left no valid will or no executor able to serve.

questions.explanation: Examiners test this because distinguishing executor and administrator conveyances helps the abstracter read estate links correctly. The correct statement is: An administrator deed is used when a court-appointed administrator conveys real estate of a decedent who left no valid will or no executor able to serve.

questions.question: Studying for the abstracter license, a candidate reviews tract books in the abstract plant. Which statement reflects how it works?

answers.text: Tract books organize plant entries alphabetically by the buyers surname with no reference to land.
Tract books record only tax payments and contain no entries for deeds or mortgages.
Tract books organize plant entries by the legal description of each tract so all instruments affecting that tract can be found together.
Tract books are kept by the county and an abstract firm is forbidden to maintain its own.

questions.explanation: Examiners test this because searching by tract is how the abstracter avoids missing an instrument on the described land. The correct statement is: Tract books organize plant entries by the legal description of each tract so all instruments affecting that tract can be found together.

questions.question: For a licensing candidate, a candidate studying legal descriptions and liens for the Kansas examination, reviewing aliquot parts of a section matters. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Aliquot parts are irregular fragments left over when a section is crossed by a river or a road.
Aliquot parts are the regular subdivisions of a section created by dividing it into halves and quarters, such as the northeast quarter or the southwest quarter of the section.
Aliquot parts are parcels created by a private survey using bearings and distances.
Aliquot parts are the numbered lots along the north and west edges of a township.

questions.explanation: Examiners test aliquot parts because most Kansas farm descriptions are built from them and candidates must separate them from lots and metes parcels. The correct statement is: Aliquot parts are the regular subdivisions of a section created by dividing it into halves and quarters, such as the northeast quarter or the southwest quarter of the section.

questions.question: A licensing candidate reads up on mechanic and other statutory lien records before a study session. Which statement reflects how it works?

answers.text: Records of statutory liens for improvements are filed only with the builder and never in a public office.
Records of statutory liens affect only the personal property of the landowner.
Records of statutory liens, such as statements filed by those who furnished labor or materials for improvements, are part of a complete search because they can claim against the improved land.
Records of statutory liens can be ignored whenever a deed in the chain is a warranty deed.

questions.explanation: Examiners test this because improvement liens arise outside deeds and surprise buyers who searched nothing else. The correct statement is: Records of statutory liens, such as statements filed by those who furnished labor or materials for improvements, are part of a complete search because they can claim against the improved land.

questions.question: A candidate, a candidate preparing for the Kansas abstracter licensing examination, is evaluating extension for a new transaction before the licensing examination. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: When an abstract is extended for a new transaction, the abstracter searches the interval since the last certification and shows every new matter affecting the title.
When an abstract is extended for a new transaction, the abstracter searches only the records of the register of deeds and skips the courts.
When an abstract is extended, matters recorded before the last certificate may be removed to make the abstract shorter.
When an abstract is extended, the new buyer is responsible for searching the gap and telling the abstracter what to add.

questions.explanation: Examiners test extensions because a gap in the search interval is exactly where a new lien or conveyance can hide. The correct statement is: When an abstract is extended for a new transaction, the abstracter searches the interval since the last certification and shows every new matter affecting the title.

questions.question: For a licensing candidate, an employee of a Kansas abstract firm preparing for licensure, reviewing marital interests in Kansas land matters. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Marriage never creates any interest in a spouse's Kansas land, so only the titled spouse ever needs to sign.
A spouse's interest is extinguished automatically whenever the titled spouse records a deed to a stranger.
A spouse can hold an interest in Kansas land of the other spouse, so deeds and releases in a chain are examined for whether both spouses joined where their interests required it.
Marital interests matter only for personal property and are never considered in examining title to land.

questions.explanation: Examiners test marital interests because a missing spousal signature or release is a common reason an apparent chain is incomplete. The correct statement is: A spouse can hold an interest in Kansas land of the other spouse, so deeds and releases in a chain are examined for whether both spouses joined where their interests required it.

questions.question: For a licensing candidate, an abstracter trainee studying Kansas title practice for the Board examination, reviewing abstracter duty to search taxes matters. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: The abstracter searches the county tax records for the described land and shows the tax status found in those records.
The abstracter may skip the tax search if the seller states that all taxes have been paid.
The abstracter searches only federal records and never looks at county tax records.
The abstracter decides what the tax should have been and substitutes that figure for the record.

questions.explanation: Examiners test this because a complete tax search is a core part of every Kansas abstract of title. The correct statement is: The abstracter searches the county tax records for the described land and shows the tax status found in those records.

questions.question: For a licensing candidate, an employee of a Kansas abstract firm preparing for licensure, reviewing closing corners in the government survey matters. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: A closing corner is a corner shared equally by the four sections that meet at a correction line.
A closing corner is a temporary point used only until the final plat is approved.
A closing corner is a corner set where a survey line closes upon and ends at another line, such as a standard parallel, and it marks the end of the line being run rather than a corner of both tracts.
A closing corner may be moved by later surveyors to make the adjoining townships line up evenly.

questions.explanation: Examiners test closing corners because treating one as a standard corner misreads the offsets that correction lines create in the grid. The correct statement is: A closing corner is a corner set where a survey line closes upon and ends at another line, such as a standard parallel, and it marks the end of the line being run rather than a corner of both tracts.

questions.question: A candidate, a candidate studying legal descriptions and liens for the Kansas examination, is preparing for the licensing examination. Which statement about comparing descriptions across the search is accurate?

answers.text: Comparing the legal description in each instrument found during the search confirms that every link concerns the same land and exposes instruments that describe different or additional ground.
Comparing descriptions across the search is unnecessary once the owner names match.
Comparing descriptions across the search matters only for the first deed in the chain.
Comparing descriptions across the search should be skipped when the instruments are lengthy.

questions.explanation: Examiners test this because a chain of the right names describing the wrong land is not a chain for the parcel at all. The correct statement is: Comparing the legal description in each instrument found during the search confirms that every link concerns the same land and exposes instruments that describe different or additional ground.

questions.question: While planning revision, a group including an employee of a Kansas abstract firm preparing for licensure discusses abstracter check of execution formalities. Which statement is true?

answers.text: An abstracter checks that a power of attorney was properly executed by the principal, including signature and any acknowledgment the record shows, before relying on an act done under it.
An abstracter should rely on a power even when the principal signature is missing from the recorded copy.
Execution formalities matter only for deeds and never for the powers under which deeds are signed.
An acknowledgment defect in a power can be ignored whenever the agent signature looks genuine.

questions.explanation: Examiners test this because a defect in executing the power undermines every later act that depends on that power. The correct statement is: An abstracter checks that a power of attorney was properly executed by the principal, including signature and any acknowledgment the record shows, before relying on an act done under it.

faa-ap-airframe.quiz_title: FAA A&P - Airframe Exam Prep FREE Sample Exam

questions.question: Which statement gives the most accurate picture of thread inspection?

answers.text: Stripped threads may be built up with sealant so the nut feels tight.
A nut that binds partway on a bolt is evidence of extra locking strength.
Thread damage matters only on large bolts and never on smaller airframe fasteners.
Threads are kept clean and are checked so the nut runs on properly and reaches the required grip and engagement.

questions.explanation: Sound threads deliver full clamping force and locking action, so thread condition is a direct measure of whether a joint can be trusted. The statement that holds here is that threads are kept clean and are checked so the nut runs on properly and reaches the required grip and engagement.

questions.question: Which statement best describes hydraulic pressure transmission principle?

answers.text: Because fluid does not compress like air, hydraulic actuators respond promptly and can hold position under load when valves trap the fluid.
Hydraulic fluid compresses greatly, and that compression is what moves actuators.
Pressure in a confined fluid acts only in the direction of pump flow and nowhere else.
Air is preferred inside hydraulic lines because it makes actuator movement softer and more precise.

questions.explanation: Every hydraulic troubleshooting decision rests on pressure transmitted through an incompressible fluid, so grasping that principle turns circuit diagrams into predictable cause and effect. The statement that holds here is that because fluid does not compress like air, hydraulic actuators respond promptly and can hold position under load when valves trap the fluid.

questions.question: On the subject of static port blockage effects, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: A blocked static port causes the attitude indicator gyro to stop spinning.
Static blockage drains vacuum from the directional gyro and has no effect on the altimeter.
With static pressure trapped, an altimeter tends to hold a stale reading instead of following a climb or descent.
Static blockage affects only the magnetic compass and leaves pressure instruments unchanged.

questions.explanation: Recognizing blockage symptoms helps a mechanic trace an instrument complaint to the system rather than replacing a good instrument. Contamination, tape, and insect debris at a port are simple causes with serious flight effects. The statement that holds here is that with static pressure trapped, an altimeter tends to hold a stale reading instead of following a climb or descent.

questions.question: In the area of detector system testing, which of the following is accurate?

answers.text: Testing a fire loop requires setting an actual fire in the nacelle.
Detector systems have no self monitoring for wiring faults.
Fault indications may be ignored because the system still works perfectly.
A successful test proves the indication path works from the control unit to the flight deck.

questions.explanation: Regular testing is how latent faults are found on the ground instead of during the emergency the system exists for. The statement that holds here is that a successful test proves the indication path works from the control unit to the flight deck.

questions.question: Which statement most accurately describes cable inspection findings?

answers.text: Broken cable strands can be soldered back together and the cable returned to service.
Corrosion on a cable is cause for close evaluation because internal corrosion can weaken strands that still look sound outside.
Wear at pulleys is expected to polish strands bright and is never a rejection cause.
Cables hidden inside structure do not need inspection access or attention.

questions.explanation: Control cables fail strand by strand in wear areas long before they part, so careful inspection at pulleys and fairleads catches a failure while it is still preventable. The statement that holds here is that corrosion on a cable is cause for close evaluation because internal corrosion can weaken strands that still look sound outside.

questions.question: Regarding composite fiber and resin basics, which of the following statements is accurate?

answers.text: Fiber direction has no effect on strength as long as enough layers are used.
The fibers carry most of the load, while the resin matrix holds the fibers in position and transfers load between them.
The resin matrix alone is designed to carry the primary structural loads.
Fiberglass, carbon fiber, and aramid fibers are interchangeable in a repair with no change in properties.

questions.explanation: Understanding fibers and resin helps a mechanic handle and repair composites so the restored part keeps its designed strength and stiffness. The statement that holds here is that the fibers carry most of the load, while the resin matrix holds the fibers in position and transfers load between them.

questions.question: For a specialist explaining steering and towing limits to a trainee, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Powered steering gears can be towed against their actuators with no bypass needed on any design.
Damage from overtravel would always be visible as a broken part.
Towing uses the correct tow bar and shear protection where fitted, and steering disconnect or bypass procedures in the manual are followed on powered steering gears.
Shear pins in tow bars are a nuisance and stronger pins are an improvement.

questions.explanation: Ground crews move aircraft daily with powerful tugs, so respecting steering and towing limits prevents hidden gear damage that later shows up as shimmy and steering failures. The statement that holds here is that towing uses the correct tow bar and shear protection where fitted, and steering disconnect or bypass procedures in the manual are followed on powered steering gears.

questions.question: Pick the statement that best captures fuel line routing and chafing protection.

answers.text: Support clamps keep vibration from fatiguing lines and fittings.
Fuel lines may rest directly on sharp structure if the run is short.
Chafing on a fuel line is cosmetic and never causes leaks.
Clamps are optional on lines that feel stiff enough to hold shape.

questions.explanation: Vibration will saw an unprotected line against structure over time. Correct routing, cushion clamps, and clearance checks are quiet work that prevents leaks and fires. The statement that holds here is that support clamps keep vibration from fatiguing lines and fittings.

questions.question: For a specialist explaining waste tank level indication to a trainee, which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Level sensors work by weighing the aircraft on its gear struts.
No warning is provided because toilets simply stop mattering when full.
Sensors in the tank report level to an indicator used by the crew and by servicing personnel.
A tank can accept waste indefinitely once the full indication appears.

questions.explanation: An overflowing or disabled waste system is a serious cabin problem on a long flight. Level awareness lets crews manage use and lets servicers act before departure. The statement that holds here is that sensors in the tank report level to an indicator used by the crew and by servicing personnel.

questions.question: A workshop speaker is covering propeller ice protection. Which statement from the talk is accurate?

answers.text: Electric propeller deice uses heated elements on the blade roots or leading portions to loosen ice so centrifugal force sheds it.
Propeller blades never collect ice because they spin too fast.
Electric prop deice heats the engine cylinders to keep blades warm.
Propeller ice is useful because it adds flywheel weight to the blades.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: Balanced shedding matters as much as removal, so prop deice timing and element checks are part of vibration prevention. The statement that holds here is that electric propeller deice uses heated elements on the blade roots or leading portions to loosen ice so centrifugal force sheds it.

questions.question: A trainee asks a senior specialist about fabric strength testing. Which reply is accurate?

answers.text: Fabric strength testing is done by pulling on the covering by hand and judging the stretch.
If fabric looks bright and clean, strength testing is unnecessary regardless of age or exposure.
Fabric strength is evaluated to decide whether a covering can remain in service or must be replaced.
A punch tester reading may be taken over a rib or tape because support under the fabric does not affect the result.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: Objective strength testing prevents aged, weakened fabric from being kept in service on appearance alone until it tears in flight. The statement that holds here is that fabric strength is evaluated to decide whether a covering can remain in service or must be replaced.

questions.question: Which of these statements best sums up combustion heater operation and safety?

answers.text: A combustion heater warms the cabin by mixing exhaust gas directly with cabin air.
Combustion heaters use engine coolant as their heat source.
Heater fuel is supplied from the cabin ventilation ducts.
Heater controls include ignition, fuel control, and protective switches that shut the heater down when operation is unsafe.

questions.explanation: A combustion heater gives strong heat independent of engine bleed air, but it burns fuel inside the airframe. Careful inspection of the chamber, exhaust, and safety controls prevents fire and exhaust contamination. The statement that holds here is that heater controls include ignition, fuel control, and protective switches that shut the heater down when operation is unsafe.

questions.question: Stay with the published framework. Which statement about conformity and return to service is correct?

answers.text: Any person who helped with the work may approve the aircraft for return to service.
Return to service after inspection or maintenance is made by a person authorized for that work, after the work is found to conform to approved data.
Return to service may be signed before the work is finished to save time later.
Conformity is judged by appearance alone, without reference to approved data.

questions.explanation: Authorized return to service is the formal statement that the aircraft conforms and is safe, so it must rest on completed, correct work. The statement that holds here is that return to service after inspection or maintenance is made by a person authorized for that work, after the work is found to conform to approved data.

questions.question: At a study session on oxygen system types and servicing caution, which statement on the slides is correct?

answers.text: Aircraft oxygen may be supplied as stored gas in cylinders or generated chemically when a chemical candle is activated.
Gaseous oxygen cylinders may be serviced with ordinary shop tools covered in grease.
Oxygen system cleanliness matters only for appearance, not for safety.
Chemical oxygen generators can be turned off and restarted as needed in flight.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: Oxygen greatly increases fire risk when it contacts hydrocarbons, and a contaminated fitting can ignite. Clean hands, clean tools, and approved materials are nonnegotiable habits around oxygen servicing. The statement that holds here is that aircraft oxygen may be supplied as stored gas in cylinders or generated chemically when a chemical candle is activated.

questions.question: A trainee asks a senior specialist about aircraft antenna mounting and bonding. Which reply is accurate?

answers.text: An aircraft antenna must be mounted securely and bonded well to the airframe so it has a proper electrical ground plane and a reliable signal path.
Antennas may be mounted loosely so vibration keeps the connector clean.
Sealing an antenna mount is harmful because antennas must breathe outside air.
An antenna works best when it is electrically isolated from the airframe by thick rubber.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: Many weak radio complaints trace back to the antenna installation rather than the radio. Inspecting mounts, bonding, and sealing protects range and clarity for every system on board. The statement that holds here is that an aircraft antenna must be mounted securely and bonded well to the airframe so it has a proper electrical ground plane and a reliable signal path.

questions.question: Read the item and decide. Which of the following statements about mast and hub components is NOT correct?

answers.text: The mast is a nonstructural tube that carries only electrical wiring.
Retaining hardware and blade grips on the hub are inspected for security, wear, and correct installation.
The mast carries drive torque and flight loads between the transmission and the rotor hub.
The hub connects the blades to the mast and houses the hinges, bearings, or flexing elements of the head.

questions.explanation: The mast and hub are the load path for the whole aircraft in flight, so their hardware standards are uncompromising. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that the mast is a nonstructural tube that carries only electrical wiring.

questions.question: A workshop speaker is covering steering and towing limits. Which statement from the talk is accurate?

answers.text: Nose gear steering and towing have angle limits that must not be exceeded, or steering links, stops, and strut structure can be damaged.
Powered steering gears can be towed against their actuators with no bypass needed on any design.
Damage from overtravel would always be visible as a broken part.
Any tow angle the tug can reach is safe for the nose gear.

questions.explanation: In practice, accuracy matters: Ground crews move aircraft daily with powerful tugs, so respecting steering and towing limits prevents hidden gear damage that later shows up as shimmy and steering failures. The statement that holds here is that nose gear steering and towing have angle limits that must not be exceeded, or steering links, stops, and strut structure can be damaged.

questions.question: Apply the standard approach here. Which of the following statements about cable inspection findings is NOT correct?

answers.text: Corrosion on a cable is cause for close evaluation because internal corrosion can weaken strands that still look sound outside.
Control cable inspection looks for broken strands, wear where cables pass over pulleys and through fairleads, corrosion, and fraying.
A cable with broken strands in a critical wear area must be replaced as the manual directs rather than dressed or taped.
Broken cable strands can be soldered back together and the cable returned to service.

questions.explanation: Control cables fail strand by strand in wear areas long before they part, so careful inspection at pulleys and fairleads catches a failure while it is still preventable. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that broken cable strands can be soldered back together and the cable returned to service.

questions.question: This is a foundational item. Which of the following statements about battery servicing safety practices is NOT correct?

answers.text: Charging batteries in a sealed unventilated box is recommended.
Jewelry and loose metal near battery terminals create a short circuit and burn hazard and must be kept away.
Battery servicing requires ventilation because charging can release flammable gas from the cells.
Spilled acid is neutralized with an appropriate mild alkaline solution, while alkaline electrolyte spills use a suitable mild acid solution, as the manual directs.

questions.explanation: Batteries combine stored energy, corrosive chemicals, and flammable gas in a small space. Ventilation, neutralization knowledge, and terminal discipline keep routine servicing from becoming an injury. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that charging batteries in a sealed unventilated box is recommended.

questions.question: One option fits the principle best. Which of the following statements about aluminum alloy heat treatment awareness is NOT correct?

answers.text: Uncontrolled heating of heat-treated structure, such as from welding or fire exposure, can reduce its strength and requires evaluation.
All aluminum alloys respond to heat treatment in the same way and reach the same strength.
Heat treatment changes the strength of certain aluminum alloys through controlled heating and cooling processes.
The temper of an aluminum alloy affects its strength and formability, so the correct alloy and temper must be used in a repair.

questions.explanation: Respecting alloy temper keeps repairs at design strength and prevents well-meant heating from silently weakening the structure. The statement that does NOT hold — the one this item asks for — is the claim that all aluminum alloys respond to heat treatment in the same way and reach the same strength.
